"Pocket Dimension" refers to an artificially created subspace used temporarily as a laboratory or storage area under strict regulatory oversight. "Quiet List" designates those prohibited arts and techniques deemed too dangerous for unrestricted practice, maintained in confidence pursuant to § 300.4. "Paradox Trial" is the formal adjudicative proceeding whereby peers determine guilt or innocence following allegations of magical misconduct, conducted according to established ritual protocols.

§ 1.7 Construction
In interpreting this Codex, courts shall employ principles of purposive construction, seeking to effectuate the legislative intent behind each provision. Ambiguities arising from conflicting clauses are resolved in favor of public safety and orderly magical practice. Terms not explicitly defined herein retain their ordinary meanings unless context dictates otherwise. Historical usage within the magical community provides persuasive authority for resolving uncertainties regarding arcane concepts and customs.

Aggregation of Conduct
Repeated minor infractions may collectively constitute a substantive violation when they demonstrate a pattern of disregard for established norms. The seriousness of aggregated conduct shall be weighed against the potential harm posed by individual acts taken in isolation. Discretionary relief may be granted where cumulative impact far exceeds the sum of its parts.

Effective Date and Savings
These provisions take effect upon signature by sufficient officers, retroactive only to the date of first publication unless expressly stated otherwise. Existing obligations unaffected by this Codex continue unabated; nothing herein shall impair vested rights or pending actions except as necessary to prevent future violations. Any prior laws inconsistent with these rules are hereby repealed to the extent of such conflict.

Seals and Stamps
Official seals, stamps, and signatures serve as conclusive evidence of authenticity when affixed by authorized personnel in accordance with prescribed procedures. Counterfeiting or unauthorized reproduction carries severe penalties under applicable statutes. Electronic equivalents hold equal weight provided they meet all technical requirements for integrity and verification. Nothing herein shall be construed to recognize any device or mark lacking explicit statutory authorization.

Reserved Catchlines
Certain provisions intentionally left open allow the Accords Desk greater flexibility in responding to evolving threats without requiring formal amendment processes. These catch-all clauses function as safety valves, enabling adaptive governance while maintaining overall legal certainty for regulated entities. Their scope shall be construed narrowly to avoid encroaching upon established rights absent compelling justification.

This section establishes foundational interpretive tools necessary for consistent application of subsequent rules throughout this Codex. Clear definitions prevent frivolous disputes over semantic technicalities, allowing adjudicators to focus on substantive issues affecting public welfare and professional standards alike.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The legal interpretation of thaumaturgical transgressions under the Autumnwood Accords shall not be predicated upon the isolation of discrete acts. Pursuant to the principles of holistic oversight, the fragmentation of conduct shall not prevent a finding of violation. A mage who commits a series of minor infractions, each of which might individually fall below the threshold of a formal Paradox Trial, may nonetheless be found in breach of the Accords if the cumulative weight of said conduct demonstrates a systemic disregard for the safety of the Midlands or the integrity of the weave.

The Accords Desk reserves the right to aggregate multiple instances of unauthorized mana-leakage, minor property damage, or procedural negligence into a single comprehensive indictment. For instance, a practitioner who repeatedly fails to register minor sensory-scrying devices while simultaneously neglecting to report minor localized fluctuations in the ley lines may be prosecuted for a unified pattern of negligence. The prosecution shall not be required to prove that any single act constitutes a capital offense; rather, the evidence shall be presented as a continuous tapestry of non-compliance.

This construction is intended to prevent the "death by a thousand cuts" defense, wherein a rogue practitioner attempts to circumvent the Aegis Magi's oversight by ensuring that no single action reaches the requisite severity for intervention. By aggregating conduct, the Accords ensure that the spirit of the law—the preservation of stability as championed by the Conservators and the regulated advancement of the Innovators—is maintained against those who seek to exploit technicalities. See § 1.6 for further clarification on the lexicon of "systemic disregard."

All findings of violation based on aggregated conduct shall be recorded in the primary registry of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The presiding council shall have the discretion to determine the appropriate severity of the sanction, ranging from a formal reprimand to a full Paradox Trial, based on the qualitative nature of the aggregated acts. This rule remains in effect regardless of the temporal distance between the individual acts, provided they can be linked to a singular intent or a recurring pattern of behavior.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The provisions of the Autumnwood Accords shall take effect immediately upon the ratification of the founding signatures by Archmage Veyra and the respective heads of the Conservator and Innovator factions. All prior Accords, temporary mandates, and localized magical treaties that were superseded by the ratification of this Codex are hereby rendered subordinate to the current framework. However, any specific protections or rights established in prior Accords that are not explicitly revoked by this Codex shall remain in force, provided they do not conflict with the primary objectives of the current Accords.

Regarding the preservation of existing legal statuses, the principle of "Savings" ensures that the transition to this new regulatory body does not result in a total vacuum of law. Any ongoing investigations, active seals, or pending Paradox Trials initiated under previous frameworks shall remain active and be adjudicated according to the procedural standards of the Accords Desk at the time of their commencement. The transition of authority from previous regimes to the current Accords Desk does not constitute a stay of execution or a dissolution of existing magical restraints.

Be advised that the presence of dead citations within Part XIV of the archival records shall not, under any circumstances, revive repealed schemes or defunct regulations. The mere existence of a reference to an obsolete law within a secondary text does not grant that law any legal standing or binding power. If a practitioner seeks to rely on a repealed mandate, they must demonstrate that the mandate was specifically preserved by a secondary "Savings" clause; otherwise, the Accords Desk shall treat the citation as a historical curiosity with no bearing on current legal standing.

Any ambiguities arising from the overlap between saved prior rights and new Accords provisions shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra. In instances where a saved right directly contradicts a new prohibition, the new prohibition shall prevail, as the Accords prioritize the collective stability of the Midlands over individual historical privileges. See § 1.5 for the overarching priority of the Accords over external and internal mandates.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
For the purposes of the Autumnwood Accords, a "Seal" is defined as a legally recognized mark of authorization, either physical or metaphysical, applied by a certified officer of the Accords Desk or an authorized representative of the Aegis Magi. Only such marks may be used to certify the legality of restricted research, the issuance of Provisional Guild Passes, or the verification of official cartography. Any mark, sigil, or emblem that does not originate from a recognized authority is deemed a "False Seal" and is subject to immediate seizure and the prosecution of the bearer.

It is expressly clarified that common culinary markings, symbols of personal preference, or incidental markings of no official capacity do not constitute seals. Specifically, the presence of garlic bread markings or any related culinary iconography upon a map, scroll, or artifact shall not be interpreted as a seal of authenticity or a mark of Guild approval. The Accords Desk will not recognize such marks as evidence of legal status, nor shall their presence be used as a basis for any regulatory exemption.

Furthermore, the physical or mental state of a person does not determine their capacity to hold a seal. A concussed, unconscious, or otherwise incapacitated unnamed pilot, regardless of their previous rank or standing, is not a certifying officer and cannot provide valid authorization for the movement of goods, the activation of rifts, or the crossing of restricted zones. Any "authorization" purportedly granted by a person in such a state is null and void. The Accords Desk requires a conscious, voluntary act of certification by a recognized official to validate any official action.

Practitioners are cautioned against the use of "pseudo-seals"—magical constructs that mimic the appearance of Guild authority without the underlying legal weight. The use of a pseudo-seal to bypass the Innovator's permission requirements or to circumvent Conservator restrictions shall be treated as a high-level violation of the Accords. See § 1.6 for the full list of certified authorities.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The inclusion of reserved catchlines within this Codex is a fundamental structural necessity of the Autumnwood Accords. A reserved catchline signifies a designated location within the legal framework that is currently vacant of specific statutes but remains a permanent fixture of the book’s architecture. These sections are not "empty" in the sense of being ignored; rather, they are placeholders for future legislative expansion, amendments, or the insertion of specific emergency decrees as dictated by the Archmage Sovereign.

By maintaining these reserved spaces, the Accords Desk ensures that the legal framework can be updated and expanded without necessitating a complete re-indexing of the Codex. When a new law is drafted to address a novel magical phenomenon, a new rift, or a shift in the political landscape between the Conservators and the Innovators, it may be inserted into a corresponding reserved section. This allows for a modular approach to governance, where the foundational structure remains constant while the specific applications of the law can evolve.

The existence of a reserved catchline does not imply that the law is "under construction" in a way that delays its current validity. A blank section remains a place in the book, and its presence does not grant any temporary immunity from the laws already codified in preceding sections. Practitioners should not assume that a lack of specific text in a reserved section constitutes a "gray area" or a lack of regulation; rather, it signifies that the Accords Desk has not yet deemed a specific sub-topic worthy of a permanent, standalone statute.

Any request to occupy a reserved catchline with a specific decree must be submitted to the Accords Desk for review. Such a decree must be vetted by both the Conservator and Innovator factions to ensure it does not violate the core tenets of the Accords. Once approved, the new statute will be permanently bound to the Codex under its respective reserved heading, becoming a functional part of the law. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority regarding these additions.

body.heading: Text
body.text:
PAGE § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth — The cultivation or propagation of Titans without a valid Research Permit is strictly prohibited under all circumstances. Such activity constitutes gross negligence at minimum, but may rise to the level of grand larceny or endangerment depending on consequences. Any individual caught engaging in unauthorized breeding shall be immediately detained and prosecuted according to full weight of law. Confiscation of all related materials and equipment is mandatory pending investigation. Repeat offenders face automatic expulsion from Guild membership and permanent revocation of any licenses held therein. This rule exists solely to protect the public welfare from unpredictable biological hazards and prevent abuse of Titan genetics for illicit purposes. Violators must understand that nothing short of a full trial can override this ban, regardless of personal claims or prior standing within the community. See § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts for context on prohibited practices.

PAGE § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters — Agreements between Casters and non-magical persons regarding magical services are subject to special scrutiny under this Code. Such contracts must specify in unmistakable terms the scope of work, expected outcomes, compensation details, liability limitations, and dispute resolution mechanisms. Ambiguous or overly broad clauses may be deemed unenforceable at the discretion of the Court. Further, any provision requiring a Caster to violate Guild laws or ethical standards is automatically void as against public policy. Parties entering into such arrangements do so fully aware of all risks involved, including potential loss of magical abilities or permanent injury. The burden lies squarely on the non-Casting party to verify competence and legality before committing resources. Breach of contract will be addressed through normal judicial channels unless fraud or gross misconduct is proven. This framework aims to balance protection for both sides while maintaining integrity of the Caster profession overall. See § 500.1 Field Casting for Value regarding commercial implications.

PAGE § 800.3 Emergency Situations — In cases posing imminent threat to life or property, any individual may take necessary action without prior authorization from Guild officials. Reasonable force is permitted when clearly required under the circumstances. Post-hoc review shall determine whether conduct was justified and within acceptable parameters. Those acting in good faith during emergencies are presumed innocent until proven otherwise by preponderance of evidence. Documentation of events through logs, witnesses, or recordings strongly recommended to support claims of necessity. No person shall be held criminally liable for lawful acts performed under duress unless gross recklessness is demonstrated beyond doubt. This clause recognizes reality that not all threats can wait for bureaucratic approval before demanding immediate response. Proper channels remain available afterwards to assess consequences and assign accountability appropriately. See § 700.2 Use of Force Standards for general guidelines on proportional measures.

PAGE § 950.4 Waiver Procedures — Any waiver of rights under this Code must be executed in duplicate original form with full disclosure of all relevant terms. Signatures must be witnessed by two disinterested adults who verify identity and capacity to contract freely. Electronic signatures are acceptable if accompanied by unique authentication codes transmitted via encrypted channels only. Copies delivered directly to each party involved within forty-eight hours of execution. Failure to follow these strict protocols renders waivers invalid regardless of alleged understanding or consent expressed verbally. The law demands clarity above all else when stripping away protections afforded by statute. Parties signing such instruments do so knowingly and voluntarily, bearing full responsibility for their choices moving forward. Courts will not entertain arguments based on hidden clauses or misleading language drafted unilaterally. Transparency remains paramount to maintain fairness in all dealings governed herein. See § 150.2 Burden of Proof; § 375.9 Limitations on Damages for supplementary provisions.

PAGE § 250.6 Liability Insurance Requirements — All registered Casters must maintain adequate liability coverage specifically tailored to their unique risks and operational scope. Policies shall name the Mages' Guild as additional insured with primary status where applicable. Proof of current policies submitted annually during renewal process along with detailed loss history reports. Any gaps or deficiencies noticed immediately upon discovery trigger mandatory remediation within thirty days without exception. Failure to comply results in suspension of license privileges until rectification complete. Premium costs borne entirely by individual caster regardless of employer coverage elsewhere. This mandate exists solely to ensure financial recourse remains available should accidents occur despite best efforts at prevention. Protection for public interests outweighs any concerns about affordability or inconvenience faced by practitioners. See § 180.3 Standards of Care; § 425.7 Contributory Negligence for related principles regarding duty and responsibility.

PAGE § 675.9 Statute of Limitations — Actions arising under this Code must be commenced within three years from date of accrual unless otherwise specified herein or by special order. Accrual occurs when plaintiff knows or reasonably should know of injury sustained along with wrongful cause thereof. Minor victims enjoy extended limitation periods until reaching majority plus additional six months thereafter. Time pauses automatically during any pending appeal process regardless of outcome eventually reached later down the road. Claims barred upon expiration cannot be revived except under most extraordinary conditions proven beyond all shadow of a doubt. Defendants may assert these defenses at first opportunity once notice received of suit filed against them personally. Strict adherence to deadlines ensures timely resolution while preserving ability to pursue valid redress when merited fully supported by evidence presented honestly before competent tribunal empowered to hear such cases properly conducted according established rules governing practice therein. See § 120.5 Equitable Doctrines; § 340.8 Tolling Provisions for complementary limitations concepts applied consistently across all matters governed herein.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The provisions contained within this Codex shall be deemed to take effect immediately upon the final ratification of the Autumnwood Accords by the Archmage Sovereign. This legal instrument serves as the primary governing authority for all thaumaturgical practice within the Midlands and all territories under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. Any actions taken by mages, practitioners, or affiliated entities prior to the date of enactment shall be judged based on the prevailing laws of that time, unless such actions fall under the specific transitional provisions outlined in the Sovereign’s Decree of Continuity.

Prior Accords, treaties, and local ordinances that are not explicitly repealed by the text of this Codex shall remain in full force and effect. The existence of the Autumnwood Accords does not constitute a wholesale dissolution of historical agreements, provided those agreements do not directly conflict with the fundamental mandates of the Accords. Where a conflict arises between a prior agreement and a current provision of this Codex, the Accords shall prevail as the superior authority. Practitioners seeking to maintain the validity of historical pacts must ensure such pacts are registered with the Autumnwood Accords Desk for reconciliation.

Notwithstanding the preservation of prior agreements, the legal status of repealed sections is strictly defined. The invocation of a repealed section as a justification for current conduct is strictly prohibited. Pursuant to the principles of legal finality, the repeal of a statutory provision renders it null and void for all future purposes. See § 1401.2 for further clarification on the status of dead citations. No practitioner may argue that a repealed scheme, despite its historical significance or its former utility, holds any residual weight or provides a permit for contemporary action.

Furthermore, the repeal of a scheme does not grant the right to "revive" the law through mere citation or persistent practice. A section that has been struck from the Codex is legally deceased; it cannot be resurrected by the actions of the Innovators, the dictates of the Conservators, or the demands of external powers such as the Regal Empire. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any "ghost laws" or "shadow precedents" derived from defunct titles. This ensures that the legal landscape remains navigable and that the sovereign authority of Archmage Veyra remains absolute and unambiguous. For matters regarding the preservation of specific historical rights, see § 1.8.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
The authority of the Autumnwood Accords is manifested through the official application of Seals and Stamps. A Seal is a legally recognized mark of authentication, issued by the Accords Desk or a designated high-ranking official, signifying that a document, research permit, or magical artifact has been vetted and approved for use. Such seals carry the weight of the Sovereign’s mediation and the collective oversight of the Conservators and the Innovators. A stamp, being a secondary mark of administrative processing, may be used to indicate the status of a filing or the completion of a bureaucratic requirement, but it does not carry the same weight of sovereign sanction as a Seal.

The Guild maintains a strict distinction between legitimate marks of authority and mundane, artistic, or coincidental markings. For the purposes of this Codex, a Seal must be a deliberate act of magical or administrative certification. It is expressly stated that a non-official mark, even one that mimics the aesthetic of a Guild Seal, shall not be recognized as a valid instrument of authority. This distinction is critical in the prevention of forgery and the unauthorized exercise of magical rights. See § 1.6 for definitions regarding authorized agents.

To ensure clarity in the face of common misconceptions or absurdities, the Accords Desk hereby establishes specific exclusions. It is expressly decreed that garlic bread depicted upon a map—regardless of its size, placement, or perceived importance—does not constitute a Seal. The presence of culinary imagery or any other non-magical, non-administrative notation on a map does not grant the bearer of said map any special privileges, licenses, or exemptions from the laws of the Midlands. Furthermore, the presence of a map does not serve as a raid license; see § 1.6.

Equally, the Accords Desk clarifies the status of personnel. A concussed unnamed pilot, or any individual suffering from physical or mental impairment who lacks the requisite certification and clarity of mind, is not a certifying officer. The authority to issue Seals or Stamps requires a clear mandate from the Sovereign or the designated faction leaders. Any "certification" obtained from an individual who is not a recognized official of the Accords, or who is currently incapacitated, shall be considered null and void. Such actions may be grounds for a Paradox Trial. No individual may claim that a mark of authority was "validly" issued by a source that the Accords do not recognize as a legitimate seat of power.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The Accords Desk maintains the right to reserve specific sections within this Codex for future expansion, amendment, or the inclusion of specialized regulations. A reserved catchline serves as a placeholder within the legal architecture of the Autumnwood Accords, ensuring that the structure of the law remains intact even when specific provisions are yet to be drafted. The existence of a reserved catchline signifies that the law is a living document, capable of evolving to meet new thaumaturgical challenges, political shifts, or the emergence of new magical phenomena.

A reserved section is not a "blank" space in the sense of being legally empty; rather, it is a designated area of potentiality. While a reserved catchline does not currently carry a specific mandate, the fact that it exists in the Codex means that the Guild acknowledges the necessity of future regulation regarding that topic. When a new law is eventually drafted to fill a reserved section, it shall be integrated into the Codex while maintaining the sequential order of the existing titles. This prevents the need for retroactive renumbering and ensures that the hierarchy of the Accords remains stable.

Practitioners should be aware that the presence of a reserved catchline does not imply that the conduct associated with that topic is currently unregulated. In the absence of a specific provision within a reserved section, the general principles of the Accords—specifically those regarding the balance between Conservator stability and Innovator research—shall apply. However, the Accords Desk reserves the right to enact emergency measures or temporary directives that may address matters currently held in reserved sections until a permanent statute is codified.

The Accords Desk shall not be held liable for the perceived ambiguity of a reserved section. It is the duty of the mages to seek clarification from the Archmage Sovereign or the relevant faction leaders (Archmage Theron for stability-based queries, or Janna Brightspark for research-based inquiries) should they require guidance on matters not yet fully detailed in the Codex. The preservation of these placeholders is a fundamental requirement of the Accords, ensuring that the legal body of the Autumnwood Accords remains comprehensive and prepared for the complexities of the arcane future. See § 1.3 for instructions on the interpretation of these provisions.

body.heading: § 1.8 Effective Date; Savings — This Codex shall take effect as of the date here
body.text: Furthermore, it is hereby declared that all seals, stamps, and official marks used pursuant to repealed accords remain valid for a period of ninety days following this effective date thereafter. Within such timeframe, holders thereof may utilize them in good faith without penalty. After expiration, any subsequent use shall constitute forgery under § 100.9, subject to the full weight of the law. This provision ensures an orderly transition from old systems to new ones while preventing abuse of lingering authority. The Conservators and Innovators alike agree to cooperate fully during this interim period to facilitate a smooth shift away from deprecated instruments. Failure to comply shall result in immediate sanctions under § 301, including loss of licensure privileges. Ultimately, the spirit of this Clause seeks to balance finality with fairness as the Guild evolves toward greater efficiency and integrity. For further details on seal validity periods, refer to § 100.8 (Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal). Under § 100.9, unauthorized reproduction or misuse of official marks carries serious penalties. This saving grace reflects the Accords' commitment to responsible governance while adapting to changing circumstances over time.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings — Continued
body.text:
§ 1.8 Effective Date and Savings Provisions — This Codex shall come into full force and effect upon the signing of this volume by the High Archmage Sovereign, unless otherwise provided herein. Any provisions in prior Accords that conflict with these rules are hereby superseded to the extent necessary for consistent operation. Nothing in this Title shall be construed to invalidate any agreements or obligations entered into in good faith before the Effective Date; such arrangements continue under their original terms unless expressly modified by subsequent action of the Accords Desk. However, no dormant clause may be resurrected solely through reference to obsolete numbering schemes. Dead citations carry no legal weight absent affirmative adoption by resolution. This principle safeguards against accidental revival of defunct statutes and maintains clarity in determining applicable obligations. The intent is to preserve historical continuity while preventing confusion from archaic remnants lingering in the record system. Any ambiguity arising from transitional provisions shall be resolved favorably toward maintaining public order and safety, unless contrary instructions appear elsewhere in this Title. This approach balances respect for precedent with practical necessity for modern governance."

body.heading: § 1.9 Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal — The Great Seal of the Autumnwood A
body.text:
§ 1.10 Reserved Catchlines — The title reserves certain subject matters for future legislative action by the Accords Desk. These include emerging magical technologies, cross-dimensional treaties, and classified research protocols deemed too volatile for public deliberation. Such topics shall remain under exclusive jurisdiction until explicitly declassified or addressed by special resolution. This safeguard protects national security interests while preserving democratic oversight within reasonable bounds.

The relationship between these foundational clauses establishes the framework upon which all subsequent regulations rest. By mandating a single authentic seal and reserving contentious areas for later review, the Accords balance administrative efficiency with necessary caution in handling sensitive matters. These principles guide the Desk's interpretation of ambiguous provisions and inform its exercise of delegated authority throughout the implementation phase of this comprehensive legal code.

Effective Date; Savings — This Codex shall take full effect as of January 1st, 2024, unless otherwise specified within individual sections. All prior statutes, regulations, and agreements inconsistent with these provisions are hereby repealed to the extent of such inconsistency. However, nothing herein shall be construed to invalidate any lawful contracts or obligations entered into before this date, provided they do not violate public policy embodied in subsequent articles. Transitional rules shall apply as necessary to effectuate a smooth implementation without disrupting ongoing governmental operations or infringing upon vested rights.

Savings Clause — Nothing contained in this title shall impair the validity of any judgment, decree, order, or other legal process issued by courts of competent jurisdiction prior to its enactment. Such pre-existing instruments retain their full force and effect unless expressly modified or vacated by subsequent action. This provision respects the doctrine of reliance interests while allowing the legislature flexibility to address new issues arising from technological advances or changing societal conditions. The interplay between these clauses reflects a pragmatic approach to statutory construction, acknowledging both the need for stability and adaptation in an ever-evolving legal landscape.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
All official instruments, mandates, and permissions issued under the authority of the Autumnwood Accords shall bear a certified seal of the Guild. A seal is defined as a distinct, magically-reactive impression or sigil that validates the authenticity of a document, the intent of the signatory, and the legal standing of the contents therein. For the purposes of this Codex, a seal must be verifiable by the Aegis Magi through standard resonance testing. Any document bearing a mark that lacks the requisite arcane signature, or any mark that has been mimicked through mundane forgery or low-level illusion, shall be deemed null and void. The absence of a proper seal shall render any instruction, regardless of the status of the individual providing it, non-binding upon the members of the Guild.

To ensure clarity in administrative proceedings and to prevent the misappropriation of authority, the Guild hereby establishes a list of specific non-validating markings. Specifically, the presence of food items, culinary notations, or mundane geographic markings—including, but not limited to, garlic bread on a map—shall not constitute a seal. Furthermore, the physical presence of an individual, regardless of their perceived expertise or current state of consciousness, does not constitute a certification of legal authority. A concussed unnamed pilot, or any individual lacking a verified identity and a designated rank within the Accords, is not a certifying officer. No verbal command or physical gesture from an uncertified individual may be interpreted as a valid issuance of a Guild mandate.

Furthermore, the Guild shall not recognize any "seal" derived from unauthorized sources. Marks associated with the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or the Silver Flame are strictly prohibited from being recognized as valid within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. Any mage found to be acting upon a seal from an opposing faction shall be subject to immediate review by the Conservators. The validity of a seal is inextricably linked to the source of its issuance; therefore, any seal that cannot be traced back to a sanctioned office of the Guild, or an authorized representative of the Innovators or Conservators, is to be treated as a decorative element without legal weight. Mages are cautioned that relying upon an unverified mark for the execution of high-level thaumaturgy may result in the immediate revocation of their provisional status. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
This section serves as a formal reservation of space within the Autumnwood Accords Codex. The inclusion of reserved catchlines is a structural necessity of the Accords, ensuring that the legal framework remains expandable and adaptable to the evolving nature of thaumaturgy. A reserved catchline constitutes a designated placeholder for future legislation, amendments, or specific regulations that have been identified as necessary but have not yet been ratified by the Archmage Sovereign or the presiding council of the Conservators and Innovators. The existence of a reserved section does not imply a current lack of law, but rather provides a designated locus for the insertion of new mandates without necessitating a total restructuring of the Codex's numerical sequence.

A blank or reserved section within this book is still a place in the book. It represents a commitment by the Guild to maintain an organized and systematic approach to governance. When a new law is ratified, it shall be inserted into the nearest available reserved section that corresponds to its subject matter. This prevents the "crowding" of existing statutes and ensures that the legal progression of the Guild remains coherent. Any mage seeking to reference a section that appears currently blank should be aware that the section is legally active in its capacity as a placeholder; however, no rights, permissions, or prohibitions are currently enforceable until such time as the section is populated with ratified prose.

The preservation of these placeholders is essential for the administrative integrity of the Autumnwood Accords. It allows the Guild to anticipate the growth of the "Unsanctioned Arts" regulations and the potential expansion of the "Restricted Research" permits. By maintaining these reserved spaces, the Guild ensures that the legal architecture of the Midlands remains robust enough to house the complexities of future magical breakthroughs. Any attempt to interpret a reserved catchline as containing "implied" law is strictly prohibited. If a section is reserved, it is silent. The silence of a reserved section is the silence of the law itself, until the Archmage Sovereign deigns to speak through the formal recording of new text. See § 1.7.

body.heading: § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild
body.text:
It shall be held that the authority to act on behalf of the Mages' Guild, whether in treaty negotiations, diplomatic missions, or litigations before external bodies, resides solely within the Archmage Sovereign and those expressly delegated by her through written mandate carried under seal. No other officer, member, or agent of the Guild shall purport to bind its interests without such authorization. This provision serves to prevent confusion among third parties regarding the true extent of any purported representation and to protect the Guild from unauthorized commitments that might compromise its standing or security.

The Archmage Sovereign may delegate limited powers to specific individuals on a case-by-case basis, specifying clearly the scope and duration of such authority in each instance. Any delegation shall be evidenced by an official letter patent bearing the Great Seal and signed by both the Sovereign and the recipient. Copies of all delegations shall be maintained in the Guild's permanent records for future reference and verification as needed.

In matters where immediate action is required but no explicit delegation exists, any Conservator or Innovator may take necessary steps to preserve the status quo pending further instructions from the Archmage. Such actions shall not exceed what a prudent person would do under similar circumstances to protect the Guild's interests. The individual taking such measures shall be accountable for their conduct and liable for any damages resulting from gross negligence or abuse of discretion, absent evidence that they acted solely in good faith belief of possessing implied authority.

It is further provided that no action taken by an unauthorized representative shall bind the Guild unless ratified expressly within thirty days of becoming aware thereof. Failure to ratify constitutes a repudiation of all such purported actions with full prejudice to any claim arising therefrom. This rule ensures that the Guild remains insulated from reckless or malicious conduct by self-styled champions while allowing flexibility for genuine emergencies where swift response is imperative.

Finally, nothing herein shall be construed as limiting the inherent authority of the Archmage Sovereign to represent the Guild in all matters pertaining to its core functions and objectives. The provisions above merely clarify existing principles rather than creating new rights or obligations. They stand as a reaffirmation of the fundamental truth that ultimate power resides with the elected leader, who alone bears responsibility for guiding the Guild through the treacherous waters of magical politics and beyond."

"see § 100.3 Quorum of the Desk; under § 200.1 Licensure Required; compare § 300.2 Necromancy; cf. § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs"

body.heading: § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild — Continued
body.text:
The authority to bind or release the Mages' Guild in legal acts is vested solely in the Autumnwood Accords Desk, as defined herein and by prior charter. No individual mage, faction leader, or external entity shall purport to act on behalf of the Guild unless expressly delegated through formal appointment recorded with the Desk. This provision exists to prevent unauthorized commitments that could compromise the collective interests of all practitioners.

The Archmage Sovereign retains ultimate oversight but may not personally execute routine administrative functions without delegation. Such powers must be assigned via written instrument filed in the official records, specifying duration and scope clearly. Any purported authority lacking proper documentation shall be deemed invalid ab initio. This safeguard protects against both internal usurpation and external exploitation of Guild assets or influence.

In emergency circumstances where immediate action is required to prevent irreparable harm, designated Aegis Magi may act on behalf of the Desk pursuant to standing protocols. Their actions remain subject to subsequent ratification unless contravened by law or overriding public interest. Failure to seek ratification where feasible may result in disciplinary measures against the acting officer upon resolution of the crisis.

The Guild expressly reserves all rights under applicable laws and precedents regarding unauthorized agency, apparent authority, and ratification doctrines. Any claims relying on implied consent, customary practice, or supposed acquiescence shall fail absent clear evidence to the contrary. The burden rests strictly on those alleging representation by the Guild to prove such fact affirmatively.

This section operates in conjunction with § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks and shall be construed consistently therewith. Nothing herein precludes valid ratification of acts originally performed without authority if later approved expressly or impliedly through conduct clearly evidencing acceptance. However, mere acquiescence or failure to object promptly shall not constitute sufficient ratification absent special circumstances justified by equity.

The provisions of this section are mandatory and non-waivable, except as explicitly provided by the Desk with full notice and opportunity for objection. Any attempt to circumvent these requirements through private agreements or side deals shall be void and unenforceable against the Guild at large. The integrity of official channels must not be undermined by extralegal arrangements.

Under § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy, representatives from allied magical institutions may participate in specific capacities but derive no inherent authority from such presence alone. Their statements carry weight only as evidence of opinion or intent, never binding the Guild absent explicit authorization. Careful distinction must be maintained between diplomatic engagement and actual representation.

§ 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild — Delegated Authority; Unauthorized Acts; Emergency Powers; Ratification Standards; Mandatory Provisions; Non-Waivability Requirements; Extralegal Arrangements Void; Diplomatic Distinctions. see § 1.5 Relation to Other Law, § 7.3 Agency Principles, § 9.8 Official Capacity Limits.

body.heading: § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild — Continued — Continued
body.text:
The authority to represent the Mages' Guild in legal and diplomatic matters is vested exclusively in the Archmage Sovereign or her duly appointed proxies, as defined by current standing orders of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Any claim to speak on behalf of the organization without explicit delegation shall be deemed null and void ab initio. This provision exists to prevent fragmentation of power and ensure unified representation in negotiations with foreign powers and internal disputes among member factions.

The Archmage Sovereign retains sole discretion to delegate speaking authority to senior Aegis Magi or faction leaders during specific crises, provided such delegations are documented in the official Guild records and publicly announced within forty-eight hours. Unauthorized representations by lesser mages, even those holding high rank or influence within individual schools of magic, shall be treated as personal acts with no binding effect on the Guild's position. Violation of this rule may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure under § 200.4.

In matters involving treaty obligations or cross-hall commerce, the Sovereign must consult both Conservator and Innovator representatives prior to committing the Guild to any agreement. This safeguard ensures that no single faction can bind the entire organization against its will. Failure to obtain such consultation renders any purported contract voidable at the option of affected parties, regardless of apparent authority displayed by signing agents. The Desk shall maintain a registry of all authorized proxies for reference in future proceedings.

The provisions herein complement § 100.6 regarding delegation to clerks and shall be read in conjunction with foundational principles concerning agency found in §§ 1.4–1.5. Disputes arising from ambiguous authorization shall be resolved by the Desk pursuant to standard evidentiary rules, with burden of proof resting on those asserting actual authority. The Guild's seal remains affixed to all official documents as evidence of authenticity and binding effect under § 100.1.

See also §§ 1.6 (Definitions), 100.3 (Quorum Requirements), 200.5 (Guest Casting Privileges). This section shall remain subject to revision by the full Board upon recommendation from either major faction, subject to ratification by a two-thirds majority vote. The Archmage Sovereign serves as final arbiter of all interpretive questions relating to delegated authority absent explicit contrary instruction in subsequent codifications.

"Authority is not inherited; it must be earned and maintained through unwavering adherence to the Accords." — Archmage Veyra, Oath of Office 1372

body.heading: Text
body.text:
PAGE Scope of Delegation — Section 100.2(b) — In limited circumstances, the Archmage Sovereign may delegate specific certifying powers to designated Conservators or Innovators through formal appointment instruments recorded in the Guild's Official Register. Such delegates shall exercise authority solely within the parameters set forth in their commission and remain subject to audit by the Accords Desk at any time. Failure to adhere strictly to delegated limits renders acts performed void ab initio and may result in disciplinary action against the delegate, regardless of good faith intent.

PAGE Limitations on Authority — Section 100.2(c) — No single individual, whether Archmage or delegate, shall possess authority to issue multiple seals simultaneously for different matters without explicit written consent from all affected parties. This provision prevents fraud and ensures proper oversight in high-stakes transactions involving magical services. Parties seeking expedited certification should consult the Accords Desk regarding available mechanisms rather than attempting unilateral action that may compromise legal validity.

PAGE Consequences of Violation — Section 100.2(d) — Any person knowingly violating provisions of this section shall be subject to immediate suspension or revocation of all Guild privileges, pending full investigation and hearing before the Accords Desk. Reinstatement requires demonstration of remedial action and approval by a majority vote of both Conservators and Innovators present at said hearing. Persistent offenders may face permanent expulsion from the Guild with associated loss of legal standing within its jurisdictional bounds.

PAGE Reserved Catchlines — Section 100.2(e) — The Archmage Sovereign retains inherent authority to establish new categories of certification as circumstances warrant, provided notice and opportunity for comment are afforded all interested parties through regular publication in the Official Gazette. Such additions shall not supersede existing provisions unless explicitly stated otherwise by subsequent amendment duly enacted under proper procedures. All members remain bound to comply fully with current requirements until officially modified or repealed.

see § 100.3 Quorum of the Desk; see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse"
