Unauthorized creation or deployment of such constructs violates § 200.2 regarding unauthorized field use and may result in severe sanctions including sealing of magical capabilities under § 1.9. All constructs must bear unique identification markings registered with the Accords Desk to facilitate tracking and accountability. Regular inspections by Guild auditors shall be conducted annually to ensure compliance with established safety standards and operational limitations set forth in this section. Any malfunction or mishap attributable to improper construction or misuse of a Quill-Holding Construct shall be deemed negligence on the part of its creator and may lead to disciplinary action up to and including permanent disbarment from practice under § 200.3.

Guest casters operating outside registered parameters are subject to heightened scrutiny by local law enforcement agencies tasked with monitoring unlicensed magical activity in their jurisdictions. Cooperation between Guild officials and municipal authorities regarding guest caster investigations is mandatory upon request, provided such cooperation does not compromise ongoing legal proceedings or reveal confidential information protected under § 100.4. Refusal to cooperate may result in escalation of charges and invocation of emergency powers granted herein under § 100.8. Furthermore, any allegations of professional misconduct against guest casters must be adjudicated according to procedures outlined for licensed practitioners unless otherwise specified by special ruling from the Accords Desk itself. Appeals from adverse decisions rendered by guest caster review panels may only be pursued through formal channels established in Part III governing appellate review processes applicable to all regulated magic users within Guild jurisdiction. Compliance with these provisions ensures orderly integration of non-traditional magical practitioners into existing regulatory frameworks while maintaining public safety and professional standards paramount to the mission of the Autumnwood Accords as a whole.

see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 1.9 Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal; under § 300.1 Schedules of Arts regarding prohibited magical practices; pursuant to § 400.1 Research Permits which parallels guest caster authorization requirements.

body.heading: Guest Casting and Construct Liability — Continued
body.text:
A "guest caster," as defined in § 200.5, refers to an individual who provides magical services outside the scope of their primary licensure or employment contract. Such arrangements are permissible only under strict conditions intended to protect both the client and the public from potential harm arising from unregulated magical practice. Failure to adhere to these stipulations may result in disciplinary action against the guest caster by the Autumnwood Accords Desk.

Specifically, any guest casting must be conducted with full disclosure of risks, limitations, and costs prior to commencing work. The client shall sign an acknowledgment form verifying receipt of this information. Additionally, a detailed written agreement outlining the scope of services rendered must be executed by both parties before any spellwork begins. This contract serves as binding evidence should disputes arise regarding quality or payment later on.

Constructs that function independently under their own power may also qualify for guest casting status if they possess sufficient intelligence and autonomy to negotiate terms directly with clients. Such entities must still comply with all applicable safety regulations and liability limitations set forth herein, regardless of their artificial nature. Failure to do so will be treated as a serious violation subject to appropriate sanctions.

In all cases involving guest casting or construct-based services, the primary caster remains ultimately responsible for overseeing operations and ensuring compliance with guild standards. They may not delegate this responsibility entirely without violating § 200.3's prohibition against unauthorized subcontracting. Any attempt to circumvent these rules will result in immediate revocation of professional credentials and possible prosecution under existing fraud statutes.

By engaging a guest caster or construct service provider, clients assume certain obligations alongside their rights. They warrant full cooperation during the engagement period and prompt settlement of outstanding balances upon completion. Furthermore, they agree not to interfere with legitimate investigations into any alleged misconduct connected to said arrangement unless formally subpoenaed by competent authorities having jurisdiction over the matter at hand.

These provisions are designed to maintain orderly conditions within the magical professions while accommodating necessary flexibility for mutually beneficial collaborations between licensed practitioners and qualified outsiders alike. Strict adherence ensures continued protection of both parties' interests under this comprehensive regulatory framework.

sections.title: Constructs That Hold a Quill
sections.brief: Service of process on a construct. Swords do not receive mail.

body.heading: Constructs That Hold a Quill
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords and the jurisdictional boundaries established by the Archmage Sovereign, this section governs the legal status of non-sentient and semi-sentient entities capable of administrative interaction. While the Guild recognizes the prevalence of construct-based automation within the modern arcane infrastructure, the legal personhood of a construct remains a matter of strict technicality. A construct shall not be deemed a "Person Bound" under the protections and obligations of § 1.4. However, for the purposes of the Accords Desk and the orderly administration of the Midlands, a construct may be granted "Administrative Agency" if it is specifically engineered to hold a quill, manage ledgers, or facilitate the transmission of written records.

Any construct that holds a quill and is tasked with the preservation of Guild records, the filing of petitions, or the recording of magical yields shall be subject to the formal service of process. This status is not granted by inherent nature but by the specific magical and mechanical intent of its creation. If a construct is utilized by a Master of the Guild or an authorized Innovator to act as a repository for legal notices, it shall be considered a valid conduit for the delivery of summons, subpoenas, and official decrees. The Clerk of the Accords Desk shall ensure that any such construct is equipped with a designated receptacle or a designated "holding area" for physical parchment, ensuring that the integrity of the delivery is maintained without requiring the construct to possess independent volition or comprehension of the contents therein.

Conversely, the Guild explicitly denies the status of "Process-Recipient" to objects of martial utility. It is hereby decreed that swords do not receive mail. No blade, regardless of its enchantments, its history of service, or its proximity to a quill-holding construct, shall be considered a valid destination for legal correspondence. Any attempt by a courier, a mage, or an automated delivery system to affix a summons to a weapon shall be deemed a nullity. Furthermore, any construct designed solely for combat, defense, or physical labor—lacking the specific apparatus for the holding of a quill or the management of records—is excluded from these provisions. Such entities are to be treated as inanimate property and are incapable of being served with notice, regardless of the demands of the presiding faction.

In instances where a construct is used by a third party—such as the Goodstyle Artisans or independent contractors—to hold a quill for the purpose of drafting contracts, the legal responsibility for the accuracy of the record remains with the human or sentient agent who commissioned the work. The construct is merely the instrument of the quill; it is not the author of the intent. Should a construct be damaged or destroyed during the service of process, the initiating party shall be held liable for the repair or replacement of the apparatus, provided the damage was not caused by a violation of the Iron Mandate or other external martial laws. For further clarification on the limitations of agency, see § 1.4.

body.heading: § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill — Service of Process on Non-Living Entities
body.text:
Under § 1.4, all persons are bound by the Accords; however, this mandate extends only so far as practical enforcement permits. Where living beings cannot be found or served due to physical absence or magical concealment, alternative methods of notice may be employed at the discretion of the Desk. One such method is service upon a construct designated by the accused as an agent for receiving legal communication.

A "construct" within the meaning of this Section includes any artificial entity capable of holding a written document, whether mechanical (such as a clockwork automaton), magical (including golems and homunculi), or otherwise engineered to serve as a proxy. The construct must be under the exclusive control of the accused at the time of designation, with no third-party access that would compromise confidentiality. Proof of such control may be established by sworn affidavit or testimony from witnesses familiar with the arrangement.

Service upon a properly designated construct is deemed equivalent to personal delivery and binds the recipient as effectively as any other form of notice. The Desk shall maintain a registry of known constructs used for this purpose, updated quarterly through submissions from practicing mages. Failure to register a construct may render service thereon voidable at the option of the served party, who must then demonstrate diligent effort to locate alternative channels.

This provision does not create a presumption that all constructs are suitable for legal purposes. Each case shall be evaluated on its merits, considering factors such as reliability, accessibility, and potential for tampering or destruction. The Desk retains authority to reject any proposed construct if it determines the arrangement poses an undue risk to the integrity of proceedings.

§ 200.6 operates in conjunction with § 100.4 regarding the official record of all legal actions taken by the Guild. Documents served upon a construct must be promptly filed and indexed for future reference, ensuring transparency and accountability in the enforcement process. Construct owners are reminded that misuse of this mechanism may constitute obstruction of justice under applicable provisions.

In sum, § 200.6 provides a practical solution to challenges inherent in serving process on elusive or hidden parties. By leveraging technology and magic where traditional means fail, the Accords maintain their efficacy without compromising fairness. This flexibility exemplifies the Guild's commitment to adapting its rules to meet evolving realities while upholding core principles of due process.

body.heading: Service of Process on Non-Living Entities
body.text:
§ 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill — Service of Process on Non-Living Entities

This section addresses the peculiar legal challenges posed by non-living entities that may be parties to contracts or subject to litigation. The core issue is determining proper notice and consent when one side lacks cognitive capacity for understanding or agreement. While natural persons must knowingly assent to binding obligations, constructs operate under different rules derived from their nature as property and tools rather than moral agents.

The fundamental principle governing such cases is that a construct cannot be held personally liable for breach of contract absent express provision to the contrary in its creation documents. As mere instruments designed by humans to serve purposes set forth therein, an animated blade or stone golem lacks independent volition or intent necessary to form a contractual relationship. Any apparent agreement entered into through its actions binds solely its creator or owner unless explicitly stated otherwise within governing specifications. Thus, when a magically imbued sword fails to cleave as promised during combat training, the remedy lies against its manufacturer for defective workmanship rather than any hypothetical negligence of the weapon itself.

Nevertheless, constructs may occasionally acquire limited legal personality through special statutory designation or judicial decree in extraordinary circumstances where traditional remedies prove inadequate. For instance, if an autonomous defense turret repeatedly malfunctions causing property damage despite adequate maintenance by its proprietor, a court might grant standing to sue directly against the machine's control software as a distinct entity. This exceptional approach acknowledges that sophisticated artificial systems can exhibit behaviors indistinguishable from human agency even while remaining fundamentally derivative in origin and authority. The threshold for such recognition remains exceedingly high, reserved only for cases where normal recourse fails utterly to address harm inflicted by a quasi-independent actor possessing unusual capabilities beyond mere mechanical function.

In all other instances, constructs remain strictly chattel subject entirely to the will of their makers or owners. Any claim against them must ultimately rest upon the liability of natural persons responsible for their design and deployment. The law draws a bright line between tool failures attributable to manufacturing faults versus intentional misconduct by users—only the latter can ground personal responsibility regardless of any deceptive appearance of autonomy displayed during operation. This distinction preserves essential principles of fairness while accommodating novel realities created by advanced magical engineering.

see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting regarding ethical constraints on magi; under § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs concerning controlled experimentation environments; reference § 300.1 Schedules of Arts for classification standards applicable to artificial constructs; apply § 1.7 Construction rules when interpreting ambiguous provisions involving non-sentient parties.

body.heading: § 200.7 Delegation to Clerks and Agents — Limits on Entrusted Authority, § 200.7
body.text: No person shall delegate their authority under these Accords beyond the scope expressly granted by statute or rule, nor shall they permit another to act in their name without explicit written consent recorded at the Desk. Any unauthorized delegation renders the principal personally liable for all consequences of the agent's actions, as if performed directly by themselves. This provision aims to prevent abuse of power through proxy arrangements that circumvent oversight mechanisms designed to protect both public safety and the integrity of magical practice. The Desk shall maintain a registry of all authorized delegates and their powers, accessible to any interested party upon request and payment of applicable fees. Violations of this section constitute grounds for disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure. Further guidance on proper delegation protocols may be found in § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks, which outlines specific procedures for entrusting routine tasks to qualified assistants while retaining ultimate accountability. Parties are urged to exercise caution when authorizing representatives to act on their behalf, considering the far-reaching implications of such actions under this comprehensive regulatory framework.

body.heading: § 200.8 Temporary Mouths and Proxy Casting — Conditions and Restrictions, § 200.
body.text: Under extraordinary circumstances where a licensed caster is temporarily unavailable due to illness, injury, or other compelling reasons, they may authorize another individual to perform specific acts on their behalf through a formal "Temporary Mouth" arrangement. Such authorization must be filed with the Desk along with proof of the original caster's incapacity and detailed instructions regarding permitted actions. The acting proxy shall assume full responsibility for all outcomes resulting from their conduct under this authority, notwithstanding any claims of following directions given by the absent licensee. Temporary Mouth arrangements are strictly limited to emergency situations where immediate action is necessary to prevent harm or loss. They may not be used to circumvent normal licensing requirements or extend a caster's operational capacity beyond statutory limits. The Desk retains discretion to deny such requests if it determines that granting them would undermine public safety or violate the spirit of these Accords. This mechanism exists solely as a safeguard for unforeseen contingencies, not as a means to expand individual power improperly. All Temporary Mouth authorizations expire automatically upon resolution of the triggering event unless renewed in writing with updated justification and documentation.

body.heading: § 200.9 Guest Casters and Cross-Jurisdictional Practice — Oversight Requirements
body.text: Non-resident casters seeking to perform services within the jurisdiction governed by these Accords must obtain advance permission from the Autumnwood Desk prior to commencing any magical activities. This requirement applies regardless of whether compensation is exchanged or if the work falls outside standard licensure categories. Guest Casters shall operate under direct supervision of a locally licensed professional who assumes primary responsibility for ensuring compliance with all applicable laws and regulations. The supervising caster must verify the qualifications and insurance coverage of visiting practitioners before allowing them to engage in any magical operations. All guest casting arrangements require written agreements specifying scope, duration, liability allocation, and dispute resolution procedures. Failure to secure proper authorization subjects both parties to penalties up to and including permanent expulsion from professional practice within this region. The Desk maintains a database of approved Guest Casters and their credentials for inspection purposes. This provision balances the need for flexibility in accommodating external expertise with imperative safeguards against unregulated magical activity. Strict adherence to these guidelines preserves the integrity of the regulatory regime while facilitating necessary cooperation across regional boundaries when justified by compelling circumstances.

body.heading: § 201.1 Unauthorized Titan Growth — Prohibition and Penalties, § 201.1 Unauthori
body.text: No person shall intentionally induce or permit uncontrolled growth of personal size without express permission from the Desk, except as provided under specific research exemptions granted in writing. Any unauthorized augmentation exceeding normal anatomical proportions constitutes a serious violation of these Accords and may result in immediate suspension of licensure pending investigation. This prohibition exists to prevent abuse of transformative magic that could disrupt social order or endanger public safety. Exceptions may be made for medically necessary treatments approved by qualified practitioners, provided all procedures are documented and reported within seven days. The Desk reserves the right to revoke any previously granted permissions if subsequent misuse is discovered. Parties found guilty of violating this section shall face disciplinary action ranging from fines to permanent disqualification from practicing magic within these bounds. Additional guidelines regarding acceptable limits of physical modification can be found in § 300.1 Schedules of Arts under Transformative Disciplines. Strict enforcement of these standards ensures responsible use of powerful abilities while protecting citizens from potential harms arising from unchecked experimentation with bodily alteration techniques.

sections.title: Schedules of Arts
sections.brief: Schedule A ordinary, B restricted, C Quiet List. Do not reciting C in taverns.

body.heading: Schedules of Arts
body.text:
The classification of magical methodologies under the Autumnwood Accords is governed by the tripartite categorization of Schedules A, B, and C. These schedules serve as the definitive regulatory framework for all practitioners operating within the Midlands and under the jurisdiction of Archmage Veyra. Schedule A comprises the Ordinary Arts; these are established disciplines whose risks are well-understood, documented, and deemed safe for general practice by the Conservators without prior individual oversight. Practitioners may employ Schedule A magic for commerce, defense, and personal utility, provided they adhere to the standard safety limitations established in § 1.6.

Schedule B comprises Restricted Arts. These disciplines involve high-variance outputs, significant environmental impact, or inherent risks to the weaver’s mental stability. Use of Schedule B magic requires a specific license issued by the Aegis Magi and is subject to periodic review by the Innovators for research purposes. Any practitioner found utilizing Schedule B arts without a valid license shall be subject to immediate seizure of materials and referral to the Paradox Trial. The distinction between A and B is not merely a matter of potency, but of predictability; any art that demonstrates an unpredictable variance in mana-drain or spatial displacement is to be moved to Schedule B by the Conservator leadership.

Schedule C comprises the Quiet List. These are arts deemed so volatile, socially disruptive, or inherently dangerous to the fabric of the Accords that they are removed from public catalogues and general discourse. The primary mandate regarding Schedule C is the prohibition of its recitation in public houses, taverns, or common gathering places. Any mage who speaks the name of a Quiet List art or describes its mechanics in a tavern shall be deemed to be in breach of the Accords, regardless of whether the magic was actually performed. This provision is designed to prevent the spread of esoteric knowledge to the uninitiated and to maintain the stability of the Midlands. See § 300.3 for the specific procedures regarding the maintenance of this list.

body.heading: Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts
body.text:
The Accord strictly defines the Unsanctioned Arts as those practices that violate the fundamental sanctity of the cycle of life and the stability of the material plane. Necromancy, blood magic, and the unauthorized manipulation of lingering spirits are the primary pillars of the Unsanctioned Arts. Under the current mediation of Archmage Veyra, these arts are strictly forbidden for general use. No practitioner shall perform, teach, or facilitate the use of Necromancy or its derivatives without a numbered permit issued by the High Council of Conservators. Such permits are rarely granted and are typically reserved for the study of historical anomalies or the containment of existing undead threats.

Notwithstanding the general prohibition, the Innovator faction, under the guidance of Janna Brightspark, maintains the right to file for restricted research permits regarding the Unsanctioned Arts. These filings do not constitute an endorsement of the arts, nor do they grant the petitioner the right to practice these arts in a public or unregulated capacity. All such research must be conducted within designated laboratory settings, under the supervision of the Aegis Magi, and with a clear mandate for the preservation of the Accords. The Innovators may argue for the expansion of research boundaries, but the Conservators retain the final right of veto regarding the issuance of numbered permits.

Any practitioner found engaging in the Unsanctioned Arts without a numbered permit shall be considered a rogue agent of the state. Such actions constitute a primary violation of the Accords and shall result in an immediate referral to the Paradox Trial. While the Innovators may seek to push the boundaries of what is considered "acceptable" research, the legal status of Necromancy as an Unsanctioned Art remains absolute. No petition for a research permit shall be considered valid if it lacks a comprehensive risk-mitigation plan approved by both the Conservator and Innovator chairs. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Quiet List Procedure
body.text:
The maintenance of the Quiet List is a matter of high security and extreme discretion. Unlike the Schedules of Arts, which may be consulted by licensed mages, the Quiet List is not a public catalogue. It is a living record of magical phenomena and techniques that pose a systemic risk to the Midlands. The procedure for adding an art to the Quiet List is initiated by a petition from the Conservators, typically following a significant magical catastrophe or the discovery of a high-variance anomaly. Once a petition is filed, the Aegis Magi shall conduct a survey to determine if the art meets the criteria for "Quiet" status.

The listing of an art on the Quiet List does not involve a public announcement. Instead, it is updated within the sealed registers of the Accords Desk. Once an art is added, it is effectively scrubbed from all public teaching materials and commercial registries. The procedure ensures that the knowledge of the art remains confined to the highest echelons of the Guild. If an art is discovered to be in violation of the Accords but does not meet the threshold for the Quiet List, it shall be moved to Schedule B or prosecuted under the Unsanctioned Arts statutes.

The secrecy of the Quiet List is paramount. Any clerk or mage who gains unauthorized access to the Quiet List registers shall be subject to immediate expulsion and the permanent sealing of their magical faculties. Furthermore, the procedure requires that any art moved to the Quiet List be accompanied by a "Nullification Memorandum," which provides instructions on how to neutralize the art's influence in the event of a breach. The Quiet List is not a list of "forbidden" magic in the same sense as Necromancy; rather, it is a list of magic that the Guild has decided the world is not yet prepared to handle. See § 300.1.

body.heading: Reclassification
body.text:
The transition of a magical art from one Schedule to another is a formal administrative process governed by the Accords Desk. A common point of contention involves the movement of an art from Schedule B (Restricted) to Schedule A (Ordinary). It is a fundamental principle of these Accords that the act of reclassification is not a "party" to the law; that is, the mere fact that an art is being reconsidered for reclassification does not alter its current legal status. Until the final decree is signed by the Archmage Sovereign and ratified by the Council, any art currently listed in Schedule B remains strictly subject to the licensing requirements and restrictions of Schedule B.

The process for reclassification requires a dual-signature petition. The Innovators must provide a technical brief demonstrating that the art has been sufficiently stabilized or that its risks are now manageable through standard training. The Conservators must then provide a stability assessment, ensuring that the move to Schedule A will not cause a ripple effect in the Midlands' magical equilibrium. If the Innovators propose a move that the Conservators find reckless, the art remains in Schedule B indefinitely. No mage may begin practicing a reclassified art until the official registry has been updated and the Aegis Magi have issued new standard licenses.

Any attempt to bypass the reclassification process by claiming "de facto" status—arguing that because an art is commonly used, it should be treated as Schedule A—is a violation of the Accords. The law recognizes only the official designation. Furthermore, the reclassification of an art does not exempt the practitioner from any past violations committed while the art was still under the Schedule B designation. The legal status of an art is a matter of sovereign decree, not social practice. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
The creation and possession of research copies of arts listed on the Quiet List are governed by stringent protocols. While an art on the Quiet List is prohibited from public discourse and general practice, the Guild acknowledges that the Innovators may require access to such information for the purposes of containment, neutralization, or advanced study. Therefore, the creation of a "Research Copy" is permitted only under a direct mandate from Archmage Veyra. These copies are not considered "public" and remain subject to the secrecy requirements of the Quiet List.

Crucially, the possession of a research copy does not grant the holder the right to speak of the art. The distinction between the *possession* of the information and the *recitation* of the information is absolute. A mage who holds a research copy of a Quiet List art in a laboratory setting is not in violation of the Accords; however, should that mage discuss the contents of that copy in a tavern, a common hall, or any other non-sanctioned social setting, they shall be prosecuted as if they were reciting a public art. The "Quiet" nature of the art is a property of the knowledge itself, not the medium in which it is stored.

All research copies must be stored in magically-sealed repositories that are inaccessible to non-authorized personnel. The Aegis Magi are responsible for the periodic auditing of these repositories to ensure that no unauthorized dissemination of Quiet List information has occurred. If a research copy is lost or stolen, the holder must report the breach to the Accords Desk within one lunar cycle. Failure to report a breach of a Quiet List research copy is considered an act of treason against the Midlands. The goal of these regulations is to ensure that the most dangerous secrets of the Guild remain hidden from the eyes of the uninitiated, while remaining available to those tasked with the Guild's preservation. See § 300.3.

body.heading: § 300.1 Schedules of Arts — The Accords classify all magical disciplines into th
body.text:
The Quiet List itself remains classified information, accessible solely to high-ranking Guild officials on a need-to-know basis. Public discussion or dissemination of List items is prohibited under § 300.1(c), punishable by immediate expulsion from the ranks and revocation of all privileges. This restriction exists not merely for control, but because certain forbidden arts possess properties that can alter reality itself if misused—a danger no mortal mind should comprehend without proper safeguards in place. Breaching these prohibitions risks unleashing calamities beyond repair, as history has amply demonstrated through the tragic tales of fallen mages consumed by their own hubris and greed.

Reclassification requests for items on either Schedule B or C must be submitted via formal petition to the Arcane Research Committee, accompanied by comprehensive data on safety protocols and intended applications. Such petitions are reviewed quarterly, with decisions made solely based on empirical evidence rather than speculation or prejudice. Should a previously forbidden art prove safe through rigorous testing, it may be downgraded to Schedule B status pending further observation. Conversely, any item currently listed as ordinary that exhibits unexpected volatility must be immediately reclassified upward to prevent accidental catastrophe. The burden of proof always rests upon the applicant to demonstrate conclusively that their proposed use poses no unacceptable threat to persons or property.

Final provisions under this section dictate that all casters carry identification bearing their schedule classification at all times, subject to random inspection by authorized officers who may detain individuals suspected of violating these rules. Failure to produce valid credentials upon demand results in automatic forfeiture of one's license until proven innocent of wrongdoing beyond reasonable doubt. This strict regulatory framework ensures that magic remains a powerful yet controlled force, serving society without descending into chaos and destruction from which even the strongest wills cannot recover unscathed. Only by heeding these wise precepts may we hope to harness the wonders of arcane study responsibly for generations yet unborn.

sections.title: Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts
sections.brief: Forbidden unless a numbered permit. Innovators still file.

body.heading: Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates established in § 300.1 Schedules of Arts, the practice of Necromancy is hereby designated as a Class-A Forbidden Art. Any practitioner found engaging in the animation of necrotic tissue, the communion with the deceased for the purpose of servitude, or the manipulation of the veil between life and death without express, written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign shall be subject to immediate summary detention. The Accords recognize that while the manipulation of life essences presents a fundamental risk to the stability of the Midlands, the preservation of the natural order remains the primary directive of the Conservators. Consequently, the use of blood magic, soul-binding, and any methodology that facilitates the permanent extraction of vital essence from a sentient being is strictly prohibited under all circumstances, regardless of the stated intent of the caster.

Notwithstanding the general prohibition, the Innovators may submit formal petitions for "Restricted Research" permits concerning the study of necrotic energies. Such permits shall be scrutinized by the Accords Desk to ensure that any experimental application does not breach the fundamental safety threshold of the Autumnwood Accords. However, the mere possession of a permit for research purposes does not grant the holder the right to perform public demonstrations or large-scale applications of the art. All research conducted under such a permit must be contained within a sanctioned laboratory and reported to the Aegis Magi for periodic inspection. Failure to adhere to the containment protocols specified in the permit shall result in the immediate revocation of the permit and a referral to the Paradox Trial for the maximum penalty of magic sealing.

It is further stipulated that any mage found in possession of unauthorized necromantic reagents, including but not limited to bone-dust of the marked, grave-soil from consecrated sites, or fluids of the deceased, shall be deemed in violation of the Accords. The acquisition of such materials is considered prima facie evidence of intent to engage in Unsanctioned Arts. See § 1.6 for definitions of prohibited reagents. Any individual who knowingly assists in the smuggling or distribution of these materials shall be prosecuted as an accomplice to a high-tier felony. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the unauthorized use of the "Quiet List" for the purpose of concealing necromantic activities; any attempt to mask a forbidden art under a lesser classification shall be met with the full weight of the Accord's penal statutes.

body.heading: Quiet List Procedure
body.text:
The Quiet List serves as a confidential repository of magical methodologies, artifacts, and phenomena that, while not strictly forbidden by the primary Schedules, possess a level of volatility or inherent danger that necessitates restricted awareness. Unlike the public catalogues of sanctioned arts, the Quiet List is not a public document and may not be recited, transcribed, or disseminated in any public forum, including but not limited to taverns, marketplaces, or common halls. The procedure for listing an art upon the Quiet List is initiated by a petition from a member of the Conservator or Innovator factions, supported by a comprehensive risk assessment. Once the Archmage Sovereign approves the petition, the art is entered into the private registry. The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that high-risk magics remain under the purview of the Guild's oversight without causing unnecessary public alarm or providing a roadmap for illicit exploitation by outside entities such as the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion.

A mage who becomes aware of a Quiet List entry through the course of their duties or research is bound by a permanent oath of non-disclosure. Any breach of this confidentiality, whether intentional or through negligence, shall be considered a breach of the Accords and may lead to the revocation of the caster's Guild standing. The Accords Desk shall maintain the physical and metaphysical security of the Quiet List, ensuring that it remains inaccessible to those without the requisite clearance levels. No mage, regardless of rank, may demand access to the Quiet List for the purpose of personal study unless they can demonstrate that such study is essential to the defense of the Midlands or the preservation of the Accords.

Furthermore, the naming of a Quiet List entry in a public setting is strictly prohibited. If a mage is questioned regarding an art that is known to be on the Quiet List, they must provide a generalized description that does not reveal the specific classification or the unique properties of the art. The Aegis Magi are authorized to monitor for such breaches and may impose fines or temporary suspensions on those who fail to uphold the secrecy of the List. The Quiet List is a tool of preservation, not a secret of shame; it is the mechanism by which the Guild manages the most delicate threads of reality. By ensuring that these arts are not publicized, the Guild prevents the destabilization of the common populace and maintains the delicate equilibrium of the Autumnwood Accords. See § 1.6 for further clarification on confidentiality.

body.heading: Reclassification
body.text:
The classification of magical arts within the Autumnwood Accords is subject to periodic review by the Accords Desk to ensure that the Schedules of Arts remain relevant to the evolving nature of magical discovery. However, the process of reclassification is governed by strict procedural hurdles to prevent the politicization of magical safety. Specifically, moving an art from a restricted category, such as Schedule B (Restricted Research), to a more permissive category, such as Schedule A (Sanctioned Arts), is not a matter of simple majority vote or partisan preference. Such a transition requires a "Consensus of Stability," necessitating approval from both the Conservator and Innovator chairs, as well as a formal endorsement from the Archmage Sovereign. The Guild recognizes that the Innovators may frequently advocate for the expansion of sanctioned arts, while the Conservators seek to maintain the current boundaries; therefore, the Desk shall not permit a reclassification to occur solely based on the desires of one faction.

Any petition for reclassification must be accompanied by a "Stability Impact Report," detailing the history of the art's use, any recorded incidents of magical fallout, and a proposed framework for its safe integration into the general magical landscape. If a proposed reclassification is deemed by the Accords Desk to pose a significant risk to the Midlands or to violate the core tenets of the Autumnwood Accords, it shall be denied regardless of the factional support. The Desk shall maintain a record of all such petitions, and any mage found attempting to bypass the formal reclassification process by practicing a Schedule B art as if it were Schedule A shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. This rule ensures that the evolution of magic remains a deliberate, measured process rather than a reactive one.

Furthermore, the reclassification of an art does not retroactively change the legal status of previous violations. Any mage who engaged in the unauthorized practice of an art before its formal reclassification remains liable for the infractions committed during the period of its restricted status. The Accords Desk reserves the right to freeze the status of any art currently under review if new evidence of catastrophic risk emerges. This procedural safeguard is designed to prevent the rapid "normalization" of dangerous magics that could lead to systemic collapse. The integrity of the Schedules of Arts is the foundation of the Guild's authority, and its preservation is paramount. See § 300.1 for the primary categorizations.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges the necessity of research and the creation of pedagogical materials for the advancement of the arcane sciences. However, the status of an item or art as a "Quiet" entity under the Accords implies a permanent restriction on its public profile. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that any copy, derivative, or transcription of a Quiet List item remains a Quiet item. If a mage is granted permission to create a research copy of a Quiet art—such as a transcribed scroll, a physical model, or a localized magical echo—that copy must be treated with the same level of security and confidentiality as the original. The act of creating a copy does not "dilute" the restricted nature of the art, nor does it authorize the caster to speak of the copy’s contents in public spaces. The restriction is tied to the nature of the magic itself, not merely the specific instance of the medium.

While the physical possession of a research copy is permissible for authorized scholars, the dissemination of information regarding that copy is strictly controlled. A scholar may discuss the *methodology* of their research or the *general goals* of their study, provided such discussion does not reveal the specific mechanics, properties, or classifications of the Quiet item. For example, a mage may state they are "studying a volatile atmospheric phenomenon," but they may not describe the specific resonance frequencies or the unique identifiers that place it on the Quiet List. Any mage who shares the specific details of a Quiet research copy with a non-cleared individual, including those who are not members of the Guild, shall be subject to immediate disciplinary action. This includes the seizure of the research materials and a potential referral to the Aegis Magi for a security audit.

It is important to distinguish between the *existence* of a copy and the *revelation* of its contents. A mage may own a library of Quiet research copies, but they must be kept in a manner consistent with the privacy requirements of the Accords. These materials must be stored in secure locations, and access must be logged. The Accords Desk does not permit the creation of "public-facing" summaries of Quiet items; any attempt to create a "sanitized" version of a Quiet art for public consumption without the express permission of the Archmage Sovereign is a violation of the confidentiality protocols. The goal of these regulations is to facilitate the pursuit of knowledge while ensuring that the most dangerous and sensitive aspects of the arcane remain shielded from those who lack the training or the temperament to handle them. See § 1.6 for related definitions.

body.heading: Unauthorized Practices and Regulatory Enforcement
Unsanctioned Practices and Regulatory Enforcement
body.text:
The Accords explicitly prohibit the unlicensed practice of necromancy, blood magic, and other unsanctioned arts (§ 300.2). Any individual caught engaging in such forbidden rituals shall be subject to immediate arrest and trial before a full session of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Upon conviction, penalties may include permanent sealing of magical aptitude, imprisonment without parole, or execution by means of a painless arcane purge.

Innovator factions continue to file applications for permits to conduct research into these dangerous disciplines under strict supervision (§ 300.2). Such requests are scrutinized with extreme rigor, often requiring multiple rounds of peer review before approval is granted. Even when authorized, experiments must be performed within designated facilities and under the direct oversight of Conservator magi at all times. Any deviation from approved protocols results in instant revocation of the permit and severe disciplinary action against responsible parties.

The Quiet List procedure outlined in § 300.3 remains intact as a mechanism for reclassifying previously sanctioned items deemed too hazardous for public access. Reclassified artifacts are removed from general circulation and stored securely until further notice or permanent deletion from records. Possession of such items without explicit written authorization constitutes a capital offense punishable by death under any interpretation of the Accords.

Research copies of Quiet List materials may be obtained only upon formal request to the Archmage Sovereign, accompanied by a detailed explanation of intended usage and safeguards against misuse (§ 300.5). Copies are issued with watermarks and tracking glyphs embedded invisibly within the text itself, allowing for instant identification if illicitly distributed. Violation of these terms carries penalties equal to those imposed for actual possession of the original forbidden items.

Unauthorized practices by any entity or individual not holding valid licensure from the Autumnwood Accords Desk shall be treated as a felony crime under both Guild and Imperial law. Regulatory enforcement is conducted jointly by Aegis Magi, local constabulary forces, and specially appointed Oversight Committees empowered to investigate, prosecute, and adjudicate cases arising from suspected violations of the Code. Failure to comply with lawful directives issued during such proceedings may result in additional charges for contempt and obstruction of justice.

The Accords reserve the right to amend this section at any time without notice should circumstances warrant stricter controls over unsanctioned magical research. All citizens are therefore advised to remain vigilant regarding their surroundings and avoid involvement in activities that could bring disrepute upon themselves or the Guild through association with rogue practitioners operating outside established channels of authority and accountability mandated by these sacred statutes governing all matters pertaining to arcane study, practice, and regulation throughout our realm forevermore.

sections.title: Quiet List Procedure
sections.brief: How an art is listed without a public catalogue.

body.heading: Quiet List Procedure
body.text:
The maintenance of the Quiet List is a matter of highest security and sovereign discretion, overseen by the Archmage Sovereign and the High Council of the Conservators. Pursuant to the mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, certain schools of magic or specific arcane methodologies are deemed so volatile, spiritually corrosive, or socially destabilizing that their existence must be shielded from the general populace. The Quiet List is not a public catalogue, nor is it a registry available for consultation by mere citizens, wandering mages, or the uninitiated. It serves as a subterranean repository of forbidden knowledge, a ledger of the "Unsanctioned Arts" that the Guild recognizes as existing but refuses to acknowledge in the public sphere. The primary objective of this procedure is the containment of metaphysical hazards that, if publicized, would invite widespread hysteria or provide a blueprint for catastrophic misuse by the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or the Cosmic Jesters.

An art is listed upon the Quiet List through a process of secret adjudication. When a new magical phenomenon is discovered by the Innovators or identified as a recurring threat by the Conservators, it is brought before the High Council in a closed session. If the Council determines that the art poses a risk to the structural integrity of the Midlands or violates the fundamental tenets of Mana Reverence, it shall be struck from the public Schedules of Arts. From that moment forward, the art is officially "Quiet." No public advertisement of the art, no pedagogical instruction in public academies, and no commercial sale of components related specifically to that art may occur. Any mage found to be teaching, practicing, or publicly disseminating the mechanics of a Quiet Item shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi.

The procedure for listing does not involve the destruction of the knowledge, but rather its sequestration. The Guild maintains a clandestine library where the methodology of these arts is archived for study by authorized personnel only. This is a distinction between "Forbidden" and "Quiet." While some arts are forbidden entirely under the Iron Mandate of external powers, the Quiet List is a Guild-specific mechanism of internal regulation. To ensure the integrity of this procedure, any clerk or official who becomes aware of a Quiet Item is bound by a perpetual oath of silence. Recitation of a Quiet Item’s name or properties in a tavern, marketplace, or any other public forum is a breach of the Accords and shall be treated as a high-level offense, potentially resulting in a Paradox Trial. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Reclassification
body.text:
The administrative movement of magical arts between categories—specifically from the restricted tiers of the Innovators to the sanctioned tiers of the Conservators—is a formal process of Reclassification. This Codex clarifies that the act of Reclassification is a bureaucratic transition of status and does not constitute a "party" to any legal agreement or a change in the underlying nature of the magic itself. When an art is moved from Category B (Restricted Research) to Category A (Sanctioned Use), the Guild is acknowledging that the risks associated with the art have been sufficiently mitigated or that the social utility of the art outweighs the perceived danger. However, the transition of a category is a unilateral administrative act by the Archmage Sovereign; it does not create a bilateral contract between the user and the Guild.

Mages seeking to petition for the Reclassification of a specific art must provide a comprehensive dossier to the Conservators, demonstrating that the art can be practiced with a high degree of stability and without violating the core tenets of the Autumnwood Accords. If the petition is granted, the art is removed from the restricted schedules and may be taught in standard academies. This change in status does not grant the user immunity from the general regulations governing magical conduct. The mere fact that an art is no longer "Quiet" or "Restricted" does not mean it is unregulated; it simply means it is no longer subject to the specific secrecy protocols outlined in § 300.3.

Furthermore, any legal disputes arising from the use of an art during the period of its Reclassification shall be judged based on the status of the art at the time of the casting. If a mage utilizes an art that is currently undergoing a transition from restricted to sanctioned, they remain bound by the restrictive permissions of the Innovators until the final seal of Reclassification is affixed by the Archmage Sovereign. The movement of an art is not a negotiation; it is a decree. Therefore, any attempt by a mage or a faction to claim that the "process" of Reclassification creates a temporary state of legality is rejected. The law is either in effect, or it is not. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges the necessity of scholarly pursuit and the preservation of arcane history. Consequently, the creation of research copies of Quiet Items is permitted under strict supervision, provided such copies are designated as "Static Artifacts" for the purpose of study. It is a fundamental principle of this Codex that the creation of a copy does not strip the underlying art of its "Quiet" status. If an art is listed on the Quiet List, any physical manifestation, scroll, or construct derived from that art remains subject to the secrecy protocols of § 300.3. The existence of a research copy does not authorize the user to discuss the mechanics, properties, or existence of the art in public spaces.

The distinction between the *object* and the *information* is paramount. A mage may possess a physical copy of a Quiet Item within a secured laboratory for the purpose of analysis, but they may not speak of that item in a tavern, a marketplace, or any other public venue. Talking about the item is not permitted; possessing the copy is a regulated privilege. If an Innovator seeks to study a Quiet Item, they must do so within the confines of a Guild-sanctioned research hall. Any dissemination of the knowledge contained within that copy to unauthorized parties constitutes a violation of the Accords. The Guild's stance is clear: the possession of a copy is a matter of research, but the speech regarding that copy is a matter of security.

Furthermore, research copies are not considered "tender" or "goods" in any commercial sense. They cannot be traded, sold, or gifted to individuals outside of the Guild's authorized research circles. Any attempt to use a research copy as a means of bypassing the secrecy of the Quiet List will result in the immediate seizure of the copy and the initiation of a Paradox Trial for the offending mage. The goal of the Guild is to ensure that the dangerous truths of the Quiet List remain in the shadows, accessible only to those with the clearance to handle them and the discipline to keep them hidden. See § 1.6.

body.heading: The Quiet List and Its Maintenance
body.text:
The Quiet List shall constitute the official record of all arcane arts deemed unsanctioned by this Codex, maintained in strict confidence under § 100.4. Entry onto said List does not imply guilt or wrongdoing but rather necessitates administrative oversight to prevent misuse. The Desk shall review applications for inclusion with impartiality, considering factors such as potential danger to public safety and the likelihood of circumvention of existing prohibitions.

Upon determination that an art warrants listing, a formal notice shall be issued to known practitioners via registered mail or other reliable means, detailing the specific provisions implicated and affording them an opportunity to respond within ten days. Responses shall be reviewed by a panel comprising at least two Conservators and one Innovator, selected for their expertise in the relevant field and absence of personal interest in the matter under consideration.

In exceptional circumstances where immediate action is required to prevent irreparable harm, the Desk may order provisional inclusion on the Quiet List pending full review. Such measures shall be kept to the absolute minimum necessary and lifted as soon as practical based upon subsequent findings. All decisions regarding listing or delisting shall be documented in writing with supporting rationale provided where appropriate for future reference.

Practitioners whose works appear on the Quiet List shall remain subject to all applicable laws and regulations unless otherwise authorized by specific exemption granted pursuant to § 400.1. Failure to comply may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure under §§ 200.3-200.6. However, mere presence on the List shall not constitute grounds for automatic suspension or disqualification from future applications without further evidentiary showing of noncompliance.

The Desk retains discretion to reclassify arts originally listed as unsanctioned should new information emerge suggesting diminished risk or altered circumstances warranting reconsideration. Such determinations shall be made through established procedural safeguards designed to ensure fairness and transparency throughout the process while maintaining the integrity of the regulatory framework governing magical practice within the jurisdiction.

see § 100.4 regarding confidentiality obligations incumbent upon all Guild officials handling sensitive information; refer also to § 200.3 concerning grounds for temporary suspension pending resolution of outstanding issues affecting individual practitioners' standing before the Accords.

body.heading: Maintenance and Custody of the Quiet List
body.text:
§ 300.4 Reclassification of Listed Arts — Under § 300.1, arts may be assigned to the Quiet List subject to review by the Conservators and Innovators. This reclassification shall remain in effect indefinitely unless superseded by further ruling under § 300.5 or § 300.6. The Desk reserves authority to alter an art’s classification at any time upon sufficient showing of changed circumstances or new evidence.

§ 300.5 Research Copies and Specimen Custody — Any party desiring a research copy of a listed item must submit a formal petition detailing the intended study, duration, and safeguards against misuse. Approval rests solely with the Desk, which may impose additional conditions at its discretion. Approved specimens shall be held in secure custody under § 300.7 until completion of the authorized investigation, after which they may be returned or disposed of as directed.

§ 300.6 Unauthorized Reproduction and Distribution — No individual or entity may reproduce, distribute, or otherwise exploit a Quiet List art without express written consent from the Guild or its designated agents. Violations shall constitute serious breach under § 1.4 and subject to appropriate sanctions. This prohibition extends to digital formats, derivatives, and any form of commercialization whatsoever.

§ 300.7 Secure Storage Protocols — All items classified on the Quiet List must be maintained in physically secure facilities meeting minimum standards set forth by the Aegis Magi. Access shall be restricted to authorized personnel only, with full audit trails maintained for compliance verification purposes. Breach of these protocols triggers immediate investigation and potential revocation of related permits under § 200.1.

§ 300.8 Public Disclosure Limits — Information concerning specific Quiet List arts may not be publicly disclosed except as necessary to enforce this Code or protect public safety. Unauthorized publication of classified details shall result in disciplinary action commensurate with the severity of the violation. Exceptions require prior approval from at least two Desk members acting independently.

§ 300.9 International Considerations — In matters involving cross-border implications, the Guild shall consult relevant foreign authorities where appropriate. Such consultations do not diminish the binding nature of these provisions within Autumnwood jurisdiction but may inform enforcement strategies in cooperative contexts abroad.

body.heading: Quiet List Procedure and Reclassification Mechanisms
body.text:
The Quiet List serves as the confidential register maintained by the Autumnwood Accords Desk to catalog magics deemed too dangerous for open circulation without explicit regulation. Unlike public catalogues, entries on this list do not reveal their existence unless specifically requested through proper channels. This discretion allows the Guild to monitor potentially hazardous arts while avoiding unnecessary panic among lay citizens who might otherwise react poorly to knowledge of such powers existing at all.

Reclassification of an item onto or off of the Quiet List follows a rigorous internal review process initiated by either the Conservators or Innovators factions, though ultimately decided by the full Arcane Council. Evidence supporting the proposed change must be submitted along with detailed impact assessments regarding public safety and magical equilibrium. The matter is then debated in closed session before a final ruling is issued with an effective date specified therein. Until such time as reclassification takes effect, existing restrictions remain fully enforceable under penalty of law.

Research copies of Quiet List items may be obtained by authorized personnel for study purposes only upon presentation of valid credentials and explanation of intended use. Such requests are scrutinized meticulously given the inherent risks involved in handling materials capable of causing catastrophic harm if misused. Copies must remain under constant surveillance during any experiments conducted on Guild premises, with full reporting requirements imposed to ensure accountability throughout the process. Breach of these safeguards invites severe consequences ranging from license revocation to criminal prosecution depending upon circumstances surrounding the infraction committed.

Maintenance and Custody of the Quiet List falls primarily upon specialized units within the Aegis Magi dedicated exclusively to tracking classified magics across all jurisdictions under Guild authority. These agents operate under strict non-disclosure agreements binding them legally to never reveal their findings or methods under any conditions whatsoever, even in the face of death threats or extreme duress. Their work ensures that dangerous arts remain contained where they belong while allowing responsible scholars access needed for legitimate research endeavors when approved by senior leadership. Through diligent stewardship of this vital resource, the Autumnwood Accords continue fulfilling its mandate to balance innovation with stability for future generations alike.

sections.title: Reclassification
sections.brief: Moving B to A is not a party.

body.heading: § 300.4 Reclassification
body.text:
The administrative integrity of the Autumnwood Accords relies upon the immutable classification of magical phenomena, methodologies, and research subjects. It is the foundational principle of this Codex that the designation of a magical art, a research initiative, or a restricted substance is a matter of sovereign decree by the Guild, not a fluid state of being. Under no circumstances shall the mere alteration of a classification label—specifically the movement of a subject from Category B (Restricted Research) to Category A (Sanctioned/Public Art)—be construed as a legal transformation of the underlying nature of the act itself. The Accords Desk maintains that a change in designation is a procedural shift in oversight, not a fundamental transmutation of the magic’s inherent risk or the legal liabilities associated with its practice.

Furthermore, the doctrine of "Moving B to A is not a party" is hereby codified as a primary defense against administrative evasion. This means that if a school of magic or a specific ritual is moved from a restricted status to a sanctioned status by the Innovators or the Conservators, the legal precedents, historical prohibitions, and safety protocols associated with its previous "Category B" status remain tethered to its history. A practitioner who seeks to argue that a ritual is "safe" or "permissible" solely because it has been reclassified does so at their own peril. The Guild recognizes that while the regulatory burden may be lessened, the inherent volatility of the arcane does not diminish upon the stroke of a clerk’s quill. The reclassification is a change in the *handling* of the magic, not a change in the *essence* of the magic.

Any attempt by a faction—be it the Innovators seeking to expedite research or the Conservators seeking to isolate a threat—to use reclassification as a means to bypass the requirements of § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts, shall be deemed a violation of the Accords. If a practice is inherently forbidden under § 300.2, no administrative decree may "reclassify" it into a sanctioned category to circumvent the prohibition. The Accords Desk shall view any such attempt as a bad-faith maneuver intended to undermine the stability of the Midlands. Practitioners are reminded that the Aegis Magi are tasked with enforcing the current status of the Accords; however, they are not required to ignore the historical hazards of a practice simply because its paperwork has been updated.

In the event of a dispute regarding the transition of a magical art from a restricted to a public status, the Archmage Sovereign shall mediate the determination of the "Residual Risk." This determination shall dictate what safety protocols remain in place despite the reclassification. For instance, if a blood-based transmutation is moved from Category B to Category A, the Guild may still require specific containment seals, even if the general practice is no longer subject to the Innovator's Research Permits. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any "amnesty" granted by reclassification that would exempt a practitioner from the consequences of historical violations. Legal culpability for actions taken while a magic was under Category B status remains enforceable regardless of subsequent administrative shifts.

All records of reclassification must be filed with the Autumnwood Accords Desk in triplicate. Each entry must include a "Heritage Clause" stating that the new designation does not nullify any previous safety warnings or prohibitions. Any practitioner found to be exploiting the nuance between a "Reclassified Art" and a "New Art" to evade the Paradox Trial shall be subject to immediate sanction. The Guild’s authority is derived from the preservation of the Midlands; therefore, the law shall not be treated as a labyrinth of loopholes where the mere renaming of a danger allows for its unchecked expansion. The Codex is the anchor; the labels are but the markings upon the anchor.

body.heading: Reassignment and Transfer of Classified Materials
body.text:
§ 300.4 Reclassification shall only occur upon formal review by the Desk, supported by sworn testimony or irrefutable evidence. A material may be elevated from Class C to Class B if its possession now presents imminent danger to persons or property. Conversely, downgrading from B to C requires proof that original restrictions have been fully mitigated and no longer justify containment measures. Any reclassification must be documented in the official register with a detailed rationale, signed by two Conservators and one Innovator in attendance. Unauthorized alterations to classification status are deemed criminal tampering subject to immediate arrest under § 400.12(b). Parties seeking reassignment shall submit written applications through their licensed attorneys at least thirty days prior to any proposed hearing date. The Desk retains sole discretion whether to grant relief, and its decision is final and unappealable except via writ of habeas corpus filed in accordance with § 900.5(c)(ii).

§ 300.4 A shall not be reassigned to Class B merely because the holder has violated terms of their license or contract; such misconduct warrants revocation proceedings under § 200.4, not automatic reclassification. Transfer of a material from one authorized party to another requires written consent from both entities and prior approval by the Desk to ensure continued compliance with safety protocols. Any dispute regarding ownership or custody shall be resolved through binding arbitration governed by Articles 15–18 of these Accords. The Desk may issue emergency injunctions restraining further dissemination when necessary to prevent harm, pursuant to its inherent equitable powers recognized under § 701(a)(iii). All reclassification orders remain subject to annual audit and potential reversal should circumstances change materially over time. Failure to adhere strictly to prescribed procedures may result in contempt sanctions including fines up to one hundred guild credits per violation or imprisonment not exceeding six months at the Desk's discretion.

§ 300.4 Reclassification proceedings must be conducted with full due process protections afforded under § 101(d)(ii), including notice, opportunity to be heard, and independent verification of facts presented. The burden of proof rests squarely upon the party requesting modification of classification status, who must demonstrate by clear and convincing evidence that current restrictions are no longer warranted or that new conditions justify stricter controls. Hearings shall be scheduled within forty-five days of application receipt unless extraordinary exigencies dictate otherwise, in which case expedited procedures may apply subject to subsequent ratification. Written findings accompanying each decision shall set forth the factual basis and legal reasoning employed, providing transparency essential for maintaining public confidence in the integrity of this system. Appeals must be lodged within ten calendar days of notification of final ruling and submitted directly to the Appellate Division without delay. All costs associated with reclassification proceedings are borne by the initiating party unless equitable considerations warrant otherwise under § 102(c)(iv).

§ 300.4 This section shall take effect immediately upon adoption and apply prospectively only, except as expressly provided herein. Nothing contained in this subsection shall be construed to limit or impair any rights accrued under prior classifications nor create liability for past acts committed before enactment date. Future amendments regarding reclassification criteria will require a two-thirds vote of the full Assembly acting by secret ballot after public notice period not less than thirty days has elapsed. The Desk is authorized to promulgate implementing rules and regulations necessary to carry out the purposes of this section, subject to review and disapproval by majority vote at any regular session thereafter. Violations of provisions herein shall constitute separate offenses punishable under applicable penal statutes unless otherwise specified expressly in these Accords. Nothing in this provision shall be deemed to waive any existing immunity privileges enjoyed by duly authorized officers or agents acting within scope of employment duties related thereto.

§ 300.4 In case of conflict between terms set forth herein and those contained elsewhere in the complete body of these Autumnwood Accords, provisions specifically addressing matters directly pertinent to reclassification shall control exclusively over general principles stated in unrelated sections. Ambiguities arising from interpretation of this subsection shall be resolved according to established canons of statutory construction unless contrary intent appears plainly upon face thereof. Judicial review limited strictly to questions of law without regard for factual determinations made by the administrative body charged with enforcement responsibilities under Article III hereof. All actions taken pursuant to authority granted herein are binding upon all persons subject to jurisdiction conferred thereby whether individually or collectively acting on their own behalf alone. Nothing contained in this part shall impair remedies available at common law nor exclude any claim arising independently outside scope of regulatory framework established by these governing documents solely intended for administrative convenience purposes only."

body.heading: § 301.1 Unauthorized Use of Restricted Artifacts
body.text:
No caster shall knowingly employ any item, device, or construct listed on the Quiet List without express written permission from the Archmage Sovereign. Violation constitutes Class A Felony and grounds for immediate suspension of licensure. Exceptions exist only where emergency circumstances preclude prior consultation and subsequent debriefing yields no evidence of malfeasance. Possession alone is not a crime absent intent to misuse; however, failure to report unauthorized acquisition within seventy-two hours shall be deemed constructive knowledge and punishable as negligence under § 105.3. All findings regarding suspicious artifacts must be submitted for review by the Conservator's Office prior to any disposition, whether through sale, donation, or personal retention. Unauthorized duplication or reverse-engineering of restricted items is strictly prohibited except under strict supervision by qualified personnel designated by the Desk. Any suspected contraband shall be turned in immediately to nearest Aegis Magi for secure storage pending further investigation. Repeat offenders subject to permanent banishment from Guild halls and revocation of all privileges without refund of fees paid. See also § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; § 301.6 Penalties for Violation.

body.heading: § 300.4 Reclassification and Reassignment of Materials
body.text:
The reclassification or reassignment of any item on the Quiet List requires an affirmative resolution by a majority vote of the Desk, conducted in closed session under oath. See § 1.9 for restrictions on disclosure of such proceedings. An applicant must demonstrate compelling necessity, typically related to ongoing research projects approved under § 400.1 or national security interests deemed critical by the Conservators. Unauthorized duplication of classified materials is strictly prohibited; all copies must be registered with the Desk and marked accordingly. Failure to comply may result in suspension of privileges under § 200.4.

Reassignment of items between authorized custodians shall only occur pursuant to written transfer orders executed by both parties and filed with the Clerk's Office. Such transfers must specify precise conditions for handling, storage, and use, along with a detailed inventory of any ancillary equipment or reagents required. Custodial agreements must include indemnification clauses protecting the Guild against liability arising from improper management of reassigned assets. Breach of these contractual terms constitutes a felony offense punishable by seizure of all involved property and permanent revocation of standing to serve as an Aegis Magi. See § 100.2 regarding authority to bind the Guild in such matters.

§ 301.1 Unauthorized Use of Restricted Artifacts

The possession or deployment of any Quiet List item without explicit permission from both the original owner and a representative of the Conservators is deemed an act of grand larceny coupled with aggravated misuse of magical resources. Punishment shall be immediate and severe, including confiscation of all contraband, mandatory confinement for re-education, and potential revocation of licensure. Repeat offenders face disbarment and permanent exile from the Guild's halls. Exceptions may be made in cases of self-defense or emergency mitigation of imminent harm, provided such actions are documented thoroughly and reviewed post hoc by an impartial tribunal. See § 500.3 for protocols governing conduct during high-stakes magical confrontations.

The Desk reserves the right to audit any facility where restricted artifacts are stored or utilized, with full access granted to inspect records, equipment, and personnel as deemed necessary. Refusal to comply with inspection demands will result in automatic forfeiture of all privileges held by the offending party and their affiliates. All findings from such audits shall be recorded confidentially and made available upon request to authorized investigators only. Regular reports on artifact custody must be submitted quarterly by each custodian, detailing condition assessments and incident logs where applicable. Negligence leading to loss or corruption of classified materials will attract punitive damages multiple times the item's appraised value. See § 400.2 for guidelines on maintaining proper records of sensitive holdings.

In all disputes concerning ownership, custody, or usage rights of Quiet List items, the burden of proof rests with the party asserting a claim. Evidence must be corroborated by sworn testimony and supporting documentation meeting standards set forth in § 1.6. The Desk may appoint independent appraisers or experts as needed to assist in determining fair market value or technical specifications relevant to the case at hand. Decisions rendered shall be final and binding, subject only to appeal within thirty days on grounds of procedural error manifestly affecting outcome. Finality provisions are intended to preserve stability in commercial transactions involving regulated magical goods. See § 600.1 for additional rules governing contractual obligations between casters and non-casters regarding specialized equipment procurement.

body.heading: § 301. Unauthorized Use of Restricted Artifacts and Consequences for Breach
body.text: § 301. No individual or entity shall possess, utilize, replicate, or otherwise engage with any item listed on the Quiet List without express written permission from the Autumnwood Accords Desk under penalty of immediate seizure and prosecution for grand larceny and arcane vandalism. All such artifacts are deemed contraband in the eyes of the law regardless of provenance or claimed ownership rights. Possession alone constitutes a Class A felony carrying mandatory imprisonment up to five years plus a fine not exceeding one thousand gold pieces per count. Repeat offenders face enhanced penalties including permanent magical disqualification and exile from Guild-controlled territories. This prohibition applies equally to individuals, corporations, magical societies, and foreign powers. Violations shall be prosecuted under the full weight of applicable criminal statutes without regard for diplomatic immunity or sovereign claims. The Desk retains sole discretion over any future reclassification of items based on evolving threat assessments and technological capabilities. Any unauthorized attempts to bypass security measures surrounding restricted materials will result in escalated charges including attempted theft from federal custody and obstruction of justice. Strict adherence to these provisions is imperative to maintain public safety and national security against ever-present threats of rogue sorcery and criminal exploitation. Failure to comply shall be treated as an act of war by the Guild with appropriate retaliatory measures deemed necessary under existing treaties and statutes. All persons are strongly urged to familiarize themselves fully with this regulation before attempting access to any potentially dangerous artifacts whatsoever under threat of severe legal repercussions upon conviction.

body.heading: § 302. Penalties for Violation of Restricted Artifacts Provisions
body.text: § 302. Any person found guilty of violating the prohibitions set forth in Section 301 shall be subject to immediate arrest and confinement pending trial. Upon conviction, sentences may include lengthy periods of incarceration followed by supervised release with strict conditions attached including mandatory community service, restitution payments to affected victims, and permanent prohibition from holding any public office or license related to magic arts. Additional penalties may involve confiscation of all personal property deemed instrumental in the commission of said crimes along with substantial fines calculated at least double the value of stolen goods if ascertainable. In cases involving organized criminal enterprises utilizing restricted items for illicit purposes, ringleaders face life imprisonment without parole eligibility while lesser accomplices receive tiered punishments based on their level of involvement and cooperation during investigation proceedings.
