Civil lawsuits brought by harmed parties may result in further monetary damages awards exceeding any statutory caps applicable elsewhere under relevant laws. Repeat offenders commit aggravated offenses warranting enhanced sentencing guidelines with minimum terms doubled for each prior conviction within the last decade. The state reserves the right to seek capital punishment in extreme circumstances where violation resulted directly in death or catastrophic environmental damage through reckless misuse of forbidden powers. Full compliance with these stringent rules remains non-negotiable given the existential risks posed by unchecked access to such dangerous technologies throughout our society today. Everyone must recognize their individual responsibilities toward preserving collective safety above all personal gain whatsoever at this critical juncture in history!

sections.title: Research Copies of Quiet Items
sections.brief: Copies are still Quiet. Talking about them is not.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
Copies are still Quiet. Talking about them is not.

The protocols governing the Quiet List are designed to ensure that certain sensitive, volatile, or socially disruptive magical phenomena remain outside the public consciousness. Under the Accords, the "Quiet" status of an item refers to its inherent nature and the Guild's determination that its public dissemination poses a risk to the stability of the Midlands or the safety of the populace. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that the creation of a secondary representation—be it a physical manuscript, a mental projection, or a magical duplicate—does not strip the original subject of its Quiet status. A copy of a Quiet Item is, by definition, a Quiet Item.

While the physical possession of a copy is subject to the standard restrictions of the Quiet List, the act of discussing the existence of such a copy in a private, scholarly, or authorized setting does not constitute a violation of the Accords. The prohibition is against the *recitation* of the Quiet Item’s specific mechanics, incantations, or secret histories in public forums, such as taverns or marketplaces. The mere mention that a researcher possesses a "Quiet Copy" for the purpose of authorized study is permissible, provided the contents of that copy are not revealed. The law distinguishes between the *subject* of the research and the *act* of research.

Scholars affiliated with the Innovators may hold copies of Quiet Items for the purpose of restricted research, provided they have obtained the requisite permissions from Archmage Veyra or her designated deputies. These researchers may speak of their work in peer-reviewed settings, discussing the *implications* of the research without revealing the *specifics* of the Quiet Item itself. However, should a researcher describe the specificities of a Quiet Item—regardless of whether they are describing the original or a copy—they shall be subject to immediate sanction. The copy is a shadow of the original; if the shadow is cast into the light of public discourse, the prohibition is breached.

This distinction is vital for the continued advancement of the arcane arts. It allows for the progress of the Innovators to continue in the shadows of the Hall of Autumn Wood without alerting the Regal Empire or the Silver Flame to the Guild's internal methodologies. The Guild recognizes that knowledge is power, but the Accords recognize that *public* knowledge of certain powers is a liability. Therefore, while the copy remains bound by the silence of the List, the researcher is permitted to speak of the *process* of the research. See § 300.2. Any violation of this distinction by a practitioner shall be referred to the Desk for a Paradox Trial to determine the extent of the breach.

body.heading: § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
The Desk hereby establishes the procedure for obtaining research copies of items listed on the Quiet List, recognizing that such materials may be essential to legitimate magical inquiry despite their sensitive nature. Under § 1.4, all persons bound by the Accords must comply with lawful requests from authorized researchers in good faith.

An applicant seeking a copy of a Quiet Item shall submit a formal petition to the Desk, detailing the intended research purposes and demonstrating competence through prior licensing under § 200.1 or established academic credentials. The petition must include a sworn statement that the material will be used solely for scholarly advancement and not for personal gain or prohibited ends as defined in § 300.2.

Upon receipt of a complete application, the Desk shall review it within seven (7) days. If approved, a research copy shall be issued containing only the necessary components for study while omitting any dangerous activation sequences or full schematics. The recipient must affix their seal as required by § 1.9 and sign an agreement to return all materials upon completion of their work or at the Desk's discretion.

Failure to adhere to these terms constitutes a breach of the Accords subject to penalties under § 500 et seq., including potential revocation of licensing privileges and referral for Paradox Trial proceedings per § 300.4. The Desk reserves the right to audit research facilities and seize unauthorized copies without notice, pursuant to its broad regulatory authority vested by this Code.

This provision balances the need for safe access to magical knowledge with appropriate safeguards against misuse, embodying the Accords' dual commitment to innovation and stability as outlined in § 100.7. The Desk shall issue further implementing guidelines as deemed necessary from time to time.

body.heading: § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items — Continued
body.text: § 300.5 prohibits the duplication or distribution of items on the Quiet List without explicit authorization from the Desk. This restriction extends to both physical artifacts and their magical signatures, which may be embedded within other objects or structures. Unauthorized reproduction of a Quiet Item's unique properties constitutes a violation akin to theft or sabotage, regardless of intent. The prohibition remains in full force even when discussing such items hypothetically or academically; any disclosure that could facilitate illicit acquisition is deemed actionable under § 300.5(a). Exceptions are granted solely through formal petitions reviewed by the Desk, which may impose conditions such as secure storage, limited access, and mandatory reporting of usage. Violations trigger automatic revocation of all existing permits held by the offender and subject them to disciplinary proceedings under Part IV-B. The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to demonstrate that a copy existed and was obtained improperly; mere suspicion is insufficient for sanctions. This provision exists to prevent the proliferation of dangerous or destabilizing magic into the hands of unscrupulous individuals, thereby safeguarding both public safety and the integrity of the arcane arts. Failure to comply with § 300.5 may result in permanent disqualification from practicing magic within Autumnwood jurisdiction, along with financial penalties assessed according to prevailing rates for legal services rendered during enforcement actions.

body.heading: Research Copies and the Sanctity of Secrecy
body.text:
§ 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items

A "research copy" refers to an authorized reproduction or derivative work based upon an item from the Quiet List, created for scholarly study rather than commercial exploitation. The production of such copies is strictly regulated under this section to preserve the integrity of the original artifact and prevent unauthorized distribution. All requests for research copies must be submitted in writing by a duly credentialed member of the Guild or its affiliated institutions. Each application shall include a detailed description of the intended use, potential risks, and measures taken to mitigate any adverse effects on public safety.

Upon receipt of an application, the Desk shall convene a special committee consisting of representatives from relevant departments to evaluate the request. Factors considered in this evaluation include the necessity of the research for advancing magical knowledge, the competence and character of the applicant, and the likelihood that the proposed work will yield beneficial results without compromising security protocols. The committee shall render a decision within thirty days of receiving the complete application package.

If approved, the original item shall be temporarily transferred to the requesting party under agreed-upon conditions of custody and handling. These conditions may include mandatory insurance coverage, strict limits on access to unaccredited personnel, and regular inspections by Guild auditors. Failure to adhere to any term of the agreement shall result in immediate revocation of permission and possible disciplinary action against the responsible individuals.

Any unauthorized creation or dissemination of research copies constitutes a serious offense subject to severe penalties under applicable provisions of the Accords. Offenders may face suspension of credentials, fines up to one hundred thousand gold pieces per violation, imprisonment for up to five years, or expulsion from the Guild entirely at the sole discretion of the Archmage Sovereign. Repeat offenders shall be treated with particular severity in accordance with the spirit of this section and the broader goals of maintaining order within our ranks.

It is further provided that nothing herein shall be construed as granting any implied license to reverse engineer, decompile, or otherwise analyze the internal workings of a Quiet Item beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose of research. Such activities remain prohibited without explicit written consent from both the item's owner and the Guild itself. Violations of this prohibition may lead to civil liability in addition to criminal sanctions as outlined above.

This section shall be interpreted liberally to effectuate its purposes, which include fostering innovation while safeguarding against misuse. Ambiguities arising hereunder shall be resolved in favor of protecting public welfare and upholding the principles laid forth throughout these Accords. Any attempts to evade or circumvent the requirements imposed by this provision through technicalities or subterfuge are hereby expressly forbidden.

The provisions contained herein reflect a careful balance between promoting scientific progress and ensuring responsible stewardship of powerful artifacts. As such, they shall remain in full force until amended or repealed by proper authority acting pursuant to established procedures outlined elsewhere within these laws. Future developments in the field of magical technology may necessitate periodic review and adjustment of this framework to address emerging challenges effectively.

body.heading: § 300.5 Research Copies and the Sanctity of Secrecy
body.text:
The sanctity of secrecy underpins the very fabric of the Quiet List, and any breach thereof is treated with the utmost gravity by the Mages' Guild. A research copy of a Quiet Item shall retain its classified status regardless of physical separation from the original repository, provided that no unauthorized dissemination occurs. However, mere discussion or speculation concerning such items within prohibited venues—including but not limited to taverns, marketplaces, and other public gathering places—is strictly forbidden. Violators face severe penalties for compromising the confidentiality of Guild affairs.

Furthermore, any attempt to reverse-engineer a research copy with intent to replicate its effects is deemed an act of high treason against the Accords. Such endeavors shall be immediately halted by Aegis Magi upon discovery, and all parties involved subjected to trial for breach of contract and conspiracy. The penalties imposed may range from permanent revocation of licensure to imprisonment in a magical containment facility. In cases where evidence suggests broader collusion or sabotage of Guild operations, additional charges will be pursued to the fullest extent of the law.

It is imperative that all mages uphold their oaths of silence regarding Quiet Items under any circumstances whatsoever. Failure to do so not only endangers individuals but threatens the stability of society at large. The Mages' Guild remains vigilant in protecting its interests and enforcing these principles without exception or leniency. Any perceived weakness or deviation from established protocols will be met with swift and decisive action to rectify the situation. Restraint, discretion, and unwavering loyalty are non-negotiable expectations for those privileged to serve within this esteemed organization. By adhering strictly to these mandates, mages ensure the continued prosperity and security of all whom they protect through their mastery of arcane arts.

see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts
see § 1.7 Construction: Aggregation of Conduct
see § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth
see § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill"

body.heading: § 300.5 Research Copies and the Sanctity of Secrecy — Continued
body.text:
The creation, distribution, and utilization of research copies remain subject to strict confidentiality protocols designed to preserve their inherent secrecy. Under no circumstances shall a research copy be disclosed to unauthorized parties or employed in contexts inconsistent with its intended scholarly purpose. Violations of these provisions constitute serious breaches of Guild trust and may result in immediate revocation of the original license and subsequent disciplinary action.

The sanctity of secrecy extends beyond mere physical possession, encompassing all forms of communication regarding a research copy's existence, specifications, or capabilities. Even indirect references that might enable reverse engineering or unauthorized replication are prohibited. Researchers must exercise utmost discretion when discussing their work with colleagues, superiors, or third parties, ensuring no actionable intelligence falls into disreputable hands.

Failure to adhere to these confidentiality mandates exposes not only the individual responsible but also the Guild's broader interests to grave risk. Consequently, all members bound by this Codex are held personally accountable for maintaining rigorous control over research copies and preventing any unauthorized dissemination of sensitive information. Breaches will be met with swift and severe penalties commensurate with the degree of negligence or malice involved.

In sum, the preservation of secrecy remains paramount to safeguarding both individual researchers and the integrity of magical knowledge itself. All parties must approach their stewardship of research copies with unwavering diligence, recognizing that even seemingly innocuous lapses can have catastrophic downstream effects on Guild stability and security. Vigilance against inadvertent leaks is thus a non-negotiable imperative under § 300.5.

see § 1.4 Persons Bound regarding obligations applicable to all covered entities; see § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill for analogous restrictions on automated agents; see § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure establishing foundational principles of secrecy enforcement; and see § 300.2 Necromancy defining prohibited schools of magic that may be implicated in improper research copy usage.

sections.title: Research Permits
sections.brief: Form, fee, who signs.

body.heading: Research Permits
body.text:
§ 400.1 Research Permits — Form, fee, who signs.

All inquiries into the manipulation of high-density mana, the exploration of restricted schools, or the creation of volatile arcane phenomena shall be subject to the rigorous oversight of the Autumnwood Accords. No mage, regardless of standing or lineage, may commence any undertaking that risks the integrity of the Midlands or the stability of the local weave without a valid Research Permit issued by the Accords Desk. The application for such a permit must be submitted on the Official Form 400-A, which requires a comprehensive description of the intended methodology, a projected duration of the research, and a detailed risk assessment of potential blowback. Failure to provide a complete risk assessment shall result in an immediate summary rejection of the application without the possibility of appeal for a period of three lunar cycles.

The fee for a Research Permit is calculated based on the magnitude of the arcane flux expected during the proceedings. This fee is non-refundable and must be deposited in the Guild’s treasury prior to the signing of the permit. For research involving high-risk categories, such as those bordering on the forbidden schools outlined in § 300.2, the fee shall be tripled to account for the increased surveillance requirements. It is strictly understood that these fees do not constitute a payment for the right to perform the magic, but rather a tax on the potential hazard posed to the public and the Guild's interests. The Accords Desk reserves the right to adjust fee structures based on the current volatility of the regional mana ley lines.

The authority to sign and validate a Research Permit rests solely with the presiding leadership of the relevant faction, as mediated by Archmage Veyra. For standard research, a signature from a Senior Conservator or a High Innovator is sufficient, provided it is countersigned by an Aegis Mage to ensure enforcement capabilities are available. In cases of extreme complexity or novelty, the Archmage Sovereign must personally review and sign the permit. No provisional permits shall be issued by lower-ranking officials, nor shall a permit granted by a Conservator be superseded by an Innovator without a formal decree from the Desk. All signed permits shall be stamped with the official seal of the Accords; see § 1.9. Any researcher found operating under an expired permit, or an altered permit, shall be subject to immediate seizure of materials and referral to the Paradox Trial for sentencing.

body.heading: Research Permits and Authorization Protocols
body.text:
§ 400.1 No research into the Schedules of Arts may commence without first obtaining a valid Research Permit issued by the Autumnwood Accords Desk in accordance with this Section. The permit serves as both an authorization to proceed and a record of the permitted scope, conditions, and reporting requirements applicable to the proposed work.

Applicants for permits must submit a detailed proposal outlining the objectives, methodology, expected outcomes, safety measures, and duration of the research project. Where appropriate, applicants shall also provide qualifications demonstrating competency in the relevant fields of study. The Desk shall review all submissions with diligence, consulting with subject matter experts as necessary to assess potential risks and benefits.

Permit fees are set at rates sufficient to cover administrative costs and compensate for any loss of revenue resulting from the temporary suspension of related activities during the research period. Fees vary according to the complexity, scale, and duration of the proposed work. Payment shall be made in Guild tender prior to issuance of the permit. Failure to remit required fees may result in denial of the application or revocation of an already granted permit with associated penalties.

The permit must be signed by both the applicant and a representative of the Desk attesting to understanding of all terms and conditions set forth therein. Each party retains a copy for their records. The permit shall specify any limitations on methods, materials, locations, or personnel permitted during the research engagement. Deviation from approved parameters without prior written consent constitutes a material breach and may lead to immediate termination of authorization along with potential sanctions under applicable statutes.

Throughout the duration of the project, researchers are required to maintain accurate logs documenting all activities conducted pursuant to the permit terms. Final reports summarizing results achieved and any adverse impacts incurred must be submitted within thirty days following completion or earlier if requested by the Desk. Prompt submission of complete documentation is mandatory for processing subsequent applications and maintaining good standing with the Guild.

Violations of these provisions shall be addressed through established enforcement mechanisms including but not limited to fines, suspension of privileges, imprisonment, and permanent disqualification from future permit eligibility at the sole discretion of the presiding authority. Repeat offenders may face enhanced penalties commensurate with severity of infractions committed. All parties are urged to comply fully with research permit regulations as a means of ensuring safe, responsible advancement of magical knowledge for the greater good of society.

body.heading: § 400.1 Research Permits
body.text:
§ 400.1 All research into Schedule I and II magical arts requires an active Permit to Conduct Restricted Investigation, issued by the Innovators' Oversight Committee pursuant to § 300.5. No caster may engage in such study without first obtaining said permit; failure to do so constitutes a Class C violation under § 200.1(b).

Permits are granted on a case-by-case basis after review of the applicant's credentials, intended methodology, and risk assessment. Fees vary according to duration and complexity but shall not exceed the standard rate established by the Conservators' Fiscal Board. Applications must be submitted in triplicate via secure courier or encrypted transmission, accompanied by proof of adequate containment facilities and emergency protocols.

Upon approval, each permit specifies exact parameters including location, timeframe, permitted subjects, and authorized personnel. Deviation from these terms voids the authorization immediately and triggers an automatic audit by Aegis Magi. Violation may result in suspension or revocation of all future permits held by the responsible party.

All research conducted under valid permit must be logged daily with detailed records of procedures, outcomes, and any adverse effects observed on participants or environment. Final reports are due upon conclusion of the project and shall remain subject to random inspection by Guild auditors. Failure to maintain proper documentation may lead to disciplinary action regardless of successful results.

The purpose of this system is twofold: first, to ensure that dangerous experiments proceed with adequate safeguards in place; second, to provide a mechanism for tracking emerging trends and potential threats posed by unchecked magical innovation. Through careful oversight, the Guild seeks to balance the pursuit of knowledge with responsibility to public safety.

See also § 400.2 regarding special provisions for pocket dimension laboratories, and § 300.5 governing the scope and limitations of permitted research activities. Under § 1.7, all terms herein have their ordinary meaning unless defined otherwise within this Part or by subsequent amendment. Nothing in these rules shall be construed to limit inherent rights of free speech or academic inquiry where no harm is imminent.

[END PAGE]

body.heading: Research Permits and Authorization Protocols — Continued
body.text:
§ 400.1 Research Permits. All research involving Class IV or higher magical phenomena requires prior authorization in the form of a formal Permit to Conduct Investigations, issued by the Conservatorial Oversight Committee ("the Committee"). Application forms must detail the intended scope, methodology, potential risks, and containment measures proposed by the researcher. The Permit shall specify duration, location, personnel authorized to participate, and reporting obligations. Failure to secure a valid Permit constitutes a Class C Infraction under § 200.1(d).

The fee for issuance of a Research Permit is set at five thousand silver pieces, payable in advance via Wario Coin or equivalent liquid assets. All receipts shall be documented on the official Registry maintained by the Guild Treasurer's Office. Fees may be adjusted periodically to account for inflation and administrative costs associated with oversight activities. Non-payment results in automatic denial of the application and potential blacklisting from future permits.

Permits are non-transferable and strictly tied to the named principal investigator and their immediate research team as listed on the original filing. Substitution of personnel requires written notification to the Committee at least seventy-two hours prior to commencement of work, accompanied by updated credentials and background checks for all incoming members. Unauthorized delegation violates § 200.5(c) regarding unapproved proxies.

Violations of Permit terms constitute grounds for immediate revocation and suspension of future applications until such time as compliance can be demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Committee. Repeat offenses may result in permanent disqualification from conducting regulated research, at the sole discretion of Archmage Veyra upon recommendation by the Oversight Council. Disciplinary proceedings shall follow standard protocols outlined in Part II, Section C of this Code.

Researchers found operating without valid permits or in contravention thereof are subject to seizure of equipment and materials, imposition of monetary penalties ranging from two hundred to one thousand silver pieces per violation, and mandatory remedial training approved by the Guild's Educational Standards Board. Refusal to comply with these requirements may lead to escalation under § 300.4(a)(ii) concerning obstruction of lawful enforcement actions.

The Committee retains discretion to impose additional conditions deemed necessary for public safety or environmental protection, which must be adhered to without question. Failure to meet such stipulations warrants immediate termination of the Permit and initiation of proceedings for gross negligence under applicable statutes. All disputes arising from permit administration shall be resolved exclusively through formal arbitration channels established herein, precluding judicial intervention except in extraordinary circumstances involving imminent threat to life or property.

This provision operates subject to existing laws governing intellectual property rights, environmental hazards, and occupational health standards as may apply by force of circumstance. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to diminish the authority of duly constituted governmental bodies to regulate magical activities within their jurisdictions pursuant to statutory mandates. Interjurisdictional conflicts shall be resolved through diplomatic negotiation between relevant authorities or binding arbitration ordered by a competent tribunal upon petition.

For purposes of clarity and consistency, all references throughout this section to "research," "investigation," or similar terms encompass any systematic effort to acquire knowledge pertaining to magical theory, practice, or application, whether conducted for educational, commercial, or personal reasons. The prohibition extends equally to theoretical speculation and empirical experimentation unless expressly permitted under valid authorization granted hereunder. Breaches of these guidelines are treated with utmost seriousness given their potential consequences for societal stability.

Researchers violating this section face severe repercussions including revocation of licensure, bans on future employment within the industry, and possible criminal charges depending on severity of offense and harm caused. The Guild maintains vigilant oversight to ensure adherence and will pursue all available remedies against those who flout these rules. Compliance remains paramount for safeguarding both individual interests and broader community welfare alike.

"see § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs; see § 300.1 Schedules of Arts; see § 200.5 Guest Casters"

body.heading: § 400.1 Research Permits — Authorization Protocols
body.text:
Every application for a research permit must be submitted in triplicate, each copy bearing the original signature and seal of the applicant or their duly authorized agent. The forms prescribed by the Guild shall be used exclusively; any deviation constitutes grounds for immediate rejection without further notice. All supporting documentation must accompany the initial submission, including detailed project proposals, risk assessments, safety protocols, and proof of adequate insurance coverage where applicable. Failure to provide complete information may result in indefinite processing delays or outright denial.

Upon receipt, the application shall be assigned a unique identification number by the Clerk's Office for tracking purposes. This number must appear prominently on all subsequent correspondence related to the matter. The designated reviewing officer will then conduct a preliminary examination within seven working days, checking for compliance with formal requirements and obvious deficiencies. Should any errors or omissions be detected, the applicant shall be notified in writing specifying the necessary corrections. Amended submissions are subject to the same rigorous scrutiny as original applications.

Once cleared for full review, the matter proceeds to committee evaluation by qualified peers specializing in the relevant field of inquiry. The committee convenes no sooner than ten days after all materials have been filed and no later than thirty days thereafter unless extenuating circumstances arise. During deliberations, witnesses may be called upon to testify under oath regarding aspects pertinent to the application's merits. All proceedings remain confidential except as required by law or with explicit consent from all parties involved.

The committee renders its decision via majority vote after thorough consideration of written arguments submitted within a stipulated timeframe. Dissenting opinions may accompany final determinations but hold no legal force whatsoever. Approved applications are notified in writing along with conditions precedent to activation, if any exist. Rejected requests receive formal denial citing specific deficiencies found during evaluation. Appeals must be lodged within fourteen days of notification using the prescribed procedure outlined herein.

All permits granted hereunder expire automatically after one calendar year unless renewed pursuant to these provisions. Renewal applicants bear the burden of demonstrating continued compliance with all applicable laws and regulations governing their activities. Late filings incur additional fees calculated at double the original rate plus administrative penalties as determined by the Desk's discretion. Permits operating beyond their expiration date are void ab initio, rendering any actions taken thereunder invalid and subject to punitive sanctions under § 500.1 et seq.

The Guild reserves absolute authority to revoke or suspend permits at will upon demonstration of cause supported by competent evidence. Notice thereof shall be delivered personally or via certified mail return receipt requested. Affected parties retain the right to contest such actions through established adjudicative channels but must post bond equivalent to potential damages pending resolution. Uncontested revocations take effect immediately without further notice whatsoever. Any attempts to operate under nullified permits constitute contempt of court and invite severe reprisals accordingly.

In witness whereof, the seal of the Autumnwood Accords is affixed hereto this day in accordance with due process requirements set forth above. Let all concerned take heed lest they tread where none dare venture without proper authorization secured first! 📜✨⚖️"

body.heading: § 400.1 Research Permits — Authorization Protocols — Continued
body.text:
All applications for research permits must be submitted in triplicate on standard Guild forms, accompanied by payment of the requisite fee as set forth annually by the Accords Desk. The application shall include a detailed description of the proposed study, the intended methods of investigation, and an assessment of potential risks to persons or property. A sworn statement from the applicant affirming their competence to conduct the research safely must also be attached.

Upon receipt, the application will be reviewed by two independent magi appointed by the Desk. These reviewers shall have no financial interest in the outcome of the request. Their evaluation shall consider whether the proposed work aligns with current safety standards and whether adequate safeguards are planned. Any concerns raised during review may result in additional scrutiny or outright denial of the permit.

If approved, a signed authorization certificate will be issued to the principal researcher. This document serves as proof of legal authority to proceed with the stated project under specified conditions. Copies shall be filed in both the applicant's personal records and the central registry maintained by the Guild. Violation of any terms outlined in the certificate may lead to immediate revocation and subsequent penalties.

Permits granted for high-risk studies require enhanced monitoring throughout execution. Designated observers from the Conservators or Aegis Magi may accompany researchers at all times during active experimentation. Their role is strictly supervisory; they shall not interfere with legitimate investigative activities unless safety protocols are breached. Failure to comply with these oversight requirements constitutes grounds for disciplinary action against both the researcher and any negligent supervisors.

In cases where multiple parties seek permits relating to overlapping subject matter, priority shall be determined by date of submission and scope of work approved by the reviewers. The Desk retains discretion to deny competing applications deemed redundant or potentially disruptive. Disputes arising from such determinations will be resolved through established grievance procedures rather than direct confrontation between applicants.

This section is without prejudice to any existing obligations under separate contracts, patents, or trade secrets. Researchers remain fully liable for protecting confidential information obtained during permitted studies. Unauthorized disclosure of proprietary data may result in civil liability independent of any criminal penalties imposed by this Code. All parties are advised to consult legal counsel regarding specific rights and responsibilities arising from their participation in regulated research programs.

See also § 200.5 Guest Casters; § 300.1 Schedules of Arts; § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs under related provisions governing controlled magical practice. Under § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks, certain administrative tasks may be delegated to qualified assistants under strict supervision. As noted in § 1.7 Construction, ambiguous terms shall be construed narrowly against the drafter unless context dictates otherwise. This policy reflects the fundamental principle that extraordinary powers demand exceptional accountability measures.

sections.title: Pocket Dimensions as Labs
sections.brief: Hours inside a pocket are still hours for the other party.

body.heading: Pocket Dimensions as Labs
body.text:
Pursuant to the regulatory framework established by the Autumnwood Accords and the subsequent oversight of the Conservators, all researchers seeking to utilize extra-planar spaces or artificially generated pocket dimensions for the purpose of laboratory experimentation must adhere to the temporal parity standards set forth herein. While the physical laws of a pocket dimension may be significantly altered from those of the Midlands, the temporal flow remains subject to the Guild’s primary oversight regarding labor, duration, and cognitive preservation. Specifically, any research conducted within a pocket dimension, regardless of its internal expansion or spatial distortion, shall be measured against the standard chronometry of the primary plane of existence from which the laboratory originated.

The intent of this provision is to prevent the exploitation of "dilated" time as a means to circumvent the standard duration limits imposed on restricted research permits. Under the authority of Archmage Theron, no researcher may claim that a week of experimentation occurred in a matter of seconds—or vice versa—for the purpose of reporting progress or fulfilling the temporal requirements of a permit. If a researcher enters a pocket dimension that experiences a slower temporal flow, the Guild shall recognize the duration based on the external world's clock. Conversely, if a researcher utilizes a pocket dimension where time accelerates, the Guild shall view the total duration of the experiment as being equal to the time elapsed in the external world. This ensures that the cognitive toll on the practitioner and the potential for catastrophic instability remain within the manageable parameters defined by the Conservators.

Furthermore, all logistical requirements, including the consumption of resources, the degradation of reagents, and the expiration of temporary mouths, shall be calculated based on the external time. Should a researcher be trapped or detained within a pocket dimension, the Guild’s rescue protocols shall initiate based on the external duration of the disappearance. All laboratory equipment, regardless of its location in a pocket dimension, remains subject to the maintenance schedules of the Guild. See § 1.6 for relevant definitions of "Pocket Dimension" and "Primary Plane." Failure to maintain temporal parity during research shall result in the immediate revocation of the researcher's permit and a referral to the Aegis Magi for a formal audit of the laboratory's stability.

body.heading: Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes a strict prohibition against the use of time-stop magic or any temporal stasis effects as a means of stalling, extending, or manipulating legal settlements, debt repayments, or the fulfillment of guild-mandated duties. In any instance where a mage is engaged in a legal proceeding, a debt negotiation, or a contractual dispute, the application of time-stop magic shall not be recognized as a pause in the proceedings. For the purposes of the Accords, time-stop during a settlement is still considered active time. Any party attempting to utilize such magic to "freeze" a situation to their advantage shall be deemed in violation of the Guild's integrity protocols.

The principle of "Interest in Time" dictates that if a mage uses magic to halt the flow of time for others while they proceed with a specific action—be it the completion of a task, the movement of goods, or the negotiation of a contract—the Guild shall treat the duration of the stasis as active time for the purpose of all calculations. This includes, but is not limited to, the expiration of deadlines, the accrual of interest on debts, and the expiration of temporary licenses. If a mage spends what they perceive as one hour in a time-stopped state to complete a task, the Guild shall record that hour as having elapsed in the standard flow of the Midlands. No "borrowed" time shall be granted to the practitioner; the magic used to halt the world does not grant the user a reprieve from the responsibilities of the world.

Furthermore, any attempt to use time-stop magic to evade the consequences of a Paradox Trial shall be met with the highest tier of sanction. The use of such magic to delay the arrival of an Aegis Magi enforcement team or to stall a peer review shall be considered an aggravating factor in the determination of guilt. All mages are reminded that while the mastery of time is a sophisticated pursuit, it does not exempt the practitioner from the temporal obligations of the Autumnwood Accords. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Temporal Stasis" and "Settlement."

body.heading: Specimen Custody
body.text:
All biological or inorganic entities of significant size, complexity, or magical potency that are captured, restrained, or petrified by a practitioner shall be classified as "Inventory" under the Guild’s custody regulations. This classification holds until such time as the specimen is officially released, destroyed, or permanently integrated into a controlled environment. No specimen, regardless of its current state of animation or petrification, shall be considered a "Trophy" or a "Personal Possession" for the purposes of Guild transport or public display until the proper documentation of release or destruction is filed with the Desk.

A petrified monster, for instance, remains a hazardous specimen under the jurisdiction of the Conservators. Because a petrified entity retains the potential for sudden reanimation or magical resonance, it must be handled with the same safety protocols as a living creature. Practitioners are prohibited from transporting such specimens across the Midlands without a certified containment vessel and a valid transport permit. The classification as "Inventory" ensures that the Guild maintains a record of all hazardous materials in circulation, preventing the clandestine movement of dangerous entities by rogue mages or radical Innovators.

The transition from "Inventory" to "Trophy" may only occur upon the formal "Decommissioning of Threat" by a certified Aegis Mage or the "Sanctioned Release" by a Conservator. Until such a certification is issued, the practitioner is responsible for the maintenance, containment, and safety of the specimen. Any loss of a specimen while it is still classified as Inventory shall be treated as a breach of safety protocol, potentially resulting in a Paradox Trial. Furthermore, the possession of such specimens in private residences or unauthorized laboratories is strictly forbidden under the research restrictions of the Innovators. See § 400.1 for research permit requirements.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The Guild hereby clarifies the distinction between "Controlled Research" and "Unauthorized Field Use" regarding the growth of large-scale magical structures or entities. Any instance of growth magic—including the rapid expansion of flora, the scaling of architectural constructs, or the somatic growth of biological entities—that occurs within a public street, marketplace, or any other non-sanctioned public space shall be automatically classified as "Unauthorized Field Use." This classification remains final and absolute, regardless of whether the practitioner claims the growth was a byproduct of an accident or if the practitioner intends to study the results of said growth at a later date.

The Innovators may argue that such growth provides a unique opportunity for observation and data collection; however, the Conservators maintain that the risks to public safety and structural integrity in the Midlands outweigh the benefits of such field experiments. Because the growth occurs in a public sphere, it is subject to immediate intervention by the Aegis Magi. The fact that a mage may later seek to study the growth in a laboratory does not retroactively grant the initial growth "Research" status. To be classified as research, the growth must occur within a licensed laboratory or a designated "Wilderness Study Zone" with a pre-approved permit from Janna Brightspark’s office.

Any mage found to be responsible for unauthorized titan growth in a public area shall be subject to immediate fines and a mandatory review of their licensing. If the growth poses an immediate threat to life or property, the Aegis Magi are authorized to use whatever force is necessary to neutralize the growth, with the practitioner being held liable for all damages. This law serves to protect the infrastructure of the Autumnwood Accords from the reckless expansionism often associated with radical innovation. See § 200.1 for licensure requirements and § 400.1 for research permits.

body.heading: § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Laboratories and Time Interest
body.text:
It is hereby declared that pocket dimensions, when utilized for lawful research or storage purposes under permit, constitute temporary laboratories within the meaning of the Accords. All temporal measurements taken within such spaces shall be accorded full legal effect outside thereof. This ensures equitable treatment between researcher and subject regardless of spatial displacement. See also § 400.3 regarding borrowed hours and interest therein.

Specimens held in pocket containment retain their natural properties and must be treated with appropriate care during extraction. Any alteration resulting from prolonged sequestration constitutes unauthorized modification under § 200.4. Researchers bear sole responsibility for safe return or destruction of materials post-study. Failure to comply shall result in permit revocation and potential sanctions. Refer to § 500.5 regarding undue influence through specimen manipulation.

Unauthorized expansion of pocket capacity beyond permitted limits is strictly prohibited. Such activity violates core safety protocols established by the Conservators. Penalties include immediate seizure of equipment, suspension of privileges, and possible criminal charges under Article III. Exceptions may be granted only upon formal application demonstrating compelling scientific merit. See § 100.6 for delegation procedures concerning technical specifications.

The Guild reserves right to audit any facility employing dimensional storage techniques at reasonable intervals. Non-compliance with inspection mandates will incur escalating fines and loss of standing within the magical community. Refusal to submit to oversight renders all subsequent operations void ab initio. This provision exists solely to maintain public safety while enabling legitimate research pursuits. Under § 300.1, all such activities require prior approval from the Aegis Magi.

In conclusion, § 400.2 balances scientific advancement with necessary safeguards against abuse of powerful technologies. By clearly defining temporal equivalence and specimen integrity requirements, the Accords promote responsible innovation while protecting societal interests. All parties are urged to familiarize themselves thoroughly with these obligations before undertaking any work involving pocket dimensions or related phenomena. Negligence in this regard may lead to severe consequences under existing law. Consult § 500.2 for further guidance on weather-related contingencies affecting experimental outcomes.

body.heading: § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Laboratories and Time Interest — Continued
body.text:
A pocket dimension, when invoked for the purpose of research or experimentation, shall be deemed an extension of the caster's own laboratory space. Any temporal effects occurring within such a realm—including but not limited to accelerated aging, rapid decay, or localized time dilation—shall accrue directly against the casting entity unless expressly waived in advance by written agreement. This provision applies regardless of whether the pocket dimension is maintained through conventional magical means or illicit artifacts.

The conservation and protection of specimens extracted from pocket dimensions falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Conservators. Unauthorized possession, modification, or dissemination of such materials constitutes a Class A felony punishable by permanent sealing of magical abilities. Violation of these custodial mandates may result in immediate arrest and trial before the High Council on charges of endangerment to public safety.

Unauthorized expansion of pocket dimensions beyond agreed-upon parameters is strictly prohibited and shall be treated as an act of aggression against all other casters. Such actions require prior approval from both the Innovators' Research Committee and the Conservatory Oversight Board. Failure to obtain such permission renders any subsequent use of the expanded capacity void ab initio, leaving the user fully liable for all resulting damages and consequences.

The interests of third parties whose time and lives may be affected by pocket dimension usage shall always take precedence over academic curiosity or personal gain. In cases where conflicting claims arise regarding temporal allocation within a shared magical space, the matter shall be adjudicated according to established precedents set forth in Part 700 of this Codex. Until such guidelines are promulgated, all casters are directed to exercise utmost prudence and restraint when operating within communal realms.

This section supersedes any prior understandings or informal arrangements concerning pocket dimension usage that may exist between individual practitioners or organizations. Any disputes arising from non-compliance with these provisions shall be resolved through binding arbitration by a panel of three impartial mages appointed by the Archmage Sovereign, whose decision shall be final and enforceable throughout all member territories.

The provisions herein are intended to safeguard both the integrity of magical research and the broader well-being of society at large. By establishing clear boundaries for acceptable conduct within pocket dimensions, the Guild aims to foster an environment where innovation can flourish safely and responsibly under careful supervision. All members are urged to acquaint themselves thoroughly with these guidelines and adhere strictly thereto in all their dealings.

sections.title: Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
sections.brief: Time-stop during settlement is still time.

body.heading: Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching tenets of the Autumnwood Accords, specifically regarding the temporal stability of the Midlands, any mage who employs chronomancy or time-dilation effects during the duration of a legal settlement, a debt negotiation, or a formal mediation process shall be held to the standard of continuous temporal progression. It is hereby codified that the suspension of the flow of time for the purpose of deliberation, contemplation, or the cooling oftempers does not constitute a cessation of the legal clock. For the purposes of the Guild, time-stop during settlement is still time. If a party to a dispute invokes a chronomantic stasis to prolong a negotiation, the interest accrued on any outstanding magical debts or temporal reparations shall continue to calculate at the standard rate prescribed by Archmage Veyra.

The Innovators may argue that a frozen moment is a vacuum of progression, yet the Conservators maintain that the intent of the mage is the primary driver of the Accord's jurisdiction. Therefore, any attempt to utilize "Borrowed Hours" to evade the consequences of a delayed agreement shall be viewed as a bad-faith manipulation of the arcane weave. Mages seeking to enter a period of stasis for the purpose of intensive study or meditation must first secure a research permit under § 400.1, and even such permits do not exempt the individual from the temporal taxes of the Guild. Any mage found attempting to "pause" the legalities of a contract while continuing to benefit from the status quo of that contract shall be subject to a Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, the Aegis Magi are authorized to impose a "Temporal Interest Penalty" on any individual who purposefully creates a localized time-stop to prevent the expiration of a temporary mouth or a provisional license. The Guild recognizes that time is a sacred resource, and its artificial manipulation for the sake of administrative evasion is a violation of Mana Reverence. See § 1.6 for definitions regarding temporal flux and magical debt. Any disputes arising from the calculation of interest during a period of suspended animation shall be adjudicated by the Desk, with the Archmage Sovereign holding final authority on the determination of "active" versus "passive" temporal states.

body.heading: Specimen Custody
body.text:
The possession and transport of biological entities, whether living, dormant, or petrified, are governed by strict protocols to ensure the preservation of the Midlands' ecological and magical integrity. Under the Accords, any creature of significant magical potency or size that has been rendered into a state of petrification, stasis, or permanent slumber is strictly classified as inventory, not a trophy. This classification remains in effect regardless of the owner's intent, the aesthetic value of the specimen, or the degree of martial prowess required to achieve the petrification. A petrified monster is inventory, not a trophy, until released.

Owners of such specimens are required to register the entity with the nearest Guild outpost within three lunar cycles of acquisition. This registration serves as a manifest of the specimen's origin, its current state of stasis, and the specific seals used to maintain its condition. The failure to register a petrified specimen constitutes a violation of the research safety protocols outlined in § 400.1. Furthermore, the transport of such inventory across provincial lines requires a verified transport manifest; if a specimen is seized by the Aegis Magi without proper documentation, it shall be impounded as unauthorized material and may be subject to immediate destruction if it poses a risk to the public.

The distinction between inventory and trophy is critical for the purposes of the Paradox Trial. A mage who displays a petrified creature as a mark of personal achievement in a public forum may be cited for "Ostentatious Display of Forbidden Stasis," especially if the creature belongs to a species protected by the Conservators. Conversely, a mage who treats a petrified entity as a mere object of trade without proper licensing may be charged with "Negligent Handling of High-Potency Remains." No specimen may be "released"—whether through the reversal of a petrification spell or the termination of a stasis field—without a formal release permit issued by the Desk. See § 1.6 for further clarification on the definition of "High-Potency Remains."

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the manifestation of large-scale, rapid-growth magic in non-designated zones. Any instance of growth magic utilized within a public thoroughfare, residential district, or any area not specifically zoned for agricultural or botanical experimentation is strictly classified as unauthorized field use. This classification is absolute and pertains to the act of manifestation itself, rather than the subsequent academic pursuit of the perpetrator. Growth magic in a street is field use, not research, even if someone later studies it.

The Innovators frequently advocate for the "experimental freedom" of the arts, yet the Accord dictates that the safety of the populace overrides the curiosity of the individual. If a mage utilizes growth charms to manifest flora, structures, or biological masses in a street, the resulting infrastructure is considered a public hazard. Even if the practitioner subsequently submits a retrospective request for research credit or seeks to categorize the growth as a "controlled experiment," the Guild shall not grant such status retroactively. The act of casting in a public space bypasses the protections and privileges afforded by § 400.1, and the practitioner shall be liable for all damages and the costs of removal as determined by the Aegis Magi.

Furthermore, any growth that results in the obstruction of trade routes, the damage to Goodstyle Artisan products, or the endangerment of common travelers will result in immediate summary judgment. The Guild does not recognize "unintentional growth" as a valid defense if the mage failed to consult the local cartography or the one-T cartography for land-use restrictions. Because the growth occurs in a public domain, the legal status of the magic is "Field Use," which carries a higher penalty of sanction and seal than "Restricted Research." Any mage found in violation of this clause may be required to undergo a Paradox Trial to determine the extent of their negligence. See § 1.6 for the distinction between "Field Use" and "Restricted Research."

body.heading: § 400.4 Specimen Custody and Unauthorized Expansion
body.text:
The possession, transport, or storage of any specimen classified as Tier I+ requires an active Research Permit issued by the Mages' Guild Desk. Any failure to maintain proper custody shall be deemed a violation of § 200.1 Licensure Required. In addition, all specimens must remain under direct supervision of a licensed Arcanist at all times; unattended specimens are subject to immediate seizure and destruction without notice or compensation to the owner.

Any specimen that expands beyond its designated containment parameters shall be considered "Unauthorized Titan Growth" under § 400.5. Such growth is strictly prohibited and constitutes a Class A violation punishable by forfeiture of the specimen and fines up to one hundred gold pieces per percent of excess mass. The owner or custodian of the specimen shall bear full responsibility for any damages resulting from Unauthorized Titan Growth, including but not limited to structural damage, ecological disruption, and personal injury.

Furthermore, all specimens must be kept in a secure facility approved by the Guild, with access restricted solely to licensed personnel. Any attempt to remove a specimen from its designated location without explicit written permission shall result in immediate revocation of the Research Permit and potential criminal charges under § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting. The Mages' Guild reserves the right to inspect any facility holding specimens at any time, with or without notice, and to seize any suspected contraband for analysis.

Violations of this section shall be prosecuted aggressively by the Aegis Magi and other enforcement officials. Repeat offenders may face permanent disqualification from all research activities and expulsion from the Guild. The Desk shall maintain a detailed log of all specimen movements and conditions to ensure full compliance with these regulations at all times. Failure to adhere to § 400.4 Specimen Custody and Unauthorized Expansion is grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of any relevant permits or licenses held by the offending party.

Under § 1.9 Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal, any unauthorized alteration or tampering with specimen containment vessels shall be treated as desecration of sacred relics and punished accordingly. Additionally, per § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts, certain types of specimens may contain residual magical energies capable of affecting nearby casters. Caution must be exercised when handling such items to avoid unintended consequences. Consult with a qualified Arcanist before attempting any manipulation or study of these volatile substances without proper authorization.

body.heading: § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
body.text:
Under this Article, "Borrowed Hours" refers to the temporary suspension or dilation of temporal flow within a localized area, effectuated through ritual or magical means. Such an alteration of natural time does not negate the passage of actual minutes, nor does it exempt participants from their contractual obligations accrued prior to the onset of the phenomenon. The Guild maintains that all casters remain fully liable for damages sustained during periods of distorted chronometry, as such effects are deemed an inherent risk of practice rather than a force majeure event.

Where "Interest in Time" is concerned, any unauthorized accumulation of temporal debt incurred by a caster shall be adjudicated under the provisions governing delinquent fees and penalties. The accruing interest rate on overdue payments shall increase proportionally to the duration of the time distortion, calculated according to standard actuarial tables adjusted for magical variance. Failure to remit said obligations within thirty days of notification may result in immediate suspension of licensure until full restitution is made.

Closely related to these provisions is the issue of "Specimen Custody," which mandates that all materials used in conjuring Borrowed Hours must be secured and returned post-event, subject to inspection by Guild inspectors. Any loss or damage to said items shall be compensated at fair market value plus a punitive surcharge equivalent to one hundred percent of the original cost. This policy exists to prevent rogue practitioners from hoarding volatile components for potential misuse in future incidents.

Finally, any "Unauthorized Expansion" resulting directly from improper application of time-altering techniques shall be treated as a serious violation of the Accords. Such acts may lead to revocation of licensure and referral to disciplinary proceedings under the Paradox Trial system. The Guild emphasizes that responsible stewardship of temporal forces requires not only technical proficiency but also ethical foresight, ensuring that no single individual or entity gains undue advantage through manipulation of reality itself.

body.heading: § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time — Continued
body.text:
A caster who pauses the flow of magic for any reason, whether to consult notes or simply admire their own handiwork, incurs a penalty known as 'Borrowed Hours.' Each moment spent outside active casting reduces the total duration available by one minute, regardless of whether the clock has ticked forward. This rule prevents mages from artificially inflating their output through dilatory tactics.

Interest in Time applies when a spell's effects outlast its initial incantation. A fireball may burn for seconds after being launched, but that lingering heat counts as additional casting time. Similarly, a healing ward may activate later if triggered by an external event, extending the original expenditure of magical hours. The Desk assesses interest based on observable consequences rather than theoretical possibilities.

Specimen Custody mandates safekeeping of volatile materials until their purpose is fulfilled. A potion-brewer must secure her ingredients against theft or accidental exposure; failure to do so results in forfeiture of any remaining value. This obligation persists even after the contract concludes, for a rogue reagent could destabilize an entire batch of finished goods.

Unauthorized Titan Growth refers to spontaneous increases in spell potency beyond what was contracted. While welcome bonuses, they still draw from the caster's allocated hours. If a healing ritual unexpectedly restores more health than agreed upon, that surplus counts against the original allotment. The Desk discourages such windfalls as inherently unfair to the client who paid for specific results.

§ 400.3 further clarifies that time stops only when casting is truly suspended—not merely interrupted by minor distractions. A mage distracted by a sudden noise must resume from where they left off, not from the beginning of the spell. This provision preserves the integrity of contracted services while acknowledging reality's chaotic nature.

Ultimately, these rules exist to ensure predictability and fairness in magical commerce. By standardizing how time is measured and allocated, the Guild protects both casters and clients from exploitation or misunderstanding. The Desk remains vigilant against any attempts to circumvent these principles for personal gain.

sections.title: Specimen Custody
sections.brief: A petrified monster is inventory, not a trophy, until released.

body.heading: Specimen Custody
body.text:
Pursuant to the oversight of the Autumnwood Accords, all biological or semi-biological entities that have undergone petrification, stasis, or arcane crystallization shall be classified as Guild Inventory rather than personal trophies, spoils of war, or decorative acquisitions. This classification applies to any creature, beast, or sentient being rendered immobile by high-level transmutation or temporal suspension. The Accords Desk asserts that the inherent potential for animation within a petrified specimen constitutes a lingering arcane signature that must be accounted for within the Guild's safety protocols. Any mage who secures such a specimen is strictly prohibited from displaying it in public spaces, taverns, or non-sanctioned residences without a verified containment permit issued by the Conservators.

The distinction between inventory and trophy is a legal necessity to prevent the misappropriation of hazardous magical assets. A trophy is a static object of personal vanity; a petrified monster is a dormant hazard capable of sudden, uncontrolled restoration or violent expiration. Should a specimen be released from its state of stasis—whether by intent, accident, or environmental decay—the responsibility for its containment shifts from passive inventory to active containment. Any mage found in possession of a released specimen that has not been properly neutralized or bound shall be subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi. The Guild maintains that the preservation of the public's safety outweighs the individual's right to own a "curiosity" of such volatile nature.

Furthermore, the transportation of petrified specimens across the Midlands requires a manifest of transit. If a specimen is moved from a private laboratory to a public thoroughfare, it must be accompanied by a clerk or a licensed handler who possesses the knowledge to initiate a "Cold Seal" in the event of a breach. Failure to provide such documentation shall result in the immediate revocation of the owner's Research Permit and a referral to the Paradox Trial for reckless endangerment of the populace. See § 1.6 for definitions regarding "Arcane Signature" and "Cold Seal." All specimens held in private vaults must be reported to the Archmage Veyra’s office biennially for audit.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The application of growth magic within any urban center, village, or public thoroughfare is hereby defined as unauthorized field use, regardless of the caster's stated intent or the eventual academic utility of the results. This provision serves to distinguish between controlled laboratory experimentation and the reckless expansion of magical flora or fauna in civilian spheres. If a mage utilizes growth enchantments to produce oversized produce, decorative greenery, or structural reinforcements in a street or marketplace, the act is automatically classified as a violation of the Accords. The fact that a mage may subsequently attempt to study the resulting growth as part of a research project does not retroactively合法ize the initial casting. The initial act of expansion is the primary offense; the study of the consequence is a separate, and often secondary, matter of record.

The Accords Desk recognizes the Innovators' desire to push the boundaries of botanical and structural transmutation. However, the Conservators maintain that the unpredictable nature of "Titan Growth" poses an unacceptable risk to the structural integrity of the Midlands. Growth magic of this magnitude can cause unintended structural collapse, the choking of water supplies, or the creation of ecological dead zones. Therefore, any mage seeking to experiment with growth magnitudes exceeding standard horticultural limits must do so within a designated research zone or a pocket dimension as authorized under § 400.2. The use of such magic in a street is a breach of the public peace and an affront to the stability of the Accord.

Mages who engage in unauthorized field growth are liable for all costs associated with the removal of the growth and the restoration of the affected area. If the growth results in property damage or the endangerment of life, the caster shall be summoned before a council of peers for a Paradox Trial. The penalty for such violations may range from the Sanction and Seal of the caster's growth-related schools to the full sequestration of their research materials. See § 1.6 for further clarification on the "Midlands Public Thoroughfare" boundaries. No "Wario Coin" or other non-tender currency shall be accepted as restitution for damages caused by unauthorized growth. All restitution must be paid in standard Guild-approved currency or through labor-service to the Goodstyle Artisans for reconstruction.

body.heading: § 400.4 Specimen Custody; Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The Guild's exclusive right to collect, store, and study magical artifacts extends to all specimens under its lawful control, whether seized during inspections or surrendered by licensees upon expiry of their permits. Specimens shall be maintained in secure facilities equipped with climate-controlled environments, containment wards, and monitoring sensors to prevent accidental activation or contamination of adjacent areas. Unauthorized possession, transfer, or modification of Guild property constitutes a serious violation subject to immediate suspension and potential revocation of licensure.

In the event that any specimen begins to undergo spontaneous metamorphosis or exhibits anomalous growth patterns inconsistent with known biological processes, all personnel must cease operations immediately and report findings to their direct supervisor. The affected area shall be evacuated except for designated safety officers equipped with appropriate protective gear and countermeasures. Under no circumstances shall an individual attempt to contain or neutralize a growing anomaly without explicit authorization from the Desk's Safety Division; unauthorized intervention may result in catastrophic escalation of the situation and severe personal injury or death.

Should an artifact escape containment or suffer structural failure resulting in release of hazardous energies, affected parties must initiate emergency protocols outlined in Appendix D without delay. This includes sealing off impacted zones with magical barriers, summoning specialized cleanup crews trained in biohazard mitigation, and conducting thorough decontamination procedures to neutralize lingering residues. Failure to comply with these obligations may expose the responsible party to civil liability for damages incurred by third parties, as well as criminal charges under applicable statutes regulating dangerous substances and materials.

The Guild reserves the right to inspect any premises licensed for magical research at reasonable times and frequencies deemed necessary to ensure compliance with safety standards and regulatory requirements. Inspectors shall be accompanied by a representative of the host organization during all examinations unless otherwise directed by law or exigent circumstances. Findings of violations will be documented in writing and communicated promptly to the concerned entity, which shall then have an opportunity to respond before any punitive measures are imposed. Repeated noncompliance may lead to termination of the license and referral for disciplinary action as warranted under the Accords.

It is hereby declared that all specimens collected or held by the Guild fall within its proprietary interest and shall be protected accordingly against theft, destruction, or misuse by unauthorized persons. Any individual found in possession of such items without proper documentation may be subject to seizure proceedings initiated by the Enforcement Corps acting on behalf of the organization. Penalties for unlawful acquisition range from fines proportional to market value up to imprisonment for repeat offenders, depending upon severity and intent established during adjudication.

body.heading: § 400.4 Specimen Custody and Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The lawful possession of any specimen, whether captured in the wild or synthesized in a laboratory, shall be conducted only under strict supervision by a licensed caster or their duly appointed proxy. No individual, regardless of rank or status, shall take matters into their own hands without explicit authorization from the Mages' Guild Desk. This prohibition extends to all forms of acquisition, including but not limited to hunting, mining, harvesting, and theft.

The unauthorized cultivation or enhancement of a specimen's mass beyond its natural limits, known as "Titan Growth," is strictly forbidden unless conducted pursuant to a valid research permit issued under § 400.1. Any individual found guilty of engaging in illicit Titan Growth shall be subject to immediate revocation of their license and potential criminal prosecution for magical misuse. Furthermore, all specimens must be maintained in secure storage facilities approved by the Guild, with regular inspections to ensure compliance with safety protocols. Failure to adhere to these requirements may result in severe penalties, including fines, suspension, or permanent disqualification from practice.

The Mages' Guild reserves the right to inspect any premises suspected of harboring unauthorized specimens or engaged in illicit Titan Growth activities upon reasonable suspicion. Such inspections shall be conducted by duly appointed conservators or their agents, who shall have full authority to seize evidence and question individuals involved. Resistance to lawful inspection may be construed as an admission of guilt and subject to enhanced sanctions under applicable penal provisions.

All citizens are hereby put on notice that ignorance of the law shall not serve as a defense against accusations of violating specimen custody statutes. The Guild urges all practitioners to familiarize themselves with these regulations and seek clarification from official channels should any uncertainties arise. By adhering strictly to established protocols, we safeguard both ourselves and the greater community from the dangers posed by unchecked magical experimentation.

Let it be known that the Autumnwood Accords stand as a bulwark against chaos and excess. Within their bounds lies freedom for those willing to play by the rules. Without them, we descend into barbarism, each seeking power at another's expense. Choose wisely: you may find yourselves on opposite sides of an irreconcilable divide before long. Act now while there is still time to make amends and secure your future under this code. For in upholding these laws lies the strength to build a better world for all.

body.heading: § 400.4 Specimen Custody and Unauthorized Titan Growth — Continued
body.text:
No person shall knowingly possess, transport, or display any specimen derived from a controlled entity without prior authorization from the Conservators' Bureau of Biosecurity. Violation constitutes possession of contraband under § 215.3(a). Furthermore, no mage shall intentionally accelerate the growth rate of such specimens beyond natural limits, whether through direct magical intervention or indirect manipulation of environmental conditions. Such acts are deemed reckless endangerment and may result in revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4(b).

Specimens acquired legally by a licensed caster retain status as controlled property even after release from the original containment unit. The owner must maintain adequate security measures proportional to the specimen's inherent danger level, failing which it shall be seized upon discovery by any sworn peace officer or Guild Inspector. Failure to comply with these storage mandates may lead to forfeiture of the item and additional penalties under § 320.6.

In cases where a specimen escapes containment due to no fault of its owner, immediate reporting is required within one hour via emergency channel 9-1-1-MAGI. The owner shall cooperate fully in efforts to locate and recapture the loose asset. Prompt disclosure may mitigate fines but does not absolve liability for any damages incurred during the escape interval. Deliberate concealment of an escaped specimen doubles all applicable penalties under § 216.7.

Unauthorized modification of a specimen's genetic makeup or magical constitution is strictly prohibited absent written permission from both the original owner and the Conservators' Research Division. Such tampering may render the specimen unpredictable and highly hazardous to surrounding populations. Any resulting injuries or property losses shall be borne solely by the responsible party, regardless of good faith intent. This restriction applies equally to hybrid specimens created through cross-breeding techniques permitted under § 405.2.

It is hereby declared that any attempt to weaponize a controlled specimen for personal gain, whether through direct combat use or deployment as an improvised explosive device, shall be prosecuted as a Class A Felony and subject to immediate termination of licensure without appeal. Repeat offenders face permanent disqualification from the practice of magic within this jurisdiction. Such actions represent not merely a breach of contractual obligation but a fundamental threat to public safety warranting the most severe sanctions available under existing law.

This provision serves to balance the legitimate interests of researchers and collectors with the paramount need to protect society from potential misuse of dangerous entities. By establishing clear boundaries for specimen handling and modification, these regulations aim to prevent catastrophic accidents while preserving opportunities for beneficial study. All casters are reminded that their privileges carry corresponding responsibilities, particularly when dealing with materials capable of causing irreparable harm if mishandled. Adherence to these guidelines ensures continued safe operation of the magical community within our borders.

body.heading: Specimen Custody and Unauthorized Titan Growth — Continued
body.text:
Specimens acquired in lawful research contexts shall remain under the exclusive custody of the granting Permittee until such time as they are returned to their natural state or otherwise disposed of pursuant to this Code. No researcher, whether licensed or otherwise, shall retain specimens for personal gain, display, or resale without express written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign. Violation of this provision constitutes a Class C infraction subject to sanctions up to and including permit revocation and imprisonment at the discretion of the Paradox Trial Council.

Unauthorized Titan Growth refers to any spontaneous magical manifestation not directly attributable to permitted experimental procedures. Such phenomena shall be immediately reported to Guild oversight within one solar cycle or face automatic forfeiture of all research permits held by the responsible party. Failure to report may indicate malicious intent and trigger an immediate investigation under § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items. Penalties for unauthorized growth range from monetary fines proportional to market value of affected materials to permanent exile from Guild circles depending on severity and frequency.

The burden of proof regarding lawful acquisition versus illicit possession rests solely upon the accused researcher who asserts innocence. In cases where provenance cannot be conclusively established, conservative measures shall prevail: seizure of suspect specimens pending further analysis by certified Aegis Magi.
