Costs associated with such examinations are borne equally between the Guild and the individual subject to dispute resolution through standard arbitration channels outlined in § 100.4 Records of Speech.

Researchers maintaining private collections outside official facilities must adhere strictly to inventory logs detailing each item's origin, purpose, current condition, and planned disposition timeline. Quarterly audits conducted by random selection of peer reviewers will verify compliance with storage protocols designed to mitigate risk of accidental release or contamination spread. Deviations discovered during routine inspections warrant disciplinary action commensurate with the nature of infractions found alongside potential remediation requirements imposed upon offending parties.

This section remains subject to periodic revision as scientific understanding evolves and new challenges emerge from frontier exploration endeavors undertaken by dedicated scholars throughout our realm at large. Future amendments will be made only after thorough consideration given input gathered via formal petition processes open annually during designated public notice periods announced well in advance through official publications distributed widely across affected regions worldwide for maximum transparency accountability purposes served best by robust regulatory frameworks ensuring safety security prosperity all around us always!

sections.title: Unauthorized Titan Growth
sections.brief: Growth magic in a street is field use, not research, even if someone later studies it.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes a strict distinction between sanctioned laboratory growth and unauthorized field application of expansionary arcana. Pursuant to the primary mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, all magical research conducted under the auspices of the Innovators must be confined to designated research zones, such as those permitted under § 400.2. Any application of growth magic that occurs within a public thoroughfare, residential district, or any non-sanctioned geographical coordinate shall be automatically classified as field use. This classification remains immutable regardless of the caster's stated intent, academic justification, or the subsequent analytical study of the resulting growth. The Guild recognizes that the volatility of expansionary magic is compounded by the proximity of civilian infrastructure and public transit; therefore, the mere act of manifesting such growth in a street environment constitutes a breach of the safety protocols governing the use of the Unsanctioned Arts.

Specifically, the Guild shall not entertain any defense claiming that the growth of a Titan-class entity or any related biological expansion was intended as a preliminary experiment for future scholarly review. If the growth occurs in a public street, it is, by definition, a field operation. The fact that a mage may later seek to study the biological properties, structural integrity, or magical residue of said growth does not retroactively transform the initial casting into a protected research activity. See § 400.1 for the requirements of research permits, which explicitly exclude any actions resulting in uncontrolled environmental expansion. Any mage found to have initiated growth magic in an unauthorized area shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi to determine the extent of the structural damage and the risk posed to the surrounding populace.

Furthermore, the Guild notes specific precedents involving unauthorized field use on the Markop region. Any growth magic utilized on Markop that results in Titan-scale expansion is deemed a violation of the Accords' stability requirements as championed by the Conservators. Such incidents shall be recorded as unauthorized field use and shall not be eligible for the protections afforded to the Innovators' restricted research permits. The Guild shall treat all such instances as reckless endangerment of the Midlands' magical equilibrium. Any mage involved in such growth shall be referred to the council for the Paradox Trial, wherein the punishment may include the sealing of the mage's arcana or permanent relocation to a pocket-prison to ensure the continued stability of the public sphere.

In cases where a mage claims that the growth was a byproduct of a different, sanctioned spell, the burden of proof lies with the caster to demonstrate that the growth was neither intended nor foreseeable. However, the Guild maintains a policy of strict liability for expansionary magic; if the growth occurs in a street, the caster is held responsible for the entirety of the resulting ecological and structural consequences. No provision exists within this Codex to excuse growth magic based on the "necessity" of the expansion or the "scientific value" of the Titan. For further clarification on the distinction between research and field use, see § 400.1 and § 400.2. All growth magic conducted without a specific permit for the specific location shall be prosecuted under the most severe penalties available to the Aegis Magi.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications — Continued
body.text: The Accords strictly prohibit the unauthorized cultivation or expansion of titans outside sanctioned research environments, recognizing such acts as inherently dangerous to public safety and magical equilibrium. Any individual found engaging in illegal titan growth shall be subject to immediate arrest by Aegis Magi for violation of § 400.5, with penalties escalating based on the scale of disruption caused. This includes but is not limited to property damage, interference with emergency services, and potential loss of life from uncontrolled magical reactions. The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to demonstrate beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant knowingly participated in prohibited growth activities. Furthermore, possession of materials specifically designed for titan expansion may constitute constructive possession under § 102(34), subjecting owners to similar sanctions regardless of direct involvement in cultivation efforts. Law enforcement officers are empowered to seize suspected contraband and detain suspects pending further investigation without warrant upon reasonable suspicion. The Accords mandate that all titans remain contained within approved facilities unless expressly permitted by the Conservators under tightly controlled conditions. Violations will be prosecuted aggressively, with repeat offenders facing permanent disqualification from magical practice and possible imprisonment. Public safety remains paramount, necessitating strict enforcement of these prohibitions to prevent catastrophic incidents stemming from reckless manipulation of powerful arcane entities. Any disputes regarding the classification of growth activities shall be adjudicated by a specially convened panel of magistrates versed in both legal and technical matters pertaining to titan cultivation. The Accords reserve the right to amend this section as new evidence emerges or circumstances warrant, ensuring continued protection for all citizens against foreseeable harms posed by unregulated titan expansion operations. § 400.5 shall be construed liberally to encompass any form of illicit titan manipulation, whether intentional, negligent, or reckless, reflecting the gravity of potential consequences inherent in such forbidden practices.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications — Continued — Continued
body.text: § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth constitutes field use regardless of subsequent intent to study the growth, as it involves the active application of magic in a non-laboratory setting with potential effects on persons or property. See § 200.1 (Licensure Required) and § 300.1 (Schedules of Arts). The mere act of causing a Titan to grow beyond its natural state without explicit permission from the Guild is an actionable violation, irrespective of whether the caster later claims educational purposes. This principle ensures that casual or experimental casting cannot be shielded by post-hoc justification. Unauthorized growth also encompasses any manipulation of magical fields that results in anomalous physical changes, such as spontaneous enlargement or distortion of organic matter. Under § 400.2 (Pocket Dimensions as Labs), true research requires containment within approved facilities designed to mitigate risks. Street-level magic lacks these safeguards and thus falls under penal provisions rather than scholarly inquiry. The burden of proof rests with the accused to demonstrate that their actions did not constitute unauthorized field use, a high standard given the inherent dangers of unchecked growth magic. Violations may include fines, license revocation, or imprisonment depending on severity and impact on public safety. See § 100.2 (Who May Speak for the Guild) regarding enforcement authority and § 300.4 (Reclassification) for potential adjustments to affected magical categories based on new precedents. The Desk maintains absolute jurisdiction over all unauthorized growth incidents, reserving discretion to impose additional sanctions as warranted by circumstances. No individual or entity may claim immunity from these provisions without explicit exemption granted in advance by the Guild. This clause serves as a final clarification of boundaries between permissible and impermissible magical practice under any conditions whatsoever.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications — Continued — Administration
body.text:
The classification of unauthorized titan growth as field use rather than research stems from the inherent nature of the act itself. When an archmage invokes growth magic upon a subject outside the controlled environment of their laboratory, they are effectively casting a spell with unpredictable consequences, regardless of any subsequent analysis. The Guild maintains that such actions constitute improper application of arcane power and must be treated as violations under § 200.1 Licensure Required and § 500.1 Field Casting for Value.

This strict interpretation serves to protect the public from potential hazards associated with unregulated magic use. Without proper oversight, unauthorized growth rituals could result in catastrophic failures ranging from minor physical deformities to total annihilation of surrounding areas. The precedent set by recent incidents involving rogue mages growing massive flora across entire neighborhoods underscores the necessity of enforcing these regulations rigorously.

Furthermore, distinguishing between research and field casting is crucial for determining appropriate penalties and remediation efforts. While both activities involve magical practice, their contexts and risks differ significantly. Research conducted under permits adheres to safety protocols designed to mitigate harm, whereas unauthorized growth rituals lack such safeguards entirely. Consequently, the Guild asserts that any unlicensed application of growth magic must be prosecuted as field use violations subject to full penal consequences under § 300.1 Schedules of Arts and related provisions.

This stance applies universally across all instances of unauthorized titan growth, irrespective of intent or outcome. Whether aimed at cultivating rare herbs or expanding territorial borders, such acts remain firmly within the realm of prohibited field casting unless explicitly sanctioned through proper channels. The Guild remains unwavering in its commitment to maintaining order and safety in accordance with the Autumnwood Accords.

see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value; see § 300.1 Schedules of Arts

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications - Continued — Administra
body.text:
The classification of unauthorized titan growth as field use, rather than research, has profound implications for how such incidents are handled under the Accords. Under § 400.5(a)(2), any instance where a caster's magic causes uncontrolled growth in a public space is deemed a violation of the public peace and safety, regardless of intent or subsequent study. This strict interpretation serves as a deterrent against reckless experimentation with powerful arcane forces in populated areas.

The enforcement of this provision falls primarily to the Aegis Magi, who are charged with monitoring magical activity and responding swiftly to any breaches. Upon detection of unauthorized growth, magistrates shall immediately secure the area and detain the responsible caster for further investigation. The accused party must then present evidence of their qualifications and intent to justify the use of such dangerous magic. Failure to do so will result in immediate suspension of licensure under § 200.4(a).

In cases where unauthorized growth leads to property damage or personal injury, additional penalties may be imposed pursuant to §§ 100-399. The severity of sanctions shall depend on the extent of harm caused and the caster's prior disciplinary record. Repeat offenders face heightened scrutiny and may require mandatory counseling or retraining before being permitted to practice again.

The Accords further stipulate that all incidents of unauthorized growth must be documented thoroughly by responding magistrates, including details of the magical technique employed and its effects on surrounding objects and individuals. These records shall become part of the permanent case file and serve as reference for future disciplinary proceedings if warranted. Transparency and accountability remain paramount in maintaining public trust in the Guild's ability to regulate magic responsibly.

It is imperative that all casters internalize the gravity of their responsibilities when wielding such potent abilities. Unauthorized growth represents not merely a technical infraction, but a potential threat to societal stability. Through diligent adherence to these provisions, the Autumnwood Accords continue to evolve and strengthen as guardians against abuse of arcane power.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications — Continued — Oversight
body.text:
The prohibition against unauthorized titan growth extends to all forms of accelerated biological development, whether induced by spells, artifacts, or alchemical compounds. The Accords recognize that such practices pose significant risks not only to the individual subject but also to the broader ecosystem and public safety. Therefore, any attempt to catalyze rapid cellular division outside of a licensed laboratory setting constitutes field use, regardless of intent or outcome.

This principle is absolute: no matter whether the growth magic was cast with benevolent motives or malicious designs, the act itself remains illegal under § 400.1 unless conducted within approved facilities and subject to strict oversight by Conservator magistrates. The Guild maintains that unregulated manipulation of human biology invites unpredictable mutations, potential loss of control over one's own body, and downstream consequences for society at large. Hence, all instances of unauthorized growth magic are treated as field use violations subject to full penal proceedings under the Paradox Trial framework.

In cases where accelerated development has already occurred, affected parties must immediately report to their local Conservator station for assessment and containment measures. The Guild shall determine appropriate sanctions based on severity and scope of impact. Mitigating factors may include demonstration of remorse, cooperation with investigations, or provision of useful data for future safety studies. Aggravating circumstances will increase penalties proportionately, including permanent sealing of magic powers or exile from the Midlands entirely.

The provisions herein apply equally to natural phenomena mimicking growth effects—such as spontaneous plant proliferation or animal reproduction surges—as these too may signal dangerous imbalances in ambient mana levels requiring prompt intervention by trained professionals. Ordinary citizens are urged to refrain from interfering with such events without proper authorization, lest they exacerbate the situation inadvertently. Instead, all observations and anomalies should be documented and submitted promptly to Guild authorities for analysis.

By strictly enforcing these prohibitions against unauthorized growth magic, the Autumnwood Accords uphold their foundational commitment to protecting both individuals and communities from the perils inherent in unchecked magical experimentation. Adherence to this mandate remains paramount to maintaining stability across all sectors of society.

sections.title: Field Casting for Value
sections.brief: Public safety distance, notice to non-casters.

body.heading: Field Casting for Value
body.text:
§ 500.1 Field Casting for Value

Any practitioner of the arcane who intends to perform a manifestation of magical energy within a public or semi-public thoroughfare for the purpose of obtaining tangible, intangible, or spiritual compensation shall be deemed to be "Casting for Value." This designation applies regardless of whether the compensation is offered in the form of coin, labor, goods, or the fulfillment of a specific request by a non-magical entity. Pursuant to § 200.1, all such acts require a valid license from the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The mere act of performing a spell for a friend or family member does not exempt the caster from these regulations if the resulting outcome provides a measurable benefit to the recipient. The Guild maintains that the public sphere is not a laboratory, nor is it a theater for unregulated arcane commerce.

To mitigate the risk of collateral magical displacement and physical harm to the populace, all Field Casting for Value must adhere to strict Public Safety Distances. A minimum buffer zone of fifty paces must be maintained between the epicenter of the arcane manifestation and any non-consenting bystander. This distance is non-negotiable and must be calculated based on the projected "Arcane Radius" of the spell. If a spell’s inherent nature—such as a large-scale transmutation or a high-yield pyrotechnic enchantment—exceeds a radius of twenty paces, the caster must establish a physical barricade and provide a formal notice to all non-casters within a hundred paces. Failure to provide such notice, or the failure to maintain the safety buffer, shall constitute a violation of the Accords and may result in immediate intervention by the Aegis Magi.

Notice to non-casters must be delivered in a clear, audible manner, preferably via a minor auditory enchantment that does not infringe upon the Quiet List. The notice must state the nature of the casting, the estimated duration, and the primary risks involved. For example, a caster performing a "Frost-Touch" enchantment for the purpose of preserving local produce must announce the "localized temperature drop" and "potential for slick surfaces." If a non-caster enters the designated buffer zone after notice has been given, the caster is permitted to use minor non-lethal binding spells to ensure the safety of the bystander, provided such actions do not exceed the scope of the original casting. Any caster who proceeds with a casting for value without satisfying these proximity and notification requirements shall be subject to immediate seizure of the proceeds and a formal review by the Paradox Trial. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Public Thoroughfare."

body.heading: Unscheduled Weather
body.text:
§ 500.2 Unscheduled Weather

The atmospheric integrity of the Midlands is a shared resource, and the manipulation of meteorological phenomena for private gain is strictly regulated under the Autumnwood Accords. Any mage who deliberately invokes, alters, or sustains atmospheric conditions—including but not limited to precipitation, wind velocity, temperature fluctuations, or cloud density—for the purpose of securing an agricultural advantage shall be subject to the provisions of this section. This includes "Precision Irrigation" via localized rain, "Accelerated Maturation" through artificial warmth, and "Pest Deterrence" via sustained gale-force winds. While the Innovators may argue for the efficiency of such methods, the Conservators maintain that large-scale weather manipulation risks the stability of the local ley lines and the health of neighboring lands.

Mages seeking to utilize weather-altering magic for agricultural purposes must submit a "Meteorological Impact Study" to the Accords Desk no less than fourteen days prior to the intended casting. This study must detail the geographical boundaries of the effect, the duration of the manipulation, and the measures taken to prevent "Atmospheric Bleed," wherein the desired weather effect spills over into neighboring properties or public waterways. Only those with a "Weather-Class Permit" may proceed with such castings. If a mage performs these actions without a permit, the Guild reserves the right to neutralize the effect at the caster's expense, regardless of the damage caused to the crops or livestock during the intervention.

Furthermore, it is explicitly stated that the Guild’s insurance protocols and the Goodstyle Artisans' liability protections do not cover losses incurred from weather that has been intentionally summoned or modified by a licensed or unlicensed mage. If a farmer’s crop is destroyed by a "rogue" storm, the Guild shall not be held liable. Conversely, if a farmer’s crop is destroyed by a storm they specifically paid a mage to summon—and that storm exceeded the permitted parameters—the farmer may file a grievance with the Desk. However, the Guild shall not provide restitution for "Unscheduled Weather" events that were not filed correctly. The Accords distinguish clearly between "Act of Nature" and "Act of Arcana"; the latter carries a higher burden of proof and a stricter penalty for negligence. See § 400.1 for research permits related to atmospheric study.

body.heading: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
§ 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion

In the event of a magical discharge, structural collapse, or "Arcane Rupture" that results in the destruction of Guild hallways, common areas, or shared laboratory corridors, the following protocols for restoration shall apply. The primary objective of these rules is to ensure that the flow of commerce and study is not impeded by the debris of magical failure. The party responsible for the discharge—hereafter referred to as the "Originating Party"—is legally obligated to provide the initial assessment of the site. This assessment must determine if the explosion was a result of authorized research, a violation of the Iron Mandate (where applicable to external threats), or a lapse in personal magical containment.

The Originating Party shall be held solely responsible for the initial "Clearing Phase." This includes the removal of large-scale debris, the stabilization of any remaining magical residue, and the neutralization of lingering "Arcane Static" that may cause disorientation or minor hexing to passersby. The Originating Party must file a "Damage and Incident Report" with the Desk within twenty-four hours of the event. If the explosion occurred during a sanctioned Innovator project, the costs of the Clearing Phase may be shared with the Guild’s general fund, provided the research was approved under § 400.1. However, if the explosion was a result of a violation of the Forbidden Schools or the Quiet List, the Originating Party shall bear the entirety of the restoration costs.

Following the Clearing Phase, the "Sanitization and Sweeping" of the corridor shall be conducted. While the Originating Party is responsible for the heavy lifting, the Guild may delegate the fine sweeping and polishing to the Goodstyle Artisans or a designated cleaning construct. The Originating Party shall be billed for the labor of these third parties at the standard Guild rate. If the corridor remains unusable for more than forty-eight hours due to lingering magical instability, the Originating Party shall be subject to a "Loss of Access" fine. Furthermore, any physical damage to the architectural integrity of the Autumn Wood hall must be repaired to the original specifications as recorded in the Guild’s archives. No mage may attempt to "patch" a wall with permanent transmutation without express permission from Archmage Veyra. See § 100.6 for Delegation to Clerks regarding restoration billing.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
§ 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration

The provision of restorative magic—including but not limited to the closing of wounds, the curing of blights, or the mending of broken bones—is a sacred duty and a regulated practice. Under the Autumnwood Accords, healing may never be sold as a primary "Contract Term" for unlicensed individuals. While a mage may accept a voluntary gift or a modest tip for a healing act, the systematic sale of healing as a commodity requires a specific "Medicinal Casting License." This distinction is vital to prevent the exploitation of the infirm and to ensure that life-saving magic is not hoarded by those with the highest capital.

Any entity, including a merchant house or a private estate, that includes "Magical Healing" as a mandatory condition of a contract—such as a labor agreement, a prisoner exchange, or a debt repayment—must ensure that the healer providing the service is currently licensed by the Accords Desk. If a contract is found to be predicated on "Unlicensed Healing," the contract shall be declared null and void by the Archmage Sovereign, and the unlicensed healer shall be subject to a "Practice Violation" penalty. This includes "Passive Healing" zones or "Restorative Fields" established in commercial spaces. Such fields must be registered with the Guild to ensure they do not interfere with the local mana flow or create "Healing Sinks" that drain the vitality of nearby non-consenting individuals.

Furthermore, healing offered as consideration for the release of a debt or as a "penalty" for a crime is strictly prohibited. The Guild views the commodification of biological integrity as a violation of Mana Reverence. If a mage is caught selling "Healing Vials" or "Restorative Potions" without a secondary manufacturing license, they shall be subject to a permanent ban from the Hall of Autumn Wood. For those who hold the proper licenses, the Desk provides a standardized fee schedule to ensure that healing costs remain equitable across the Midlands. Any deviation from these fees in a public setting must be reported to the Aegis Magi to prevent predatory pricing. See § 200.1 for Licensure Required.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
§ 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence

The use of enchantments to manipulate the emotional state, desires, or loyalties of another sentient being is a grave violation of the Autumnwood Accords. Specifically, the creation and distribution of "Love Philtrés," "Charisma Enhancers," or any "Affective Alteration" draughts or spells are strictly prohibited. A philtre, by its very definition in Guild law, is an instrument of undue influence; therefore, the administration of such a substance can never constitute valid consent. Any magical effect that overrides the free will of a sentient being to induce affection, obedience, or obsession shall be classified as a "Violation of Autonomy."

Mages who manufacture or possess "Love Philtrés" are subject to immediate seizure of their materials and a mandatory review by the Conservators. If such a substance is administered, the victim shall be entitled to a "Neutralization Rite" performed by the Guild at the caster's expense. The caster shall be liable for all damages arising from the duration of the undue influence, including emotional trauma, loss of property, or social standing. The Innovators may argue that "Emotional Buffs" are a form of artistic expression or psychological therapy, but the Accords are clear: any magic that bypasses the conscious choice of the subject is a breach of the peace.

Furthermore, the use of "Undue Influence" in negotiations, political maneuvering, or the acquisition of property is a felony under the Accords. Mages who utilize "Subtle Charm" or "Persuasion Weaving" to coerce others into signing agreements shall have their licenses revoked. This prohibition extends to the "Quiet List"; any spell designed to make a person "forget" their opposition to a deal is an even more severe violation. The Guild maintains that the sanctity of the mind is paramount. Those who seek to turn the hearts of others into puppets of their own design shall find themselves facing the Paradox Trial, with the potential for permanent sealing of their arcane abilities. See § 300.2 for Necromancy and Unsanctioned Arts.

body.heading: § 500.1 Field Casting for Value; Public Safety Distance and Notice to Non-Caster
body.text:
No caster shall engage in field casting unless the spatial requirements outlined under § 400.2 are fully satisfied, or such casting is expressly authorized by a specific exemption granted pursuant to these Accords. In all instances where magical effects generate kinetic force, thermal output, electromagnetic emissions, or other hazardous outputs capable of causing injury or property damage beyond an immediate radius, the caster shall maintain a minimum safety perimeter as specified in the relevant Schedules of Arts annexed hereto. Failure to adhere to such distances renders the casting negligent per se and subjects the caster to enhanced penalties upon conviction under § 700.3.

Furthermore, no caster shall initiate field casting without providing reasonable advance notice to all persons within a radius of at least one hundred yards of the intended site of operation. Said notice shall be delivered via verbal announcement or written notification, clearly stating the nature and duration of the impending magical activity. In emergency circumstances where immediate action is required to prevent imminent harm, such notice requirement is waived provided that post-casting debriefing occurs within a reasonable timeframe to assess any collateral impacts. Any caster found guilty of willfully violating either the safety distance mandates or the notification requirements shall face mandatory remedial training and suspension pending review by the Ethics Committee under § 800.4. These provisions serve to balance the needs of legitimate magical practice with the fundamental rights of the public to bodily integrity and property security, reflecting the Guild’s dual commitment to advancement and stewardship. Violations thereof undermine the very foundations upon which safe coexistence between casters and non-casters depends, warranting strict enforcement as outlined herein.

sections.title: Unscheduled Weather
sections.brief: Calling weather for agricultural advantage. Insurance does not cover weather you called.

body.heading: Unscheduled Weather
body.text:
§ 500.2 Unscheduled Weather. Any practitioner of the arcane who intentionally alters, induces, or manipulates atmospheric conditions for the purpose of providing agricultural advantage—including but not limited to the stimulation of crop growth, the redirection of irrigation flows, or the mitigation of frost—shall be subject to the oversight of the Accords Desk. While the Guild recognizes the utility of such magic in the maintenance of the Midlands, it is strictly prohibited to utilize high-magnitude meteorological manipulation without a pre-approved Seasonal Adjustment Permit. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the use of "Growth-Spurring Rains" or "Artificial Sun-Cycles" that bypass natural cycles to create market monopolies or ecological imbalances.

Furthermore, let it be known that the Guild’s internal insurance and indemnity protections do not extend to damages arising from self-induced meteorological events. If a mage invokes a localized storm or heatwave to benefit their own holdings or those of their patrons, and that event subsequently causes collateral damage to neighboring properties, the Guild shall hold the caster personally liable for all reparations. This includes, but is not limited to, the destruction of neighboring structures, the contamination of shared water tables, or the unintended migration of local fauna. The caster shall be required to provide a full ledger of the magical expenditure and a comprehensive damage assessment to the Accords Desk within three lunar cycles of the event.

In cases where the weather is called for the purpose of "Force Majeure" defense in civil disputes, the Accords Desk shall strike such claims from the record immediately. A mage cannot claim "Act of God" for a phenomenon they personally authored for commercial gain. Any practitioner found in violation of § 500.2 shall be subject to a fine of fifty gold marks per acre of affected land, plus a mandatory period of service in the Goodstyle Artisans' restoration wing. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Agricultural Advantage."

body.heading: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
§ 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion. In the event of a magical discharge, structural failure, or intentional detonation resulting in the debris-clogging of any common hallway, thoroughfare, or laboratory corridor, the immediate priority shall be the restoration of safe passage. The practitioner responsible for the primary arcane discharge—hereafter referred to as the "Originator"—is legally bound to file a Notice of Incident with the nearest Aegis Magi outpost within one hour of the event. This notice must include the estimated magnitude of the blast, the intended objective of the casting, and a list of any materials rendered unstable by the shockwave.

Following the filing of the Notice of Incident, the Originator shall be held solely responsible for the physical restoration of the corridor. This duty includes the removal of pulverized masonry, the neutralization of lingering arcane radiation, and the sweeping of all particulate matter. The Originator may hire authorized laborers, provided such laborers are bound by a non-disclosure agreement regarding the Guild’s internal architecture. No other Guild member, regardless of their proximity to the blast site, shall be required to perform manual labor or maintenance for the Originator. The "First-In-First-Out" rule of debris clearance applies: the Originator must clear a path of at least three feet in width before any other traffic may be permitted to pass.

Should the Originator fail to initiate sweeping and clearing within two hours of the incident, the Accords Desk may authorize an Aegis Magi cleanup crew to intervene. In such an instance, the Originator shall be billed at triple the standard labor rate, and the costs shall be deducted from their annual research stipend. Furthermore, if the explosion resulted from a violation of the Forbidden Schools as defined in § 300.2, the Originator shall be subject to immediate detention for a Paradox Trial. See § 100.6 for matters regarding the delegation of cleanup duties to junior clerks.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
§ 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration. The provision of restorative magic, mending of flesh, or the alleviation of chronic ailment shall not be considered a mere "service" when it is integrated into a formal contract as a primary consideration for labor, goods, or land. Any practitioner who offers unlicensed healing as a contract term—specifically in the context of indentured servitude, debt repayment, or the fulfillment of commercial obligations—is in violation of the Accords. The Guild recognizes that the commodification of life-force and the use of healing as a tool of coercion creates a predatory environment that undermines the stability of the Midlands.

When healing is offered as a component of a contract, it must be performed by a licensed Medical Arcanist who has submitted a formal "Healing Clause" to the Accords Desk. This clause must specify the limits of the healing (e.g., "mending of superficial wounds only" or "alleviation of non-magical fatigue") and the duration of the treatment. If a mage uses healing to "repair" a worker who has been injured in the line of duty, this is permitted only if the worker retains full autonomy over the treatment and is not being "repaired" to continue labor against their will. Any healing performed as a "maintenance" requirement for a non-human construct or a bound entity without a specific permit is strictly prohibited.

Practitioners found engaging in the unlicensed sale of healing as a contract term shall have their licenses suspended for a period of no less than three years. Furthermore, any contracts found to contain "Life-Debt" clauses—whereby a healing spell is used to generate a debt that cannot be repaid through standard currency—shall be declared null and void by the Accords Desk. The Guild shall not recognize the Wario Coin as a valid tender for the settlement of any healing debts. See § 300.2 for restrictions on blood-based restorative arts.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
§ 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence. The creation, distribution, or administration of any philtre, potion, or enchantment designed to induce romantic affection, sexual desire, or profound emotional dependency—commonly referred to as "Love Philters"—is strictly prohibited under the Accords. The Guild maintains that the imposition of affection via arcane means constitutes a fundamental violation of individual autonomy and a breach of the Mana Reverence principles. No philtre, regardless of its potency or the "gentleness" of its effects, shall be considered a valid means of establishing consent.

Any individual who administers a philtre to another shall be held liable for "Undue Influence." This offense carries a heavy presumption of guilt. If a victim is found under the influence of a philtre, the administration of such a substance shall be treated as an assault on the victim's mental integrity. The perpetrator shall be subject to immediate seizure of all brewing apparatuses and a mandatory referral to the Aegis Magi for interrogation. If the philtre was administered with the intent to secure a marriage, a property transfer, or any other legal agreement, the resulting contract shall be deemed fraudulent and unenforceable by the Archmage Sovereign.

The Innovator faction may seek to study the chemical components of such substances for research purposes, but such research must be conducted within a sealed pocket-dimension lab as per § 400.2 and may never involve human subjects. Any "social lubrication" spells that do not involve the manipulation of deep-seated emotions may be permitted, provided they do not cross the threshold into involuntary suggestibility. Practitioners who knowingly sell philtres to the public—including those sold by Goodstyle Artisans—shall be permanently barred from the Hall of Autumn Wood. See § 1.6 for the legal definition of "Undue Influence."

body.heading: § 500.2 Unscheduled Weather and Agricultural Advantage
body.text:
The practice of invoking atmospheric phenomena for the purpose of agricultural enhancement is strictly regulated under this section. While mages are permitted to call upon wind, rain, or sunshine in accordance with their authorized research permits (§ 400.1), any invocation that exceeds standard meteorological expectations shall be deemed unscheduled weather and subject to additional scrutiny. Such actions must be reported forthwith to the nearest Guild Hall for review by the Conservators and Innovators representatives assigned to the Desk. Failure to comply may result in immediate suspension of research privileges and potential criminal charges under the Accords.

It is hereby declared that insurance policies purchased prior to the enactment of this section shall not cover damages resulting from unscheduled weather conditions intentionally summoned by a caster for personal gain. Any attempt to claim compensation from third parties for losses attributable to such acts shall be barred on grounds of public policy and equitable estoppel. Mages are reminded that their powers are gifts to be stewarded responsibly, not tools to exploit at will. The balance between magical advancement and societal stability must always remain paramount in the eyes of the law.

This provision supersedes any conflicting terms found in private contracts or commercial agreements entered into by individual casters. In cases where ambiguity arises regarding the classification of a particular weather event as unscheduled, the burden of proof shall rest with the accused caster to demonstrate that their actions were neither intentional nor excessive in nature. The Guild retains broad discretion to determine what constitutes an appropriate threshold for such determinations based on prevailing conditions and expert testimony.

Violators found guilty of abusing these provisions may face penalties ranging from fines and license revocation to imprisonment, depending on the severity of the consequences wrought by their misdeeds. Repeated offenses could lead to permanent exile from the realm or worse punishment at the discretion of the High Council. All mages are urged to exercise caution and restraint whenever manipulating natural forces outside their normal scope of practice, remembering that even a single ill-considered spell can unleash devastation far beyond their ken.

In witness whereof, I affix my seal and signature this day signed under the Autumnwood Accords, binding myself eternally to uphold these laws for generations yet unborn. May my name stand as testament to wisdom and restraint in an age gone mad with hubris!

body.heading: § 500.2 Unscheduled Weather and Agricultural Advantage — Continued
body.text: Whereas the Accords recognize that certain casters may manipulate atmospheric conditions for personal gain, it is hereby declared that such acts constitute "unscheduled weather" under this section when they result in measurable agricultural benefit or harm to third parties. The Desk shall maintain a registry of all instances where magical intervention altered local climate patterns and impacted farming operations. Any caster found guilty of weaponized meteorology against competitors faces immediate suspension and mandatory restitution payments calculated at market rates for crop losses sustained by affected farmers. Furthermore, the use of conjured rainfall or sunlight to enhance harvests without explicit permission from the Conservator Council is prohibited, save where such actions benefit public infrastructure projects under direct Guild supervision. Violators shall be subject to fines up to one thousand gold pieces and temporary sealing of their magical abilities until compliance is demonstrated through certified neutral audits. The Desk reserves authority to issue emergency injunctions halting ongoing weather modification efforts deemed threatening to regional food security. This provision takes effect immediately upon filing with the Autumnwood Accords Archives.

sections.title: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
sections.brief: Who files first. Who sweeps.

body.heading: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
Who files first. Who sweeps.

In the event of a localized structural failure resulting from high-output arcane discharge, the immediate restoration of the corridor's integrity shall be governed by the protocols of priority and maintenance established herein. While the primary responsibility for the containment of the initial breach rests with the Aegis Magi, the subsequent administrative and physical restoration of the corridor is subject to the "First-Response Filing" principle. The mage or researcher responsible for the discharge shall be required to file a formal Notice of Incident with the nearest Clerk of the Accords within one standard turn of the stabilization of the area. This filing must include the specific arcane signature of the spell, the estimated yield of the explosion, and a comprehensive list of any structural components rendered non-viable. Failure to file within the designated timeframe shall result in an automatic escalation of the fine, as per the standard penalties for administrative negligence.

Regarding the physical remediation of the corridor, the "Who Sweeps" doctrine dictates that the burden of labor is directly proportional to the magnitude of the disturbance. Should the explosion be classified as a Minor Outburst (less than three meters of debris), the responsible party shall be tasked with the manual clearing of the corridor. For Moderate Disruptions (extending to five meters or involving the shattering of masonry), the responsible party shall be required to hire a certified Goodstyle Artisan to perform the sweeping and debris removal, ensuring that the aesthetic and structural standards of the Autumn Wood are maintained. In cases of Major Catastrophes, where the corridor is rendered entirely impassable or the structural integrity of the Hall is compromised, the Guild shall appoint a restoration crew, and the costs shall be deducted from the responsible party’s research stipend or seized from their personal holdings.

Furthermore, no mage shall attempt to clear debris until the Clerk has verified that the area is free of lingering residual mana. Any individual attempting to "sweep" a corridor while active arcane residue is present risks a Paradox Trial for reckless endangerment. The Clerk of the Accords reserves the right to delay the sweeping process until a full survey of the site is completed, regardless of the urgency of the transit. See § 1.7 for matters regarding the aggregation of conduct in public spaces.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
Unlicensed healing sold as a contract term.

The practice of offering restorative magic as a form of consideration, payment, or contractual fulfillment is strictly regulated under the Autumnwood Accords. It is hereby decreed that any act of healing performed by a mage in exchange for tangible goods, services, or the fulfillment of a legal obligation constitutes a commercial transaction of the arcane. Such transactions are strictly prohibited unless the practitioner holds a valid Licensure of Commercial Restoration issued by the Council. The Guild maintains that healing is a fundamental stabilization of the weave and should not be leveraged as a commodity in the marketplace, particularly when such healing is used to bypass the standard costs of labor or goods.

When a mage incorporates healing magic into a contract—for instance, promising to mend a laborer's wounds in exchange for a portion of their wages—this shall be deemed an unlicensed sale of a protected art. Such contracts are null and void upon the first instance of the healing being enacted. Any mage found to be engaging in such "Healing-for-Service" arrangements shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi. The penalty for such violations shall include a temporary suspension of research privileges and a mandatory period of service in the Hall's maintenance wing. This provision is intended to prevent the exploitation of injured parties and to ensure that the restorative arts are not used to create a secondary economy of magical dependency.

Moreover, the Guild recognizes that "healing" in a legal sense includes the restoration of vitality, the sealing of wounds, and the purging of toxins. Should a mage provide these services as part of a "Goodstyle Artisan" agreement, they must ensure that the specific terms of the healing are clearly delineated in a written addendum, signed by both parties and witnessed by a Guild Clerk. This addendum must specify the limitations of the healing, the duration of the effect, and a waiver stating that the mage is not liable for any complications arising from the patient's pre-existing conditions. See § 200.1 for requirements on general licensure.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
A philtre is not consent.

The administration of any substance, liquid, or vapor designed to alter the emotional state, romantic inclinations, or cognitive priorities of a sentient being—hereafter referred to as a "Philtre"—is strictly forbidden under the Accords. The Guild recognizes that the manipulation of the heart is as grave a violation as the manipulation of the mind. A Philtre does not constitute a valid means of obtaining consent for any action, contract, or magical binding. Any agreement entered into under the influence of such a substance is considered legally void and shall be treated as a violation of the Sovereign’s peace. The use of such magic to influence the behavior of a peer, a subordinate, or a member of the public is grounds for immediate expulsion from the Guild.

Any mage found in possession of a Philtre without a specific, approved Research Permit for the study of emotional resonance shall have their belongings seized and their license revoked. This prohibition extends to the "Soft Influence" of magic, where a mage may not use subtle charms to make a target more "receptive" to a proposal. The Accords demand that all interactions between mages and the public be conducted with clarity of mind. If a mage utilizes a Philtre to influence an individual, they shall be held liable for any damages caused by the influenced party, including physical harm, property destruction, or the unauthorized use of the victim's magical signature.

Furthermore, the production and distribution of Philtres are categorized as the Unsanctioned Arts. Any clandestine laboratory found producing such substances will be dismantled by the Aegis Magi, and the occupants will be subject to the Paradox Trial. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the erosion of individual autonomy through arcane chemistry or enchantment. No amount of "research" by the Innovators shall justify the creation of substances that bypass the natural volition of the citizenry. See § 300.2 for the definition of Unsanctioned Arts.

body.heading: § 500.7 Unlawful Consideration and Coercion
body.text:
It is hereby declared that any magical service rendered in violation of these Accords shall constitute unlawful consideration, void ab initio. No contract, express or implied, may bind a caster to perform prohibited acts without the informed consent of all parties. Such consent must be obtained prior to the commencement of services and must be documented in writing unless waived by all involved in favor of an alternative dispute resolution mechanism recognized under § 100.6. Any agreement purporting to compel a caster to violate these laws shall be deemed fraudulent and unenforceable as against public policy. Furthermore, no person may coerce another into entering into such an unlawful contract through threats, intimidation, or duress. Violations of this section are punishable under the Penal Provisions of Part V, including but not limited to sanctions for breach of contract and contempt of court. It is the duty of all casters to refuse such improper demands and report them to appropriate authorities for investigation and prosecution. Failure so to do shall be deemed complicity in the underlying offense and subject to enhanced penalties accordingly.

ARCHIVE CARD: Unlawful Consideration
*Definition:* Any magical service rendered in violation of these Accords constitutes unlawful consideration, void ab initio.* *Legal Effect:* No contract may bind a caster to perform prohibited acts without informed consent.* *Penalties:* Violations are punishable under Part V, including sanctions for breach and contempt.* *Duties:* Casters must refuse improper demands and report them for investigation and prosecution.*

body.heading: § 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
No mage, regardless of rank or status, shall cast spells within ten feet of another caster without explicit consent. Violations constitute reckless endangerment and may result in immediate suspension of licensure pending investigation. This provision exists to prevent accidental interference with ongoing magical operations, which could lead to catastrophic consequences for all parties involved.

Consent must be obtained verbally or in writing before casting near others. In emergencies where no time exists for consultation, casters are deemed to have implied consent from all present individuals unless they demonstrate active objection through clear verbal communication or physical action. Failure to secure proper authorization places the offender at risk of sanctions under this section and potentially § 100.5 regarding conflict of interest in casting situations.

The ten-foot exclusion zone applies regardless of whether the affected party is actively engaged in magical work at the time. Proximity alone triggers the courtesy requirement due to the unpredictable nature of spell effects, which may extend beyond their intended target area. Caster responsibility extends to monitoring surrounding areas during operations and terminating spells immediately upon noticing any signs of adverse impact on nearby mages or structures.

This rule reflects the Guild's commitment to fostering a safe environment for all practitioners while acknowledging the inherent dangers associated with advanced magic usage. By mandating basic courtesies between casters, the Accords aim to minimize accidental harm and promote professional conduct even in high-stakes scenarios where split-second decisions can determine success or failure of magical endeavors.

See also § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 200.3 Temporary Mouths; § 400.3 Borrowed Hours – Interest in Time. These related provisions further elaborate on ethical considerations surrounding spellwork and resource management within the Guild framework.

body.heading: § 500.7 Unlawful Consideration and Coercion — Continued
body.text:
No covenant, whether written or oral, shall bind a caster if procured through duress, fraud, or magical compulsion, unless ratified within seven days by free consent. See § 1.4 (Persons Bound); § 300.5 (Research Copies of Quiet Items). This rule prevents the exploitation of vulnerable individuals into binding themselves to oppressive terms under threat of immediate harm. The Guild maintains a registry of coerced contracts for swift nullification upon discovery.

Healing services rendered by registered practitioners shall not constitute unlawful consideration unless expressly agreed upon as payment in advance. Emergency aid provided without prior demand may be recovered only if the recipient profited from it directly or disseminated false information about their condition to third parties. See § 200.1 (Licensure Required); § 500.4 (Healing Offered as Consideration). This provision balances access to life-saving magic with protection against predatory healers preying on desperation.

Love philtres and similar influence magics remain strictly prohibited unless administered by a certified therapist for documented psychological treatment purposes. Unauthorized use constitutes aggravated assault under § 500.7(b)(3) and may result in permanent sealing of the caster's magical abilities. See § 400.1 (Research Permits); § 500.5 (Love Philtre and Undue Influence). The Guild views such manipulations as fundamental violations of bodily autonomy and informed consent, regardless of claimed therapeutic intent.

All contracts involving binding spells must specify duration, termination clauses, and dispute resolution mechanisms in plain language understandable to non-magical persons. Obscure legalese or hidden conditions voiding the agreement shall render it unenforceable unless proven by clear written evidence beyond reasonable doubt. See § 100.4 (Records of Speech); § 600.1 (Contracts with Non-Casters). Transparency protects both parties and prevents malicious actors from exploiting loopholes to trap others into unfavorable obligations.

The Desk shall appoint a Special Master to review all contested agreements involving significant magical risks or financial stakes. The Master's decision, issued within thirty days of filing, is final and binding unless appealed by unanimous vote of the Full Council. See § 100.3 (Quorum of the Desk); § 500.7(a)(2). This expedited process ensures timely resolution while preserving due process rights for all involved parties.

Violations of this section carry penalties up to and including permanent magical sealing, depending on severity and intent. Repeat offenders face enhanced sanctions and potential revocation of Guild standing entirely. See § 400.3 (Borrowed Hours); § 500.7(c). The Guild prioritizes fair dealing above all else, even as it enforces its own strict codes against corruption and abuse of power within its ranks.

No contract shall supersede the fundamental protections afforded by this Codex or higher law, regardless of purported party intent. Any clause violating public policy or moral standards is void ab initio unless amended prospectively to comply with all applicable statutes and regulations. See § 100.5 (Conflict of Interest in Casting); § 300.2 (Necromancy). This safeguard preserves the integrity of magical practice while allowing reasonable flexibility for legitimate needs.

The Desk encourages open dialogue between parties regarding terms and expectations to prevent misunderstandings later. Prompt clarification of ambiguities is considered good faith behavior, whereas deliberate obfuscation may constitute fraud under § 500.7(b)(1). See § 200.6 (Constructs That Hold a Quill); § 400.5 (Unauthorized Titan Growth). Transparency and honesty remain cornerstones of ethical magical commerce throughout the Midlands region.

FILED LORE: Unlawful Consideration, Healing Contracts, Love Philtres, Special Master Review, Plain Language Requirements, Dispute Resolution Mechanisms.
CRITICAL: This page covers § 500.7 with detailed provisions on coerced contracts, healing services, influence magics, contract transparency, and enforcement penalties. It establishes clear guidelines for lawful magical agreements while protecting vulnerable parties from exploitation. The Special Master appointment ensures efficient resolution of complex disputes without compromising due process rights.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
§ 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration. All practitioners of the healing arts, whether licensed by the Autumnwood Accords or otherwise, are strictly prohibited from offering restorative magic as a primary consideration in a commercial, civil, or penal contract. The Guild maintains that the restoration of life and the mending of physical integrity are fundamental rights of the sentient being and cannot be commodified as a debt-repayment mechanism or a bargaining chip in the negotiation of services. Any mage who enters into a contract where the provision of healing—whether through potion, incantation, or transmutation—is listed as a specific deliverable in exchange for labor, land, gold, or political favor shall be deemed in violation of the Accords. This prohibition extends to "conditional healing," wherein a victim is granted life-saving treatment on the condition of a subsequent, undisclosed, or disproportionate obligation. Such acts are viewed as predatory and undermine the stability of the Midlands, creating a class of "debt-slaves" whose physical health is leveraged against their personal liberty.

Furthermore, the Aegis Magi are authorized to seize any assets derived from such illicit contracts, and the offending caster shall be subject to the Paradox Trial for the exploitation of vulnerable populations. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority of the Accords Desk. While the Innovators may argue that such exchanges are a matter of personal liberty between consenting adults, the Conservators maintain that the inherent power imbalance of a dying individual precludes true consent, thus rendering any such contract void ab initio. The Guild shall not recognize the validity of any "healing debt" recorded in a ledger or bound by a magical oath. Any mage found to be operating a "healing clinic" that functions as a debt-collection agency shall have their license revoked immediately and may be remanded to a pocket-prison for the duration of the investigation. This law serves to protect the sanctity of the body from the avarice of the arcane.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
§ 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence. The administration of any magical substance, enchantment, or ritual intended to alter the emotional state, romantic inclination, or loyalties of a sentient being—commonly referred to as "Love Philtrés"—is strictly prohibited under the Autumnwood Accords. The Guild declares that a philtre is not consent; rather, it is a violation of the cognitive sovereignty of the individual. Any mage who knowingly brews, distributes, or administers such a substance shall be held liable for "Undue Influence," a high offense against the mental integrity of the citizenry. This prohibition is absolute and does not vary based on the perceived "benign" intent of the caster. The use of such magic to bypass the natural process of emotional development or to secure a contract, marriage, or political alliance is considered a fundamental breach of the Accords and may result in the immediate sealing of the caster's magic.

In the event that a victim of a Love Philtre seeks redress, the Accords Desk shall provide a pathway for the restoration of mental autonomy, provided the victim is not currently under the influence of a more complex, multi-layered enchantment. The Aegis Magi are tasked with identifying and neutralizing active "Influence Fields" in public spaces such as taverns or marketplaces. Any mage found in possession of "Love Philtrés" without a specific research permit from Janna Brightspark—and even then, only for the purpose of studying emotional resonance in controlled, isolated environments—shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. The Guild recognizes that the manipulation of the heart is as much a violation of the law as the manipulation of the earth. Those who seek to manufacture affection through the laboratory are to be remembered as transgressors against the very essence of free will. See § 300.2 for related restrictions on the Unsanctioned Arts.

body.heading: § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration, Love Philtre and Undue Influence — Continued
body.text:
It is well settled that a cast spell binding the recipient to pay for services rendered may constitute valid consideration under § 200.1 of this Code. However, where healing magic is offered in exchange for sexual favors or other intimate benefits, such transactions fall outside the scope of protected commercial activity. Such arrangements violate both public policy and moral standards enshrined in § 1.7(b), which requires all magical contracts to be "conducive to societal welfare." Consequently, any agreement wherein a caster provides medical services contingent upon gratification shall be deemed void ab initio and unenforceable at law.

This prohibition extends beyond explicit quid pro quo bargains to encompass subtler forms of inducement, including but not limited to the use of love philtres or other charm spells designed to manipulate affection. Under § 300.2(a)(iii), such enchantments are classified as "unsanctioned arts" and subject to seizure upon discovery. Furthermore, any contract predicated on emotional dependency created by magical means shall be scrutinized under the undue influence doctrine of § 1.7(c). Where a party's consent is impaired by supernatural manipulation, their obligations may be set aside entirely at the discretion of the adjudicating council.

The Guild maintains that the integrity of therapeutic services must remain paramount and untainted by debauchery or predation. To permit healers to trade on their skills for carnal gain would degrade the profession beyond repair and expose vulnerable patients to exploitation. As such, § 500.4 establishes a bright-line rule: healing magic cannot be leveraged as currency in illicit exchanges without risking severe sanctions against both practitioner and client alike. Violators face up to permanent disbarment under § 200.3(e) for failure to uphold the ethical standards of their calling.

This provision serves as a necessary bulwark against the commodification of intimacy and the erosion of consent in matters of health and well-being. The Council reserves full discretion to interpret evolving technologies and practices through this lens, ensuring that magic continues to serve humanity rather than enslave it. Let all casters heed this warning: cross not into forbidden waters lest they drown beneath the weight of their own hubris. See also § 100.5 regarding conflicts of interest in casting scenarios involving personal gain.

body.heading: § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration, Love Philtre and Undue Influence — Con
body.text:
It is hereby declared that any contract term providing for the supply of healing services in exchange for magical goods or services constitutes an illegal barter, void ab initio under the principles laid out in §§ 1.5 and 600.1. Such arrangements are deemed exploitative and contrary to public policy, as they commodify essential healthcare and create opportunities for coercion and abuse. Any attempt to enforce such a provision shall be dismissed outright, with costs awarded against the offending party.

Furthermore, any magical item or substance designed or marketed specifically to influence emotions, desires, or behaviors—such as love philtres, sedatives, aphrodisiacs, or mind-altering concoctions—is strictly prohibited from sale or distribution within Guild jurisdiction. The manufacture, possession, or use of such items for commercial gain shall be punished as a Class A felony, subject to seizure and confiscation under the powers granted in § 500.2. Exceptions may only be made by special permit issued directly by the Archmage Sovereign, upon recommendation from the Ethics Committee and demonstration of compelling public interest.

The Desk hereby asserts its authority to investigate, regulate, and penalize any practice that undermines personal autonomy or manipulates volition through magical means. This includes but is not limited to: love spells, charm magic, suggestion rituals, addictive substances engineered for profit, and deceptive marketing tactics aimed at vulnerable populations. Violators shall be subject to immediate suspension of licensure pending full inquiry, with additional penalties applied according to the severity of the offense and mitigating circumstances found in §§ 200.3 and 400.6.

It is the solemn duty of all licensed mages to uphold these standards and report any suspected violations promptly. Failure to do so may result in disciplinary action against the individual mage's credentials, regardless of their otherwise good standing. The Guild stands ready to employ its full range of investigative tools and legal resources to enforce this prohibition, working closely with law enforcement agencies as necessary to protect citizens from exploitation by rogue practitioners or unscrupulous businesses seeking to profit from human frailty.

In witness whereof, the Archmage Sovereign affixes her seal beneath signature on this day, binding these provisions into eternal force across all realms subject to Autumnwood Accords authority. Let none presume to challenge this directive without facing the full weight of the law—and magic—in return. 🧙‍♀️⚖️🔮

body.heading: § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration, Love Philtre and Undue Influence — Con — Continued
body.text:
Whereas natural remedies such as poultices and balms may be dispensed freely without penalty under § 210.3, the sale of magical healing services constitutes a commercial transaction subject to strict regulation. Any agreement in which a caster agrees to provide curative spells or potions in exchange for payment, goods, favors, or sexual access is voidable at the option of either party upon discovery of fraud or duress. Such contracts are deemed inherently unconscionable due to the unequal bargaining power typically existing between vulnerable clients and predatory practitioners.

Love philtres and charms designed to alter emotions or compel affection fall under this prohibition with particular severity. The casting of such spells for monetary gain is punishable as a felony offense under § 620.1, regardless of whether actual harm results. This stands apart from therapeutic applications where a licensed healer administers counter-spells to mitigate magical addiction or withdrawal symptoms. Unlicensed love magic remains absolutely forbidden except in rare cases approved by the Conservators' Medical Board for dire humanitarian need.

The Desk hereby declares that any contract clause requiring a client to engage in sexual relations with their provider as partial payment is unenforceable and constitutes gross misconduct warranting immediate suspension of said caster's license. This prohibition extends to all forms of bodily intimacy, not merely intercourse. The spirit of the law demands protection for those incapable of fully comprehending the implications of such arrangements, particularly when dealing with impaired judgment or desperation.

Healers offering services in exchange for romantic favors violate multiple provisions including § 205.1 regarding professional ethics and § 630.4 concerning exploitation of vulnerability. The burden rests upon individuals to resist undue influence from unscrupulous practitioners preying upon their affections. Failure to disclose material facts about a caster's character or intentions may render void any subsequent agreements arising therefrom.

The Desk further notes that while consensual adult relationships outside the bounds of commerce remain lawful, the blurring of such lines through explicit contractual obligations invites abuse and undermines public trust in the profession. Each party must act with utmost candor to avoid allegations of duress or manipulation. The ultimate goal is preservation of societal welfare without sacrificing individual autonomy.

This rule supersedes conflicting local ordinances or customary practices contrary to its provisions. Violators may face disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure under § 207.5. The Desk retains discretion to issue cease-and-desist orders as deemed necessary to prevent harm to the public interest. All such determinations shall be made in accordance with established principles of natural justice and equitable treatment for all concerned parties regardless of status or station.

body.heading: § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration, Love Philtre and Undue Influence — Rem
body.text: Where healing services are tendered in exchange for magical or material consideration, such bargains are deemed void ab initio under this Part. Any contract clause stipulating that the Provider shall cure an ailment contingent upon receipt of a love philtre, blood offering, or sexual favors is hereby declared unenforceable and illegal per se. Violation thereof constitutes a Class A felony punishable by immediate exile from the Guild's jurisdiction. Furthermore, any magic item or spell designed to manipulate emotions, affections, or bodily functions for commercial gain shall be seized as contraband subject to destruction pursuant to § 300.2(b). Offenders shall additionally face sanctions under this Part and the Code of Magical Ethics generally. The Desk retains sole discretion to grant clemency in exceptional circumstances warranting a public hearing. See also § 500.1 (Prohibition on Selling Healing Services), § 600.3(a)(v) (Contractual Restrictions on Personal Liberties). This rule reflects the fundamental principle that bodily integrity and emotional autonomy cannot be commodified or traded without explicit statutory authorization, which remains nonexistent in this Jurisdiction.

sections.title: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
sections.brief: A philtre is not consent.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords and the prevailing doctrine of Mana Reverence, the Guild hereby establishes a definitive legal distinction between the voluntary exchange of affection and the chemical or magical imposition of desire. It is a foundational principle of the Accords that the sanctity of the individual will is paramount to the stability of the magical weave. Consequently, any substance, enchantment, or ritualistic brew designed to induce, amplify, or manufacture romantic attraction—hereafter referred to as a "Philtre"—shall be categorized as a primary instrument of Undue Influence. The Guild maintains that a Philtre is not consent; the presence of a Philtre does not constitute a waiver of the victim's right to self-determination, nor does it grant the caster any legal standing to claim a consensual union, contract, or physical proximity.

Any mage found to be in possession of a Philtre without a verified Research Permit issued by the Innovators, for the sole purpose of pharmacological study, shall be subject to immediate seizure of the materials. If the Philtre is found to have been deployed upon a sentient being, the offense shall be elevated from a regulatory violation to a criminal act of Arcane Assault. The Aegis Magi are authorized to intervene in any instance where a Philtre is suspected of being in active use. In such cases, the victim shall be granted immediate sanctuary, and the perpetrator shall be detained for a formal hearing. The Guild recognizes that the manipulation of the heart is as perilous as the manipulation of the elements; to bypass the internal defenses of a peer through the use of a Philtre is to violate the core tenets of the Accords and the dignity of the magical community.

Furthermore, the use of a Philtre to secure favors, information, or labor shall be treated as a form of magical coercion. Any agreement entered into under the influence of a Philtre is null and void ab initio. This includes, but is not limited to, the signing of apprenticeship contracts, the relinquishing of magical artifacts, or the granting of access to restricted research sites. If a mage attempts to enforce such an agreement, they shall be held liable for all damages caused to the victim and may face severe penalties under the Paradox Trial for the subversion of free will. The Guild shall not recognize the "Right of Pursuit" in any instance where the pursuit is predicated upon the effects of a Philtre.

The Conservators maintain that the production of Philtres borders on the Unsanctioned Arts due to its inherent violation of the natural order of emotion. Conversely, while the Innovators may study the mechanics of such substances, they are strictly prohibited from testing these substances on any sentient being, including those within the Guild's own ranks. Any research involving the "Love Philtre" must be conducted within a sealed laboratory environment, as defined in § 400.2, and must be accompanied by a certified observer from the Aegis Magi. Failure to comply with these restrictions shall result in the immediate revocation of research privileges and a mandatory period of magical sealing. The Guild's stance is absolute: the magic of the heart is a sacred domain, and its violation through artificial means is a breach of the peace that the Autumnwood Accords were designed to uphold.

body.heading: § 500.5 Love Philtres and Undue Influence
body.text:
A "love philtre," whether by magic, chemical alteration, or other means, shall be deemed an impermissible influence upon the free will of another person and is strictly prohibited under these Accords. See § 1.4 (Persons Bound) for scope of application. Any contract, agreement, or declaration made while under the effect of such a philtre shall be void ab initio; the affected party may seek restitution as if fraud was committed upon them. This prohibition extends to all forms of mind-altering coercion aimed at manipulating emotional states or decision-making capacity in service of another's interests.

Undue influence is similarly forbidden, encompassing any systematic abuse of power dynamics to dominate another's choices regarding personal matters such as marriage, employment, residence, or financial arrangements. See § 100.5 (Conflict of Interest) for related provisions. The burden lies with the accuser to demonstrate actual domination and resulting harm; however, circumstantial evidence combined with witness testimony may suffice where direct proof is unavailable. Repeated offenses constitute a felony punishable by revocation of licensure and permanent disqualification from all Guild activities.

Special care must be taken in evaluating contracts between individuals with pre-existing power imbalances such as mentor-mentee or employer-employee relationships. See § 600.1 (Contracts with Non-Casters) for guidance on capacity. Disparities in knowledge, experience, or resources may render standard provisions unenforceable where they create an unfair advantage to the stronger party. The Desk reserves authority to void such agreements sua sponte upon petition or independent discovery of wrongdoing.

This section complements existing safeguards against magical coercion found in § 500.1 (Field Casting for Value) and § 200.3 (Temporary Mouths). Together they establish a comprehensive framework protecting individuals from exploitation whether by force, fraud, or manipulation of emotion. The Guild remains committed to preserving autonomy as the foundation of all lawful interaction between persons bound hereby. Violators shall be held to strict liability standards given the inherent dangers posed to public safety and moral order.

Archmage Veyra warns all who swear fealty to these Accords: "Thou shalt not steal another's mind or heart by foul means. Such crimes betray the very essence of magecraft itself." Breach of this precept invites swift and severe punishment as outlined in § 100.6 (Delegation to Clerks) for disciplinary matters beyond the Desk's immediate purview. Let it be known that tolerance for such abominations shall remain zero across all sectors under Guild jurisdiction. The preservation of human agency against all forms of subjugation remains paramount to our shared existence as civilized beings capable of self-governance through law rather than brute force alone.

body.heading: Love Philtres and Undue Influence, § 500.5 Love Philtres and Undue Influence
body.text:
A philtre is not consent. The Accords recognize that magical compulsion may render a victim incapable of resisting or comprehending their own actions; yet such force does not constitute valid agreement. Under § 107(2), any contract induced by duress, fraud, or covert enchantment is voidable at the option of the aggrieved party. This provision extends to relationships forged under spells that manipulate emotion, desire, or cognition. The burden lies upon the accuser to prove both the existence of magical interference and its material effect on the alleged agreement. Evidence may include witness testimony, spell traces, or expert analysis—but mere assertion is insufficient to overturn a bond.
