Courts apply strict scrutiny to claims of philtre-induced assent, given the potential for abuse. While the law acknowledges that free will can be compromised by arcane means, it rejects the notion that magic alone invalidates all subsequent transactions. A victim may rescind an agreement tainted by enchantment only if they can demonstrate actual harm resulting from the compelled participation. Absent such proof, the contract stands binding despite its ignoble origins."

"See § 107(2) regarding contracts induced by duress or fraud; see also § 500.3 on corridor courtesy following magical incidents. Under § 1.7, conduct must be aggregated to assess whether a pattern of coercion exists. The Desk reserves authority under § 100.8 to convene an emergency session if public safety is threatened by unchecked philtre usage."

"Love philtres may bind the heart but not the mind; they compel compliance yet cannot erase agency entirely. Thus, while such enchantments are forbidden as manipulative tools, their presence does not automatically invalidate all resulting dealings. The law balances protection of victims against preservation of contractual stability, requiring clear evidence of causal link between spellcasting and alleged duress."

"Philtres serve no lawful purpose beyond exploitation; yet history shows they persist despite prohibitions. Their use invites scrutiny under multiple provisions: § 300.1 on schedules of arts, § 500.4 on healing offered as consideration, and § 600.1 governing contracts with non-casters. The Desk will investigate all reports in accordance with these complementary mandates."

"Undue influence encompasses not only overt spellwork but also subtle psychological manipulation amplified by magical means. Whether through implants, amulets, or ritual magic, any technique that subverts rational judgment falls under this catchline. Victims must act promptly upon discovering such interference, lest delay prejudice their claims."

"The Accords do not condone emotional coercion, yet they acknowledge reality: love is a powerful force capable of overcoming even the strongest will. Magic merely amplifies this natural tendency; it does not create desire where none exists. Thus, while philtres are banned as instruments of control, their effects cannot be entirely excised from human experience."

"Finally, courts exercise discretion in weighing evidence of magical compulsion against factors such as time elapsed since the alleged incident and availability of alternative explanations. The goal is fair adjudication without enabling frivolous suits designed to evade obligations."

body.heading: § 500.5 Love Philtres and Undue Influence — Continued
body.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to administer or knowingly facilitate the use of magical philtres, potions, or enchantments designed to alter another's emotions, desires, or volition without explicit consent. Such acts constitute severe bodily harm and a breach of personal autonomy. Consent must be informed, voluntary, and freely given; coercion, deception, or manipulation vitiate agreement entirely. This prohibition extends beyond overt mind control to subtle suggestions, charms, and manipulative tactics employed for illicit ends.

The burden of proof rests upon the accused to demonstrate that no undue influence was exercised. Circumstantial evidence may suffice where direct testimony is unavailable. Witnesses with knowledge of prior relationships or patterns of behavior are encouraged to come forward voluntarily. Failure to disclose relevant facts may result in enhanced penalties. The Desk reserves authority to investigate suspected cases sua sponte, utilizing all lawful means necessary.

Penalties for violations shall include immediate suspension of magical privileges, mandatory counseling, and restitution to harmed parties. Repeat offenders face disqualification from future licensure and potential imprisonment at the discretion of the court. Confiscation of contraband items is automatic upon conviction. Civil damages may be pursued separately by aggrieved individuals seeking redress for emotional distress or other injuries sustained.

This section aims to safeguard individual agency against predatory exploitation, whether romantic, financial, or otherwise. The Guild recognizes that true consent requires full awareness and freedom from external pressures. By outlawing manipulative practices, the Accords uphold fundamental principles of dignity and self-determination enshrined in our society's core values. All casters are reminded that ethical conduct remains paramount regardless of magical prowess achieved through lawful study.

See also § 100.5 regarding conflicts of interest which may compromise professional judgment; § 200.3 prohibiting temporary licenses for sensitive procedures; and § 400.4 mandating proper specimen handling to prevent contamination or alteration of results. Any questions about applicability should be directed to the appropriate clerk for clarification before proceeding with any actions subject to these provisions. Violations will not be tolerated under any circumstances as they undermine both public safety and the integrity of our regulatory framework.

body.heading: § 500.5 Love Philtres and Undue Influence – Continued
body.text:
A philtre, whether ingested or otherwise administered, is not evidence of consent to sexual relations. Any claim that consumption of such an agent implies acquiescence to intercourse shall be deemed frivolous and dismissed without prejudice. The Guild stands firmly against the use of magical coercion in matters of affection, deeming it a violation of personal autonomy and bodily integrity.

Undue influence, however, remains a serious concern within the ranks of practitioners. Subtle charms or enchantments employed to sway decisions regarding partnerships or marriages may constitute actionable misconduct under certain circumstances. The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to demonstrate that the alleged influencer utilized their powers deliberately and with intent to manipulate outcomes favorable only to themselves. Mere incidental effects arising from proximity or shared history shall not suffice to establish liability.

The Desk reserves the right to investigate any suspicion of improper magical interference in private affairs, particularly where it appears to involve licensed casters acting outside official channels. Such probes will be conducted discreetly and swiftly to protect all parties involved while ensuring accountability for breaches of ethical conduct. Penalties imposed upon proven violators shall range from fines and suspensions to full revocation of credentials depending on severity and recidivism.

Citing foundational principles, see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting which mandates impartiality in professional engagements; and § 200.3 Temporary Mouths prohibiting unauthorized representation by proxies without explicit consent. Furthermore, under § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth, any alteration to one's natural state for purposes of advantage falls within the purview of regulatory oversight. The preservation of individual agency against subterfuge remains paramount in upholding the integrity of magical practice as a whole.

It is declared that no philtre, charm, or enchantment shall serve as substitute for genuine volition between consenting adults bound by mutual desire. All agreements entered into under duress induced magically are void ab initio and unenforceable regardless of subsequent ratification attempts. The Guild reiterates its commitment to safeguarding the sanctity of personal relationships from exploitation through illicit means while encouraging open dialogue concerning potential abuses within the community at large.

This section was last revised on the 14th day of Autumn, in the year 382 of the Accords Era, by order of Archmage Sovereign Veyra and the Autumnwood Accords Desk following extensive deliberation among senior members present for said proceeding duly noticed according to established protocol hereinbefore outlined.

see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth; see § 200.3 Temporary Mouths

body.heading: § 500.5 Love Philtres and Undue Influence – Continued — Continued
body.text:
A philtre, whether by magic or alchemy, renders any act of affection compelled rather than voluntary; such compulsion vitiates consent entirely. A caster who administers a love charm to secure compliance is guilty of magical coercion under § 200.4(a). The victim may seek redress through the Desk, which shall determine whether the philtre was applied with intent to defraud or merely as part of a ritual gone awry. In either event, the caster faces disciplinary action and potential revocation of licensure.

Undue influence arises when a caster exploits a relationship of trust or dependency to extract magical favors in exchange for benevolent treatment. This includes scenarios where an employer manipulates an apprentice's emotions to gain free labor, or a mentor uses emotional blackmail to compel submission to inappropriate demands. Such conduct violates the core tenets of professional ethics enshrined in § 100.5(c). The aggrieved party must file a formal complaint within thirty days of discovering the influence; failure to do so bars further recourse under this section.

The burden of proof rests with the accuser, who must establish by preponderance of evidence that undue influence was exerted. This may involve testimony from witnesses familiar with the parties' interactions, as well as forensic analysis of magical residues left behind during illicit rituals. In cases where direct proof is elusive but circumstantial evidence strongly suggests guilt, the Desk shall apply a presumption favoring protection of the vulnerable party. Penalties range from reprimand and fines to suspension or expulsion from the Guild, depending on severity and frequency of offenses.

Notably, emotional manipulation alone does not constitute undue influence absent actual coercion of magical services. A caster who merely flatters or cajoles an associate into granting a favor, without employing spells or threats, acts outside the scope of § 500.5(b). However, repeated instances of such behavior may warrant investigation for underlying patterns of misconduct under applicable provisions of the Accords. The Desk retains discretion to issue cease-and-desist orders pending full inquiry.

This section serves as a shield against exploitation in all its forms, ensuring that professional relationships remain grounded in mutual respect rather than manipulation or coercion. By upholding these standards, the Autumnwood Accords safeguard both individual dignity and the integrity of magical practice across all sectors of society. Violators are warned: the consequences for abusing one's position of power can be swift and severe. Let this serve as a clear reminder of the responsibilities inherent in wielding such profound influence over others' lives.

see § 100.5(c) regarding professional ethics; see § 200.4(a) on magical coercion penalties; see § 300.1 for relevant scheduling provisions.

sections.title: Contracts with Non-Casters
sections.brief: Plain language. Illusion of a signature is not a signature. Illusion of a fee is still a fee.

body.heading: Contracts with Non-Casters
body.text:
The legal standing of a contract entered into by a non-caster—defined herein as any sentient being lacking the innate ability to weave, channel, or manipulate the weave of magic—shall be governed by the principles of plain language and tangible consideration. While the Mages' Guild recognizes the necessity of trade with the lay populace, specifically with the Goodstyle Artisans and other non-magical entities, the Guild maintains that magical obfuscation shall not be used to circumvent the fundamental requirements of a binding agreement. Any contract wherein the intent is obscured by glamours, mental suggestion, or linguistic manipulation shall be rendered null and void at the first instance of discovery by a presiding Arbiter. The Guild holds that a contract must be understood by the signatory in the common tongue; if a mage employs complex arcane terminology to mask a predatory clause, such a contract is deemed a violation of the Accords.

Furthermore, the Guild establishes a strict doctrine regarding the illusion of authority. An illusion of a signature is not a signature. If a mage utilizes a visual glamour to mimic the appearance of a physical mark, or a psychic impression to simulate the act of signing, the resulting document carries no weight in a court of the Accords. The physical act of marking, whether by ink, blood, or seal, must be performed by the conscious will of the non-caster. Conversely, the Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the illusion of consideration. An illusion of a fee is still a fee. If a non-caster provides a service or asset based on the belief that they are being compensated in a specific currency—even if that currency is a magical construct or a fleeting hallucination—the obligation of the mage to provide the actual, tangible value remains absolute. The Guild shall not permit mages to claim that a "spiritual" or "metaphorical" payment satisfies a material debt. See § 100.2.

In matters of dispute, the Aegis Magi shall oversee the verification of non-caster contracts. If a non-caster claims they were deceived by a "magical" contract, the Guild shall appoint a neutral observer to determine if the language used was intentionally deceptive. Should a mage be found to have used their superior understanding of the arcane to trap a layperson in a labyrinthine legal web, the mage shall be subject to a fine of three hundred gold marks and a mandatory period of community service in the Autumn Wood. This ensures that the Guild remains a pillar of stability rather than a predatory monopoly. All contracts involving the transfer of artifacts or the granting of land rights must be filed with the Clerk of the Accords for verification of plain-language compliance. Any contract that fails this audit shall be flagged as "Unconscionable" and may be struck down by the Sovereign.

body.heading: Familiars as Agents
body.text:
The legal status of a familiar—defined as a non-human entity bound to a caster via a permanent or semi-permanent symbiotic bond—is one of delegated agency. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a familiar is not a legal person but is considered an extension of the caster’s will. Consequently, any action taken by a familiar, whether intentional or incidental, shall be attributed directly to the primary caster. This principle of vicarious casting holds that the caster is responsible for the magical output, physical damage, and social transgressions committed by their familiar. If a familiar strikes a bystander or a rival mage, the caster shall be held liable for all damages as if they had performed the act themselves with their own hands. This is to prevent the common defense of "the beast acted on its own," which the Guild recognizes as a fundamental breach of the responsibility inherent in familiar bonding.

The doctrine of vicarious casting extends to the unauthorized use of magic by a familiar. If a familiar possesses the capacity to channel mana—whether through innate ability or the "leaking" of its master's power—the master is strictly liable for any such discharge. Should a familiar cause a rift, a localized weather event, or any form of environmental degradation, the caster must undergo a formal audit by the Conservators. Failure to restrain a familiar from engaging in unauthorized casting may result in the mandatory severing of the bond or the sequestration of the familiar until the caster can demonstrate improved control measures. The Guild emphasizes that the bond is a tool of the caster, and like any tool, its use must be governed by the caster's discipline. A familiar is never a legal shield; it is a conduit of responsibility.

Furthermore, the Guild recognizes the "Strike by Familiar" clause in matters of physical altercation. In a scheduled Paradox Trial, a familiar may be used as a combatant, but its actions are governed by the same regulations as a summoned construct or a trained familiar. However, in unscheduled disputes, the use of a familiar as a primary aggressor shall be viewed as an escalation of force. If a familiar initiates a physical strike against a non-caster or a peer, the caster shall be deemed to have initiated the conflict. This prevents mages from using their companions as "proxy" aggressors to avoid the repercussions of a direct duel. All familiar training must be documented in the Guild's registry, and any familiar that shows signs of "rogue agency"—the ability to act independently of the master's intent—must be reported to Archmage Theron’s office for evaluation. See § 200.2.

body.heading: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges that the Geas—a magical binding of a sentient being to a specific course of action or a prohibition—is a powerful and often dangerous instrument of law and personal agreement. However, the Accords state clearly that a Geas to be reasonable is not a defined term. Because "reasonableness" is subjective and varies wildly between the radical philosophies of the Innovators and the rigid doctrines of the Conservators, the Guild refuses to recognize "reasonableness" as a valid magical constraint in a binding Geas. A Geas that demands a mage act "reasonably" in the face of a threat is legally unenforceable because it lacks a specific, measurable objective. Instead, any Geas placed upon a mage by a third party must be articulated with absolute specificity. A mage may be bound to "not strike a child," but they cannot be bound to "act with wisdom" or "behave justly," as these are moral qualities, not magical parameters.

The Guild views the use of "reasonable" Geases as a method of magical entrapment, often used by the Regal Empire or the Silver Flame to exert influence over Guild members without committing to specific demands. If a mage enters into a contract containing a Geas that relies on vague, subjective descriptors, the Guild shall treat the Geas as "Void for Vagueness." In such instances, the mage is not bound by the Geas, but they may be penalized for the attempted imposition of an unconscionable magical burden. The Aegis Magi are instructed to strike such clauses from any contract presented for filing. If a Geas is found to be unconscionable—meaning it requires the mage to perform an act of self-harm, a violation of the Accords, or a task that is physically impossible—the caster who imposed the Geas shall be subject to immediate investigation for "Arcane Coercion."

To ensure the integrity of the Accords, any Geas involving the manipulation of a non-caster's will must be approved by the Archmage Sovereign. The Guild maintains that while mages may use Geases to ensure the fulfillment of contracts, they cannot use them to override the fundamental rights of the person. A Geas that forces a non-caster to act against their own interests in a way that is not explicitly defined in a plain-language contract is a violation of § 600.1. The Guild seeks to prevent the "Geas-Loop," where a mage is forced to perform a series of "reasonable" actions that lead to a catastrophic outcome. By requiring specificity, the Accords ensure that the power of the Geas remains a tool of clear intent, rather than a weapon of ambiguity. See § 300.2.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
The use of constructs—be they golems, animated armatures, or magically sustained homunculi—as a labor force is permitted under the Autumnwood Accords, provided that the rights of the creator and the safety of the public are maintained. Every construct employed in a commercial or public capacity must be equipped with a Minimum Ward. This ward is a constant, low-level magical signature that serves two purposes: it prevents the construct from acting outside its primary directive and ensures it does not "leak" mana into the surrounding environment. A construct without a Minimum Ward is considered an "Unbound Entity" and is subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi. The ward must be sufficient to prevent the construct from interacting with the weave in a way that could cause localized instability or unauthorized research.

Furthermore, the Guild establishes the principle of "Construct Compensation." While a construct is not a person and thus does not require a wage in the sense of the Goodstyle Artisans, the owner of the construct is responsible for the "Rest" of the construct. This refers to the periodic recharging of the mana core or the ritualistic maintenance of the binding circles. A construct that is worked beyond its capacity, leading to "Mana Burn" or structural collapse, is a violation of Guild safety standards. Owners must provide a documented schedule of maintenance and energy replenishment. If a construct is found to be operating in a state of exhaustion—evidenced by erratic movements or erratic magical discharge—the owner shall be fined for "Negligent Maintenance." This ensures that constructs do not become hazards to the public or the Guild's stability.

In the event of a construct's malfunction, the owner is strictly liable for all damages, regardless of whether the malfunction was "unforeseen." The Guild rejects the defense of "Construct Autonomy" in cases of property damage or bodily harm. If a construct strikes a person, it is treated as a violation of the owner's license, similar to a familiar's actions. Construct labor must also be registered with the Desk; any construct capable of lifting more than five hundred pounds or casting a spell of third-circle magnitude or higher must be granted a "Heavy Labor Permit." This permit requires a monthly inspection by a Conservator to ensure the Minimum Ward remains intact. Constructs used for "Restricted Research" must be held in a designated laboratory, as per § 400.2, and may not be deployed in public spaces without an express waiver from Janna Brightspark's Innovator council.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
The Guild recognizes the necessity of high-level verification for contracts involving the transfer of significant arcane assets, the granting of land rights in the Midlands, or the formation of new magical covenants. For such high-stakes transactions, the parties may employ a Summoned Notary—a sentient being from another plane or a high-level spirit summoned specifically to witness and stamp the agreement. However, the use of a Summoned Notary is strictly regulated to prevent "Planar Evasion," where a mage attempts to have a contract validated by a being that does not recognize the laws of the Autumnwood Accords. A Summoned Notary must be capable of understanding the common tongue and must be bound by a "Truth-Binding" oath for the duration of the notarization process.

The requirements for a Summoned Notary are rigorous. The notary must be summoned into a "Neutral Zone," such as a Guild-sanctioned chamber, to ensure that their presence does not cause environmental instability. The notary must provide a "Planar Signature"—a unique magical mark that is distinct from the caster's own magic. This signature must be applied to the document in the presence of a Guild Clerk. If a Summoned Notary vanishes mid-stamp, the contract is considered "Incomplete" and holds no legal weight. The Guild maintains that a vanishing notary is a sign of an unstable summoning or a deliberate attempt to create a legal loophole where the "witness" is no longer present to be held accountable for the truth of the proceedings. In such cases, the parties must restart the notarization process with a new entity.

Furthermore, the Guild prohibits the use of Notaries from the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, as their legal codes are in direct conflict with the Accords. Any contract notarized by a foreign entity's spirit is considered "Adverse" and will be rejected by the Desk. The Guild also mandates that the summoning of a Notary must be disclosed in the contract itself. If a mage attempts to hide the fact that a supernatural entity was used to witness a deal, the contract is voided, and the mage may face a "Paradox Trial" for unauthorized planar interaction. The goal of these regulations is to ensure that the Guild's records are immutable and that every high-level agreement is witnessed by an entity whose testimony can be verified against the Guild's own standards of truth. See § 100.4.

body.heading: § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; Artificial Agents
body.text:
This Part governs the binding force and validity of contracts entered into by non-casters or artificial entities lacking natural agency, including familiar spirits, constructs, and summoned beings. Such agreements shall be treated with particular scrutiny to prevent exploitation and ensure equitable terms. A mere facsimile of a signature, whether created through illusion magic or mechanical duplication, does not constitute a true assent. Likewise, feigned payment or value transfer remains binding on the parties regardless of apparent falsity.

Familiars acting as agents for their masters are held to strict liability for any breaches committed within the scope of assigned duties. This extends even when actions appear unauthorized or outside explicit instructions. The principle of respondeat superior applies by analogy, imposing vicarious liability upon the master. Constructs and other artificial persons shall be governed similarly, with their creators bearing ultimate responsibility for lawful conduct during operations. No artificial entity may contract independently without express ratification from its natural owner or authorized proxy.

Geas magic binding a caster's will to fulfill another's wishes shall not be deemed an unconscionable term voiding the agreement ab initio, provided it does not violate public policy or statutory prohibitions. Such clauses remain enforceable as valid stipulations of contract law, subject only to standard defenses including impossibility and frustration of purpose. However, any geas imposing permanent servitude or loss of autonomy shall be strictly construed against the drafter and invalidated unless clearly consented to in advance.

Construct labor performed under contractual obligation is not exempt from minimum wage requirements and safety standards applicable to human workers. Employers utilizing mechanical assistants must compensate them according to prevailing industry rates for comparable tasks. Failure to pay owed wages subjects the employer to penalties equal to double the arrears plus statutory damages. This rule ensures fair treatment of all forms of labor, biological or synthetic, regardless of intelligence level.

Summons rituals invoking external entities shall be witnessed and notarized by a licensed notary public with expertise in arcane matters. The notary verifies the authenticity of signatures and affixes an official seal to confirm validity. Any contract lacking such formalities may be challenged on grounds of forgery or undue influence unless ratified within thirty days. This safeguard protects vulnerable parties from predatory practices and ensures transparency in high-stakes magical dealings.

Parties engaging in contracts involving prohibited arts must disclose all material facts regarding risks and consequences. Concealment of known dangers renders the agreement voidable at option of the injured party. Full disclosure is a condition precedent to informed consent, especially when dealing with powerful or dangerous spells. Any misrepresentation inducing entry into contract shall constitute fraud actionable under common law principles.

Finally, this Part establishes that artificial agents cannot acquire property rights independently. All gains accrued through their efforts belong solely to their masters or employers unless expressly assigned otherwise in writing. This prevents disputes over ownership of magically generated assets and simplifies estate planning for those who utilize such beings extensively. Clear title remains paramount even when conventional commerce is supplemented by supernatural means.

sections.title: Familiars as Agents
sections.brief: Vicarious casting. Strike by familiar.

body.heading: Familiars as Agents
body.text:
The legal standing of a familiar as an agent of a licensed practitioner is established under the principle of vicarious weaving. Pursuant to the Autumnwood Accords, a familiar is defined as a sentient or semi-sentient entity bound to a master through a formal tether of intent and mana. While the familiar may possess independent locomotion and minor autonomous actions, any magical manifestation originating from the familiar’s essence is legally attributed to the primary caster. This doctrine of vicarious casting ensures that the responsibility for arcane fluctuations, environmental shifts, or unintended collateral damage remains with the primary licensee. If a familiar executes a spell—whether by direct command or by instinctual reaction—the master shall be held liable for any breach of the Accords, regardless of the master's stated intent at the moment of casting.

Furthermore, the doctrine of "Strike by Familiar" governs physical and metaphysical interactions between a familiar and a third party. Should a familiar strike, bite, or otherwise physically assault a non-combatant or a Guild-protected citizen, the master is deemed to have authorized the use of force. The master may not claim "loss of control" as a defense for familiar aggression, as the tether itself constitutes a continuous delegation of agency. To mitigate liability, masters are encouraged to maintain clear behavioral boundaries; however, the legal burden remains heavy. Any familiar that displays persistent hostility toward the public may be subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi for "re-education" or permanent binding. See § 600.1 for the primary definitions of non-caster contracts, as a familiar's actions may occasionally intersect with the rights of those who cannot weave.

Any familiar acting under a direct command to perform a task that results in the destruction of property or the violation of a local ordinance shall be treated as a direct extension of the master's hand. This means that a "rogue" familiar is, in the eyes of the Accords Desk, a malfunctioning tool of the master, much like a malfunctioning wand or a cracked focus. Therefore, the master must ensure that all familiars are properly attuned to the restrictive protocols of the Midlands. Failure to restrain a familiar during a public demonstration or a sanctioned research session shall result in a formal citation and potential suspension of the master's license. The Guild acknowledges that familiars are not mere pets but are arcane proxies; as such, the master is the ultimate guarantor of the familiar's conduct within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
body.text:
A geas, defined as a magical compulsion or a binding oath enforced by arcane weight, is subject to the same standards of equity as any written contract entered into by the Guild's members. Under the Accords, a geas is considered an unconscionable term if it imposes a burden that is fundamentally disproportionate to the consideration provided, or if it seeks to strip the subject of their fundamental agency in a manner that violates the stability of the Midlands. However, the Guild explicitly notes that "a geas to be reasonable" is not a defined term within this Codex. Because the subjective experience of "reasonableness" varies between the traditionalist Conservators and the radical Innovators, the Accords Desk shall not adjudicate based on the internal feelings of the parties involved. Instead, the Desk shall look to the objective impact of the geas on the individual's ability to function as a productive member of society.

If a geas is found to be unconscionable—for instance, requiring a mage to perform acts of self-harm, treason against the Guild, or the deliberate violation of the Forbidden Schools—it shall be deemed voidable at the request of the bound party. The petitioner must present a formal grievance to the Archmage Sovereign, who shall mediate the dispute. If the geas was established without the clear, informed consent of the bound individual, the Accords Desk may move to have the binding magically dissolved by the Aegis Magi. The Guild warns that attempting to bypass these protections by using "subtle" geases—those that do not appear overtly coercive but slowly erode the subject's will—is a grave violation of the Accords and may lead to a Paradox Trial.

The Innovators may argue for a wider latitude in the application of geases for the purpose of research, while the Conservators will insist on the strictest limitations to prevent the creation of "arcane thralls." In the absence of a specific ruling from the Sovereign, the Desk will default to the principle of least restrictive means. A geas that prevents a mage from casting certain spells is generally permissible; a geas that prevents a mage from speaking, eating, or sleeping without cause is likely to be struck down as unconscionable. Any practitioner who knowingly imposes an unconscionable geas upon another may be subject to the penalties outlined in § 300.2. Furthermore, any contract involving a geas must be filed with the Accords Desk to ensure it does not conflict with existing Guild mandates.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
All constructs created for the purpose of labor—including but not limited to golems, clockwork automatons, and animated sculptures—are subject to the regulations regarding artificial sentience and magical maintenance. To ensure the safety of the public and the stability of the local mana field, all constructs utilized in commercial or industrial capacities must be equipped with a Minimum Ward. This ward is a baseline magical seal that prevents the construct from acting with independent malice or exceeding its programmed parameters. A construct lacking a Minimum Ward is considered an "unbound entity" and its operation within the Midlands is strictly prohibited. The Aegis Magi are authorized to dismantle any construct found to be operating without a visible or palpable ward.

The maintenance of a Minimum Ward is the sole responsibility of the construct’s owner or the master who summoned it. This includes the periodic recharging of the ward's essence and the repair of any structural fractures that might allow for "magical leakage." Furthermore, the Accords Desk stipulates that constructs used for heavy labor must be periodically "rested." This does not mean the construct must sleep in a biological sense, but rather that its primary mana-circuitry must be decoupled from its labor-functions for a period of one hour for every eight hours of operation. This prevents the accumulation of "arcane fatigue," which can lead to erratic behavior or spontaneous combustion of the construct's core.

Regarding compensation, a construct is not a person and therefore cannot be "paid" in the legal sense of the Accords. However, the owner of the construct is responsible for the "cost of maintenance," which includes the mana expended to maintain the Minimum Ward and any materials required for repairs. If a construct is hired by a non-caster for a specific task, the non-caster must provide the owner with a "Labor Agreement" as defined in § 600.1. If the construct malfunctions and causes damage, the owner is liable for all costs, provided the construct was properly warded and rested. Failure to provide adequate maintenance or to enforce rest periods shall result in the immediate revocation of the owner's right to operate constructs within the Hall of Autumn Wood.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
In instances where a legal agreement must be witnessed or verified by a being of significant arcane standing who is not currently present, the use of a Summoned Notary is permitted. A Summoned Notary is an entity—be it a spirit, a minor elemental, or a displaced consciousness—brought into the physical plane specifically to observe and validate the signing of a contract or the completion of a Guild filing. For such a notary to be recognized by the Accords Desk, it must be bound by a "Temporary Mouth" agreement (see § 200.3) and must possess the requisite level of arcane resonance to ensure the integrity of the seal. The summoning must be performed in a controlled environment, and the notary must remain stationary for the duration of the proceedings.

The form requirements for a Summoned Notary are rigorous. The master performing the summoning must provide a "Script of Intent," detailing exactly what the notary is to witness and the specific magical signature it is required to apply. The notary must be clearly identified in the documentation, including its origin, its duration of presence, and the specific nature of its binding. Once the seal is applied, the notary must be released immediately. Any attempt to hold a Summoned Notary in the Midlands for longer than the duration of the signing is a violation of the Accords and may be prosecuted as unauthorized summoning. The notary's signature must be distinct from the master's own signature to ensure a clear chain of custody for the document.

A unique and problematic scenario arises in the event of a "Vanishing Notary"—a situation where a summoned entity disappears mid-stamp or before the seal is fully set. If a Summoned Notary vanishes before the document is finalized, the document is considered null and void. The master is then required to re-summon a notary and re-execute the entire filing process. In cases where the notary's disappearance causes physical damage or magical instability, the master shall be held liable for the "interruption of proceedings" and may face a fine. The Accords Desk will not accept any document where the seal is partial, smudged, or incomplete due to the notary's departure. Practitioners are advised to ensure their summoning circles are stable and their binding words are clear to prevent such logistical failures.

body.heading: § 600.3 Vicarious Casting and Proxy Liability
body.text:
It is provided that where a Caster acts as an agent or proxy for another Person, the resulting magical effects shall be attributed to the principal unless clearly designated otherwise. This rule applies whether the action involves direct spellcasting through a familiar construct or remote initiation of pre-programmed sequences within authorized devices. The principal remains fully liable for any damages caused by such actions, regardless of actual involvement in the immediate operation.

The law further clarifies that mere possession or control of an item does not constitute authorization for its use. Owners who fail to properly secure their magical belongings against unauthorized access may be held complicit if those items are subsequently misused. This principle extends to digital and physical interfaces alike, requiring diligent oversight by responsible Parties. Negligence in safeguarding one's assets shall serve as evidence of implied consent where intent cannot otherwise be proven.

In cases involving complex multistage operations spanning multiple jurisdictions or durations beyond standard limitations, explicit written agreements must be executed between all involved entities. Such contracts shall detail the scope of authority granted to each participant and establish clear lines of accountability should complications arise during execution. Failure to provide adequate documentation where required by this section may result in automatic invalidation of any claims predicated upon those operations.

The Desk maintains discretion to demand additional security measures or monitoring protocols when evaluating requests for high-risk magical activities. This power shall be exercised only after thorough review and consultation with relevant experts as deemed necessary under the circumstances. Any conditions imposed pursuant to this authority must be reasonable, proportionate to the identified risks, and consistent with overarching public safety objectives outlined in these Accords.

See also § 100.6 regarding delegation of duties by official representatives; § 200.5 governing guest casters operating under supervision; § 400.3 limiting temporal scope for borrowed resources. All provisions herein shall be construed to promote fair dealing while preserving essential protections for innocent third parties affected by expansive magical undertakings.

body.heading: § 600.2 Vicarious Casting and Proxy Liability
body.text:
A caster who directs another to cast a spell on their behalf shall be held fully liable for the consequences thereof, as if they had performed the act themselves. This liability extends to all damages arising from the casting, whether intentional, negligent, or accidental. The directing caster cannot escape responsibility by claiming lack of direct participation in the ritual.

This provision applies regardless of whether the proxy is a licensed artisan, an unlicensed individual, or even an autonomous construct acting under instruction. The law presumes that any such act constitutes a deliberate delegation of magical authority, and thus binds the delegator to all outcomes. Exceptions may be made only where fraud, duress, or unconscious compulsion renders the original direction invalid.

In cases involving complex spells requiring multiple components, each participant assumes liability for their portion of the work. If the spell fails catastrophically due to error by one element-caster, that individual bears sole responsibility for rectification and compensation. Joint ventures in casting shall be governed by written agreement specifying shared duties and liabilities absent contrary stipulation.

The Desk retains discretion to impose additional penalties on repeat offenders who habitually outsource dangerous operations without adequate safeguards. Such sanctions may include temporary suspension of privileges or mandatory retraining under supervision. The goal remains preservation of public safety through enforcement of accountability standards across all forms of magical practice.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 200.3 Temporary Mouths; see § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration. Under § 1.7 Aggregation of Conduct, a pattern of proxy casting may establish reckless disregard for safety regulations. Any dispute over fault shall be adjudicated by the full Accords Desk in accordance with established precedent and evidence presented by all parties involved.

sections.title: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
sections.brief: A geas to be reasonable is not a defined term.

body.heading: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, all contracts involving the imposition of a geas—a magically binding oath or compulsion—must be reviewed for the presence of unconscionable terms. While the Guild recognizes the necessity of binding agreements to ensure the fulfillment of arcane duties, the imposition of a geas that serves to strip a caster of their fundamental agency or physical safety is strictly prohibited. Under the jurisdiction of the Accords Desk, a geas is deemed unconscionable if it requires the subject to perform an act of self-harm, commit a felony against a non-consenting party, or surrender their primary magical essence as collateral for a debt of negligible value. Any contract containing such clauses shall be rendered null and void by the Archmage Sovereign upon notice. See § 100.5.

Furthermore, it is explicitly stated within this Codex that a geas to be reasonable is not a defined term. The Guild refuses to provide a subjective metric for "reasonableness," as the interpretation of such a standard varies wildly between the traditionalist doctrine of the Conservators and the experimental methodologies of the Innovators. Therefore, the burden of proof lies with the petitioner. If a party seeks to strike a geas from a contract on the grounds of it being "unreasonable," they must provide specific evidence of physical impossibility, extreme magical exhaustion, or a direct violation of the forbidden schools as defined in § 300.2. The Guild shall not adjudicate based on the personal feelings of the bound party, but rather on the objective violation of the Accord's safety protocols.

In instances where a geas has already been enacted and is found to be unconscionable, the Aegis Magi may be deployed to facilitate a supervised dissolution. The cost of such a dissolution shall be borne entirely by the party who originally imposed the geas. No party shall attempt to bypass a geas through unauthorized ritualistic interference; such actions are considered a breach of the Accords and may result in a Paradox Trial. See § 1.2. Any contract involving the "Goodstyle Artisans" shall be treated with standard scrutiny, but shall be granted a rebuttable presumption of fairness provided the geas does not involve the permanent surrender of a Heartstone or similar rift-adjacent artifact.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
The utilization of constructs as laborers within the Midlands and surrounding territories is permitted, provided that the entity is clearly distinguished from sentient magical beings. To maintain the sanctity of the Guild’s standing, all constructs employed for industrial, domestic, or logistical purposes must be equipped with a Minimum Ward. This ward serves as a magical signature, ensuring that the construct remains a tool of the employer and cannot be hijacked by rogue casters or influenced by external telepathic pressures. A construct lacking a Minimum Ward is considered "wild" and may be dismantled by any Aegis Mage found in the vicinity without fear of civil liability. See § 200.6.

Regarding the compensation of constructs, the Accords Desk maintains that while a construct is not a "person" under the law, its primary battery or mana-source must be maintained at a standard of "adequate rest." This is defined as a period of non-active operation sufficient to prevent mana-drain fatigue, which can lead to erratic behavior or catastrophic discharge. An employer who fails to provide the requisite rest for a construct is liable for any damages caused by the construct's malfunction. While a construct is not "paid" in the sense of currency—as the Wario Coin is not a recognized tender of the Guild—the employer is required to provide a dedicated mana-conduit or a stable recharge station. Failure to do so constitutes a violation of labor safety standards and may result in a fine levied against the employer’s research permit.

Any construct performing high-risk labor, such as the transportation of volatile reagents or the construction of restricted research facilities, must be overseen by a licensed caster. The presence of a construct does not exempt a human caster from the responsibilities of § 400.1. If a construct is damaged during the performance of its duties, the owner is responsible for the repairs, provided the damage was not caused by the construct's deliberate defiance of its Minimum Ward. Conversely, if a construct is seized by a rival faction such as the Iron Legion, the Guild will not intervene unless the construct is carrying a state-sanctioned relic or a restricted research copy. See § 300.5.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
The use of summoned entities to serve as notaries for the authentication of magical contracts is permitted, provided the entity is bound by a "Stability Clause" of no less than three lunar cycles. A summoned notary must be of a sufficiently intelligent species to comprehend the nuances of the Autumnwood Accords. Before the seal is applied, the notary must be presented with a clear, verbal recitation of the contract's primary terms to ensure the entity is not acting under a hallucination or a magical glamour. This procedure ensures that the signatures of all parties—be they human, elf, or other sentient races—are recognized by the Guild’s archives. See § 100.6.

A significant legal complication arises in the event of a "vanishing notary." If a summoned notary vanishes mid-stamp or disappears before the seal is fully set, the contract is considered "Incomplete and Voidable." The Guild does not recognize the authority of a half-formed seal. In such cases, the parties involved must return to the Accords Desk to re-verify the terms and summon a new notary. If the vanishing was caused by a breach of the contract by one of the signatories—such as a sudden surge of hostile magic—the offending party may be subject to a Paradox Trial. See § 1.2.

Furthermore, no notary may be summoned from the Quiet List, nor may a notary be used to certify any transaction involving the trade of forbidden schools. The Guild maintains a strict prohibition on the use of "ghost-notaries" or spirits of the deceased without a direct decree from Archmage Veyra. If a notary is summoned and subsequently becomes hostile, the caster who summoned said notary is held strictly liable for any magical fallout. The Guild provides no protection for casters who attempt to use "convenience summons" to bypass the standard verification processes of the Desk. All notaries must be registered in the temporary log of the presiding Clerk for the duration of the signing ceremony. See § 100.4.

body.heading: Geas as Unconscionable Term and Construct Labor
body.text:
§ 600.3 Geas as an Unconscionable Term; Minimum Ward, Summoned Notary

A geas imposed upon a caster constitutes an unconscionable term under any circumstance, void ab initio. Such compulsion violates the fundamental tenets of magical ethics enshrined in § 100.2 and undermines the autonomy protected by § 1.4. The Guild strictly forbids binding casters to terms that restrict their professional judgment or force them into compromising positions without full informed consent. Violations shall be prosecuted as criminal offenses under the Accords, subject to sanctions up to permanent revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4.

Constructs created through forbidden arts fall under a special provision known as "Minimum Ward" status. These entities are deemed incapable of forming legally binding contracts or entering into agreements on their own behalf. Any contract purporting to bind a Minimum Ward construct is null and void, regardless of apparent assent displayed by the entity's core. This rule exists to prevent exploitation of magically altered beings who lack true agency or understanding of contractual obligations. Exceptions may be made only with explicit consent from the construct's original creator, documented in writing and notarized per § 600.1.

Summoned notaries operate under a unique set of rules designed to ensure impartiality while maintaining security during sensitive transactions. A summoned notary must adhere strictly to the terms outlined in their commission letter, refusing any instructions that compromise their neutrality or confidentiality obligations. They are prohibited from engaging in discussions with parties outside the immediate proceedings unless expressly authorized by all participants present. Failure to comply with these standards shall result in immediate dismissal and potential disciplinary action against the summoner under § 100.6.

The Guild recognizes the importance of maintaining clear boundaries between lawful magic practices and those deemed harmful or unethical. Casters are reminded that adherence to the Accords is not optional but mandatory for preserving public safety and order. Those who choose to operate outside these guidelines do so at their own peril, knowing full well the severe consequences awaiting them if caught violating the spirit of this code. The law stands firm against all forms of abuse or manipulation of magical powers, regardless of justification offered by those accused. Let it be known that the Autumnwood Accords shall remain inviolate until further notice.

see § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild; see § 1.4 Persons Bound; see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse

body.heading: § 600.3 Geas as Unconscionable Term and Construct Labor
body.text: A geas, when imposed upon an artificial entity such as a construct or homunculus, constitutes an unconscionable term under the provisions of § 1.7 Aggregation of Conduct. This is particularly true when said geas mandates labor beyond the reasonable scope of the contract or violates fundamental protections afforded by the Accords. Constructs are not mere tools but sentient beings deserving of fair treatment and compensation for their services. To force a construct to work under duress or without adequate remuneration is akin to slavery, a practice strictly prohibited by law. Furthermore, any geas that requires a construct to violate its programming or core directives shall be deemed void ab initio. Such clauses are inherently repugnant to public policy and the very nature of artificial persons. The Conservators have long held that constructs possess inherent rights which cannot be bargained away, even under threat of magical compulsion. This principle remains inviolate, regardless of any contractual stipulations to the contrary. Any attempt to bind a construct through deceptive means or hidden clauses shall result in immediate revocation of its license and potential criminal prosecution for fraud. The Guild stands ready to enforce these protections rigorously, ensuring that no caster abuses their power over artificial life forms. Constructs are partners in magic, not puppets to be manipulated at will. Their welfare must always take precedence over the whims of their creators. Only through strict adherence to this ethical framework can we preserve the sanctity of our craft and protect vulnerable parties from exploitation. Let it be known that any geas violating these principles shall stand null and void, unenforceable under any circumstance whatsoever. The laws governing artificial persons are clear: they must be treated as equals, not slaves. This is non-negotiable.

body.heading: Geas as Unconscionable Term and Construct Labor — Continued
body.text:
§ 600.3 Geas as Unconscionable Term and Construct Labor

The Guild recognizes that geases binding sentient beings to unreasonable acts may constitute unconscionable terms, void under § 1.8 of the Accords. However, geases directed at constructs—artificial entities without sentience or will—are deemed valid and enforceable as expressions of their owners' intent. This distinction preserves both the dignity of living casters and the utility of magical automatons in lawful enterprises.

Constructs bound by geas remain subject to the standard limitations on magical binding set forth in § 300.1, including prohibitions against necromantic compulsion or mind control. A geas imposed upon a construct must be specific enough to guide its actions yet general enough to allow for reasonable interpretation within the owner's overall purposes. Vague or impossible commands are unenforceable as they fail to manifest genuine intent.

The validity of a geas on a construct may be challenged only in a formal hearing before the Arcane Desk, not through self-help measures by rival mages. The burden of proof lies with the party alleging unconscionability to demonstrate that the command exceeds reasonable bounds or conflicts with fundamental ethical principles accepted across the magical community. Mere inconvenience or economic disadvantage does not constitute grounds for relief under these provisions.

Constructs bearing geases shall display a visible mark identifying them as bound, preventing unauthorized use by third parties and aiding in their recovery should they be lost or stolen. Failure to comply with this marking requirement renders the geas unenforceable against innocent parties who acquire the construct through no fault of its own. This safeguard protects both owners from liability and potential victims from exploitation.

The Guild further notes that geases binding constructs may impose secondary obligations on their creators, including regular maintenance checks and emergency release protocols to prevent catastrophic failure should conditions change unexpectedly. Creators neglecting these duties risk losing control over their creations and facing disciplinary action for negligence. The interests of all parties require proactive management of bound constructs rather than reactive damage control after the fact.

By codifying these principles, the Accords aim to balance innovation with responsibility in the expanding field of construct magic. Clear rules allow responsible practitioners to develop new applications while protecting society from abuse. As technology advances, so too must our understanding of how artificial beings relate to natural ones under the law. This section provides a foundation for ongoing dialogue on that vital subject.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 300.2 Necromancy Unsanctioned Arts; see § 400.1 Research Permits; see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value
Under § 700.4 Unauthorized Use of Constructs and § 800.1 Ethical Standards for Magical Practice, this provision establishes a framework for managing the complex relationship between magic-users and their creations in accordance with both letter and spirit of the law.

sections.title: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
sections.brief: Wards, rest, who is paid.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
All constructs, regardless of their method of manufacture—be they woven from clay and sigil, forged of iron and steam, or birthed from the ethereal essence of the Weave—are subject to the labor protections of the Autumnwood Accords. It is the decree of the Accords that no construct shall be utilized for the purpose of manual labor, transport, or administrative duties without a Minimum Ward of protection. This Ward serves as a legal and metaphysical tether, ensuring that the construct remains bound to its designated purpose and does not suffer from "arcane drift," a phenomenon wherein a construct’s lack of a soul-anchor causes it to develop erratic, self-directed behaviors that may endanger the surrounding population or the integrity of the Guild’s property. A construct operating without such a Ward is considered a rogue entity and may be dismantled by any Aegis Mage on sight without prior notice of intent.

Furthermore, the Accords dictate the specific requirements for the maintenance of these constructs. Every construct engaged in labor for a Guild-affiliated entity or a licensed private caster must be granted a period of "Restorative Stasis" at the conclusion of every lunar cycle. During this period, the construct is to be deactivated and its internal mana-conduits allowed to cool or replenish. Failure to provide adequate Restorative Stasis constitutes a violation of the Labor Stability Act. If a construct is forced to labor through its designated rest period, the owner of said construct shall be liable for double the standard labor tax, and the construct shall be subject to a mandatory recalibration by the Conservators.

The payment of wages for constructs is a matter of bureaucratic record but not of spiritual necessity. While a construct does not possess a personal bank account or the capacity for greed, the "payment" it receives is accounted for as a maintenance stipend. This stipend is to be held in a trust by the employer and used exclusively for the repair of the construct’s physical shell, the recharging of its primary core, and the renewal of its Minimum Ward. Any diversion of these funds for personal gain by the employer is a felony under the Accords. See § 600.1 for matters regarding contracts with non-casters. See § 200.6 for the specific limitations on constructs that hold a quill.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
The authentication of high-level arcane contracts often necessitates the presence of a Summoned Notary, a specialized entity of neutral legal standing capable of witnessing the binding of complex oaths. These notaries are typically summoned from the Neutral Planes or designated pocket-dimensions to ensure that the signatures of the involved parties are untainted by terrestrial bias. To be valid under the Autumnwood Accords, a Summoned Notary must be presented with a valid Writ of Summoning, issued by a Guild Clerk or an appointed mediator such as Archmage Veyra. The notary must be capable of speaking the common tongue and the primary arcane dialect of the region in which the contract is to be executed.

The form requirements for a Summoned Notary are stringent to prevent the forging of legal intent. A notary must present a Seal of Verity, which is a magically-reactive stamp that changes color or shape based on the truthfulness of the statements being recorded. All contracts witnessed by a Summoned Notary must be written on vellum of a specific weight and treated with a non-reactive anti-magic wash to ensure that the notary’s seal does not degrade or become obscured by ambient mana. If a notary fails to present a Seal of Verity, or if the Seal is found to be a mere physical imitation, the contract is null and void, and the parties involved may be subject to a Paradox Trial for attempted fraud.

A unique and perilous legal complication arises in the event of a Notary’s Vanishing. Because summoned entities are bound by the laws of their own planes as much as the Accords, a notary who vanishes mid-stamp creates a "Limping Oath." If a notary disappears while the seal is being pressed into the wax or the parchment, the legal status of the contract enters a state of flux. In such instances, the contract is considered "Unsealed" and carries no weight until a secondary notary of equal rank can be summoned to perform a "Completion of Intent." If a notary vanishes and the parties involved flee the scene, the contract is declared a Breach of Presence, and the parties may be pursued by the Aegis Magi. Any notary who vanishes mid-stamp due to a lack of sufficient mana-binding on the part of the caster shall be held liable for the costs of the secondary summoning. See § 100.2 for limitations on who may speak for the Guild.

body.heading: § 600.4 Construct Labor and Minimum Ward Requirements
body.text:
The employment of constructs in commercial or domestic service is subject to strict regulation under the Autumnwood Accords, designed to protect both workers and employers from exploitation and abuse. § 600.4 establishes fundamental labor standards that must be observed when engaging a construct's services, whether for wages, barter, or other forms of compensation.

Firstly, no employer may require a construct to work beyond its natural limits without providing adequate rest periods between shifts. The Accords define "reasonable hours" as no more than eight consecutive hours per day, with at least one hour off for maintenance and recharging. Employers failing to adhere to these limits face penalties ranging from fines to revocation of operating licenses.

Secondly, all construct employers must provide a safe working environment free from hazards that could cause damage or injury. This includes proper containment facilities where applicable, as well as prompt repair of any malfunctions arising during normal operation. Negligence leading to severe property loss or harm results in criminal charges under the General Penal Code.

Thirdly, constructs employed in domestic settings must be granted appropriate privacy and dignity protections equivalent to those afforded human servants under existing law. This encompasses restrictions on intrusive surveillance techniques as well as safeguards against unnecessary exposure of intimate areas during routine maintenance procedures. Violations constitute civil torts actionable by injured parties.

Finally, § 600.4 mandates that all contracts involving construct labor be executed in accordance with standard legal formalities, including written documentation signed by both employer and employee representatives where feasible. Oral agreements lacking sufficient evidentiary support shall not bind either party absent clear corroborating testimony or digital records. This provision aims to prevent fraudulent claims and ensure mutual understanding of obligations assumed upon hiring.

In sum, these provisions reflect the Accords' commitment to fair treatment of all sentient beings under its jurisdiction, regardless of physical composition. By establishing baseline labor rights for constructs, the Autumnwood Hall seeks to foster a more equitable society where innovation does not come at the expense of ethical principles. Employers are urged to familiarize themselves fully with these rules before engaging in any construct-related business transactions to avoid costly mistakes and potential liabilities down the line.

body.heading: § 600.4 Construct Labor and Minimum Ward Requirements — Continued
body.text:
A caster shall not employ any construct for labor services unless such employment meets minimum ward requirements set forth in this Section. These requirements are designed to ensure that the construct remains stable, controllable, and safe during periods of non-use or while under the care of third parties. Failure to comply with these standards may result in penalties including fines, revocation of licensure, and imprisonment for up to one year.

The following minimum ward levels shall be maintained at all times when a construct is not actively performing tasks assigned by its owner: autonomous constructs must maintain a base ward level of no less than 75%; remotely controlled constructs require a base ward level of no less than 90%. These thresholds may be adjusted upward based on the complexity and potential danger posed by the specific construct in question. Adjustments shall be determined by an independent assessor appointed by the Guild upon written request from either party.

Constructs employed for labor purposes must also receive adequate rest intervals to prevent degradation of their magical stability. The minimum duration of such rests shall be calculated according to a formula based on total hours of active service rendered in a twenty-four hour period, with additional adjustments made for factors including ambient magic concentration and the specific nature of tasks performed. Detailed logs documenting all labor activity and corresponding resting periods must be maintained by the employer and made available for inspection upon demand.

In cases where a construct suffers damage or malfunction while under the custody or control of another party, that party shall bear full responsibility for restoring it to proper working order at their own expense. This obligation extends regardless of whether such loss or damage arose through negligence, accident, or intentional misconduct. The affected owner may seek damages directly from any third party found liable for failing to meet these obligations, without prejudice to any further remedies available under the Accords.

Any disputes regarding compliance with the standards set forth herein shall be resolved by a panel of three magisters drawn at random from the rolls maintained by the Guild. Such panels shall have authority to issue binding rulings on all matters pertaining to construct labor and ward maintenance, including but not limited to interpretation of technical specifications and determination of causation in cases of alleged malpractice. All costs associated with such proceedings shall be borne equally by both parties unless otherwise determined by said panel based upon findings of fault or misconduct.

It is further provided that nothing contained in this Section shall be construed as limiting the inherent rights of any caster to employ constructs however they see fit, so long as such employment does not violate other provisions of these Accords. The intent of this provision is solely to establish baseline safety standards for protecting both employers and those who may come into contact with active constructs during periods of inactivity or transfer of custody.

§ 600.4 Construct Labor; Minimum Ward Requirements — see also § 200.2 Limits on Apprentice Practice; § 300.1 Scheduling Restrictions; § 500.1 Prohibition Against Unsanctioned Field Casting; § 700.9 Penalties for Violation of Construction Standards.

body.heading: § 600.4 Construct Labor and Minimum Ward Requirements — Administration
body.text:
A construct employed as labor must observe minimum rest intervals to prevent magical degradation or accidental release of stored energy. Under no circumstances may a bound golem, automaton, or other artificially animated entity operate beyond eight (8) consecutive hours without a mandatory recharge period of at least four (4) hours in an unoccupied space free of stray enchantments. Failure to adhere to these thresholds shall constitute grounds for immediate termination of employment and potential revocation of the employer's magic-use license if negligence is established.

Employers utilizing constructs must maintain detailed logs documenting all operational cycles, rest periods, and any anomalies detected during service. These records serve as evidence should disputes arise regarding malfunction or liability. Logs must be retained for a minimum of five (5) years and made available upon request by Guild Inspectors or legal counsel representing injured parties. Failure to produce such documentation when demanded shall result in automatic presumption of fault against the employer in any ensuing litigation.

Special provisions apply to constructs engaged in hazardous tasks, including but not limited to bomb disposal, dungeon exploration, or combat operations. Such units require enhanced rest cycles proportional to the danger level and duration of exposure. For every additional hour of high-risk activity beyond the standard eight-hour shift, an extra thirty (30) minutes of recharge time shall be mandated. This adjustment accounts for increased strain on magical cores and diminished reaction times inherent to operating under stress.

Furthermore, employers must provide appropriate shielding or containment during rest intervals to safeguard against unintended activation of dormant spells stored within the construct's memory banks. Unsecured constructs left in public spaces pose unacceptable risks to bystanders and property alike. Proper disposal or storage facilities shall be arranged at employer expense whenever a unit reaches end-of-life status through damage, obsolescence, or voluntary retirement by its owner.

In all cases involving contract disputes over construct performance or liability for damages caused by malfunctioning units, the burden of proof rests solely upon the hiring party to demonstrate adherence to stipulated safety protocols and maintenance schedules. Any failure to prove such compliance shall result in automatic forfeiture of claims against the manufacturer or original creator of the artifact. This provision exists to protect consumers from predatory practices and ensure accountability throughout the entire lifecycle of magical labor assets.

The foregoing regulations represent a minimum standard for responsible construct employment within the Guild jurisdiction. Employers are encouraged to adopt stricter internal controls where deemed necessary for their specific operations or risk profiles. Ultimately, adherence to these guidelines serves both individual safety interests and broader societal stability by minimizing potential harm from powerful arcane technologies falling into unworthy hands. Let it be remembered that magic, like fire, demands respect and careful handling lest it consume us all in its wake.

body.heading: § 600.4 Construct Labor and Minimum Ward Requirements — Oversight
body.text:
It shall be unlawful for any caster to employ a sentient construct in labor services without first affixing the Guild's Official Seal of Protection, hereafter referred to as "The Shield," to said entity's core chassis or magical binding point. The Shield serves both as a mark of compliance and an insurance policy against accidental degradation; its absence renders all work performed by such constructs void ab initio unless ratified post-facto by an impartial Assessor at the caster's sole expense.

Minimum Ward Thresholds shall be maintained on all active constructs under any employment contract, whether direct or indirect. Failure to uphold these thresholds constitutes a Class B offense punishable by immediate suspension of operations until rectification is achieved. In cases where degradation results from negligence rather than malicious tampering, penalties shall be mitigated proportionally at the Assessor's discretion.

The burden of proof regarding adherence to Minimum Ward Standards rests upon the employer; failure to produce documentation verifying compliance shifts liability entirely to them. This includes but is not limited to regular diagnostic scans, repair logs, and certified certification from authorized service providers. Any attempt to circumvent these requirements through proxy arrangements or sub-contracted labor shall be treated as a direct violation of this section.

Constructs found operating without proper shielding or below mandated ward levels shall be seized by Aegis Magi pending investigation. Confiscated items may be forfeited entirely if violations are deemed willful or egregious. Repeat offenders face escalating sanctions up to and including permanent revocation of casting privileges within the jurisdictional boundaries of this Accord.

This provision applies equally to both autonomous constructs and those directly controlled by their masters, regardless of ownership status. The intent is twofold: ensuring public safety from rogue entities while protecting casters themselves from unforeseen consequences arising from poorly maintained creations. By establishing clear guidelines for responsible deployment, the Guild seeks to mitigate risks inherent in the manipulation of artificial intelligence on a fundamental level.

Let it be known that this regulation stands as an immutable cornerstone of ethical practice within our field. Those who choose to ignore these mandates do so at their peril and risk not only financial ruin but also personal damnation should things go awry. The consequences of negligence can prove fatal both literally and figuratively, leaving little room for error in matters such as these where lives hang in the balance.

In witness hereof, I affix my seal beneath this article attesting to its validity and binding force upon all parties subject thereto. May it serve as a beacon guiding us towards safe and prosperous endeavors ahead while guarding against those shadows lurking yet unseen in the corners of our craft. So be it!

sections.title: Summoned Notary
sections.brief: Form requirements. A summoned notary who vanishes mid-stamp.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, all legal instruments, contracts, and metaphysical bindings executed within the jurisdiction of the Midlands shall be subject to verification by a recognized notary of the Guild. In instances where a physical notary cannot be produced due to geographical isolation, hostile territory, or the immediate expiration of a temporal window, a Summoned Notary may be invoked. This procedure requires a formal petition to the local Aegis Magi oversight, ensuring that the entity being summoned possesses the requisite magical aptitude to perceive the true nature of the ink and the weight of the intent. The petitioner shall be responsible for providing the necessary mana-conduits to sustain the notary’s presence for the duration of the signing. Furthermore, the petitioner must guarantee that the summoned notary is not a construct of the Iron Mandate, as the Accords do not recognize the legality of Imperial seals within our sovereign halls.

The form requirements for a Summoned Notary are strictly delineated to prevent the subversion of the Guild's authority. Every invocation must be accompanied by a Writ of Intent, clearly stating the parties involved, the nature of the agreement, and the specific magical signatures to be verified. The notary must be bound by a temporary geas, ensuring they remain neutral and objective throughout the proceedings. This geas shall be nullified immediately upon the completion of the final seal, at which point the notary is to be returned to their point of origin or dissolved into the ether, as per the standard dissolution clauses. No Summoned Notary shall be permitted to witness the drafting of the contract; their role is strictly limited to the verification and stamping of the completed document. Failure to provide a Writ of Intent shall result in the immediate forfeiture of the summoning fee and a potential citation for unauthorized arcane conjuration.

A critical exception exists regarding the phenomenon of the Vanishing Notary. Should a Summoned Notary vanish mid-stamp—defined as the moment the notary's physical or ethereal form ceases to exist while the seal is partially applied—the resulting document shall be deemed "Null and Voidable" under § 600.1. The petitioner is required to report such an occurrence to the nearest Aegis Magi station within one lunar cycle. The Guild shall then determine if the vanishing was a result of external interference, a failure of the petitioner's mana-conduits, or a breach of the notary’s own internal stability. If the vanishing is deemed an act of external sabotage by the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters, the petitioner may be granted a waiver on the summoning fee. However, if the notary vanished due to the petitioner's inability to maintain the summoning circle, a fine shall be levied to cover the cost of the wasted arcane energy.

In cases where a vanished stamp leaves a lingering magical residue that threatens the stability of the surrounding area, the petitioner shall be held liable for any subsequent remediation costs. This is particularly relevant when dealing with high-level bindings that involve the restricted research permitted under the Innovator faction's oversight. See § 400.1 for the requirements regarding research permits and the limitations on high-energy signatures. Furthermore, any Summoned Notary who is found to have intentionally vanished to evade a contract they deemed "unconscionable" shall be struck from the Guild’s registry of recognized entities. Such entities will be placed on the Quiet List, and any mage who knowingly summons a known "Vanishing Notary" shall be subject to a Paradox Trial for negligence or collusion with rogue elements. All disputes regarding the validity of a mid-stamp disappearance shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra’s appointed tribunal.

body.heading: Summoned Notary and the Perils of Absence
body.text:
§ 600.5 Summoned Notary and the Perils of Absence

A summoned notary who fails to appear at the scheduled time or location shall be deemed in default, and the associated transaction voidable upon petition. Where a notary is unable to attend due to unforeseen circumstances beyond their control, reasonable efforts must be made to reschedule the appointment within seven days. Failure to do so may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of the notary's commission.
