In cases where a summoned notary vanishes without explanation mid-transaction, leaving an incomplete or forged record behind, they shall face immediate suspension pending investigation into potential fraud or malfeasance. Such incidents highlight the critical importance of verifying credentials and maintaining clear lines of communication between all parties involved in any notarized activity. The Guild retains sole discretion to determine whether a given absence constitutes mere negligence or willful misconduct warranting harsher penalties. All summoned notaries are urged to prioritize punctuality and reliability as fundamental tenets of their professional practice, thereby safeguarding the integrity of the entire certification system upon which so many depend. See also § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild; under § 1.6 Definitions, "Notary" encompasses all individuals authorized by the Accords to administer oaths and certify documents. Under § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure, unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information can lead to severe sanctions. As outlined in § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs, proper containment protocols must be observed at all times during any experimental work involving potentially hazardous materials or energies. Failure to comply with these guidelines may result not only in personal liability but also broader consequences for public safety and order. It is thus incumbent upon every practitioner of magic to adhere strictly to the established rules governing their craft, lest they find themselves ensnared by far more dire repercussions than a simple missing signature ever could be. The stakes are always high when dealing with forces beyond mortal comprehension – let us hope we never have cause to test them firsthand.

body.heading: § 600.5 Summoned Notary and the Perils of Absence
body.text:
Where a summoned notary fails to appear at the appointed hour for any reason, whether due to illness, accident, or simple forgetfulness, the contract remains incomplete and unenforceable until such time as the absent party returns to finalize the document under oath. In the interim, no remedies may be pursued against either party, nor shall any damages accrue by mere passage of time without further action on behalf of the aggrieved side. The burden rests solely upon the notary to secure their own presence and punctuality, for failure thereof constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty under § 100.2(b).

Should the absent notary ultimately refuse to appear or act despite reasonable notice and demand, the contract is deemed void ab initio and may be rescinded at any time by either party upon written declaration. No claim may thereafter arise out of the failed transaction except for actual losses directly caused by reliance on the notary's misrepresentation of their availability—a narrow ground requiring clear proof of damages. This provision exists to protect all parties from being bound indefinitely to a stale agreement while awaiting uncertain performance from an unavailable agent.

Furthermore, no substitute notary may be appointed in lieu of the originally summoned individual without prior written consent from both contracting parties. Any such substitution attempted unilaterally shall be deemed null and void under § 600.1(c), regardless of whether the substitute possesses equivalent qualifications or capabilities. This strict requirement ensures that each party retains full control over who represents their interests in executing legally binding instruments, preventing unwanted surprises down the line.

In cases where emergency circumstances prevent timely appearance by the designated notary, either party may petition the Autumnwood Accords Desk for relief under § 100.8, providing evidence of good faith efforts to secure alternative arrangements. Discretionary approval may be granted if delay would cause irreparable harm and no reasonable alternatives exist. However, such exceptions shall be construed narrowly and never undermine the fundamental principle that only properly summoned officials possess authority to validate contractual obligations.

This section underscores the critical importance of diligence in fulfilling all procedural requirements when dealing with magical notaries. Parties must anticipate potential obstacles and plan accordingly to avoid being left hanging on a technicality. The law favors certainty over convenience, requiring strict adherence to established protocols lest consequences ensue. Only through careful attention to these details can one ensure that their agreements stand firm against future challenges.

body.heading: § 600.5 Summoned Notary and the Perils of Absence — Continued
body.text:
A summoned notary who fails to appear at the designated time and place shall be deemed in default, resulting in the automatic nullification of any documents executed under their authority. This provision exists to ensure the integrity of the notarization process and prevent fraud or abuse. In such cases, the Guild may impose sanctions on the absent notary, ranging from fines to permanent revocation of their credentials, depending on the severity of the breach and whether it was willful.

Furthermore, a summoned notary who leaves the premises without permission before completing all required duties shall be subject to immediate removal and replacement by another qualified notary at their own expense. Any delays or errors caused by such premature departure shall be borne solely by the defaulting notary and may result in additional liabilities for any parties affected thereby. This rule underscores the critical nature of a notary's presence throughout the entire notarization ceremony, as their oversight is indispensable to validating the authenticity of signatures and contents.

The Guild reserves the right to investigate any suspicious patterns of absence or non-compliance by summoned notaries, particularly when linked to allegations of corruption or collusion with signatories. In extreme circumstances, a blanket suspension of all summoning privileges may be enacted pending thorough review and resolution of underlying issues. Such measures are designed to uphold public trust in the notarization system and safeguard against potential malfeasance within the ranks of commissioned officials.

Ultimately, adherence to these stipulations is paramount for maintaining the efficacy and reliability of legal instruments dependent upon notarial attestation. By holding summoned notaries accountable for their obligations, the Guild strives to preserve the highest standards of professionalism and ethical conduct among its membership. Failure to abide by these mandates risks undermining the very foundation upon which notarized transactions rely, with far-reaching consequences for individuals, businesses, and society at large. Thus, all parties must recognize the gravity of their roles in this essential function of modern commerce and governance.

body.heading: § 600.5 Summoned Notary and the Perils of Absence — Continued — Continued
body.text:
The absence of a summoned notary during critical phases of authentication shall not invalidate the entire transaction, provided that adequate substitutes are engaged in accordance with established procedures. In instances where the original notary fails to appear within a reasonable timeframe due to unforeseen circumstances beyond their control, an authorized deputy or alternate may be appointed by the Guild Sovereign to complete the sealing process. Such deputies must possess equivalent credentials and experience as required of primary notaries.

However, any delay in finalizing the seal resulting from a notary's absence shall be attributed solely to the negligence of the absent party and may incur penalties under § 600.10 Failure to Appear. These penalties range from fines proportional to lost fees to temporary suspension of licensure, depending on the severity and frequency of infractions. Repeat offenders risk permanent revocation of their notary commissions for breach of trust.

Furthermore, no notary shall intentionally abscond mid-transaction regardless of personal animus toward the client or competing interests. Such conduct constitutes a grave violation of professional ethics codified in § 600.8 Code of Conduct and may trigger immediate disciplinary action up to and including expulsion from the Guild. In extreme cases where flight renders recovery impossible, legal recourse shall be pursued through standard civil channels for breach of contract and unjust enrichment.

The Guild retains sole discretion to determine whether a notary's absence warrants mitigation or escalation of sanctions based on mitigating factors unique to each circumstance. Clients aggrieved by delays should promptly petition the Arcane Tribunal rather than resorting to extrajudicial measures which could complicate ongoing proceedings. Patience and adherence to due process remain paramount even when frustration mounts under pressure.

Ultimately, the integrity of magical seals depends upon unwavering commitment from all participants involved. While no system can perfectly anticipate every contingency, robust safeguards exist to maintain order amidst chaos should issues arise unexpectedly. Trust in these mechanisms shall guide practitioners through adversity until resolution is achieved satisfactorily for all concerned parties alike.

body.heading: § 600.5 Summoned Notary and the Perils of Absence — Continued — Administration
body.text:
A summoned notary who departs the Hall before completing their duties shall be deemed in default, subject to penalties under § 100.2 and § 300.4(e). Such absence constitutes a breach of contract and may result in revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4(a)(iii). The Archmage Sovereign reserves the right to initiate disciplinary proceedings against any notary found guilty of dereliction of duty, whether intentional or negligent.

Furthermore, a summoned notary who fails to appear as directed shall be held in contempt of court and may face imprisonment for up to one year without bail, as provided by § 150.7(b). The Guild further retains the authority to impose fines totaling no more than two hundred gold pieces per violation, payable within thirty days or subject to additional sanctions under § 900.2(c)(vii). In cases of repeated offenses, cumulative penalties shall apply with increased severity based on prior convictions recorded in the Central Registry.

It is expressly forbidden for any notary to delegate their responsibilities to another individual unless specifically authorized by written consent from both parties involved and approved by the Archmage Sovereign's Office. Unauthorized delegation renders all subsequent actions invalid and subject to nullification at the discretion of the Guild. Violators shall be liable for any damages incurred as a result of such misconduct, including but not limited to financial losses, emotional distress, and reputational harm suffered by affected individuals or entities.

The provisions herein are intended to safeguard the integrity of the summoning process and protect all stakeholders from potential abuses arising from improper conduct by summoned notaries. Failure to comply with these regulations may lead to severe consequences ranging from loss of livelihood to criminal prosecution under applicable laws enforced by local authorities in conjunction with the Guild's internal disciplinary mechanisms.

This clause stands as a testament to the unwavering commitment of the Autumnwood Accords Desk to maintain order, fairness, and accountability within our magical community. By adhering strictly to these guidelines, we ensure that our cherished traditions continue to flourish for generations yet unborn while fostering an environment conducive to growth and innovation under wise stewardship guided by principles rooted deeply in history itself.

sections.title: Evidence Generally
sections.brief: What a filing must contain.

body.heading: Evidence Generally
body.text:
§ 700.1 Evidence Generally — What a filing must contain.

All evidentiary submissions presented before the High Court of Autumnwood or any sub-committee of the Accords Desk shall be deemed null and void unless they conform strictly to the standards of clarity, provenance, and magical integrity established herein. A filing is not merely a statement of fact but a formal anchoring of reality within the Guild’s legal framework. To ensure that the truth of a proceeding is not distorted by the very nature of the arcane, every piece of evidence—be it a written scroll, a physical artifact, a recorded memory, or a summoned testimony—must be accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity signed by a licensed Clerk or a recognized Aegis Mage. This certificate must verify that the evidence has not been subjected to unauthorized alteration, transmutation, or temporal shifting since its initial collection.

The filing must contain a comprehensive description of the evidence’s origin, including the geographic coordinates of its discovery, the date of its acquisition, and the identities of all individuals involved in its handling. In cases involving items of significant magical potency, such as those involving the Heartstone or other rift-adjacent materials, the filing must also include a detailed survey of the item’s current mana signature to prevent the accidental triggering of environmental hazards during the hearing. Furthermore, any evidence that is inherently volatile, ephemeral, or capable of self-replication must be housed in a stabilized containment vessel as approved by the Conservators. Failure to provide a sufficient description of the evidence's nature shall result in the immediate dismissal of the filing and a potential citation for negligence under the oversight of Archmage Veyra.

Furthermore, the filing must explicitly state any known associations with the Quiet List. While the contents of the Quiet List are not to be recited in public venues, any evidence derived from such sources must be flagged for restricted viewing. The Clerk shall ensure that such evidence is only accessible to the presiding judges and the immediate parties involved, under a seal of non-disclosure. Any attempt to circumvent these restrictions or to present "hidden" evidence in a public forum shall be treated as a violation of the Accords. The Accords Desk reserves the right to reject any filing that utilizes "Wario Coin" as a form of collateral or tender, as such currency holds no recognized value within the Guild's legal system. For matters regarding the specific requirements of physical artifacts, see § 400.4. For matters regarding the handling of unauthorized research materials, see § 400.1.

body.heading: Scrying of Closed Books
body.text:
§ 700.2 Scrying of Closed Books — Warrant. Spoliation even if nothing was taken.

The sanctity of a private library or a closed grimoire is a cornerstone of the Autumnwood Accords, yet the Guild acknowledges that the pursuit of stability may necessitate the inspection of restricted materials. No mage, regardless of their standing among the Innovators or the Conservators, shall engage in the unauthorized scrying, mental probing, or ethereal peering into a closed book or a sealed repository. Such actions are strictly prohibited unless the individual possesses a valid Writ of Inspection issued by the Sovereign Archmage or a designated Aegis Magistrate. This writ must specify the scope of the scrying, the duration of the access, and the specific reasons for the inquiry. Any scrying conducted without such a warrant shall be deemed a criminal trespass of the mind and a violation of the privacy protections afforded to all registered mages.

Crucially, the Accords establish a strict doctrine of spoliation regarding the act of scrying. The mere act of peering into a closed book via arcane means constitutes a "metaphysical breach" of the object's integrity. Even if the scrying process is successful and no physical pages are removed, no secrets are stolen, and no ink is blurred, the act itself is sufficient to constitute spoliation. The Guild holds that the "observation of the arcane" is often an "alteration of the arcane"; therefore, a book that has been scried is no longer in its original state. In any legal proceeding where a book has been subjected to unauthorized scrying, the contents of that book may be ruled inadmissible as evidence, as its reliability can no longer be guaranteed by the Conservators.

The penalty for such spoliation shall be determined by the presiding council, but it shall typically involve a formal reprimand and a temporary suspension of the offender's research privileges. If the scrying was performed on a volume containing Quiet List materials, the penalties shall be significantly escalated, potentially leading to a Paradox Trial. Mages who find their libraries subjected to such unauthorized scrying are entitled to seek restitution for the "spiritual wear" caused to their collections. For procedures regarding the issuance of Writs of Inspection, see § 400.1. For the consequences of severe magical breaches, see § 300.1.

body.heading: Memory Charm as Spoliation
body.text:
§ 700.3 Memory Charm as Spoliation — Forgetting is not a defense if you paid for the forgetting.

In the pursuit of justice, the Guild recognizes that the human—and demi-human—mind is a fragile vessel, easily manipulated by the very arts it seeks to master. However, the use of memory charms, amnesia spells, or any form of cognitive erasure to avoid the consequences of a legal proceeding is strictly forbidden. Under the Accords, a mage who undergoes a memory erasure to "purge" their knowledge of a crime or a breach of contract does not receive a legal reprieve. The law shall look past the veil of the missing memory to the actions that necessitated the erasure. If it can be demonstrated that a mage purposefully induced a state of forgetting to evade testimony or to shield themselves from the repercussions of their actions, the court shall treat the erasure as a deliberate act of spoliation of evidence.

The legal principle of "Constructive Knowledge" shall apply in these instances. If a mage was aware of a violation at the time of the act, the fact that they no longer possess that memory is irrelevant to their liability. Furthermore, the Guild explicitly prohibits the use of memory charms as a method of "cleansing" one's record. A mage who pays a third party, or utilizes their own magic, to forget a specific event shall be held to the same standard of accountability as if the memory were perfectly intact. The Guild maintains that "forgetting is not a defense," particularly when the act of forgetting is a calculated maneuver to obstruct the truth. Any mage found to have utilized such charms to obstruct a Paradox Trial shall face immediate escalation of their sentencing.

Furthermore, the use of memory charms on witnesses or victims is considered a severe felony under the Accords. Such actions shall result in the immediate sealing of the offender's magic and a mandatory period of isolation. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any plea of ignorance based on self-induced amnesia. If a mage claims they cannot testify because they have "purged" the event, the court may compel them to provide evidence of the charm's usage, which shall serve as prima facie evidence of guilt or obstruction. For matters concerning the sealing of magic, see § 300.1. For the management of restricted research that might involve cognitive manipulation, see § 400.1.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
§ 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony — A copy may not swear for the original.

The integrity of the High Court relies upon the presence of the living, sentient being before whom the oath is sworn. Consequently, the use of a simulacrum, illusion, or any magically-constructed duplicate to provide testimony in a legal proceeding is strictly prohibited. A simulacrum, by its very nature as a "copy," lacks the inherent soul-binding or consciousness required to enter into a binding legal oath. While a simulacrum may be used to demonstrate a visual reconstruction of a past event—provided it is clearly labeled as a "Visual Reconstruction" and not "Testimony"—it may never be permitted to speak on behalf of the original entity or to provide subjective accounts of events.

Any attempt to present a simulacrum as a valid witness shall be met with an immediate stay of proceedings and a formal investigation into the authenticity of the claimant's actions. The law distinguishes clearly between a "Visual Reconstruction," which is a tool of education and evidence, and "Simulacrum Testimony," which is a fraudulent attempt to bypass the requirements of the Accords. If a mage seeks to provide a visual reconstruction of a crime scene or a historical event, they must obtain a permit from the Conservators to ensure the reconstruction does not contain unauthorized magical effects or "hallucinations" that could mislead the court. The original entity must be present to oversee the reconstruction and must be available to answer clarifying questions in real-time.

Should a party attempt to substitute a simulacrum for an absent witness, the court may rule that the party is in "Contempt of the Accords." In such cases, the evidence provided by the simulacrum shall be struck from the record, and the party may be subject to a Paradox Trial for attempting to subvert the judicial process. This rule ensures that the "human element"—the weight of personal responsibility—remains at the center of the Guild's legal framework. For matters regarding the use of constructs in legal settings, see § 600.4. For the definition of forbidden schools that might involve the creation of sentient duplicates, see § 300.2.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
§ 700.5 Clone as Duplicate Claimant — One claim. The later body files an amendment.

In instances where a mage has undergone the process of cloning—whether for research, labor, or survival—the legal status of the resulting bodies must be clearly defined to prevent the "Multiplicity of Claims" paradox. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a single magical signature or "Identity Essence" may only hold one primary legal standing at any given time. If a mage possesses multiple bodies through cloning, they are considered a single legal person with multiple physical manifestations. Therefore, only one body may act as the primary claimant in a legal suit, hold property, or enter into contracts. The "Original" body is typically designated as the primary claimant by default, unless a formal "Transfer of Primacy" is filed with the Accords Desk.

If a mage wishes to pursue a legal claim using a secondary body, they must first file a "Notice of Intent to Claim" with the Clerk. Once the intent is filed, the secondary body may act as the representative for the legal proceedings. However, should a dispute arise between the bodies regarding the direction of the claim, the Accords dictate that the primary body's wishes shall prevail. If the primary body is incapacitated or destroyed, the secondary body must file a "Petition for Amendment of Primacy" to become the sole legal claimant. This ensures that the Guild's records remain clean and that no single mage can use their clones to "double-file" claims or circumvent the limits of the Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, any property or assets acquired by a clone during a period of "Secondary Status" are considered the property of the primary identity. Should a clone be destroyed, the assets do not revert to the public but remain with the primary body. This prevents the "fragmentation of wealth" that often plagues the Innovators' more radical experiments with biological and magical replication. Any mage who attempts to file a claim with a clone without first filing the required amendment or notice shall have their claim dismissed as a "Duplicate Filing." For matters regarding the use of clones as labor, see § 600.4. For the overarching rules on research permits involving such replication, see § 400.1.

body.heading: § 700.1 Evidence Generally
body.text:
The Accords recognize that disputes over magical practice often hinge upon contested facts, requiring reliable proof to establish liability. Accordingly, the Desk shall accept as admissible any evidence obtained lawfully and relevant to the issues at hand. This includes written records, physical artifacts, witness testimony, and direct observation of conduct. The burden of production lies with the party asserting a claim or defense, who must produce sufficient evidence to meet the prima facie standard before an opposing rebuttal becomes necessary.

Notably, scrying techniques used to view private conversations or actions constitute spoliation of evidence unless expressly authorized by a court order. Any magical enhancement intended solely to bolster testimony beyond natural capability shall be deemed fraudulent and subject to dismissal with prejudice. Conversely, memory charms administered for therapeutic purposes remain lawful so long as they do not distort recollection materially. Such procedures require prior consent from all affected parties and documentation filed with the Guild.

Simulacra summoned under controlled conditions may provide valuable insight into past events or hidden knowledge. However, their use in lieu of direct testimony is strictly limited to illustrative purposes only. The Desk shall determine admissibility based on necessity and probative value versus prejudicial effect. Similarly, duplicate claimants arising from cloning technologies must demonstrate clear chain of custody and identity verification before being permitted to participate in legal proceedings. Failure to do so results in automatic disqualification from the case.

Ultimately, the integrity of the evidentiary process underpins all adjudicative outcomes within the Accords framework. Parties are urged to seek qualified counsel when navigating these complex rules of proof. The Desk retains ultimate discretion to exclude any material deemed unreliable or improperly obtained in furtherance of justice. Adherence to these standards ensures fair treatment for all litigants while safeguarding against abuse of magical powers within judicial contexts.

See also § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 200.3 Temporary Mouths; § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs; § 600.2 Familiars as Agents. Under § 1.7 Construction, Aggregation of Conduct applies where multiple evidentiary points converge to establish a pattern of behavior warranting disciplinary action. The Desk shall evaluate each case on its merits while maintaining consistency with established precedents.

sections.title: Scrying of Closed Books
sections.brief: Warrant. Spoliation even if nothing was taken.

body.heading: Scrying of Closed Books
body.text:
The act of scrying, whether through a crystal lens, a scrying pool, or a direct mental projection, into a volume that has been formally sealed by the Archmage Sovereign or the presiding High Conservator is strictly prohibited under the Autumnwood Accords. A closed book is not merely a physical object of bound paper and ink; it is a legal state of existence wherein the information contained therein has been sequestered from the public and private spheres for reasons of stability, security, or the preservation of the Quiet List. Any attempt to bypass these seals via divination, ethereal peering, or any other arcane method of observation constitutes a breach of the sanctity of the Archive. Such actions are treated as a prima facie violation of the privacy of the Guild's internal records and the personal property rights of the authors.

To initiate a legal inquiry into a closed volume, a caster must first obtain a formal Warrant of Inspection from the Accords Desk. This warrant must specify the exact nature of the information sought, the necessity of the inquiry for the preservation of the Guild or the safety of the Midlands, and the specific limitations of the scrying duration. Without a warrant, any scrying of a closed book shall be met with immediate seizure of the scrying apparatus and a mandatory period of magical silence for the offending caster. The mere intent to observe is sufficient for prosecution, as the volatile nature of forbidden knowledge means that even a glance can cause irreparable ripples in the local weave.

Furthermore, the law of Spoliation applies to all scrying attempts regardless of the outcome. If a caster successfully scries into a closed book without a warrant, the contents of that book are deemed "spoliated" in the eyes of the Accords. This means that even if the caster takes no physical notes, reveals no secrets to third parties, and admits no knowledge of the contents, the integrity of the text is considered compromised. The Guild shall treat the book as if its contents were leaked, and the original author or the presiding Conservator may demand that the volume be moved to a more secure, high-containment vault. The caster shall be liable for the costs of re-sealing and the administrative fees associated with the relocation of the text. See § 700.1.

body.heading: Memory Charm as Spoliation
body.text:
The use of memory charms, cognitive erasure, or any mnemonic suppression spell intended to remove knowledge of a Guild-related offense or a restricted research violation is strictly prohibited as a method of evading justice. The Accords Desk holds the firm position that "forgetting is not a defense if you paid for the forgetting." If a caster utilizes a charm to erase their own memory of a crime, or if they employ a charm on a witness to suppress their testimony, the act of erasure is itself considered a secondary offense of Spoliation. The law recognizes that the voluntary removal of a memory creates a void in the legal record that can be exploited to obstruct the Paradox Trial. Therefore, the existence of a memory charm is sufficient evidence of a desire to obstruct, regardless of whether the caster can currently recall the specific details of the act.

In any proceeding before a council of peers, the presence of a memory charm—whether active or recently expired—shall be treated as a confession of the underlying act. If a caster is found to have sought out a memory charm to "cleanse" their mind of a specific event, the Guild shall presume that the event occurred as described in the initial accusation. The caster shall not be permitted to argue a lack of intent or a lack of memory as a mitigating factor; rather, the proactive seeking of oblivion shall be viewed as an admission of guilt. This prevents the "clean slate" defense where a rogue mage might attempt to render themselves legally incapable of understanding their own crimes.

Furthermore, any caster who provides a memory charm to a third party for the purpose of concealing evidence or silencing a victim shall be subject to immediate arrest by the Aegis Magi. Such actions are viewed as a direct assault on the transparency of the Accords. The Guild maintains that the truth of the past is a communal responsibility, and the artificial deletion of that truth to protect an individual's reputation or freedom is a violation of the collective security of the Midlands. See § 700.1.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
A simulacrum, whether it be a physical construct of flesh and bone, a magical duplicate, or a lingering psychic echo, may not swear testimony or provide evidence in any formal hearing before the Accords Desk. The law of Identity requires that only a sentient being of recognized legal standing—specifically a living mage, a non-magical citizen of the Midlands, or a sanctioned Goodstyle Artisan—may participate in the testimony of a Paradox Trial. A copy may not swear for the original, as the nature of magic allows for the creation of perfect mimics that lack the moral weight and soul-binding oaths required by the Guild's judicial processes.

If a party to a legal dispute seeks to present the testimony of a simulacrum, they must first prove that the original entity is deceased and that the simulacrum is a "Living Record" of the original's intent, which is a standard rarely granted. Even in such cases, the simulacrum may only be used to provide historical context and cannot be used to swear an oath or provide "new" testimony. The use of a simulacrum to testify as if it were the original person is strictly forbidden and shall be considered a form of identity theft and a violation of the Sanctity of the Self. Any attempt to do so will result in the immediate dismissal of the evidence and a heavy fine against the presenting party.

The Accords Desk further stipulates that a simulacrum may not be used to bypass the "Quiet List" restrictions. If a simulacrum were allowed to speak, it could potentially recite forbidden knowledge without the caster facing the direct consequences of such a violation. Therefore, any simulacrum that speaks during a legal proceeding must be bound by a permanent silence ward unless specifically authorized by Archmage Veyra. The preservation of the distinction between the "Original" and the "Copy" is fundamental to the prevention of magical fraud within the Guild's jurisdiction.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
In matters of property, intellectual research, or magical rights, a clone shall be considered a Duplicate Claimant rather than a separate legal entity. Under the Autumnwood Accords, the existence of a clone does not grant the secondary body a separate right to claim ownership, nor does it allow for the doubling of resources. One claim is permitted per original identity. If a mage creates a clone to claim a share of a research grant or a portion of a physical estate, the Guild shall recognize only the primary body as the legal owner. The clone is viewed as an extension of the original's reach, not a new person.

Should a situation arise where a clone is granted its own Provisional Guild Pass or seeks to establish independent research permits, the Guild shall treat this as a violation of the Unsanctioned Arts. The clone is legally tethered to the original. If the original body is incapacitated, the clone may act as a temporary proxy, but it cannot hold property in its own name. In cases where a clone attempts to file for independent status, the Guild shall require a "Severance of Identity" hearing, which is notoriously difficult to achieve and requires the express permission of the Conservators.

In the event of a dispute between a primary body and its clone regarding the use of shared resources—such as a laboratory or a specific mana source—the primary body shall always hold the dominant legal right. The later body, or the clone, must file an amendment to the original's charter to request specific hours of usage. This ensures that the creation of clones cannot be used as a tactic to dilute the authority of a single mage or to circumvent the limits on research copies of Quiet Items. The law is clear: the soul (or the primary arcane signature) owns the claim; the body is merely the vessel. See § 400.5.

body.heading: § 700.2 Spoliation by Forbidden Divination
body.text:
A mage shall not employ scrying or other forms of forbidden divination to breach the privacy of any person, household, or establishment without express consent from all parties concerned. Such acts constitute a grave violation of the sanctity of private life and are subject to severe penalties under this Code. Violators shall be liable for treble damages plus punitive fines assessed at the discretion of the court based on the severity of the intrusion and resulting harm suffered by the aggrieved party.

The prohibition extends not only to direct scrying but also to indirect methods of espionage through enchanted mirrors, animated dolls, or other devices designed to observe private spaces surreptitiously. Any such contraptions found in possession shall be seized and destroyed at public expense, with costs borne by the offending caster. Repeat offenders may face permanent revocation of their magical licensure and mandatory exile from the jurisdiction for a period not less than one solar year.

Furthermore, this section expressly forbids the use of memory charms or other enchantments designed to erase or alter recollections in the service of spoliating evidence relevant to pending litigation. Such machinations violate fundamental principles of fair play and justice, undermining the integrity of the judicial process itself. Courts shall presume bad faith on the part of any party found guilty of employing forbidden divination or memory manipulation for evidentiary purposes, with adverse inference drawn against them accordingly.

It is hereby declared that no simaculum or artificial duplicate may testify as a competent witness in any matter unless expressly authorized by law. The identity and consciousness of each individual remain inviolate; attempts to subvert this through cloning technologies shall be prosecuted under existing statutes regarding fraud, impersonation, and unauthorized human experimentation. Any claim arising from the wrongful creation or use of simulacra shall be adjudicated on its merits without regard for any technical defenses based upon the artificial nature of the alleged plaintiff-defendant.

This section shall apply with equal force to all forms of remote sensing technology capable of penetrating physical barriers, including but not limited to thermal imaging, lidar scanning, and magnetic resonance profiling. Operators thereof are reminded that privacy expectations remain high even in the digital age; mere suspicion of wrongdoing does not justify wholesale surveillance without probable cause supported by oath or affirmation. Unauthorized gathering of sensitive data shall be treated as a felony offense subject to harsh punishment upon conviction.

The spirit of this provision is intended to safeguard individuals against invasive prying into their most intimate thoughts and actions without warrant. While legitimate investigative techniques have their place, they must never compromise the core values of trust and dignity that undergird civilized society. Let all casters remember: power granted by magic comes with solemn obligations; misuse thereof brings swift retribution from both Heaven and Earth alike!

body.heading: § 700.2 Spoliation by Forbidden Divination — Continued
body.text:
Forbidden divination, including scrying operations conducted without the explicit permission of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, constitutes spoliation under § 100.4(c) regardless of whether physical evidence was removed or altered. The mere act of illicitly accessing protected magical records or attempting to peer into sealed archives infers an intent to interfere with the integrity and confidentiality of Guild data. Such conduct shall be presumed to have compromised the sanctity of the materials in question, triggering automatic sanctions pursuant to § 700.2(b).

The burden of proof rests upon the accused caster to demonstrate that their unauthorized divination efforts had no impact whatsoever on the security or availability of the targeted information. Absent compelling evidence to the contrary, the Desk shall deem spoliation complete and impose penalties accordingly. This strict liability standard reflects the grave risks inherent in unrestricted access to potent arcane knowledge; once a seal is broken, even momentarily, the damage may prove irreparable.

Divination techniques capable of penetrating closed books or revealing hidden truths are classified as high-risk manipulations under § 300.1(s). Practitioners engaged in such activities without proper authorization violate both the spirit and letter of the Accords. Repeat offenses may lead to revocation of licensure and referral for criminal prosecution. The Desk retains sole discretion to grant exceptions on a case-by-case basis, contingent upon rigorous vetting procedures and adequate safeguards.

The prohibition against forbidden divination extends beyond physical archives to include digital or simulated equivalents stored within secure databases. Any attempt to breach these electronic barriers shall be treated identically to unauthorized access of tangible records. Automated monitoring systems are employed to detect suspicious activity and initiate immediate alerts to enforcement agents. Violators face swift disciplinary action upon confirmation of guilt.

This provision serves as a deterrent against reckless experimentation with dangerous magical arts. By maintaining strict control over sensitive data, the Guild safeguards not only its own interests but also those of all who rely upon the stable functioning of arcane systems. Unauthorized divination threatens this delicate equilibrium and must be met with decisive measures to preserve order and security across the realm.

see § 100.4(c) Spoliation Generally; § 300.1(s) High-Risk Manipulations; § 700.2(b) Penalties for Spoliation; § 500.6 Automated Monitoring Systems; under § 900.3 Strict Liability Standards.

sections.title: Memory Charm as Spoliation
sections.brief: Forgetting is not a defense if you paid for the forgetting.

body.heading: Memory Charm as Spoliation
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes that the intentional erasure of cognitive data via magical means does not constitute a valid defense against the withholding of evidence, nor does it grant the practitioner immunity from the consequences of their prior actions. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a mage who undergoes a Memory Charm to obfuscate their knowledge of a transgression is deemed to have committed an act of Spoliation. The legal principle of "Cognitive Integrity" dictates that the burden of memory remains with the individual regardless of the method by which that memory is suppressed. If a mage is summoned to provide testimony or evidence regarding a breach of the Accords and claims ignorance due to a self-inflicted Memory Charm, such a claim shall be dismissed by the presiding council.

Furthermore, the Guild recognizes that the act of paying for, commissioning, or self-administering a Memory Charm constitutes a willful attempt to subvert the judicial process. In all proceedings, the court shall treat the existence of a Memory Charm as a prima facie admission of guilt regarding the underlying matter being suppressed. The mere fact of forgetting is not a shield; rather, the methodology of forgetting serves as a confession of the existence of the fact. Practitioners who seek to utilize such charms to evade the Paradox Trial shall find their magic subject to immediate Sealment under the authority of the Conservators. Any individual found to have induced a state of amnesia to avoid the disclosure of illicit research or unauthorized field casting shall be prosecuted as if the original information were still held in clear and present mind.

See § 700.1 for general evidence standards. See § 700.2 regarding the limitations of scrying. The Guild maintains that the preservation of the truth is paramount to the stability of the Midlands. Any attempt to treat a blank mind as a clean slate in the eyes of the law is a violation of the sanctity of the Accords. The cost of the charm, whether paid in gold, mana, or personal sacrifice, is irrelevant to the determination of spoliation. The law focuses on the result: the deliberate removal of evidence from the sphere of human consciousness to hinder the Guild's ability to maintain order.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
A simulacrum, whether created through high-level illusion, somatic projection, or complex material transmutation, lacks the legal standing to provide sworn testimony or enter into binding contracts on behalf of its progenitor. The Guild recognizes that while a simulacrum may possess the appearance, voice, and perceived personality of a specific mage, it lacks the "Arcane Signature of Intent" required for legal recognition. Therefore, a copy may not swear for the original. Any attempt to utilize a simulacrum to bypass the requirements of the Paradox Trial or to provide false testimony in a dispute of the Accords shall be treated as a felony of Deceptive Casting.

When a mage is summoned to appear before the High Council or an Aegis Magi tribunal, they must present their own physical form. The use of a simulacrum as a proxy is strictly prohibited, as the Guild cannot verify the internal state of a magical construct. If a simulacrum is presented in place of a mage, the proceedings shall be suspended, and the mage in question shall be subject to a summary citation for evasion. This rule ensures that the nuances of the mage's conscience and the weight of their personal oaths are properly weighed by the peers of the Guild. A copy is a reflection of a truth, not the truth itself; it cannot bear the weight of a vow, nor can it be held liable for the consequences of its words.

Furthermore, any contract signed by a simulacrum is null and void ab initio. If a mage seeks to conduct business with the Goodstyle Artisans or other entities, they must ensure that their own hand—not a magical duplicate—affixes the seal. Failure to adhere to this requirement may result in the immediate revocation of research permits under § 400.1. The Guild's stance is clear: the law governs the soul and the intent of the caster, neither of which can be replicated by the mere mastery of form. For those who believe their simulacrums are sufficiently "real" to stand in court, the Guild reminds them that the Accords are bound by the essence of the individual, not the shadow they cast.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
In instances where a mage undergoes biological or magical replication resulting in the creation of a clone, the Guild recognizes a singular legal identity for the purpose of claims, debts, and privileges. The doctrine of "Unitary Essence" dictates that while two bodies may exist, only one legal entity may hold the primary standing. The first body to register with the Accords shall be recognized as the Primary Claimant. Any subsequent body produced via cloning shall be designated as a Duplicate Claimant. The Duplicate Claimant possesses no independent rights to Guild assets, research privileges, or the right to vote within the factions of the Conservators or Innovators.

To resolve conflicts of interest between a Primary and a Duplicate Claimant, the law requires that the later body files a formal amendment to the original registration. This amendment must explicitly state the intended role of the Duplicate Claimant—whether it be as a servant, a research vessel, or a secondary laborer—and must be approved by the presiding Archmage. If a Duplicate Claimant attempts to assert independent ownership of a laboratory, a research permit, or a position within the Guild, such claims shall be summarily struck down. The law does not recognize the "right of replication" as a right of "multiplication" of legal status. One mage, regardless of the number of physical vessels they may inhabit, may only hold one seat of power or one license of practice.

Should a dispute arise regarding the distribution of resources between a Primary and a Duplicate Claimant, the Guild shall default to the Primary Claimant's rights unless a prior written agreement, notarized by a Summoned Notary under § 600.5, states otherwise. The Duplicate Claimant may be utilized for the purposes of research or field work, provided that the Primary Claimant remains the sole bearer of legal responsibility for any violations of the Accords. Any attempt to split the ownership of a licensed artifact or a restricted research copy between two bodies shall be viewed as an unauthorized division of the Guild's interests. The Accords are designed to prevent the dilution of responsibility; therefore, the clone must follow the lead of the original, and the law shall treat them as a single thread in the tapestry of the Midlands.

body.heading: § 700.3 Memory Charm as Spoliation and Evidence
body.text:
The use of memory charms or amnestic magic to alter a witness's recollection constitutes spoliation of evidence, subjecting the caster to severe penalties under §§ 1.5 and 200.4. Such acts undermine the integrity of judicial proceedings by rendering testimony unreliable and compromising the truth-finding function of the court. The burden lies upon any party claiming altered memory to prove the charm's application by clear and convincing evidence, failing which such claims shall be disregarded as frivolous and vexatious under § 100.5.

In matters involving simuli or artificial constructs bearing personal memories or personality traits, their testimony shall be deemed admissible only upon passage of a rigorous authenticity test administered by independent arcane experts. This evaluation must verify that the construct's recollections are not merely programmed responses but genuine reflections of actual events witnessed firsthand. Failure to meet these standards will result in automatic exclusion of such evidence as tainted and inadmissible under § 700.2 and related provisions governing hearsay exceptions.

Furthermore, any claimant seeking to establish identity based upon cloned or duplicated persons must first demonstrate the legal status of said duplicates through a formal hearing before the Archmagi's Court. Mere assertion of kinship or resemblance shall be insufficient grounds for recognizing duplicate entities as legitimate representatives in matters of inheritance, liability, or contractual obligation. The court retains broad discretion to deny such standing when fraud or manipulation is suspected, acting sua sponte upon reasonable cause shown under §§ 100.2 and 300.4.

This section serves to protect the sanctity of judicial fact-finding by preventing subversion through magical interference with human cognition or artificial consciousness alike. Violators face not only immediate sanctions but also potential revocation of all licenses held within the Guild's jurisdiction under § 200.1 and its implementing regulations. The principles herein are designed to maintain public confidence in the impartiality and reliability of legal processes administered by the Accords Desk, ensuring that truth prevails even in the face of arcane deceptions.

body.heading: § 700.3 Memory Charm as Spoliation and Evidence Preservation
body.text: § 700.3 Memory Charm as Spoliation and Evidence Preservation. The casting or attempted casting of a memory charm upon a material witness constitutes spoliation of evidence under § 1.4(e). Such acts shall be deemed intentional interference with the administration of justice, punishable by sanctions including but not limited to fines up to one thousand gold pieces per instance and permanent revocation of licensure. This provision applies regardless of whether the charm was successfully enacted or merely attempted. The burden of proof rests upon the accused caster to demonstrate that no such act occurred, absent evidence to the contrary. In cases where a memory charm is cast in good faith under duress or without knowledge of the witness's status as a material fact-witness, sanctions may be mitigated at the discretion of the presiding adjudicator. However, this mitigation shall not apply if the accused caster failed to disclose relevant circumstances that would have precluded them from casting such a charm lawfully. Furthermore, any party found guilty of employing memory charms for evidentiary purposes shall be barred from appearing before the Accords Desk in their own defense for a period of one lunar cycle following imposition of sanctions, unless granted an exception by special dispensation. This clause is intended to preserve the integrity of legal proceedings and prevent parties from undermining judicial processes through magical interference with human cognition. Violations of this section shall be prosecuted ex officio by the Guild's Office of Disciplinary Affairs in conjunction with relevant law enforcement agencies as appropriate under existing statutes governing criminal acts related to magic use. The principles set forth herein reflect the Accords' longstanding commitment to maintaining fair and transparent adjudication while safeguarding against abuses of magical power within judicial contexts. Any ambiguities arising from this provision shall be resolved by reference to foundational sections pertaining to evidence standards, witness protection obligations, and prohibitions on tampering with official records or persons thereof. See also §§ 700.1 through 700.2 regarding general evidentiary rules; § 850 concerning specific restrictions on memory alteration techniques; and Part IV-A for comprehensive guidelines surrounding spoliation of evidence in all its forms.

body.heading: § 700.4 Memory Charm and Admissibility
body.text:
The use of memory charms in litigation presents unique evidentiary challenges requiring careful consideration by the tribunal. Under § 700.3, when an accused mage employs a memory charm to evade detection or accountability, this act constitutes spoliation of evidence and may warrant severe sanctions against the offending party. The court retains discretion to draw adverse inferences from such conduct and impose additional penalties beyond those originally sought.

In instances where a memory charm has been successfully deployed, the burden shifts to the accuser to demonstrate by clear and convincing proof that the charm was ineffective or bypassed entirely. Failure to meet this heightened standard results in dismissal of charges, regardless of any subsequent revelations regarding underlying wrongdoing. This elevated threshold reflects the extraordinary power inherent in magical alteration of consciousness and memory.

When multiple parties claim conflicting recollections of events, particularly where memory charms may have been involved, the tribunal shall apply a rigorous scrutiny of each testimony. Corroborating evidence, witness statements, physical records, and any available magical traces must all be weighed carefully before reaching a determination of credibility. The court maintains absolute authority to order further investigations as deemed necessary for a just resolution.

Simulacra generated through advanced illusion magic may offer additional avenues for fact-finding where direct testimony proves elusive. However, the admissibility of such constructs remains subject to strict safeguards designed to prevent abuse and protect against unreliable conclusions drawn from inherently unstable sources. The tribunal shall exercise its discretion prudently when considering evidentiary value attributed to simulated representations.

Ultimately, the core principle guiding all proceedings involving memory manipulation is the preservation of truth-seeking integrity within the legal framework. While acknowledging the potent capabilities afforded by magical arts, the court must remain vigilant against erosion of factual accuracy essential for equitable justice. Balanced application of these guidelines ensures fair adjudication even in cases complicated by extraordinary supernatural elements.

sections.title: Simulacrum Testimony
sections.brief: A copy may not swear for the original.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
A copy may not swear for the original. Any entity produced via the method of arcane duplication, illusion, or somatic mirroring—collectively referred to as a "Simulacrum"—is strictly prohibited from providing testimony, depositions, or sworn statements before a tribunal of the Autumnwood Accords. The legal fiction of the Guild maintains that a Simulacrum possesses the likeness and, in some instances, the memories of the progenitor, yet it lacks the metaphysical "weight" required to bind a soul to a truth. Consequently, any statement extracted from a Simulacrum is deemed inadmissible as primary evidence. This restriction applies regardless of the degree of fidelity achieved by the caster. Even if a Simulacrum is indistinguishable from the original to the naked eye, or if it possesses the ability to replicate the vocal nuances and mannerisms of the source, it remains a mere echo. Under the Accords, only a living, sentient body of the original caster may be held accountable for the truth of their actions.

Furthermore, the use of a Simulacrum to obstruct justice by providing a "false" testimony that mirrors a "true" one is considered a grave offense. If a party seeks to utilize a Simulacrum for the purpose of information retrieval, they must first petition the Aegis Magi for a Research Permit to ensure the process does not violate the sanctity of the original's cognitive privacy. See § 400.1. Any attempt to bypass these restrictions by weaving complex "truth-binding" spells onto a duplicate shall be viewed as an attempt to circumvent the inherent limitations of the Accords and may result in a Paradox Trial. The Guild recognizes that while a copy may hold data, it cannot hold the "burden of conscience." Therefore, any legal proceeding involving a Simulacrum shall require the physical presence of the original caster to verify the authenticity of the information provided. Failure to produce the original caster for verification shall result in the immediate dismissal of the testimony and a formal warning against the use of unauthorized arcane proxies.

In cases where the original caster is deceased, a Simulacrum may be used solely for the purpose of "archival visualization" to assist the tribunal in understanding the context of past events, provided that such visualization is not presented as evidence of fact. The Clerk of the Accords shall ensure that all such visualizations are clearly marked as "Non-Testimonial Visualizations" in the court record. Any party found to be attempting to pass off a Simulacrum’s speech as the original's sworn word shall be subject to immediate sanctions, including potential sealing of their casting abilities. This law serves to protect the integrity of the Accords against the manipulation of reality by those who would seek to manufacture witnesses from the ether. See § 700.2.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
One claim. The later body files an amendment. In the event that a single magical consciousness inhabits multiple biological vessels—specifically through the process of cloning or somatic splitting—the Guild recognizes the "Doctrine of Primacy." This doctrine dictates that the first viable body to manifest or exist in a state of independent consciousness shall be the primary claimant for all legal, financial, and contractual obligations. The Guild does not recognize the existence of "multiple" citizens when the underlying magical signature is identical. Therefore, should a mage or artisan create a clone, the clone is viewed as a legal extension of the original, rather than a separate entity capable of independent litigation or contract formation. This prevents the "doubling" of assets or the "dilution" of liability within the Midlands.

When a second body is produced, it is considered a "Subordinate Vessel." If the Subordinate Vessel seeks to engage in independent commerce, property ownership, or the signing of Accords, it must first file a Formal Amendment of Status with the Accords Desk. This amendment requires the Primary Claimant to explicitly delegate specific rights to the Subordinate Vessel. Without such a filing, any contract signed by the clone is legally voidable at the whim of the Primary Claimant, as the Guild views the clone as a mere tool or "construct" of the original's will. This mirrors the protections found in § 600.4 regarding construct labor, as the Guild refuses to grant full personhood to bodies that are manufactured by the intent of another. The Primary Claimant retains all core rights, including the right to the original's Guild license and the responsibility for any debts incurred by the Subordinate Vessel.

If a dispute arises between two bodies of the same consciousness regarding the ownership of a specific artifact or land, the Guild shall default to the Primary Claimant's claim unless a prior "Splitting of Essence" decree has been filed. Such a decree is a rare and difficult-to-obtain legal maneuver, requiring a high-level mediation by Archmage Veyra herself. In the absence of such a decree, the "later body" is legally subordinate. Any attempt by a clone to file a separate claim of ownership without the Primary Claimant's signature shall be treated as an unauthorized expansion of magical influence and may be subject to a Paradox Trial. This ensures that the radical Innovators cannot use cloning to circumvent the limitations of the Accords or to multiply their influence within the Autumn Wood. See § 200.1.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony and Duplicate Claims
body.text:
§ 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony; The Original's Voice
A simulative construct, regardless of its fidelity or autonomy, may not testify as the original caster in matters pertaining to the latter's intent, state of mind, or personal knowledge. While a high-resolution copy may replicate speech patterns and mannerisms with uncanny accuracy, it lacks the requisite consciousness to bear witness truthfully. Any attempt to introduce simulatory testimony in place of the original shall be deemed a violation of § 700.1. Exceptions apply only where the original is legally unavailable and a court order has been granted permitting the use of a certified duplicate under strict evidentiary safeguards.

In cases involving multiple duplicates, each claimant must establish their unique identity beyond reasonable doubt. Mere possession of a simulative token does not confer standing to represent the true self. The burden rests upon the alleged original to prove continuity of consciousness and agency from birth until the present moment. Failure to do so results in dismissal of the claim and potential sanctions for false pretenses under § 800.2.

The Desk retains discretion to appoint an independent arbiter of identity whose findings shall be binding absent proof of error or corruption. Such appointments are made only when necessary to resolve disputes over authentic selfhood that threaten public order or undermine judicial integrity. The cost thereof is borne equally by all parties unless otherwise ordered.

This provision reflects the fundamental principle that no artificial intelligence, however advanced, can fully embody the complex web of human experience that defines an individual's soul. To conflate simulation with substance risks eroding the very fabric of personhood itself—a danger far greater than any mere inconvenience to litigants. Thus stands the rule: let copies mimic as they may; the true self remains inviolate, guarded by law and reason alike.

"see § 1.4 Persons Bound", "under § 700.1 Evidence Generally", "refer to § 800.2 Sanctions for False Pretenses".

body.heading: 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony and Duplicate Claimants
body.text:
A simulacrum, whether conjured through forbidden rites or engineered by artificers, shall possess no legal capacity to testify on its own behalf. The fundamental principle remains that a duplicate may not swear for the original; such testimony is inherently suspect and inadmissible without corroboration from independent witnesses. This restriction applies equally to simulacrums created via magical transmutation as it does to those manufactured through mechanical means.

However, where a simulacrum has been granted artificial sentience sufficient to understand and communicate truthfully, its statements may be admitted as secondary evidence upon showing of necessity. The burden lies upon the proponent to demonstrate that no other practical alternative exists for obtaining relevant information, given the unavailability or inability of the true self to participate in proceedings. Such testimony shall carry diminished evidentiary weight compared to direct observation or primary documentation.

In cases involving duplicate claimants arising from cloning procedures, the initial clone retains standing as a separate entity until proven otherwise by preponderance of evidence. Any assertion that a later-created simulacrum supersedes an earlier one must be supported by clear proof of intentional obfuscation or fraudulent misrepresentation by the first party involved. Absent such demonstration, each duplicate maintains distinct legal status and rights under the Accords.

The Desk reserves discretion to admit simulacrum testimony in exceptional circumstances where strict application of this rule would unjustly prejudice a litigant's ability to present their case fully. Such rulings shall be made only after careful consideration of all relevant factors and with explicit findings recorded in the official docket. Any party objecting must raise such grounds at the earliest convenient time, failing which may constitute a waiver thereof.

Ultimately, the guiding principle remains that a copy cannot supplant the original without clear justification. While technological advancements continue to blur traditional distinctions between persons and their reproductions, this foundational tenet of personal integrity shall endure as a bulwark against abuse and manipulation within the arcane community. The Desk stands ready to address novel challenges posed by evolving practices while maintaining fidelity to established precedents.

see § 700.1 Evidence Generally; see § 600.2 Familiars as Agents; under § 3.7 Burden of Proof; pursuant to § 4.9 Judicial Discretion. A simulacrum's words hold little weight without corroboration or necessity. Each duplicate stands alone until proven otherwise. The Desk balances fairness with precedent, ready to adapt to new realities while guarding core values. Legal capacity remains tied to true selfhood, even in an age of artificial replication.

body.heading: § 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony and Duplicate Claimants
body.text:
Simulacrums generated through lawful duplication processes retain all memories, skills, and personality traits of the original caster at the time of replication. However, they possess no legal standing distinct from their source. When a simulacrum invokes rights or asserts claims in its own name, such acts are deemed void ab initio unless ratified by the original individual under duress or undue influence.

In cases where multiple duplicates exist simultaneously, each shall be treated as an independent entity for the purposes of magical research and development only. No duplicate may represent the interests of another without explicit authorization granted in writing and witnessed by two disinterested mages registered with the Guild. Unauthorized duplication beyond permitted limits constitutes a Class C felony under § 200.1(a)(3).

The original caster retains sole authority to revoke any previously issued duplications at will, provided adequate notice is given to all affected parties. Failure to provide such notice renders subsequent revocations null and void unless accompanied by proof of immediate danger posed by continued existence of the duplicates.

When disputes arise concerning ownership or control of duplicate entities, resolution shall follow standard arbitration procedures outlined in §§ 600-799. Parties may petition the Desk for a provisional injunction to halt further replication activities pending final determination on the merits of their respective claims.

This provision exists to prevent exploitation and abuse of duplication technology while recognizing its legitimate applications within the bounds set forth by these Accords. Any circumvention thereof shall be prosecuted as an aggravating circumstance in accordance with applicable penal statutes.

body.heading: § 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony and Duplicate Claimants — Continued
body.text: A simulated duplicate possesses no legal personality independent of its source, and may not testify or plead in the stead thereof unless expressly authorized by the court upon showing of necessity. Any attempt to bind a duplicate's signature or testimony against its original shall be deemed void ab initio for want of capacity. However, where an original is irretrievably lost or destroyed, a duplicate sworn before two disinterested witnesses may stand as sufficient evidence in lieu thereof. The burden lies squarely on the party producing such substitute proof to demonstrate both the chain of custody and the authenticity of the duplication process beyond reasonable doubt. Failure so to do shall result in dismissal of any claim predicated upon said duplicate's purported assertions or admissions. This provision exists solely to mitigate undue hardship where physical presence of a litigant proves impossible, not to circumvent fundamental fairness requirements inherent to adversarial proceedings. As such, courts retain broad discretion to deny substitution requests whenever they deem the risks of fraud or perjury outweigh the convenience offered by remote participation via simulacra.

sections.title: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
sections.brief: One claim. The later body files an amendment.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
In the event that a legal claimant presents a physical duplicate of their person—whether through the use of high-fidelity transmutation, sophisticated illusionary weaving, or the biological replication of cellular matter—the Guild shall recognize only the primary biological entity as the rightful holder of any and all legal claims, properties, or titles. The existence of a secondary body does not constitute a secondary right of ownership, nor does it grant the duplicate the standing to act as a joint tenant or a co-claimant in any matter before the Accords. Any attempt to utilize a duplicate body to circumvent debt, evade the Paradox Trial, or assert multiple interests in a single asset shall be deemed an act ofarcane fraud and a violation of the foundational principles of the Autumnwood Accords.

The Guild’s stance on replication is predicated on the principle of singular identity. When a mage or a layperson produces a clone, that clone is viewed by the Accords as an extension of the original's will, not as an independent legal persona. Consequently, if a claimant possesses a duplicate, the Guild shall treat all actions taken by the duplicate as if they were taken by the primary body. If the duplicate is used to acquire property, that property belongs to the primary; if the duplicate is used to incur debt, the primary is liable. This prevents the "doubling" of rights which would otherwise destabilize the economic and social fabric of the Midlands.

Should a legal dispute arise involving both the primary body and a duplicate, the Guild shall permit the later-manifested body to file a formal amendment to the primary's status. This amendment may be used to define the specific operational boundaries of the duplicate—for instance, designating it as a "Laborer Entity" or a "Research Proxy"—but it cannot be used to sever the link of ownership. The filing of such an amendment serves to clarify the intent of the primary claimant and to ensure that the Guild’s records reflect the intended use of the replication. Failure to file an amendment within three lunar cycles of the duplicate’s manifestation shall result in the Guild assuming a default "Proxy Status," wherein the duplicate is granted no rights beyond those of a common construct, as defined in § 600.4.

Furthermore, any attempt to claim that a duplicate is a separate legal "person" for the purpose of splitting a single inheritance or a single license shall be summarily dismissed. The Guild acknowledges the complexities of replication, yet it maintains that a soul—or the arcane signature associated with a legal identity—cannot be partitioned without a specific, high-level decree from Archmage Veyra. See § 700.1 for general evidence requirements regarding identity. Any mage found attempting to use a duplicate to bypass the restrictions of § 200.1 or to manufacture "new" claimants for the purpose of illicit trade shall be subject to immediate referral for a Paradox Trial. The Aegis Magi are authorized to seize all assets of a duplicate that are not explicitly bonded to the primary body in a filed amendment.

body.heading: § 700.5 Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
In the event that a caster creates a duplicate of their own form through means such as cloning, duplication magic, or transference rituals, both entities shall be deemed distinct legal persons under these Accords, each bearing full responsibility for their respective actions and obligations. The original caster retains ownership of any magical knowledge, artifacts, or rights accrued prior to the creation of the clone, unless explicitly transferred via binding contract witnessed by a neutral party.

However, should either the original or the cloned entity violate the provisions of these Accords, both shall be held jointly liable for any resulting damages or penalties imposed upon them collectively by the Mages' Guild. This joint liability provision exists to discourage reckless experimentation with duplication technologies that could lead to unpredictable and potentially catastrophic outcomes should one form fail or act independently without coordination.

Furthermore, in situations where the original caster's identity has been fully subsumed into the cloned entity through complete magical integration, the new composite being shall be recognized as the sole legal successor to all prior rights and duties of its constituent parts. This principle ensures continuity of responsibility even when the precise boundaries between self and other have become obscured by advanced transference techniques.

It is expressly forbidden for any caster to create multiple duplicates with the intent of evading liability or distributing guilt among several forms. Such malicious gaming of the system shall be punished as a felony offense under these Accords, subject to maximum sanctions including permanent sealing of magical abilities and exile from civilized society at the discretion of the presiding judge.

This clause serves to clarify the complex legal implications arising from duplication magic while maintaining accountability for all actions taken by casters regardless of their physical manifestation. The Mages' Guild remains committed to upholding these principles to ensure fair and consistent application of justice within our shared reality.

body.heading: § 700.5 Duplicate Claimants and the Priority Rule
body.text:
In cases where multiple parties assert competing claims to the same magical effect, object, or benefit derived therefrom, this Code establishes a clear framework for determining precedence based on temporal priority of entitlement. Where two or more individuals or entities find themselves in possession of identical rights to exploit an arcane resource, the party whose claim vests first in time shall be accorded exclusive dominion over said asset during the pendency of any ensuing dispute resolution process. This principle applies regardless of whether the competing interests are mutually exclusive or capable of concurrent enjoyment; mere existence of conflicting titles precludes simultaneous exercise thereof without express consent from all concerned parties.

The temporal priority rule serves as a default mechanism for allocating scarce magical goods when contractual provisions fail to address specific scenarios arising from overlapping claims. It is premised upon the notion that earlier entitlement warrants preferential treatment, reflecting both fairness and practical necessity in an environment where rivalries may escalate rapidly into violence should access remain ambiguous. Parties entering into agreements involving shared resources are advised to specify priority mechanisms within their operative clauses rather than relying upon this statutory fallback. Nevertheless, absent such stipulation, first-in-time shall govern unless contrary intent appears clearly on the face of the instrument or is otherwise demonstrated by reliable extrinsic evidence.

This provision does not extinguish superior equitable interests merely accrued subsequent to initial vesting, nor does it absolve later claimants from liability for tortious interference with established rights where such conduct occurs despite knowledge thereof. Rather, it creates a presumption favoring the primacy of antecedent titles absent affirmative waiver or modification by all affected stakeholders. Courts charged with adjudicating such disputes are directed to apply this rule diligently and impartially, ensuring that no party gains improper advantage through manipulation of procedural timelines or misrepresentation of facts surrounding origin of claim. Only upon full resolution of competing interests may subsequent arrangements be finalized without risk of challenge based on prior occupancy status.

See also §§ 700.1 Evidence Generally; 700.2 Scrying of Closed Books; 600.4 Construct Labor and Minimum Ward Requirements. Under § 1.8 Effective Date, these provisions shall remain in force until explicitly amended or superseded by subsequent enactments deemed necessary to address evolving circumstances within the Guild's jurisdictional sphere. Archmage Veyra reserves authority to issue supplementary guidelines as needed to clarify application of this priority framework across diverse factual contexts encountered in practice.

body.heading: § 700.5 Duplicate Claimants and the Priority Rule — Continued
body.text:
Where two or more claimants assert identical interests in the same subject matter, priority shall be determined by temporal precedence under § 1.4 (Persons Bound). The first duly filed claim takes precedence over subsequent filings unless fraud or bad faith is proven on the face of the record. See also § 600.3 (Geas as an Unconscionable Term) regarding duress in contract formation, and § 700.2 (Scrying of Closed Books) for admissibility standards.

In cases involving artificial duplicates—whether magically conjured similes or legally replicated instruments—the original document retains primacy unless expressly superseded by a later amendment executed with full formalities. Under § 400.1 (Research Permits), any modification to an authorized act requires separate approval and re-certification, not mere clerical alteration. This principle extends analogously to duplicate claims, where the initial filing establishes the foundational right subject only to valid revocation or novation pursuant to governing statutes.

Where conflicting titles arise from parallel filings occurring within the same calendar hour, such as during system-wide outages or emergency sessions convened under § 100.8 (Emergency Sitting), tie-breaking shall follow a randomized algorithm overseen by an impartial arbiter selected via lot. The resulting determination becomes binding absent manifest error or procedural irregularity demonstrable on its face. See § 100.4 (Records of Speech) for authentication protocols and § 700.3 (Memory Charm as Spoliation) regarding evidentiary burdens in disputed scenarios.

Parties seeking to challenge a priority ruling must petition the Autumnwood Accords Desk within seven lunar cycles of notification, providing sworn affidavits substantiating their case under oath. Failure to comply with this timeline constitutes waiver of further recourse except through extraordinary writs granted solely at the discretion of Archmage Veyra personally.
