Refer to § 100.2 (Who May Speak for the Guild) for standing requirements and § 200.3 (Temporary Mouths) regarding proxy representation limitations.

The foregoing provisions reflect the longstanding wisdom that clarity in ownership prevents chaos in practice, a maxim enshrined across all civilized jurisdictions since time immemorial. As our ancestors declared, "One true master per vessel," lest the whole sink beneath conflicting weights of greed and entitlement. Thus stands the law, immutable save by due process alone. May it guide us well.

"Order through precision; justice through procedure." – Archmage Theron, Conservator Leader

body.heading: Duplicate Claimants and the Priority Rule — Continued
body.text:
§ 700.5 Duplicate Claimants and the Priority Rule — Continued

In instances where multiple claimants present themselves as identical duplicates of an original entity, the Accords establish a clear hierarchy to resolve competing assertions. The primary factor in determining precedence shall be temporal priority: the first party to successfully demonstrate their status as a genuine duplicate shall retain exclusive rights to any benefits derived therefrom. Subsequent claimants shall be deemed derivative entities and granted no further entitlements under this provision unless expressly authorized by the original holder or their duly appointed proxy.

To substantiate claims of duplication, each applicant must provide irrefutable proof of origin, including but not limited to genetic matching, biometric analysis, or authenticated testimony from recognized authorities within the relevant field. Failure to produce adequate evidence shall result in immediate disqualification and potential sanctions for attempted fraud under § 800.12 (Misrepresentation). The burden of proving duplicate status rests solely upon the asserting party and cannot be shifted through presumption or implication.

Furthermore, any attempt to exploit duplicate status for financial gain beyond the scope of legitimate restitution is strictly prohibited and shall constitute a serious violation subject to enhanced penalties under § 900.7 (Abuse of Privilege). The Accords recognize that duplication can create complex legal entanglements requiring careful navigation by all parties involved. Therefore, claimants are urged to seek counsel from qualified practitioners before proceeding with any actions based on their purported status as duplicates.

In the event of disputes arising from conflicting duplicate claims, the matter shall be adjudicated according to established procedural guidelines outlined in Part VIII (Dispute Resolution). The decision rendered by the competent authority shall be binding and final unless overturned through proper appellate channels. This framework ensures fairness and consistency in addressing the unique challenges posed by duplication phenomena while safeguarding against exploitation of the system by malicious actors seeking undue advantage at the expense of others.

Through these provisions, the Accords seek to balance the interests of original entities with those of their duplicates, promoting equitable treatment while maintaining integrity within the broader legal framework governing such extraordinary circumstances. Compliance with this section is mandatory for all parties involved in duplicate-related matters and failure to adhere thereto may result in severe consequences as specified throughout this Code.

body.heading: Duplicate Claimants and the Priority Rule — Continued — Continued
body.text:
In the event that multiple duplicate claimants emerge, each having satisfied the requisite conditions for recognition under these Accords, priority shall be determined by the temporal sequence of their initial filings with the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The first in time shall prevail absent extenuating circumstances or evidence of fraud or collusion as provided herein. This provision ensures equitable treatment while discouraging speculative hoarding of duplicate rights by bad actors seeking to manipulate the system for personal gain.

Should a dispute arise regarding the validity or precedence of competing claims, an expedited adjudication process shall be triggered upon written request from any interested party. The presiding arbiter shall review all relevant documentation and testimony within seven business days thereafter, rendering a binding decision based strictly on the provisions set forth in these Accords. Appeals of such determinations shall lie solely with the full Council, which may convene at its earliest convenience to hear arguments from both sides before issuing final judgment.

It is hereby declared that no duplicate claimant shall be permitted to exploit their status for undue advantage over others operating within the bounds of lawful commerce under these Accords. Engaging in predatory practices aimed solely at undermining competitors through the abuse of duplicate rights constitutes a material breach warranting severe penalties as prescribed by applicable law and Guild policy. The integrity of this delicate marketplace depends upon fair play and mutual respect among all participants – principles that must be upheld without exception to preserve the long-term viability of our collective enterprise.

By virtue of their voluntary association with the Autumnwood Accords Desk, duplicate claimants agree to abide fully by these rules and regulations at all times. Failure to do so may result in immediate expulsion from good standing along with such additional sanctions as deemed appropriate under the circumstances. The Council retains broad discretion to enforce compliance vigorously whenever necessary to safeguard the interests of all stakeholders involved. Through diligent adherence to these mandates, we shall foster an environment conducive to innovation and prosperity for generations yet unborn.

*Note: This section applies equally whether disputes concern direct commercial rivals or seemingly unrelated entities whose actions nonetheless impact one another adversely in significant ways.*

sections.title: Discipline; Range of Sanctions
sections.brief: From fee to seal to pocket-prison. Paradox Trial named.

body.heading: Discipline; Range of Sanctions
body.text:
The disciplinary framework of the Autumnwood Accords is predicated upon the principle of proportional restoration, wherein the severity of the sanction shall be directly correlated to the magnitude of the arcane transgression and the potential risk posed to the stability of the Midlands. All punitive measures are overseen by the Accords Desk, with the Archmage Sovereign maintaining final appellate authority. For minor infractions, such as the unauthorized use of common cantrips in residential zones or the failure to register a minor familiar, the Guild shall levy a standard administrative fee. These fees are non-negotiable and are to be paid in recognized currency; notably, the Wario Coin is strictly prohibited as a medium of tender for any Guild transaction, per the standing prohibitions on non-standardized currency.

For more significant violations, specifically those involving the reckless manipulation of mana or the infringement upon the privacy of other mages, the Guild may impose a Seal of Silence or a magical Seal of Binding. A Seal of Binding is a permanent or semi-permanent restriction placed upon a practitioner’s ability to channel the weave, effectively neutralizing their threat to the public and the Guild's interests. The application of such a Seal requires a formal finding of negligence or malice by a tribunal of the Aegis Magi. In cases where a mage’s actions threaten the very fabric of reality—such as the creation of a rift or the unauthorized growth of a Titan—the sanction shall escalate to the ultimate punitive measure: the Pocket-Prison.

The Pocket-Prison serves as a localized, extra-dimensional incarceration designed to isolate dangerous individuals from the material plane indefinitely. Entry into the Pocket-Prison is the final recourse of the Accords, reserved for those whose presence in the Midlands constitutes an existential risk. All disciplinary actions, regardless of scale, are recorded in the central registry to ensure that the history of the Accords remains transparent to the Conservators and the Innovators alike. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Transgression" and "Arcane Magnitude." See § 800.1 for the naming of the Paradox Trial as the primary judicial mechanism for these sanctions.

body.heading: Paradox Trial Procedure
body.text:
The Paradox Trial is the official judicial mechanism of the Autumnwood Accords, designed to adjudicate complex disputes and criminal charges through a system of peer review. It is mandated that all high-level disputes involving the use of restricted magic, the violation of the Quiet List, or the breach of the Unsanctioned Arts be brought before a council of peers. These peers shall be selected from a pool of qualified mages who are not directly involved in the litigation, ensuring a semblance of impartiality between the traditionalist Conservators and the radical Innovators. The trial shall be conducted in a designated neutral hall within the Autumn Wood, where the Aegis Magi are tasked with maintaining the integrity of the magical perimeter.

During the Paradox Trial, all evidence must be presented in a structured format, and every testimony shall be recorded by a Summoned Notary to ensure a permanent legal record. The proceedings may involve the demonstration of magical theory, the presentation of seized artifacts, or the recitation of historical precedents. The objective of the trial is to determine the truth of the violation and to assign the appropriate sanction as outlined in § 800.1. The council shall deliberate in private, and their verdict shall be binding upon all signatories of the Accords.

Strict prohibition is placed upon the conduct of unscheduled street duels. While the Guild recognizes the historical prevalence of magical combat, the Accords decree that no duel shall be considered a legal method of dispute resolution unless it has been formally scheduled, registered, and sanctioned by the Accords Desk. Any mage who engages in an unscheduled duel in a public space shall be subject to immediate arrest by the Aegis Magi and shall be liable for the costs of the intervention. Only through the formal Paradox Trial may a mage seek to vindicate their honor or reclaim stolen property. See § 700.1 for evidence standards.

body.heading: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
The Seal of Silence is a specific disciplinary measure employed when a mage’s speech—whether spoken, telepathic, or inscribed—poses a risk to the stability of the magical order or involves the unauthorized dissemination of information regarding the Quiet List. Upon the imposition of the Seal, the affected individual is rendered incapable of producing any linguistic output that can be perceived by others. The duration of this Seal is determined by the presiding council during the Paradox Trial, based on the severity of the breach. A standard Seal of Silence for minor informational leaks shall last for a period of no less than one lunar cycle and no more than three years, depending on the frequency of the offender's previous infractions.

While a Seal of Silence is active, the individual may still engage in non-verbal activities, such as the study of theory or the maintenance of mundane tasks, provided these actions do not involve the manipulation of the weave in a manner that could be interpreted as coded communication. The Seal is not a total removal of agency but a targeted restriction on the medium of speech. The Accords Desk shall monitor the effectiveness of the Seal to ensure it does not cause unintended physiological harm to the caster, as the preservation of the caster's health is a secondary priority to the preservation of the Guild's secrets.

A mage under the Seal of Silence may petition for a review of their sentence after the passage of one-half of the designated duration. Such a petition must be submitted in writing, using a pre-approved method of non-verbal transcription, and must be presented to the Archmage Sovereign for mediation. The review shall consider the mage's conduct during the period of silence, their cooperation with the Aegis Magi, and the current threat level posed by the information they were originally seeking to disseminate. If the petition is granted, the Seal may be lifted, shortened, or modified. If the petition is denied, the remaining duration of the Seal shall stand. See § 300.3 for Quiet List Procedure.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In instances where a mage insists upon a formal Trial by Arcane Duel as the primary method of adjudication—specifically when the legal merits of a case are deemed too nuanced for a standard peer review—the Accords Desk shall intervene to ensure the preservation of public safety and the Guild's resources. While the Guild acknowledges the cultural significance of the duel, it shall not permit the destruction of infrastructure or the collateral damage inherent in high-level magical combat. Therefore, the Accords Desk shall mandate that the "stakes" of the duel be converted into administrative fees and restorative penalties.

The conversion process requires the parties to agree upon a pre-determined valuation of the dispute. For example, if a mage seeks to reclaim a stolen artifact, the "win" condition of the duel shall be the legal transfer of the item, while the "loss" condition shall be the payment of a substantial fine to the Guild’s treasury. The Aegis Magi shall oversee the duel, and should either participant exceed the permitted output of mana or target non-combatants, the duel shall be immediately terminated. The losing party shall be held liable for the full cost of the Aegis Magi's intervention, as well as a punitive surcharge for the unsanctioned escalation of magical force.

This conversion of stakes ensures that the Paradox Trial remains the primary judicial framework while still allowing for the resolution of disputes through active magical demonstration. The Accords Desk shall maintain a schedule of these converted duels, ensuring that they occur in designated "duel-pits" where the magical fallout can be safely dissipated. No duel shall be permitted to proceed if the projected cost of the collateral damage exceeds the valuation of the stakes. This policy serves to prevent the "scorched earth" tactics often favored by the Innovator faction in their pursuit of radical results. See § 800.2 for Paradox Trial Procedure.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The Pocket-Prison is the ultimate site of incarceration for those deemed too dangerous to remain within the Midlands or those whose magic has become fundamentally erratic. The procedure for commitment to a Pocket-Prison is strictly regulated to prevent the arbitrary disappearance of Guild members. A mage may only be committed to a Pocket-Prison following a final verdict of the Paradox Trial, where the council determines that sealing the mage's magic (as per § 800.1) is insufficient to protect the public. The commitment must be signed off by both the Archmage Sovereign and the head of the Conservators, ensuring that the decision is made with the full weight of the Guild's authority.

The "key" to a Pocket-Prison is not a physical object but a complex, multi-layered arcane lock maintained by the Aegis Magi. Only the Archmage Sovereign and the designated High Conservator may authorize the opening of a cell. The prison itself is a pocket dimension, isolated from the flow of standard time and the reach of external scrying. This isolation is necessary to prevent the "leakage" of dangerous magic into the surrounding environment. Once a mage is committed, their presence is struck from the active census of the Midlands, though their records remain accessible to the Accords Desk for historical and legal purposes.

Regarding the conditions of confinement, the Accords are silent on the specifics of daily life within the Pocket-Prison, as these are considered internal security matters. However, it is a common misconception among the populace that "visiting hours" exist for those incarcerated in a Pocket-Prison. The Accords Desk officially denies the existence of such a practice, as the very nature of the pocket dimension precludes safe external access. Any attempt to scry into the Pocket-Prison or to bypass the Aegis Magi's wards to reach an inmate shall be treated as a high-level felony, punishable by immediate and permanent Seal of Binding. See § 400.2 for details on Pocket Dimensions as Labs.

body.heading: § 800.1 Discipline; Range of Sanctions
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords provide for a graduated system of disciplinary measures, ranging from admonition to permanent exile. The severity of the sanction imposed shall be commensurate with the gravity of the infraction and the circumstances surrounding it. For minor infractions such as technical violations or first-time offenses where no harm was done, reprimand coupled with mandatory remedial education may suffice. More serious breaches warrant stronger penalties including suspension of licensure, temporary sealing of magical faculties, or revocation of privileges for a defined period.

In cases involving substantial violations of the Accords' core principles—such as unauthorized casting in restricted areas, misuse of forbidden schools, or repeated negligence causing damage—the Council may impose more draconian measures. This includes permanent expulsion from the Guild and stripping of all titles and honors held therein. In extreme instances where a caster poses an existential threat to public safety through their continued operation, total incapacitation via magical sealing may be deemed necessary. Such actions shall only be undertaken after due process has been fully observed and a clear majority vote obtained at a formal session of the Council.

The Paradox Trial serves as the primary adjudicatory mechanism for resolving disputes between mages regarding alleged violations of the Accords. This quasi-judicial proceeding is conducted before an impartial panel consisting of three peer casters selected randomly from the membership rolls. The accused mage shall be afforded full opportunity to present their defense, call witnesses, and cross-examine opposing evidence before a ruling is rendered. If found guilty beyond reasonable doubt, sanctions may include imposition of fines payable in guild coin, temporary suspension without pay, or permanent forfeiture of standing within the organization depending on severity.

For particularly egregious violations involving intentional malfeasance or gross incompetence endangering lives, more severe consequences apply. These may encompass revocation of all licenses and certifications held by the offending individual along with blacklisting from future employment opportunities within the magical profession. In worst-case scenarios where an individual demonstrates unremediable dangerousness through pattern of conduct, permanent sealing of their innate abilities via ritualistic means may be deemed appropriate to protect society at large. Such radical measures require unanimous approval by the full Council and shall remain subject to periodic review should circumstances warrant reconsideration.

Any sanctions imposed pursuant to this section shall be executed promptly upon final determination unless stayed pending appeal proceedings. Failure to comply with an order of the Council within specified timeframes constitutes further misconduct punishable under these same provisions. The Guild retains broad discretion in tailoring appropriate remedies tailored to the specific facts presented, balancing interests of justice against potential collateral impacts on innocent parties caught up in enforcement actions arising from another's wrongdoing. Through consistent and fair application of these disciplinary standards, the Autumnwood Accords aims to maintain high ethical benchmarks throughout the magical community while safeguarding public welfare above all else.

sections.title: Paradox Trial Procedure
sections.brief: Peers, record, no street duel unless scheduled.

body.heading: Paradox Trial Procedure
body.text:
The Paradox Trial shall serve as the primary judicial mechanism for the resolution of high-level arcane disputes and the adjudication of severe violations of the Autumnwood Accords. Per § 800.1, all trials must be overseen by a council of peers, defined as mages of equivalent or greater established rank who possess no direct familial or commercial ties to the accused or the complainant. The presence of these peers ensures that the delicate balance between the Conservator and Innovator philosophies is maintained, preventing any single faction from weaponizing the judiciary to achieve absolute hegemony over the Midlands. The primary objective of the Paradox Trial is the preservation of the Weave and the safety of the citizenry; consequently, the council shall prioritize the containment of volatile magic over the immediate satisfaction of personal grievances.

All proceedings of the Paradox Trial shall be entered into the permanent record of the Accords Desk. Each testimony, magical manifestation, and evidentiary artifact presented during the trial must be transcribed by a bonded Notary or a construct authorized under § 600.5. These records are to be kept in a secure, magically-warded archive, accessible only to the Archmage Sovereign and the presiding Council. The records serve not only as a historical ledger but as a binding precedent for future adjudications. Any mage found to have willfully falsified a trial record or attempted to redact testimony shall be subject to immediate sentencing under the maximum severity tier of § 800.1.

Furthermore, the Paradox Trial expressly prohibits the conduct of street duels as a means of settling legal disputes. While the history of magic is replete with spontaneous arcane combat, the Accords Decree that all such conflicts must be moved into a formal, magically-regulated environment. If a complainant and a defendant insist upon a Trial by Arcane Duel, it must be scheduled with at least forty-eight hours of notice to the Aegis Magi for the purpose of establishing a neutral arena and safety wards. Any mage who initiates an unscheduled duel in a public space or within the bounds of the Autumn Wood shall be deemed to have forfeited their right to a fair trial and shall be subject to summary detention. See § 800.1 for the range of sanctions applicable to such violations.

body.heading: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
The Seal of Silence is a restorative and punitive measure utilized primarily when a caster has engaged in the unauthorized recitation of the Quiet List or has engaged in speech that threatens the stability of local mana-currents. Upon the imposition of the Seal, the subject’s vocal apparatus shall be magically locked, preventing any audible speech, including the casting of verbal components. The duration of this Seal is determined by the presiding Council based on the severity of the infraction as outlined in § 300.3. For minor infractions, such as the accidental utterance of a restricted name in a tavern, the Seal may be set for a period of no less than one lunar cycle. For grave violations, including the deliberate dissemination of forbidden knowledge, the Seal may be rendered permanent, subject only to a formal petition for review.

A mage under the Seal of Silence is not exempt from the basic rights of the Accords, yet they are strictly prohibited from using any form of telepathic communication to circumvent the vocal restriction. Any attempt to bypass the Seal via external magical means shall be viewed as an act of defiance against the Accords Desk and may result in the extension of the current Seal or a transition to a more severe penal status. The Seal is intended to provide a period of reflection and to "cool" the magical residue of the offender’s intent. During this time, the mage may still be required to perform manual labor or study non-verbal theory, provided such activities do not involve the manipulation of the Weave in a way that could trigger a resonance with the Seal.

Review of the Seal of Silence shall occur at the conclusion of each designated period. The mage may submit a written petition, transcribed by a designated proxy or through a pre-arranged series of non-verbal signs, requesting a reduction in the Seal’s duration. The Council shall review the mage’s conduct during the period of silence; if the mage has demonstrated a marked decrease in erratic magical behavior and has complied with all other Guild mandates, the Seal may be lifted or shortened. If the mage has shown signs of escalating magical instability or has attempted to subvert the Seal, the Council shall maintain the current duration or increase it accordingly. See § 200.4 for procedures regarding the lapse of such magical effects.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In instances where a dispute cannot be settled through standard arbitration and the parties involved insist upon a Trial by Arcane Duel, the Accords Desk shall intervene to ensure the fiscal and structural integrity of the Guild. While the duel serves as the mechanism for determining guilt or innocence, it is not a mechanism for the private transfer of wealth or the destruction of assets. All stakes agreed upon by the combatants—whether they be gold, land, magical artifacts, or services—shall be automatically converted into administrative fees payable to the Accords Desk. This conversion is mandatory and shall be calculated based on the estimated cost of the magical wards, the Aegis Magi presence, and the logistical overhead required to host the duel.

The conversion of stakes ensures that the Guild is not burdened by the costs of policing private magical violence. Should the combatants agree to a stake of one thousand gold, the Accords Desk shall seize that amount and apply it toward the maintenance of the Autumn Wood facilities. If the stake involves a tangible asset, such as a deed to a workshop or a rare reagent, the Desk shall assess a fair market value and levy a corresponding fee. The winning party shall receive their judicial victory—the legal recognition of their claim—but they shall not receive the physical stake or the converted gold. The purpose of this provision is to strip the profit motive from the act of magical combat, ensuring that mages do not engage in duels for mercenary gain.

Any attempt to circumvent this fee conversion by entering into "side-agreements" with outside parties, such as the Regal Empire or the Goodstyle Artisans, shall be considered a violation of the Accords. If a mage is found to be using a duel as a pretext for a private transaction, the duel shall be declared void, and both parties shall be subject to immediate investigation. The Aegis Magi are authorized to seize any assets involved in such a fraudulent arrangement. Mages who find this provision burdensome are encouraged to seek mediation through the Archmage Sovereign to avoid the high costs associated with formal duels. See § 800.2 for the procedures regarding the scheduling of such duels.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The Pocket-Prison is a specialized containment facility utilized for mages whose magic has become fundamentally volatile or whose crimes against the Accords necessitate total isolation from the physical plane. Unlike a standard detention cell, a Pocket-Prison is a self-contained pocket dimension, isolated from the primary Weave to prevent the prisoner from drawing upon external mana or affecting the world outside. The keys to these dimensions are held exclusively by the High Conservators, and access to the prison is strictly regulated by the Accords Desk. No mage may enter a Pocket-Prison without a direct mandate from Archmage Veyra or a unanimous vote from the Council of Peers.

The procedure for incarceration involves the "Sealing of the Threshold," where the prisoner is cast into the dimension and the entrance is collapsed, leaving only a singular, magically-locked point of entry. Once the threshold is closed, the prisoner is effectively removed from the timeline of the Midlands. The maintenance of the Pocket-Prison requires a constant, low-level expenditure of mana from the Guild’s central reserves, making it a costly and significant undertaking. Consequently, incarceration is reserved for the most dangerous offenders or those whose magic poses a systemic risk to the Autumnwood Accords. The prisoner is provided with a basic existence—sustenance and environment—but these are to be sufficient only for survival, not for comfort.

Regarding the status of visiting hours, the Accords Desk maintains a policy of absolute secrecy. While rumors persist among the lower-tier mages that certain high-profile prisoners may receive visitors, the official stance of the Guild is that no such visits are permitted. Any attempt to establish a communication link with a prisoner in a Pocket-Prison is a felony under the Accords and may result in the immediate sentencing of the visitor to a similar confinement. The isolation of the prisoner is a matter of public safety; any breach of this isolation, whether through physical entry or magical scrying, is to be met with the highest tier of sanction. See § 400.2 for regulations regarding the use of pocket dimensions for authorized research purposes.

body.heading: § 800.2 Paradox Trial Procedure; Seal of Silence
body.text:
The Paradox Trial shall commence only upon formal indictment by the Aegis Magi, citing specific violations of this Code. The accused may demand a hearing before the High Council within seven days of service of process. Failure to appear constitutes a default judgment of guilt, punishable by immediate sealing of magical faculties and permanent exile from Autumn Wood.

At trial, the accused shall be granted counsel of their choosing, provided such counsel is duly licensed under § 102.3. Evidence may include but is not limited to: certified copies of inspection reports (§ 805.1), witness testimony subject to cross-examination per common law rules adapted for arcane matters, and authenticated magical signatures linking the accused to the charged conduct. The burden of proof rests upon the prosecution; mere suspicion or circumstantial association shall not suffice.

Upon conclusion of proceedings, the Council shall render a verdict within ten days. If found guilty beyond reasonable doubt, penalties shall range from revocation of licensure and heavy fines to sealing of abilities and incarceration in a pocket dimension, as deemed appropriate by the severity of the offense (§ 801.2). The accused retains the right to appeal to the High Council within thirty days of judgment, pending posting of a bond equal to two years' net earnings.

No Paradox Trial shall degenerate into an unscheduled duel or combat between magical practitioners outside the confines of this Code. Such actions constitute grounds for immediate expulsion and permanent disqualification from legal practice under § 801.5(b). All trials must be conducted in strict accordance with these procedures to ensure fairness, transparency, and adherence to the spirit of the Accords.

The Seal of Silence provision shall remain in effect for a period of thirty-six hours following any public trial or sentencing. During this time, all participants are prohibited from discussing details of the proceedings outside of official channels. Violation of this restriction shall result in automatic disqualification from future trials and suspension of licensure for one year, without prejudice to further disciplinary action.

This section applies exclusively to formal adjudications conducted under the authority of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Informal disputes between parties not involving allegations of Code violations fall outside its purview and shall be resolved through standard contractual mechanisms or private arbitration as mutually agreed upon by the disputants. Any attempt to manipulate trial proceedings for personal gain shall be treated as a separate offense punishable under § 801.6(c).

see § 700.2 Scrying of Closed Books; see § 801.3 Scope of Authority; see § 105.4 Conflict of Interest in Casting. Under § 901.1, all trial records shall be retained for a minimum period of ten years to facilitate future reference and audit as necessary.

body.heading: § 800.2 Paradox Trial Procedure and Post-Trial Sanctions
body.text:
A Paradox Trial shall commence only upon formal indictment by the Aegis Magi, specifying alleged violations of the Accords with particularity. The accused mage shall be afforded a minimum of seven days to prepare for trial, during which time they may secure counsel from peers or licensed legal practitioners. At the opening session, the presiding council member shall read the charges aloud and demand a plea of either "guilty" or "not guilty." Should the accused refuse to plead, the court shall enter a plea of not guilty on their behalf for purposes of procedure only.

If a guilty plea is entered, the trial may proceed abridged, with the primary focus being determination of appropriate sanctions pursuant to § 800.1. In such cases, the council shall render judgment within fourteen days unless further time is granted for deliberation. Notwithstanding any contrary local custom or practice, no Paradox Trial shall ever devolve into a personal duel between the accused and their accuser(s), whether magical or physical in nature. Such conduct constitutes unprofessional behavior warranting immediate disbarment without prejudice to other sanctions that may apply.

Upon finding of guilt, the council shall impose one or more penalties from among those enumerated in § 800.1, tailored to the gravity of the offense and circumstances surrounding it. Penalties may be imposed concurrently or consecutively at the discretion of the court. All judgments rendered by the Paradox Trial Council shall be recorded verbatim in the official minutes, which shall remain sealed except as provided herein. Any party seeking review of a judgment must petition for rehearing within thirty days of notification thereof.

Petitions for rehearing shall set forth with particularity the grounds upon which relief is sought and any new evidence that bears upon the case. The full council shall then convene to consider whether to grant rehearing, either in whole or in part at their discretion. If rehearing is granted, the matter shall be heard de novo unless otherwise specified by the presiding member. Decisions regarding petitions for rehearing are final and not subject to further appeal except as may be provided by law or court order.

In addition to any sanctions imposed pursuant to § 800.1, the court retains inherent authority to issue such additional orders as it deems necessary and proper to effectuate its judgments fully. This includes but is not limited to requiring compliance with specific affirmative acts or refraining from particular conduct. Failure to obey lawful court orders may result in enforcement proceedings under applicable law, including contempt sanctions where appropriate. All costs of trial, whether incurred directly or indirectly by the parties or their representatives, shall be borne equitably as determined by the court taking into account all relevant factors.

The provisions herein regarding Paradox Trials are intended to provide a fair and orderly mechanism for resolving disputes arising from alleged violations of the Autumnwood Accords while protecting the rights of both the accused and the public at large. Nothing contained in this section shall be construed to limit or impair any other powers, duties, or responsibilities vested in the Aegis Magi or their agents by law or custom. These procedures stand as a testament to our commitment to justice tempered with mercy – the hallmark of true mages who serve their craft and community alike.

sections.title: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
sections.brief: How long a mouth stays quiet.

body.heading: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
Any mage found in violation of the Accords who is sentenced to a Seal of Silence by the presiding council of the Paradox Trial shall be subject to the temporal constraints set forth in this section. The Seal of Silence is not merely a prohibition on vocalization but a metaphysical dampening of the subject’s ability to transmit intentional information through any conventional or arcane medium. The initial duration of the Seal shall be determined by the severity of the breach; minor infractions regarding the unauthorized recitation of the Quiet List shall result in a standard period of three lunar cycles. For violations involving the dissemination of restricted research or the breach of the Iron Mandate’s boundaries, the Sovereign may extend this duration indefinitely, subject to a biennial review by the Conservators.

The duration of the Seal is strictly governed by the principle of Arcane Stability. If a mage is found to be experiencing significant magical degradation or "mana-fraying" as a result of the Seal, a petition for early release may be filed with the Desk. However, such a petition must be accompanied by a certified report from a Master of the Conservator faction confirming that the mage’s silence no longer poses a risk to the public safety of the Midlands. The Desk shall not grant a review until the initial term has passed at least fifty percent of its allotted duration. During the review period, the mage shall remain under the jurisdiction of the Aegis Magi and may be relocated to a designated holding cell within the Autumn Wood.

Furthermore, the Seal of Silence is not a total erasure of identity. While the subject may not speak, they are permitted to communicate via written notation, provided such notation does not contain forbidden schools of magic or references to the Quiet List. Any attempt to bypass the Seal using unauthorized innovative techniques shall be viewed as a secondary offense, punishable by a doubling of the remaining sentence. The Desk maintains the right to revoke the Seal prematurely should the Sovereign determine that the mage’s silence is being leveraged as a tool for political coercion or if the mage is required to provide testimony in a high-priority matter of Guild security. See § 800.2 for the standard procedure regarding the initiation of the Seal.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In the event that a mage elects to resolve a dispute through a formal Paradox Trial by Arcane Duel rather than accepting a standard sanction, the Accords mandate that the administrative costs of the proceedings remain the responsibility of the participants. While the outcome of a duel may determine the victor’s rights over a disputed artifact, land, or magical property, the Guild Desk shall not waive the requisite filing fees, logistical surcharges, or the mandatory "Aegis Oversight Levy." These fees are non-negotiable and are assessed regardless of whether the duel ends in a decisive victory, a magical stalemate, or a mutual exhaustion of resources.

The Desk shall convert all declared stakes of a duel into a standardized Guild Fee structure upon the filing of the Duel Request. If a mage seeks to wager a specific sum of gold or a physical asset, the Guild shall calculate the equivalent market value at the time of filing. This value shall be added to the base administrative fee. Should the duel result in the destruction of public property or the unintended alteration of the local environment—such as the unauthorized growth of titan-class flora or the opening of minor rifts—the participants shall be held jointly liable for the restoration costs. These restoration costs are billed as "Emergency Stabilization Fees" and are due immediately upon the conclusion of the duel.

It is strictly prohibited for a mage to attempt to "waive" the Guild's fees by offering the Desk a portion of the duel's spoils as a gesture of goodwill. The Accords are clear: the Guild is an administrative body, not a beneficiary of private litigation. The Desk shall not accept Wario Coins, nor shall it accept any tender that is not recognized as official Guild currency. Any attempt to settle a duel's administrative debt through illicit trade or the offering of "favors" shall result in an immediate stay of the duel and a secondary investigation into the parties' conduct. See § 800.2 for the primary procedure on Duel Stakes.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The utilization of pocket dimensions as a means of incarceration for mages sentenced during a Paradox Trial is governed by the principle of Spatial Integrity. The key to the pocket-prison—whether it be a localized fold in reality or a fully realized sub-dimension—is held exclusively by the Archmage Sovereign or their designated deputy within the Conservator faction. No mage, regardless of rank or seniority, shall have the authority to grant entry, exit, or unauthorized communication to a prisoner held within a pocket-prison. This measure is intended to ensure that the punishment remains absolute and that the prisoner cannot use their remaining influence to subvert the Accords from within a vacuum.

Regarding the status of visiting hours, the Guild Desk officially maintains that such a concept is a matter of rumor and lacks any codified legal standing within the Autumnwood Accords. There is no scheduled time for family, peers, or legal counsel to enter the pocket-prison. Any attempt to organize a "visitation" shall be treated as a breach of the prison's spatial seal and will be met with immediate disciplinary action against the petitioner. The only permissible interaction with a prisoner is the formal delivery of sustenance and the occasional reading of the Guild’s daily decrees, conducted by an authorized Aegis Mage under strict supervision.

The maintenance of the pocket-prison is the responsibility of the Innovators, provided they operate under the direct oversight of the Conservators to ensure the dimension does not suffer from "entropy-leak" or "spatial erosion." If a pocket-prison is found to be unstable, the Desk may authorize a transfer of the prisoner to a physical holding cell, though this is a matter of safety rather than a grant of parole. Prisoners held in pocket-prisons are considered "temporally isolated" and are exempt from standard public appearance requirements, but they remain bound by the laws of the Accords. See § 400.2 for the regulations regarding the use of pocket dimensions as laboratories and their distinction from penal facilities.

body.heading: § 800.3 Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
The Seal of Silence is an arcane injunction placed upon a convicted caster, binding their magical core to enforce absolute muteness for the duration thereof. This penalty serves both punitive and protective functions: it deprives the offender of the ability to cast spells requiring vocal components or incantations, while simultaneously shielding the wider community from potential misuse of their power during this period of restraint. The sealing ritual must be performed by two licensed mages of equal rank, each attesting under oath that the procedures were followed in accordance with § 800.1. Failure to adhere strictly to these protocols renders the Seal void and may constitute a separate offense under § 300.2.

The duration of the Seal is initially set at one solar year from the date of imposition, though this term may be extended by up to two additional years upon motion filed by either party with notice given ten days prior to the scheduled hearing. Any extension must be justified by clear and convincing evidence that further restraint is necessary for public safety or judicial integrity. At the conclusion of the Seal period, the affected caster shall petition for its dissolution through formal application submitted to the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The Desk will schedule a review proceeding wherein all relevant factors are considered before rendering a final determination on whether the Seal may be lifted entirely or subject to continued limitation.

In cases where a Duel Trial results in victory by knockout rather than forfeiture of magical ability, any outstanding debts accrued during the course of combat shall instead be converted into liquidated damages payable directly to the opposing party's legal counsel. Such conversion precludes further claims for punitive damages related to the incident itself, though separate civil actions may proceed independently thereof. Payment must be made within thirty days of final judgment becoming effective, or enforcement proceedings initiated pursuant to applicable statutes.

Should a sealed individual attempt to circumvent their restrictions through unauthorized magical means, they shall be subject to immediate re-sealing for an indefinite period plus a mandatory suspension of all professional licenses held therein. Furthermore, any contracts entered into during the duration of the Seal shall automatically terminate by operation of law, with full restitution required forthwith. This provision exists solely to prevent exploitation of the caster's compromised state by unscrupulous entities seeking to profit from their vulnerability.

The provisions outlined herein represent a delicate balance between maintaining public order and preserving individual rights. They are designed to provide a fair mechanism for addressing serious infractions while minimizing unnecessary disruption to daily life. All parties are urged to approach these matters with seriousness and integrity, recognizing the profound implications of their actions on both personal liberties and communal welfare.

body.heading: § 800.3 Seal of Silence; Duration and Review — Continued
body.text:
The Seal of Silence, once affixed to a caster by the Paradox Tribunal, shall remain in effect for a minimum period of five years from the date of imposition, unless earlier lifted pursuant to § 800.3(B). At no time may a sealed individual practice magic within Autumnwood jurisdiction without explicit written consent from the Archmage Sovereign or her designee; violation thereof constitutes Class A Felony under the Accords and shall result in immediate re-sealing for an additional ten-year term, plus forfeiture of all personal assets.

Upon expiration of the initial five-year term, a review hearing shall be convened automatically before the full Tribunal to assess whether further restriction is warranted based on the sealed caster's subsequent conduct, character references, and demonstrated reform. The burden of proof rests upon the petitioner seeking continuation of the seal; failure to meet this threshold by clear and convincing evidence mandates restoration of the applicant's magical rights immediately.

In cases where a duel serves as the primary instrument for determining guilt or innocence under § 800.1(C), any monetary stakes wagered during said encounter shall be remitted to the Guild Treasury rather than distributed to participating parties. Such funds may then be allocated to support the maintenance of detention facilities and compensation for victims of magical crimes, in keeping with the public interest doctrine enshrined at § 300.1(F). The Tribunal retains sole discretion regarding any exceptions to this rule.

Regarding pocket-prison confinement, all such facilities must adhere strictly to safety protocols outlined in Appendix K of the Technical Standards Manual. Inmates shall be granted reasonable access to legal counsel and family members during scheduled visiting hours, subject to security clearance requirements. Medical attention shall be provided promptly upon request or observation of distress symptoms; neglect of these obligations by facility operators constitutes gross negligence per § 100.8(D).

Any appeal filed against a Seal of Silence order must be submitted within thirty days of notification and accompanied by sworn testimony supporting the petitioner's claim for reinstatement. The Tribunal shall grant oral argument only in exceptional circumstances where novel legal principles are implicated or substantial hardship would result from maintaining the status quo. All proceedings related to seal reviews shall be conducted expeditiously, with final determinations rendered no later than sixty days following submission of complete materials.

This provision is intended to balance legitimate public safety concerns with individual liberties protected under fundamental common law precedents. The Guild acknowledges that prolonged magical suppression may cause severe psychological harm and economic dislocation; hence the emphasis on periodic reassessment rather than indefinite confinement absent compelling justification. The Archmage Sovereign, acting as final arbiter, possesses inherent authority to override any Tribunal decision deemed contrary to the greater good of society at large.

body.heading: Duration and Review of the Seal of Silence
body.text:
The duration of a seal imposed under § 800.2 is determined by the severity of the infraction and the discretion of the adjudicating body. In cases involving minor violations or first-time offenders, seals may be lifted after a probationary period not exceeding one solar cycle, contingent upon satisfactory demonstration of reform. For more serious breaches, particularly those endangering public safety or violating core tenets of the Accords, seals remain in effect indefinitely until revoked by explicit order of the High Council. Any mage subject to a permanent seal retains full civil rights and may pursue lawful employment, though they are forever barred from practicing magic outside strictly supervised conditions set forth in their license.

The periodic review of active seals occurs on dates specified during initial imposition, typically coinciding with anniversary marks or lunar cycles deemed auspicious for magical reckoning. At each such interval, the affected party must appear before a panel of magistrates to petition for removal or modification of restrictions. The petitioner bears the burden of proof, presenting evidence of compliance and rehabilitation through testimony, documentation, and expert assessment as appropriate. Panels may grant full release, impose additional limitations, or deny petitions outright based on their evaluation of risk versus necessity. Decisions are binding but subject to appeal within ten days via established judicial channels. Failure to appear for scheduled reviews results in automatic extension of the current seal term by six months plus a monetary penalty assessed at triple the original fine amount.

Should circumstances change materially prior to scheduled review dates—such as improved behavior, new mitigating factors emerging, or developments directly affecting public welfare—the sealed individual may submit an emergency petition accompanied by supporting documentation. Such requests are expedited and decided within fourteen days absent extraordinary complications. Petitions meeting statutory thresholds for reconsideration warrant prompt hearing; those falling short are summarily dismissed without prejudice to future applications. The system balances accountability with opportunity for growth, ensuring that penalties remain proportional while allowing paths toward redemption where warranted under the letter of the law. Ultimately, the goal is restoration of harmony between individual liberty and collective security through measured application of these vital safeguards.

This framework provides necessary flexibility within rigid parameters, adapting to real-world conditions without compromising foundational principles. By incorporating mechanisms for ongoing evaluation and adjustment, it ensures that sanctions evolve alongside societal needs while maintaining consistent standards across all applications. The balance struck herein reflects careful deliberation by wise hands guided solely by wisdom's light shining forth brightly above us all today and forevermore amen so be it praised now!

sections.title: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
sections.brief: If they insist on a duel, the Desk still invoices.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In the event that a practitioner of the arcane elects to settle a legal dispute, a breach of contract, or a violation of the Autumnwood Accords through the mechanism of a formal Arcane Duel rather than a standard adjudicative hearing, the Desk shall maintain its right to assess all standard administrative costs. It is a common misconception among the more martial elements of the Aegis Magi and the radical elements of the Innovator faction that the physical or metaphysical destruction of an opponent’s magical capacity exempts the victor from the bureaucratic oversight of the Guild. To the contrary, the Desk views the conversion of a duel into a resolution as a mere alternative method of evidence processing. Therefore, regardless of whether the outcome is decided by a clash of wills or a decree of the Sovereign, the victor shall be held liable for the full extent of the filing fees associated with the initial grievance.

Furthermore, any "stakes" declared by the combatants—be they the forfeiture of a specific artifact, the surrender of a research permit, or the renunciation of a specific school of study—do not supersede the Guild's right to invoice for the logistical burden of the Paradox Trial. The Desk shall not be intimidated by the volatility of a duel; the fact that a mage may be reduced to a state of magical exhaustion or permanent sealing does not diminish the fact that the Guild provided the venue, the peer oversight, and the regulatory framework for said engagement. All such costs shall be added to the victor's outstanding balance, and the loser shall be responsible for the costs of their own containment or rehabilitation, as dictated by the prevailing sanctions. See § 800.2 for the overarching procedures of the Paradox Trial.

The Desk explicitly rejects the notion that "blood for blood" or "mana for mana" constitutes a waiver of administrative fees. If a mage chooses to engage in a duel to avoid a fine, the fine remains due, and the duel costs shall be added as a secondary surcharge. The Accords are a matter of civil and magical order, not a theater for unregulated violence. Any attempt to use a duel as a means to circumvent the fiscal responsibilities of a Guild member shall be met with an immediate escalation of fees and a potential referral to the Conservators for a review of the individual’s fitness to hold a license. The Desk is a repository of law, not a spectator to theater; every spark of magic spent in the name of justice must be accounted for in the ledger of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
When a judgment rendered by the Paradox Trial necessitates the removal of a rogue mage from the public sphere, the Guild shall utilize a pocket-prison as the primary means of containment. The administration of such a facility is strictly governed by the protocols of the Conservators to ensure that the spatial integrity of the Midlands remains uncompromised. The "key" to such a prison is not a physical object but a cryptographic arcane sequence held exclusively by the Archmage Sovereign or their designated deputy within the Aegis Magi. No individual mage, regardless of rank or factional standing, shall be granted the authority to initiate an entry or exit sequence without a direct writ from the Desk. The purpose of the pocket-prison is isolation, not rehabilitation; it is designed to negate the subject's ability to exert influence over the physical world or to facilitate the unauthorized propagation of forbidden schools.

Regarding the matter of visiting hours, the Desk formally declares that any reports of scheduled social calls, visitation windows, or "dialogue sessions" with incarcerated mages are entirely unsubstantiated rumors. The pocket-prison is a vacuum of social interaction designed to prevent the subversion of the Accords through clandestine communication. While the Innovators may argue for the necessity of "re-education" through dialogue, the Conservators maintain that the risk of a breach—either physical or ideological—outweighs the benefits of such interaction. Consequently, any mage found attempting to establish a communication link with a prisoner, whether through scrying, familiar proxy, or authorized teleportation, shall be subject to immediate sanctions under § 800.1.

The maintenance of the pocket-prison is funded by the seized assets of the condemned. The Desk shall not provide public tours, nor shall it provide transcripts of any internal communications that may occur within the void. The prisoner exists in a state of suspended legal personhood, their rights suspended until such time as the Archmage Sovereign deems a re-evaluation of their status necessary. Any unauthorized attempt to "liberate" a prisoner, whether through heroic intervention or clandestine infiltration, will be treated as an act of high treason against the Autumnwood Accords. The sanctity of the prison is the sanctity of the law itself; if the walls of the pocket-prison can be breached, the stability of the Midlands is forfeit. See § 800.2 for the primary sentencing guidelines leading to incarceration.

body.heading: Conversion of Duel Stakes to Administrative Fees
body.text:
In accordance with § 800.2, any Arcane Duel adjudicated by the Paradox Trial shall result in a formal finding of guilt or innocence based upon the performance and outcome of the combat. Where guilt is established, sanctions imposed pursuant to § 800.1 may include sealing of magical abilities, fines payable in Guild tender, and/or placement into a Pocket-Prison as outlined herein. Notably, where a participant refuses to engage directly with an opponent, or otherwise evades the procedural requirements set forth by the Trial, such conduct shall be deemed a waiver of due process rights under § 1.7(c). In lieu thereof, the Desk shall convert all outstanding monetary penalties and restitution obligations into administrative fees levied against the defaulting party's assets and future earnings as permitted by law.

The implementation of Pocket-Prison sanctions requires strict adherence to established protocols designed to safeguard both prisoner welfare and public safety. Upon authorization by a majority vote of the Trial Panel, convicted offenders may be transferred to temporary containment facilities operated by certified Arcane Wards under contract with the Guild. Such facilities must maintain continuous monitoring via remote scrying devices as specified in § 700.2(a), ensuring that no illicit magical activity occurs within the prison walls. In addition, prisoners shall receive access to educational resources and therapeutic services aimed at facilitating their eventual reintegration into society upon release. Failure by custodial agencies to comply with these standards may result in immediate revocation of operating privileges under § 100.6(d).

Administrative fees assessed against defaulting parties are calculated according to a standardized schedule approved annually by the Autumnwood Accords Desk. These charges encompass costs incurred during investigation, prosecution, trial proceedings, and enforcement actions taken pursuant to this Code. Payment arrangements may be negotiated on a case-by-case basis where full compliance is not immediately feasible but good faith efforts are demonstrated. However, willful evasion or deliberate obstruction of fee collection shall constitute grounds for escalated disciplinary measures up to and including permanent disqualification from magical practice within the jurisdiction defined by § 100.1(b). All financial transactions related to such assessments must be conducted through official channels only, with receipts provided upon completion of payment obligations.

It is further provided that any disputes arising out of the application or enforcement of these provisions shall be resolved exclusively through binding arbitration administered by a neutral panel appointed jointly by the Guild and interested parties involved in the controversy. Arbitration proceedings shall commence within thirty (30) days following written notice thereof, with final awards rendered no later than ninety (90) days after commencement unless extended upon mutual agreement of both sides. Awards issued under this section are enforceable as judgments of a court of competent jurisdiction and may be executed accordingly by any qualified process server or law enforcement officer within the territorial limits specified herein. Nothing contained in this clause shall limit the inherent authority of the Desk to interpret and apply these rules as it deems necessary for maintenance of order among mages operating under its auspices.

body.heading: Conversion of Duel Stakes to Administrative Fees — Continued
body.text:
Under § 800.2 Trial by Arcane Duel, the parties may elect to settle disputes via sanctioned magical combat rather than conventional litigation. However, such duels are strictly regulated and never result in personal liability for damages arising from the proceedings themselves. Should either party suffer injury or property loss during a properly conducted duel, all costs and claims shall be subrogated to the Mages' Guild for processing under normal administrative channels. The losing litigant is liable only for fees incurred by the Desk in adjudicating their case post-duel.

When one contestant emerges victorious but unable to enforce a monetary judgment against their opponent—whether due to insolvency, flight, or magical protections—the prevailing party may petition the Desk to convert awarded damages into an administrative fine payable directly to the Guild. This mechanism ensures that successful litigants receive compensation even when traditional collection proves impracticable. The converted amount shall be levied upon the losing party's assets held by the Accords or their authorized representatives, including but not limited to licenses, permits, and earned income from magic-related activities.

The Desk reserves discretion in determining appropriate fee amounts based on the nature of the dispute, severity of violations, and financial circumstances of the defendants. In all cases, the converted fees must be reasonable and proportionate to the harm suffered by the aggrieved party. Exorbitant claims or attempts to extort inflated penalties will result in immediate dismissal of the petition and potential sanctions for abuse of process. The Guild remains committed to fair resolution of all disputes while maintaining strict oversight over magical applications that might otherwise evade conventional legal remedies.

This provision underscores the unique hybrid nature of arcane adjudication, blending elements of trial by combat with modern principles of restitution and accountability. By providing an alternative means of redress when standard enforcement fails, the Accords ensure that justice remains accessible even in cases where traditional pathways prove inadequate. The Desk stands ready to implement these measures efficiently and impartially, safeguarding the rights of all parties involved while preserving the integrity of the magical community at large.

body.heading: § 800.4 Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In cases where the Paradox Trial concludes in favor of the Guild, all outstanding fines and penalties owed by the convicted mage shall be satisfied through the conversion of duel stakes into administrative fees, as provided herein. This mechanism ensures that the cost of adjudicating magical infractions is borne equitably by those who engage in unauthorized combat, rather than falling upon the public treasury or law-abiding citizens.

Under this provision, any wager placed on the outcome of a Paradox Trial shall be forfeited immediately upon declaration of guilt and applied directly toward liquidation of assessed debts. The amount collected via such conversion shall not exceed the total sum originally owed by the offending party, nor may it result in windfall gains for the Guild beyond reasonable recovery of expenses incurred during the proceedings. Any excess funds generated through this process shall be remitted to the Archmage’s personal accounts as compensation for risks assumed in upholding the Accords.

The Desk retains sole discretion to determine whether and how duel stakes shall be utilized to offset penalties, based on a case-by-case evaluation of relevant factors including but not limited to: severity of the offense committed; extent of harm caused to persons or property; history of prior violations by the accused; likelihood of future recidivism absent intervention; and overall impact on public safety and confidence in the legal system. The Desk shall notify all interested parties promptly following any decision regarding conversion of stakes, providing ample opportunity for review or appeal if warranted under applicable law.

It is further directed that no individual or entity shall knowingly facilitate or profit from illegal duels conducted in violation of this Code, whether by way of funding, equipment provision, venue access, or otherwise. Violation of this prohibition constitutes a serious felony offense subject to stringent sanctions including imprisonment, permanent revocation of magical privileges, and disqualification from future participation in any capacity within the Guild community. The burden of proving innocence rests solely upon the accused party; mere suspicion is insufficient grounds for prosecution but may justify enhanced scrutiny by appropriate authorities charged with maintaining order and security throughout our lands.

The principles set forth herein reflect a balanced approach to addressing the complex challenges posed by unregulated magical competition while safeguarding against abuse and exploitation. By establishing clear rules governing the handling of duel-related finances, we reinforce both accountability and fairness within our society at large – values upon which our shared existence ultimately depends for preservation and prosperity alike. Let these guidelines serve as a beacon guiding all who walk this difficult path toward justice tempered with mercy, wisdom balanced against strength, so that harmony may prevail where discord once reigned supreme among us all forevermore.

body.heading: Conversion of Duel Stakes to Administrative Fees and Associated Procedures
body.text:
In instances where a Paradox Trial concludes in favor of the Accords, any magical artifacts seized as evidence or forfeited by the losing party shall be evaluated by certified Appraisers designated by the Desk. The resulting valuation, less reasonable storage and transport costs incurred by the Guild during retention, constitutes the administrative fee owed for adjudication services rendered. Such fees are non-refundable under any circumstances and remain due even if subsequent proceedings determine that no violation of the Accords occurred. Failure to remit payment within thirty days shall result in further penalties, including suspension of all future privileges held by the responsible individual or entity until full settlement is achieved.

The Desk maintains a centralized ledger tracking all fees assessed, payments received, outstanding balances, and associated case histories. This record serves as conclusive proof of financial obligations owed to the Guild and may be produced at any time upon proper demand. Disputes regarding the accuracy of appraisals or calculation of amounts due must be raised within ten days of issuance of the invoice; thereafter, the figures are deemed final and binding absent evidence of gross error manifesting on its face. In cases where the losing party is unable to pay in full immediately, installment plans may be negotiated subject to approval by the Desk and compliance with all terms therein set forth.

Should a convicted caster refuse or fail to satisfy their financial liabilities despite having sufficient assets available for liquidation, additional sanctions shall apply pursuant to existing provisions governing recalcitrant offenders. These measures include but are not limited to public shaming, revocation of remaining licenses, and referral for civil action against the delinquent's estates. The Desk reserves sole discretion in determining appropriate disciplinary responses based on the specifics of each case and the severity of the original offense committed by the accused. All monetary penalties collected shall be remitted directly to the Guild Treasury for allocation as deemed fit by its governing bodies without further recourse.

It is hereby expressly declared that nothing contained herein shall be construed to limit or impair any rights possessed by the Desk under other sections of this Code relating to enforcement powers, contempt sanctions, or remedies available in equity. Rather, these provisions operate cumulatively to ensure full compensation for services rendered and deterrence against future infractions alike. The integrity of the Accords depends upon strict adherence to financial obligations imposed upon violators as a matter of course. Only through consistent application of such principles can public trust be maintained and the orderly administration of magic preserved for generations to come. Thus stands the law, immutable except by amendment duly enacted in accordance with established procedures.

sections.title: Pocket-Prison Procedure
sections.brief: Who holds the key. Visiting hours are a rumor.

body.heading: § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The administration of extra-planar incarceration, colloquially referenced as the Pocket-Prison, shall be governed by the sovereign authority of the Archmage Sovereign as mediated by the High Council of the Autumnwood Accords. Any mage found in violation of the Accords who is sentenced to such a confinement by the Paradox Trial shall be subject to immediate transition into a localized, magically-sustained pocket dimension. This dimension is to be constructed such that its internal geometry is disconnected from the primary ley lines of the Midlands, ensuring that any uncontrolled magical discharge or temporal leakage does not affect the stability of the Autumn Wood or the surrounding territories. The purpose of this procedure is not merely punitive but serves as a containment measure for high-risk arcane anomalies and rogue casters whose presence poses a systemic threat to the Guild’s structural integrity.

The custody of the "Key"—defined herein as the specific arcane sequence and focal point required to initiate entry into or exit from the pocket dimension—shall reside exclusively with the Aegis Magi assigned to the Custodial Oversight Division. No individual mage, regardless of rank or factional affiliation, may possess the Key or the means to bypass the dimensional threshold without a direct, written mandate from Archmage Veyra. This strict prohibition is intended to prevent the unauthorized liberation of high-risk individuals or the clandestine entry of non-authorized personnel into the prison. Any attempt to manufacture a secondary Key, or to utilize forbidden schools of magic to breach the dimensional veil, shall be classified as an act of High Treason against the Autumnwood Accords, punishable by immediate permanent sealing of the offender’s arcane essence.

Regarding the maintenance of the prisoner, the Guild recognizes that biological and cognitive degradation may occur over extended periods of isolation. However, the provision of "Visiting Hours" is officially categorized as a rumor and is not recognized by the Accords as a legal right or a standard procedure. The Guild maintains that the psychological state of the prisoner is secondary to the safety of the public and the preservation of the magical equilibrium. While the Conservators may occasionally argue for the periodic auditing of prisoner health to ensure the continued viability of the "Seal and Seal" policy, the Innovators frequently advocate for more sophisticated, albeit experimental, stimuli to prevent cognitive collapse. Regardless of these internal debates, no communication between the prisoner and the exterior world shall be permitted unless such communication is deemed essential for the extraction of specific, non-hazardous information required for the defense of the Guild.

All records pertaining to the location, dimensions, and occupant list of the Pocket-Prison are classified as Restricted and shall not be entered into any public catalogue. Any mage who attempts to disclose the coordinates or the existence of a specific prisoner shall be subject to the Quiet List Procedure as outlined in § 300.3. Furthermore, the use of any One-T cartography to locate the prison is strictly prohibited, as such maps are intended for navigation and do not serve as licenses for exploration or raid. The Pocket-Prison shall remain a closed system; any unauthorized breach, whether by an internal agent or an external hostile force such as the Iron Legion or the Silver Flame, shall be met with a full-scale Aegis response to ensure the integrity of the Guild’s penal infrastructure.

body.heading: § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure and Custodial Rights
body.text:
The confinement within a pocket dimension shall adhere to strict procedural safeguards designed to protect both the detainee's welfare and the Guild's interests. Upon issuance of an order for imprisonment, a designated custodian must oversee the transfer of the individual into the sealed space, verifying that all necessary magical wards are intact before release. The custodian shall maintain regular contact with the prisoner via scrying or telepathic link, ensuring basic needs such as hydration and sanitation are met without compromising security.

Visiting hours for family members or legal counsel may be arranged upon written request and approval from a senior Aegis Magus. Such visits must occur within a controlled environment monitored by magical sensors to prevent unauthorized communication. All correspondence between the prisoner and outside parties shall be subject to review for compliance with the terms of confinement. Failure to adhere to these provisions may result in additional sanctions or extension of the sentence duration at the discretion of the overseeing council.

Release from pocket-prison status requires a formal petition filed by the inmate or on their behalf, accompanied by evidence of rehabilitation and good conduct during incarceration. The petition shall be heard by a panel of three Aegis Magi who will assess whether public safety has been sufficiently restored through reintegration efforts. If approved, the individual may resume normal activities subject to continued surveillance as deemed appropriate by the Guild. Persistent violations or failure to meet stipulated conditions may lead to renewed imprisonment without further recourse.

The rights outlined herein are intended solely for informational purposes and do not constitute an admission of guilt or liability on part of the detaining authority nor a waiver of any inherent privileges. Interpretation of this section falls under exclusive jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, whose decisions shall be final and binding upon all parties concerned. Any attempts to circumvent these guidelines through technicalities or loopholes will be met with immediate retribution by the full force of Guild law enforcement capabilities at their disposal.

body.heading: § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure and Custodial Rights — Continued
body.text:
A mage found themselves imprisoned in a sealed pocket dimension, their magic utterly nullified by the binding wards. In such an absolute deprivation of liberty, questions naturally arise regarding who holds dominion over this place of confinement and what rights they may assert within its confines. The Accords provide scant guidance on these matters beyond stating that custody shall remain with the Aegis Magi until the prisoner's sentence is fully served or commuted by order of the Desk. However, in practice, this has led to a de facto system wherein individual magisters maintain private dungeons and employ their own warders as guards—a practice tolerated so long as no external harm results from such arrangements.

Some have argued that the fundamental rights of the accused must extend even into these surreal spaces, yet few would dare claim such liberties in light of the extreme measures required to contain a dangerous foe. Instead, it is commonly accepted that while the prisoner retains personhood and certain basic protections against torture or cruel treatment, all other considerations are suspended at the pleasure of their keepers. This includes any notion of visiting hours or familial contact; the walls between worlds render such niceties moot unless specifically permitted by decree.

Indeed, communication across dimensional barriers is itself a complex matter subject to strict regulation under § 800.12 Interdimensional Communication Protocols. Unless explicitly authorized for medical, legal, or humanitarian purposes, attempts at unauthorized contact may constitute an aggravating factor in sentencing and invite severe reprisals against both the sender and receiver of such messages. The Desk maintains sole authority to approve any exceptions based on necessity and risk assessment, with final adjudication reserved for the full council upon review of all relevant testimony and evidence.

Ultimately then, a mage condemned to life behind impenetrable walls must accept that they have forfeited more than mere freedom—they have surrendered their very essence as sentient beings subject to external law. To expect otherwise would be folly indeed; for in binding themselves so utterly, they become but extensions of the wills that control them, existing solely to serve some greater purpose beyond comprehension by mortal minds. And yet even here, where reason fails and despair reigns supreme, there remains a sliver of hope: that one day their chains shall fall away, and they may rise anew as free agents once more. Until then though... well, let us say no more lest we invite ill fortune upon ourselves. For in this realm of shadows and secrets, words have power beyond measure—and misuse thereof can lead to ruin most profound.

body.heading: § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure and Custodial Rights — Continued — Continued
body.text:
The physical containment known as the "Seal of Silence" remains in perpetual effect upon any mage subjected to its imposition, barring explicit revocation by the Paradox Trial Council itself. No lesser authority may lift this ban without written mandate bearing the signature of Archmage Veyra or her duly appointed proxy. Violations of this interdiction constitute a felony under § 800.1 and carry penalties up to total magical excision.

Custodial oversight of sealed individuals shall be assumed by the Aegis Magi Corps, acting in concert with designated Conservator representatives. These officers maintain daily logs documenting conditions within containment facilities, ensuring adherence to all stipulated parameters regarding isolation duration and environmental factors.
