Failure to comply with these standards renders custodians liable for resultant damages or escape attempts.

Visitation rights are expressly denied to sealed subjects during the primary term of their sentence. Exceptions may be granted only upon unanimous council vote, necessitating sworn affidavits from prospective visitors attesting to non-malicious intent and lack of ties to opposition factions. All meetings conducted under such permission shall be recorded and reviewed post-facto for potential misconduct or influence peddling.

Correspondence between incarcerated mages and their families is permitted solely via censored electronic transmission systems monitored by Aegis overseers. Any attempt at circumventing these protocols, whether through conventional means or magical interference, will result in immediate extension of confinement terms and punitive sanctions against the offending parties.

Release proceedings shall commence only upon expiration of the original sentence period, absent extenuating circumstances warranting early termination per § 800.3. Petitions for commutation must demonstrate irrefutable evidence of rehabilitation and pose no threat to public safety prior to consideration by the full council. Denials carry force of final judgment unless appealed within thirty days under established rules of procedure.

Post-release reintegration shall be supervised by assigned mentors chosen from among trusted guild members, reporting regularly on progress toward societal re-entry goals. Failure to meet milestones may trigger mandatory review of sentence length and conditions imposed initially. Continued compliance guarantees gradual easing of remaining restrictions over a period not exceeding one standard year following discharge.

Any questions regarding interpretation or enforcement of this section shall be referred directly to the High Council for definitive ruling. Lower authorities are forbidden from rendering discretionary judgments outside their clearly defined purview lest they incur personal liability for ensuing consequences. Strict adherence to these guidelines ensures fairness and consistency in administering justice under the Autumnwood Accords regime.

See also § 800.1 Discipline; Range of Sanctions; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill; § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time. Under § 700.1 Evidence Generally, all claims must be substantiated by credible proof rather than mere speculation or rumor. The Accords stand as the ultimate arbiter of magical conduct and consequence within our realm.

body.heading: § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure and Custodial Rights — Continued — Administration
body.text:
The confinement of an accused within a pocket dimension shall not constitute mere detention, but rather the imposition of a strict custodial regime governed by this section. The arresting officer or their duly appointed proxy shall serve as the primary warden, responsible for maintaining order and preventing escape. No other persons shall enter the prison without explicit written authorization from the Presiding Magistrate, absent an emergency threatening life limb or property. Such emergencies require immediate notification to the Desk upon resolution.

Visiting hours are strictly limited to one hour per week, scheduled at least seven days in advance through the officer in charge. Visitors must present valid identification and pass a background check approved by the Conservators' Oversight Committee. During visits, all interactions shall occur within sight of a surveillance construct or sworn guard. Any attempt to smuggle contraband, transmit unauthorized messages, or otherwise interfere with the prisoner's isolation will result in instant revocation of visiting privileges and potential criminal charges against the offender.

Correspondence between incarcerated individuals and their families shall be subject to review by the warden before delivery. All mail must be written in plain language only; any code, cipher, or magical compulsion embedded therein renders it void and punishable as subversion. Exceptions may be granted for medical consultations or religious observances upon petition and approval. Failure to comply with these provisions will lead to disciplinary action ranging from solitary confinement to indefinite extension of the sentence at the discretion of the Presiding Magistrate.

The warden shall submit a detailed monthly report on each prisoner's behavior, health status, and any incidents occurring within their charge. These reports are confidential until released by court order or upon expiration of the custodial term. Any breach of confidentiality constitutes grounds for immediate dismissal from service and possible prosecution under the Accords' Espionage Provisions. Furthermore, all records pertaining to the prisoner shall be retained permanently unless expunged by judicial decree following successful completion of sentencing requirements.

Custodians are prohibited from engaging in any abusive, humiliating, or degrading conduct toward their charges beyond what is necessary for security and discipline purposes. Excessive force may only be employed when absolutely warranted to prevent serious harm or escape attempts. Any allegations of misconduct must be investigated promptly by an independent panel convened by the Archmage Sovereign's Office. Conviction results in removal from duty, permanent disqualification from holding public office related to magical affairs, and potential revocation of licensure pending further review.

This comprehensive framework ensures that those deprived of their liberty due to suspected violations of the Autumnwood Accords are treated with dignity while remaining securely confined until such time as their guilt or innocence can be fully determined according to law. Any deviation from these protocols undermines both the integrity of the judicial process and public confidence in our system of justice. Thus, strict adherence is mandatory for all involved parties without exception under any circumstances whatsoever.

body.heading: § 800.5 Custodial Authority and Access Rights; § 800.6 Review and Release Proced
body.text:
Under § 800.1, the Paradox Trial may result in a mage being placed under seal or imprisoned within a pocket dimension. When this occurs, custodial authority vests solely with the Aegis Magi acting on behalf of the Guild Sovereign, regardless of which faction sponsored the trial. No individual member of the Conservator or Innovator factions shall claim rights to visit or communicate with a sealed prisoner without express authorization from the Desk. Unauthorized contact is punishable as a felony under § 100.2(d).

Visiting hours for detained mages are established by local custom but vary widely across regions. In practice, access is often denied entirely unless paid for directly or negotiated through third parties. Such arrangements must be reported to the Desk within seven days of execution; failure to do so constitutes grounds for revocation of future trial participation privileges under § 800.1(c). Prisoners held in pocket dimensions may request periodic review by an independent panel appointed by the Sovereign, but such panels have no power to alter existing sentences absent new evidence of abuse or misconduct.

Detained mages remain liable for all outstanding fines and damages incurred prior to their apprehension. Any sums owed shall be deducted from future payments made on their behalf by employers or clients until fully satisfied. Failure to settle these debts may result in extension of confinement duration at the discretion of the presiding judge. Similarly, compensation must be paid for any physical injuries sustained during capture or transit, calculated according to standard medical tariff schedules adjusted for magical enhancements where applicable.

Escape attempts constitute an aggravating circumstance that may lead to enhanced penalties upon retrial. Even unsuccessful breaches of containment are treated as serious violations warranting increased surveillance and stricter terms on subsequent releases. Recidivists caught evading custody risk permanent sealing or execution, depending on the gravity of their offenses and resources available for pursuit. The Guild reserves the right to deploy any lawful means necessary to apprehend fugitives, including use of deadly force if absolutely required to prevent loss of life or destruction of property.

All records pertaining to sealed individuals shall be maintained in strict confidence under § 700.2, accessible only to authorized officials and their agents. Disclosure of such information to unauthorized parties constitutes a grave breach of trust subject to severe sanctions up to and including disbarment. Exceptions exist for emergency situations where release may pose imminent threat to public safety; however, any such disclosures must be documented meticulously with justification supporting the necessity thereof. This provision remains in effect indefinitely unless expressly amended by future legislation enacted through proper channels.

sections.title: Duty to File Before Casting
sections.brief: If value, composition, or risk will move, file first.

body.heading: Duty to File Before Casting
body.text:
The preservation of the weave and the stability of the Midlands require that all significant alterations to reality, whether intentional or incidental, be documented by the Accords Desk prior to the initiation of the somatic or verbal components of the spell. Under the authority of the Archmage Sovereign, all practitioners of the arts are hereby commanded to submit a formal Notice of Intent to Cast (NIC) whenever the intended enchantment, transmutation, or evocation is likely to result in a measurable shift in material value, a fundamental change in chemical or metaphysical composition, or a demonstrable increase in environmental risk. This duty is not merely a bureaucratic formality; it is a preventative measure designed to ensure that the Aegis Magi can monitor for potential paradoxes or violations of the forbidden schools as defined in § 300.2. A mage who proceeds with a casting that meets these criteria without a filed and acknowledged NIC is in immediate breach of the Accords and may be subject to the sanctions detailed in § 800.1.

Furthermore, the "filing first" requirement dictates that the documentation must be physically or magically deposited at the Accords Desk before the first syllable of the incantation is uttered. Failure to comply shall result in the immediate forfeiture of any protections afforded by the Guild and may lead to an immediate summons for a Paradox Trial as outlined in § 800.2. In instances where the risk of the casting is deemed "imminent" by the practitioner—such as in cases of self-defense or the containment of a burgeoning rift—the practitioner may act first but must provide a sworn affidavit of emergency within one hour of the event's conclusion. Such affidavits must be notarized by a summoned notary as per § 600.5. If the casting results in a permanent alteration of the landscape or the creation of a permanent magical construct, the practitioner shall be held liable for all subsequent registry fees and maintenance costs. See § 900.2 for reporting thresholds.

body.heading: Reporting of Material Enchantments
body.text:
Any enchantment that imparts a permanent or semi-permanent property to a physical object, known as a Material Enchantment, must be reported to the Accords Desk to ensure the integrity of the regional market and the safety of the citizenry. The threshold for mandatory reporting is set at a minimum of fifty gold pieces in perceived material value, or any enchantment that alters the weight, volume, or elemental state of an object beyond a five percent variance from its natural state. For example, a blade that glows is a minor enchantment requiring no filing, but a blade that cuts through stone as if it were silk constitutes a Material Enchantment and requires full disclosure. Practitioners who fail to report such enchantments are liable for a "Late Reporting Surcharge." This surcharge shall accrue at a fixed rate of ten percent of the estimated market value per sunrise, calculated in the caster's original time zone.

The reporting period begins at the moment the enchantment is finalized and the object is released from the casting circle. Should a practitioner attempt to obfuscate the nature of the enchantment by claiming it is a mere "aesthetic flourish," the Aegis Magi reserve the right to seize the object for inspection. If the object is found to exceed the reporting thresholds, the practitioner shall be fined the full accrued surcharge plus a penalty of double the base fee. This ensures that the Innovators do not flood the markets with unregulated, high-potency items while the Conservators maintain the stability of the Midlands. For questions regarding the specific chemical changes of materials, see § 1001.7. For the disposal of failed enchantments, see § 400.4.

body.heading: Record Retention
body.text:
The Mages' Guild Accords Desk serves as the ultimate repository of magical history, and as such, the retention of records is paramount to the continuity of the Accord. All filings, including Notices of Intent to Cast, Material Enchantment reports, and Paradox Trial transcripts, shall be preserved in the Guild archives for a minimum duration of seven years. However, in the event that a record pertains to a "Geological Age" event—defined as any enchantment or ritual that results in the formation of new landmasses, the shifting of tectonic plates, or the creation of permanent, non-degradable geological features—the record shall be maintained indefinitely. The determination of whether a record qualifies as a "Geological Age" event is at the sole discretion of the Clerk of the Accords Desk, based on the Clerk's subjective assessment of the "humor" or "significance" of the event's permanence.

During the standard seven-year retention period, records may be accessed by authorized Conservators or Innovators for the purposes of research or litigation. During this time, the Desk may redact sensitive information regarding the Quiet List to protect the privacy of the high-ranking mages involved. Once a record is deemed to have reached its retention limit, it may be moved to the deep archives or, if the Clerk deems the content sufficiently trivial or amusing, may be ceremonially incinerated. No mage shall have the right to demand the destruction of their personal records before the expiration of the mandatory retention period. For the specific procedures regarding the redaction of sensitive data, see § 300.3.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
The administration of the Autumnwood Accords is a self-sustaining bureaucratic entity; therefore, the Guild shall not provide administrative services, permit processing, or enforcement actions gratis. Every action taken by the Accords Desk—from the filing of a Notice of Intent to Cast to the adjudication of a Paradox Trial—incurs a mandatory Administrative Fee. The fundamental principle of the Accords regarding these costs is simple: the individual who requests the service is the individual who shall bear the burden of the cost. The Accords Desk is expressly prohibited from waiving these fees for any reason, including political pressure from the Regal Empire, requests from the Silver Flame, or appeals from the Innovator faction.

The person who asks for the magical privilege pays for the bureaucratic oversight. This applies to all interactions with the Aegis Magi, who may levy additional "Enforcement Surcharges" if a mage's actions require the deployment of Guild resources to contain a magical anomaly. It is strictly forbidden for a third party to pay the fees on behalf of a mage without a signed Power of Attorney and a pre-payment of the "Proxy Fee." Furthermore, the Guild shall not accept Wario Coins as a valid form of tender for any official fees; all payments must be rendered in gold, mana-crystals, or other approved Guild-recognized currencies. Any attempt to bribe a Clerk with unauthorized tender is a felony offense punishable by immediate referral to the Paradox Trial. For details on the conversion of duel stakes into administrative fees, see § 800.4.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The Accords Desk serves as the arbiter of truth regarding the history and origin of magical artifacts. A common misconception among the lay public and even some novice casters is that a compelling narrative or a "story" constitutes a valid chain of title for a relic. The Accords Desk formally declares that a story is not a chain of title. For an artifact to be registered with a valid provenance, the owner must provide a continuous, documented history of ownership, including the names of previous keepers, the locations of previous storage, and the specific magical signatures of those who have held the item. A tale of a "lost king" or a "fallen civilization" is insufficient for the purpose of legal registration or the removal of restrictive wards.

If a practitioner attempts to register a relic based solely on oral tradition or unverified mythos, the filing shall be rejected as "Speculative Provenance." The practitioner may be required to submit to a forensic arcane audit, wherein the Aegis Magi will attempt to trace the magical "echoes" of the object's history. If the audit reveals that the artifact's history has been intentionally obscured or falsified—such as attempting to hide a relic's origin from the Conservators—the practitioner shall be subject to immediate prosecution for Fraudulent Provenance. This law is designed to prevent the illicit trade of stolen artifacts and to ensure that the Guild can properly monitor the movement of high-risk items. For the protocols regarding the scrying of closed books to verify provenance, see § 700.2.

body.heading: § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; Reportable Enchantments and Relics
body.text:
Every caster shall file an advance notice with the Accords Desk prior to casting any spell of Level Five or higher, unless exempted by special dispensation under § 200.3. Failure to comply constitutes a Class B violation subject to fines up to one thousand gold crowns per instance. Notice must be submitted at least forty-eight hours before intended casting date and hour, specifying location, purpose, estimated duration, and potential hazards. See § 100.6 for delegation requirements regarding notice submission by proxy representatives.

Reportable enchantments include all items possessing intrinsic magical properties exceeding a value threshold of fifty gold crowns. Owners must disclose such artifacts during initial licensing applications and promptly notify the Desk of any newly acquired pieces meeting criteria. Concealment or misrepresentation shall result in immediate suspension pending investigation, with penalties escalating based on proven intent to defraud. False claims regarding item origin may trigger criminal charges under relevant statutes governing theft and forgery. Record retention obligations mandate maintenance of detailed logs documenting all filed notices and reported objects for a minimum period of seven calendar years. These records serve as official reference materials during enforcement proceedings and audits conducted by appointed inspectors.

Responsibility for filing rests exclusively with the individual caster or entity initiating magical operations, irrespective of whether services are rendered gratuitously or for compensation. Exceptions exist only where explicit written authorization is granted by the Conservators' Council to proceed without advance warning due to exigent circumstances threatening public safety or national security interests. In such rare instances, post-facto reporting becomes mandatory within seventy-two hours following event conclusion. Any discrepancies discovered during subsequent review shall be addressed through formal disciplinary channels as outlined in § 800.1 et seq.

Identification fees associated with processing filings vary according to spell complexity and anticipated impact zone size. Standard rates apply unless waived by the Archmage Sovereign upon determination of compelling public benefit arising from proposed work. Payment must accompany submission of all required documentation, including sworn affidavits attesting to caster competency and insurance coverage limits adequate to cover potential damages. Late submissions incur additional surcharges calculated at twice the base filing fee plus twenty percent monthly accruals until resolved satisfactorily by the Desk's adjudicators acting in their sole discretion guided by applicable regulations herein established.

Provenance verification of all reportable relics requires submission of authenticating certificates issued by accredited appraisers familiar with relevant historical contexts surrounding each artifact's creation and ownership history. Absence thereof renders acceptance of materials provisional pending further scrutiny, potentially delaying commencement dates for associated projects accordingly. Fraudulent attempts to bypass provenance checks via falsified paperwork will be treated as aggravated offenses warranting enhanced punitive measures beyond those specified above without further notice whatsoever given beforehand directly involved parties concerned regarding matters herein addressed comprehensively throughout this section dedicated solely explaining duties imposed upon casters operating within jurisdictional bounds defined hereinabove clearly delineated explicitly leaving no room whatsoever for ambiguity whatsoever concerning responsibilities laid out forthwith below...

sections.brief: Thresholds. Late reports accrue per sunrise in the caster's original time zone.

body.heading: Reporting of Material Enchantments
body.text:
All mages operating under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords shall be mandated to register any enchantment of a material nature that exceeds the standard threshold of common utility. A "Material Enchantment" is defined herein as any permanent or semi-permanent alteration of physical matter, including but not limiteded to the infusion of mana into structural masonry, the creation of sentient constructs, or the transmutation of base metals into durable alloys for commercial use. Any enchantment that possesses the capacity to affect a public thoroughfare, a private residence, or a communal resource must be filed with the Accords Desk within three lunar cycles of its completion. Failure to report such enchantments constitutes a breach of the Guild’s transparency protocols and may result in the immediate seizure of the enchanted object for safety inspection.

The threshold for mandatory reporting is determined by the magnitude of the arcane resonance. Minor household charms, such as self-lighting lanterns or cooling stones, do not require filing. However, any enchantment capable of sustaining a continuous magical output of more than fifty units of mana per hour, or any object capable of independent locomotion without a direct tether to a caster, falls under the mandatory reporting category. Mages who neglect to file these reports shall be subject to administrative fines. In the event of a failure to report, late reports shall accrue a penalty of twenty gold sovereigns per sunrise in the caster's original time zone. This penalty is designed to ensure that the Guild maintains an accurate and timely ledger of all active arcane signatures within the Midlands.

Furthermore, mages who engage in the mass production of material enchantments for sale to non-casters must provide a certificate of stability signed by a recognized Conservator. This is to prevent the proliferation of unstable artifacts that may lead to localized mana-voids or structural collapses. See § 900.1 for general duty to file before casting. See § 400.1 for research permits regarding experimental enchantments. All records of reported enchantments are subject to audit by the Aegis Magi at any time without prior notice. The Guild reserves the right to reclassify any "common" enchantment as a "Material Enchantment" if it is found to be utilized in a manner inconsistent with public safety or the preservation of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Record Retention
body.text:
The Mages' Guild Accords Desk shall maintain a rigorous system of record retention to ensure the continuity of magical jurisprudence and the preservation of historical precedent. All filings, including but not limited to research permits, contract notations, and incident reports, shall be preserved for a period of seven years. This timeframe is intended to provide sufficient historical context for the adjudication of ongoing disputes and to ensure that the lineage of magical permissions remains unbroken for the duration of a standard practitioner's career. During this period, records may be accessed by authorized officials, including Archmage Veyra and her appointed deputies, for the purposes of auditing or mediation.

Notwithstanding the standard seven-year rule, certain records may be held indefinitely if they pertain to "High-Risk" arcane activities, such as those involving the Forbidden Schools or restricted research. In such cases, the Clerk of the Accords Desk shall determine the retention period based on the enduring nature of the magical threat. For records involving the preservation of the Midlands' geological or ecological integrity, the Guild acknowledges the principle of "Geological Age." Specifically, records pertaining to the shifting of ley lines, the creation of permanent geographic features, or the stabilization of deep-earth rifts may be held for one geological age, or until such time as the Clerk finds the humor in the passage of time to be sufficiently profound to warrant archival rotation.

The determination of "funny" in the context of geological age is at the sole discretion of the presiding Clerk. This serves as a safeguard against the infinite accumulation of data that does not serve a practical administrative purpose, while still honoring the necessity of preserving ancient pacts. Records that have exceeded their retention period but are deemed of significant cultural or historical value may be moved to the deep archives, where they shall remain unless requested by the High Council. The destruction of records prior to the expiration of the seven-year period is strictly prohibited without a signed waiver from the Archmage Sovereign. See § 300.4 for reclassification of records.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
The administration of the Autumnwood Accords requires the collection of various fees to maintain the infrastructure of the Hall and the salaries of the clerks. These fees include, but are not limited to, filing fees for new enchantments, processing fees for Paradox Trials, and licensing fees for the use of restricted research facilities. It is the established policy of the Accords Desk that the responsibility for the payment of these fees rests solely upon the individual who initiated the request. The Desk shall not be held liable for the procurement of funds, nor shall it provide credit or extensions of payment to mages who lack the necessary capital.

The Desk is a neutral administrative body and does not function as a lending institution. Therefore, if a mage seeks a permit for a project, a license for a familiar, or a notation for a new contract, that mage is the primary debtor. If a third party provides the funding for such a project, that third party may be designated as the "Payor of Record," but the "Requesting Party" remains legally responsible for the completion of the payment. Should a payment fail to materialize, the Desk shall suspend all pending applications and revoke any temporary permissions granted during the application phase. No magic, including the transmutation of currency or the manipulation of debt, shall be used to circumvent these fees.

Furthermore, the Desk shall not be compelled to provide services for free under the guise of "public interest" unless a direct decree is issued by Archmage Veyra. While the Guild serves the Midlands, the administrative costs of maintaining the Accords are a burden that must be borne by those who benefit from the protections and privileges of the law. Mages who find the fees to be burdensome are encouraged to seek sponsorship from the Goodstyle Artisans or other licensed commercial entities. The Desk shall not accept Wario Coins as a valid form of tender for any administrative fees, as they are not recognized as legal currency under the Accords. See § 800.4 for duel stakes converted to fees.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The integrity of the magical marketplace and the historical record relies upon the accurate provenance of all artifacts, relics, and enchanted items brought before the Guild for registration or appraisal. A mage who presents a relic for official recognition must provide a verifiable chain of custody. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that a story is not a chain of title. While the Guild acknowledges the importance of oral tradition and the mystical "weight" of a narrative, these elements do not constitute legal evidence of ownership or origin. A compelling tale of a relic's journey through the hands of heroes does not grant the bearer the right to claim it as a sanctioned artifact if the physical evidence of its history is lacking.

Mages who knowingly submit false provenance records to the Accords Desk shall be subject to immediate investigation. This includes the fabrication of historical documents, the forging of signatures from deceased masters, or the invention of "ancient" origins for newly created items. The Guild seeks to prevent the flooding of the market with fraudulent "relics" that could mislead other casters or lead to the misappropriation of significant cultural items. If a relic's history is murky or purely anecdotal, it shall be registered as an "Artifact of Unknown Origin" rather than being granted a prestigious designation. The Desk shall not be responsible for correcting the historical record once a false claim has been entered into the ledger.

Furthermore, the provenance of a relic must be sufficient to prove that the item was not acquired through illicit means, such as the theft of Guild property or the violation of the Iron Mandate. While the Accords Desk does not recognize the laws of the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, it does maintain a policy against the trade of stolen goods. Any item whose provenance is tied to a known crime or a violation of the Accords shall be confiscated. Mages are advised to maintain meticulous records of their acquisitions to ensure that their collections remain in good standing. See § 700.1 for evidence generally. See § 300.5 for research copies of quiet items.

body.heading: § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments
body.text:
Material enchantments, as defined herein to include but not limited to warded items, inscribed artifacts, and enchanted constructs, shall be reported by the caster within seven days of completion or acquisition, whichever applies first. Failure to file such reports constitutes a Class C violation subject to fines up to one hundred gold crowns per day until compliance is achieved. See § 100.2 regarding authorized representatives for Guild filings.

The reporting form prescribed under § 900.5 must be submitted in triplicate, with the original retained by the Clerk of the Desk and copies distributed to relevant regulatory bodies as directed by current policy memoranda. All forms shall bear a unique tracking number assigned upon receipt, which must be referenced on any subsequent communications concerning said item. See §§ 1.7, 300.4 for instructions on form completion and data protection requirements.

Records of all reported material enchantments shall be maintained in the Central Registry accessible only to duly authorized personnel under strict confidentiality protocols outlined in § 1.9. Access requests must be submitted via official channels with justification documented in writing; approval rests solely with Archmage Veyra or her designee. Unauthorized viewing or dissemination of Registry data is punishable as grand larceny plus additional penalties under the Accords.

Fees associated with the reporting process are calculated according to the complexity and power rating of each enchantment, as determined by certified appraisers appointed by the Guild. These fees offset administrative costs incurred during verification, storage, and risk assessment procedures. Payment must be rendered within ten business days of invoice issuance; late payments incur monthly interest charges at eight percent above prevailing market rates for magical services. See § 200.6 regarding fee waivers for indigent practitioners under exceptional circumstances only.

False statements or omissions material to the reporting requirement shall result in immediate revocation of licensure and referral to the Disciplinary Tribunal for possible suspension or expulsion from membership entirely. Repeat offenders may face permanent disqualification from practicing magic within Guild jurisdiction indefinitely. See §§ 600.1, 800.1 for further disciplinary guidelines applicable to this offense category specifically.

All reports filed under this section become public record unless classified restrictions apply pursuant to § 900.3. Interested parties may petition the Desk for access subject to redaction of sensitive information where appropriate. Petitioners must demonstrate a legitimate need-to-know basis supported by sworn affidavit attesting to professional relevance and absence of malicious intent. Approval rates typically range between sixty and eighty percent depending on demonstrated necessity versus potential harm considerations weighed case-by-case.

This provision ensures transparency while protecting proprietary knowledge held within the Guild community. Compliance facilitates safe coexistence among diverse magical practitioners operating in shared spaces under this legal framework governing arcane arts throughout Autumnwood region exclusively. Breach thereof undermines public trust essential to maintaining orderly function of all regulated activities involving supernatural capabilities whatsoever.

body.heading: § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments — Continued
body.text:
Every mage holding an enchanted object must file a report within seven days of acquiring it. Failure to do so is grounds for immediate revocation and suspension. Reports must include the item's name, origin, enchantment type, and full provenance history. Any attempt to falsify or hide such information constitutes perjury under these Accords. Violators face harsh penalties including sealing of their magic until further notice.

The Guild maintains a central database of all reported items for monitoring purposes. Unauthorized possession or sale of restricted artifacts is strictly prohibited. Exceptions require written permission from the High Council and may only be granted in cases of extreme necessity. All reports submitted to the Desk are kept confidential unless otherwise directed by law enforcement agencies with proper jurisdiction.

Casters found in violation of this section shall forfeit all rights to practice magic within Autumnwood territory indefinitely. Repeat offenders will have their licenses permanently revoked and names added to the Quiet List forevermore. In addition, they may be subject to arrest and prosecution under existing criminal statutes governing theft and fraud. The burden of proof rests solely upon the accused mage to demonstrate innocence beyond a reasonable doubt when charged with such offenses.

Mages are reminded that transparency regarding one's magical possessions is essential for maintaining public trust in our institutions. By promptly disclosing all relevant details about enchanted items in their possession, practitioners uphold their duties both as individuals and members of this great brotherhood bound by ancient oaths sworn across generations past and present alike unto eternity itself."

"§ 900.3 False Provenance Penalty: Any mage caught misrepresenting an object's origins faces automatic expulsion from the Guild and permanent disqualification from ever casting spells again within these borders." "See also § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill."

"Under no circumstances shall any member fail to report new acquisitions promptly without risking severe consequences upon themselves and their loved ones alike!" *This clause ensures accountability among all registered practitioners while preserving individual privacy rights where appropriate under applicable laws.* "Remember always that true strength lies not in hiding one's weaknesses but rather embracing them fully despite whatever hardships may come." *With this solemn vow made before our assembled colleagues today, we renew our commitment together as guardians of knowledge and protectors against darkness looming ever closer on the horizon ahead...* "Together we stand united forevermore!" 🎉✨🔥⚡💫🌟🍀🌈🧚‍♀️🦄🐲👻💞❤️🩷"

sections.title: Record Retention
sections.brief: Seven years or one geological age, whichever the clerk finds funnier.

body.heading: Record Retention
body.text:
The Archival Integrity of the Autumnwood Accords dictates that the preservation of magical records is paramount to the stability of the Midlands. All filings, including but not limited to research permits, Paradox Trial transcripts, and unauthorized field use reports, shall be maintained in the permanent registry of the Mages' Guild. The duration of such retention is governed by the principle of Perpetual Continuity; specifically, records shall be preserved for a period of seven years or one geological age, whichever the clerk finds funnier. This clause serves to acknowledge the inherent fluidity of temporal magic and the unpredictable nature of arcane decay. While a standard administrative cycle may suggest a fixed term, the Clerk of the Accords reserves the sole prerogative to determine the "humorous" expiration of a record based on its thematic relevance to the Guild's ongoing history.

In instances where a record pertains to a Paradox Trial, the retention period may be extended indefinitely if the resulting pocket-prison remains active, as the existence of the prison constitutes a continuous event. Conversely, records pertaining to minor infractions or the mundane activities of the Goodstyle Artisans may be subject to expedited purging should the Clerk deem the aesthetic of the archive to be cluttered. It is strictly forbidden for any mage, including those of the Innovator faction, to request the destruction of a record to obscure past transgressions. Any attempt to influence the Clerk’s sense of humor regarding retention periods shall be viewed as an act of administrative subversion. For matters regarding the specific handling of restricted research copies, see § 300.5. All records must be inscribed in a medium resistant to standard transmutation or erosion.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
The financial obligations arising from the administration of the Autumnwood Accords are governed by the Principle of Origin. It is the established mandate of the Mages' Guild that the costs associated with the filing, mediation, and enforcement of these laws shall be borne by the person who asked. This means that any mage seeking a research permit under § 400.1, requesting a Paradox Trial, or seeking mediation from Archmage Veyra is solely responsible for the procurement of necessary fees. The Desk, as a neutral administrative body, shall not be held liable for the costs of magical auditing, archival storage, or the logistical requirements of the Aegis Magi.

No fee shall be levied against the Guild's general treasury for the processing of standard requests, nor shall any fee be diverted to the Innovators or Conservators for the purpose of political lobbying. If a request involves a third party, such as a merchant from the Regal Empire or a representative of the Silver Flame, the requesting mage must provide a signed guarantee of payment from said party before the Desk will initiate the filing. The Desk shall not provide credit, nor shall it accept Wario Coins as a valid form of tender, as such currency is explicitly barred from Guild circulation. If a mage finds themselves unable to produce the required funds, the request shall be returned without action. For more information on the conversion of duel stakes to administrative fees, see § 800.4.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The authentication of magical artifacts and relics within the Midlands is subject to the Doctrine of Verifiable Lineage. A story, regardless of its narrative complexity, evocative power, or historical weight, does not constitute a chain of title. The Mages' Guild explicitly rejects "mythic provenance" as a valid legal basis for the ownership or authorized use of artifacts. To establish a valid chain of title, a relic must possess a documented history of physical transfer, verified by the signatures of previous owners or the seals of recognized authorities such as the Conservators. A tale of a relic being "gifted by a dying star" or "forged in the fires of the first rift" is considered a literary achievement but holds no weight in the eyes of the Accords.

Mages who attempt to register a relic based solely on oral tradition or "inherited legend" shall be flagged for a secondary audit. If the provenance is found to be fabricated or intentionally misleading to circumvent restrictions on the Unsanctioned Arts, the offending mage shall be subject to the Paradox Trial as outlined in § 800.2. The Desk shall not recognize any artifact whose history is obscured by the "Quiet List" protocols unless a formal waiver is granted by Archmage Veyra. Furthermore, any relic claiming to be a component of the Heartstone or a product of the Great Rift must be surveyed by a Guild-approved cartographer before a provenance can even be considered for preliminary filing. For matters regarding the scrying of closed books to determine true origins, see § 700.2.

body.heading: § 900.3 Record Retention and Fees
body.text:
The preservation of official records is paramount to the integrity of the Guild's regulatory functions, yet the sheer volume of filings generated by even a single day's operations renders total archival impractical without prohibitive cost. Consequently, this section establishes a framework for systematic retention and disposal of documents deemed less critical than others in the public interest. All records relating to licensure examinations, disciplinary hearings, and major enforcement actions shall remain in permanent storage under strict chain-of-custody protocols. Routine correspondence, preliminary drafts, and other ephemera may be reduced to digital form or destroyed after a reasonable interval provided no legal claim has been filed against such material during that time.

Archives maintained by the Autumnwood Accords Desk shall be accessible upon request by any person holding valid credentials from an accredited institution of higher learning. Researchers must submit written inquiries specifying the nature and purpose of their investigation along with proof of affiliation or employment. Access to confidential files concerning individual mages is restricted solely to authorized investigators pursuing active cases approved by the High Council. The Desk shall charge nominal fees for photocopying, scanning, or certifying documents beyond basic consultation privileges. These charges are calculated at current market rates and paid directly to the Guild Treasury in Wario Coin or equivalent lawful currency. Failure to settle outstanding balances may result in suspension of access rights until compliance is achieved.

In rare instances where original artifacts possess significant historical or scholarly value, the Desk may issue certified copies bearing official seals rather than transferring possession outright. Such replicas retain full evidentiary weight for all legal purposes while preserving the integrity and provenance of genuine items. Requests for duplication must be accompanied by a detailed justification demonstrating why reproduction alone suffices for the intended end use. The Council reserves discretion to deny applications deemed frivolous or contrary to public policy considerations weighing in favor of preservation over accessibility. Any party dissatisfied with such determinations may petition for review within thirty days following written notice of decision.

body.heading: § 900.3 Record Retention and Fees — Continued
body.text:
The Guild maintains permanent records of all filings, trials, inspections, and enforcement actions as required by this Ordinance. These official archives are the sole authoritative source for determining compliance with the Accords, superseding conflicting private documentation. Records shall be retained for a minimum duration of seven years or one geological age, whichever term proves more amenable to clerical management. Fees assessed for accessing these files vary based on volume and complexity; full tariff schedules appear in Schedule D attached hereto.

All casters must provide accurate provenance information regarding enchanted items submitted for review. Misrepresentation of origin constitutes a material defect warranting immediate rejection of the filing. The Desk retains discretion to impose additional scrutiny where ambiguity exists, potentially escalating costs to the applicant. False claims of heritage may result in sanctions up to and including permanent revocation of licensure, at the sole discretion of Archmage Veyra or her delegate.

In matters involving disputed ownership of magical artifacts, the Guild shall act as neutral arbiter solely upon submission of sworn affidavits from all claimants. Such proceedings are subject to standard filing fees plus a premium charge reflective of expedited processing requirements. Parties must exhaust administrative remedies before seeking external recourse for alleged irregularities in the evaluation process. Unauthorized attempts to influence official determinations through bribery or intimidation will be prosecuted under applicable penal statutes with exemplary severity.

The integrity of Guild records is paramount to maintaining public trust and ensuring uniform application of the Accords across all jurisdictions. Every clerk must adhere strictly to chain-of-custody protocols when handling physical evidence or digital data. Failure to follow prescribed procedures may render findings inadmissible in subsequent hearings, necessitating costly remand for reevaluation. Consequently, practitioners are advised to retain independent counsel versed in arcane jurisprudence should they anticipate challenges to the official ruling.

This provision balances the need for historical preservation with practical considerations of storage capacity and fiscal responsibility. The extended retention period accounts for the enduring nature of magical effects and their potential relevance long after initial registration. Conversely, limits on access fees prevent abuse of the system by vexatious litigants seeking to harass competitors through frivolous inquiries. Ultimately, these guidelines establish a robust framework for managing the immense volume of filings generated annually while safeguarding both individual rights and collective interests.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; § 900.5 Fees Schedule; § 800.4 Duel Stakes Converted to Fees; § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts.

body.heading: § 900.3 Record Retention and Fees — Continued — Continued
body.text: The Desk shall maintain an audit trail for all filings, preserving copies indefinitely in the event of dispute or investigation. Where fees are due at any stage, the Desk may assess additional charges to cover administrative burdens imposed by complex cases. Such surcharges must be itemized on receipts issued to applicants. Any allegation of improper fee collection shall be reported directly to Archmage Veyra for adjudication. Until then, all payments remain in suspense pending resolution. Failure to settle outstanding obligations within thirty days may result in suspension of further services until default is cleared. The Desk retains sole discretion regarding waiver or remission of assessed penalties, which shall only be granted upon written petition demonstrating compelling hardship. No verbal assurances or informal understandings shall bind the Guild without formal ratification. All financial transactions must flow through designated accounts under strict oversight to prevent embezzlement or corruption. Violations of this provision constitute grounds for immediate disciplinary action, up to and including expulsion from membership. The Desk further reserves the right to pursue civil remedies against individuals who refuse to comply with reasonable requests for payment information or documentation. Transparency in billing practices remains paramount to maintaining public trust in the Guild's integrity. Applicants are advised to review fee schedules carefully before initiating any proceedings, as costs may escalate significantly depending on case complexity and duration. Disputes over pricing shall be submitted to an independent arbitration panel convened by mutual agreement of both parties. The Desk acts solely as facilitator in these matters, without prejudice to either side's substantive claims. All records generated during the pendency of a matter become property of the Guild unless otherwise stipulated in writing prior to commencement. This policy ensures preservation of institutional knowledge while safeguarding against unauthorized disclosure or exploitation of sensitive data contained therein. Compliance with fee payment obligations is considered a fundamental duty owed by all members to the collective good of the organization. Neglect of this responsibility undermines the viability of shared resources and services upon which everyone relies for safe practice and advancement of their craft. The Desk stands ready to enforce these provisions fairly and consistently, applying them equally regardless of rank or status within the ranks of registered casters. By adhering to established protocols regarding financial accountability, practitioners contribute directly to the stability and prosperity of our community as a whole. It is hoped that all will take pride in upholding these standards with diligence and honor at every turn along their path toward mastery of the arcane arts under our watchful gaze.

sections.title: Identify Fees; Who Pays
sections.brief: The person who asked. Not the Desk.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
In the matter of identification, verification, and administrative processing of magical artifacts, relics, or items of significant arcane density, the Guild shall establish a clear distinction between the act of identification and the liability for the associated costs. Any mage, initiate, or contracted agent seeking to have an object cataloged, verified for safety, or assessed for its potential violation of the Autumnwood Accords shall be deemed the primary petitioner. Consequently, all fees associated with the identification of such items shall be the sole responsibility of the individual or entity who initiated the request. The Accords Desk serves as a neutral administrative body; it does not provide identification services as a public utility, nor shall it ever be held liable for the costs incurred during the processing of a petitioner's property.

Should a petitioner claim that the identification of an item was performed as a matter of Guild necessity—for instance, if an item was seized by the Aegis Magi for immediate containment—the petitioner shall still be held liable for the administrative fees unless a formal waiver is granted by Archmage Veyra. In cases where multiple parties claim ownership of a single relic, the Desk shall not adjudicate the underlying title; it shall instead require a deposit from all claiming parties to cover the identification costs, with the fees being refunded only upon the final resolution of the ownership dispute. The Desk is strictly prohibited from utilizing Guild treasury funds to offset the costs of private identifications.

Furthermore, any mage who attempts to have the Accords Desk assume the role of a debt collector for unpaid identification fees shall be found in violation of administrative protocol. If a petitioner fails to provide the requisite tender, the Desk shall cease all work immediately and return the item to the petitioner in its current state, with no further liability on the part of the Guild. The Desk shall not be compelled to provide identification for items of unknown origin if the petitioner refuses to provide a bond against the risk of arcane leakage during the inspection process. See § 900.4.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The Guild recognizes that the history of a magical artifact is often obscured by the passage of centuries, the erosion of memory, or the deliberate obfuscation of its previous owners. However, the Accords Desk shall maintain a strict distinction between a "narrative of origin" and a "legal chain of title." A story, regardless of its poetic depth, historical resonance, or the prestige of its supposed author, does not constitute a valid legal conveyance of ownership or a certification of the item’s provenance. Any mage attempting to register a relic based solely on oral tradition, transcribed legends, or "inherited" myths without corroborating evidence shall find their application for registration suspended until such time as a verifiable audit of the item's movement can be produced.

The Guild shall not accept "mythic provenance" as a substitute for legal clearance. For example, an item described as "the blade of a fallen king" provides no more legal standing than a common iron rod if the Guild cannot trace the transfer of the blade from the kingdom to the current holder. Mages seeking to register relics of high arcane potency must provide a documented history of ownership that satisfies the requirements of the Conservators. If a relic’s history is broken or lost, it must be declared "Orphaned" and subjected to the standard quarantine procedures before any identification can occur. The Desk shall not be held responsible for the validity of a petitioner’s claims; it is the petitioner’s burden to prove that the item was not stolen, cursed, or illegally extracted from a protected site.

Furthermore, any deliberate attempt to provide a false provenance to circumvent the restrictions placed upon certain schools of magic—specifically those categorized as "Forbidden" by the Conservators—shall be treated as a felony under the Accords. If a mage knowingly presents a fabricated history to gain access to restricted research facilities or to bypass the Innovators' oversight, they shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. The Guild's records are a matter of law, not a library of fiction. A story is not a chain of title, and the Desk shall not permit the romanticization of history to supersede the rigorous demands of magical safety and legal clarity. See § 300.5.

body.heading: § 900.5 False Provenance and Attribution of Magic Items
body.text:
It is hereby established that the false attribution of magical provenance to an item shall constitute prima facie evidence of fraudulent intent, absent contrary proof by clear and convincing testimony. This standard applies regardless of whether the misattribution was intentional or merely negligent on the part of the caster or seller. The rationale underlying this provision rests upon the understanding that magical items possess intrinsic histories which can significantly impact their power levels and potential for dangerous side effects. Misrepresenting an object's origins may lead to catastrophic misuse by unprepared users, causing irreparable harm to individuals and property alike.

Under § 900.5, any party knowingly presenting a magically enhanced item with fabricated or misleading background information shall be subject to immediate revocation of their licensure and a fine no less than one hundred gold crowns per violation. Repeated offenses may result in permanent disqualification from the practice of magic within the Jurisdiction. Furthermore, such fraudulent conduct may trigger an investigation into whether additional items in the perpetrator's possession are similarly tainted by deception or illegal manufacture. The burden shall rest upon the accused to demonstrate that any inaccuracies arose from honest error rather than deliberate deceit.

This provision does not preclude legitimate scholarly inquiry into magical artifacts, provided such investigations are conducted under the strict supervision of authorized personnel and comply with all applicable safety protocols. Researchers seeking information regarding an item's origins must submit formal petitions outlining their purpose and methods to the Mages' Guild for approval prior to commencing any examination. Unauthorized attempts to uncover secrets through illicit means will be met with swift and severe punishment, in accordance with § 1500 et seq.

The Desk reserves discretion to modify penalties based on mitigating circumstances, such as confession before discovery of fraud or restitution made voluntarily by the offender. Conversely, aggravating factors like prior convictions for similar offenses may lead to enhanced sanctions beyond those explicitly enumerated herein. The ultimate goal remains maintaining public safety while fostering an environment conducive to responsible magical advancement. All persons are urged to familiarize themselves fully with these obligations to avoid inadvertent violation and consequent liability under applicable law.

body.heading: § 900.5 Attribution of Magic Items and Provenance Claims
body.text:
§ 900.5 Attribution of Magic Items; Burden of Proof for Historical Relics. It shall be unlawful to falsely attribute a magic item to a known historical figure or event without clear evidence, as such misrepresentation may artificially inflate market value and encourage fraud. Any caster seeking to sell an artifact claiming ancient lineage must provide credible documentation of provenance to the Desk prior to transaction. Failure to do so renders the sale void and subject to confiscation by Aegis Magi upon reasonable suspicion of deception. This provision aims to protect consumers from overpaying for counterfeit relics while maintaining transparency in the magical economy under § 100.6.

Under no circumstances shall a magic item's true origin be concealed or misrepresented, whether through forged certificates, altered inscriptions, or outright fabrication. Violations constitute a Class B misdemeanor punishable by fines up to one thousand gold pieces and mandatory community service at the discretion of the local judge. Repeat offenders may face additional penalties including temporary suspension of their magical license per § 200.4. The burden of proof rests entirely on the seller to establish authenticity beyond reasonable doubt, adhering to standards set forth in applicable civil procedure codes outside this Codex.

The Desk reserves the right to inspect any disputed item at its own expense if a credible allegation is made against it. Such examinations must be conducted impartially by certified appraisers approved by the Guild, whose findings shall be binding unless contested within ten business days. Parties dissatisfied with initial determinations may appeal directly to Archmage Veyra for final adjudication under § 100.2. All fees associated with these review processes shall be paid upfront by the complaining party, reimbursable only if the allegation is substantiated. This framework ensures fairness and efficiency in resolving disputes while safeguarding public confidence in magical goods.

False attribution not only harms individual traders but also undermines the integrity of the entire magical marketplace. By establishing strict guidelines for provenance claims, this section seeks to preserve ethical standards and prevent exploitation by unscrupulous actors. Compliance with these provisions is essential for maintaining trust between buyers and sellers alike, fostering a thriving environment where innovation can flourish alongside tradition. All casters are expected to uphold these principles diligently in their professional endeavors.

The Desk further clarifies that this rule applies equally to both domestic and international transactions involving magic items originating from any region within or beyond the Accords' jurisdiction. Nothing herein shall be construed to limit existing laws regarding intellectual property rights, trademarks, or consumer protection statutes enacted by sovereign governments elsewhere. Rather, these regulations complement such frameworks to create a comprehensive system governing magical commerce globally. Casters are advised to familiarize themselves with all relevant legal requirements before engaging in any commercial activity related to enchanted artifacts.

In summary, § 900.5 mandates truthfulness regarding the origins and history of magic items traded within the Guild's purview. Sellers bear the responsibility of verifying and disclosing accurate information, facing appropriate consequences for violations. Through diligent enforcement of these guidelines, the Autumnwood Accords Desk strives to cultivate a fair and reliable marketplace where honest dealing prevails over deceitful practices. All members are urged to adhere strictly to this standard in their daily operations.

see § 100.2 Authority of the Archmage; see § 200.4 Suspension Procedures; see § 300.3 Quiet List Filing Requirements; see § 700.1 General Evidence Standards

body.heading: § 900.4 Fees for Identification Services and Allocation of Costs
body.text: § 900.4 Identify Fees; Who Pays. Any caster providing identification services under this section shall charge a reasonable fee to compensate for time spent, risk assumed, and expertise applied. Such fees shall be agreed upon in advance between the parties or determined by an independent appraiser if disputed. The client engaging the caster's services bears full responsibility for paying said fees promptly upon completion of work. Failure to do so may result in termination of the agreement without refund and potential legal action for breach of contract. No portion of any fee collected shall be subject to seizure under the Iron Mandate or similar extraneous statutes unless expressly authorized by this Codex. All costs associated with identifying an item's magical properties remain solely the responsibility of the requesting party, regardless of outcome or success rate achieved during examination. The Guild Desk reserves no right to recoup such expenses from general funds nor shall it accept payment in kind except as otherwise provided herein. Clients are advised that fees may vary significantly based on complexity of analysis required and rarity of materials involved in the item being appraised. Written estimates must be furnished prior to commencement of services whenever practicable to avoid misunderstandings regarding final charges incurred throughout duration of engagement period established between provider and consumer thereof. Disputes arising over quantum or quality of service rendered shall be resolved through binding arbitration administered by designated magisters appointed annually by vote of active members in good standing within relevant jurisdictional boundaries applicable at time dispute arises under these provisions set forth above herein.

body.heading: § 900.4 Identification Fees and Allocation of Costs
body.text:
All requests for identification services submitted under these Accords shall be subject to an initial consultation fee payable in advance by the submitting party. This fee, set at no less than five gold coins per item or one hundred gold coins per batch thereof, serves as a non-refundable administrative charge covering the Desk's preliminary assessment of potential hazards and logistical requirements. Should further extensive analysis prove necessary, additional costs shall accrue pro-rata based on complexity and duration, billed upon completion of said services. Refunds are granted only in cases where no substantive work was performed due to client error or withdrawal prior to commencement of actual evaluation.

Payment obligations extend beyond mere transactional exchanges; they embody a broader commitment to responsible stewardship within the arcane community. By electing to engage Guild expertise, clients implicitly acknowledge their duty to share in the burdens attendant thereto, whether financial or otherwise. This principle undergirds not only fee structures but also liability frameworks governing subsequent interactions between parties. Failure to honor payment terms may result in immediate suspension of all further services rendered until outstanding balances are satisfied in full, plus applicable penalties as prescribed by law.

In matters involving disputed provenance claims regarding magical artifacts, the burden of proof rests squarely upon the asserting party to establish credibility through corroborating evidence and expert testimony where feasible. Mere assertions lacking substantiation carry no weight whatsoever under these Accords, regardless of persuasive rhetoric employed to bolster such positions. The Desk reserves absolute discretion to reject outright any submissions deemed frivolous or intended solely for gain without legitimate purpose, thereby preserving precious resources for bona fide inquiries requiring genuine attention.

Ultimately, the equitable distribution of costs reflects a fundamental truth: magic remains an inherently dangerous force demanding careful handling from all who seek its power. Whether through formal channels established herein or informal arrangements made outside thereof, every participant bears responsibility for mitigating risks associated with their actions. Only by embracing this shared accountability can we hope to foster a safer environment wherein both innovation and tradition may flourish harmoniously under the watchful gaze of Archmage Veyra herself."

sections.title: False Provenance of Relics
sections.brief: A story is not a chain of title.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
Any individual, entity, or faction seeking to introduce a relic, artifact, or enchanted object into the public sphere, the Guild’s archives, or any sanctioned marketplace under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords shall be held strictly liable for the veracity of the item’s provenance. The Accords Desk hereby establishes that the mere existence of a narrative surrounding an object does not constitute a legal chain of title. A story, regardless of its antiquity, poetic resonance, or perceived historical weight, is not a substitute for documented evidence of lawful acquisition or ancestral right. Practitioners who attempt to bypass the rigorous standards of § 1101.2 Relics; Chain of Title by weaving elaborate tapestries of mythic origin are subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi.

The Guild recognizes that the "mystique" of an object often serves as a veil for illicit trafficking or the misappropriation of cultural heritage. Therefore, any claim of provenance based solely on oral tradition, "found-item" anecdotes, or "ancestral memory" without corroborating physical evidence of transition shall be deemed insufficient for the purposes of legal registration. To prevent the laundering of stolen goods through the manufacture of convenient legends, the Accords Desk requires a verifiable paper trail—or its magical equivalent—detailing the movement of the object from its point of origin to the current holder. If the lineage of an object is broken by a period of "lost history," the burden of proof remains on the claimant to demonstrate that the acquisition was not performed through coercion, theft, or violation of previous sovereign treaties.

Furthermore, the intentional fabrication of a false provenance is classified as a Grade III Arcane Fraud. Any mage or merchant found to have knowingly authored a fictitious history for a relic to increase its market value, influence political standing, or obscure its dangerous nature shall face immediate referral to the Paradox Trial for adjudication. During such proceedings, the court shall weigh the discrepancy between the "story" provided and the actual magical signature of the item. If the magical resonance of the relic contradicts the stated history—for instance, if an object claimed to be a gift of peace displays a signature of violent subjugation—the provenance shall be struck from the record, and the item may be seized as contraband.

In instances where an object’s history is genuinely unknowable due to the destruction of records, the owner must register the item as "Unverified Origin." Such items may be held privately but are prohibited from being sold, gifted, or traded within the Midlands without a specific waiver from the Archmage Sovereign. The Accords Desk shall not be misled by the eloquence of a scholar or the passion of a collector; a story is a matter of art, while a chain of title is a matter of law. For further guidance on the required documentation for relic registration, see § 1101.2. For matters regarding the preservation of existing records, see § 900.3.

body.heading: § 900.6 Relic Authentication and Appraisal Standards
body.text:
The Guild recognizes the value of historical magical artifacts, herein termed "relics," in establishing precedent for dispute resolution. To ensure integrity in relic valuation, all appraisals shall be conducted by certified Guild assessors utilizing standardized testing protocols outlined in Exhibit B-14. False certification or tampering with a relic's provenance constitutes forgery under § 601 and may result in revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4(d). Assessors must disclose any conflicts of interest per § 100.5 prior to commencing evaluation services. Relics seized during inspections shall be held in secure vaults until disposition is finalized by the Desk. Parties contesting an appraisal may request a second opinion at their own expense within thirty days of initial assessment results. Failure to comply with these authentication requirements renders relics inadmissible as evidence unless corroborated by independent testimony meeting evidentiary standards set forth in § 700.1(c). The Guild reserves the right to re-evaluate relic valuations periodically based on new information or technological advancements affecting appraisal methodologies. All relic transactions must be registered with the Guild within ten business days of completion to maintain accurate records for future reference and regulatory oversight purposes as mandated by this section and related provisions herein.

"Relic authentication requires expertise beyond ordinary knowledge. Certified assessors exist precisely to prevent fraud through rigorous testing procedures. Any party seeking to challenge an appraisal bears the burden of proof and associated costs." - Archmage Theron, Conservator Council

"The provenance of magical artifacts is sacred ground. Tampering with such items violates both letter and spirit of our Accords. We must remain vigilant guardians against deception." - Janna Brightspark, Innovator Representative

"Standardized protocols ensure fairness across all relic evaluations. Transparency in appraisal processes builds trust within the Guild community." - Senior Clerk Elara Vane, Autumnwood Accords Desk

*See also: § 300.2 Prohibited Practices Regarding Antiquities; § 600.1 Contractual Obligations Relating to Historical Items*

body.heading: § 900.5 False Provenance of Relics; § 900.6 Relic Authentication and Appraisal S
body.text:
No caster shall knowingly misrepresent the origin, age, or magical potency of an item for commercial or fraudulent purposes, such representations constituting a material breach of contract under these Accords. See § 1.4 (Persons Bound) and § 300.5 (Research Copies of Quiet Items). Any party discovering such falsification must immediately notify the nearest Guild Office in accordance with § 900.1 (Duty to File Before Casting), failing which they incur liability for all resulting damages.

All disputed artifacts shall be submitted for independent appraisal by two certified Relic Appraisers appointed by the Archmage Sovereign, their findings binding unless successfully challenged within thirty days under oath before the Desk. The costs of such verification shall be borne equally between disputing parties until one party prevails, at which point reimbursement follows standard civil procedure. See § 700.1 (Evidence Generally) and § 900.4 (Identify Fees).

Relics deemed counterfeit or fraudulently marketed shall be seized pursuant to § 800.1 (Discipline; Range of Sanctions) and destroyed after judicial review, unless their value exceeds one hundred gold crowns, in which case they shall be sold at public auction with proceeds distributed to the Guild’s General Fund for future research initiatives. See § 900.2 (Reporting of Material Enchantments).

The Guild retains sole authority to authenticate relics and determine their true nature, rejecting all claims by unauthorized bodies or individuals. This includes but is not limited to self-proclaimed historians, connoisseurs, or relic hunters lacking formal certification. Violation of this clause constitutes grounds for immediate suspension of licensure under § 200.4 (Suspension and Lapse). See also § 100.2 (Who May Speak for the Guild).

Appraisal fees shall be assessed at a flat rate of fifty crowns per item, payable upon filing with the Appraisers’ Bureau. Additional charges apply for complex artifacts requiring extended examination or specialized equipment. Payment must be rendered in Wario Coin or equivalent lawful tender; foreign currencies require conversion at current market rates plus a five percent premium to cover exchange risk. See § 100.6 (Delegation to Clerks) and § 200.5 (Guest Casters).

Parties aggrieved by Appraisal findings may petition for rehearing within ten days, providing new evidence or testimony relevant to authenticity determinations. Such motions shall be heard expeditiously by a special tribunal convened solely for this purpose, with final rulings issued no later than sixty days from initial submission. See § 700.2 (Scrying of Closed Books) and § 800.3 (Seal of Silence; Duration and Review).

Relic Authentication and Appraisal Standards shall be promulgated annually by the Archmage Sovereign in consultation with the Conservator Council and Innovator Representatives, ensuring alignment with evolving magical theory and technological advancement. These standards carry the force of law under these Accords and must be strictly enforced to maintain public trust in Guild oversight mechanisms. See § 100.5 (Conflict of Interest in Casting) and § 900.3 (Record Retention).

This comprehensive framework governs relic authentication, fraud prevention, and dispute resolution, reflecting the Guild’s unwavering commitment to integrity in all matters pertaining to magical artifacts. By adhering thereto, casters safeguard both their own interests and those of the broader community dependent upon responsible stewardship of arcane treasures. For further guidance on specific scenarios not addressed herein, consult the official commentaries maintained by the Autumnwood Accords Desk or seek counsel from licensed legal practitioners specializing in Artificer Law. See § 100.7 (Foreign Halls and Courtesy) and § 200.6 (Constructs That Hold a Quill).

body.heading: § 900.5 False Provenance of Relics and Related Deceptions
body.text:
It is forbidden to misrepresent the origin, authorship, or historical significance of any magical artifact in a manner that induces another into purchasing it under false pretenses. Such acts constitute fraud and undermine public trust in the antiquities market. Violators shall be subject to penalties commensurate with the degree of harm caused.

This provision addresses the deliberate fabrication of provenance narratives designed to inflate an item's perceived value or desirability. Examples include falsely attributing a spellbook to a legendary archmage, claiming a wand was wielded by a historical hero, or asserting that a trinket contains residual enchantments from its original creator where none exist. The intent is typically financial gain through deception rather than mere exaggeration of facts.

In cases where the misrepresentation results in material loss to an unsuspecting buyer, restitution shall be ordered along with punitive sanctions. Where no direct victim can be identified, a fine payable to the Guild fund will apply. Persistent offenders may face suspension or revocation of their licensure if they hold any form of official standing within the magical community.

The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to demonstrate that false claims were made knowingly and with specific intent to deceive. Vague assertions about an item's "ancient roots" or "mystical past," absent evidence of affirmative misrepresentation, will not suffice to trigger liability under this section. However, patterns of deceptive behavior may warrant further investigation by the appropriate authorities.

This rule complements existing provisions concerning contract fraud and unfair trade practices. It reflects the Guild's commitment to maintaining integrity within the marketplace for magical goods and services. All participants are expected to adhere to ethical standards when discussing or transacting in artifacts of historical importance. Failure to do so risks not only financial consequences but also professional ruin.

see § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild, § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters, § 700.1 Evidence Generally
"Truthfulness is the cornerstone of commerce. Deception erodes trust and damages all concerned." — Archmage Theron, Conservator Manifesto

body.heading: § 900.5 False Provenance of Relics and Related Deceptions — Continued
body.text:
The use of spurious provenance to inflate the value or status of magical artifacts is expressly prohibited under this section. Any representation that a relic possesses ancient lineage, noble ownership, or sacred consecration which is demonstrably false shall constitute grounds for immediate revocation of licensure and potential criminal prosecution. The Desk maintains an independent authentication board empowered to investigate claims of provenance fraud upon receipt of credible evidence.

Relics obtained through deception regarding their origin are subject to forfeiture and destruction at the Guild's discretion. Penalties may be enhanced if false representations were made with intent to defraud or manipulate market conditions. Repeated violations will result in permanent disqualification from participating in any licensed magical trade activities. The Desk reserves the right to impose additional sanctions as deemed necessary to protect public welfare.
