Only through rigorous enforcement can we ensure that the sanctity of monetary systems remains inviolate amidst the ever-evolving landscape of magical possibilities.

sections.title: Invisibility of Liens
sections.brief: A hidden lien is still a lien. An invisible one is a violation.

body.heading: Invisibility of Liens
body.text:
A lien, whether it be a magical debt, a property encumbrance, or a soul-binding obligation, is a legal reality that exists independently of its visibility to the naked eye or to standard scrying methods. The fact that a lien has been rendered invisible, obscured by a veil of secrecy, or hidden within a complex series of nested enchantments does not negate its existence. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a hidden lien is still a lien; it remains a valid legal claim on the asset in question.

The deliberate use of invisibility magic to conceal a lien is a primary violation of the Guild’s transparency requirements. If a mage sells an enchanted item that is secretly encumbered by a debt to a third party—rendered invisible to the buyer to facilitate a "clean" sale—the seller is liable for all penalties associated with the hidden debt. The Aegis Magi are authorized to use "Deep-Sense" detection to uncover such hidden encumbrances during any contested trade. Any asset found to have an invisible lien attached to it shall be subject to immediate seizure until the debt is satisfied.

Furthermore, this rule applies to "quiet" debts—those that are not publicly recorded but are nonetheless agreed upon between two mages. While the Guild does not require the public posting of every minor debt, the use of magic to hide a major lien from the Guild’s oversight is a criminal offense. If a lien is invisible, it is a violation. The Guild shall treat all such instances as intentional fraud, and the perpetrator may face a Paradox Trial for the deliberate subversion of the Accords’ transparency mandates.

body.heading: Invisibility of Liens and the Doctrine of Constructive Notice
body.text:
A fundamental tenet of the Accords is that magical encumbrances, regardless of their visibility to the naked eye or conscious perception of the subject, constitute valid liens upon the person or property they bind. The legal fiction of constructive notice operates such that any mage capable of detecting a spell through conventional divination techniques is deemed to have actual knowledge of its existence. Consequently, failure to perceive an invisible enchantment does not negate its binding force; rather, it merely delays discovery and compounds liability under § 1001.10(b). This principle ensures that mages cannot evade obligations by cloaking them in obscurity, thereby preserving the integrity of magical commerce and personal accountability.

The mechanism of constructive notice is particularly salient where complex or subtle wards are employed to conceal their presence. Such spells may be designed expressly to deceive even experienced practitioners, creating a false sense of security while silently draining the victim's resources or autonomy over time. Under § 1001.10(c), any mage who knowingly employs deceptive enchantments for the purpose of obscuring liens commits the offense of Concealment by Trickery and is subject to enhanced penalties upon conviction. The burden of proof rests with the accuser to demonstrate that the accused had the capacity for detection yet willfully avoided it, a standard typically met through expert testimony or circumstantial evidence such as anomalous energy readings.

Furthermore, the doctrine extends beyond mere physical concealment to include psychological manipulation designed to induce amnesia or suggestibility in the subject. Techniques such as Memory Wipe and Mind Blank are expressly prohibited in commercial contexts under § 1001.5(d), as they violate the sanctity of personal autonomy and informed consent. Even when employed ostensibly for therapeutic purposes, these practices constitute a breach of fiduciary duty if used to obscure the true nature of magical bonds. Violators face severe sanctions including permanent revocation of licensure and mandatory exile from the Guild ranks under § 800.2(e).

The implications of this rule reach far beyond individual disputes, touching upon the very fabric of magical society. By establishing that invisible liens are binding just as those visible to all, the Accords uphold a baseline of fairness and transparency in dealings between mages. This prevents exploitation through subterfuge and ensures that no party can claim ignorance where reasonable diligence would have revealed the truth. As stated in § 1001.10(d), "A lien cast with intent binds whether seen or unseen," affirming that the efficacy of magical contracts depends upon the caster's purpose rather than the subject's awareness."

In practice, this doctrine necessitates heightened vigilance among all practitioners regarding the spells they employ and those affecting them. Regular scans for hidden enchantments using approved divination tools are now considered standard operating procedure in professional settings. Failure to conduct such screenings may itself constitute negligence under § 700.4(b), opening the door to liability should adverse consequences arise later. The ultimate goal remains the preservation of a trustworthy environment where magical interactions can occur with confidence that all parties enter into agreements fully informed of their rights and obligations."

"see § 1001.5(d) Prohibited Spells in Commercial Contexts; see § 800.2(e) Permanent Revocation for Gross Misconduct; see § 700.4(b) Negligence in Detection Procedures. A lien cast with intent binds whether seen or unseen."

body.heading: § 1001.10 Invisibility of Liens and the Doctrine of Constructive Notice
body.text:
A lien, whether visible or concealed, remains valid upon its creation notwithstanding any attempt to obscure its existence from view. Under this Article, all liens arising under the Accords are deemed constructive notice to all persons who deal with the encumbered property, regardless of their actual knowledge thereof. This principle serves to protect the integrity of magical commerce by preventing fraudulent attempts to evade obligations through clandestine arrangements.

The doctrine of constructive notice operates on the presumption that any individual engaging in business dealings within the jurisdiction has access to and duty to review official records maintained by the Guild's Bureau of Magical Property Rights. Failure to consult these archives constitutes negligence at worst, but may constitute willful misconduct if done with intent to defraud creditors or other parties. The burden is upon those claiming ignorance of a lien's existence to demonstrate that they exercised reasonable diligence in verifying their counterparty's standing prior to transacting.

This provision reflects the Accords' broader commitment to transparency and accountability in magical transactions. By establishing an irrebuttable presumption that all liens are publicly recorded, the law removes any ambiguity regarding the true state of title for enchanted assets. It thereby deters opportunistic behavior by bad-faith actors who might otherwise seek to exploit information asymmetries between buyers and sellers.

Exceptions exist only where the lien is manifestly impossible to discover through ordinary means, such as those attached by supernatural entities beyond mortal comprehension or jurisdiction. Even in such cases, however, the affected party retains the right to petition the Guild for relief upon proper notice and proof of harm suffered as a direct result of the undisclosed encumbrance.

The principles outlined herein shall govern all disputes concerning the visibility and discoverability of liens, whether arising inter partes or vis-à-vis third parties claiming an interest in the same subject matter. They represent a fundamental shift away from traditional notions of actual notice toward a more robust system designed to safeguard the collective welfare of the magical community as a whole.

body.heading: § 1001.10 Invisibility of Liens and the Doctrine of Constructive Notice — Continued
body.text:
Nothing in this Part shall be construed to validate or enforce any hidden lien, encumbrance, or magical claim that has not been duly registered with the Autumnwood Accords Desk in accordance with § 900.1 et seq. See § 900.2 (Reporting of Material Enchantments). An invisible lien is void ab initio and unenforceable under any circumstances. Under no condition may a party rely on an undisclosed magical claim as grounds for rescission, damages, or specific performance. This rule applies equally to liens created by spellwork, runes, sigils, or other arcane mechanisms. See § 1001.6 (Endowments and Gifts of Magical Assets).

The Doctrine of Constructive Notice is hereby expressly rejected in the context of hidden magical claims. Unlike conventional property interests subject to public recording statutes, arcane encumbrances do not benefit from presumed knowledge through registration alone. Each party bears a duty of reasonable inquiry into potential magical defects before entering binding agreements involving enchanted assets or services. Failure to conduct such inquiries does not excuse breach of contract under § 1001.7 (Disclosure of Composition, Value, and Risk). However, constructive notice principles may inform the allocation of risk where parties knowingly engage in high-risk magical transactions without full disclosure. See § 1001.4 (Illusion-Based Fraud) for related guidance on material misrepresentation.

In cases where an invisible lien is discovered post-formation, the aggrieved party may seek remedies under the general provisions governing breach and fraud. This includes damages for reliance losses, restitution of transferred value, and potentially punitive sanctions if intentional deception is proven. The burden of proof rests squarely with the claimant to establish the existence and terms of the hidden encumbrance. Ambiguities regarding magical claims are resolved strictly against the drafter or party asserting such an interest. See § 700.1 (Evidence Generally) and § 900.4 (Identify Fees; Who Pays).

This section does not preclude the existence of valid, registered liens that operate invisibly to untrained observers. Such claims remain enforceable when properly documented under Part IX. The prohibition targets only those deliberately concealed from all but a select few, designed to exploit ignorance or bypass standard safeguards. Parties are advised to consult qualified legal and magical counsel before assuming obligations involving enchanted items or services of significant value. Prudence is paramount in navigating the complex interplay between conventional contract law and arcane realities. See § 1001.2 (Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets) for additional context on regulatory boundaries.

body.heading: § 1001.10 Invisibility of Liens and the Doctrine of Constructive Notice — Contin
body.text:
The invisibility of liens serves as both shield and sword in the arcane marketplace. While it protects lenders from immediate default, it undermines trust among merchants who cannot discern hidden encumbrances on assets they purchase or invest in. This opacity breeds suspicion and depresses overall transaction volumes unless remedied through greater transparency mechanisms.

To address this dilemma, the Accords mandate that all active liens be recorded in a public registry accessible to interested parties upon request. The cost of registration falls upon the lienholder, who bears responsibility for maintaining accurate records throughout the duration of their security interest. Failure to comply exposes them to penalties including fines and potential forfeiture of claimed priority status.

Furthermore, the Accords establish presumptions regarding unknown liens based on reasonable diligence inquiries undertaken by prospective buyers or investors. If a party fails to discover an encumbrance despite exercising ordinary care in researching title history and public filings, they may be estopped from asserting claims against innocent third parties relying on apparent ownership rights.

These provisions balance competing interests between protecting established security interests while preserving market fluidity for honest traders operating in good faith. By requiring disclosure of existing obligations upfront, the Accords promote clarity and reduce disputes arising from concealed liabilities surfacing unexpectedly down the line. Ultimately, this approach fosters greater confidence in commercial dealings involving magical goods and services across the realm.

see § 1001.6 Endowments and Gifts of Magical Assets; see § 200.3 Temporary Mouths; see § 900.4 Identify Fees; Who Pays. The interplay between lien visibility, registration obligations, and equitable notice principles shapes how magic-infused commerce unfolds in practice under the Autumnwood Accords regime.

body.heading: § 1001.10 Invisibility of Liens and the Doctrine of Constructive Notice — Contin — Continued
body.text:
The doctrine of constructive notice operates as an exception to the general rule of invisibility, wherein a party may be deemed aware of a lien despite lacking actual knowledge thereof. Under this principle, if a mage reasonably should have been cognizant of an encumbrance given the circumstances surrounding their transaction, they shall bear the consequences as though such awareness were explicit. This equitable construct serves to prevent negligent parties from escaping liability through claims of ignorance when red flags ought to have prompted further inquiry.

In practice, constructive notice attaches where a lien's existence is rendered obvious by extrinsic factors beyond mere secrecy. For instance, if a caster fails to disclose a substantial magical debt while actively promoting their services under a false name, they may be held liable for defrauding subsequent clients who relied upon their purported unencumbered status. Similarly, when a construct owner permits unauthorized modifications to their automaton that degrade its utility without informing the original purchaser, constructive notice may attach regarding latent defects known only to the modifier.

The burden of proving actual or constructive knowledge rests squarely with the party alleging such awareness. They must present compelling evidence demonstrating how the hidden lien should have been apparent under ordinary diligence. Mere speculation about potential conflicts does not suffice; there must be a tangible nexus between the undisclosed encumbrance and the transaction at issue. Courts will scrutinize these claims closely to avoid undermining the foundational principle that liens remain invisible unless properly registered.

This provision ensures fairness in an era where magical assets often carry complex histories beyond their physical form. By holding actors accountable for failing to investigate obvious risks, it promotes transparency while preserving the sanctity of undisclosed obligations. The balance struck here reflects a pragmatic approach to evolving commercial norms without compromising established legal precedents.

See also § 1001.2 Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets regarding disclosure requirements; § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure for analogous secrecy provisions; and § 700.5 Clone as Duplicate Claimant for issues of apparent ownership versus actual rights. Under § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting, all material interests must be registered prior to deployment in commerce. As noted under § 400.3 Borrowed Hours, misuse of temporal assets similarly violates fiduciary duties owed to clients. The Desk reminds all parties that vigilance remains paramount when dealing with enchanted goods or services.

sections.title: Wish Used to Rewrite a Filed Return
sections.brief: A wish does not rewrite the stamp.

body.heading: Wish Used to Rewrite a Filed Return
body.text:
The Guild clarifies that the use of high-level reality-altering magic, specifically "Wish" level enchantments or similar reality-warping phenomena, does not grant a mage the authority to retroactively alter, erase, or rewrite a filed and stamped magical tax return or a finalized Guild contract. A wish does not rewrite the stamp. Once a document has been submitted to the Clerk’s Desk and received the official Guild seal, it is considered a fixed point in the administrative timeline.

Any attempt to use a wish to "undo" a debt, "re-write" a contract, or "erase" a reporting failure is considered an act of administrative sabotage. The Guild recognizes that while a wish may alter the physical reality of the world, it does not possess the jurisdictional authority to overwrite the bureaucratic reality of the Accords. If a mage uses a wish to change the fact that they owed a debt, the debt remains on the Guild's ledger as a "Wish-Nullified Liability." The mage will still be required to pay the original fee, and they may be charged an additional "Reality Interference Surcharge" for attempting to subvert the Guild’s records.

This rule serves to prevent the erosion of the Guild’s authority by those who believe their personal magical potency exempts them from the Accords. The Guild is the mediator of magic, and its records are the foundation of that mediation. To allow mages to simply "wish" away their obligations would create a catastrophic instability in the Guild’s ability to regulate the Midlands. Any mage found attempting to use a wish for the purpose of administrative revision shall be immediately detained for questioning by the Conservators.

body.heading: § 1001.11 Wish Used to Rewrite a Filed Return
body.text:
No act of magic, however potent, shall undo the finality of an executed filing before the Desk or its authorized proxies. A casting that purports to erase, alter, or nullify a return once stamped valid is void ab initio and constitutes material fraud under § 1001.6. This rule exists not merely to preserve administrative order but to safeguard the sanctity of contractual certainty—a bedrock principle upon which all magical commerce rests. To permit such retroactive revision would be to invite chaos, for it would render every filed document a mere suggestion subject to whimsical revision by rogue spellcasters.

The Desk has observed with growing alarm an uptick in attempts to manipulate the filing process through supernatural means. Instances include the use of wish spells to "un-cast" returns after issuance, or the invocation of temporal loops to revisit and amend submitted forms. Such acts are explicitly prohibited and punishable as serious offenses under the Accords. The Desk maintains that once a return is properly executed, it stands immutable except by due process before a judicial body or competent tribunal. Any party seeking to challenge the validity of a filing must do so through established legal channels, not by force of magic alone.

It shall be noted that this prohibition applies regardless of whether the wish was cast knowingly or unknowingly by the filer or their agents. The burden lies upon all parties to verify the completeness and accuracy of their submissions prior to execution. Failure to do so may result in rejection of subsequent filings until such time as the offending return is formally withdrawn or corrected through proper procedure. The Desk reserves the right to deny service to any entity found guilty of repeated violations of this clause.

Furthermore, attempts to circumvent this prohibition by employing proxies, simulacra, or other avatars are equally forbidden. The intent behind the law is clear: no magical trickery shall undermine the integrity of the filing process. Parties seeking exceptions must petition the Desk directly with compelling justification and evidence of necessity. Mere assertion of power is insufficient grounds for waiver of this fundamental rule.

In sum, § 1001.11 serves as a bulwark against the most insidious forms of magical malfeasance. By establishing clear boundaries on what may and may not be done post-filing, the Desk ensures that all participants operate within a predictable framework conducive to fair dealing. Those who would test this limit do so at their peril, for the consequences can be dire indeed—from immediate revocation of privileges to permanent expulsion from good standing before the Guild. Let it be remembered: once stamped, forever sealed unless reversed through lawful means alone.

body.heading: § 1001.11 Wish Used to Rewrite a Filed Return — Continued
body.text:
A wish cast directly upon a filed return, or an instrument thereon, does not constitute a valid alteration under these Accords. The immutable nature of the official seal and ink renders such attempts null and void ab initio. Any party seeking modification must submit a formal amendment request pursuant to § 1001.6, accompanied by appropriate fees as set forth in Schedule A.

Furthermore, the use of illusion magic to mask or obscure material facts within a return is strictly prohibited. Such conduct shall be deemed fraud under § 1001.4 and subject to enhanced penalties. The burden of disclosure rests squarely upon the filer, who must ensure complete accuracy and transparency at all times. Failure to do so invites rigorous scrutiny from the Desk's auditors.

In addition, any attempt to employ a wish for the purpose of evading regulatory oversight is expressly forbidden. This includes but is not limited to uses designed to conceal illicit activities or misrepresent financial position. The Accords stand firm in their commitment to maintaining the integrity of magical commerce through diligent supervision and enforcement.

It is hereby declared that no magic, however potent, shall supersede the authority of the Autumnwood Guild Desk in matters relating to its regulatory purview. All parties are reminded of their obligation to comply fully with these provisions without exception or evasion. The consequences for non-compliance range from monetary fines up to and including permanent disqualification from practicing within the jurisdiction.

The spirit of this section shall be liberally construed to effectuate a comprehensive ban on magical tampering with filed documents. Plain language prevails in all interpretations, and any doubts are resolved against those attempting to circumvent these clear mandates. The Guild reserves the right to pursue civil and criminal remedies as appropriate under applicable laws.

This provision serves as an unequivocal warning against abusing supernatural powers for regulatory gain or evasion. The Desk expects adherence to established protocols rather than creative shortcuts that risk undermining public trust. Violations will be addressed swiftly and severely, with no leniency shown for those who choose to flout these rules.

In sum, the Accords maintain an ironclad stance on protecting the sanctity of official records from magical manipulation. Any perceived loopholes are hereby closed by forceful language leaving no room for misinterpretation. The Desk remains vigilant in its mission to uphold justice through unwavering enforcement of this critical safeguard.

body.heading: § 1001.12 Retroactive Alchemy of Financial Instruments
body.text:
A wish shall not retroactively alter the legal effect of a filed financial instrument, even if such alteration would benefit the caster or their associates. The binding nature of sealed contracts persists regardless of subsequent magical manipulation aimed at nullifying obligations. Any attempt to use arcane means to erase debts, void liabilities, or rewrite transaction histories after the fact constitutes high-level fraud and grounds for immediate sanction under § 800.1.

The Desk maintains that financial instruments carry inherent legal weight once properly executed, independent of external forces. While mages are free to employ their skills in commerce, they may not exploit loopholes created by wishful thinking or reality-warping abilities to undermine established obligations. Such actions violate the core principles of contract law and threaten the integrity of economic exchange within the Accords' jurisdiction.

Consequences for violating this provision range from heavy fines to permanent revocation of licensure, depending on severity and intent. Repeat offenders may face additional penalties including exile from Guild territory or sealing of their magical faculties under § 800.2. The burden lies with any party claiming a contract has been magically altered to prove such alteration occurred beyond a reasonable doubt. Absent conclusive evidence, the original terms shall prevail.

This rule exists to prevent abuse of powerful artifacts and abilities in financial contexts, ensuring that magic does not become an unchecked variable destabilizing economic systems. The Desk acknowledges the potential for creative circumvention but maintains firm boundaries regarding the finality of legal agreements once sealed with proper authority. Mages must operate within established frameworks when engaging in commercial activities, avoiding shortcuts that compromise fairness or transparency.

Failure to comply with this mandate renders a caster subject to disciplinary action under § 800.1 and possible civil liability for damages resulting from fraudulent practices. The Desk reserves the right to investigate allegations of magical tampering at its sole discretion, employing all necessary means to ascertain facts fully. Any party aggrieved by perceived violations may petition for review through standard appellate channels outlined in applicable sections herein.

Ultimately, this provision reinforces the principle that magic serves as a tool within defined parameters rather than an omnipotent force subject only to individual will. By maintaining strict controls over how and when arcane abilities interact with financial instruments, the Guild protects both its members and the broader community from exploitation arising from unchecked power dynamics between mages and merchants alike.

body.heading: § 1001.13 Irrevocable Nature of Filed Statements
body.text: The written record submitted to the Autumnwood Accords Desk constitutes an immutable fact for all legal purposes, regardless of subsequent alteration by magical means. Even a Wish spell cast retroactively cannot erase the original submission from history's memory; it can only obscure or disguise its true nature. Any attempt to rewrite past filings using supernatural intervention shall be treated as aggravated fraud subject to enhanced penalties under § 1001.14 and related provisions. The Desk maintains independent verification processes designed specifically to detect such manipulative tactics, employing a variety of arcane sensing techniques unavailable to ordinary mages. Parties are reminded that the integrity of the financial registry depends upon strict adherence to these protocols at all times. See also §§ 600.3 (Geas as Unconscionable Term), 900.1 (Duty to File Before Casting), and 1001.7 (Disclosure Requirements). Violation of this principle undermines the entire regulatory framework governing magical commerce, warranting swift and severe action by the Aegis Magi upon discovery.

body.heading: § 1001.14 Aggravated Fraud Penalties
body.text: Any individual or entity found guilty of magically altering filed financial statements commits aggravated fraud under these Accords, carrying a mandatory minimum penalty of permanent sealing of their magical abilities along with substantial monetary fines. The Desk reserves the right to escalate charges to criminal proceedings in appropriate cases, seeking imprisonment for particularly egregious offenders. Repeat violators may face additional sanctions including expulsion from the Guild and blacklisting throughout the region. Enforcement actions shall be initiated immediately upon notification by any authorized party, without prejudice to further remedies available under applicable law. These stringent measures reflect the critical importance of maintaining public confidence in the fairness and accuracy of magical markets. See §§ 800.1 (Range of Sanctions), 900.5 (False Provenance Punishment), and 1001.2 (Prohibited Spells in Markets). The Guild remains committed to protecting consumers from predatory practices while ensuring fair competition among lawful participants. All members are urged to report suspected violations promptly through established channels to facilitate timely intervention before damage occurs.

sections.title: Wario Coin; Non-Recognition
sections.brief: Private tender. Points even less so. Cite only to refuse.

body.heading: Wario Coin; Non-Recognition
body.text:
The Guild officially declares that the "Wario Coin" is not a recognized tender of the Autumnwood Accords. It is classified as private tender and holds no legal weight in any official Guild transaction, tax payment, or contract settlement. The Guild does not provide any valuation for Wario Coins, nor does it accept them as a means of satisfying any fees, fines, or debts. In the eyes of the Accords, a Wario Coin is functionally equivalent to a decorative button; it has value only in private, informal agreements between individuals who have voluntarily agreed to its use.

Because Wario Coins are not recognized tender, they may not be used to purchase Guild-sanctioned materials, licenses, or services. Any merchant who attempts to accept Wario Coins as payment for Guild-regulated goods may be investigated for "Unsanctioned Economic Interference." The Guild will not mediate disputes involving Wario Coins, as they fall outside the scope of the Accords’ financial regulations. If a mage wishes to trade in Wario Coins, they must do so at their own risk in the private markets, and the Guild shall not be held responsible for any losses incurred from such trades.

In any dispute where Wario Coins are presented as a form of payment for a Guild-related obligation, the Guild shall simply refuse the tender. This refusal is not a judgment on the coin's inherent worth, but a strict adherence to the Guild's recognized monetary standards. Mages are advised to use standard Midlands currency for all matters involving the Accords. Cite only to refuse.

body.heading: Wario Coin; Non-Recognition — Continued
body.text: The Autumnwood Accords expressly reject the Wario Coin as valid legal tender within the jurisdiction of the Mages' Guild Hall. Although such tokens may circulate freely in informal markets and private transactions, they carry no official standing under the Codex or its subordinate regulations. Any attempt to use Wario Coin for settlement of debts incurred before the Desk shall be deemed ineffective, leaving the obligor liable only for payment in standard coinage or guild-approved scrip. This rule reflects the broader principle that all financial instruments must conform to established norms and oversight mechanisms; unregulated currencies pose inherent risks of fraud, inflation, and manipulation by unscrupulous actors. The Guild reserves the right to seize and confiscate any Wario Coin found within its purview without compensation, treating such acts as potential evidence of economic destabilization efforts. Furthermore, no clerk or officer shall be compelled to accept Wario Coin in satisfaction of fees, penalties, or fines imposed by virtue of this Office. Parties desiring to discharge obligations using non-standard currency must first obtain written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign or her duly appointed delegates. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in escalated sanctions, including revocation of licensure and referral for punitive trial under § 800 et seq. The Desk maintains a strict policy against acknowledging any claims predicated solely on Wario Coin holdings; such assertions shall be dismissed summarily unless corroborated by independent verification from a recognized assessor or auditing body. This stance underscores the Accords' commitment to preserving financial integrity and preventing the erosion of monetary standards through illicit means. All transactions involving alternative currencies must adhere to rigorous disclosure requirements set forth in § 1001, ensuring transparency and accountability throughout the system. By firmly rejecting the validity of Wario Coin, the Mages' Guild safeguards its regulatory authority and protects citizens from exploitative practices that could undermine economic stability. Any organization or individual found violating these provisions shall face severe consequences, including but not limited to expulsion from guild membership and criminal prosecution under applicable statutes. The Desk expects all participants in magical commerce to recognize and respect these mandates without exception or equivocation. Compliance is non-negotiable, as upholding the sanctity of currency forms a cornerstone of sound governance within this realm.

body.heading: Non-Recognition of Wario Coin as Tender
body.text:
§ 1001.12 Wario Coin; Non-Recognition
The Autumnwood Accords Desk hereby declares that any coinage bearing the likeness or signature of Wario, whether minted by private parties or state authorities, shall not be recognized as legal tender within the jurisdiction of the Guild Halls. This provision supersedes all prior customs and practices to the contrary. The rationale for this stance is twofold: first, such currency lacks any intrinsic value beyond its face denomination, rendering it worthless in times of economic distress; second, the proliferation of Wario Coin facilitates illicit transactions and undermines the integrity of the Guild's monetary system.

It shall be unlawful for any licensed mage or construct to accept payment in Wario Coin for services rendered, goods delivered, or debts incurred. Violation of this prohibition shall constitute a Class A misdemeanor subject to penalties under § 800.1 Discipline; Range of Sanctions. Furthermore, the possession and circulation of Wario Coin within Guild-controlled zones is strictly prohibited, with exceptions granted only by written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign. Any individual found in violation thereof may be subjected to confiscation of said currency and imposition of a fine up to five hundred gold crowns per offense.

This regulation shall remain in full force and effect until amended or repealed by the Autumnwood Accords Desk acting pursuant to § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild. The Desk reserves the right to issue additional guidance and interpretations as necessary to ensure compliance with this mandate. All persons bound hereby are directed to familiarize themselves fully with its terms and consequences, failing which they shall be held responsible for any resulting liabilities or damages. By virtue of the authority vested in this Codex, let it be known that Wario Coin is henceforth deemed null and void for all intents and purposes within our realm.

body.heading: § 1001.12 Wario Coin; Non-Recognition of Private Tender
body.text:
No coinage struck under the aegis of Wario or any affiliated entity shall be recognized as legal tender within Autumn Wood jurisdiction, regardless of face value or purported backing. This prohibition extends to all forms of private currency, whether minted domestically or imported from foreign lands, unless expressly authorized by the Archmage Sovereign through formal decree. The Guild reserves absolute discretion to determine the authenticity and acceptability of any monetary instrument presented for settlement of debts, fines, or fees owed under these Accords.

Any attempt to discharge an obligation using non-compliant tender shall be deemed a deliberate refusal to pay, punishable as contempt of court. Repeated offenses may result in suspension of licensure or revocation of standing practice privileges until such time as full redress is made in lawful means. Merchants and service providers are expressly forbidden from demanding payment exclusively via Wario Coin or similar instruments; failure to comply constitutes unfair trade practice under existing statutes governing consumer protection and fair dealing.

The Guild maintains a comprehensive registry of approved currencies, updated quarterly to reflect market conditions and political developments. This list shall be made publicly available at all official desks and online portals for easy reference by citizens and practitioners alike. Any queries regarding the status of specific coinage should be directed to the Clerk in writing for prompt resolution. Unauthorized issuance or circulation of counterfeit money is a felony offense carrying severe penalties upon conviction.

Archmage Veyra, exercising her plenary powers as head of state, hereby declares null and void all prior rulings that permitted acceptance of Wario Coin. This order supersedes conflicting provisions in local ordinances or customary practice to the contrary. All parties are enjoined from violating this directive under pain of immediate prosecution. The Guild shall take whatever measures necessary to enforce compliance, including but not limited to seizure of offending assets and initiation of disciplinary proceedings against recalcitrant individuals or entities.

Let it be understood that the integrity of our monetary system is paramount to maintaining social order and economic stability in Autumn Wood. Any undermining thereof threatens the very foundations upon which this society rests. Citizens are urged to report suspicious activity involving illicit currency promptly to their local law enforcement authorities. Together, we shall safeguard our shared prosperity against those who would seek to profit from chaos and deceit. So mote it be!

body.heading: § 1001.12 Wario Coin; Non-Recognition of Private Tender — Continued
body.text:
Wario Coin, the proprietary currency issued by certain commercial entities within the Guild's jurisdiction, shall not be accepted as lawful tender for any transaction regulated under these Accords. This prohibition extends to all forms of payment including goods, services, debts, fines, fees, and settlements. The invalidity of Wario Coin stems from its lack of official backing and the inherent volatility associated with private issuance.

Under § 1001.6 Endowments and Gifts of Magical Assets, any attempt to use Wario Coin as a medium of exchange constitutes a material misrepresentation of value and risk. Similarly, § 1001.3 Valuation After Alteration applies mutatis mutandis to transactions conducted in private tender, rendering them subject to re-evaluation should the coin's worth fluctuate significantly post-exchange. The Desk retains discretion to void any contract predicated upon Wario Coin if fraud or duress is alleged.

The non-recognition policy reflects the Accords' commitment to maintaining a stable and transparent economic ecosystem. By refusing private tender, the Guild safeguards against speculative bubbles and predatory lending practices that could undermine public confidence in its regulatory framework. Parties dealing exclusively in Wario Coin must bear all associated risks without recourse under these laws. Violators may face disciplinary action up to and including suspension of licensure for repeated offenses.

This provision operates independently from broader prohibitions on financial fraud (§ 1001.1) or manipulation (§ 1001.2), yet complements them in preserving market integrity. No exemptions are granted regardless of the parties' status or intent. The Desk shall issue periodic guidance clarifying specific applications as needed to ensure uniform enforcement across all jurisdictions under its purview.

body.heading: § 1001.12 Private Tender and Non-Recognition
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords Desk expressly disclaims any obligation to recognize or accept Wario Coin, whether issued by the Wario Kingdom or otherwise, as legal tender within the jurisdiction of the Guild or its member states. Any private agreement purporting to establish such status shall be void ab initio and unenforceable under this Code. This prohibition extends to all forms of scrip, tokens, digital assets, or other non-state currencies that lack explicit authorization from a sovereign authority recognized by the Accords.

Mages who knowingly accept Wario Coin in lieu of lawful coinage for services rendered shall be subject to disciplinary proceedings upon complaint. Repeat offenders may face sanctions up to and including temporary suspension of their licensure. The Desk retains broad discretion to determine whether any given form of private tender falls within the ambit of this prohibition, taking into account factors such as the issuer's credibility, the currency's liquidity in local markets, and its potential for facilitating illicit transactions.

The provisions of this section shall not be construed to limit or restrict the Guild's right to establish its own internal accounting systems and payment methods as it deems necessary to further the purposes of the Accords. Nothing herein shall impair the Desk's power to require all filings and reports submitted under this Code to be denominated exclusively in lawful coinage, unless otherwise specified by subsequent rulemaking.

See also § 1001.8 Reporting Thresholds for material transactions; § 900.4 Identification Fees payable to the Guild upon filing of new accounts or amendments thereto. Under § 700.2 Scrying Prohibited in Private Spaces, any attempts to circumvent this ban through technological means shall be treated as willful violations subject to enhanced penalties. Nothing in this section shall affect the validity of contracts executed prior to the effective date hereof, except where expressly provided otherwise by the Accords Desk.

This provision represents a deliberate policy choice by the Guild to maintain strict control over all monetary flows within its domain and to prevent potential abuse of private currencies for evading regulatory oversight. The Desk reserves the right to amend these rules at any time without notice or hearing, as part of its ongoing efforts to adapt to evolving economic conditions and threats to public order.

In sum, Wario Coin remains firmly excluded from the realm of acceptable tender under the Autumnwood Accords, with severe consequences for those who dare to challenge this fundamental tenet of Guild law. The Desk stands ready to enforce these provisions rigorously, utilizing all means at its disposal to preserve the integrity and stability of the local economy against external pressures and internal subversion.

sections.title: Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault
sections.brief: Off-books is still books if a clerk can smell it.

body.heading: Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault
body.text:
The use of extra-dimensional storage, specifically the Bag of Holding and similar "pocket" containers, does not exempt the contents of such containers from the Guild’s oversight. The legal maxim "off-books is still books if a clerk can smell it" is hereby codified. If a mage uses a Bag of Holding to store enchanted items, transmuted ores, or restricted research materials, those items are still subject to all reporting, taxation, and safety regulations.

Mages may not claim that items stored in a pocket dimension are "hidden" from the Guild’s jurisdiction. If an item is owned by a Guild member and is capable of being retrieved for use, it is subject to the Accords. The use of a Bag of Holding as a "black site" for the storage of illegal artifacts or unreported magical assets is a grave violation. If a Guild inspector finds a Bag of Holding in a mage's possession, they are authorized to demand a full inventory of its contents. The "hidden" nature of the storage does not provide a legal shield against the requirements of § 900.2.

Furthermore, the storage of "Off-Books" items in a Bag of Holding is considered an attempt to evade the Guild's mandatory reporting. Any items discovered in such a vault that have not been properly filed will be seized, and the owner will be charged with "Intentional Obscuration of Assets." The Guild’s goal is to ensure that all magical materials are accounted for to prevent the clandestine buildup of dangerous artifacts. See § 900.3 for record retention requirements.

body.heading: § 1001.13 Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault
body.text:
§ 1001.13 Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault: Use of Extra-Dimensional Storage for Concealment or Evasion of Taxation and Regulation is Prohibited

The Accords explicitly forbid the use of extra-dimensional containers, such as bags of holding or similar artifacts, to conceal taxable goods, evaded duties, or prohibited items from detection by Guild Inspectors. Such practices constitute a material breach of filing obligations and undermine the integrity of the economic system regulated thereby. Any party found utilizing dimensional storage for illicit purposes shall be subject to immediate seizure of assets and prosecution under applicable penal statutes.

The intent behind this prohibition is clear: extra-dimensional space must not serve as a loophole to circumvent lawful oversight. The Guild recognizes that advanced magical technology can render conventional inspection methods obsolete, hence the need for specific restrictions on their application in commercial contexts. Parties are urged to exercise prudence and transparency when employing such devices, ensuring full compliance with all relevant Accords at all times.

Violations of § 1001.13 may result in severe penalties, including permanent revocation of licensure, monetary fines, and criminal charges depending on the circumstances. The Guild reserves the right to enforce this provision rigorously to protect public safety and maintain fair trade practices within its jurisdiction. All licensed mages and entities are expected to familiarize themselves with these requirements and adhere strictly thereto without exception.

This section serves as a reminder that magical innovation must never supersede legal obligations. While new technologies offer exciting possibilities for growth and development, they cannot be allowed to erode the foundational principles upon which this society thrives. By mandating accountability and openness in the use of dimensional storage, the Accords seek to balance progress with responsible stewardship of shared resources. It is imperative that all stakeholders uphold these standards diligently to preserve the stability and prosperity of our community for generations to come.

body.heading: Off-Books Storage via Bag of Holding
body.text:
§ 1001.13 Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault
The storage of magical assets in extradimensional containers, commonly known as Bags of Holding, shall be treated as the establishment of an off-books vault under § 1001.2(b). The transfer of ownership into such a container does not constitute delivery absent physical manifestation or explicit declaration by both parties. This rule exists to prevent mages from evading tax obligations and regulatory oversight through mere verbal assertion of possession without tangible proof of control.

The burden of proving lawful acquisition rests upon the holder of the Bag of Holding at all times, see § 700.1. Failure to produce contents for inspection may result in confiscation under the Aegis Powers granted by the Accords. Any attempt to conceal the existence or location of such a vessel from Guild inspectors shall be deemed an act of evasion subject to penalties under §§ 800–900. The presence of prohibited items within an off-books vault does not alter its legal characterization but may trigger additional scrutiny regarding potential illicit activities facilitated thereby, in accordance with § 1001.5.

Mages are reminded that the Accords apply regardless of physical location or dimensional displacement. No clever wordplay shall obscure this fundamental truth. The Desk retains full authority to inspect any claimed Bag of Holding upon reasonable suspicion of violation. Refusal to comply will be treated as evidence of guilt per § 800.1(a). All holders are urged to maintain complete transparency regarding the contents and provenance of their magical storage devices to avoid unnecessary complications, see § 1001.7. The Guild stands ready to assist compliant citizens in navigating these complex regulations while ensuring fair enforcement against those who would undermine its integrity. Trust but verify; it is better to ask forgiveness than permission when dealing with the arcane. But remember: we always find out eventually.

"Thou canst not hide from thine debts, nor yet from thine masters." - Ancient Proverb, commonly cited at Arcane Courts
"Where there's smoke, there's fire. And where there's a Bag of Holding, there's trouble brewing." - Janna Brightspark, Innovator Faction Leader

body.heading: Off-Books Storage via Bag of Holding — Continued
body.text:
§ 1001.13 Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault, Off-Books Storage via Bag of Holding

It is well settled that the provisions of this Part apply regardless of whether the relevant magical item resides physically within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk or merely in a container under the control of one bound by these laws. See § 1001.8 Lead-to-Gold; Reporting Threshold. Thus, even if a Bag of Holding is located in another realm entirely, its use as an off-books vault constitutes a violation of §§ 1001.2 Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets and 1001.3 Valuation After Alteration.

A Bag of Holding may not be employed to store value-laden items outside the purview of formal reporting requirements. See § 1001.4 Illusion-Based Fraud. This prohibition extends to any item whose true worth exceeds its apparent market price, whether by virtue of rarity, enchantment, or secret provenance. Under § 1001.7 Disclosure of Composition, Value, and Risk, all such items must be declared upon acquisition, regardless of their physical location.

The mere act of transferring an asset into a Bag of Holding for the purpose of circumventing regulatory oversight is sufficient to trigger enforcement action. See § 1001.9 Polymorph of Coinage; § 1001.12 Wario Coin; Non-Recognition. Authorities are empowered to seize and inspect any such container suspected of containing undeclared valuables, with or without a warrant issued under § 700.1 Evidence Generally. Resistance to inspection shall be treated as a hostile act, justifying escalation per § 800.2 Paradox Trial Procedure.

Furthermore, possession of a Bag of Holding known to have been used for illicit storage subjects the owner to strict liability for any violations committed therein. See § 300.1 Schedules of Arts; § 400.6 Unauthorized Use of Restricted Magic. The principle of "possession is nine-tenths of the law" holds true in this context, as does the maxim that ignorance is no excuse when one knowingly facilitates prohibited activity.

In sum, the use of a Bag of Holding to evade off-books storage mandates renders it an instrumentality of fraud under § 1001.5 Material Alteration of Traded Goods and subject to immediate confiscation per § 800.2 Paradox Trial Procedure. All such containers shall be inventoried, sealed, and held pending further determination by the Desk pursuant to its statutory powers. See §§ 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; 900.5 False Provenance of Relics.

This rule is intended to close a critical loophole exploited by those seeking to conceal wealth from proper taxation and oversight, thereby preserving the integrity of the arcane economy and ensuring equitable treatment for all lawful citizens. Any attempts to circumvent this prohibition shall be met with swift and severe consequences, as outlined herein.

~END OF SECTION~

body.heading: Bag-of-Holding as Off-Books Vault § 1001.13
body.text:
The use of extradimensional containers, particularly bags of holding and similar artifacts capable of creating sealed interior spaces, shall not be employed to circumvent the provisions of this Code. Such vessels are hereby designated as "off-books vaults" when utilized for storing goods subject to taxation, assessment, or regulatory oversight without disclosure to the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The concealment of taxable items within these dimensions constitutes a deliberate evasion of fiscal obligations and is treated identically to physical smuggling across jurisdictional lines.

Parties employing bags of holding as storage facilities must file a supplemental declaration identifying the contents, their estimated value, and the intended duration of retention. This disclosure ensures proper inclusion in subsequent tax calculations and prevents inadvertent double-taxation upon retrieval. Failure to submit such documentation within ten business days of acquiring the container results in a presumptive violation under § 1001.13(a)(2). The Desk retains broad discretion to demand immediate inventory audits should irregular patterns emerge, including but not limited to unexplained increases in declared asset holdings coinciding with purchases or rentals of dimensional storage devices.

It shall be unlawful to transfer title to taxable property into the custody of a bag-of-holding contract as a means of defrauding creditors or avoiding seizure by enforcement officers. Such transactions are deemed void ab initio, and all parties thereto liable for penalties under applicable fraud statutes. The presence of concealed goods within an extradimensional space does not negate their existence for legal purposes; rather, it amplifies the gravity of the infraction due to the intentional nature of the concealment. Aggravated penalties apply when violations involve amounts exceeding one thousand gold pieces or result in demonstrable economic harm to third parties.

The Desk authorizes the use of specialized detection technologies capable of scanning for active dimensional anchors and associated artifacts. Law enforcement agencies are granted unrestricted access to such equipment for investigative purposes, with costs borne by the violating party upon confirmation of guilt. Refusal to submit to lawful inspection constitutes an additional offense under § 1001.13(b)(4), subject to separate prosecution. Repeated offenders may face enhanced sanctions including permanent revocation of magical licensure and mandatory community service related to public safety initiatives.

This provision serves as a critical safeguard against the erosion of revenue streams essential for maintaining law enforcement capabilities throughout the region. By closing this avenue of tax avoidance, the Accords preserve their integrity while acknowledging the realities of modern commerce facilitated by advanced magical technology. Compliance remains voluntary but highly advisable given the severe consequences of non-cooperation. The Desk stands ready to assist bona fide users in navigating these complex regulations through approved channels and professional consultation services.

"Smuggling isn't about where you hide it - it's about whether anyone knows." ~ Anonymous Merchant, circa 742 AR

body.heading: § 1001.13 Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault — Continued
body.text:
The use of extradimensional containers, specifically the bag of holding and its variants, presents unique challenges to the Accords' framework regarding financial transparency and liability. Under this section, it is established that any attempt to utilize such items for the purpose of concealing assets or evading reporting requirements constitutes a direct violation of § 1001.1 Financial Fraud and Manipulation Generally. The Desk presumes knowledge of such contrivances on the part of all licensed practitioners and imposes strict prohibitions against their deployment in financial contexts without explicit authorization.

The core principle underlying this provision is that magic cannot be employed to circumvent established fiscal obligations. Whether through direct invocation, enchanted artifacts, or any other arcane means, efforts to mask wealth or obscure transactional trails are deemed unacceptable. This extends beyond simple hoarding; it encompasses active subversion of the reporting system designed to maintain market stability and protect consumers from predatory practices. Any individual found using such methods faces immediate suspension pending further review under § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse.

Furthermore, this clause clarifies that possession alone does not constitute a violation; rather, intent is key. The mere ownership of an extradimensional container carries no inherent wrongdoing. It becomes illicit only when deliberately exploited to evade disclosure mandates or facilitate fraudulent activities. Practitioners are urged to exercise utmost caution regarding such items and consult with the Desk before engaging in any potentially problematic applications. Failure to do so may result in severe penalties, including permanent revocation of licensure under § 800.3 Seal of Silence.

The Desk retains broad discretion in interpreting and enforcing this provision as necessary to safeguard the integrity of financial markets. This includes the authority to mandate additional audits or impose heightened reporting requirements on those suspected of circumventing the rules through magical means. By explicitly addressing these novel scenarios, the Accords aim to preemptively close loopholes that could otherwise be exploited by unscrupulous actors seeking to undermine the system's safeguards. All practitioners are expected to adhere strictly to these guidelines in order to preserve public confidence and ensure fair competition within the industry.

see § 1001.2 Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets; see § 1001.3 Valuation After Alteration; under § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments, practitioners must disclose all relevant magical influences affecting their assets. Failure to do so may result in charges of concealment and manipulation under this section.

sections.title: Secured Transactions in Bound Objects
sections.brief: Collateral that can walk away.

body.heading: Secured Transactions in Bound Objects
body.text:
The Guild recognizes the inherent danger in the trade of "Bound Objects"—items that possess a degree of sentience, independent movement, or the ability to act as an agent of their owner. When such objects are used as collateral or as part of a secured transaction, they are subject to unique "Walk-Away" clauses. Because a bound object can potentially move itself out of a physical vault or flee a site of seizure, the owner must provide a "Binding Guarantee" that the object will remain stationary and compliant during the duration of the transaction.

Any contract involving a bound object as collateral must include a "Stationary Clause." If the object "walks away" during a period of legal encumbrance, the owner is held strictly liable for the loss of the asset and for any damage caused by the object’s flight. The Guild considers the loss of a bound object from a secured location as a breach of the Accord's stability measures. Sellers of bound objects must disclose the object’s level of autonomy and its history of compliance.

In the event that a bound object flees its designated location, the Aegis Magi may be authorized to track and retrieve it using "Recall" magic, the costs of which shall be borne by the owner. Transactions involving objects with high levels of agency (such as golems or sentient constructs) must be overseen by a Guild Notary to ensure that the "binding" is sufficient to prevent the asset from abandoning its legal obligations. Collateral that can walk away requires extraordinary security; failure to provide such security is a violation of the Accord.

body.heading: Secured Transactions in Bound Objects — Continued
body.text:
§ 1001.14 Secured Transactions in Bound Objects

A critical ambiguity arises where tangible property, once bound by magic or enchantment, transitions into the realm of intangible rights. This section addresses the priority and perfection of security interests attached to such hybrid assets. Where a spell permanently alters an item's nature—transforming lead to gold, or flesh to stone—the original chattel ceases to exist in its prior form. The value resides instead in the magical state itself. A creditor extending funds for this transformation acquires only a contractual right against the debtor, unless specific steps are taken to perfect their interest. To secure a claim on such enchanted goods, the creditor must obtain a lien via official registration with the Accords Desk within thirty days of perfection. Failure to register renders any subsequent bona fide purchaser or mortgagee superior to the unperfected lienholder. Moreover, any attempt to re-magically alter an already secured item without disclosing the prior encumbrance constitutes fraud under § 1001.1 and shall be punished accordingly. The Desk may demand production of all relevant scrolls or artifacts to verify the extent of the magical binding before approving a security interest. This provision ensures clarity in commercial dealings involving magically modified goods, protecting both lenders and buyers from hidden risks. See also §§ 900.2 (reporting of material enchantments), 1001.5 (material alteration of traded goods), and 300.1 (schedules of arts). Under § 1001.14, failure to register a security interest in enchanted property within the prescribed timeframe shall result in the automatic extinguishment of that interest upon transfer of possession to another party. This rule balances the need for commercial certainty with recognition of magical uniqueness."

body.heading: § 1001.14 Secured Transactions in Bound Objects – Collateral That Can Walk Away
body.text:
§ 1001.14 Secured Transactions in Bound Objects — Continued: Collateral that Can Walk Away. A secured transaction involving a bound object presents unique risks not encountered with conventional assets, primarily due to the potential for the collateral itself to depart from the creditor's control entirely. This section establishes rules governing such scenarios to ensure equitable treatment of all parties involved.

When a bound object is pledged as security for a debt, it remains in physical possession of the debtor unless otherwise agreed upon by written instrument signed under seal. However, if the debtor breaches any material term of the agreement or becomes insolvent, the creditor may exercise remedies immediately without prior notice except where prohibited by applicable law or contract provision. Remedies available to the secured party include taking possession of the collateral pursuant to a writ issued by a Justice's Court upon application supported by affidavit stating default and value of claim relative to debt owed; selling or otherwise disposing of the property at public auction after reasonable notification published in local newspapers for fifteen days preceding sale date with proceeds applied first toward satisfaction of outstanding obligations owed hereunder then return of surplus funds if any remain following full payment thereof.

In cases where the collateral cannot be located despite diligent efforts by both parties to ascertain its whereabouts, the creditor may petition a court of competent jurisdiction for an order directing investigation into possible hiding places or alternative holdings consistent with known facts surrounding last known location along with evidence establishing bona fide security interest therein prior to granting relief sought herein. Upon approval granted by said tribunal based upon findings made after hearing conducted solely on written submissions absent oral testimony except as expressly authorized thereto, judgment shall enter against debtor for amount due plus costs associated therewith including reasonable attorney fees incurred during course of proceedings instituted hereunder unless otherwise provided herein or in any subsequent modification thereof executed voluntarily and knowingly by all interested parties involved.

Notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary, no creditor shall ever attempt to seize bound objects belonging to third persons without specific authority granted via duly executed power of attorney setting forth precise terms governing such actions including limitations on scope thereof relative to interests claimed thereby or any other restrictions deemed necessary for protection against abuse thereof by those wielding same irresponsibly. Failure to comply with these requirements renders all subsequent attempts void ab initio regardless of circumstances surrounding events leading up thereto unless ratified later in writing signed under seal by affected parties expressly waiving prior objections raised previously hereunder or elsewhere pursuant to laws applicable hereto.

This provision aims to balance competing interests between creditors seeking assurance against future defaults and debtors retaining maximum flexibility regarding use of pledged assets while preventing opportunistic exploitation arising from inherent vulnerabilities associated with immovable property types generally understood within broader legal contexts encompassing matters discussed hereinabove along with related considerations not explicitly addressed but implied therein by operation of customary usage prevailing throughout civilized lands worldwide today.

see § 1001.6 Endowments and Gifts of Magical Assets; see § 900.5 False Provenance of Relics; see § 800.3 Seal of Silence; Duration and Review.

body.heading: § 1001.14 Secured Transactions in Bound Objects – Collateral That Can Walk Away — Continued
body.text:
§ 1001.14 governs the special risks attendant to lending magical items as security for debt. Where a creditor accepts a bound object as collateral, they must acknowledge that the debtor may retain use rights unless expressly waived. Any such waiver requires written consent and explicit valuation of lost utility. Failure to account for this creates a presumption of unconscionable terms under § 1001.6.

Particular attention is paid to items possessing autonomous agency or sentience. Lending such artifacts without full disclosure subjects the lender to strict liability for any harm caused by their independent actions, pursuant to § 200.4 and related provisions on delegated authority. The creditor bears burden of proving they obtained informed consent prior to accepting security. Absent such proof, the transaction is voidable at debtor's option.

The Desk further notes that magical bonds may serve as de facto liens under certain conditions. Where a spell permanently attaches ownership markers or binding clauses to an item, this effect may supplant conventional mortgage instruments. Such "magical mortgages" are subject to separate regulatory oversight and disclosure requirements detailed in § 600.3. Creditors relying solely on enchantments without formal registration risk losing priority claims upon default.

Finally, the Desk emphasizes that neither party should assume the other lacks knowledge of inherent dangers associated with the collateral. Debtor representations regarding item condition or potential hazards carry weight under standard warranty principles outlined in § 501.2. Lenders accepting items "as-is" do so at their peril and cannot later complain of unforeseen complications arising from known defects.

In sum, § 1001.14 mandates scrupulous care when dealing with magical security interests. Both creditor and debtor must fully understand the implications before proceeding. The Desk remains available to clarify any ambiguities regarding this complex area of law. Compliance protects all parties against avoidable losses stemming from negligence or ignorance of binding obligations.

body.heading: § 1001.14 Secured Transactions in Bound Objects – Collateral That Can Walk Away — Administration
body.text:
The unique mobility and autonomy inherent to bound objects present distinctive challenges for secured creditors seeking to enforce their interests under the Accords. Unlike traditional chattel, a bound entity may elect to sever its ties with its owner entirely, rendering any prior security agreements moot. To mitigate this risk, § 1001.14 establishes specific requirements and protections governing such transactions.

Firstly, all secured parties must obtain written consent from the bound object before initiating enforcement actions against it or transferring ownership rights. This consent shall be documented in a "Severance Agreement," executed by both the creditor and debtor, detailing the scope of permitted activities and any associated compensation obligations. Failure to secure such agreement prior to action constitutes grounds for dismissal of claims and potential sanctions under § 1001.5.

Secondly, creditors are encouraged to register their security interest in the Central Registry within thirty days of execution, thereby providing public notice and priority against subsequent claimants. Registration shall include a detailed description of the bound object, its current location, and any special conditions or limitations imposed by the owner. Unregistered interests remain valid between parties but lack enforceability vis-à-vis bona fide third parties under § 1001.6.

Thirdly, in cases where the bound object refuses to comply with reasonable requests from the secured party, such as accessing internal records or providing financial statements, the creditor may petition the Guild for an emergency injunction compelling cooperation. The burden of proof rests solely on the petitioner to demonstrate a credible threat to their security position and that no less intrusive alternatives exist. Injunctive relief shall be granted only upon showing clear and present danger to the integrity of the transaction or substantial prejudice to the creditor's rights under § 1001.7.

Finally, this section applies exclusively to transactions involving bound objects classified as "High Value" pursuant to Schedules of Arts (§ 300). Lower-tier items remain subject to standard commercial lending practices without additional safeguards. The provisions herein are not intended to alter the fundamental nature of security interests under common law or create new causes of action; rather, they supplement existing frameworks with tailored mechanisms suited to the peculiarities of bound collateral. See also § 1001.2 regarding valuation methodologies and § 1001.9 concerning disclosure obligations for enchanted assets.

The interplay between secured financing and bound object autonomy demands careful navigation by all participants in the magical economy. By adhering strictly to the procedures outlined above, creditors can protect their investments while respecting the agency of those whom they bind into servitude. Ultimately, this balance ensures continued growth and innovation within the Guild's expanding marketplace. Under § 1001.8, violations may result in penalties ranging from monetary fines to outright revocation of operating licenses for non-compliant firms.

body.heading: § 1001.14 Secured Transactions in Bound Objects – Collateral That Can Walk Away — Oversight
body.text:
The unique nature of bound objects, particularly those infused with magical properties or capable of autonomous action, necessitates special provisions regarding the perfection and enforcement of security interests therein. Where collateral possesses inherent mobility or the potential to escape the control of the secured party, additional steps may be required to preserve the priority position established under this Part.

In instances where the bound object is a living creature, construct, or sentient entity, mere attachment of a lien shall not suffice to perfect the security interest against subsequent bona fide purchasers or encumbrancers. Rather, the creditor must effectuate physical possession or registration with an appropriate governmental authority having jurisdiction over such entities. Failure to do so may result in subordination of claims should the collateral transfer hands without notice of the prior security agreement.

Furthermore, creditors holding security interests in bound objects shall exercise due diligence in monitoring the condition and location thereof throughout the duration of the credit extension. Unreasonable neglect or failure to inspect may constitute waiver of rights under applicable law and custom. In particular, where the object exhibits signs of distress, degradation, or attempted liquidation by unauthorized parties, prompt remedial action must be taken to mitigate losses.

Where collateral is capable of self-replication or metamorphosis, additional safeguards shall be employed to prevent dilution or depreciation of value. This may include contractual restrictions on reproduction methods or mandatory submission of newly created units for inspection and certification. Any material deviation from approved specifications shall constitute an event of default triggering acceleration of obligations under the security instrument.

In sum, the secured party must maintain vigilant oversight of collateral possessing unusual characteristics to preserve its priority status. Adherence to these heightened standards ensures fair treatment of all parties engaged in transactions involving bound objects within the commercial framework established by this Code.

sections.title: Layered Transfiguration Schemes
sections.brief: Read as one scheme if a reasonable toad would be confused.

body.heading: Layered Transfiguration Schemes
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes the "Reasonable Toad" standard for the interpretation of complex magical transmutations. If a mage employs a series of layered transfigurations—where an object is changed into one form, then another, then a third, and so on—the entire sequence shall be read as a single, continuous scheme if a reasonable toad would be confused by the intermediate steps. This prevents mages from using "nested" transmutations to bypass the Guild’s reporting thresholds or to hide the original nature of an asset.

For example, if a mage transmutes lead into a copper pot, then into a silver bowl, and finally into a gold goblet, the Guild will view this as a single transmutation of lead into gold. The intermediate steps of "copper" and "silver" do not reset the reporting requirements or exempt the mage from the taxes associated with the final gold product. The intent of the mage is the primary factor in legal determination; if the sequence of changes is clearly designed to obfuscate the final result from the Assay Desk, it shall be treated as a fraudulent "Layered Scheme."

All mages who engage in complex transmutations are required to file a "Sequence of Intent" form before beginning the process. This form must outline the final intended form and the steps required to reach it. If a mage fails to file such a form and the final result is found to be a violation of the Accords, the Guild may impose the maximum penalty for "Deceptive Transmutation." The Guild's goal is to ensure that the complexity of a spell does not provide a loophole for the evasion of the Accords.

body.heading: § 1001.15 Layered Transfiguration Schemes
body.text:
A transaction utilizing multiple, sequentially applied transfigurations to obscure the true nature or value of goods constitutes a violation of this section. Whether the spells are cast contemporaneously or in succession is irrelevant; what matters is their combined effect on the item's provenance and worth. For example, an enchanted chest containing gold may be first wrapped in lead to prevent detection by divination magic, then covered in fur to mimic a beastskin pouch, and finally treated with illusion wards to appear empty upon inspection. Each layer serves to mask reality from prying eyes or magical scrutiny, rendering the scheme inherently deceptive under § 1001.7.

The Desk finds that such layered manipulations often indicate an attempt to evade existing prohibitions on specific magics or commodities. In one notable case, a merchant sought to smuggle restricted alchemical reagents by encasing them in lead-lined boxes coated with anti-scrying residue and disguised as mundane crates. The intent was clear: to bypass both physical searches and magical inspections simultaneously. This approach directly contravenes the spirit of § 300.2 regarding controlled substances, even if technically falling outside its literal scope.

Layered schemes also frequently arise in attempts to launder illicit gains through complex chains of ownership and transmutation. A criminal might first polymorph stolen artifacts into base materials, then recombine them using intricate enchantments that erase all traces of their origin. The end result is a seemingly ordinary object with no connection whatsoever to its unlawful source. Such obfuscation undermines the very purpose of financial reporting mandated by § 1001.7 and enables money laundering via magical means.

The burden rests on any party claiming good faith reliance on such schemes to prove beyond reasonable doubt that they had no knowledge of their deceptive nature. Given the sophisticated technology available in modern mages' guilds, ignorance is seldom an acceptable defense against charges of fraud or evasion. The Desk will presume guilt unless rebutted by compelling evidence of innocence or duress.

Ultimately, § 1001.15 exists to curb increasingly cunning attempts to game the system through arcane artifice. As magical technology advances, so too do methods of concealment and obfuscation. This provision ensures that no matter how elaborate the scheme becomes, it remains subject to scrutiny and sanction under the Accords. The Desk retains broad discretion to interpret what constitutes a "layered transfiguration" in light of evolving practices and precedents.

see § 1001.4 for guidance on illusion-based fraud; see § 1001.5 regarding material alteration of goods; see § 1001.7 for obligations of disclosure; see § 900.2 on reporting requirements for enchanted items. Violations of this section may result in sanctions up to and including permanent sealing under § 800.3, depending on circumstances.

body.heading: § 1001.15 Layered Transfiguration Schemes — Continued
body.text:
A "Layered Transfiguration Scheme" is defined herein as any sequence of spells or procedures wherein an initial alteration creates conditions that facilitate subsequent, more profound changes to the subject matter. Such schemes are deemed inherently deceptive and thus prohibited under this section. The prohibition extends not only to the final result but also to every intermediate step employed to achieve it.

For example, a caster who first uses a minor illusion spell to conceal the true nature of an item, then employs a more powerful enchantment to permanently alter its properties, has engaged in a Layered Transfiguration Scheme even though each individual spell might otherwise be legal. The scheme lies in the deliberate ordering of operations designed to circumvent detection and regulation.

The burden of proof rests upon the Accuser to demonstrate that the accused utilized multiple steps with the intent of evading oversight. This may include testimony from witnesses, analysis of magical residue, or reconstruction of events based on available evidence. Mere suspicion is insufficient for conviction; however, a preponderance of circumstantial indicators will suffice given the clandestine nature of such activities.
