If a mage purchases a map of a restricted zone, they are still bound by the same restrictions as any other unaffiliated traveler. To obtain a license to raid or perform research in such areas, the mage must petition the Innovators for a research grant or the Conservators for a stability clearance, depending on the nature of the activity. A map is a map; it is not a key, a shield, or a license. Any attempt to conflate the two in a legal defense shall be dismissed by the Accords Desk without prejudice.

body.heading: § 1201.1 Transit Stamps and Planar Tolls; Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet C
body.text:
Any spellcaster who casts an arcane effect outside the physical bounds of their Hall must affix a valid Transit Stamp to all materials involved, including reagents, tools, or even bodily fluids if magically contaminated. Failure to do so constitutes a Class C misdemeanor subject to fine and suspension under § 200.4. Planar Tolls apply when casting across dimensional thresholds; the caster must pay the appropriate fee to the Halls of Origin and Destination before proceeding. These fees fund infrastructure maintenance and offset liability for collateral damage, as outlined in § 100.7.

Casting into a Diet Chamber without prior authorization is prohibited except under emergency circumstances defined by local law enforcement. Such unauthorized intrusion may be treated as trespassing or even assault depending on the severity of consequences inflicted upon occupants. Any damages caused shall be pursued through civil litigation per standard procedures outlined in § 100.6. Cartography sold by recognized mapping firms includes only navigational data; it does not convey rights to raid uncharted regions under its cover. Unauthorized exploration beyond marked boundaries remains subject to arrest and prosecution under §§ 200.3–4.

Archie Miser's invoices bearing provisional passes are not a defense against charges of unauthorized field casting. Such documents merely indicate temporary permission granted pending further review; they do not absolve the caster of ongoing compliance obligations outlined herein. All disputes regarding valid credentials must be resolved through formal grievance processes administered by the Autumnwood Accords Desk, not private settlements outside official channels.

See also §§ 100.7 (Foreign Halls and Courtesy), 200.3–4 (Suspension and Lapse); § 300.5 (Research Copies of Quiet Items) for related provisions governing inter-jurisdictional magical activity and liability allocation.

body.heading: § 1201.1 Transit Stamps and Planar Tolls; Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet C — Continued
body.text:
§ 1201.1 Transit Stamps and Planar Tolls. Any mage casting an arcane effect across a planar boundary without prior approval shall pay the applicable toll to the Hall of Origin or Destination, whichever imposes the greater fee. Failure to remit said toll within thirty days constitutes a misdemeanor under § 800.1(A)(2). The Desk reserves the right to audit all transit records and impose surcharges for detected discrepancies. Planar instability resulting from unauthorized crossings shall be remedied at the offender's expense. See also § 300.5 (research copies of quiet items), § 900.1(duty to file before casting), and § 400.2(pocket dimensions as labs).

§ 1201.1 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber. A caster who intentionally projects an effect into the interior of another's dwelling without permission shall be deemed to have violated that dwelling owner's rights under common law and the Accords alike. Such acts are punishable by fine or imprisonment at the discretion of the presiding judge. Exceptions apply for emergency situations where immediate action is necessary to prevent loss of life or limb. Proof of intent may be inferred from circumstantial evidence including proximity, timing, and prior warnings issued by the Desk. Reference § 100.6(delegation to clerks), § 700.5(clone as duplicate claimant), and § 200.4(suspension and lapse).

This section governs the extraterritorial application of magical effects, particularly those occurring within private dwellings. The Desk maintains strict jurisdiction over such matters to protect individual privacy and property rights. Casters must exercise due diligence when projecting spells beyond their immediate vicinity to avoid legal repercussions. Violations will be prosecuted with severity commensurate with the harm caused. See further § 100.5(conflict of interest in casting), § 900.2(reporting of material enchantments), and § 300.1(schedules of arts).

sections.title: Planar Tolls
sections.brief: Evasion. Corridor courtesy.

body.heading: Planar Tolls
body.text:
Evasion. Corridor courtesy.

Pursuant to the jurisdictional oversight established under the Autumnwood Accords, all mages who facilitate the transit of sentient beings, goods, or essence across planar boundaries shall be held strictly liable for the payment of designated Planar Tolls. The Accords Desk maintains that the stabilization of the Midlands’ local reality necessitates a standardized taxation of inter-planar flux. Any mage who utilizes a rift, gateway, or dimensional fold to bypass these established checkpoints shall be deemed in violation of the Accord. Such evasion is categorized as a breach of corridor courtesy, as it places an undue burden on the structural integrity of the local weave and risks the degradation of the surrounding geography. All transit fees are to be calculated by the volume of mana displaced and the duration of the aperture maintained.

Mages seeking to move assets across planes must consult the current schedules maintained by the Accords Desk. Failure to declare a planned transit prior to activation may result in the immediate seizure of the traveling assets by the Aegis Magi. Furthermore, any mage who intentionally obscures the nature of their cargo to circumvent toll assessment shall face a formal inquiry. The Accords Desk emphasizes that "corridor courtesy" is not merely a social suggestion but a legal requirement for the continued stability of the Midlands. Mages who refuse to acknowledge the necessity of these tolls are viewed as contributing to the entropy of the realm. See § 1.2 for the overarching authority of the Accords Desk in matters of inter-planar regulation.

Regarding the physical maintenance of transit points, any mage who creates a temporary rift or gateway is responsible for the immediate stabilization of the exit point. If a gateway results in structural damage to the local environment—be it cracked stone, scorched earth, or lingering arcane radiation—the initiating mage is liable for all repair costs. This includes the hiring of Goodstyle Artisans for physical reconstruction if the damage exceeds minor surface abrasions. If the exit point is located within a public thoroughfare, the mage must ensure that no debris or residual mana lingers for more than one standard hour. Failure to clear the "corridor" of magical residue is a violation of local ordinances and shall be prosecuted as a public nuisance.

In instances where a planar toll cannot be paid due to the immediate threat of a predatory entity or an imminent collapse of the rift, a "Force Majeure" petition must be filed with the Accords Desk within three days of the event. Until such a petition is granted, the mage remains liable for the full toll. The Accords Desk reserves the right to levy additional penalties for any mage who repeatedly utilizes "emergency" exemptions to avoid their fiscal obligations to the Guild. For further details on the classification of planar entities and their associated toll rates, see § 1201.1.

body.heading: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
body.text:
Do not. File a letter instead.

The Autumnwood Accords strictly prohibit the direct casting of offensive, transformative, or high-variance magic into any designated "Diet Chamber" or sanctuary of sustenance. A Diet Chamber is defined as any consecrated or secular space dedicated to the preparation, storage, or consumption of food and drink, where the sanctity of the meal is protected from arcane interference. This prohibition is absolute and applies regardless of the location of the casting. A mage who casts a spell into such a chamber—whether for the purpose of preservation, flavor enhancement, or hostile disruption—shall be subject to immediate sanctions under the Paradox Trial. The Guild recognizes that the integrity of sustenance is a fundamental pillar of civil stability; to corrupt a meal is to corrupt the social fabric of the Midlands.

Mages who find it necessary to alter the properties of food or drink through arcane means must do so via the approved "Sanctified Modification" process. This process requires the mage to submit a formal request to the Accords Desk for a specific permit. Once the permit is granted, the mage may proceed with the modification, provided they do not exceed the parameters outlined in the approved petition. If a mage believes that a Diet Chamber requires a permanent arcane enhancement, they are strictly forbidden from casting such a spell directly into the chamber. Instead, the mage shall draft and file a formal letter of intent with the Accords Desk, detailing the desired outcome, the safety measures to be employed, and the intended duration of the effect.

The filing of a letter of intent allows the Conservators and Innovators to review the proposed magic for potential risks to the local weave and the safety of the consumers. If the request is denied, the mage must seek an alternative method of modification that does not involve direct casting into the sanctuary. Any mage caught casting into a Diet Chamber without a filed letter and a corresponding permit shall be apprehended by the Aegis Magi. The penalty for such an act shall be determined by the severity of the contamination; minor alterations may result in a fine, while the corruption of a communal feast or the poisoning of a public well may result in a full Seal of Silence or a transition to a pocket-prison.

Furthermore, this regulation extends to the "flavoring" of beverages with ephemeral magic. While the Innovators may argue for the creative freedom of such arts, the Conservators maintain that the unpredictable nature of such magic can lead to unintended physiological consequences for the consumer. Therefore, all "flavor-casting" must be documented and the ingredients of the magic must be disclosed to the Guild. Mages who refuse to file the necessary paperwork for their culinary enchantments are considered to be acting in bad faith against the Accords. For guidance on the submission of formal letters to the Desk, see § 900.1.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
One-T mountain. A map is a map. It is not a permit.

The Accords Desk hereby clarifies the legal distinction between the acquisition of geographical data and the authorization of martial action. It is a frequent point of contention among the Innovators that the possession of a detailed map of a restricted area, such as the One-T mountain or other contested territories, constitutes a tacit permission to explore or occupy said region. This is a legal fallacy. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a map is merely a record of topographical and arcane data; it confers no rights of passage, no license to harvest resources, and no permit to engage in hostile action. A mage who purchases or commissions a map of a restricted zone is merely acquiring information. The use of that information to bypass Guild-sanctioned boundaries or to initiate a raid is a separate and punishable offense.

Mages who intend to enter restricted territories for the purpose of research, trade, or exploration must secure a formal "Field Expedition Permit" from the Accords Desk. This permit must be filed well in advance and must specify the duration of the stay, the number of participants, and the intended scope of activity. The possession of a map, even a high-fidelity one provided by a Goodstyle Artisan, does not exempt the mage from this requirement. Should a mage be intercepted by the Aegis Magi while in a restricted zone, the mere possession of a map shall not serve as a defense. The mage must produce a valid, stamped Expedition Permit to avoid immediate detention and potential referral to a Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, the sale of maps that include "tactical notations"—such as identified weak points in defenses, hidden ingress points, or unguarded resource deposits—is strictly regulated. Such maps are classified as "Sensitive Intelligence" and may only be sold to Guild-affiliated entities with the express permission of Archmage Veyra. Any third party caught selling such maps to non-Guild actors, including the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, shall be prosecuted for espionage. The Accords Desk reminds all mages that while knowledge is power, the unauthorized application of that knowledge in a manner that threatens the stability of the Midlands is a breach of the Accord.

In the event that a mage discovers a new geographical feature or a previously unmapped rift during a sanctioned expedition, they are required to report these findings to the Accords Desk within forty-eight hours. Failure to report new data, or the deliberate withholding of such information for private gain, is a violation of the Guild's data-sharing protocols. A map is a tool for navigation; a permit is a tool for legality. The two are not interchangeable. Mages who attempt to use the "I only had a map" defense during a seizure of assets shall be subject to the maximum fines as outlined in § 1001.4. For information on obtaining a Field Expedition Permit, see § 900.2.

body.heading: § 1201.2 Planar Tolls and Extraterritorial Casting
body.text:
It is hereby declared that any casting directed at or through a Diet Chamber, regardless of the caster's physical location, shall be deemed an extraterritorial act subject to this Accords Desk's full jurisdiction. The presence of a Channeling Arc in the target zone establishes sufficient nexus for regulation and enforcement. See § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments.

Cartographic works depicting planar topography, particularly those revealing ingress points or resource nodes, are classified as strategic secrets under § 300.4 Reclassification procedures. The unauthorized sale or distribution of such maps constitutes a felony offense punishable by permanent license revocation and imprisonment in the Pocket Prison. Under § 1201.5 Penalties for Strategic Espionage.

Diet Chambers themselves shall be registered with this Desk upon establishment, disclosing their location, purpose, and intended frequency of use. Failure to register may result in immediate seizure and destruction of the facility as contrabon. See § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill.

All casters are reminded that their actions extend beyond mere spell effects, encompassing the broader consequences thereof. A well-intentioned ritual performed in ignorance of local laws may still incur liability for resulting damages or disruptions. Counsel is available at no cost to clarify obligations and responsibilities under these provisions. Refer to § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; § 500.1 Field Casting for Value.

This Section shall be cited as the Planar Tolls Provision in all future proceedings involving extraterritorial casting or related activities. Any ambiguities herein shall be resolved by reference to the spirit and intent of these Accords, not a literalist interpretation that undermines their efficacy. See § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy; § 800.2 Paradox Trial Procedure.

The Desk reserves the right to investigate any suspected violations proactively without prior notice or warrant. Cooperation is mandatory unless specific protections apply under established legal frameworks. Refusal may result in escalated penalties including asset seizure and criminal charges. Consult § 100.1 Licensure Required; § 700.5 Administrative Detention Powers.

It is the goal of this regulation to balance individual freedoms with collective safety, ensuring that magical practices enhance rather than endanger our society. Through diligent enforcement and education, we shall maintain order amidst innovation for generations to come. As always: abide by the law or face the consequences accordingly."

body.heading: § 1201.2 Planar Tolls and Extraterritorial Casting — Continued
body.text: No casting shall occur within the jurisdictional limits of another Hall without prior written consent, under penalty of immediate arrest for unauthorized practice. This prohibition extends to all forms of transdimensional projection, including but not limited to planar travel, pocket-space manipulation, and spell-based teleportation. Violators shall be subject to full investigation and prosecution per § 800.1 et seq., with fines set at twice the estimated value of any illicit magical effects produced. The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to establish that the accused knowingly entered a restricted zone for the purpose of casting. Defense by accident or ignorance is not valid unless corroborated by witness testimony or official records. Exceptions may be granted only via special permit issued by the Archmage Sovereign, subject to strict oversight and reporting requirements. All permits must specify exact coordinates, duration, and intended uses, with failure to adhere to terms constituting breach of contract and grounds for revocation. Penalties escalate based on severity and repetition, ranging from suspension of license to permanent expulsion from the Guild. Repeat offenders face additional sanctions including mandatory rehabilitation courses and public shaming via the Quiet List. The Desk retains sole discretion to waive penalties in cases of genuine emergency or force majeure, provided full disclosure is made within forty-eight hours of the event. Refusal to comply with these regulations shall be deemed a serious felony offense under the Accords, warranting expedited trial and maximum punishment. The Guild maintains an active surveillance network to detect and deter illegal planar activity, employing both technological means and human informants. Any suspected violator may be intercepted at any time, regardless of location or claimed immunity, for immediate search and seizure proceedings. Failure to submit to lawful detention shall result in escalation of charges and imposition of harsher penalties upon conviction. The provisions herein are designed to protect the integrity of inter-Hall relations and prevent unintended consequences arising from unregulated dimensional interference. All parties agree that compliance with these rules is essential to maintaining peace and order within the broader magical community. Violation of this section shall be treated as a direct affront to the authority of the Autumnwood Accords, inviting swift and severe retribution. The Desk reserves the right to amend or expand upon these guidelines at its sole discretion, without prior notice or consultation. Refusal to abide by updated regulations shall constitute grounds for immediate disciplinary action up to and including expulsion from membership in perpetuity. Ultimately, adherence to these strictures is non-negotiable for all licensed practitioners operating within Guild jurisdiction. Failure to comply will not be tolerated under any circumstances whatsoever. The Accords stand absolute, binding all signatories regardless of status or influence. Any attempt to circumvent or undermine this provision shall be met with utmost severity, ensuring the continued dominance and prestige of the Autumnwood Hall in the magical world at large.

body.heading: § 1201.2 Planar Tolls and Extraterritorial Casting — Continued: Jurisdictional R
body.text:
The provisions herein govern the conduct of magicians who effect translocations beyond recognized boundaries, whether by intentional projection or inadvertent slip. Such acts constitute a form of extraterritorial casting that triggers unique legal considerations under § 1201.1(a)(ii). When an individual leaves the physical plane without proper authorization, they subject themselves to the full force of the Autumnwood Accords upon re-entry, regardless of prior location at time of departure. This principle applies equally to temporary excursions and permanent departures.

Any caster found guilty of unlicensed planar travel faces immediate suspension under § 200.4 until completion of mandatory re-certification courses covering cross-dimensional safety protocols and jurisdictional compliance. Repeat offenders may be subject to revocation of magical licensure entirely per § 800.1(c). Furthermore, all artifacts acquired during unauthorized excursions must undergo rigorous inspection before release back into lawful commerce, with associated fees assessed pursuant to § 900.4(b)(viii).

The Desk retains broad discretion to impose additional sanctions deemed necessary for public protection and regulatory integrity, within the limits set forth in § 100.6(d)(ii) regarding delegated authority. Failure to comply fully with these requirements constitutes a Class B infraction punishable by fine up to one thousand gold pieces or imprisonment not exceeding six months at Archmage's Discretion per § 800.1(e)(iii).

It is hereby declared that all clauses contained in this section shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding any contrary provisions existing under other statutes or local ordinances which may conflict therewith, by virtue of the superior standing accorded to these binding accords throughout the entire realm. Any attempts to circumvent these regulations through subterfuge or technicality will be met with swift and severe consequences as determined solely by the Council's judgment in each case upon review of all pertinent facts presented at hearing.

see § 1201.1 for foundational definitions regarding planar boundaries and unauthorized translocation; under § 800.1(c) concerning suspension procedures and re-certification requirements applicable to violators; reference also § 900.4(b)(viii) relating to artifact inspection protocols and fee assessments imposed upon recovered items seized during enforcement actions initiated pursuant hereto. All persons subject to the jurisdiction of this Code are hereby put on formal notice that continued operation outside established parameters shall result in graduated penalties escalating with each subsequent offense until ultimate compliance is achieved or punitive measures rendered permanent as circumstances dictate by the presiding authority acting within its statutory mandate.

sections.title: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
sections.brief: Do not. File a letter instead.

body.heading: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
body.text:
Any practitioner of the arcane who intends to project, manifest, or otherwise exert magical influence upon a designated Diet Chamber—defined as a consecrated space for the consumption of sustenance by non-magical entities or for the communal nourishment of those under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords—is strictly prohibited from performing such actions if the target chamber exists outside the immediate terrestrial boundaries of the Midlands. This prohibition is absolute and applies to all schools of magic, including but not limited to transmutation of food, telekinetic delivery of beverages, or any atmospheric manipulation intended to enhance the olfactory profile of a meal. The Guild recognizes that while the logistical needs of travelers and diplomats are significant, the risk of cross-planar contamination, unintended caloric inflation, or the disruption of local culinary sanctity outweighs any perceived convenience of such remote casting.

Furthermore, any mage found in violation of this clause shall be subject to immediate review by the Aegis Magi. The intent of the caster is irrelevant; the mere act of reaching across a jurisdictional boundary to influence a dining environment constitutes a breach of the Accords. This is particularly relevant when dealing with the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, as their culinary standards are considered sovereign and their reactions to unsolicited magical intervention are often hostile. Mages seeking to provide logistical support to allies, such as the Goodstyle Artisans, must ensure that all such services are performed within the physical vicinity of the recipient. If a request for remote nourishment arises, the mage shall not utilize arcana to bridge the distance.

In instances where a mage feels compelled to provide sustenance to a party in a remote location, they are hereby commanded to forgo all magical intervention and instead utilize traditional courier methods. See § 1201.1 regarding transit stamps for such couriers. If the distance is prohibitive for physical transit, the mage may instead draft a formal letter of intent and request that the local authorities or the host party arrange for local procurement. This letter must be filed with the Accords Desk and bear the official seal of the caster’s faction, be it Conservator or Innovator. No exceptions shall be granted for "emergency" hunger, provided the emergency was not caused by the mage's own failure to plan for sufficient supplies. Failure to comply with this directive will result in a referral to the Paradox Trial for review of the caster's stability.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
The production, sale, and distribution of topographical records, hereafter referred to as Cartography, are governed by the principles of objective observation. It is strictly forbidden for any Cartographer, Merchant, or Mage to represent a map of a geographical feature—specifically the One-T mountain range or any similar landmark—as a license, permit, or authorization to engage in "raiding," "looting," or "resource extraction." A map is a tool of navigation and spatial awareness; it confers no legal right to the contents of the terrain it depicts. Any individual attempting to sell a map with the express intent of implying it grants the bearer permission to bypass local defenses or enter restricted zones is committing a felony of Deception under the Accords.

The Guild finds that the "One-T mountain" has been the subject of frequent confusion regarding its status. While the map of the mountain is a public utility for those seeking to traverse the Midlands, the mountain itself remains subject to the laws of the presiding sovereign or the territorial claims of the dominant faction. The presence of a map in a traveler's possession does not mitigate the penalties associated with trespassing or the unauthorized seizure of materials. If a mage or adventurer intends to conduct a raid, they must secure a formal Raid License from the appropriate regional authority. A map is not a substitute for a license, and the sale of a map as such shall be treated as a fraudulent transaction, subject to the penalties outlined in § 1001.1.

Furthermore, the Cartography Department of the Accords Desk warns that the sale of "Tactical Maps" which include notations on "weak points" or "unprotected entrances" does not exempt the buyer from the consequences of an assault. Such notations are considered descriptive, not permissive. If a mage is caught utilizing a map to conduct an unauthorized raid, the map itself may be seized as evidence of premeditation. Practitioners of the Innovator faction are specifically cautioned against creating "dynamic maps" that update in real-time to show the movements of guards or the location of hidden caches, as these may be classified as forbidden surveillance tools. For all matters regarding the legal acquisition of land or the right to harvest resources, mages must consult the proper civic channels rather than relying on the mere possession of a parchment.

body.heading: § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; Cartography Sold as a Lic
body.text:
No mage shall cast within the confines of an Autumn Wood Diet Chamber unless expressly invited by the presiding Archmage or her duly appointed substitute, nor shall any such casting extend beyond the immediate physical boundaries thereof without prior written consent. Violation of this provision constitutes both a breach of protocol and a potential act of war against the Guild itself, subject to immediate expulsion from the premises and subsequent penal proceedings under § 800 et seq.

It is further deemed unlawful for any individual or entity to market, distribute, or otherwise disseminate cartographic representations of protected lands, territories, or strategic locations without explicit authorization from the Autumn Wood Council. Such maps, whether drawn by hand or conjured through magical means, shall be treated as contraband upon discovery and subject to seizure under § 1201.5. Unauthorized possession or use of such materials may result in severe penalties, including permanent revocation of licensure and imprisonment for up to one hundred years without benefit of parole.

The sale or exchange of cartographic data shall be strictly regulated by the Autumn Wood Office of Geospatial Intelligence, which maintains a centralized registry of all approved maps and related documentation. Any entity seeking access to such information must submit a formal application accompanied by proof of need, security clearance, and indemnification against misuse. Failure to comply with these requirements shall constitute grounds for immediate suspension of privileges and possible criminal charges under applicable statutes.

It is hereby declared null and void any contract or agreement purporting to grant rights of entry, transit, or operation within the exclusive jurisdiction of an Autumn Wood Diet Chamber unless executed in accordance with this section. Such instruments shall be deemed unenforceable at law and subject to invalidation upon application by the Guild or its authorized representatives. Any party found guilty of violating this provision shall forfeit all claims thereto and be liable for damages arising therefrom, including but not limited to legal fees, court costs, and punitive assessments as determined in the sole discretion of the presiding magistrate.

This section shall take effect immediately upon final approval by the Autumn Wood Council and publication herein. Any existing arrangements inconsistent with these provisions are hereby superseded and void ab initio. All persons having an interest in matters governed thereby are directed to consult this section carefully before proceeding further, lest they incur grievous consequences for their ignorance thereof.

body.heading: § 1201.4 Unauthorized Titan Growth and Rift Expansion
body.text: It is hereby declared that any deliberate or negligent act resulting in the unauthorized expansion of rifts, portals, or planar anomalies shall constitute a Class A violation under these Accords. This includes but is not limited to: (a) casting spells designed to enlarge existing breaches; (b) neglecting maintenance duties required by one's license agreement; and (c) failing to report suspected instabilities within twenty-four hours of discovery. Such infractions may result in immediate suspension of all magical privileges, revocation of licensure without compensation, and imprisonment for up to five years at the discretion of the Consistory. Furthermore, any individual found guilty of this offense shall be held jointly and severally liable for all damages arising from said expansion, including but not limited to property destruction, loss of life or limb, and environmental contamination by raw arcane energy." "The Conservators argue that unchecked growth poses an existential threat to reality itself, citing the catastrophic events of the Last Conflagration as proof positive. Innovators counter that such fears are unfounded so long as regulations are followed, pointing to decades of safe operation under current statutes. The Archmage Sovereign remains neutral on this matter, deferring judgment until further study can be conducted." "In any event, all parties are reminded that the Accords exist for the protection and ordering of society—not merely the convenience of powerful individuals seeking unfettered access to forbidden arts. Those who would undermine these fundamental principles do so at their own peril, risking not only their freedom but perhaps their very souls in the process." "The undersigned hereby certify that this section was duly read, debated, and approved by a majority vote of the Mages' Guild Consistory on this 17th day of Autumnwood, in the year of our Lord two thousand and twenty-three." "[Seal of Archmage Veyra]" "[Signature of Archmage Theron]" "[Signature of Janna Brightspark]" "[Witnessed by Two Credible Witnesses]" "So let it be written, so shall it be done!" "For as long as magic shall endure..."

body.heading: § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; Cartography Sold as a Lic — Continued
body.text:
No mage shall cast spells beyond the borders of their Hall without express permission from the Archmage Sovereign and written authorization from the relevant sovereign state or governing body. Violation constitutes unauthorized field use under § 500.1 and subjecting the offender to immediate seizure and trial for breach of contract. The Desk retains sole discretion to approve or deny such requests based on necessity, risk assessment, and diplomatic considerations.

Cartographic products depicting magical phenomena, ley lines, rift locations, or other sensitive data shall not be sold, leased, or distributed without a full disclosure of their intended use and explicit consent from the original creator. Any attempt to market maps as "raid licenses" or "exploration permits" is hereby declared fraudulent misrepresentation under § 1001.2 and punishable by revocation of licensure and permanent disqualification from Guild activities. The sale of such items without proper labeling and warnings shall be deemed a Class A felony offense.

This section takes precedence over any conflicting provisions in private contracts or local ordinances. Archmage Veyra reserves the right to override her own decisions if new evidence emerges suggesting greater risk to public safety than initially assessed. Failure to comply with these rules constitutes grounds for disciplinary action up to and including permanent expulsion from the Guild and referral to law enforcement authorities.

The Desk encourages all members to report suspected violations promptly through established channels to ensure swift intervention before harm occurs. Anonymous tip lines are available via encrypted messaging apps and secure mailboxes located at each Hall entrance. Whistleblowers acting in good faith shall receive protection against retaliation under § 1002.3, though false accusations may result in punitive measures including fines and imprisonment.

It is the collective responsibility of every mage to uphold these standards for the greater good of society. By adhering strictly to the guidelines herein, we safeguard both ourselves and those around us from the dangers inherent in unchecked magical experimentation. Let this serve as a clarion call to renewed vigilance and mutual accountability among all practitioners within our sacred order.

SEE ALSO: § 500.1 Unauthorized Field Use; § 700.2 Diplomatic Immunity Exceptions; § 800.1 Jurisdictional Boundaries; § 900.4 Privacy Clauses in Contracts; § 1001.3 Fraudulent Misrepresentation Standards.

body.heading: § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; Cartography Sold as a Lic — Administration
body.text:
Any act of magical casting, whether for combat or utility purposes, that occurs within the jurisdictional bounds of a Diet Hall is subject to immediate seizure by Aegis Magi unless covered under an active Permit to Work. This includes any spell component, verbal utterance, somatic gesture, or mental projection originating from outside the Chamber but directed inwardly. See § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; § 500.1 Field Casting for Value.

Cartographic representations of contested territories, including those marked as "Restricted" or "No-Go," constitute actionable evidence of intent and preparation for unauthorized operation. Sale, distribution, or possession thereof without explicit written consent from the Archmage Sovereign is prohibited under penalty of confiscation and permanent revocation of licensure. Such maps are deemed integral to the planning of illicit expeditions and thus fall within the scope of § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time.

The expansion or unauthorized modification of existing rifts, portals, or planar anomalies shall require prior written authorization from the Guild's Planar Oversight Committee. Any such activity discovered without proper documentation will be treated as a Class A violation subject to full investigation and potential prosecution under § 800.1 Penalty for Unauthorized Arcane Operation. See also § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs; § 500.2 Unscheduled Magic in Public Spaces.

All mages are reminded that the Autumnwood Accords extend their authority beyond mere physical territory, encompassing all acts of magical expression that may impact public order or safety. Failure to comply with these provisions shall result in escalated sanctions up to and including suspension from practice indefinitely. The Desk retains sole discretion to interpret ambiguities arising under this section without recourse to external bodies. Under § 100.4 Records of Speech; § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse.

This provision was enacted following the widespread misuse of cartographic data during the recent Titan Incident, wherein several novice casters inadvertently triggered a catastrophic rift collapse by misinterpreting terrain markers on an improperly sourced map. The resulting devastation underscored the need for stricter controls over sensitive information bearing potential tactical value in conflict scenarios. Reference § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth; § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments.

By signing this Codex, each licensed practitioner acknowledges their full understanding and acceptance of these obligations as binding conditions precedent to continued operation within the Guild framework. Violations shall be addressed swiftly and severely in accordance with established procedure. The Desk reserves absolute authority to enforce compliance through any lawful means necessary to preserve public safety and maintain regulatory integrity. As stated in § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy: "No exceptions apply."

sections.title: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
sections.brief: One-T mountain. A map is a map. It is not a permit.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords, as mediated by Archmage Veyra, maintain a strict distinction between the acquisition of geographical knowledge and the authorization of hostile incursions. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that the possession of a map, regardless of its detail, historical depth, or the arcane means by which it was compiled, does not constitute a legal license for the seizure, pillaging, or tactical engagement within the designated territory. This distinction is particularly critical regarding the One-T mountain range, where historical precedents of unauthorized "treasure expeditions" have led to significant ecological and arcane destabilization. Any individual, entity, or guild-affiliated party found to be asserting that a purchased map grants them sovereign right of entry for the purpose of raiding shall be subject to immediate summary citation.

The Accords Desk hereby clarifies that cartography is a scholarly pursuit and a tool for navigation, not a instrument of martial permission. Under these statutes, a map serves only to define the physical boundaries of a landmass; it does not supersede the territorial rights of the local inhabitants, the sovereign claims of the regional powers, or the environmental preservation mandates established by the Conservators. Any entity attempting to use the purchase of a One-T mountain chart as a justification for bypassing the standard requisitioning process for exploration shall be deemed to be in violation of the peace. The presence of a map in one's possession shall not be admitted as evidence of "prior consent" from the land's overseers.

Furthermore, the Guild warns against the illicit sale of "Raid Licenses" disguised as topographical scrolls. Merchants or clandestine brokers who market maps with clauses implying permission to enter restricted zones, extract resources, or engage in combat are in direct violation of the Accords. Such sales are considered fraudulent and may lead to the seizure of the maps in question and the revocation of the seller's mercantile privileges. The Accords Desk recognizes that the One-T mountain range is a sensitive zone; therefore, any expeditionary force must secure a formal Permit of Incursion from the appropriate regional authority. A map is a representation of the world, not a key to its secrets.

Mages and explorers who rely on the "Cartographic Exemption"—the notion that a map provides a legal shield against charges of trespassing or looting—shall find such defenses void. If a party is apprehended within the One-T mountains without a valid, stamped Permit of Incursion, the mere production of a map shall not serve as a mitigating factor in their sentencing. The Aegis Magi are instructed to prioritize the apprehension of those who use "exploratory intent" as a veneer for unauthorized raiding. See § 1.2 for matters regarding the enacting authority of the Accords Desk. All parties seeking to survey the One-T range are reminded that one-T cartography is a map, not a raid license.

body.heading: § 1201.4 Cartography as Evidence, Not Authority
body.text:
A map or chart depicting terrain features, magical concentrations, or strategic advantages is merely documentary evidence and confers no rights upon its possessor. Under § 1201.3, only an official permit signed by the Sovereign grants authority to enter contested zones; a privately held cartographic reproduction does not substitute therefor. Courts consistently hold that possession of detailed maps alone cannot justify unauthorized incursions into restricted areas, regardless of their accuracy or specificity. See § 1200.5 regarding the presumption of innocence absent formal adjudication.

The Guild maintains that all intelligence gathering must proceed through lawful channels established by statute. While individuals may observe and record external phenomena consistent with general observation rights under § 130.2, covert operations requiring infiltration or deception fall outside these protections. Cartographic analysis remains a valid investigative tool when conducted openly, but it does not transform the holder into an agent of state power capable of overriding territorial sovereignty claims. This principle protects both citizen privacy and the integrity of official investigations alike.

Furthermore, the distribution of sensitive maps raises concerns regarding national security and public safety that exceed private property disputes. The Sovereign retains discretion to regulate access to such materials on a case-by-case basis, weighing potential harms against freedoms of information protected by other provisions. Unauthorized circulation may constitute contempt for obstructing lawful inquiry or revealing classified data under § 150.7. Parties found guilty of disseminating prohibited cartographic works face penalties up to and including permanent sealing of magical abilities per § 800.3(b).

Ultimately, the legal status of maps mirrors that of other informational assets covered by the Accords: they are subject to reasonable restrictions designed to prevent abuse while preserving legitimate interests in knowledge acquisition. Possession does not equal possession of power; rather, it represents a responsibility to use such information wisely and responsibly within bounds set forth by competent authority. Failure to recognize this distinction risks severe consequences ranging from civil liability to criminal prosecution under applicable statutes. All citizens are urged to consult official sources before acting upon unverified intelligence derived from commercial or personal mapping efforts.

"Under § 1201.3, only an official permit grants authority to enter contested zones; a privately held cartographic reproduction does not substitute therefor."
"Unauthorized circulation may constitute contempt for obstructing lawful inquiry or revealing classified data under § 150.7."
"The Sovereign retains discretion to regulate access to such materials on a case-by-case basis..."
"Citizens are urged to consult official sources before acting upon unverified intelligence derived from commercial mapping efforts."

body.heading: § 1201.4 Cartography as Evidence, Not Authority — Continued
body.text:
A map constitutes documentary evidence only; it confers no rights or privileges by its mere possession. The acquisition or sale of cartographic representations, including those marked with restricted zones or tactical notations, shall be treated as the transfer of informational assets subject to standard commercial regulations. No individual may invoke ownership of a planar chart to justify unauthorized entry into sovereign space or violation of local ordinances. Violators face penalties under §§ 1201.3 and 800.6 for trespass and reckless magical exposure respectively.

The Guild Desk shall retain exclusive authority to interpret spatial data within its jurisdiction. Disputes regarding the accuracy, scope, or validity of any mapping product must be adjudicated by appointed magistrates empowered with technical expertise in surveying and dimensional geometry. Until such official review is complete, all parties are directed to suspend operations pending resolution. Failure to comply may result in injunctions pursuant to § 601.2 and temporary suspension of magical licensure per § 200.4(b).

This provision does not impede lawful research or educational use of cartographic materials obtained through proper channels under §§ 300.5 and 900.2(c). Institutions maintaining bona fide academic programs may request copies from the Desk subject to nondisclosure agreements and usage restrictions outlined in Appendix G. All requests must be submitted on official letterhead with proof of institutional standing and faculty credentials attached.

Cartographic fraud remains a serious offense under this Article and related statutes. The intentional falsification, alteration, or misrepresentation of spatial information for illicit purposes shall constitute grand larceny enhanced by magical endangerment per § 1003.7(c). Convicted offenders face imprisonment up to ten years plus mandatory sealing of all magical abilities via § 800.3(a)(ii). Recidivists are subject to permanent disenfranchisement and exile from the Guild territories without recourse.

Nothing herein shall be construed to diminish existing treaty obligations between member nations regarding shared borders, resource rights, or defense pacts. Diplomatic agreements supersede conflicting provisions in this Code unless explicitly amended by unanimous vote of the Hall under § 201.5. The Desk maintains a register of all international accords affecting planar geography for reference purposes only; consultation is available upon request to accredited representatives.

This Section shall take effect immediately upon filing and remains in force indefinitely unless repealed or substantially revised by subsequent legislation passed through proper channels. Any ambiguities arising from its implementation shall be resolved in favor of public safety and equitable treatment of all parties involved. The Guild reserves the right to issue clarifying guidance memos as needed without altering the substantive text. Compliance with this directive is mandatory for all licensed practitioners operating within Autumnwood Accords territory.

see §§ 1201.3, 800.6; under § 900.2(c); per Appendix G and § 201.5; pursuant to § 1003.7(c) and § 800.3(a)(ii).

body.heading: § 1201.4 Cartography as Evidence, Not Authority — Continued — Continued
body.text:
Whereas the One-T Mountain map constitutes an expression of cartographic opinion and artistic license rather than a binding legal instrument, it remains admissible evidence in proceedings concerning territorial disputes or unauthorized field use under §§ 500.3 and 901.2. The Guild shall weigh such representations alongside other admissible facts, including witness testimony, physical inspection of terrain features, and official survey records maintained by the Conservators. No single document, however compelling its visual presentation may appear to the untrained eye, shall be deemed conclusive proof of ownership or right-of-way without corroboration from multiple independent sources. This rule serves to prevent frivolous claims based solely upon speculative depictions while preserving the integrity of sworn statements and verified data. Violations of this provision shall be treated as contempt of court and subject to sanctions pursuant to § 1502.1(e).

The Desk further notes that any party relying on the One-T map for purposes beyond mere reference must first obtain explicit authorization from the appropriate authorities in accordance with established protocols set forth in §§ 700.4 through 700.6. Failure to secure such permission prior to engaging in activities within the mapped area shall constitute a breach of contract and potentially expose the offending entity to liability for damages arising therefrom. The Guild retains sole discretion to determine whether any given action constitutes "unauthorized field use" under § 500.3, with final adjudication resting with the High Council convened by Archmage Veyra upon referral from the local Magistrate. All determinations shall be made in accordance with applicable laws and regulations governing magical research and exploration practices within the Accords jurisdiction. Any disputes regarding interpretation of this clause shall be resolved through binding arbitration administered by a panel of retired Conservators appointed jointly by the Innovator faction leadership and the Aegis Magi Order.

It is hereby declared that the One-T Mountain map, in whatever form it may exist—whether as digitized file, printed publication, or oral tradition—is neither a deed nor a leasehold instrument but rather an informational resource intended to aid navigators familiar with planar geography. Parties seeking title or usage rights must pursue such interests through proper channels and under the supervision of duly licensed appraisers accredited by the Guild's Certification Board. Unauthorized possession or distribution of classified survey data shall be prosecuted as theft of government secrets pursuant to Title 18, Chapter 37 of the United States Code, with penalties enhanced where magical components are involved. The Desk warns that attempts to exploit ambiguities in cartographic notation for illicit gain will meet with swift and severe consequences, including revocation of operating licenses and permanent expulsion from the professional ranks of Arcane Practitioners recognized by this Accord. Let all who read these words take heed: knowledge carries great responsibility, and misuse thereof brings retribution sure as winter's frost. So let it be written in stone and sealed with blood oath!

body.heading: Cartography as Evidence, Not Authority — Continued
body.text:
The mere possession or distribution of a detailed map of the One-T does not constitute proof of intent to raid or breach any laws under this Code. Maps are commercial products that may be traded freely between private parties without implicating criminal liability absent additional facts indicating unlawful purpose. To convict an individual solely on grounds that they owned or viewed such cartographic material would violate fundamental principles of fair notice and proportionality enshrined in §§ 1.4–1.5 and 700.1(b).

However, where a map is coupled with other incriminating circumstances—such as purchase from known raiders, modification to include secret passages or guard rotations, or possession alongside stolen goods—it may serve as corroborating evidence of guilty knowledge under the totality-of-the-circumstances test prescribed in § 700.2. In such cases, the map becomes a material link in establishing the nexus between defendant and planned violation rather than standing alone as proof beyond reasonable doubt. Courts retain full discretion to weigh its probative value against potential prejudice pursuant to standard evidentiary rules codified at §§ 601–605.

No individual shall be held criminally liable for merely owning or displaying a map of the One-T region absent clear evidence of further incriminating conduct. Absent such proof, maps remain innocuous artifacts subject only to ordinary contract law governing their sale and transfer between consenting adults. This principle reflects our enduring commitment to presumption of innocence and avoidance of overbreadth in penal statutes—a cornerstone of just governance under §§ 10–12 and 700.3(a).

It shall be unlawful for any person knowingly to distribute maps of the One-T specifically designed to facilitate unauthorized expeditions therein, where such distribution is intended to further illegal ends. Such conduct may constitute aiding and abetting under § 502 when paired with substantive involvement in planning or executing a raid. Mere possession remains innocent unless accompanied by overt acts demonstrating criminal intent beyond a reasonable doubt as required by our shared legal traditions enshrined in §§ 10–12 and 700.3(b).

This provision shall be construed narrowly to avoid chilling legitimate cartographic study, tourism planning, or artistic expression involving the One-T region. Broad application could impermissibly infringe upon freedoms of speech, association, and movement guaranteed herein and under broader constitutional protections referenced in § 15. Courts must balance enforcement interests against these foundational liberties when adjudicating disputes arising hereunder consistent with our enduring commitment to due process as outlined in §§ 20–22 and 700.4(c).

See also §§ 300.1 (Schedules of Arts), 700.2 (Corroborating Evidence Standards), and 900.5 (Record Retention Requirements) for related provisions governing classification, proof, and documentation obligations within the Guild framework. This section stands as a critical safeguard against misuse of mapping technology while preserving lawful inquiry into one of the most treacherous regions known to humankind under our shared constitutional values referenced in § 15.

*Archmage's Note: Clarity is paramount here lest we inadvertently criminalize harmless curiosity or artistic endeavor. Let us remain vigilant guardians of both public safety and civil liberties alike.*

body.heading: § 1201.4 Cartography as Evidence, Not Authority — Continued — Administration
body.text:
The mere existence of a detailed map does not confer upon its holder the right to traverse or exploit the regions it depicts. Under § 1201.3, all planar transit requires specific tolls and stamps issued by the appropriate authority; no private document can supersede these statutory requirements. A cartographic artifact remains evidence of prior passage rather than a license for future intrusion. Any attempt to utilize such maps as a pretext for unauthorized access constitutes trespass under § 200.1 and may result in immediate suspension of the holder's licensure.

Furthermore, the Guild maintains that all publicly available plans are intended solely for educational purposes and risk assessment. They do not imply permission to engage in hazardous activities within mapped territories without explicit consent from local magistrates or landowners. Violation of this principle shall be treated as a Class A misdemeanor punishable by fines up to one hundred gold crowns and community service equivalent to ten standard workweeks. Repeat offenders face harsher penalties including permanent revocation of their arcane credentials.

It is the responsibility of every licensed mage to verify current regulations before entering unfamiliar zones, regardless of what previous records may suggest. Reliance on outdated or incomplete maps shall not excuse non-compliance with existing laws nor mitigate liability for resulting damages. The Desk retains sole discretion to modify access protocols based on emerging threats or security concerns unrelated to any individual's possession of cartographic materials.

In sum, the holding in § 1201.3 stands firm: no piece of paper grants carte blanche to explore dangerous frontiers recklessly. Mages must exercise due diligence and respect for established boundaries at all times. Failure to do so invites swift and severe consequences under this Code and those of higher precedence. Let none presume authority where none exists, lest they find themselves bound by chains far heavier than any spellbook page could contain.

sections.title: Schedule of Fees
sections.brief: Named amounts in Guild marks. No Wario Coin.

body.heading: Schedule of Fees
body.text:
The Guild shall maintain a definitive schedule of fees for all administrative, investigative, and regulatory actions performed by the Accords Desk. These fees are established to ensure the continued maintenance of the Autumnwood infrastructure and to compensate the Guild for the oversight of arcane stability. All fees must be rendered in standard Guild marks. The Guild hereby declares that any currency of irregular origin, including but not limited to the Wario Coin, is not a valid tender for the settlement of debts, fines, or administrative costs. Any attempt to utilize non-standard coinage in the settlement of a Guild fee shall result in the immediate rejection of the tender and the assessment of a secondary "Invalid Tender" surcharge as dictated by the current fiscal year's guidelines.

Fees are categorized by the severity of the violation and the complexity of the requested service. Administrative services, such as the filing of a Provisional Guild Pass or the registration of a new cartographic survey, are subject to a fixed entry fee. Investigative services, including the surveying of a Heartstone or the verification of a rift's boundaries, are billed at a rate commensurate with the risk of planar instability. All fees are non-refundable once the Accords Desk has initiated the requested procedure. See § 1301.1.

The Guild reserves the right to adjust the Schedule of Fees with a notice period of no less than three lunar cycles. Such adjustments shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra to ensure that the balance between Conservator traditionalism and Innovator expansionism is maintained in the economic health of the Guild. No individual mage, regardless of rank or factional standing, is exempt from these fees unless a formal waiver is granted by the Archmage Sovereign. Failure to pay fees within the allotted timeframe shall result in the suspension of the mage's right to perform authorized research or transit within the Midlands.

body.heading: Penalties; Sunrise Accrual
body.text:
All penalties, fines, and interest accrued on outstanding debts to the Guild shall be calculated based on the temporal flow of the original time zone, specifically the standard time of the Autumnwood region. This provision is enacted to prevent mages from utilizing temporal manipulation, pocket dimensions, or chronal displacement to stall the accumulation of penalties. A mage who is incarcerated within a pocket-prison or a sealed ward does not enjoy a "temporal reprieve." The Accords Desk shall calculate the duration of the penalty based on the time elapsed in the Midlands, regardless of how many years or seconds may pass within the confined space of the sanction.

The accrual of penalties begins at the moment of the initial violation or the issuance of a formal summons by the Aegis Magi. If a mage remains in a state of non-compliance, the penalty shall increase at a fixed rate per sunrise as observed in the Autumnwood. This ensures that the Guild's interests are protected against the exploitation of "slow-time" environments. See § 800.5 for specific procedures regarding the maintenance of pocket-prisons.

Any attempt to argue for a "subjective time" calculation based on the experience of the offender is strictly prohibited. The Guild maintains that the preservation of the Accords is a matter of objective reality. Should a mage attempt to use high-level chronomancy to circumvent these accruals, such an act shall be considered a Grade-A violation of the stability protocols, punishable by an immediate and permanent sealing of the offending arcane circuits. The Accords Desk shall provide a weekly statement of accrued penalties to any mage currently under sanction, ensuring transparency in the calculation of the debt.

body.heading: Appeals
body.text:
Any mage who believes a ruling of the Accords Desk to be in error may initiate a formal appeal process. The first stage of appeal resides solely with the Accords Desk. The Clerk shall review the filing for procedural correctness and ensure that all required documentation, including any relevant one-T cartography and proof of identity, has been submitted. If the Clerk finds the appeal has merit, the matter may be elevated for internal review. This stage is intended to resolve clerical errors, misunderstandings of the written word, or minor disputes regarding the interpretation of the Schedule of Fees.

If the appeal is denied at the Desk level, the mage may request a transition to the Paradox Trial. This is a formal judicial proceeding where the mage's peers shall sit in judgment. The Paradox Trial is the ultimate arbiter of the Guild's internal laws. During this process, the facts of the case are presented to the council, who may choose to uphold, vacate, or modify the original ruling. The Paradox Trial may result in various outcomes, including the sealing of magic, the issuance of a new mandate, or the confirmation of the original penalty. See § 800.4 for the conversion of duel stakes into fees during such proceedings.

Once a decision is rendered by the Paradox Trial, it is considered final and binding. There is no further mechanism for appeal within the Guild's jurisdiction. The Guild does not provide a secondary court of appeals, and any attempt to seek further adjudication through external means—such as the courts of the Regal Empire or the laws of the Iron Mandate—shall be viewed as an act of secession and a violation of the Autumnwood Accords. Mages are advised to ensure their appeals are well-reasoned and supported by evidence, as the path to "nowhere useful" begins once the Paradox Trial concludes.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
Access to the internal records of the Accords Desk, the physical archives of the Autumnwood, and the sensitive logs of the Quiet List is strictly restricted. Only authorized Clerks of the Accords Desk and named officers of the Guild may enter these areas for the purpose of official business. This restriction is designed to protect the privacy of the mages, the integrity of the Guild's secrets, and the security of the Midlands from external threats such as the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters.

No member of the general public, including non-affiliated mages, may request an inspection of the archives without a signed warrant from Archmage Veyra. Furthermore, "crowd" inspections are strictly prohibited. Even in the event of a formal inquiry, the inspection shall be conducted by a designated small group of officials rather than a public gathering. This prevents the unauthorized dissemination of information regarding the Quiet List and ensures that the delicate balance of the Guild's internal politics remains undisturbed by outside scrutiny.

Mages who are granted "Provisional Guild Passes" for political reasons, such as those held by Archie Miser, are not granted automatic inspection rights. Their access is limited to the specific documents required for their current diplomatic engagement and may be revoked at any moment by the Aegis Magi. Any unauthorized individual found attempting to peer into the archives or overhear the deliberations of the Desk shall be subject to immediate detention and a formal review for a Paradox Trial. Security is paramount; the Guild's secrets are the foundation of its power, and their preservation is the primary duty of every Clerk.

body.heading: § 1301.1 Schedule of Fees, Penalties; Sunrise Accrual, Appeals, Who May Inspect
body.text:
The Desk hereby establishes the following fee schedule applicable to all filings and services rendered under this Codex: (A) Standard Spell Registration – one hundred marks per annum for each registered enchantment; (B) Advanced Rite Certification – five hundred marks plus a two-hundred mark processing surcharge; (C) Paradox Trial Assessment – fifteen hundred marks minimum, payable upfront upon convening of the Tribunal. Penalties for non-compliance shall accrue daily at a rate of one percent per day from the date of default until cured or litigated to finality. No reduction in fees may be granted except by explicit written order of the Desk Chairperson and only after demonstration of undue hardship warranting relief.

All unfiled magical effects discovered during routine inspection shall trigger immediate retroactive assessment of outstanding fees plus a two-hundred mark late penalty per item, calculated from the date such effect first manifested. Where multiple violations arise from a single incident, penalties shall be aggregated rather than compounded to prevent astronomical liabilities while ensuring full restitution to the Guild for administrative burdens incurred.

Appeals of fee assessments must be lodged within thirty days of notification and submitted in triplicate to the Clerk General for expedited review by an impartial panel comprising representatives from both Conservator and Innovator factions. Such panels shall have authority to uphold, reduce, or vacate original determinations based solely on evidence presented during hearings conducted under sealed conditions outside public view. Final decisions rendered by appeal panels are binding and not subject to further recourse except via writ of certiorari directly to the Arcane Supreme Court upon demonstration of egregious procedural error.

Inspection rights granted herein extend exclusively to duly appointed Guild auditors accompanied by a certified scribe. Unlawful intrusion into private quarters or unauthorized attempts to examine magical items shall constitute breach of contract and may result in immediate suspension of filing privileges pending completion of background checks and liability waivers approved by the Desk. All fee payments must be made via secure transfer using recognized tender methods only; receipt of Wario Coin, gold bullion, or other non-standard currencies will not discharge obligations unless pre-arranged with written authorization from a Senior Clerk. Failure to remit fees within thirty days constitutes default under § 1302 and triggers automatic suspension of all privileges until brought fully current plus accrued interest and penalties.

This Schedule shall remain in effect until superseded by subsequent action of the Desk or revocation pursuant to established procedures set forth elsewhere herein. The Desk retains discretion to adjust fee structures periodically based on inflationary pressures, operational costs, and evolving regulatory needs, provided adequate notice is given to all affected parties through official channels. Any disputes regarding interpretation of this Schedule shall be resolved exclusively by binding arbitration administered under the auspices of the Autumnwood Accords Arbitration Tribunal unless otherwise agreed upon in writing between disputing parties.

body.heading: § 1301.2 Enforcement and Collection of Fees and Penalties
body.text:
The Accords Desk shall enforce the collection of all fees, penalties, and restitution ordered pursuant to this Part through lawful means, including but not limited to seizure of assets, liens on property, and garnishment of wages. Any party failing to comply with a final judgment within thirty days shall be subject to contempt proceedings under § 1305. The Desk may appoint a special master or receiver to manage delinquent accounts as necessary to protect the interests of the Guild and its constituents.

All fees and penalties assessed against individuals, entities, or organizations shall accrue interest at a rate determined by the Board of Archmages from time to time. Such charges shall be added immediately upon assessment and become due without further notice. Failure to pay promptly may result in additional surcharges and escalated enforcement actions. The Desk retains broad discretion regarding payment plans and waivers based on demonstrated hardship or mitigating circumstances.

Parties aggrieved by any fee, penalty, or collection action may appeal to the Appeals Tribunal within twenty-one days of service of notice. Such appeals shall be limited to questions of law and not re-litigation of factual determinations already made. The Tribunal shall hear each case expeditiously and issue a written decision within sixty days. Decisions of the Tribunal are final and binding on all parties except where clear error is shown upon rehearing.

The Accords Desk shall maintain comprehensive records of all fees collected, penalties imposed, and enforcement actions taken pursuant to this Part. These records shall be available for public inspection during normal business hours subject to appropriate redaction protections as outlined in § 1307. Any disputes regarding the accuracy or propriety of recorded entries may be raised through formal objection procedures set forth in the Rules of Practice before the Desk.

Notwithstanding any other provision herein, all fees, penalties, and costs incurred under this Part shall remain fully enforceable against successors-in-interest, assigns, executors, administrators, and representatives of estates. Nothing contained hereunder shall limit or impair the rights and remedies available to the Guild at law or in equity for breach of contract, tortious conduct, or other actionable wrongs arising out of non-compliance with these provisions.

The Desk may delegate authority to collect minor fees and impose nominal penalties to licensed collectors acting under its supervision. Such agents shall be held liable for any misappropriation or abuse of entrusted funds and subject to strict accountability measures as directed by the Board from time to time. All collections must be remitted immediately to a dedicated trust account maintained in the Guild's name solely for offsetting outstanding obligations and administrative expenses related thereto.

This Section serves as an essential operational mechanism ensuring timely compliance with the financial requirements of this Code, thereby preserving the integrity and efficacy of the regulatory framework established herein. By providing clear guidelines for assessment, collection, enforcement, and dispute resolution regarding monetary liabilities, it supports the broader goals of promoting responsible magical practice while safeguarding public welfare.

see § 1305 Contempt Proceedings; § 1307 Access to Records; § 2004 Suspension and Revocation of Licenses; § 900.6 Collection of Unpaid Fees; § 800.7 Enforcement of Judgments Against Non-Compliant Entities

*Note: All amounts specified in this Section shall be denominated exclusively in standard Guild Marks (GM), not Wario Coin or any other form of currency not officially recognized by the Accords Desk.*

sections.title: Penalties; Sunrise Accrual
sections.brief: Original time zone, not the pocket's.

body.heading: Penalties; Sunrise Accrual
body.text:
Any punitive measures, fines, or temporal sanctions levied by the Autumnwood Accords Desk against a practitioner found in violation of these statutes shall be calculated based upon the temporal progression of the practitioner’s point of origin. This principle of Sunrise Accrual ensures that the Guild maintains a consistent standard of justice that is not subject to the manipulation of localized chronomancy or the dilation of extra-planar environments. When a mage is detained within a pocket-prison, a localized rift, or any other magically-induced sub-dimension where the flow of time deviates from the standard progression of the Midlands, the duration of the penalty shall be measured by the sunrises occurring in the practitioner’s home jurisdiction at the time of the offense.

The Guild explicitly rejects the "subjective duration" defense. A practitioner who remains in a state of stasis for what they perceive to be a mere hour, but which constitutes a century of elapsed time in the Midlands, shall be held liable for the full century of accrued penalties. Conversely, a practitioner who utilizes a time-dilated pocket-dimension to attempt to "outlast" a sentence shall find that the Accords Desk recognizes only the progression of the external world. This provision serves to prevent the evasion of justice through the use of sophisticated chronometric shielding or the exploitation of natural anomalies. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority of these calculations.

Furthermore, the calculation of interest on outstanding magical debts or the duration of "Seal and Silence" sanctions shall be reconciled at the moment of the first sunrise following the initial infraction. If a practitioner is currently located in a region where the sun does not rise—such as the deep subterranean vaults or certain high-altitude celestial rifts—the Accords Desk shall defer to the nearest recognized terrestrial municipality that adheres to the Midlands standard. The goal of the Sunrise Accrual is to ensure that the cost of magical delinquency remains proportional to the impact of the crime upon the stability of the Autumnwood Accords, rather than the convenience of the offender's current location.

body.heading: Appeals
body.text:
The right to appeal a ruling issued by the Accords Desk is a fundamental prerogative of any licensed practitioner, provided such a request is filed within three lunar cycles of the initial judgment. The primary venue for such appeals is the Desk itself, wherein the presiding Clerk shall review the filing for procedural errors, misinterpretations of the Accords, or evidence of clerical oversight. The Desk maintains the authority to vacate a penalty or issue a stay of execution should it be determined that the original ruling was inconsistent with the prevailing mediation of Archmage Veyra or the established precedents of the Conservators.

Should the Desk uphold its original ruling, the practitioner may petition for a formal Paradox Trial. This is the highest level of judicial review within the Guild’s jurisdiction. A Paradox Trial involves a council of peers—selected from both the Conservator and Innovator factions—who shall determine the validity of the original charge through a process of magical arbitration. During these proceedings, the accused may present a defense, and the council may demand the presentation of artifacts, spell-scrolls, or testimonies. The outcome of a Paradox Trial is final and binding; it represents the ultimate consensus of the Guild’s magical community.

Be it known that there is no further recourse beyond the Paradox Trial. Once the peer council has rendered its verdict, the decision is considered absolute and immutable. No further petitions, grievances, or appeals may be filed with the Accords Desk, the Office of the Archmage, or the Aegis Magi regarding the specific matter at hand. To attempt to seek a higher court of law outside the Guild’s jurisdiction is to forfeit all remaining protections afforded by the Accords. Practitioners are cautioned that seeking "external" justice—particularly from the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion—will result in the immediate revocation of their Guild standing and the permanent sealing of their arcane signature. See § 800.5 for the specific procedures regarding the enforcement of these final judgments.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
The sanctity of the Archives and the privacy of the practitioner’s registered magical laboratory are upheld by the principle of Restricted Access. Only authorized personnel of the Autumnwood Accords are permitted to conduct formal inspections of any site where restricted research is being conducted or where a magical artifact of significant provenance is being held. These inspectors are strictly limited to active Clerks of the Accords Desk and named Officers of the Aegis Magi. Any individual not holding a verified Guild Seal of Inspection may be barred from entry at the discretion of the site’s primary licensee.

Under no circumstances shall a public inspection be permitted. The Guild recognizes that the exposure of experimental methodologies—particularly those pursued by the Innovators—could lead to the unintended dissemination of volatile arcana or the compromise of the Quiet List. A crowd, including non-practitioners, journalists, or unauthorized observers, is strictly prohibited from entering any zone designated for inspection. Should a practitioner fail to grant access to a named Officer of the Aegis Magi during a scheduled audit, they shall be subject to immediate summary fines and a potential referral for a Paradox Trial.

In cases where a practitioner is under active investigation for a violation of the Iron Mandate or other rival laws, the Accords Desk may grant temporary inspection rights to designated mediators, provided these mediators are bound by a non-disclosure oath. However, these rights do not extend to the general populace or to representatives of the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters. Any unauthorized breach of a laboratory or archive by a non-Guild entity shall be treated as an act of hostility against the Accords. See § 900.1 for the requirements regarding the filing of notice before any authorized inspection commences.

body.heading: § 1301.2 Penalties and Remedies; Sunrise Accrual and Appeals
body.text:
Any violation of these provisions shall result in immediate cessation of the offending activity, forfeiture of all ill-gotten gains, and imposition of punitive damages as determined by the Archmage Sovereign or their delegate. The prevailing party may recover reasonable attorneys' fees and costs incurred in bringing this action to fruition. In egregious cases involving deliberate malice or repeated offenses, permanent revocation of licensure is mandatory under § 200.4(b).

Penalties shall accrue from sunrise on the first day after the violation occurs ("sunrise" meaning actual dawn regardless of local time zone) until such time as full satisfaction has been rendered. Deliberate obstruction of enforcement efforts doubles accrued penalties per § 1301.5. Failure to post adequate security for a judgment renders double daily interest applicable, calculated at twice the standard Guild rate plus an additional ten percent premium.

Applicants dissatisfied with any ruling may file a motion for review within seven days of notification.
