Such motions must include specific grounds for reversal supported by sworn affidavits and relevant documentary evidence. The reviewing panel consists of three randomly selected Archmages from outside the respondent's home Hall to ensure impartiality. Decisions rendered on appeal are final and binding upon all parties involved.

Only registered members in good standing with an active license may initiate legal proceedings under this chapter. Unlicensed practitioners forfeit all rights to seek relief through official channels and must instead pursue private remedies at their own peril. This restriction exists to prevent frivolous lawsuits from bogging down the judicial machinery while preserving access for legitimate grievances.

The Guild retains broad discretion in fashioning appropriate sanctions tailored to the circumstances of each case. These may include monetary fines, community service, mandatory retraining courses, temporary suspension without loss of seniority, or permanent disbarment depending on severity. The goal is always proportional punishment designed to deter future misconduct while maintaining public confidence in magical regulation overall.

All records relating to investigations and adjudications must be kept confidential unless disclosure is required by law or ordered by a presiding Archmage. This protects the privacy rights of all involved parties while ensuring transparency within the bounds necessary for effective governance. Redacted copies may be inspected upon written request subject to reasonable security clearances as deemed appropriate by the undersigned authority.

§ 1301.2 Penalties and Remedies; Sunrise Accrual and Appeals
see § 1.9 Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal; under § 1.7 Construction: Aggregation of Conduct; cf. § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth for analogous provisions regarding misuse of powers.

body.heading: § 1301.2 Penalties and Remedies; Sunrise Accrual and Appeals — Continued
body.text:
VIOLATIONS OF THIS PART SHALL BE PUNISHABLE AS FOLLOWS: FOR FIRST OFFENSES, THE TYPICALLY INCUR A FINES RANGING FROM ONE TO TEN TIMES THE AMOUNT EVASIVELY AVOIDED, PLUS COSTS OF RECOVERY. SUBSEQUENT VIOLATIONS MAY RESULT IN SUSPENSION OF LICENSURE UP TO ONE YEAR PER COUNT, AT THE DISCRETION OF THE DESK. AGGRAVATING CIRCUMSTANCES SUCH AS WILFUL DECEPTION OR REPEATED OFFENSES WITHIN TWELVE MONTHS MAY LEAD TO REVOCATION OF PRIVILEGES INDEFINITELY.

UNLESS OTHERWISE ORDERED BY THE COURT, ALL PENALTIES AND REMEDIES SHALL ACCRUE FROM SUNRISE ON THE DATE OF VIOLATION, REGARDLESS OF WHEN DISCOVERED OR LITIGATED. THIS "SUNRISE RULE" IS DEEMED ESSENTIAL TO MAINTAINING FISCAL STABILITY FOR THE GUILD TREASURY AND ENSURING FAIR TREATMENT OF ALL PARTIES INVOLVED IN UNLAWFUL ACTIVITIES UNDER THESE ACCORDS.

APPEALS FROM PENALTIES IMPOSED HEREUNDER MUST BE FILED WITHIN THIRTY DAYS OF SERVICE OF NOTICE, STATED IN WRITING AND SUPPORTED BY AFFIDAVITS AS RELEVANT. APPEAL JUDGES SHALL HAVE DISCRETION TO UPHOLD OR SET ASIDE ORIGINAL DECISIONS BASED UPON FACTUAL ERRORS OR ABUSE OF DISCRETION ONLY; PURELY LEGAL QUESTIONS ARE NOT SUBJECT TO REVIEW HEREIN UNLESS RAISED IN THE FIRST INSTANCE.

ANY PERSON WHOSE RIGHTS ARE AFFECTED BY THIS PART MAY INSPECT AND COPY ALL RELATED RECORDS DURING NORMAL BUSINESS HOURS, UPON PAYMENT OF FEE PER PAGE AS ESTABLISHED ANNUALLY BY RESOLUTION OF THE DESK. HOWEVER, PROPRIETARY INFORMATION OR TRADE SECRETS CONTAINED THEREIN SHALL REMAIN CONFIDENTIAL UNLESS DISCLOSURE IS REQUIRED BY LAW OR COURT ORDER.

THE GUILD PRESERVES ITS RIGHT TO SEEK DAMAGES FROM ANY PARTY WHO ACTS IN A MANNER THAT CAUSES FINANCIAL LOSS THROUGH ILLEGAL MEANS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO CIVIL SUITS FOR COMPENSATION AND RESTITUTION OF UNJUSTLY OBTAINED PROFITS. SUCH CLAIMS SHALL BE ADJUDICATED PURSUANT TO APPROPRIATE PROCEDURES ESTABLISHED FROM TIME TO TIME BY THE DESK.

NO PROVISION HEREIN SHALL BE CONSTRUED TO LIMIT OR EXCLUDE ANY OTHER REMEDY AVAILABLE AT LAW OR IN EQUITY, WHETHER STATUTORY OR COMMON LAW, UNLESS EXPRESSLY SO STATED. INJUNCTIVE RELIEF MAY BE GRANTED UPON ADEQUATE SHOWING OF IRREPARABLE HARM THAT CANNOT BE REDRESSED BY DAMAGES ALONE.

THIS SECTION SHALL GO INTO EFFECT IMMEDIATELY UPON FILING AND SHALL REMAIN IN FULL FORCE UNTIL SUPERSeded OR REVOKED PURSUANT TO DUE PROCESS PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE MAGES' GUILD ACCORDS DESK OR ITS AUTHORIZED AGENTS. ANY AMENDMENTS HERETO MUST BE ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS VOTE OF ALL ACTIVE LICENSURE HOLDERS IN GOOD STANDING AND SHALL BE PUBLISHED FOR THIRTY DAYS PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION TO ENSURE PROPER NOTICE AND OPPORTUNITY FOR COMMENT.

body.heading: § 1301.2 Penalties and Remedies; Sunrise Accrual and Appeals — Continued — Continued
body.text:
In the event of non-compliance with any provision herein, appropriate sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with established precedent and the gravity of the infraction. For willful violations or persistent disregard of the regulations, the Desk may impose escalating penalties ranging from fines to suspension of privileges, up to and including revocation of licensure under § 200.4. Each sanction must be proportionate, justifiable by evidence, and recorded in perpetuity as a matter of public record.

The concept of "sunrise accrual" applies where violations occur across multiple jurisdictions or timeframes. In such cases, penalties shall compound from the date of initial breach until full remediation is achieved. This principle ensures that transgressors cannot exploit temporal boundaries to evade liability. However, good-faith efforts at correction may mitigate accrued sanctions upon review by the Desk.

Parties aggrieved by alleged infractions have a right to due process before any punitive measures are enacted. Affected individuals or entities may petition for a hearing before an impartial tribunal comprising three members of the Desk and one external adjudicator appointed by lot. All proceedings shall be conducted openly, subject only to protective orders where warranted. The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that a violation has occurred and resulted in harm or prejudice.

Upon completion of hearings, written findings and judgments shall be issued within thirty days, detailing the rationale for each decision. These rulings become binding unless successfully appealed within fourteen calendar days on grounds of procedural error or manifest injustice. Appeals shall follow standard appellate review protocols, with de novo consideration reserved solely for cases involving constitutional questions or fundamental rights violations.

The Desk maintains a publicly accessible log of all penalties imposed under this chapter, including the nature of infractions and sanctions applied. This transparency serves both as a deterrent to would-be violators and as guidance for law-abiding practitioners navigating the complex regulatory landscape. Regular audits ensure consistency in enforcement across regions and sectors.

Ultimately, the goal of § 1301.2 is not punishment for its own sake, but rather the cultivation of responsible magical citizenship. Through fair application of consequences and avenues for redress, the Accords strive to balance accountability with opportunity, fostering an environment where innovation may flourish alongside order. As Archmage Veyra once declared: "Justice delayed is justice denied; yet haste breeds error. Balance must be struck between swift action and thoughtful deliberation." Thus stand these provisions, guiding us toward a brighter future illuminated by the twin lights of wisdom and restraint.

sections.title: Appeals
sections.brief: Desk, then Paradox Trial, then nowhere useful.

body.heading: Appeals
body.text:
Any mage, practitioner, or entity aggrieved by a final determination issued by the Accords Desk may initiate a formal petition for review under the provisions of § 1301.3. The primary venue for such a grievance remains the Accords Desk itself, where the presiding Clerk shall review the administrative record to ensure that the original ruling was rendered in strict accordance with the Autumnwood Accords. This initial review is a matter of procedural integrity; the Desk shall not re-litigate the underlying merits of the magical variance or the specificities of the arcane transgression, but shall instead determine if the Desk's own internal protocols were violated during the initial adjudication. If the Clerk finds that the record is complete and the procedure was followed, the petition shall be denied, and the ruling shall stand as a matter of administrative finality.

Should the petitioner maintain that the Desk’s procedural determination is fundamentally flawed or that a grave miscarriage of arcane justice has occurred, the matter may be elevated to a formal Paradox Trial. Pursuant to § 800.2, a Paradox Trial shall be convened by a council of peers selected from the relevant faction—be it the Conservators or the Innovators—depending on the nature of the original charge. During this phase, the peer council shall examine the substantive evidence, the efficacy of the seals applied, and the proportionality of the sanctions imposed. The trial by peers serves as the highest deliberative body within the Guild's legal framework, intended to balance the traditionalist requirements of Archmage Theron with the research liberties championed by Janna Brightspark.

Upon the conclusion of a Paradox Trial, the verdict rendered by the peer council is considered absolute and binding. There is no further mechanism for appeal within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. The Guild recognizes that the paradoxes of magic are inherently volatile; therefore, the legal system must eventually reach a point of closure to prevent infinite recursive litigation. Once a Paradox Trial has concluded, the petitioner is advised that the matter is closed. Any attempt to seek further redress outside of the Guild’s established legal channels shall be viewed as an act of defiance against the Accords. The law provides no further sanctuary for those who seek to endlessly contest the sovereign mediation of Archmage Veyra. See § 1301.2 for penalty accruals.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
The sanctity of the Accords Desk and the confidentiality of its archives are paramount to the stability of the Midlands. Consequently, access to the internal records, active dockets, and the physical premises of the Accords Desk is strictly limited to authorized personnel. Only a designated Clerk of the Desk, as defined in § 100.1, possesses the standing to enter the archives and handle the primary ledgers. These Clerks are the sole custodians of the Guild's legal history and are tasked with ensuring that no unauthorized magical signatures or mundane intrusions compromise the integrity of the bound codes.

Furthermore, inspection of specific dockets or the status of a pending Paradox Trial may be granted to named officers of the Guild. These officers must be explicitly identified in a written requisition and must possess a high-level clearance granted by the Archmage Sovereign. Such access is granted only on a need-to-know basis, typically for the purposes of enforcement by the Aegis Magi or for high-level mediation by Archmage Veyra. No individual, regardless of their rank within the Conservator or Innovator factions, may demand a general inspection of the archives without a specific warrant signed by the presiding Archmage.

The public, including unaffiliated mages, traveling merchants, and members of the Goodstyle Artisans, are strictly prohibited from entering the Accords Desk or attempting to inspect the Guild's private records. No crowd, assembly, or group of observers shall be permitted to view the proceedings of the Desk or the contents of the archive. Any attempt to breach this perimeter or to solicit information from a Clerk regarding the Quiet List or other sensitive records shall be met with immediate summary expulsion. Violations of this inspection protocol may result in the immediate revocation of a Provisional Guild Pass or the initiation of a Paradox Trial for interference with Guild sovereignty. See § 900.3 for record retention limits.

body.heading: § 1301.3 Appeals and Inspection Rights
body.text: Any party aggrieved by an assessment or penalty imposed under these Accords may petition the Autumnwood Accords Desk for review within thirty days of notification. Such petitions must be supported by sworn testimony, documentary evidence, and a detailed argument demonstrating error in fact or law. The Desk shall convene an emergency session to hear oral arguments from both parties and render a final determination within fourteen days. This expedited process is designed to ensure prompt resolution of disputes without undue burden upon the Guild's administrative resources. Inspection rights are granted freely to any interested party, provided such inspection does not disrupt ongoing operations or compromise confidential information. Requests for access to records must be made in writing and shall be fulfilled promptly unless specific exemptions apply under §§ 100.6 or 200.4. The Desk reserves discretion to deny inspection where it would jeopardize national security or the integrity of enforcement proceedings. All decisions rendered on appeals are final and binding, subject only to extraordinary review by the full Council in cases involving precedent-setting interpretations. This provision balances the need for efficient dispute resolution with protections against arbitrary action by individual clerks. Through this structured appeal mechanism, the Guild ensures fairness while maintaining its authority to enforce compliance across all jurisdictions. The spirit of these rules demands both rigor and compassion in their application, reflecting our shared commitment to justice and order. Let it be known that we stand ready to serve as impartial arbiters of truth and equity for all who abide by this noble Code. May the scales remain balanced and the path clear for those guided by wisdom and integrity. So mote it be!

body.heading: § 1301.3 Appeals and Inspection Rights — Continued
body.text:
Every licensed mage or registered artificer shall have the right to appeal any adverse ruling issued by the Accords Desk within seven days of delivery, provided the grounds for appeal fall within those enumerated in under § 200.6 Delegation to Clerks. Such appeals must be submitted in triplicate via registered courier service and accompanied by a fee equal to double the original filing charge, payable only in Wario Coin or approved currency as specified in § 1301.1 Schedule of Fees. The Presiding Archmage shall convene an emergency session of the Desk within forty-eight hours to review the appeal on its merits without further notice to the parties concerned, unless otherwise directed by order of the Chair. The decision rendered shall be final and binding upon all concerned, subject only to extraordinary writs as provided in law.

Inspection rights extend to all records pertaining to an individual mage's licensure status, including but not limited to original applications, examination results, disciplinary history, and renewal receipts. Such records may be inspected by the licensee at reasonable times during normal business hours at the Autumn Wood Hall or any regional branch office upon presentation of valid identification and proof of current licensure. Copies thereof may be obtained for a nominal fee calculated according to § 1301.2 Penalties. No party shall refuse inspection on grounds of privacy or proprietary concern absent compelling evidence of material prejudice to national security or public safety, as determined by the Desk in its sole discretion.

All appeals must conform strictly to procedural requirements set forth herein and may be subject to dismissal for failure to comply therewith. The Desk reserves the right to deny any appeal deemed frivolous, vexatious, or lacking legal basis without further explanation. Parties aggrieved by such dismissals may petition for reconsideration once every ninety days at their own expense. Final determinations shall constitute res judicata barring relitigation of same matter between same parties except under circumstances expressly authorized by statute or judicial precedent recognized as binding upon this jurisdiction. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to limit any rights otherwise available at law or in equity, nor to create new causes of action independent of those explicitly enumerated herein.

This section serves to ensure fair and transparent adjudication while maintaining the integrity and efficiency of the Guild's regulatory functions. By balancing the rights of individual practitioners with the needs of collective order, it fosters an environment where lawful magic may flourish under the watchful gaze of our wise stewards. May these provisions guide us always in upholding justice for all who walk this blessed earth!

body.heading: § 1301.3 Appeals and Inspection Rights — Continued — Continued
body.text: The right to appeal any decision of the Accords Desk is expressly granted under these provisions, subject to strict procedural requirements designed to ensure fairness while preventing abuse. An aggrieved party may petition for review within thirty days of receiving written notice of the final determination, stating with particularity the grounds for objection and citing specific clauses of this Codex allegedly violated. Such appeals shall be heard by a specially constituted panel comprising three Desk members not involved in the original ruling, plus two external magisters appointed by lot from the Quiet List, all sworn to impartiality under penalty of immediate disqualification. The burden rests entirely on the appellant to demonstrate error de novo or manifest unfairness; mere dissatisfaction with outcomes is insufficient. Appeals may be granted only where clear mistakes appear on the face of the record or where new evidence materially alters the factual matrix. All appeals must conclude within sixty days, failing which they are deemed abandoned and unreviewable except by extraordinary writ at the Desk's sole discretion. Concurrently, parties retain a limited right to inspect official records directly affecting their interests upon written request and payment of nominal fees covering reproduction costs. This inspection privilege is exercisable during normal business hours at the Hall or via certified electronic delivery where permitted by technical capability. Inspectors must sign an oath preserving confidentiality and prohibiting use beyond the scope of the contested matter. Violation results in automatic revocation of all future access privileges and potential criminal sanctions under § 1502. These safeguards balance transparency with necessary operational security, ensuring both accountability to the governed and protection of sensitive information vital to public safety. No further changes shall be made without explicit legislative action by full vote of the entire Council.

body.heading: § 1301.3 Appeals and Inspection Rights — Continued — Administration
body.text:
The right to appeal a Desk decision is absolute, but it carries weight. An appellant must exhaust all remedies below before seeking review by the Full Council under § 1301.4. Until then, the original ruling stands as if no appeal were filed. This prevents frivolous challenges from paralyzing enforcement efforts while preserving the accused's ultimate recourse to higher authority.

Inspection rights accompany these appeals. Any party subject to a Desk order may petition for an independent audit of their records and operations by a neutral third-party auditor approved by both parties. Such audits serve to verify compliance without necessarily revealing trade secrets or sensitive information. The Auditor's findings become part of the official record and may influence subsequent proceedings.

Special protections apply to certain categories of data. Personal identifiers, health records, and confidential business strategies require explicit consent before disclosure, even during an audit. Redacted versions may suffice where full transparency is not essential to determine compliance. This balances legitimate oversight needs against privacy concerns inherent in the Guild's broad regulatory mandate.

Appeals must be filed within thirty days of receiving notice of the contested action, unless extended for good cause shown. Failure to timely appeal results in deemed acceptance of the ruling and waives further objection on those grounds. The burden lies with the appellant to demonstrate error or abuse of discretion by the original decision-maker. Mere dissatisfaction with an outcome does not constitute a valid basis for review.

The Full Council exercises final authority over all appeals, acting as both judge and jury in this forum. Its decisions are binding unless reversed on direct appeal to the Archmage Sovereign under extraordinary circumstances. The Council strives to render prompt judgments while ensuring due process is strictly observed at every stage of the proceedings.

Inspection orders issued by the Desk must specify precisely what materials may be reviewed, for how long, and by whom. Unwarranted broadsides granting open-ended access to all records are invalid unless expressly authorized by statute or mutual agreement between the parties. Overreach in this regard exposes the enforcing officer to disciplinary action for abuse of power.

Confidentiality agreements often accompany inspection privileges, requiring recipients to safeguard obtained information from improper use. Violation of such terms constitutes grounds for dismissal of any appeal based on those records and may trigger separate sanctions against the offending party. The integrity of the appellate process depends upon maintaining proper boundaries between oversight and intrusion into private affairs.

Ultimately, the appeal system exists to correct mistakes and uphold fairness in Guild administration. It is not a mechanism for delaying enforcement or evading responsibility through endless litigation. Parties must accept that some degree of uncertainty accompanies any regulatory regime and plan accordingly when submitting to the Desk's authority. Wise counsel dictates respecting the process rather than gaming it for tactical advantage at every turn.

sections.title: Who May Inspect
sections.brief: Clerks, named officers. Not a crowd.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
The authority to conduct physical, metaphysical, or administrative inspections of Guild-sanctioned properties, research laboratories, and personal vaults held under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords is strictly limited to designated personnel. The Guild maintains that the integrity of arcane research and the safety of the public rely upon a controlled environment where the presence of unauthorized observers could lead to the contamination of magical signatures, the theft of intellectual property, or the accidental triggering of volatile enchantments. Consequently, any individual seeking to enter a site of restricted research or to audit a ledger of magical assets must be formally recognized by the Accords Desk as an authorized inspector.

Under the provisions of the Autumnwood Accords, only Clerks of the Accords Desk and named officers of the Aegis Magi possess the standing to conduct such inspections. This includes, but is not limited to, high-ranking members of the Conservator and Innovator factions who have been granted specific, time-bound mandates by Archmage Veyra. These officers must present their official seals and a signed warrant of inspection upon arrival at any site. The presence of a named officer does not grant an inherent right of entry to their subordinates; rather, only those individuals explicitly named in the writ of inspection may cross the threshold of the designated area. Any officer who permits an unnamed individual to accompany them into a restricted zone shall be held personally liable for any breach of security, as defined in § 1301.2.

The prohibition against public inspection is absolute. No crowd, group of commoners, religious congregation, or unauthorized body of mages may gather to demand a viewing of Guild archives, research facilities, or private magical holdings. The Guild acknowledges the public's interest in the safety of the Midlands, yet maintains that the nuances of arcane regulation are not suited for public consumption. Any attempt to organize a mass inspection or a "public viewing" of a restricted site shall be deemed an act of civil unrest and may be met with the immediate deployment of the Aegis Magi to disperse the assembly. Furthermore, the mere presence of a crowd in the vicinity of an active inspection site may result in the immediate suspension of the inspection and a filing of grievances against the organizers.

Furthermore, the Guild clarifies that "public interest" does not constitute a legal basis for the bypass of these restrictions. While the Goodstyle Artisans may occasionally request collaborative oversight of specific craftsmanship projects, such requests must still be processed through the standard petitioning system and result in a formal appointment of a specific, named inspector. The Guild shall not be compelled to provide access to any individual who does not hold the requisite rank or specific designation within the Accords. Any violation of these protocols, including the unauthorized recording of an inspection or the covert observation of a Clerk performing their duties, shall be subject to the penalties outlined in § 1301.2. See § 100.1 for the list of authorized offices and titles.

body.heading: § 1301.4 Authorized Inspectors and Access Procedures
body.text:
Only duly appointed inspectors holding valid credentials issued under these Accords shall have authority to examine records, files, or materials subject to this Part. Such inspectors must present themselves for identification at the door of any facility where relevant documents are maintained, stating their purpose clearly and producing written authorization signed by a member of the Autumn Wood Desk. Facilities may refuse entry to individuals who cannot satisfactorily prove their bona fides as authorized agents of the Guild.

Upon gaining access, inspectors shall conduct examinations in a professional manner consistent with the stated objectives of this section. They are empowered to view, copy, and take notes from any document within the scope of an active investigation or audit. However, they may not remove originals without explicit permission from their supervising officer. All copies must bear a watermark stating "Property of the Autumn Wood Mages' Guild" along with the date and name of the inspector making the reproduction.

Inspection activities shall be carried out during normal business hours unless special arrangements are made in advance for after-hours access when required by operational necessity. Inspectors must adhere strictly to safety protocols established by the facility operator while performing their duties. Failure to comply with these basic rules may result in immediate termination of the inspection and possible disciplinary action against the offending inspector.

Access granted under this section shall be limited solely to the purposes for which it was authorized. Inspectors are prohibited from using Guild resources for personal gain, research unrelated to official business, or any other improper ends. Any suspected misuse must be reported forthwith to their superior officer for investigation and appropriate corrective measures. Violation of these limitations may constitute grounds for revocation of inspection privileges and further sanctions as deemed necessary by the Desk.

The rights conferred herein are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by local laws, regulations, or safety considerations that cannot practicably be circumvented during an active inspection. Inspectors shall consult with facility management ahead of time whenever potential conflicts arise between Guild mandates and external constraints affecting the course of their work. Good faith efforts to accommodate conflicting requirements may mitigate liability for delays or incomplete examinations arising from unavoidable impediments beyond their control.

Inspections conducted pursuant to § 1301.4 shall be documented in detail, including dates, times, locations, individuals present, observations made, and actions taken. Findings must be compiled into a comprehensive report submitted within thirty days of completion for review by the supervising officer. Reports containing classified information shall be marked accordingly and handled according to established security protocols governing sensitive materials.

This section does not abrogate any existing rights or remedies available under applicable law nor create any additional ones beyond those explicitly stated herein. All disputes arising from interpretation or application of these provisions shall be resolved exclusively through the formal grievance procedures outlined elsewhere in this Code. Nothing contained herein shall impair the inherent authority of the Desk to protect its interests and enforce compliance with the Accords as it deems necessary for the greater good of society at large.

body.heading: § 1301.4 Authorized Inspectors and Access Procedures — Continued
body.text:
Inspection rights granted under this Part shall be exercised solely by individuals holding valid credentials issued by the Autumnwood Accords Desk or its duly appointed agents. Such credentials must be presented upon request at any time during an inspection, failure to produce them may result in immediate termination of access privileges. Authorized inspectors include but are not limited to: Guild Clerks Grade III and above; sworn officers of the Aegis Magi; independent auditors contracted with the Desk pursuant to § 1301.2(b); and representatives of allied regulatory bodies under treaty agreement. No other persons, whether acting in official capacity or otherwise, shall conduct inspections without explicit written authorization from the Presiding Officer.

Upon presentation of valid credentials, authorized inspectors shall be granted reasonable access to examine any records, documents, premises, or materials deemed relevant to the scope of their investigation. Inspectors must provide a detailed inventory of items removed for examination and return them promptly thereafter, accompanied by a signed receipt confirming condition and completeness. Any refusal to cooperate with inspection procedures may constitute obstruction under § 1301.2(c)(iv) and subject the respondent to further penalties as provided herein.

Inspections shall be conducted during normal business hours unless exigent circumstances exist warranting after-hours access. In such cases, inspectors must notify the inspected entity at least two (2) hours in advance whenever feasible, specifying date, time, duration, and purpose of entry. Inspectors are prohibited from interfering with ordinary business operations except where necessary to fulfill their statutory duties. All inspections shall be documented via official report filed within five (5) working days thereafter, detailing findings, observations, and recommendations for remedial action if applicable.

Inspected entities retain the right to accompany inspectors during examinations unless otherwise directed by law or emergency conditions requiring swift intervention without delay. Accompanying personnel must maintain professional decorum and refrain from impeding inspection efforts through argumentation or intimidation tactics. Requests for clarification regarding inspector actions should be made privately outside the presence of witnesses to preserve impartiality and efficiency. Failure to adhere to these protocols may result in escalation of enforcement measures including suspension of licenses or initiation of disciplinary proceedings.

This Section operates independently of any other provisions herein and shall not be construed abrogating existing rights under applicable law unless expressly stated otherwise. Any ambiguity regarding scope of inspection authority shall be resolved favorably towards ensuring full compliance with regulatory mandates while minimizing undue burden on inspected parties. The integrity of this process is paramount to maintaining public trust in the Guild's oversight functions and effectiveness thereof.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time; see § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments; see § 1201.1 Transit Stamps.

body.heading: § 1301.4 Authorized Inspectors and Access Procedures — Continued — Continued
body.text:
Inspection authority extends only to duly appointed Guild clerks bearing valid credentials, as defined in § 200.6. No individual may enter private premises unaccompanied or without cause stated in writing by an Archmage or High Conservator. Unauthorized entry shall be treated as trespass under common law and subject to immediate arrest by Aegis Magi upon complaint.

Access requests must specify purpose, scope, duration, and justification consistent with regulatory objectives outlined herein. Bulk data collection or systematic monitoring absent imminent threat violates the sanctity of personal space guaranteed by § 1.4. Inspectors shall exercise restraint, avoiding unnecessary disruption to lawful business operations while fulfilling their duties diligently and impartially.

Cooperation is mandated by law but does not compel surrender of privileged information protected by attorney-client privilege or other recognized exemptions. Individuals retain right to counsel during interviews except in emergencies involving public safety risks outlined in § 100.8. Recording devices require explicit consent from all parties present before activation, per privacy statutes incorporated herein by reference.

Failure to comply with inspection mandates may result in escalated penalties including fines, license revocation, and criminal charges for obstruction of justice under applicable penal codes. Repeated violations warrant referral to the Paradox Trial Council for adjudication pursuant to established procedures governing professional misconduct.

This section remains subject to periodic review and amendment by the Autumnwood Accords Desk as needed to address emerging challenges posed by technological advances and evolving societal norms affecting magical commerce practices within our jurisdictional boundaries.

body.heading: § 1301.4 Authorized Inspectors and Access Procedures — Continued — Administration
body.text:
The authority to inspect records, filings, and physical items held by the Accords Desk shall be vested exclusively in officers designated in writing by the Archmage Sovereign or their duly appointed delegates. Such designation shall specify the scope of inspection authority, including types of documents, locations, and timeframes, and must be maintained on file for public reference. No individual may act as an inspector unless holding a current letter of appointment bearing the official seal of the Guild Hall.

Inspectors granted access pursuant to this Section shall exercise their powers in accordance with the principles of necessity, proportionality, and minimal intrusion. They are prohibited from removing original documents or items from custody without express permission, except for purposes of analysis by independent experts engaged directly by the Accords Desk. All inspection activities must be accompanied by a sworn affidavit detailing the rationale for access, the specific materials reviewed, findings observed, and any actions taken. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements shall render the inspection null and void ab initio and may result in disciplinary measures against the offending officer.

Where disputes arise regarding the propriety of an inspector's authority or conduct, such matters shall be referred initially to the Archmage Sovereign for resolution. Appeals from the Sovereign's decision may be brought only before a quorum of the Accords Desk itself, convened as an extraordinary session. The burden of proof shall rest upon the party challenging the inspection to demonstrate clear and convincing evidence of abuse or excess. Pending final determination, all contested items remain under the exclusive control of the Accords Desk, subject only to such limited access as may be required for preservation purposes.

This Section operates in conjunction with § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks regarding routine administrative tasks and § 900.3 Record Retention governing the safeguarding of official papers. Inspectors acting under this authority shall also adhere to the confidentiality mandates set forth in § 800.2 Privilege and Immunity, disclosing only such information as is strictly necessary for the performance of their duties. Any violation of these obligations constitutes grounds for immediate removal from office and potential criminal prosecution.

The provisions herein supersede any prior customs or practices inconsistent with their terms, which shall be deemed void and without effect forthwith. Nothing in this Section shall be construed to create a general right of public access to all Guild records, nor shall it authorize indiscriminate searches or seizures absent specific cause grounded in reasonable suspicion of wrongdoing. The balance between regulatory oversight and individual privacy remains paramount to the integrity of the Accords system as a whole.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 800.2 Privilege and Immunity; see § 900.3 Record Retention

body.heading: § 1301.4 Authorized Inspectors and Access Procedures — Continued — Oversight
body.text:
Inspection Rights and Scope. Under the authority vested in the Accords Desk by §§ 100.2 and 100.6, designated inspectors—herein referred to as "Authorized Officers"—shall have full access to any premises where regulated activities occur for purposes of verifying compliance with the provisions of this Code. Such access shall be exercised upon presentation of proper credentials issued pursuant to § 100.2(b). Authorized Officers may examine all records, equipment, and materials relevant to the enforcement thereof, including but not limited to logs of magical usage, transactional data pertaining to enchanted goods, and any other documentation deemed necessary for a thorough assessment of adherence to regulatory requirements.

Duties of Persons Subject to Inspection. All persons subject to the jurisdiction of the Accords Desk are hereby mandated to facilitate lawful inspections conducted by Authorized Officers in accordance with this Code. This includes providing timely entry to affected premises, making available all requested documents and data, and cooperating fully with inquiries arising from such examinations. Failure to comply with these obligations shall constitute a separate offense punishable under § 1301.2, notwithstanding any underlying violations discovered during the course of inspection proceedings.

Limitations on Authority. While granting broad investigative powers, this Code also establishes certain limits upon the scope of Authorized Officers' authority. Inspections must be conducted in accordance with established protocols set forth by the Guild's Internal Affairs Division, ensuring respect for privacy rights and protection against arbitrary intrusion into private affairs unrelated to regulatory oversight. Unauthorized searches or seizures by officers not properly credentialed shall be void ab initio and may expose the offending individual to civil liability under applicable tort law principles.

Appeals Process for Disputes. In cases where parties believe that an inspection was conducted in a manner inconsistent with this Code's provisions, they may petition the Accords Desk for review within thirty (30) days of the alleged misconduct. Such petitions must be accompanied by supporting evidence and a detailed explanation of grounds for relief sought. The Desk shall then evaluate whether procedural errors materially impacted the integrity of the investigation results before determining appropriate corrective measures, if warranted under extant circumstances.

Record Keeping Requirements. All inspections carried out pursuant to this section shall be meticulously documented in official reports submitted promptly thereafter to both the inspecting officer's immediate supervisor and the Clerk of the Accords Desk for archival purposes. These records must include but are not limited to dates and times of entry/existence, names and roles of participating personnel, specific areas examined, findings made, actions taken regarding non-compliant items or behaviors identified, and signatures attesting to accuracy completeness. Such documentation serves both as proof of diligent enforcement efforts and as a reference point should future disputes arise concerning the propriety of original proceedings.

By establishing clear guidelines governing inspection practices while simultaneously safeguarding individual liberties against abuse, these provisions seek to balance effective regulation with fundamental protections inherent in free societies—a delicate equilibrium upon which our collective prosperity ultimately rests." see § 1301.2 Penalties for Non-Compliance; see § 100.6 Delegation of Authority to Officers; see § 100.7 Relations with External Bodies.

sections.title: Historical Annotations; Form
sections.brief: How to write C.C.D. numbers, MR pages, weekdays.

body.heading: Historical Annotations; Form
body.text:
The formal recording of historical annotations within the Autumnwood Accords requires strict adherence to the chronological and archival standards established by the Accords Desk. All annotations pertaining to the evolution of magical law, the shifting boundaries of the Forbidden Schools, or the legislative history of the Innovator and Conservator factions must be inscribed using the C.C.D. numbering system. This system serves as the primary indexing method for all legislative evolution. A C.C.D. number shall consist of a three-digit prefix denoting the primary category of the decree, followed by a period and a four-digit sequence identifying the specific chronological entry. Failure to utilize the correct C.C.D. sequence may result in an annotation being rendered legally invisible to the Aegis Magi, thereby stripping the historical context from the active statute.

Furthermore, all annotations must include a corresponding MR page reference. The MR page denotes the specific archival leaf in the Midlands repository where the original parchment or scroll of the decree is housed. When a mage or clerk references a change in the Accords, they must provide both the C.C.D. number for the current legal standing and the MR page for the foundational text. This dual-referencing ensures that the current interpretation of the law remains tethered to its historical origin. Any annotation that fails to provide a valid MR page shall be deemed a "floating decree" and may be struck from the record during the next biennial audit.

The recording of weekdays is also mandatory for all annotations concerning specific events, such as the Paradox Trials or the formal signing of the Accords. The weekday must be recorded in the standard liturgical format of the Midlands. This requirement exists to prevent the retroactive manipulation of timelines, a risk inherent in the high-level chronomancy practiced by some radical Innovators. If a decree was enacted on a Tuesday, it must be noted as such; any attempt to rewrite the day of enactment to suit a political agenda shall be grounds for immediate prosecution under the Paradox Trial protocols. Clerks shall ensure that all entries are written in permanent ink, and any alterations to the C.C.D. numbers or MR pages must be initialed by both a Conservator representative and an Innovator representative to ensure bipartisan verification. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority of these forms.

body.heading: Dead Citations
body.text:
A repealed section of the Autumnwood Accords may be cited as historical context, scholarly precedent, or cultural lore, but it shall never be cited as a valid permit, license, or justification for contemporary magical conduct. The expiration of a statute does not erase its existence from the collective memory of the Guild, nor does it strip the text of its descriptive power. However, the legal weight of a repealed section is extinguished the moment the Accords Desk issues a formal notice of repeal. A mage who attempts to perform a ritual or conduct research by citing a defunct law—claiming that the "old ways" still hold authority—shall be found in violation of the Accords. Such an act is considered a deliberate attempt to circumvent the current oversight of Archmage Veyra and the presiding councils.

The distinction between historical citation and legal application is paramount. For instance, a mage may study the historical records of the Forbidden Schools to understand the dangers of necromancy; however, they may not use those records to argue that the prohibition on such magic was once relaxed and therefore remains valid. The Accords Desk maintains a "Graveyard of Statutes" where these repealed sections are stored. While they are available for study by licensed researchers—provided they have the express permission of the Innovators—they possess no power to grant rights or waive duties. Any petition for a magical variance that relies upon the authority of a dead citation will be summarily rejected without a hearing.

Furthermore, the use of dead citations in public discourse, particularly in taverns or common areas, is strictly regulated. While a scholar may discuss the history of the Accords, they must clearly preface such discussions with the "Historical Notice" disclaimer to ensure the public does not mistake old law for current mandate. The Aegis Magi are instructed to monitor for any attempts to weaponize defunct laws against the Guild's current standing. If a peer is found to be actively advocating for the restoration of a repealed school or practice by citing it as a living permit, they shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. See § 1.6 for the general rules of citation.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
The jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords is absolute within the Midlands and across all territories where the Guild maintains recognized sovereignty. This title, and all statutes contained herein, shall not be repealed, superseded, or rendered null by the mere existence of the Iron Mandate, nor by any proclamation issued by the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or any other external political entity. The Accords are a sovereign magical compact, not a civil contract subject to the whims of secular empires. Should an external power issue a decree that conflicts with the Accords, the Guild shall recognize only the Accords as the governing law for all mages under its protection. Any mage who attempts to obey the Iron Mandate in a manner that violates the Accords shall be deemed to be in breach of their oath to the Guild.

The Guild acknowledges that the Regal Empire and the Iron Legion may exert significant physical and economic pressure upon the Midlands. However, the magical infrastructure of the Accords is independent of the Mandate's administrative reach. No "shouting" by an Empire—whether expressed through military threat, economic sanction, or diplomatic coercion—constitutes a legal mechanism for the alteration of Guild law. The Accords Desk serves as a fortress of legal stability; it does not buckle under the weight of external demands. Mages who are pressured by Imperial agents to surrender their magical rights or to acknowledge the Mandate as a superior legal authority are to report such interactions to Archmage Veyra immediately.

Furthermore, any attempt by the Iron Legion to impose their "Mandate" laws upon the Guild's internal proceedings is to be treated as a hostile act of magical and political aggression. The Guild does not recognize the Iron Mandate as a valid source of magical regulation. While the Guild may engage in trade or diplomacy with entities subject to the Mandate, such interactions must be conducted under the "Foreign Exchange" protocols and must never involve the surrender of the Accords' jurisdiction. The stability of the Midlands depends upon the unwavering nature of these laws; if the Accords were to yield to every external shout, the very fabric of the Guild's authority would unravel. The Accords remain, as always, the primary and final word on the use of magic.

body.heading: § 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form; Dead Citations; Savings Against the Iron
body.text:
The provisions contained herein shall be construed in light of the historical annotations that follow each section, which are provided solely for interpretive guidance and do not constitute independent legal authority. These annotations reflect the original intent of the Drafting Committee at the time of enactment and may shed light on ambiguous terms or contested applications. They are to be cited only when necessary to clarify the plain meaning of the text, never as a substitute for statutory language itself.

Where any provision references another section of this Code that has since been repealed, amended beyond recognition, or simply does not exist in its current form, such reference shall be deemed "dead" and carries no operative effect unless expressly revived by subsequent legislation. In no event may a dead citation serve as the sole basis for imposing liability or granting relief absent clear evidentiary support linking it to an active duty. This principle ensures that practitioners are judged only upon existing law, not on ghost provisions long since expunged from the record.

Notwithstanding any contrary implication in this Code, nothing herein shall be construed to invalidate or override the Iron Mandate of the Regal Empire where such laws conflict with the express terms hereof. Where a dispute arises between competing jurisdictions—such as when an act occurs partly within the Autumnwood Hall and partly beyond its borders—the more restrictive standard shall prevail unless a specific exception applies under § 1405.3. In cases of genuine ambiguity regarding which regime controls, the burden falls upon the party asserting violation to prove that their conduct clearly violated applicable norms in all relevant forums.

The Desk reserves discretion to issue advisory opinions on novel situations not anticipated by the written text, provided such guidance does not contravene established principles or create undue hardship for regulated entities. These non-binding interpretations may evolve over time as circumstances dictate and should be consulted when facing unique challenges outside the scope of routine practice. However, they shall never supersede the authoritative weight of duly enacted statutes nor bind future iterations of this Code absent explicit incorporation by reference.

body.heading: Historical Annotations and Dead Citations
body.text:
§ 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form. All annotations appended to the text of this Code shall bear the prefix "Hist." followed by the year of enactment, e.g., Hist. 2078. Such annotations are not part of the operative provisions but serve as guidance for interpretation. Dead citations—references to repealed or superseded sections—are permitted where necessary to explain legislative history, provided they are clearly marked as non-binding. The Desk may issue supplementary notes on ambiguous historical contexts at its discretion.

Savings Against the Iron Mandate. Provisions of this Code that directly conflict with the Imperial Decree 8009-A (the "Iron Mandate") shall be deemed void to the extent of such conflict, unless explicitly validated by a subsequent ruling of the Autarch's High Council. In cases of apparent contradiction between the Accords and the Mandate, the more stringent standard prevails, unless overriding national security concerns dictate otherwise. The Desk retains authority to clarify such conflicts through binding precedent where feasible.

§ 1402.1 Application of Dead Code; Severability. Any section of this Code declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction shall be severed from the remainder without affecting the legality of other provisions. Where possible, the intent behind stricken language shall be preserved through reasonable construction consistent with applicable policy goals. If severance renders an entire subsection unenforceable, the Desk may draft remedial measures to restore functionality absent undue delay.

§ 1403.1 Interpretive Canons; Purpose of Law. In resolving ambiguities in this Code, courts shall favor interpretations that advance its stated purposes and policies over those that frustrate them. Literal readings giving rise to absurd or unjust results may be corrected through implied exceptions unless doing so would undermine core principles. The spirit of the law governs as much as its letter; equity informs every judgment rendered under these provisions.

§ 1404.1 Legislative Intent; Historical Context. Where textual analysis fails to yield clarity, extrinsic aids including committee reports, floor debates, and prior drafts may be consulted to discern legislative purpose. Such materials are admissible only when explicitly requested by a party and deemed relevant by the presiding officer. Courts shall avoid unnecessary resort to these sources absent genuine difficulty in applying plain language rules.

§ 1405.1 Presumptions; Burden of Proof. In proceedings brought under this Code, statutory presumptions apply as written unless rebutted by clear and convincing evidence. The burden of proof rests upon the party asserting a fact favorable to their position, except where expressly allocated otherwise by provision or rule. Failure to meet this burden results in dismissal of claims or defenses predicated thereon.

§ 1406.1 Judicial Discretion; Equitable Remedies. Judges retain broad discretion to fashion appropriate remedies tailored to the unique circumstances presented, including but not limited to injunctions, restitution, specific performance, and punitive damages. Such relief shall be granted sparingly and only when traditional monetary sanctions prove inadequate to redress harm inflicted upon persons or entities protected by these laws.

§ 1407.1 Standing; Who May Sue Only those directly aggrieved by a violation of this Code possess standing to initiate legal action, whether as individual plaintiffs or class representatives acting on behalf similarly situated parties. Proxy litigation absent demonstrable injury is strictly prohibited except in exceptional cases where public interest demands intervention. The Desk may designate amicus curiae advisors to assist in complex matters requiring specialized expertise beyond ordinary judicial competence.

§ 1408.1 Finality; Exhaustion of Remedies Parties must exhaust all available administrative appeals before seeking judicial review unless extraordinary circumstances justify immediate recourse to the courts. Failure to comply with this requirement bars further proceedings until proper exhaustion occurs, thereby preventing piecemeal adjudication and preserving institutional integrity. The Desk may waive these prerequisites upon a showing of good cause supported by substantial evidence.

§ 1409.1 Emergency Measures; Temporary Injunctions During periods of acute crisis threatening widespread harm, the Desk may issue emergency orders effective immediately without prior notice or hearing if strict necessity warrants such expedited action. Such measures shall remain in force only until formal proceedings can be convened and concluded, at which point their validity will be fully reviewed de novo. Parties aggrieved by emergency decrees retain full rights to contest them through established channels thereafter.

§ 1410.1 Compliance; Enforcement Mechanisms All persons subject to the obligations imposed herein shall take all reasonable steps necessary to achieve full compliance within prescribed timelines. Failure to do so may result in escalating penalties ranging from fines and license revocation up to imprisonment for willful defiance. The Desk maintains robust enforcement powers backed by armed security forces dedicated solely to ensuring adherence to these vital regulations governing magical practice throughout the realm.

body.heading: § 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form and Authority
body.text:
§ 1401.1 prescribes the standardized format for all historical annotations appended to this Code, ensuring clarity and uniformity in legal interpretation across all Mages' Guild jurisdictions. Each annotation must commence with a bolded header identifying the source material—whether textual passage, oral testimony, magical artifact inscription, or official record—and shall cite the relevant case law or precedent where applicable. Subsequent paragraphs shall then elaborate upon the factual context, logical deductions drawn therefrom, and any dissenting opinions recorded by participating magisters. All annotations must conclude with a signature line affixed by the presiding archmage or duly appointed clerk, thereby authenticating the document's official status under seal of the Autumnwood Accords Desk.

Dead citations shall be flagged prominently within the body text using brackets [ ] and accompanied by a concise explanatory note detailing why such references no longer hold legal validity in current practice. This includes obsolescence due to repeal, superseding legislation, or fundamental shifts in magical theory rendering prior rulings moot. Failure to identify dead citations may result in dismissal of subsequent arguments relying thereon, as courts will not permit parties to invoke phantom precedents absent explicit acknowledgement of their defunct nature. The burden rests squarely upon the asserting party to demonstrate why an outdated rule should nonetheless govern present-day disputes.

Savings provisions shall be meticulously crafted to preserve beneficial legal principles embedded within superseded statutes where feasible and consistent with overarching goals of fairness, equity, and public safety. Such savings clauses serve as bridges between eras of magical governance, allowing continuity of meaningful protections even as laws evolve. Where no direct analogue exists in extant legislation, judges retain discretion to fashion equitable remedies based on analogous provisions or general tenets of natural justice, always mindful of maintaining balance between innovation and stability in the ever-changing landscape of arcane jurisprudence.

It shall be further noted that this section does not purport to exhaustively enumerate every possible scenario requiring annotation; rather, it provides a framework adaptable to myriad contingencies arising from rapid technological advancement and societal transformation inherent to our field. As new challenges emerge, so too must our legal systems adapt accordingly, guided by wisdom gleaned from both past mistakes and triumphs alike. Only through such diligent stewardship can we ensure that the Autumnwood Accords continue to serve as a beacon of enlightened rule for generations yet unborn.

see § 1.4 Persons Bound; see § 100.3 Quorum of the Desk; under § 200.1 Licensure Required and related provisions governing professional conduct standards applicable to all registered practitioners subject to Accords oversight mechanisms outlined hereinabove with particular attention paid to ongoing education requirements designed to keep pace with developments in both theory and application within our dynamic discipline.

sections.title: Dead Citations
sections.brief: A repealed section may be cited as history, not as a permit.

body.heading: Dead Citations
body.text:
§ 1401.2 Dead Citations. A repealed section may be cited as history, not as a permit.

The integrity of the Autumnwood Accords rests upon the continuity of its own administrative evolution. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords Desk that the act of legislative repeal does not constitute a retroactive erasure of the facts of the past, nor does it grant a license for the continued application of the repealed substance. When a statute, decree, or sub-clause is struck from the active Codex, it is moved into the state of "Dead Citation." A mage or entity may reference such a section for the purposes of historical analysis, genealogical research of magical doctrine, or the demonstration of prior precedents; however, any attempt to invoke the legal protections, permissions, or obligations contained within that repealed section shall be deemed a nullity. The mere existence of a text in the archives does not grant it the force of law.

Furthermore, the citation of a Dead Citation in a formal petition or a Paradox Trial shall be interpreted by the presiding council as an admission of ignorance regarding current regulations. While the Archivists may allow the inclusion of such citations to provide context for the development of specific schools of magic—particularly those involving the transition from the Conservator-led restrictions to the Innovator-led permissions—the petitioner must explicitly state that the citation is for historical reference only. Any submission that seeks to use a repealed section as a basis for a current legal defense, a request for restricted research, or a claim of immunity shall be summarily dismissed. The Accords Desk shall not be bound by the logic of a defunct law, and the Aegis Magi are instructed to ignore any "rights" claimed under the authority of a Dead Citation.

This distinction is vital for maintaining the stability of the Midlands. If an old law regarding the handling of rift-energy were to be cited as a current permit, it could lead to catastrophic breaches that the current Accords were specifically designed to prevent. Therefore, any scholar seeking to utilize the data of a repealed section must ensure that their application clearly delineates between "historical fact" and "current mandate." See § 1.2 for the authority of the Desk to maintain these distinctions. Failure to comply with this distinction may result in a summary fine or a referral to the Paradox Trial for the willful subversion of current legal reality.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
§ 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate. This title does not repeal itself because an Empire shouted.

The jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords is sovereign and absolute within the established boundaries of the Midlands and the territories governed by the Archmage Veyra. It is hereby decreed that the Accords are not subject to the external pressures, declarations, or legislative overreach of the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or any other external geopolitical body. Specifically, this title serves as a permanent stay against the "Iron Mandate"—the legal framework imposed by the Empire and the Legion—asserting that the Accords do not recognize the Mandate as a superior legal authority. The Accords Desk shall not, under any circumstances, voluntarily cede its jurisdiction to the Iron Mandate, nor shall it allow the Mandate’s statutes to supersede the Guild’s internal regulations regarding the study of magic, the conduct of mages, or the distribution of magical assets.

Any attempt by external agents, including the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters, to argue that the Accords are superseded by the Mandate due to "geopolitical necessity" or "military cooperation" is strictly prohibited. The Accords are a binding agreement of the magical community, not a treaty of submission. While the Guild may engage in diplomacy with the Regal Empire, such diplomacy does not equate to a legal merger of codes. The Aegis Magi are authorized to use all necessary force to repel any attempt to enforce Mandate-specific laws on Guild grounds or upon any mage currently under the protection of the Accords. Any mage who attempts to "voluntarily" submit to the Iron Mandate while still holding a valid Guild license shall be investigated for potential treason against the Accords and may be subject to a Paradox Trial.

Moreover, the Accords Desk shall not be intimidated by the "shouting" of empires. The mere presence of Iron Legion forces or the threat of Imperial sanctions does not grant the Mandate the power to rewrite the internal laws of the Autumnwood Accords. If a conflict arises between a Mandate decree and an Accord statute, the Accord statute shall prevail in all matters of magical conduct and internal Guild governance. This title ensures that the delicate balance between the Conservators and the Innovators remains undisturbed by the crude legalisms of the outside world. The Guild’s internal friction is its own; the Mandate’s external pressure is a nuisance to be ignored or resisted, but never integrated. See § 1301.2 for the determination of penalties regarding the unauthorized importation of Mandate-governed mandates into the Midlands.

body.heading: § 1401.2 Dead Citations and Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
A provision formally repealed, annulled, or superseded by subsequent legislation shall not be deemed valid for any purpose whatsoever, except to evidence prior lawful conduct that may constitute a defense in ongoing proceedings. However, no repeal shall affect any vested rights acquired under the authority of such now-invalidated clause before its effective date, nor shall it impair pending causes of action accrued therefrom. This principle is hereby codified as an exception to the general rule against retroactive application of new statutes, grounded in the fundamental tenet that individuals must be afforded reasonable notice and opportunity to comply with legal mandates before facing penalty for non-compliance.

The Iron Mandate of the Regal Empire, while possessing extraterritorial force within its borders of origin, lacks recognition as binding law anywhere beyond those confines unless expressly adopted by local governing bodies. Consequently, any attempt to invoke provisions thereof in the courts or councils of this Realm shall be summarily dismissed without prejudice to underlying factual disputes. Parties relying upon such foreign enactments do so at their peril, bearing full responsibility for any adverse consequences arising from misplaced faith in their validity under domestic law. This safeguard exists to preserve the integrity of our own legislative processes and prevent undue influence from abroad upon matters of local concern.

Where a previously valid citation has since been invalidated due to changes in status or jurisdiction, its continued invocation may still yield favorable outcomes if supported by competent evidence establishing compliance at the relevant time. Such instances shall be treated as savings clauses, preserving accrued benefits despite subsequent alterations in legal landscape. The burden rests upon the asserting party to demonstrate prima facie entitlement under the former regime, after which opposing interests must rebut with contrary proof to defeat their claim. This balanced approach ensures fairness while maintaining respect for the primacy of current law.

Finally, it is hereby clarified that no provision herein shall be construed to validate any act previously prohibited solely because a regulating authority failed to timely enforce its prohibitions upon discovery thereof. Laches alone does not confer immunity from liability; rather, such circumstances may serve merely as mitigating factors in determining appropriate remedies or penalties imposed upon offending parties. The right to seek redress remains intact regardless of delays in governmental action, subject only to equitable considerations relevant to the specific facts at hand. This position underscores our commitment to holding all actors accountable for their actions while acknowledging practical limitations inherent in administering justice effectively across diverse contexts.

body.heading: Dead Citations and Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
§ 1401.2 Dead Citations and Savings Against the Iron Mandate

A provision in this Code that has been repealed or superseded may be cited as evidence of legislative intent or historical practice, but not as a grant of authority to violate current law. See § 1.9 (Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal); § 1001.2 (Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets). Any conflict between this Code and the Iron Mandate is resolved by reference to the latter's higher order status under international treaty obligations, unless explicitly exempted here. Under § 500.2 (Unscheduled Warfare) and § 600.3 (Rogue Spellcasting), no action may be taken that would undermine the sovereignty of Veyra or destabilize the Midlands without explicit consent.

The Desk reserves the right to declare any section void ab initio upon finding it contrary to public policy, as defined in § 1.7(b). This includes but is not limited to provisions facilitating magical slavery, ritual murder, or gross violation of bodily autonomy. Such determinations shall be made by majority vote following full disclosure and opportunity for rebuttal. See also § 200.4 (Suspension and Lapse) regarding automatic termination of powers upon breach of core tenets.

Nothing in this Code shall be construed to authorize the use of forbidden schools of magic under any circumstances, except as expressly provided herein. The prohibition against necromancy, blood sorcery, and similar practices remains absolute, reflecting the fundamental values of Autumnwood society. Violation constitutes a serious offense subject to immediate arrest and trial by peers. Refer to § 300.2 (Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts) for detailed guidance on permissible vs prohibited techniques.

In emergency situations where delay would cause irreparable harm, any licensed caster may take necessary action without prior authorization, provided they later justify their conduct to the Desk. This limited exception does not excuse failure to comply with subsequent orders or report the incident fully within forty-eight hours. See § 100.5 (Conflict of Interest in Casting) for related provisions on disclosure obligations.

The provisions herein are intended solely for the guidance of law-abiding citizens and shall not be used as a shield against prosecution under applicable statutes, treaties, or customary practices. The Desk retains plenary authority to interpret and enforce this Code as it deems necessary to protect public safety and magical order. Any challenges must be raised through proper channels and may result in sanctions up to and including revocation of licensure. Consult § 1301.2 (Penalties) for a full list of disciplinary measures available to the Guild.

This section shall come into effect upon final approval by Archmage Veyra and publication in the Autumnwood Gazette. Previous versions are hereby rescinded with immediate effect, except as preserved herein. All parties acknowledge receipt and understanding of these terms and conditions governing magical practice within the jurisdiction of the Accords Desk. Failure to comply may result in severe consequences under both civil and criminal law. For further assistance or clarification, contact the nearest Guild office directly. We thank you for your cooperation in maintaining a safe and prosperous community for all.

body.heading: Revocation and Nullification of Prior Enactments
body.text:
§ 1401.2 Dead Citations and Savings Against the Iron Mandate

All provisions of prior laws, statutes, ordinances, or regulations that are inconsistent with this Code are hereby repealed to the extent of such inconsistency. No enactment shall be deemed invalid solely on account of any defect in its formality or procedure unless expressly stated herein. However, no provision of this Code shall operate to validate any act, transaction, or agreement that was void under applicable law at the time it was made. The rights and obligations of parties hereto shall continue to be governed by the laws and principles existing immediately before the effective date hereof, except as otherwise provided in this section. This includes all rules, regulations, and orders issued by the Iron Mandate or any other authority having jurisdiction over the matter. Nothing herein shall affect the validity of any contract or obligation entered into prior to the enactment of this Code, unless such contract or obligation is expressly declared void by this Code. Any pending proceedings before courts, tribunals, or administrative agencies shall continue in accordance with the laws and procedures applicable at the time such proceedings were commenced, except as otherwise provided herein. This section does not impair any right accrued under prior law, nor does it affect the validity of any judgment rendered thereunder. All provisions of this Code shall be construed to give effect to its purpose and intent, which is to establish a comprehensive regulatory regime for the use and control of magic within the jurisdiction. Nothing in this section shall be construed as limiting the inherent powers of the governing body to enact such additional laws or regulations as may be necessary to carry out its duties under this Code. Any conflict between this Code and other laws, rules, regulations, or ordinances shall be resolved by applying this Code unless otherwise expressly provided herein. This provision ensures continuity and stability in the legal framework while allowing for necessary updates and refinements over time. It also protects against unintended consequences of legislative changes by preserving existing rights and obligations where appropriate. The savings clause serves to maintain the integrity of prior transactions and agreements, recognizing that parties may have relied on the law as it existed at the time of their dealings. By specifying that nothing in this Code invalidates pre-existing contracts or judgments absent express declaration, it provides certainty for all concerned and prevents disruption of established commercial arrangements. This careful balancing act reflects the complex interplay between legislative innovation and respect for vested interests inherent in any comprehensive regulatory scheme.

sections.title: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
sections.brief: This title does not repeal itself because an Empire shouted.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
It is hereby established by the sovereign authority of the Autumnwood Accords that this Codex of Law remains the primary and binding legal framework for all practitioners of the arcane within the jurisdiction of the Midlands and the territories served by the Guild. The existence of external legislative bodies, specifically those of the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, shall not constitute a valid mechanism for the revocation, amendment, or repeal of the Accords. Any decree issued by the Iron Legion or the Regal Empire—collectively referred to herein as "External Mandates"—that seeks to supersede, diminish, or nullify the rights and responsibilities of the Guild members is deemed legally void and unenforceable within the sovereign magical space of the Autumnwood.

The Accords recognize that the Iron Mandate, passed by the Midlands Diet on the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF, represents an emergency measure of secular and martial nature. While the Guild acknowledges the existence of the Iron Legion and the Regal Empire as geopolitical entities, the magical laws governing the manipulation of the Weave, the conduct of the Aegis Magi, and the adjudication of the Paradox Trial are not subject to the whims of secular military authority. No shout from an Emperor, no proclamation from a General, and no emergency decree from a Diet may strip a mage of their standing under the Accords, nor may such decrees impose restrictions on the practice of the Unsanctioned Arts that were not already established by the Conservators and the Innovators.

Furthermore, any attempt by an external power to enforce the Iron Mandate upon a Guild member in a manner that conflicts with the Accords shall be viewed as a violation of the Sovereign Mediation of Archmage Veyra. In instances where the Iron Legion attempts to seize magical artifacts or enforce martial labor on mages, the Guild shall maintain its right to sanctuary and legal autonomy. The Accords do not bow to the "emergency" status of the Iron Mandate; the stability of the Weave is a permanent concern, not a temporary one subject to the shifting tides of imperial warfare. Consequently, the provisions of this Codex shall persist in perpetuity, regardless of the political climate, the presence of the Silver Flame, or the expansionist desires of the Regal Empire.

Any practitioner who attempts to use the Iron Mandate as a legal defense for the violation of a Guild statute shall be found in breach of the Accords. The Guild does not recognize "Imperial Necessity" as a valid excuse for the unauthorized use of forbidden schools or the evasion of the Paradox Trial. See § 1.2 for the definition of Enacting Authority. Should an external entity attempt to impose a competing legal reality, the Aegis Magi are authorized to defend the integrity of the Accords with all necessary arcane measures. The Accords are the law of the land; the Iron Mandate is merely the noise of the world outside our gates. This title does not repeal itself because an Empire shouted.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Continued
body.text:
§ 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate

The provisions herein are without prejudice to any rights, privileges, or defenses that may exist at law or in equity against claims arising under the Iron Mandate of the Regal Empire, whether by statute, charter, custom, or otherwise. No rule within this Accords shall be construed to diminish or impair such protections unless expressly waived in writing and voluntarily executed by the affected party with full knowledge of their rights hereinbefore enjoyed.

It is recognized that certain obligations imposed by the Iron Mandate may conflict with duties owed under this Codex. In instances where such a clash arises, the following principles shall govern resolution: first, any ambiguity or doubt regarding scope or application shall be resolved most favorably toward preserving the integrity of existing legal relationships established prior to imposition of the foreign decree; second, no penalty or sanction shall be enforced until due process has been afforded consistent with this Accords' standards for fair hearing and adequate representation; third, all claims must be adjudicated on their merits before any remedial action is taken, allowing full opportunity for defense and counterargument.

Parties bound hereby acknowledge that while they accept the general authority of the Autumnwood Council over matters pertaining to magical practice within its jurisdiction, this acceptance does not extend to surrendering fundamental liberties guaranteed by prior law. The Accords are intended as a regulatory framework, not an instrument of domination or subjugation.
