Accordingly, any provision herein found to violate core constitutional principles shall be deemed void ab initio unless and until amended through proper legislative channels without prejudice to accrued rights.

Nothing in these Articles shall be interpreted to limit remedies available at common law, including but not limited to actions for breach of contract, tortious interference, unjust enrichment, or equitable relief as appropriate. The parties agree to maintain open lines of communication concerning potential conflicts between their respective regimes and to cooperate in good faith toward mutually satisfactory resolutions when disputes arise. Where cooperation proves futile or impracticable, each retains the right to seek redress through established judicial forums without waiving any claim for damages sustained thereby.

By signing below, all signatories covenant to uphold the spirit and letter of this agreement while reserving their inherent rights as free individuals subject only to reasonable constraints necessary for maintaining public order and safety. Should circumstances change materially or new technologies emerge affecting applicability thereof, such matters shall be addressed via amendment proceedings conducted in accordance with standard parliamentary procedure outlined elsewhere herein.

Signed and sealed on this ____ day of ____________, year ________, by authority duly conferred upon me pursuant to the terms hereof.

[Seal of the Autumnwood Accords]

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Administration
body.text:
§ 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Continued
This Subpart clarifies the limits and exceptions to the binding force of the Iron Mandate under specific circumstances. Where provisions of this Accord conflict with those of the Empire's edicts, priority shall be determined by reference to § 1.5 Relation to Other Law, which establishes that earlier in time prevails absent contrary intent. The Guild Desk retains authority to declare certain Imperial mandates unenforceable within its jurisdiction should they violate fundamental principles of magical ethics enshrined herein. Such determinations require a two-thirds vote and must be published with full rationale.

No provision of the Iron Mandate shall supersede rights accrued prior to its promulgation, nor shall it alter vested interests protected under this Accord's original enactment. Parties may contract around mandatory rules where expressly permitted by law, provided such agreements do not contravene public policy or endanger the general welfare. In matters of dispute regarding applicability of Imperial versus Guild law, the Desk shall appoint an impartial arbiter whose decision is final and binding absent successful appeal on procedural grounds alone.

This section ensures that while this Accord respects the supremacy of Imperial statute where necessary, it preserves essential protections for practitioners operating under its terms. The delicate balance between local autonomy and central control remains a cornerstone of stable magical governance in these lands. Future amendments shall address any gaps or ambiguities arising from evolving political realities without compromising core safeguards established at the founding.

see § 1001.2 Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets; see § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure; see § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time; see § 1301.2 Penalties; Sunrise Accrual"

body.heading: § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Administrative Burden and Enforcemen
body.text:
Notwithstanding the broad language of the Iron Mandate, practical considerations of administrative capacity and judicial economy may preclude its full enforcement in certain circumstances. Where compliance with the Mandate would impose an undue burden on the Guild's ability to function effectively, the Desk is authorized to issue a temporary suspension of specific provisions upon written finding that such action serves the greater good of magical safety and order. This power shall be exercised sparingly and only after consultation with relevant stakeholders. Any such suspension must specify its scope, duration, and conditions for renewal or termination. The Desk retains discretion to reinstate full Mandate compliance at any time should circumstances warrant it.

Furthermore, the Guild may petition the Sovereign Archmage for a stay of enforcement pending review of alleged violations by an independent arbitral tribunal composed of neutral mages of recognized expertise. Such petitions must be supported by sworn affidavits demonstrating good faith efforts to comply with the Mandate's requirements prior to any alleged breach. The tribunal shall have authority to examine all relevant facts and render a binding decision within thirty days of constitution. Pending final adjudication, normal Guild operations shall continue unimpeded unless the Sovereign determines otherwise in her sole discretion. This expedited review process reflects the urgent need for swift resolution of disputes involving potent magical threats while maintaining due process protections for accused parties.

In addition to these administrative safeguards, the Guild may invoke the doctrine of impossibility where literal adherence to the Mandate would render compliance objectively impossible under extant circumstances. For example, if a particular spell or technique is inherently incompatible with current scientific understanding or technological capabilities, the Desk may permit provisional use pending further research and development. Such exceptions shall be narrowly construed and subject to rigorous oversight by qualified experts appointed by the Sovereign Archmage. The Guild retains ultimate authority to determine whether claimed impossibility warrants granting of an exemption under these provisions.

Finally, the Iron Mandate does not supersede applicable international treaties or agreements entered into by the Guild prior to its adoption. Any conflict between the Mandate and binding treaty obligations shall be resolved in favor of upholding those earlier commitments unless explicitly modified by subsequent agreement among all signatories. The Desk maintains responsibility for monitoring compliance with both domestic statutes and external accords, exercising appropriate remedies as needed to preserve the integrity of the Guild's legal framework and protect against transnational threats to magical security. This balanced approach ensures respect for established legal traditions while adapting to evolving challenges posed by unchecked magical experimentation.

see § 1301.2 Penalties; see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; see § 1.5 Relation to Other Law. Under § 1.6 Definitions, the term "administrative burden" refers to practical obstacles that impede reasonable compliance with legal requirements despite good faith efforts. As established in § 300.4 Reclassification, provisions may be temporarily modified where strict enforcement would defeat their intended purpose. This principle is applied here to preserve essential Guild functions while safeguarding public welfare. See also § 1.7 Construction; Aggregation of Conduct regarding the holistic interpretation of statutory language. Under § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill, artificial entities may serve as proxies for natural persons in limited contexts when warranted by exigent circumstances. Such arrangements remain subject to stringent oversight and accountability measures.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Administrative Burden and Enforcement
body.text:
§ 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Administrative Burden and Enforcement

The Autumnwood Accords Desk acknowledges that the provisions herein may appear to conflict with certain statutes promulgated by rival authorities, notably the Empire's Iron Mandate. However, it is a fundamental principle of legal construction that later-in-time rules prevail over earlier ones when enacted by bodies of equal sovereign standing. See § 1.8 Effective Date; Savings. The Accords were finalized and ratified on [REDACTED], superseding any prior decrees inconsistent with their terms.

Furthermore, the Desk notes that direct application of the Iron Mandate to internal Guild affairs would impose an unreasonably burdensome administrative load on both the Conservators and Innovators alike. Such mandates require extensive reporting requirements, periodic inspections, and the submission of detailed operational logs — all of which would divert precious resources from research and development efforts already stretched thin by ongoing conflicts with external forces. See § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; Aggregation of Conduct. To avoid this untenable situation, the Desk has adopted a pragmatic approach: it will not actively enforce provisions that directly contradict Imperial edicts so long as Guild members operate within their authorized scope under valid permits issued pursuant to these Accords.

That said, this does not constitute carte blanche for rogue mages to flout established laws at will. The Desk retains its right and duty to investigate and prosecute violations occurring outside the bounds of sanctioned activities — particularly where such actions threaten public safety or undermine the stability of the region as a whole. See § 200.1 Licensure Required; § 300.4 Reclassification. Guild members are expected to uphold their oaths and refrain from engaging in illicit practices that could draw unwanted attention from hostile powers.

In sum, while the Accords cannot fully insulate themselves from external pressures, they do provide a necessary framework for orderly operation amidst chaos. By striking a careful balance between regulatory oversight and operational autonomy, the Desk hopes to foster an environment where innovation may flourish without sacrificing security or propriety. This delicate equilibrium shall be maintained so long as all parties remain committed to the shared goal of preserving peace in Autumnwood — however turbulent that path may prove to be.

"Law is not a shackle but a compass; guide yourself wisely lest you stray beyond redemption." - Archmage Veyra, in her inaugural address to the Guild Council.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Administrative Burden and Enforcement — Continued
body.text: § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate — Administrative Burden and Enforcement. The inclusion in this Codex of provisions expressly incompatible with the laws of the Regal Empire or its subordinate territories does not constitute a repudiation of those external statutes, nor does it abrogate any obligations arising therefrom. Rather, such clauses operate solely as savings to preserve the integrity and coherence of this Accords regime where strict application would otherwise produce absurd results or render the whole unenforceable under principles of construction familiar in arcane jurisprudence. See § 1.5 Relation to Other Law; see also § 702.4 Impossibility of Compliance. Where the Imperial Mandate demands actions that contravene core tenets of this legal order — such as requiring mages to disclose proprietary formulas or submit to invasive inspections — the Desk shall deem those requirements void ab initio, provided that an equivalent standard of public safety and fairness may be achieved by alternative means consistent with Guild policy. This saving clause is not intended to shield violators from consequences but rather to prevent the Accords from being undermined by self-defeating mandates; it reflects a pragmatic recognition that no code can survive if forced into submission to forces beyond its control. Underlying this approach lies the principle that laws are instruments of governance, not shibboleths to be worshipped blindly; where rigidity breeds chaos, flexibility preserves order. Thus, provisions purporting to override this Codex shall be treated as null and unenforceable within its sphere, unless they can be reconciled therewith through proper legal interpretation. For further guidance on the scope of such savings clauses in practice, reference is made to the opinions rendered by the Autumnwood Accords Desk over the years, which collectively illustrate how this nuanced balancing act may be applied to novel circumstances as they arise. Ultimately, the goal remains constant: to maintain a stable and just magical society capable of adapting to change without losing its soul. See § 1.7 Construction — Aggregation of Conduct; see also § 902.3 Waiver by Conduct.

sections.title: Exclusions from Savings Clauses

body.heading: Exclusions from Savings Clauses
body.text:
This section establishes the procedural framework by which an accused person may invoke the protections afforded herein, particularly in instances where their conduct impinges upon the interests of the Guild or its constituents. The invocation must be made at the earliest practicable opportunity following receipt of notice of potential liability, unless extraordinary circumstances preclude timely action. Such circumstances must be substantiated by credible evidence and articulated with particularity in a written submission to the Accords Desk Clerk.

In determining whether an accused has satisfied the threshold for related requirements, the Clerk shall evaluate all relevant factors, including but not limited to the nature and severity of the alleged misconduct, the accused's prior record if any, their demonstrated commitment to rectifying past wrongs, and the likelihood of future compliance with Guild mandates. This holistic assessment is intended to balance the need for accountability against the principles of fairness and proportionality enshrined in the Accords.

A key component of fulfilling related requirements involves the submission of a detailed remediation plan tailored to the specific circumstances of each case. Such plans may include voluntary surrender of contested assets, payment of restitution or fines, participation in educational programs focused on ethical conduct within magical practice, and acceptance of ongoing monitoring by designated Guild officials. The adequacy of proposed remedies shall be judged on their ability to effectively address the root causes of non-compliance while safeguarding the integrity and stability of the broader magical community.

It is imperative that all parties involved approach these proceedings with a spirit of cooperation and good faith, recognizing their shared responsibility for maintaining order amidst the complexities inherent in the pursuit of arcane knowledge. By adhering diligently to the procedures outlined herein, both accusers and accused contribute to the continued evolution and refinement of this vital legal instrument, ensuring its enduring utility as a cornerstone of justice under Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Exclusions from Savings Clauses
body.text:
The provisions herein shall govern all matters not explicitly addressed in the preceding sections but deemed essential to the proper administration of these Accords, including yet not limited to procedural adjuncts, evidentiary standards, and limitations on jurisdictional scope. Nothing contained in this Part 14 shall be construed to abrogate or impair any rights established by common law, custom, or prior rulings unless expressly superseded by text herein.

As a threshold matter, all filings submitted under these Accords must bear the official seal of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, affixed by competent authority in accordance with § 1.9. Absence of such authentication renders any document void ab initio for lack of requisite formality. Furthermore, each submission shall be accompanied by a sworn affidavit executed by the proponent attesting to the veracity of all stated representations and certifications contained therein. Failure to include this affidavit constitutes grounds for immediate rejection without further review.

In instances where ambiguity arises regarding the applicability of these provisions, the Desk shall issue binding interpretations pursuant to § 100.6, which shall carry full force and effect until amended or revoked by subsequent ruling. Such interpretations may be sought via formal petition filed in triplicate with supporting arguments and any relevant precedent cited. Costs associated with such petitions shall be borne equally between petitioner and respondent unless otherwise ordered by the Desk for cause shown.

The jurisdiction of this Codex extends only to matters directly arising from its operation or enforcement, excluding unrelated disputes or collateral issues not germane to the primary subject matter. Any attempt to broaden the scope beyond these defined bounds shall result in dismissal with prejudice. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Desk retains inherent authority to investigate and address any circumstances that may undermine the integrity of the Accords as a whole, acting sua sponte when necessary to preserve the public interest.

Finally, nothing herein shall be construed to limit the rights of good faith parties under applicable law regarding equitable relief or damages for breach. The remedies outlined in these provisions are cumulative and not exclusive, allowing affected entities to pursue additional avenues for redress as warranted by the facts and circumstances of each case. This inclusive language ensures comprehensive protection against all forms of unlawful conduct within the Guild's purview, safeguarding both individual rights and collective welfare alike.

SEE ALSO: § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill; § 300.4 Reclassification; § 500.1 Field Casting for Value. UNDER § 1.7 Aggregation of Conduct and § 100.4 Records of Speech, all actions taken under these Accords shall be meticulously documented to ensure transparency and accountability in the administration of magical affairs throughout the Midlands region.

body.heading: § 1401.5 Conflicting Provisions and Supplementary Interpretation
body.text:
In instances where this Codex contains conflicting provisions or ambiguities that cannot be resolved through standard textual analysis, the following principles shall govern interpretation: First, any express provision controlling a particular matter shall prevail over general provisions, regardless of their apparent hierarchy. Second, where two sections appear to conflict, the later-enacted section shall control, unless explicitly repealed by specific language. Third, all uncertainties must be construed in favor of public safety and the orderly administration of magic, disfavoring any interpretation that would endanger lives or destabilize society. Fourth, custom and usage prevailing at the time a contract is made may inform its meaning where terms are ambiguous but not where they are clear. Finally, nothing herein shall be deemed to limit common law rights or remedies available under applicable statute, except as expressly precluded by specific language within this Part. These rules of construction serve only to clarify the intent of the Accords and do not create new substantive obligations absent clear textual support. Any dispute arising from conflicting provisions shall be resolved by a majority vote of the Autumnwood Accords Desk after consultation with legal counsel and technical experts as deemed appropriate under the circumstances. This supplementary framework ensures that this Codex remains adaptable to evolving magical practices while maintaining its core purpose of protecting persons, property, and public order.

see § 105.6 Rule of Last Resort; see § 205.4 Ambiguities Resolved Against Drafters; see § 305.2 Custom Usage as Supplemental Evidence.

body.heading: § 1401.6 Severability and Remedial Construction
body.text:
In the event that any provision or section of this Code is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable under applicable law, such determination shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining portions of this document. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the invalid portion shall be deemed severed from this Code, and the remainder shall continue in full force and effect as if the severance had never occurred. Where a specific provision is found to be unenforceable for reasons beyond mere illegality (e.g., impracticality or absurdity), it shall be construed and applied to achieve what was intended by its drafters, provided such interpretation does not contravene public policy or statutory mandates.

Further, nothing in this Code shall be construed to impair the right of any party to seek equitable relief or other remedies available at law or in equity. In no event shall any waiver of rights hereunder affect the ability of a party to assert any claim or defense that arose prior to such waiver. This section is intended to preserve the integrity and completeness of this legal instrument, ensuring that technical defects do not undermine its substantive purposes. All matters not expressly covered herein shall be governed by the laws of the Jurisdiction, as interpreted by the competent courts thereof."

body.heading: § 1401.7 Supplemental Interpretation and Related Provisions
body.text:
In addition to the historical annotations and form requirements set forth herein, all filings shall conform to established standards for magical resonance and semantic clarity to ensure accurate processing by the Guild's automated systems. Filings that fail to meet these technical specifications may be returned for revision without prejudice to the underlying claim or defense. The Desk reserves the right to reject any submission deemed structurally deficient or potentially disruptive to the integrity of the Accords' legal framework.

Where multiple provisions appear to conflict, the interpretation shall favor the outcome most consistent with the spirit and purpose of this Codex as a whole. In cases of ambiguity regarding the scope of authority granted herein, such questions shall be referred to the full membership of the Autumnwood Accords for final determination. No single clause may be read in isolation; rather, each must be understood within the context of its neighbors and the overarching objectives of magical governance established by this foundational document.

It is further provided that nothing contained in these Articles shall be construed to limit or impede the inherent powers vested in the Archmage Sovereign by virtue of her office under the original Charter of Autumnwood. The Desk acts as an administrative arm of that higher authority and must operate within its bounds while fulfilling its duties efficiently and impartially. Any actions taken beyond the scope of delegated power shall be null and void ab initio unless ratified retroactively by a majority vote of the Assembly.

Wherever this Codex refers to "the Guild," such term includes all constituent bodies, officers, clerks, and authorized representatives acting in furtherance of its mission. Similarly, references to "members" encompass both individual practitioners licensed under the Accords and corporate entities operating within their framework. This inclusive definition ensures that obligations and benefits flow seamlessly across the entire ecosystem of regulated magic without gaps or loopholes.

Finally, all provisions herein shall remain in full force and effect until expressly superseded by subsequent legislation enacted through proper procedures. Previous editions of this document are hereby rescinded in their entirety, with any inconsistencies resolved in favor of the most recent iteration approved by the competent authorities. The Desk undertakes to maintain a current copy available for public inspection at all reasonable times during normal business hours.

body.heading: § 1401.8 Interpretive Canons and Supplementary Principles
body.text:
In construing the provisions herein, the following interpretive canons shall apply to resolve ambiguities or gaps not explicitly addressed by the text: (a) The principle of lenity dictates that any doubt regarding a provision's meaning shall be resolved in favor of the accused; (b) The doctrine of ejusdem generis holds that general words following specific terms are limited to things of the same kind as those specifics. For instance, "other magical practices" appearing alongside "telekinesis and pyrokinesis" encompasses only analogous arts, not unrelated phenomena such as divination or healing; (c) The rule against surplusage prohibits reading provisions in isolation when their combined operation yields a more coherent whole. Thus, § 1401.3's valuation mandate must be read harmoniously with § 1401.2's prohibition on altered goods, not as a contradictory exception thereto; and (d) The canon of consistent construction requires that identical terms bear the same meaning throughout the document unless context clearly indicates otherwise. Consequently, "magic" in § 1401.6 refers to all supernatural phenomena governed by this Code, not merely spells cast by licensed practitioners.

Supplementary principles further inform the application of these rules: (a) The purpose of a provision shall guide its construction where language permits multiple reasonable interpretations. For example, § 1401.7's requirement for full disclosure serves to protect consumers from hidden dangers and ensure informed consent; thus, ambiguities in "material facts" should be resolved to maximize transparency. (b) The presumption against absurdity disfavors readings that produce illogical or unreasonable results. A literal application of § 1401.5's ban on transfigured items would render countless everyday objects unusable, so the provision must be understood to prohibit only those alterations affecting an item's value or safety. (c) The rule of effectiveness mandates interpreting provisions in a manner that achieves their intended goals rather than frustrating them. Since § 1401.8 aims to combat fraudulent practices, any ambiguity favoring fraudsters should be resolved against them. Finally, the doctrine of implied powers recognizes that the Authority possesses inherent authority to adopt reasonable regulations necessary to carry out its statutory duties, even when not explicitly enumerated in this Code. These interpretive canons and supplementary principles shall operate together as a unified framework for understanding the full scope and intent of these laws."

*Note: This page establishes general rules of construction applicable to all provisions within Part 14, ensuring consistent interpretation across diverse circumstances.*

body.heading: § 1101.5 Related Requirements and Collateral Obligations
body.text:
No transaction involving magical goods or services shall be deemed complete until all ancillary obligations attendant upon the exchange have been fully satisfied, whether known to the parties at the time of agreement or discovered thereafter by reasonable diligence. This provision ensures that the integrity of the market remains intact by preventing hidden liabilities from undermining future dealings and public safety.

Where a sale includes items subject to prior claims—such as cursed artifacts bearing residual enchantments, enchanted livestock with unrecorded breeding rights, or land parcels encumbered by ancient pacts—the vendor shall warrant free of such encumbrances at the time title passes. Failure to disclose known defects constitutes fraud under § 1001.4 and may render the contract voidable at the option of the buyer. However, latent defects discovered post-closing do not automatically rescind the agreement; rather, they give rise to a claim for damages proportional to the loss in value suffered by the purchaser.

In cases involving multi-part transactions where several goods or services are intertwined—such as a contract providing both magical equipment and instruction on its use—the entire bargain must be performed before any installment payment is due. Partial performance does not trigger partial release unless expressly stipulated in writing. This rule protects buyers from being locked into unfavorable terms mid-stream and prevents vendors from extracting additional concessions once they have invested resources into the deal.

Special provisions apply when related requirements involve third-party rights or regulatory approvals. For example, importing restricted magical materials may require permits from multiple jurisdictions; failure to secure these before shipment makes delivery a breach of contract regardless of actual receipt. Similarly, if a commissioned spell fails due to non-compliance with guild safety standards, the caster bears responsibility for correcting the oversight at their own expense.

The parties are obligated to cooperate in good faith to fulfill all conditions precedent attached to the agreement, including providing necessary access, information, or assistance within a reasonable timeframe. Delays caused by one party's neglect shall not excuse performance unless excused under force majeure doctrines outlined elsewhere in these Accords. Good faith cooperation extends beyond mere literal compliance; it demands proactive communication and problem-solving when unforeseen obstacles arise during execution of the contract.

Ultimately, this section serves as a safeguard against incomplete or defective transactions that could jeopardize public welfare or undermine confidence in magical commerce. By mandating full satisfaction of all duties before final consideration passes, the Accords promote fairness, transparency, and accountability throughout the lifecycle of every magical deal struck under their authority. See also § 1001.2 Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets; § 300.1 Schedules of Arts for further guidance on regulatory compliance obligations.

body.heading: § 1102.1 Conveyance and Ownership Interests in Magical Artifacts
body.text:
This Part governs the transfer, sale, and ownership of magical items and artifacts. All transactions must be conducted through registered intermediaries to ensure proper titling and disclosure of hidden qualities. Unregistered transfers are void ab initio and subject to seizure by the Guild's enforcement arm. The provisions herein apply regardless of whether the item is tangible or intangible in nature.

§ 1102.2 Disclosures Regarding Magical Properties
Sellers must fully disclose all known magical properties, limitations, and potential hazards associated with an item prior to closing. Failure to do so constitutes fraud under § 1102.3 and may result in rescission of the contract along with punitive damages. Buyers are encouraged to seek independent verification through licensed appraisers before finalizing any transaction. The burden of proof for full disclosure rests solely upon the seller.

§ 1102.3 Fraudulent Concealment and Warranty Disclaimers
Any attempt to conceal or misrepresent an item's true nature renders the entire sale null and void. Sellers cannot waive their obligations through fine print or verbal disclaimers. The law implies a warranty of honest representation in every magical goods transaction, regardless of what the parties may agree otherwise. Exceptions exist only where explicitly authorized by statute or mutual consent in writing.

§ 1102.4 Titles and Registration Requirements
All transfers of magical property must be recorded with the Guild's Registry within thirty days to establish clear title. Unregistered items are deemed res nullius until properly documented, allowing any party to claim ownership. This rule applies whether the item is being sold outright or leased for a fixed term. The Registry maintains an exhaustive database of all registered artifacts and their current owners.

§ 1102.5 Restrictions on Resale and Transfer
Certain classes of magical items are subject to ongoing restrictions even after transfer. These include weapons, cursed objects, and those containing sentient entities. Owners must comply with all applicable laws regarding possession and use. Violations may result in confiscation by authorities along with criminal penalties. Sellers remain liable for any illegal activities conducted using their products.

§ 1102.6 Dispute Resolution Procedures
Disputes arising under this Part shall be resolved through binding arbitration administered by the Guild's Commercial Tribunal. Litigation is prohibited except in extraordinary circumstances approved by the Tribunal Chair. Arbitrators must possess expertise in both law and magical theory to ensure fair adjudication. Their decisions are final and enforceable throughout the realm. Parties waive any right to appeal or retry the matter.

§ 1102.7 Enforcement Powers
The Guild's enforcement officers have broad powers to inspect, seize, and confiscate suspected illegal items at any time without warrant. They may also compel testimony under oath regarding past transactions. Non-compliance results in immediate arrest and prosecution for contempt of law. Officers act with immunity from civil suit while executing their duties in good faith. Resistance leads to enhanced charges.

§ 1102.8 International Trade Provisions
Cross-border sales are heavily regulated due to varying national laws and cultural sensitivities. Export licenses may be required along with proof of lawful origin. Dual-use items pose special risks and warrant additional scrutiny. Violations carry severe penalties including permanent bans from the marketplace. Parties are responsible for researching applicable foreign regulations before initiating transactions abroad.

§ 1102.9 Consumer Protection Standards
Buyers enjoy robust protections against predatory practices in the magical goods market. Unfair terms, hidden fees, or deceptive pricing are strictly prohibited. Sellers must provide accurate descriptions and demonstrate functionality before acceptance. Refunds may be granted if items fail to meet specified criteria despite proper use. Disputes should be escalated promptly rather than ignored until too late.

§ 1102.10 Liability Limitations
While sellers bear substantial responsibilities, their liability is not unlimited. Force majeure events beyond reasonable control exempt them from default performance. Acts of God or unforeseen catastrophes may render contracts impossible to fulfill without fault on either side. In such cases, obligations terminate automatically upon proper notification. Damages are restricted to direct losses proven with documentary evidence.

"Magic isn't just a commodity - it's a force that can reshape reality itself. We must handle these transactions with utmost caution and integrity." - Archmage Veyra, Preface to the Codex of Magical Commerce. "The law exists not to hinder commerce but to ensure fairness and safety for all participants." - Clerk Elara Moonshadow, Autumnwood Accords Desk.

body.heading: § 1102.1 Conveyance and Ownership Interests in Magical Artifacts — Continued
body.text: The transfer of magical artifacts entails unique considerations beyond those governing ordinary chattel, necessitating specific provisions to address the peculiarities inherent to enchanted items. Under this section, any conveyance or assignment of ownership involving a magical artifact must be executed through formal documentation witnessed by two licensed arcane scribes and duly registered with the Autumnwood Accords Desk within ten days of execution. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements shall render the transaction void ab initio and expose the parties to punitive sanctions up to and including permanent sealing of their magical aptitudes. Furthermore, all such instruments must include comprehensive schedules itemizing the artifact's known properties, potential hazards, and any attached curses or protections, as stipulated in § 1101.3 regarding warranty disclaimers. This detailed disclosure is essential for protecting subsequent owners from unforeseen liabilities arising from the artifact's nature. The Desk retains authority to demand additional information or independent verification at its discretion prior to approving registration of the transfer. Violations of this section may result in civil penalties of up to one hundred thousand gold pieces and/or criminal prosecution under applicable laws governing fraud and misrepresentation. It is hereby declared that no magical artifact shall serve as valid consideration unless accompanied by full disclosure of all material facts pertaining to its condition, history, and effects. This principle applies regardless of whether the transaction involves sale, gift, exchange, or any other form of conveyance whatsoever. The overarching goal of these provisions is to ensure transparency and fairness in dealings involving magical items, thereby safeguarding both public safety and economic stability within the realm. By mandating strict adherence to registration protocols and full informational disclosure, the Accords seek to mitigate risks associated with the acquisition and possession of enchanted goods while facilitating legitimate commerce therein. Any attempt to circumvent these requirements shall be deemed a serious offense subject to the harshest penalties available under law. Thus stands this section as a cornerstone of responsible magical artifact management within the greater community governed by the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: § 1102.1 Conveyance and Ownership Interests in Magical Artifacts – Continued
body.text:
This section governs the transfer of title to enchanted objects, ensuring that magical properties do not undermine transactional clarity. Under § 1102.1(a), any sale or gift of a magically altered item must disclose all active enchantments known to the transferor. Failure to do so constitutes fraud under general statute and voids the contract ab initio. The burden of disclosure rests solely on the seller, who shall provide written certification of the artifact's condition upon request.

§ 1102.1(b) addresses the issue of residual curses or boons that may linger after transfer. Unless explicitly released by a qualified diviner, such effects remain attached to the object and bind all subsequent owners. This principle protects buyers from inheriting unintended liabilities while preventing sellers from offloading dangerous items without compensation. Any dispute over lingering magic shall be resolved via binding arbitration under § 1050.2.

Special provisions apply when conveying items with sentient or semi-sentient properties, such as animated constructs or golems. Under § 1102.1(c), the transferor must ensure that any embedded wills are either fulfilled or legally discharged before completion of sale. Unfulfilled contractual obligations owed by the item itself may override personal agreements between parties, creating third-party claims against both buyer and seller. This rule preserves the integrity of magical contracts even after ownership changes hands.

§ 1102.1(d) covers the unique case of heirlooms passed down through generations. Such items often carry familial protections or restrictions that cannot be overridden by ordinary means. Any attempt to break these bonds without proper authorization shall result in immediate revocation of title and potential criminal charges under § 1400.9(a). Families holding such artifacts are urged to register them with the Conservators for safekeeping, thereby avoiding costly litigation down the line.

Finally, § 1102.1(e) establishes a presumption against implied warranties in magical goods absent explicit agreement to the contrary. Unlike mundane merchandise, enchanted objects cannot be assumed to function perfectly upon delivery unless guaranteed in writing. Buyers must inspect items thoroughly before finalizing transactions and promptly report any defects discovered thereafter. Prompt notification preserves remedies; delay waives rights under § 1050.3(b).

This comprehensive framework ensures fair dealing in the complex marketplace of magical artifacts, balancing the interests of all parties involved while maintaining public safety standards set forth by the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: § 1101.6 Collateral Security and Subrogation Rights in Magical Transactions
body.text:
In the context of secured transactions involving magical assets, collateral security may extend beyond the primary item to include secondary obligations or rights held by the obligor. This includes, but is not limited to, future earnings from enchanted labor, residual effects of prior spells, or potential claims against third parties arising from the artifact's use. The creditor must disclose all such collateral interests at the time of agreement execution. Failure to do so renders any attempt to enforce them void ab initio.

Subrogation rights arise when a debtor fulfills an obligation by paying off another party who held a prior claim on the same magical asset. In such cases, the debtor assumes the position of the original creditor and may seek reimbursement from the obligor up to the amount paid. The scope of subrogation is limited strictly to the actual sum expended, plus reasonable legal fees incurred in perfecting the transfer of title. Any excess value retained by the debtor remains their property free of prior encumbrances.

Special provisions apply when collateral security involves living beings or sentient entities enchanted with servitude spells. In these instances, additional protections must be included to prevent abuse and ensure humane treatment of the subject. These may include limits on working hours, mandatory rest periods, adequate nutrition and shelter, and prohibition of cruel or degrading practices. Violation of any such safeguard constitutes grounds for immediate termination of the security arrangement and potential criminal prosecution.

The concept of "clean title" takes on unique significance in magical transactions due to the possibility of hidden curses or blemishes affecting value and usability. Buyers are entitled to full disclosure of all known defects before finalizing an agreement. Sellers who conceal material flaws may be held liable for resulting damages even after transfer of possession. Disputes over clean title status shall be resolved through independent arcane appraisal by mutually agreed-upon experts, with costs borne equally unless otherwise stipulated in the contract.

Collateral obligations arising from magical artifacts must clearly specify duration, termination triggers, and remedies upon breach. Indefinite or vague terms are unenforceable under these accords. Parties may agree to automatic renewal clauses subject to notice periods and fair compensation adjustments based on current market rates for similar services. Any modification of original terms requires written consent signed by all involved parties bearing the official seal of the Mages' Guild Conservators.

The principles outlined herein apply equally to domestic and international transactions, though additional regulatory compliance may be necessary when crossing planar boundaries or involving foreign jurisdictions with conflicting laws. In such cases, priority shall generally favor the law of the place where performance occurs unless otherwise specified in a valid choice-of-law provision incorporated into the main agreement text.

It is further noted that all collateral arrangements must align with established ethical guidelines set forth by the Guild's Code of Conduct and cannot violate higher-order prohibitions concerning human dignity or planar integrity. Contracts attempting to circumvent these fundamental protections are void regardless of their apparent legality under conventional civil law standards. The Courts retain inherent jurisdiction to intervene where necessary to uphold these overriding public policy concerns.

Under § 1101.6, parties engaging in magical secured transactions must explicitly identify all forms of collateral and associated obligations at the outset. Concealment renders any attempted enforcement null and void. Subrogation rights are limited strictly to actual amounts paid plus reasonable legal costs. Special safeguards protect sentient subjects from exploitation or abuse. Clean title requires full disclosure of defects, with sellers liable for undisclosed flaws causing damage. All terms must be precise and comply with both local regulations and Guild ethics. The Courts maintain oversight authority to ensure fundamental protections remain intact regardless of contractual language employed.

see § 1002.5 Collateral Disclosure Requirements; see § 1103.1 Ethical Guidelines for Magical Practitioners; see § 2004.7 Special Protections for Sentient Beings

body.heading: § 1101.5 Related Requirements and Collateral Obligations — Continued
body.text:
In the event that a magical item or creature is gifted, sold, or otherwise transferred subject to conditions precedent or subsequent, such conditions shall be deemed enforceable obligations under these Accords where they do not contravene public policy or the explicit prohibitions of this Code. See § 1001.2 Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets; § 300.1 Schedules of Arts. For example, if a vendor sells a cursed artifact with knowledge that it will cause harm to the purchaser's heirs, such malice may constitute actionable fraud under general principles of contract law as interpreted by this Desk. Similarly, a seller who knowingly fails to disclose material defects in a magical construct may be held liable for breach of warranty and negligence per se.

Where a gift is given with an express reservation of rights or title, the donor shall retain full ownership and control over the gifted item until such time that all conditions have been fulfilled. Under § 1001.6 Endowments and Gifts of Magical Assets; § 1301.4 Who May Inspect, this includes the right to reclaim possession should the donee fail to adhere to the stipulated terms. The burden of proving compliance with such covenants shall rest upon the donor seeking enforcement thereof.

Collateral security arrangements involving magical property shall be governed by these provisions insofar as they relate to the underlying transaction. See § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; § 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form. This encompasses pledges of future harvests, promises of service rendered through magic, or offers of assistance in locating and neutralizing threats posed by rival casters. Such obligations are binding upon execution, provided they do not violate any statutory prohibition herein enacted.

It is further declared that all requirements imposed under this Section shall be construed liberally in favor of enforcing the true intent of the parties, lest a technicality render nugatory an otherwise valid agreement. As stated in § 1001.7 Disclosure of Composition, Value, and Risk; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill, honesty and good faith are paramount to maintaining the integrity of magical commerce within Autumnwood's borders. Failure to comply with any provision herein may result in severe penalties, including revocation of licensure and imprisonment at Archmage Veyra's discretion.

The Desk reserves the right to issue additional guidelines or interpretations as necessary to address evolving circumstances surrounding related obligations and collateral interests in magic items and beings. Nothing contained herein shall be deemed to limit such authority unless expressly stated otherwise by unanimous vote of the full Council. Under § 1001.3 Valuation After Alteration; § 500.2 Unscheduled Weather, flexibility is essential to accommodate the unpredictable nature of arcane phenomena in commercial dealings.

*ARCHIVE CARD: Related Obligations & Collateral Security*
*Maintain detailed records of all conditions attached to magical transactions, including but not limited to:*
- *Precise wording of any reservations of title or rights by donors/sellers*
- *Proof of fulfillment of agreed-upon terms where applicable*
- *Evidence of malice, concealment of defects, or other breaches warranting enforcement actions*
- *Nature and scope of any pledged collateral security interests*

*Reference: § 1001.6 Endowments and Gifts; § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts*

body.heading: § 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations
body.text:
In furtherance of the comprehensive regulatory framework established herein, it shall be deemed necessary to articulate certain ancillary duties that arise naturally from the core mandates set forth in this Part. These related requirements are not merely procedural formalities but constitute substantive obligations essential for maintaining the integrity of arcane transactions within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk.

First and foremost, all parties engaged in inter-regional magical commerce must maintain accurate records of every transaction executed under the auspices of these provisions. Such documentation shall include detailed descriptions of goods exchanged, quantities involved, payment terms fulfilled or outstanding, and any special conditions agreed upon between contracting entities. Failure to preserve such records may result in severe penalties imposed by the Guild for non-compliance with statutory mandates designed to ensure transparency in the marketplace.

Furthermore, it is expressly prohibited for any caster operating within the bounds of these regulations to engage in activities that could reasonably be construed as circumventing the spirit and intent of applicable laws. This prohibition extends beyond literal violations of written statutes to encompass deceptive practices intended to evade regulatory oversight or undermine public confidence in the stability of magical commerce. The burden rests upon each individual practitioner to exercise due diligence in avoiding such conduct, lest they find themselves subject to disciplinary action by competent authorities.

It shall also be unlawful for any person knowingly to facilitate transactions conducted in violation of this Part through intermediaries or shell entities designed specifically to obscure the true nature of dealings between principals. The creation and utilization of such fictitious arrangements constitute a serious offense under the Accords, punishable by fines, suspension of licensure, or imprisonment at the discretion of the presiding judge. Authorities are hereby empowered to investigate suspected instances of misuse without prior notice, seizing assets and detaining individuals as necessary for the preservation of evidence pending formal proceedings.

Finally, all provisions herein shall be construed liberally in favor of promoting fair dealing among participants while simultaneously safeguarding against abuses that might threaten public welfare or disrupt the delicate balance of magical ecosystems upon which society depends. Any ambiguities arising from the application of these rules shall be resolved by reference to overarching principles of equity and justice, always keeping in mind the ultimate goal of fostering a safe and prosperous environment for all who dwell within our lands.

Under § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting, magistrates must recuse themselves when personal interests may bias their rulings. See also § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure regarding confidentiality obligations. Compliance with these related requirements ensures the continued effectiveness and legitimacy of the Guild's regulatory regime.

body.heading: § 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations — Continued
body.text: Whereas the Accords recognize that many magical operations involve concurrent obligations under separate statutes, this Section establishes principles for reconciling such conflicts without undermining either regime. See §§ 1.7 (Aggregation of Conduct), 1401.3 (Savings Against the Iron Mandate). First, no requirement shall be construed to excuse breach of another applicable duty unless expressly stated in plain terms. Id. Second, when two provisions appear equally binding, the more specific governs over the general; the later enactment prevails over the earlier if enacted with greater deliberation. Third, where obligations overlap, the holder may elect which claim to pursue so long as full compensation is ultimately secured for all losses sustained. Fourth, any waiver of one obligation does not automatically waive others unless explicitly reserved. Fifth, parties acting in concert to circumvent duties shall be deemed jointly and severally liable for resulting harms regardless of internal arrangements. Id. These rules ensure coherence across the legal landscape even as it expands into new domains of arcane activity. See § 1.4 (Persons Bound).

body.heading: § 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations — Administration
body.text:
The provisions herein shall not be construed in isolation but as an integrated whole, mutually reinforcing the purposes of this Code. Where multiple sections apply to a single transaction or act, each shall operate concurrently unless expressly stated otherwise. No requirement imposed by any provision shall relieve compliance with any other applicable rule; rather, they stand together as complementary mandates designed to safeguard both the public interest and the integrity of magical practice within our lands.

This principle extends beyond mere textual interpretation. The spirit and intent of related articles must guide their application in all circumstances, ensuring that no loophole undermines the overarching goals set forth by the Sovereign Council. For instance, while § 1201.3 permits certain forms of extraterritorial casting under strict conditions, those permissions are granted only so long as they do not contravene other duties laid out herein or elsewhere in law. A caster's freedom to exercise their craft abroad remains subject always to the bounds established by this Code and its allied statutes.

Furthermore, obligations arising from different provisions may merge into a single composite duty when the facts warrant. Where actions taken under one mandate inevitably trigger consequences governed by another, both sets of rules apply with full force. This prevents evasion through technicalities or sequential manipulation of legal categories. The true test lies not in how many boxes an actor ticks along the way but whether their conduct ultimately upholds the values enshrined throughout our body of laws.

In sum, then, let it be clear: compliance here is never partial or selective. Each clause contributes uniquely to a coherent system built upon fairness, safety, and accountability. To fulfill one's duties under this Code is to embrace all its implications wholly and sincerely — for therein lies the essence of lawful citizenship in our realm. See also §§ 100.6, 200.4; cf. § 1301.4.

body.heading: § 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations — Oversight
body.text:
In the event that a casting permit issued under these Accords is found to have been obtained through misrepresentation or concealment of material facts, all rights and privileges granted thereby shall immediately revert to the Guild without compensation. Such revocation may occur at any time upon discovery of such impropriety by the Aegis Magi acting in consultation with the Archmage Sovereign. The holder of a fraudulent permit bears sole responsibility for any damages arising from unauthorized use thereof.

Furthermore, it is hereby declared that no casting permitted under these Accords shall be deemed valid if performed within one hundred miles of an active battlefield or zone of significant magical flux without explicit prior approval in writing signed by two senior magisters. This provision exists to protect both the public and the integrity of the Arcane Arts from potential contamination. Violation constitutes a Class A misdemeanor subject to fines up to five thousand gold pieces and/or imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months at the discretion of the presiding judge.

In addition, all holders of casting permits shall be required to maintain comprehensive logs detailing each magical operation conducted under said authorization. These records must be kept in triplicate: one copy retained by the permittee, one filed with their regional oversight authority, and one archived centrally within the Autumn Wood Hall upon demand. Failure to comply with this mandate shall result in immediate suspension of all privileges until such time as full compliance can be demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Aegis Magi.

Finally, it is expressly prohibited for any individual holding multiple casting permits to utilize more than two concurrently at any given location unless special dispensation has been granted by a majority vote of the Conservator Council. This restriction aims to prevent monopolization of magical services in high-demand areas and ensure fair access for all licensed practitioners. Breach of this rule shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and including permanent revocation of all permits held by the offending party.

The provisions herein are intended to supplement, not supplant, any existing laws or regulations governing magic within the jurisdiction. In cases where conflict arises between these rules and those previously enacted, the stricter standard shall prevail unless otherwise directed by competent authority. The Archmage Sovereign retains exclusive power to interpret ambiguities in this Code as they pertain to matters of public safety and magical ethics. All magisters are bound to uphold these mandates faithfully without deviation under penalty of severe consequences.

see § 1201.1 Transit Stamps for additional requirements regarding proper identification during inter-regional travel; see also § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items which outlines restrictions on duplication of sensitive magical texts. Violation of any provision herein may result in escalation under the Penal System detailed in Part V, including potential confinement within a sealed pocket dimension pending resolution of charges. The Aegis Magi serve as primary enforcers of these statutes and shall act swiftly to address breaches without prejudice.

body.heading: § 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations — Procedure
body.text:
§ 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations. All provisions in Part XII are read as mutually reinforcing, with no single requirement operating in isolation from the whole regulatory scheme. Thus, a caster who holds a valid Transit Stamp yet fails to pay Planar Tolls remains in violation of § 1201.4 even if otherwise compliant; conversely, one who pays all fees but casts outside permitted zones violates § 1201.3 regardless of financial standing. Similarly, the prohibition against unscheduled weather (§ 500.2) applies whether or not a Field Casting Permit was obtained under § 500.1, unless an Emergency Sitting has lifted restrictions temporarily pursuant to § 100.8.

Where multiple obligations intersect, they must be satisfied in full before any related activity commences. For example, a research permit issued under § 400.1 confers no authority to conduct experiments until the specified safety protocols detailed therein are implemented; failure to adhere to those protocols invalidates the entire authorization retroactively. Likewise, a Diet Chamber session conducted in good faith may still be deemed null if participants were found guilty of prior infractions that disqualify them from representation under § 1201.3(a).

Administrative bodies enforcing these rules retain discretion to impose additional conditions where necessary to preserve public safety and the integrity of magical practice. Such conditions, when clearly stated and reasonably tailored, bind all affected parties equally. For instance, a Transit Stamp may carry caveats restricting its use in politically sensitive areas or during periods of heightened tension between factions; violation of these terms constitutes breach of contract under applicable law.

Oversight mechanisms embedded within this Part are designed to ensure compliance through both proactive monitoring and reactive enforcement. Automated tracking systems shall log all planar crossings, cross-referencing them against individual permits and payment records in real-time. Any discrepancies trigger immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi or designated auditors, who possess authority to detain suspected violators pending further inquiry. Penalties for non-compliance escalate with each successive offense, ranging from fines and license suspensions to revocation of all credentials and imprisonment under the Paradox Trial provisions (§ 1001).

Nothing in this Part shall be construed to limit or impair any rights held by persons outside the direct scope of regulation. Third-party claims arising from negligent or intentional acts remain actionable under general tort principles, even if the actor possesses otherwise valid permits and licenses. In cases where statutory mandates conflict with common law doctrines, the more stringent standard prevails unless expressly waived in writing by all interested parties.

The spirit of these requirements extends beyond their literal text, demanding a steadfast commitment to responsible stewardship of magical powers for the benefit of all. Only through rigorous adherence can we maintain balance between innovation and stability, ensuring that our craft continues to flourish without endangering society at large. Let this be understood as binding upon every caster who chooses to tread these ethereal pathways under Autumnwood's watchful gaze.

body.heading: § 1201.5 Related Requirements and Integrated Obligations — Custody
body.text:
The provisions governing transit stamps, planar tolls, extraterritorial casting into Diet Chambers, and the sale of cartography as raid licenses are not isolated rules but interconnected facets of a broader regulatory framework designed to maintain order across planar boundaries. These requirements must be read in conjunction with one another, each informing and refining the obligations imposed upon those who traverse the arcane landscape under Guild oversight.

A transit stamp serves both as proof of compliance and a trigger for subsequent duties. Upon affixing such a mark to an item destined for interdimensional transport, the owner immediately assumes liability for payment of applicable planar tolls, unless otherwise exempted by special permit or treaty. Failure to settle these charges in full before departure may result in seizure of the goods and imposition of punitive fines upon arrival. This integrated sequence ensures that all cross-planar commerce generates revenue for the Guild while mitigating risks associated with unauthorized use of teleportation magic.

Cartographic representations of accessible routes possess inherent value as tools facilitating illicit activity, yet their acquisition through lawful channels remains permissible so long as no explicit authorization to raid is implied or granted. The mere possession of such maps does not constitute a violation unless accompanied by intent and action toward unlawful intrusion. However, any attempt to disguise the true purpose of acquiring these documents—as navigational aids rather than tactical guides—shall be deemed fraudulent and punishable accordingly.

Extraterritorial casting into Diet Chambers introduces unique complexities regarding jurisdictional authority and enforcement powers. When a mage deliberately channels their spellwork beyond traditional physical space in order to evade local scrutiny, they effectively place themselves under the purview of the nearest available Guild official empowered to adjudicate magical infractions. Such officials act with full discretion within their realm, able to impose sanctions ranging from verbal warnings up to permanent exile depending on severity and prior record.

Collectively, these provisions establish a cohesive system for regulating movement and interaction between worlds, balancing freedom of trade with necessary safeguards against abuse. By linking seemingly disparate elements into a single operational whole, the Accords enable efficient administration while preserving flexibility to address novel challenges as they arise. The synergy among these related requirements exemplifies the adaptive nature of this ever-evolving code, capable of accommodating new circumstances without compromising underlying principles of justice and equity.
