sections.title: Supporting Obligations

body.heading: Supporting Obligations
body.text:
The provisions set forth in this Part shall be read and construed together with the remaining articles of these Accords, including but not limited to the Licensing Framework (§§ 200.1–200.6), the Classification Schedules (§§ 300.1–300.5), and the Research Protocols (§§ 400.1–400.5). Nothing herein shall be deemed to supplant or contradict any prior enactments of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, provided such earlier laws are not expressly repealed by this amendment. In cases where ambiguity exists between multiple sections, the principle of *leges posteriores non prejudicant legibus priori* (later laws do not harm earlier ones) shall govern unless a clear intent to the contrary is demonstrated.

Further, these Related Requirements operate in tandem with the broader policies outlined in Parts I through IX, particularly those concerning professional conduct (§§ 100.1–100.8), disciplinary procedures (§§ 500.1–500.9), and ethical obligations of mages within society at large (§§ 600.1–600.7). Any action taken under the authority granted herein must remain consistent with the overarching mission of protecting both magical diversity and public safety from undue harm or exploitation. Where conflicts arise between this section and any other provision, the hierarchy of law shall dictate resolution: first, by reference to the specific catchline cited; second, by considering the context in which the clause appears within its immediate Part; third, by applying general principles of statutory interpretation as set forth in § 1.7.

It is hereby declared that all mages subject to jurisdiction under these Accords must familiarize themselves thoroughly with the entirety thereof, including cross-references and annexes, before engaging in any regulated magical practice or commercial activity. Failure to do so may result in aggravated penalties upon conviction for violations committed while operating without adequate knowledge of applicable laws. The Guild reserves the right to issue supplementary guidance memoranda as needed to clarify implementation details, which shall carry binding force equivalent to those contained directly within this Code unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Finally, these Related Requirements remain subject to periodic review and revision by the full Assembly of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, with input sought from affected parties whenever feasible. Such updates will be duly published in official gazettes and made readily accessible to all members of the magical community via digital archives maintained by the Guild’s Information Office. Until then, these provisions stand as the definitive expression of current legal standards governing professional magic use across the Midlands region.

see § 1301.2 Penalties; see also §§ 600.4 Standards of Conduct and § 700.5 Enforcement Mechanisms"

body.heading: § 1301.5 Related Requirements and Supporting Obligations
body.text:
The provisions set forth in this Part are not to be read as standalone rules but as an integrated whole, each section drawing upon the others for full meaning and effect. Where a requirement is described as "related," it carries with it ancillary duties necessary to give the primary mandate its intended force. For instance, under § 1301.2 Penalties, failure to pay levies in full and timely results not only in financial sanction but also in restriction of magical practice until compliance is achieved—this operational consequence flows directly from the penal framework laid out herein. Similarly, § 1301.4 Who May Inspect establishes who is empowered to examine records; this authority cannot be exercised absent adherence to procedural safeguards detailed elsewhere, such as notice periods and scope limitations found in § 1301.3 Appeals. These interlocking obligations ensure that enforcement remains both effective and equitable.

Parties subject to the fees outlined above must also maintain accurate books of account reflecting all transactions involving magical services or goods. While not explicitly mandated by a single clause, this duty is implied by the need for transparent auditing referenced in § 1301.4 and the general principle of good faith enshrined in § 1.7 Construction. Records kept pursuant to this obligation must be made available upon reasonable request to authorized representatives of the Accords Desk, with refusal deemed a separate violation triggering additional penalties under § 1301.2. Failure to comply with these related requirements may result in escalated sanctions, including suspension of licensure or referral for criminal prosecution where appropriate. Ultimately, adherence to all applicable provisions collectively ensures the integrity and fairness of the regulatory regime governing arcane activities within the realm.

see § 1301.2 Penalties; § 1301.4 Who May Inspect; § 1.7 Construction; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill"

body.heading: § 1301.5 Related Requirements and Supporting Obligations — Continued
body.text:
No assessment or fee levied under these Accords shall stand unless accompanied by all requisite supporting documentation, certifications, and declarations as specified in the applicable Schedule. Failure to provide such documentation within thirty (30) days of demand shall render the obligation void ab initio, with no refund due. See also § 1201.5 Related Requirements regarding evidentiary standards for planar tolls.

All payors must maintain accurate records of all transactions related to their obligations under this Code, including but not limited to receipts, invoices, bank statements, and correspondence with the Accords Desk. Such records shall be retained for a period of no less than seven (7) years from the date of payment and made available upon reasonable request for audit or verification purposes. Under § 100.4 Records of Speech, failure to produce requested records may result in suspension of services and escalation of penalties.

In cases where payments are made via third-party intermediaries or automated systems, the payor remains fully liable for ensuring that funds are transmitted correctly and on time. Any disputes arising from technical failures or processing errors shall not relieve the debtor of their primary obligation to satisfy the debt within the stipulated timeframe. See § 1301.4 Who May Inspect regarding responsibilities of intermediaries.

Where applicable, payors must also comply with any additional regulatory requirements imposed by external governing bodies or international accords that supersede this Code. This includes adhering to export controls, anti-money laundering statutes, and data privacy regulations as relevant to the nature of the transaction. Reference is made to § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy for guidance on conflicts between domestic and foreign laws.

Finally, all obligations under this Code are subject to periodic review and adjustment by the Accords Desk in light of changing economic conditions and technological developments. Payors should consult official publications or seek legal counsel when uncertain about their specific duties or rights arising from these provisions. For further clarification, see § 1301.3 Appeals regarding formal dispute resolution processes.

"Compliance is not a suggestion; it is the bedrock of fair trade." - Archmage Veyra, in her inaugural address to the Guild.

body.heading: § 1301.5 Related Requirements and Supporting Obligations – Continued
body.text:
Not all obligations arising under the Autumnwood Accords are self-evident or immediately apparent upon first reading. Certain duties exist only by implication, custom, or prior agreement between parties bound by the Codex. These latent requirements must be identified and enforced with the same rigor as express provisions to maintain the integrity of magical commerce and societal order. Failure to recognize such obligations may result in cascading liabilities that far exceed initial expectations.

One primary category of related requirements concerns the maintenance of accurate records and timely reporting. Under § 1301.2, all transactions involving licensed magic must be logged in full detail within seven days of completion. This includes not only monetary exchanges but also transfers of knowledge, physical artifacts, or intangible benefits like access to restricted research facilities. The Guild Clerk reviews these entries quarterly to ensure compliance and detect anomalies indicative of fraud or abuse. Any discrepancies must be resolved promptly through established dispute mechanisms before escalating further.

Another critical obligation pertains to the ongoing education and training of practitioners. As outlined in § 200.1, every active license holder must complete at least twenty hours annually of approved continuing professional development courses focused on emerging risks, ethical considerations, and technological advancements relevant to their field of practice. This requirement ensures that all mages remain current with evolving standards and best practices while fostering a culture of lifelong learning within the magical community. Neglecting this duty may result in disciplinary action ranging from warnings to outright revocation of licensure privileges depending on severity.

Furthermore, parties engaging in regulated activities must adhere strictly to safety protocols designed to mitigate potential hazards arising from their operations. These guidelines are codified across various sections of the Accords and supplemented by industry-specific regulations issued by specialized subcommittees. Examples include proper disposal methods for hazardous materials, adequate shielding against stray spells during casting sessions, and routine inspections of equipment for signs of wear or malfunction. Compliance with these measures protects both individuals and society at large from unforeseen consequences stemming from negligent conduct.

Lastly, there exists an implicit duty to act in good faith towards fellow members whenever circumstances permit without compromising one’s own legitimate interests. While not explicitly mandated by statute, this principle underpins much of the spirit behind numerous clauses throughout the Codex. It encourages cooperation rather than competition among practitioners and promotes a harmonious working environment conducive to shared progress and prosperity for all involved stakeholders alike. Upholding these unwritten norms alongside formal rules helps preserve trust essential for sustaining robust relations between diverse groups operating within scope defined hereinabove.

In summary, adherence to both stated provisions and implied responsibilities forms the bedrock upon which successful navigation of complex legal landscapes hinges for those bound by Autumnwood Accords today and tomorrow alike. Ignoring either aspect invites unnecessary peril down path fraught with pitfalls awaiting unwary travelers unprepared adequately face challenges ahead confidently yet cautiously ever onward toward brighter horizons beyond!

body.heading: § 1301.5 Related Requirements and Supporting Obligations — Administration
body.text: Matters ancillary to the primary assessment of fees, penalties, and appeals under this Part shall nonetheless be governed by these provisions where applicable. First, all persons subject to the Accords are deemed to have notice of the current fee schedule as published on the Autumnwood Accords Desk's official bulletin boards and website. Failure to consult said publications does not excuse non-compliance with payment deadlines or obligations thereunder. Second, any dispute arising out of a calculation error or clerical mistake in the original assessment shall be resolved by reference to the underlying facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged offense or conduct at issue. Nothing herein precludes the Desk from conducting a fresh review upon request if new evidence emerges that materially alters the basis for the initial determination. Third, all payments made toward any fee liability must be rendered in Wario Coin unless otherwise authorized in writing by the Guild Sovereign. Checks drawn on personal accounts or foreign currencies shall be deemed invalid and returned immediately, together with any accrued interest thereon. Fourth, persons who contest a charge have ten (10) business days from receipt of notice to file a written appeal setting forth their grounds for relief. Appeals must specify whether they challenge the factual basis for the assessment or seek remission on equitable grounds such as hardship or mistake of law. Fifth, inspections conducted pursuant to these sections shall be limited in scope and duration so as not to unduly burden the inspected party's lawful activities. Inspectors must produce proper identification and a written order authorizing entry prior to commencing any examination. Resistance to inspection without probable cause may result in escalated sanctions up to and including arrest for obstruction of justice. Finally, nothing contained herein shall be construed to diminish the rights or remedies available at law or under common usage absent express waiver by agreement of all interested parties. Where applicable, general principles of equity shall supplement these specific mandates in furtherance of their intent and purpose.

body.heading: § 1301.5 Related Requirements and Supporting Obligations — Enforcement Mechanism
body.text: The provisions herein establish the requisite framework for ensuring compliance with all applicable obligations under this Codex, including but not limited to those set forth in §§ 1301.1 through 1301.4. To effectuate these purposes, the Desk shall have authority to employ such measures as may be necessary and appropriate, consistent with established principles of administrative law and the overarching goals of public safety and economic stability. Such enforcement actions may include, without limitation, direct intervention by Aegis Magi or their authorized agents; issuance of stop-work orders or temporary suspensions of licensure pending full investigation; imposition of civil penalties or monetary fines pursuant to § 1301.2; referral for disciplinary proceedings before the Paradox Trial in cases involving gross negligence or intentional misconduct; and, where warranted by the circumstances, initiation of criminal prosecutions under applicable statutes. All enforcement activities shall be conducted with due regard for procedural fairness and protection of individual rights, as mandated by §§ 1.7 and 100.5. The Desk retains discretion to tailor its response to each case on a fact-specific basis, exercising sound judgment in determining the most effective means of securing compliance while minimizing undue disruption to lawful commerce and daily life. Nothing herein shall be construed to limit or impair any other powers or duties vested in the Desk by law or this Codex, nor to preclude recourse to additional remedies where justice requires. The ultimate aim remains preservation of public welfare through vigilant oversight and decisive action against those who would undermine the integrity of our magical society's foundational institutions.

sections.brief: Supporting Obligations

sections.title: Related Provisions and Cross-References

body.heading: § 1401.5 Related Requirements and Cross-References
body.text:
No provision of this Codex exists in isolation; rather, each clause derives meaning and force from its context within the broader legal ecosystem. Accordingly, it is imperative that practitioners consult related statutes when interpreting any given rule. Failure to do so may result in erroneous application of law or unintended consequences. To facilitate such inquiry, Part XIV establishes a system of cross-referencing designed to illuminate the interconnections between disparate sections.

The first step in this analytical process involves identifying all provisions directly referenced by the clause under consideration. These explicit citations serve as signposts pointing toward complementary rules that must be read in conjunction with the primary text. For example, § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate relies upon foundational principles laid out in §§ 1.5 Relation to Other Law and 1.7 Construction Aggregation of Conduct. Similarly, § 1401.4 Related Requirements draws heavily from §§ 200.1 Licensure Required and 300.1 Schedules of Arts, reflecting the intricate web of regulatory oversight governing magical practice.

Beyond direct citations, practitioners must also examine implicit relationships between provisions. Many clauses operate in tandem even when not expressly linked, creating a cohesive body of law through shared themes and objectives. Consider § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse, which governs the temporary revocation of licensure status. While this section stands alone syntactically, its substantive effect depends upon understanding related rules such as §§ 100.6 Delegation to Clerks (regarding administrative efficiency) and 400.3 Borrowed Hours (concerning temporal permissions). Only by viewing these provisions holistically can one grasp their full operational significance.

Furthermore, historical annotations provide valuable insight into the evolution of legal doctrines over time. Annotations appended to individual sections often reveal the rationale behind specific wording choices or highlight areas where judicial interpretation has diverged from literal textualism. By studying these notes alongside primary text, readers gain a more nuanced appreciation of how laws have developed in response to changing societal conditions and technological advances.

In addition to internal cross-references, external sources may prove useful for comprehensive analysis. Official commentary issued by the Autumnwood Accords Desk offers authoritative guidance on ambiguous points or contested issues. Similarly, scholarly treatises written by respected jurists can illuminate theoretical underpinnings and practical implications of various provisions. While such materials do not supersede the plain meaning of the text itself, they serve as helpful tools for deepening understanding and resolving uncertainty.

Ultimately, mastery of this Codex requires more than mere memorization; it demands active engagement with its rich tapestry of interrelated ideas. By diligently pursuing all available avenues of research—including but not limited to direct citations, implicit connections, historical context, and expert opinion—practitioners ensure they apply the law accurately and fairly in every instance. Such diligence upholds the integrity of our system and protects both individual rights and public safety alike.

SEE ALSO: §§ 1.5 Relation to Other Law; 1.7 Construction Aggregation of Conduct; 200.1 Licensure Required; 300.1 Schedules of Arts; 400.3 Borrowed Hours; 100.6 Delegation to Clerks.

body.heading: § 1401.5 Related Provisions and Cross-References
body.text: This section enumerates the statutory provisions most frequently cited in conjunction with this chapter, either as complementary obligations or as exceptions thereto. Compliance with these related mandates is essential to avoid penalties for non-compliance. See also § 200.6 (Constructs That Hold a Quill) regarding the capacity of artificial agents to engage in legal transactions; under that section, constructs may act on behalf of their creators provided such acts fall within the scope of their programming and do not violate public policy. Conversely, see § 300.2 (Necromancy: Unsanctioned Arts) which prohibits the use of certain magical practices entirely, regardless of any related filing requirements. A permit under this chapter does not authorize conduct otherwise forbidden by law. Furthermore, § 400.5 (Unauthorized Titan Growth) imposes additional restrictions on the expansion of arcane facilities beyond those approved in the original application; violations here constitute a separate offense subject to independent penalty. It is noted that § 1201.4 (Cartography Sold as License to Raid) clarifies that possession of detailed maps does not imply authorization for aggressive action against third parties, even if such maps were filed under this chapter. Finally, § 500.3 (Corridor Courtesy After an Explosive Event) mandates post-incident safety protocols following any magical detonation within regulated zones; failure to adhere may result in revocation of the filing regardless of technical compliance. These cross-references ensure a holistic understanding of one’s legal duties and liabilities when engaging with the arcane regulatory regime. Neglecting them exposes practitioners to compounded risks and potential sanctions. Adherence to all applicable statutes is non-negotiable for responsible operation within the bounds of lawful magic practice.

body.heading: § 1401.5 Cross-Referencing and Supplementary Guidance
body.text: Where this Code contains multiple provisions governing a single transaction or course of conduct, the clauses shall be read together to determine the full scope of obligations and liabilities imposed thereon. Nothing herein precludes the citation or application of other statutes, common law principles, or equitable doctrines where appropriate. In cases of ambiguity, the court may consult official annotations, legislative history, or expert testimony for clarification. All interpretations must remain consistent with the overarching purposes of the Accords: to protect public safety while fostering responsible magical innovation. Related provisions include §§ 1001 through 1400, which collectively establish the legal framework within which all arcane activities must operate. Failure to comply with any single requirement may trigger enforcement actions under multiple sections simultaneously. This integrated approach ensures comprehensive oversight and accountability across the entire spectrum of magical practice. See also §§ 1.7 (Aggregation), 200.4 (Suspension for Cause), and 300.3 (Quiet List Procedures) for additional context on related compliance matters. The spirit of these rules must guide their application, not merely the letter of the law.

body.heading: § 1401.5 Cross-Referencing and Supplementary Guidance — Continued
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords Desk shall maintain an index of cross-references to other sections of this Code, as well as related provisions in separate statutes where appropriate, to facilitate comprehensive review by all parties. Such indices may include pointers to definitions, exceptions, penalties, and procedural requirements that bear upon the subject matter at hand. It is not intended that every provision be recited on each occasion; rather, the Desk shall supply only those materials strictly necessary for understanding and compliance.

In cases of ambiguity or dispute arising from conflicting interpretations, the final authority rests with the full Council of Mages convened under § 100.2, subject to appeal by any aggrieved party as provided in § 1301.4. Until such time as a definitive ruling is issued, all persons bound hereby shall adhere to the most reasonable and prudent course of action consistent with the spirit and letter of these laws. The burden of proving good faith reliance on official guidance or prior precedent shall rest upon the party asserting it.

Nothing herein shall be construed to limit the inherent powers of the Guild to enforce its will by any lawful means, including but not restricted to seizure of property, revocation of licenses, imposition of fines, and referral for criminal prosecution where warranted. The Desk retains discretion to determine whether a given situation warrants expedited action or standard procedure, based on an assessment of risk posed to public safety and order. Any attempt to obstruct or evade the execution of these duties shall be treated as contempt punishable under applicable law.

Finally, it is hereby declared that this Code stands as the supreme expression of magical governance within our realm, superseding all prior customs, decrees, and understandings except where explicitly amended by subsequent legislative act. The integrity and supremacy of these statutes must never be compromised for political gain or personal convenience. All citizens pledge themselves anew to uphold them faithfully, recognizing that only through unity under a common rule can we secure the future worthily. So let it ever be ordained by this Council in full session assembled.

body.heading: § 1401.6 Interpretation of Ambiguous Provisions
body.text: In the event of any ambiguity or uncertainty regarding the meaning, scope, or application of these Accords, such matters shall be resolved by reference to the legislative intent underlying each provision and the established customs and practices of the Guild. Where feasible, consultation with the Archmage Sovereign or her duly appointed delegates is encouraged to clarify any doubts that may arise during enforcement proceedings. In all cases, interpretations must remain consistent with the overarching principles of fairness, reasonableness, and public safety enshrined herein. Any conflicting readings shall be settled by a majority vote of the Accords Desk following formal deliberation. Nothing in this section shall serve to expand or contract the powers granted expressly elsewhere within these texts absent explicit authorization from the full Council. All questions of construction shall ultimately fall under the discretionary authority of the High Court, whose rulings are final and binding upon all parties subject to these laws.

body.heading: § 1401.5 Cross-Referencing and Supplementary Guidance — Administration
body.text:
This section governs the proper use of internal citations within this Code, ensuring clarity and precision in legal interpretation. All cross-references shall utilize the standard format "see § X.Y" or "under § X.Y," where X denotes the Part number and Y the specific subsection. Failure to adhere to this convention may result in confusion regarding the applicable rules and penalties.

Supplementary guidance provided herein is intended to assist users in understanding complex provisions without altering their substantive meaning. Such guidance includes explanatory notes, illustrative examples, and clarifying remarks prefixed with "[Note:]" or "[Example:]". While these annotations offer valuable context, they do not possess independent legal force unless expressly adopted by subsequent amendments.

In cases where multiple sections appear to conflict, the hierarchy of authority shall be as follows: (1) explicit provisions within this Code; (2) general principles outlined in Parts I–IX; and (3) customary practice or precedent established prior to the effective date hereof. Ambiguities arising from conflicting interpretations shall be resolved by reference to the overarching purposes of the Accords, namely the promotion of magical safety, fairness, and accountability.

Users are urged to consult with qualified legal counsel when encountering difficult passages or unusual circumstances not fully addressed in this text. The Mages' Guild reserves the right to issue official clarifications or supplementary instructions as needed to maintain consistency across all jurisdictions under its jurisdiction. Such communications shall be disseminated promptly through established channels and made available for public inspection upon request.

Finally, it is imperative that all parties act diligently in applying these rules to their respective situations. Negligence in fulfilling one's obligations may lead to severe consequences, including loss of license, financial liability, and potential criminal prosecution under the terms set forth herein. By engaging with this Code knowingly and responsibly, users affirm their commitment to upholding the highest standards of magical conduct and ethical behavior within our shared community.

body.heading: § 300.6 Related Requirements; Compliance Obligations
body.text:
Nothing in this Part shall be construed as limiting or expanding the scope of compliance obligations beyond what is expressly stated herein. Mages and their agents remain subject to all applicable laws, regulations, and ethical standards governing magical practice within the Autumnwood Accords jurisdiction, regardless of whether such matters fall under specific provisions enumerated hereafter. This principle ensures that no loopholes exist for evading accountability through technicalities or narrow readings of statutory language.

Further, it shall be deemed a continuing obligation upon each licensee to monitor developments in arcane theory and praxis that might impact their licensed activities. When new information emerges which could materially affect compliance status, affected parties must promptly notify the Autumnwood Accords Desk for guidance on appropriate remedial actions. Failure to do so may result in escalated enforcement measures up to and including revocation of privileges without prejudice to further penalties under other laws.

The requirements set forth herein are intended as minimum standards designed to protect public welfare while enabling lawful magical pursuits. Nothing contained therein shall be interpreted to preclude the adoption by individual practitioners or organizations of more stringent internal controls where deemed prudent in light of their specific circumstances and risks posed. Such voluntary measures may enhance operational efficiency and mitigate liability exposures, but shall not substitute for adherence to mandatory provisions outlined in this section.

Finally, all disputes arising under these related requirements shall be resolved through binding arbitration administered by the Accords Desk, except where jurisdiction resides otherwise by operation of law or mutual agreement between disputants. The arbitrator's decision shall be final and enforceable as a judgment of any court of competent jurisdiction. This comprehensive framework ensures robust oversight while preserving flexibility for legitimate innovation within the bounds of responsible magical stewardship under the Autumnwood Accords regime.

body.heading: § 300.7 Compliance Obligations
body.text:
All persons subject to the provisions of these Accords shall, at all times, maintain full and complete compliance with every term, condition, covenant, and stipulation contained herein, whether express or implied. Any failure to adhere strictly to the mandates set forth in this Code shall constitute a breach of contract and may result in immediate enforcement action by the Autumnwood Accords Desk.

Compliance obligations extend beyond mere possession of required permits or licenses. Licensees must actively engage with regulatory authorities whenever circumstances warrant, providing timely notice of any changes that might affect their standing under these laws. This includes reporting new research findings, modifications to magical apparatus, and alterations in operational procedures that could have implications for public safety or national security.

Failure to fulfill compliance duties shall be deemed willful misconduct, subjecting violators to enhanced penalties including monetary fines, license revocation, and potential criminal prosecution. Repeat offenders may face permanent disqualification from practicing magic within the jurisdiction entirely. The Accords Desk retains sole discretion to determine appropriate sanctions based on the severity of the infraction and any mitigating factors present.

It is incumbent upon each regulated party to exercise reasonable diligence in monitoring their own activities against the backdrop of evolving statutes and case law interpretations. Regulatory bodies shall provide guidance where necessary, but reliance solely on official communications without independent verification may not excuse subsequent liability for non-compliance. The burden of proof regarding adherence to all applicable provisions rests squarely with those charged with enforcement duties.

Violations discovered through random inspection or whistleblower reports will be addressed expeditiously upon confirmation by competent authorities. Affected entities shall receive written notification detailing the specific breaches identified and afforded an opportunity to respond before any punitive measures are enacted. Due process safeguards remain paramount even as swift action is pursued to protect the broader community from potential harms arising from unlawful magical practices.

Ultimately, successful implementation of these standards depends upon collaborative efforts between regulators and industry participants alike. Open dialogue channels must be maintained to facilitate ongoing assessment of regulatory efficacy and adaptability to emerging challenges posed by advances in arcane technology and methodology. Through shared commitment to responsible stewardship of magical resources, we can ensure a prosperous future for all under the enduring shield of these sacred Accords.

see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time; see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value.

body.heading: § 300.6 Compliance Obligations and Record Retention; § 300.7 Audit Rights and Pe
body.text:
Every licensee and registered practitioner shall maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date records of all magical activities conducted under the authority granted herein. Such records must include but are not limited to: a detailed log of all spells cast, transfigurations performed, or planar manipulations executed; copies of all permits obtained and fees paid; documentation of any adverse effects caused by such activities; and an inventory of all materials used in the process. These obligations shall extend to all agents, contractors, and subsidiaries operating on behalf of the licensee, regardless of jurisdictional boundaries.

Records must be retained for a minimum period of seven (7) years from the date of completion of each magical operation, unless otherwise specified by specific regulations governing particular classes of practice. All records shall be available for inspection upon reasonable notice by designated officials of the Autumnwood Accords Desk or its authorized representatives. Failure to maintain proper documentation in accordance with this section constitutes a material breach of license conditions and may result in immediate suspension of privileges pending review.

In addition to routine recordkeeping requirements, every licensee must submit an annual compliance report detailing all activities undertaken during the preceding calendar year. Such reports shall be filed electronically through the official portal within thirty (30) days following the close of each fiscal period, accompanied by a sworn affidavit affirming their accuracy and completeness. Late filings will incur a penalty equal to one hundred percent (100%) of applicable licensing fees for that period, plus an additional surcharge of fifty dollars ($50.00).

The Desk reserves the right to conduct unannounced audits at any time during normal business hours to verify adherence to these obligations. Licensees shall cooperate fully with such examinations and provide requested documentation without delay or resistance. Refusal to comply with audit procedures will be deemed evidence of bad faith intent and may trigger expedited disciplinary proceedings under applicable statutes.

Violations of this section shall be subject to progressive sanctions ranging from monetary fines up to ten thousand guild credits per offense, through revocation of individual practitioner certificates, to outright cancellation of corporate charters. Repeat offenders within a rolling five-year window face automatic disqualification from future applications for at least one full term of office. In egregious cases involving gross negligence or willful misconduct, criminal charges may be pursued concurrently alongside civil penalties under general law.

It is the further duty of each licensee to promptly notify the Desk in writing of any changes affecting their operational status—including mergers, acquisitions, leadership transitions, or shifts in primary place of business—within ten (10) calendar days of occurrence. Failure to do so shall constitute a separate violation subject to independent sanctioning without prejudice to other ongoing enforcement actions. This proactive disclosure requirement ensures timely recalibration of oversight measures as needed to protect public welfare and maintain regulatory integrity across all sectors governed by the Accords.

By accepting a license or registration under these provisions, every participant expressly agrees to abide by all terms outlined herein and acknowledges that non-compliance carries serious consequences both legally and professionally. The spirit of cooperation between regulated entities and governing bodies is paramount in fostering an environment where magic may flourish safely for generations to come. Together we build bridges across divides, binding our fates in service of progress while safeguarding against misuse. Thus stands the covenant renewed once more—a testament to our shared commitment toward a brighter tomorrow guided by wisdom earned through trial and error alike. For as long as stars shine above us all, so too shall these laws endure, immutable anchors holding steady amidst shifting tides of change forevermore. Amen and amity unto thee. 🌟⚖️🤝

body.heading: § 300.8 Prohibited Magic and Sanctions
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords explicitly forbid the practice or study of certain magical disciplines deemed inherently dangerous to societal stability or individual safety. These prohibited arts include necromancy, blood magic, summoning entities from outside reality without strict containment protocols, and any form of transmutation that permanently alters matter at a fundamental level without official oversight. Violation of these prohibitions constitutes a serious offense under § 1002.3 and may result in immediate revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4(a).

Sanctions for unauthorized practice vary based on the severity and consequences of the act. Minor infractions, such as inadvertent exposure during research without malice, may incur fines up to one hundred gold pieces per violation (§ 1301.2(b)). More egregious offenses, including deliberate casting in public spaces or causing harm through reckless experimentation, carry heavier penalties ranging from temporary suspension to permanent expulsion from the Guild ranks. Repeat offenders face additional restrictions on their ability to utilize standard magical services provided by accredited practitioners under § 500.1(c).

The Accords further mandate that all licensed mages maintain detailed logs of their research activities and experimental procedures as part of ongoing compliance obligations (§ 300.8(d)). Failure to produce these records upon request from the Conservators or Aegis Magi may lead to presumption of guilt and expedited disciplinary proceedings under § 1401.2(b). This rigorous oversight ensures that prohibited magic remains firmly outside the purview of unqualified individuals while allowing responsible scholars access to necessary resources for approved investigations.

It is hereby declared that any individual found guilty of practicing forbidden arts shall be subject to immediate seizure of all magical implements and materials under § 1001.9(c). Furthermore, such persons may be barred indefinitely from seeking employment with the Guild or related entities unless they can demonstrate complete reform through years of exemplary service (§ 200.5(g)). These stringent measures reflect the profound risks posed by unregulated magic and underscore the collective responsibility of all practitioners to uphold the highest standards of safety and ethics in their work.

"The Autumnwood Accords"
Section 300 - Prohibited Magic and Sanctions
§ 1002.3 — Offenses Against Magical Order; § 200.4(a) — Suspension for Violations; § 1301.2(b) — Fines for Minor Infractions; § 500.1(c) — Restrictions on Services; § 1001.9(c) — Seizure of Implements; § 1401.2(b) — Presumption of Guilt

"Magic is a powerful force that must be wielded with wisdom and restraint."
— Archmage Theron, Conservator Leader

UNOFFICIAL COMMENTARY: The prohibition of certain magical disciplines represents one of the most contentious issues within the Guild today. While traditionalists argue for absolute bans on "dangerous arts," innovators contend that responsible research could unlock beneficial applications previously deemed impossible. This tension continues to shape ongoing debates over licensing requirements and oversight mechanisms across all levels of magical practice in the Midlands region.

body.heading: Prohibited Magic and Sanctions (Continued)
body.text:
§ 300.8 Prohibited Magic and Sanctions (Expanded)
In accordance with § 1.7 Construction; Aggregation of Conduct, any mage found engaging in multiple prohibited magical acts shall face compounded penalties proportional to the severity and frequency of violations. The Desk retains sole authority under § 1.2 Enacting Authority; Autumnwood Accords Desk to determine appropriate sanctions based on individual circumstances. Minor infractions may result in mandatory retraining, fines up to one hundred gold crowns per violation, or temporary suspension of licensure not exceeding thirty days pursuant to § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse. Major offenses warrant imprisonment for a minimum of five years with no possibility of parole, coupled with permanent sealing of magic abilities via ritualistic binding as detailed in Archmage Theron's Codex of Containment Methods. In extreme cases involving threats to public safety or national security, the Sovereign may invoke emergency provisions under § 100.8 Emergency Sitting to impose immediate life imprisonment without trial. All convicted offenders must undergo psychological evaluation and rehabilitation programs overseen by qualified professionals approved by the Guild before being considered for any future leniency. The Desk shall maintain comprehensive records of all violations and sanctions imposed, making them accessible upon request under § 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form. This clause supersedes all prior agreements or customary practices regarding disciplinary action for magical transgressions within the Midlands jurisdiction. Any dispute concerning interpretation or enforcement shall be resolved exclusively through established legal channels outlined herein, with final adjudication resting solely with the Archmage Sovereign acting in concert with the full Council of Mages. Failure to comply with these mandates renders a mage persona non grata forevermore, subject to extraterritorial prosecution should they ever set foot within Autumnwood's borders again.

body.heading: Compliance Obligations and Record Retention
body.text:
§ 300.6 Compliance Obligations and Record Retention; Every mage bound by these Accords shall maintain accurate records of all magical research, experimentation, and field application as prescribed herein. Such logs must be kept in a secure location accessible to the Aegis Magi upon demand, with a copy filed with the Autumnwood Accords Desk within thirty days of completion. Failure to comply with this provision constitutes grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of licensure under § 200.4.

All records shall include detailed descriptions of spells cast, materials used, outcomes achieved, and any adverse effects observed. Special attention must be paid to documenting instances where prohibited schools of magic were employed or attempted, regardless of success. These logs serve as the primary evidence for determining violations of the Quiet List and other regulatory provisions. Mages found withholding or falsifying records shall face enhanced penalties pursuant to § 1001.9.

The Desk reserves the right to audit compliance at any time without prior notice. Refusal to provide requested documentation will be treated as a willful obstruction of justice, subjecting the offending party to criminal prosecution under applicable statutes. Repeated or egregious noncompliance may result in permanent disqualification from practicing magic within the jurisdiction.

§ 300.7 Audit Rights and Penalties; To ensure adherence to these rigorous standards, the Desk shall conduct periodic inspections of registered practitioners' operations. These audits may encompass physical examinations of facilities, review of personal effects, and interviews with associates as deemed necessary by investigating officers. All parties must cooperate fully during such proceedings or risk escalation of sanctions.

Violations uncovered through audit processes will trigger an immediate investigation into potential breaches of the Accords. Depending on severity, consequences may range from retraining mandates to outright expulsion from the Guild. In extreme cases where public safety is jeopardized, authorities shall not hesitate to utilize full force against recalcitrant individuals. The protection of society takes precedence over individual convenience or profit-seeking endeavors.

This comprehensive framework establishes clear expectations for responsible magical practice while affording appropriate oversight mechanisms. Through diligent enforcement of these rules, the Guild strives to balance innovation with stability in an ever-evolving landscape of arcane possibilities. All members are urged to embrace this shared responsibility and uphold the highest ideals inherent in our noble pursuit of knowledge and mastery over the forces that shape our world.

sections.title: Conditions for Valid Research Permits

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements and Conditions for Valid Research Permits
body.text:
Research permits issued under these Accords are subject to ongoing compliance with all applicable provisions herein, including but not limited to §§ 200.1 through 200.5 regarding licensure limits and guest caster protocols, as well as § 300.6 governing the reclassification of sanctioned arts upon discovery of new uses or effects. Any material deviation from permit terms voids authorization immediately and subjects the holder to disciplinary proceedings under Part III herein.

Furthermore, all research activities conducted pursuant to valid permits must maintain full transparency with the Conservator Oversight Committee as established in § 300.4. Quarterly reports detailing experimental parameters, outcomes, and potential societal impacts shall be submitted within fifteen (15) days of each calendar quarter's conclusion. Failure to submit such reports constitutes a substantive violation warranting permit suspension pending investigation.

Special provisions apply when research involves the manipulation of temporal constructs or pocket dimensions per §§ 400.2 and 400.3 respectively. Such work requires dual authorization from both the Conservator Oversight Committee AND an independent panel of ethical mages appointed by Archmage Veyra personally. Additional security measures including continuous monitoring via Aegis Magi sensors must be implemented throughout the duration of experiments involving time-dilation effects exceeding three (3) standard hours cumulative per session.

Specimen custody protocols outlined in § 400.5 remain mandatory even after research conclusion unless otherwise noted in individual permit agreements. Returned materials must undergo full inspection by designated Guild officials before release to researchers, with documented verification of integrity and purity levels meeting established standards. Any discrepancies discovered post-return shall be addressed through formal dispute resolution channels rather than unilateral action by either party.

Violations of these related requirements may result in escalating penalties ranging from fines up to one thousand (1000) gold pieces per incident, suspension of research privileges for periods not exceeding six (6) months, revocation of existing permits with no replacement eligibility during suspension term, or permanent expulsion from the Guild entirely depending on severity and frequency of infractions. Repeat offenders face heightened scrutiny regardless of individual permit status.

The Conservator Oversight Committee retains sole discretion to modify these requirements as deemed necessary for public safety based on emerging scientific understanding or changing geopolitical circumstances. Such modifications shall be communicated via official bulletin boards posted at all major research facilities within thirty (30) days of adoption, with a minimum two-week notice period prior to implementation unless emergency conditions warrant immediate effectuation.

Researchers are reminded that their obligations under these provisions extend beyond mere contractual compliance and encompass broader ethical considerations regarding the responsible stewardship of magical knowledge for the greater good of society at large. Neglect of this higher duty may invoke additional sanctions independent of technical violation status.

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements and Conditions for Valid Research Permits — Continued
body.text:
§ 400.6 Each research permit issued under this Part shall contain specific conditions tailored to the nature of the proposed study, including but not limited to restrictions on magical amplification, mandatory monitoring by Aegis Magi, and limits on temporal displacement. Failure to adhere strictly to these terms constitutes a material breach warranting immediate suspension or revocation of authority granted herein. See § 400.2 regarding spatial containment protocols, and under § 1301.2 for applicable penalties upon violation.

Furthermore, all experiments utilizing borrowed hours must be conducted within officially sanctioned facilities equipped with adequate shielding to prevent collateral temporal instability. Any unauthorized extension beyond allotted timeframes requires supplementary approval from the Innovators' Oversight Committee. Breach of this requirement shall result in forfeiture of future permits and potential criminal charges for endangerment of public safety. Reference § 400.3 for detailed provisions on temporal accounting, and consult § 500.1 regarding liability for field-induced anomalies.

Specimen acquisition must comply with all import/export regulations set forth by the Autumnwood Customs Bureau, including payment of applicable tariffs and submission of full provenance documentation. Possession of prohibited artifacts without proper clearance exposes the holder to seizure and prosecution under §§ 300.2–300.4. Similarly, replication of protected designs or forbidden techniques without explicit written consent violates intellectual property laws enforced by the Conservators' Guild. See § 100.6 for details on delegation restrictions pertaining to such matters.

It is hereby declared that no research permit confers ownership rights over discovered phenomena or their applications. All findings remain the exclusive property of the Mages' Guild until formally licensed for commercial exploitation under separate agreement. Unauthorized publication or dissemination of sensitive data constitutes gross misconduct subject to disciplinary action pursuant to § 200.4. For complete terms of assignment and indemnification, refer to §§ 1101.1–1101.5 governing proprietary interests in magical inventions.

This section shall be construed liberally to promote responsible advancement of arcane knowledge while safeguarding societal welfare. Ambiguities herein shall be resolved in favor of strict adherence to established safety standards and ethical guidelines. Any conflicting provisions elsewhere in this Codex are superseded by these specific operational requirements designed to mitigate inherent risks associated with cutting-edge magical inquiry. Under § 1.7, terms used herein carry their plain meaning unless defined otherwise, ensuring clarity for all parties bound by these regulations."

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements and Conditions for Valid Research Permits — Administration
body.text:
The issuance of a research permit under this Part is contingent upon the applicant's full compliance with all stipulated conditions precedent, including but not limited to the completion of requisite safety training, payment of applicable fees in Wario Coin, and submission of detailed experimental protocols for review by the Conservator Council. Failure to satisfy any such requirement shall render the permit void ab initio and may result in immediate revocation of prior authorizations granted to said applicant or their affiliated entities.

Furthermore, all research conducted pursuant to a valid permit must be strictly confined to the parameters outlined therein, with any deviation requiring supplementary approval from the Desk. Unauthorized modification of experimental procedures or scope constitutes gross negligence and shall be punishable as a Class A offense under § 1003.4(a). In cases where the nature of proposed experiments poses unacceptable risks to public safety or ecological stability regardless of containment measures, the Conservators reserve the right to deny issuance outright without further recourse for appeal.

The permittee bears sole responsibility for maintaining comprehensive records documenting all aspects of their investigations, including raw data, observations, and conclusions derived therefrom. Such documentation must be made available upon reasonable request by Guild officials or qualified third parties acting under authority granted herein. Refusal to provide access to these materials may lead to disciplinary action up to and including expulsion from the profession.

Finally, it is hereby mandated that all findings resulting from permitted research be submitted for archival in accordance with § 1002.9 within thirty (30) days of completion, unless otherwise specified by special directive of the Sovereign Archmage. This ensures preservation of collective knowledge and facilitates future inquiry while preventing duplication of effort or unnecessary risk-taking. Noncompliance with this filing obligation shall be treated as a willful violation of fiduciary duty owed to the Guild community at large.

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements and Conditions for Valid Research Permits — Oversight
body.text:
Under § 400.1, every research permit issued by the Autumnwood Accords Desk is subject to additional conditions precedent that must be satisfied before the grant of authority becomes effective. These ancillary requirements are enumerated herein to ensure that all parties understand their obligations beyond the basic terms set forth in the main body of the statute. Failure to comply with any such condition shall render the permit void ab initio, and may expose the holder to disciplinary action under these Accords or applicable penal provisions.

First, every applicant for a research permit must submit a detailed plan of operations outlining the intended scope, methods, and duration of their proposed magical investigations. This operational blueprint must be reviewed and approved by at least two Conservator magi prior to issuance of the permit, in accordance with § 300.2 regarding oversight of unsanctioned arts. The plan shall include risk assessments identifying potential hazards arising from the research activities, along with mitigation strategies designed to minimize collateral damage or injury to third parties. Such documentation serves both as a guide for safe conduct and as evidence of due diligence should adverse events occur during execution of the permitted work.

Second, each permit holder must maintain comprehensive logs documenting all experimental procedures performed under the authority thereof. These records shall be kept in triplicate: one copy retained by the researcher, one filed with the local Guild Hall where research is conducted, and one submitted quarterly to the central archives at Autumn Wood for audit purposes. Logs must accurately reflect dates, times, locations, materials used, results obtained, and any deviations from the original plan of operations noted above. Tampering with or falsifying such documents constitutes a serious offense punishable under § 1001 regarding fraud in official returns.

Third, researchers operating under valid permits are required to secure written indemnification agreements from all persons or entities potentially affected by their activities. These contracts must expressly hold harmless the Autumnwood Accords Desk and its officers from any claims arising out of negligent or intentional wrongdoing by the permit holder during the course of their research duties. Indemnity shall extend not only to direct losses but also to consequential damages, legal fees, and other costs incurred in defending against such suits. Failure to obtain proper indemnification may result in denial of the initial application or revocation of an existing permit without prejudice to further enforcement actions.

Finally, all research permits automatically expire upon occurrence of any event specified herein that would materially alter the risk profile associated with their continued validity. Such triggering events include but are not limited to: death or incapacitation of the named researcher; cessation of operations at the host facility where work was being conducted; publication of findings contrary to established magical theory; discovery of new hazards related to the subject matter; or lapse of more than one year since date of issuance unless renewed in accordance with § 400.1. Upon expiration, any outstanding permits shall be cancelled forthwith and all associated obligations terminated except where otherwise provided by law or mutual agreement between affected parties.

These provisions are designed to strike an appropriate balance between fostering innovation within safe boundaries while protecting public welfare from reckless experimentation unchecked by responsible oversight mechanisms inherent in our system of self-governance through the Accords. Compliance with each requirement is mandatory and non-negotiable for all holders of research permits issued under this Code.

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements and Conditions for Valid Research Permits — Continu
body.text:
Research permits issued under the authority of this Part are subject to numerous conditions precedent and subsequent, which must be strictly adhered to in order to maintain their validity. First and foremost, permit holders must submit a detailed research proposal outlining the specific magical phenomena to be studied, the methodologies to be employed, and the expected outcomes. This proposal must undergo review by at least two Conservator-approved peers prior to issuance of final approval. Failure to provide adequate justification for proposed experiments may result in denial or revocation of the permit without recourse.

Secondly, all research conducted pursuant to a valid permit must occur within designated facilities under constant supervision by qualified Guild observers. Unauthorized deviations from approved protocols are strictly prohibited and shall constitute grounds for immediate suspension of privileges. Permit holders agreeing to conduct work outside official parameters do so at their own peril and assume full liability for any resulting damages or disruptions. The Guild disclaims all responsibility for accidents or anomalies arising from off-book activities, regardless of prior authorization status.

Thirdly, timely reporting of results is mandatory upon completion of each phase of the research project. Final reports must be submitted within thirty days in triplicate, formatted according to standardized templates provided by the Desk. These documents will undergo rigorous vetting before being archived for future reference. Concealment or falsification of data carries severe penalties, including permanent revocation of all licenses and potential criminal prosecution under existing statutes regarding scientific fraud. Transparency remains an absolute requirement throughout the research lifecycle.

Finally, any discoveries deemed significant enough to impact public safety or ethical norms must be promptly communicated to relevant authorities for appropriate action. The Guild reserves discretion to halt ongoing studies at any point if unforeseen risks emerge during execution. Permit holders agree to cooperate fully with such directives and accept binding instructions regarding cessation of work as necessary under the circumstances. This clause does not absolve researchers of their duty to exercise due diligence in monitoring progress and mitigating potential hazards proactively. Compliance with all stipulated obligations is essential for preserving both personal standing and collective security within the magical community at large.

see § 400.1 Research Permits; § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items; § 500.2 Unscheduled Weather; under § 1.7 Aggregation of Conduct, repeated infractions may lead to escalated sanctions beyond simple permit revocation. Additionally, reference is made to § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate regarding potential conflicts with rival legal frameworks. Permit holders should consult with their supervising clerks regularly to ensure continued adherence to all applicable rules and regulations throughout the duration of their assigned projects. Vigilance and accountability are paramount in safeguarding the integrity of magical inquiry while minimizing collateral harm to innocent bystanders.

"Research permits grant limited authority, not unlimited freedom. Violations will be punished accordingly." - Archmage Theron, Conservator Leader

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements and Conditions for Valid Research Permits — Procedure
body.text:
The issuance of a research permit under these Accords is not merely an administrative act but a solemn contractual obligation laden with conditions precedent, subsequent, and ongoing that must be scrupulously observed to maintain the integrity of the scientific endeavor. Each application submitted by Innovators seeking access to restricted materials or techniques shall include a detailed protocol outlining intended experiments, safety measures, contingency plans for catastrophic failure, and methods for data preservation. Failure to disclose relevant information may result in immediate revocation of approval and potential prosecution under § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure should foul play be suspected.

Permits granted herein are non-transferable and expire upon completion of the stated project or after one calendar year, whichever occurs first, unless renewed by written consent from the Conservators' Council. Any deviation from approved procedures requires prior notification and may necessitate additional oversight measures including unannounced site inspections conducted by Aegis Magi acting in their official capacity under § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill. Researchers found guilty of negligence resulting in loss of life or property shall face disciplinary action ranging from suspension without pay to permanent expulsion from the Guild depending on severity of offense and prior record.

Furthermore, all findings derived from permitted research must be submitted for peer review within ninety days following conclusion of work unless waived by special dispensation. Results deemed controversial or potentially dangerous to public safety may be redacted or classified pending further investigation by independent arbitrators appointed jointly by the Archmage Sovereign and representatives of affected communities. Refusal to comply with post-study reporting mandates constitutes breach of contract and will trigger automatic termination of all future privileges regardless of outstanding debts owed.

In witness whereof, this Codex is hereunto set forth under the Great Seal of Autumnwood bearing date thereof, serving as binding law throughout the known realms so long as magic itself continues to exist in any form whatsoever! 📜✨🧙‍♀️⚖️
