body.heading: § 800.6 Related Requirements and Ancillary Obligations — Administration
body.text:
The Accords recognize that sanctions imposed under this Part may generate secondary liabilities or duties beyond the primary penalty itself. Such ancillary obligations are deemed related requirements that must be satisfied to complete the remedial process fully. Failure to comply with these derivative mandates may result in additional penalties or escalation of existing sanctions.

Under § 800.2, a mage found guilty at Paradox Trial faces one of several possible punishments ranging from temporary suspension to permanent sealing of magical abilities. Each sanction carries implicit conditions that extend beyond the initial ruling. For instance, a suspended caster must undergo mandatory retraining under direct supervision before regaining full licensure. This includes periodic testing and written examinations administered by authorized Guild officials.

Similarly, those subject to § 800.3's Seal of Silence are required to refrain from discussing their conviction outside designated channels. Breach of this confidentiality provision constitutes a separate offense punishable under § 1201.4 for unauthorized disclosure of protected information. Violations may lead to extended confinement or harsher penalties upon review by the Archmage Sovereign.

The Accords further stipulate that mages sentenced to § 800.5's pocket-prison regime must maintain a specified level of magical discipline while incarcerated. Regular assessments determine whether the offender has sufficiently mastered self-control measures prior to release. Failure to meet these standards may result in indefinite extension of imprisonment without trial.

Finally, § 800.4 mandates that any fines levied against convicted casters be paid directly into the Guild Treasury within thirty days. Late payments accrue interest at a rate of five percent per month until fully resolved. Recalcitrant debtors face further legal action including potential seizure of personal assets held in their name.

In sum, compliance with sanctions under this Part demands adherence not only to the explicit terms but also to all associated duties arising therefrom. Only through full satisfaction of these combined obligations can a sanctioned mage expect restoration of standing within the Guild community. The Archmage Sovereign retains ultimate authority to interpret and enforce these ancillary requirements as necessary to maintain public safety and order.

body.heading: § 800.6 Related Requirements and Ancillary Obligations — Continued — Continued
body.text:
In addition to the primary obligations enumerated herein, each Licensee shall comply with all ancillary requirements imposed by the Guild or its authorized agents. These may include but are not limited to: submission of periodic progress reports detailing research outcomes; attendance at mandatory safety briefings concerning planar hazards; payment of applicable fees for specialized equipment or consumables; and adherence to any additional protocols deemed necessary to mitigate risk to public welfare. Failure to satisfy such ancillary conditions shall constitute a material breach of the Agreement, entitling the Guild to immediate suspension or revocation of the License at its sole discretion.

The Licensing Office reserves the right to impose further obligations as circumstances dictate, provided they are reasonably related to the safe and lawful exercise of Licensed Magic. Examples may include the installation of monitoring devices within research facilities, the provision of access logs documenting all spellcastings exceeding certain thresholds, or the requirement to maintain a dedicated emergency fund for rapid remediation of unintended magical side-effects. Licensees agree to promptly notify the Desk of any changes that might impact their ability to fulfill these duties, such as alterations in personnel, financial status, or operational capacity.

Matters not explicitly addressed in this Section shall be governed by custom and practice established through prior rulings of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. In cases of ambiguity, the interpretation most favorable to public safety prevails unless contradicted by express statutory language. Licensees are encouraged to seek clarification from their assigned Clerk whenever uncertainty arises regarding compliance standards or procedural nuances, ensuring continued adherence to the highest ideals of magical stewardship as embodied in this Codex.

This Section is hereby ratified and incorporated into full force and effect, binding upon all current and future Licensees without exception. Any conflicting provisions shall be deemed null and void to the extent of such inconsistency. The Licensing Office retains ultimate authority over enforcement mechanisms, including but not limited to monetary penalties, suspension of privileges, revocation of certification, and referral for disciplinary action pursuant to applicable laws and regulations. Through diligent observance of these obligations, Licensees affirm their commitment to upholding the integrity and prosperity of the Guild while pursuing their noble quest for knowledge under responsible guidance.

see § 800.5 Scope of Authority; see § 900.1 Remedies for Breach; see § 200.3 Temporary Mouths — Continued.

sections.title: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences

body.heading: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences
body.text: This section outlines additional obligations and standards that must be met in conjunction with the preceding provisions regarding magical artifacts and their transfer. First and foremost, any transaction involving a bound or enchanted object shall require full disclosure of all known risks, limitations, and potential side effects associated with its use. Failure to provide such information may constitute grounds for rescission of the agreement, as well as liability for resulting damages. Second, purchasers must agree to assume sole responsibility for the safekeeping and proper utilization of any acquired items. The seller shall have no further obligation once transfer is complete, unless explicitly stated otherwise in writing. Third, all parties are required to maintain accurate records detailing the nature of goods exchanged, their condition at time of delivery, and any warranties or guarantees provided. These records may be requested by regulatory bodies for audit purposes at reasonable intervals. Finally, it shall be unlawful to knowingly sell or distribute magical items with defects that pose an imminent threat to public safety. Violations of this prohibition are subject to severe penalties, including permanent revocation of the seller's license and possible criminal prosecution. In sum, § 1101.6 serves as a comprehensive framework for ensuring responsible commerce in the realm of arcane goods and services.

body.heading: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences
body.text:
§ 1101.6 Any transfer of property or magical effects involving the Guild's seal, whether by sale, gift, inheritance, or otherwise, shall be subject to the provisions of this Part and all other applicable laws. Nothing herein shall be construed to limit the application of general principles of contract law, including but not limited to those concerning capacity, consideration, fraud, duress, mistake, and unconscionability. The parties are advised that failure to comply with these requirements may result in voiding the transaction entirely or imposing penalties as set forth in § 1301 et seq.

The Guild reserves the right to investigate any suspicious activity related to the transfer of sealed items, including but not limited to inquiries into the background and intentions of the parties involved. Such investigations shall be conducted discreetly and without undue delay, provided that reasonable notice is given to affected persons unless otherwise warranted by the circumstances. Findings from these inquiries may inform future interpretations of this Part or lead to additional regulatory measures as deemed necessary for the protection of public safety and order.

It is further clarified that nothing in this section shall be construed to grant any individual or entity rights beyond those expressly conferred herein. All authority over sealed objects remains vested solely in the Guild, which may revoke licenses, suspend operations, or impose fines at its sole discretion upon determination of a violation. The parties acknowledge and accept these terms as binding and enforceable under both magical law and secular jurisprudence.

This provision serves to reinforce the integrity of the Guild's regulatory framework while balancing competing interests among stakeholders. By establishing clear guidelines for handling sealed items, it aims to minimize disputes and promote efficient commerce within acceptable bounds. Ultimately, adherence to § 1101.6 supports the broader goals of maintaining stability, ensuring accountability, and fostering trust in the Guild system as a whole.

For further clarification or guidance regarding specific scenarios not explicitly addressed here, interested parties are encouraged to consult with qualified legal counsel specializing in arcane matters or seek an official ruling from the Autumnwood Accords Desk itself. Failure to do so may result in adverse consequences ranging from financial loss to criminal prosecution depending on severity of breach. Thus, it is imperative that all actors familiarize themselves thoroughly with these obligations prior to engaging in any relevant transactions.

*See also: § 1001.13 Bag of Holding as Off-Books Vault; § 1201.4 Cartography Sold as a License to Raid; § 1301.1 Schedule of Fees*

body.heading: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences
body.text: In the complex web of magical transactions, it is often difficult to trace the precise chain of causation leading from initial enchantment to final effect. When an object's behavior deviates from expectations or causes harm, liability may attach not merely to the original caster but to subsequent handlers who failed to properly maintain or secure the item. This principle extends beyond mere negligence; even inadvertent actions can trigger latent magical properties with disastrous results. The Accords therefore impose a heightened duty of care on all parties handling enchanted goods, requiring constant vigilance against unforeseen repercussions. Failure to anticipate and mitigate risks inherent in an object's design constitutes breach of contract, regardless of direct intent. Courts assessing such claims must examine the full context, including any known defects or warnings provided by prior owners. Only by accounting for these variables can true responsibility be assigned in cases where magical artifacts behave unpredictably after leaving their creator's hands. This rigorous standard ensures that all stakeholders remain accountable for the ongoing dangers posed by items imbued with potent forces.

body.heading: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences
body.text: When objects traverse between planes of existence, questions arise regarding which legal regime applies to disputes arising from their journey or aftermath. The Accords establish that the laws of origin dominate unless modified by explicit agreement or subsequent events occurring on foreign soil. However, exceptions exist where local statutes impose stricter protections than those of the item's home realm. In such instances, the more protective standard prevails to safeguard innocent parties unfamiliar with exotic hazards. Furthermore, cross-planar contracts must specify governing law clearly, addressing potential conflicts that may emerge from differing magical traditions or customs. Ambiguities will be construed against the drafter who benefited from unclear terms. This framework aims to provide certainty in an inherently unstable environment where physical and metaphysical boundaries blur constantly. By defining jurisdictional priorities upfront, parties can avoid costly litigation later when disputes inevitably surface along the volatile frontier of interdimensional commerce.

body.heading: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences
body.text: The pricing mechanisms employed by mages often reflect their unique skill sets rather than conventional market values. While this flexibility benefits clients seeking specialized services, it risks creating exploitative situations where powerful practitioners charge exorbitant sums for routine tasks. To counteract such abuses, the Accords mandate transparency in all fee negotiations and prohibit hidden charges or bait-and-switch tactics. Clients retain the right to reject inflated demands and seek alternatives within reason. Additionally, sliding scales based on income levels may be applied to ensure equitable access regardless of wealth disparity. Special provisions address emergencies where immediate action is required, allowing pre-arranged rates to stand even without full disclosure beforehand. These safeguards strike a balance between preserving professional autonomy and preventing predatory practices that could undermine public trust in the magical community's integrity overall.

body.heading: Collateral Doctrine — Unintended Consequences
body.text: As time passes, details about past magical activities become obscured or lost entirely. Yet these fragments still shape present realities in subtle ways. When evaluating disputed events, courts must weigh conflicting testimonies carefully, recognizing that memory fades even under oath. Written records carry greater weight unless proven forged or tampered with through supernatural means. Oral traditions deserve respect too, serving as valuable supplements when documentation is sparse or contradictory. Special attention goes to identifying any anachronisms in witness statements that might indicate fabrication or deliberate misrepresentation. Cross-referencing multiple sources helps reconstruct what truly happened amidst the fog of uncertainty. Ultimately, truth emerges gradually through persistent investigation and open dialogue among all involved parties committed to uncovering the facts behind veiled histories shrouded by centuries of mystery.

sections.title: Transit Stamps; Planar Tolls; Extraterritorial C

body.heading: § 1201.6 Related Requirements - Transit Stamps; Planar Tolls; Extraterritorial C
body.text: The provisions set forth in §§ 1201.1 through 1201.4 operate subject to the following additional conditions and limitations, which shall be construed as integral components of the regulatory regime governing interplanar commerce and transit. First, it is hereby declared that any magical artifact or construct bearing a valid Transit Stamp issued under these Accords shall be deemed presumptively legal for entry into Autumnwood space, notwithstanding contrary assertions to the effect thereof. This presumption may only be rebutted by clear and convincing evidence of illicit manufacture or tampering with said artifact post-stamping. Second, all parties engaged in planar transport operations are required to maintain adequate insurance coverage against potential liabilities arising from accidental releases of hazardous magics during transit. Failure to secure such coverage shall result in immediate suspension of operating privileges pending remedial action. Third, no caster shall attempt to utilize extraterritorial casting techniques within a Diet Chamber without express written authorization from the Hall's governing body. Unauthorized attempts at such forbidden practices constitute serious breaches of public safety and may subject the offending party to harsh penalties under applicable law. Fourth, it is imperative that all cartographic representations sold as licenses for raiding operations accurately reflect the true nature and extent of authorized activities therein depicted. Misrepresentation or omission of material facts concerning scope of permissions granted shall render said documents void ab initio and expose the responsible vendor to civil suit and criminal prosecution at their sole discretion. Fifth, nothing contained herein shall be construed to limit in any way the inherent sovereign powers of individual Hall jurisdictions to regulate conduct within their respective territories as they see fit consistent with higher law. This includes but is not limited to enforcement of local zoning ordinances, noise abatement statutes, and nuisance laws applicable to all persons operating within said bounds regardless of foreign status or citizenship claims advanced thereto. Finally, the foregoing provisions shall apply mutatis mutandis to all forms of cross-dimensional exchange including yet not limited to itemized trades, service agreements, knowledge transfers, and technological licensing arrangements involving planar entities. Any attempt to evade these obligations through complex structuring schemes will be met with swift and decisive action by competent authorities charged with oversight duties herein established under authority vested thereby in them alone for purposes of maintaining orderly conditions conducive to peaceful coexistence among all peoples inhabiting this blessed domain collectively known as Autumnwood. Let none presume otherwise upon pain of dire consequences ensuing forthwith unless specially exempted hereunder by order of the High Council sitting en banc after full deliberation thereof duly conducted pursuant to established procedural rules governing such matters exclusively within its purview alone without regard for external influences whatsoever tending towards undermining unity and stability achieved through diligent efforts expended thus far unto this very moment in history defined solely by our shared destiny intertwined forevermore into one great tapestry woven with threads of gold and silver spun from dreams long past forgotten save only by those brave souls willing enough to risk all they have on a chance glimpse beyond the veil separating us from infinity itself. body.heading: § 1201.6 Planar Jurisdiction and the Sovereign's Reach
body.text: Under § 1201.5, related requirements bind all transit across jurisdictional boundaries, yet the precise scope of this authority requires further elaboration. This section clarifies the extent to which a Hall's laws apply beyond its physical walls, particularly when casting extends into foreign territories or higher planes. The guiding principle remains that magic is not bound by geography but by consent and contract; thus, any act performed under a valid license retains its legal integrity regardless of location. However, this does not grant unlimited freedom from local statutes or customs where they conflict with the Accords. In such cases, the Hall's laws prevail as superior authority, enforced through diplomatic channels or direct intervention if necessary. Furthermore, extraterritorial casting may trigger special provisions regarding tolls, permits, and liability for unintended consequences. Practitioners must exercise due diligence to ensure compliance with both home and host jurisdictions before proceeding. Failure to do so may result in sanctions ranging from fines to revocation of credentials. Ultimately, the goal is to maintain harmony between disparate legal systems while protecting the rights and safety of all parties involved. As § 1201.6 states clearly: "Magic knows no borders, but its practitioners must."

body.heading: § 1201.7 Planar Citizenship and Dual Allegiance
body.text: A mage licensed by one Hall may find themselves operating within another's sphere, creating complex issues of dual citizenship and conflicting obligations. This section addresses how such situations are resolved under the Accords. The fundamental rule is that a practitioner retains their primary allegiance to their home Hall while respecting the laws of any host jurisdiction they enter. However, certain acts committed abroad may still fall under the purview of the Home Authority if they violate core tenets of the Accords or constitute fraud against the licensing system itself. In these instances, the Host Hall must cooperate fully with investigations and enforcement actions initiated by the Home Office. Conversely, a practitioner temporarily residing in another region retains all rights and protections afforded to them under their original license unless explicitly stated otherwise in writing. Special provisions apply when casting crosses planes entirely; here, both origin and destination authorities share responsibility for oversight and accountability. Disputes arising from these intricate arrangements shall be settled through established dispute resolution mechanisms outlined elsewhere in this Code. As § 1201.7 affirms: "One license rules all worlds, but courtesy dictates local customs."

body.heading: § 1201.6 Planar Jurisdiction and the Sovereign's Reach — Continued
body.text:
Whereas planar transit is often governed by local customs and the whims of minor entities, this Codex establishes that all such matters ultimately fall under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. This principle holds regardless of whether the traveler enters via gateways, rifts, or natural portals. By virtue of their status as sovereigns within their respective realms, each Planar Sovereign retains exclusive authority over laws and disputes occurring on their territory. However, this sovereignty does not extend beyond their borders; a mage who crosses into another realm must immediately submit to the laws of that new domain. Failure to do so constitutes a breach of treaty obligations and may result in severe penalties, including seizure of property and permanent exile from all Planes.

The Desk maintains a Registry of Recognized Ports of Entry, wherein each location has been vetted for safety and compliance with Accords standards. Travelers are required to register at these designated points upon arrival or departure, providing proof of licensure and payment of applicable tolls. Unregistered crossings are presumed illegal and subject to immediate interdiction by Aegis Magi or their proxies. In the event of a dispute over which jurisdiction applies, the burden of proof falls upon the party asserting territorial control. They must demonstrate clear evidence that the incident occurred within their borders and under their dominion. Absent such proof, default adjudication will favor the Accords Desk in accordance with established precedent.

It is further provided that Planar Sovereigns shall cooperate fully with the Desk in enforcing these provisions, including the provision of personnel and resources as necessary. Refusal to comply may result in sanctions ranging from suspension of trade rights to revocation of recognition status altogether. In extreme cases where a Sovereign actively undermines Accords authority or engages in hostile acts against member entities, collective measures may be taken by consensus of the Hall. Such actions shall be limited to what is strictly necessary to restore order and protect innocent parties. Nothing herein shall be construed to infringe upon legitimate rights of Planar inhabitants vis-à-vis their own governments, so long as they do not violate Accords obligations or harm third parties unjustifiably. This framework ensures balanced oversight while respecting the autonomy inherent in multi-planar existence.

body.heading: Planar Sovereignty and the Limits of Jurisdiction
body.text:
§ 1201.6 Planar Sovereignty and the Limits of Jurisdiction — Continued

The authority of any sovereign extends only so far as its laws can be enforced. In the case of planar entities, this limitation is profound. While a Hall may assert dominion over its territory, it cannot extend that control beyond the threshold unless specific conditions are met. The first such condition is explicit consent from the affected party or their duly appointed representatives. Without such authorization, any attempt to impose Hall law upon another plane constitutes an act of aggression and shall be treated as such under § 1201.3.

The second condition involves the presence of a formal treaty or agreement between the two jurisdictions. Such agreements often delineate areas of mutual interest and outline procedures for resolving disputes peacefully. In their absence, each Hall retains sole discretion over how it interprets its own laws in relation to neighboring realms. This principle is designed to prevent endless litigation over matters of little consequence while reserving the right to act swiftly when necessary.

A third consideration concerns the nature of the entity attempting to extend its influence across planar boundaries. Only those possessing legitimate claim to authority may do so, and even then only within strict limits defined by their respective charters. Unauthorized attempts at expansion shall be met with resistance equal to the threat posed, regardless of whether the opposing force is armed or unarmed. This stance ensures that no single Hall can become too powerful relative to its peers without first earning their respect through fair play and transparent dealings.

Ultimately, these guidelines serve as a framework for maintaining stability in an inherently unstable environment. By establishing clear rules governing inter-planar interactions, all parties benefit from reduced conflict and increased predictability in their operations. Failure to adhere to these principles risks alienating potential allies and inviting unwanted confrontation down the line. As such, they should be regarded not merely as suggestions but as binding obligations incumbent upon every responsible citizen of this shared cosmos.

body.heading: Planar Sovereignty and the Limits of Jurisdiction — Continued
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords recognize that planar travel introduces unique challenges to traditional notions of territorial jurisdiction. Under § 1201.6, it shall be unlawful for any licensed mage to cast spells within a foreign realm without securing prior authorization from that plane's governing body. Failure to do so constitutes extraterritorial casting and subjects the caster to penalties under § 1201.3. This provision aims to prevent magical conflicts between different planar jurisdictions while maintaining the integrity of local laws.

Planar tolls, as outlined in § 1201.2, serve as a mechanism for collecting fees associated with crossing into another dimension. These tolls are assessed based on factors such as the caster's power level, duration of stay, and purpose of visitation. Collected funds are allocated to support planar infrastructure maintenance and enforcement efforts. Refusal or failure to pay applicable tolls may result in denial of re-entry privileges under § 1201.5.

Cartographic representations of other planes, whether purchased independently or as part of a research permit package, do not grant automatic access rights. As clarified in § 1201.4, possession of such maps alone does not constitute legal grounds for entering foreign realms without proper credentials. Unauthorized entry remains subject to prosecution regardless of the caster's intentions or qualifications.

The Accords further stipulate that all planar activities must remain consistent with established safety protocols designed to minimize risk to both visitors and hosts. Any deviation from these guidelines may trigger immediate investigation by local authorities upon return. Repeat offenses could lead to suspension or revocation of casting licenses under § 200.4. This framework ensures responsible engagement with exotic environments while preserving the autonomy of each distinct reality.

Ultimately, adherence to these provisions protects all parties involved in interdimensional commerce and exploration. By balancing individual freedoms with collective security concerns, the Autumnwood Accords promote sustainable growth within this boundless sphere of possibility. All mages are expected to uphold these standards diligently for the greater good of our shared existence across the multiverse.

body.heading: § 1301.6 Related Requirements for Penalty Assessment and Enforcement
body.text:
In furtherance of the Accords' commitment to proportionate justice and deterrence, any penalty imposed under this Part shall be subject to several additional procedural safeguards and substantive requirements designed to ensure fairness and consistency in their application. First, before a final judgment is rendered, the accused mage must be afforded an opportunity to present mitigating evidence or arguments that may warrant a reduction in severity of punishment. This includes but is not limited to proof of first-time offending, expressions of genuine remorse, participation in remedial programs, or circumstances beyond their control that contributed to the violation. The adjudicating body shall evaluate such submissions with discretion guided by precedent and the overarching principles of restorative justice enshrined in § 1.8.

Second, all penalties must be calibrated to achieve both retributive and rehabilitative ends. While inflicting appropriate suffering upon wrongdoers is necessary for maintaining order within the magical community, it should not serve as an end unto itself. Rather, sanctions ought to aim at reforming offending individuals so they may return safely to productive roles in society. To this effect, whenever feasible, alternative measures such as probationary periods with strict monitoring conditions, mandatory education on ethical casting practices, or compensated service to the Guild shall be considered before resorting to harsher punishments like permanent sealing of magical aptitude under § 1001.23.

Third, transparency in the assessment process is paramount to preserving public confidence in the system's integrity. Unless compelling reasons exist for keeping details confidential—for instance where national security would be compromised—findings and rationales behind penalty decisions must be publicly disclosed with sufficient clarity allowing meaningful scrutiny by all interested parties. Redactions should only occur after careful review and justification on a case-by-case basis; blanket secrecy is contrary to the spirit of open governance promoted herein. Failure to comply with these transparency mandates may result in reversal of the original ruling upon appeal, underscoring their status as mandatory prerequisites rather than mere guidelines.

Finally, mechanisms exist for periodic reassessment of penalties imposed under this Code to ensure continued relevance and effectiveness given evolving societal norms and technological developments affecting magical practice. A dedicated committee composed of representatives from various stakeholder groups shall meet annually to review existing sanctions in light of new data, expert opinions, and feedback collected through official channels. Recommended modifications will be submitted for vote by the full Governing Council with ample notice provided to all members prior to consideration. Only after thorough deliberation may changes be enacted into law retroactively if deemed necessary for correcting unjust outcomes or adapting to changing circumstances. This ongoing commitment to improvement reflects the Accord's dynamic nature as a living document meant to serve humanity rather than enslave it.

body.heading: § 1301.6 Related Requirements for Penalty Assessment and Enforcement — Continued
body.text:
The assessment and enforcement of penalties under the Autumnwood Accords shall adhere to strict procedural safeguards designed to ensure fairness and consistency in application. Prior to imposing any sanction upon a licensor or caster found guilty of violations, the Presiding Magistrate must issue a formal notice detailing the specific breaches alleged, affording the accused an opportunity to present mitigating evidence or arguments for leniency. Failure to provide such due process shall render any penal action void and unenforceable at law.

Penalties prescribed herein are calibrated according to the gravity of the infraction and the resulting harm caused thereto. Minor infractions may warrant warnings, fines commensurate with gains realized from illegal activity, or revocation of specific privileges for limited durations. More serious offenses shall attract escalating sanctions up to and including permanent licensure suspension, sealing of magical aptitudes, or expulsion from the Guild entirely. In cases involving egregious malfeasance, referral to civil authorities for criminal prosecution may be deemed appropriate at the discretion of the Court.

Enforcement actions must be conducted through duly appointed Magistrates acting within their statutory authority. Unlawful attempts by private individuals or unauthorized entities to collect penalties shall constitute trespass and potential assault, subject to separate liability proceedings. All monies collected pursuant to this Part shall be deposited into the Guild Treasury for reinvestment in regulatory programs, public education initiatives, and compensation funds for affected parties as authorized by law.

Appeals of penalty assessments may be lodged within thirty (30) days of notification thereof with the Autumnwood Accords Desk Review Board. Such appeals must be supported by written briefs setting forth grounds for relief along with relevant documentation substantiating claims made therein. The Review Board shall convene to hear arguments from both parties before rendering a final determination, either affirming, modifying, or vacating the challenged order as warranted under prevailing legal standards applicable hereto.

This Section is intended to supplement but not supersede any other provisions contained elsewhere in these Accords bearing upon matters of disciplinary discipline. In instances where ambiguity arises between conflicting mandates herein and throughout this Code, the principles of proportionality and reasonableness shall guide interpretation thereof so as best effectuate their purposes consistent with overarching values embodied by this regulatory framework.

body.heading: § 1301.6 Related Requirements for Penalty Assessment and Enforcement — Continued — Continued
body.text:
The assessment and enforcement of penalties under the Autumnwood Accords shall adhere to several additional procedural requirements designed to ensure fairness and consistency in disciplinary actions. First, all penalty determinations must be made by a quorum of at least three Aegis Magi or senior Conservators sworn to uphold this Code, acting in good faith without bias or conflict of interest. Such magisters shall deliberate privately before reaching any final ruling on charges brought against an accused caster.

Second, written notice of all penalties imposed must be formally delivered to the subject via certified magical courier or direct hand-delivery. This notice shall specify the nature and duration of each sanction, along with instructions for redress should the penalty prove excessive or unjustified. Failure to provide adequate notification may result in automatic remission of associated costs.

Third, all penalties imposed under this Code must be documented in detail within official records maintained by the Autumnwood Accords Desk. These archives shall include transcripts of proceedings, relevant evidence considered, and reasoned findings supporting each decision rendered. Such documentation serves both as a historical record and basis for future reviews or appeals.

Fourth, any penalties levied against minor casters under age sixteen require prior parental consent and must be scaled appropriately to their abilities and circumstances. Special protections afforded by § 1301.2 shall apply mutatis mutandis to such cases. In all instances involving juveniles, the primary goal remains corrective education rather than punitive retribution.

Finally, periodic audits of penalty assessments will be conducted annually by an independent panel appointed by Archmage Veyra herself. This oversight body possesses authority to review any contested rulings and issue binding corrections as needed. Their determinations are final and not subject to further appeal or revision. Through these safeguards, the Guild ensures its disciplinary system operates with integrity and equity at all times.

body.heading: § 1301.6 Related Requirements for Penalty Assessment and Enforcement — Continued — Administration
body.text:
Under § 1301.2, penalties imposed upon violators of the Autumnwood Accords are calibrated to reflect both the gravity of the infraction and the culpability of the offender. Where appropriate, sanctions may be mitigated by demonstration of genuine remorse or restitution made prior to adjudication. Conversely, aggravating circumstances—such as recidivism, premeditation, or infliction of severe harm—shall result in escalated punitive measures. The Presiding Magistrate retains discretion to adjust penalties within the statutory range based on individualized assessment of mitigating and aggravating factors.

§ 1301.2 further stipulates that penalties shall be enforced consistently across all jurisdictions under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. To this end, a unified register of sanctions imposed is maintained by the Guild's Central Registry Office in Autumn Wood. This database enables real-time tracking of cumulative infractions and facilitates coordinated enforcement efforts between regional tribunals. Violators found to have committed multiple offenses may face aggregated penalties reflecting the totality of their misconduct.

In cases where penalties exceed the authority delegated to local magistrates, referral for higher-level review shall be initiated pursuant to § 1301.4. Such referrals are reserved exclusively for extraordinary circumstances requiring intervention by senior-ranking officials within the Guild hierarchy. Appeals regarding penalty assessments may be lodged in accordance with procedures set forth in § 1301.5, subject to applicable time limits and evidentiary requirements.

It is the duty of all parties involved—whether accusers, accused, or witnesses—to cooperate fully during penalty determination proceedings. Refusal to comply with lawful orders from competent magistrates may result in additional sanctions imposed under their authority. Furthermore, any attempt to obstruct, interfere with, or otherwise undermine the administration of justice shall be treated as a serious offense in itself, subject to independent investigation and prosecution.

Ultimately, the goal of penalty assessment and enforcement is not merely retribution but rehabilitation and deterrence. By imposing proportionate consequences tailored to each unique case, the Guild seeks to uphold its commitment to fairness while maintaining order within the magical community. Through diligent application of these principles, we strive to foster an environment where magic can flourish safely under wise stewardship."

body.heading: § 1301.6 Related Requirements for Penalty Assessment and Enforcement — Continued — Oversight
body.text:
In addition to the base penalties outlined in § 1301.2, the Council retains discretion to impose supplemental sanctions tailored to the specifics of each violation and the offender's history. These may include mandatory restitution payments calculated at market value plus a fifteen percent administrative surcharge; compulsory attendance at ethics seminars or practical retraining courses relevant to the infraction; temporary suspension of privileges ranging from one day to one month depending on severity; and public shaming via guild bulletin boards, digital forums, and in-person announcements where appropriate. Reoffending within twelve months triggers an automatic fifty percent increase in subsequent penalties unless mitigating factors are presented and accepted by at least two-thirds of the Council members present.

The burden of proof for establishing a violation rests squarely with the accusers, who must demonstrate guilt beyond reasonable doubt through credible testimony, documentary evidence, or magical verification as dictated by the nature of the alleged offense. Defendants enjoy full rights to counsel, cross-examination of witnesses, and presentation of exculpatory evidence without fear of retaliation. In cases where penalties exceed one hundred gold pieces, a formal hearing before the entire Council is required prior to implementation. All proceedings are recorded verbatim in official minutes available for public inspection upon request and payment of a nominal fee.

Appeals against imposed sanctions may be filed within ten days of notification by submitting written objections outlining grounds for reversal or modification along with supporting documentation. Such appeals are reviewed de novo by an independent panel drawn randomly from among Council members not involved in the original decision. The burden remains on appellant to prove error by clear and convincing evidence. Final determinations issued by this appellate body are binding and subject only to review by the Archmage Sovereign upon petition signed by at least three-fifths of all Guildmasters. Failure to comply with duly imposed penalties constitutes contempt punishable under § 1302, including imprisonment without bail pending resolution of outstanding charges.

The Council further empowers designated Enforcement Officers to seize disputed items, freeze assets, and issue restraining orders when necessary to preserve the status quo during active investigations or litigation. All seizures are accompanied by detailed inventories itemizing quantities, descriptions, estimated values, and dates/times of recovery. Stored property remains subject to claims by rightful owners who appear promptly with proof of ownership and payment of applicable storage fees totaling ten gold pieces per month plus twenty-five percent interest annually thereafter. Unclaimed goods held for more than six months become escheat property of the Guild to be disposed of as deemed appropriate in Council discretion, netting proceeds toward general operating expenses after deducting lawful costs incurred during retention.

This section shall remain subject to periodic revision based on evolving circumstances, judicial interpretations, and recommendations from specialized subcommittees charged with monitoring implementation efficacy over time. Any proposed amendments must receive favorable votes from a majority of voting members present at duly convened meetings before becoming operative upon publication in the next issue date of this Codex. Until such changes take effect, existing provisions continue to govern conduct without modification regardless of subsequent developments outside these written pages unless explicitly superseded by later enacted statutes or regulations adopted pursuant to lawful authority vested herein.

"Justice delayed is justice denied." - Ancient Proverb
"Cruelty to animals presages cruelty to men." - Archmage Theron, circa 842 AR
"To punish a crime without punishing the criminal is a farce worthy of none but fools and knaves." - Janna Brightspark, Speech at the Grand Conclave, Autumnwood, 910 AR
"Let us be clear: we do not negotiate with criminals. We enforce our laws against them." - Council Resolution #2734-B, Section III(a)(iv)
*See also §§ 1301.1, 1301.2, 1301.3, 1302, 1303, 1304, 1305*

body.heading: § 1301.6 Related Requirements for Penalty Assessment and Enforcement — Continued — Procedure
body.text:
The oversight mechanisms provided in this Part shall operate as an independent check on the discretion vested in enforcement officers, ensuring that penalties are imposed fairly and consistently across all jurisdictions within the Autumnwood Accords. To this end, each Regional Magistrate shall establish a Standing Review Committee composed of three (3) randomly selected licensed mages per quarter, who shall audit a sample of closed cases to assess compliance with procedural due process and substantive legal standards. The composition of these Committees shall be rotated annually to prevent the development of entrenched biases or conflicts of interest among reviewers.

The primary function of each Standing Review Committee is to examine case files for errors in fact-finding, misapplication of law, or abuse of prosecutorial authority by either party. Upon completion of their review, the Committee shall issue a written report detailing any deficiencies identified and recommending corrective action where warranted. Such reports shall be filed with the Autumnwood Accords Desk and made available upon request to all interested parties, subject only to redaction of privileged communications and personally identifiable information protected under § 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form.

In addition to their periodic audits, Standing Review Committees shall maintain an ongoing dialogue with enforcement officers throughout the term of office, providing guidance on emerging legal issues and best practices for case management. This collaborative approach is intended to foster a shared understanding of evolving standards in arcane law while preserving the integrity of the adjudication process as a whole. Regular briefings and training sessions may be convened as needed to disseminate information and promote professional development among all participants in the system.

The provisions herein shall apply uniformly regardless of the nature or severity of the alleged offense, reflecting the principle that justice must be blind to status and circumstance alike. While resource constraints may necessitate certain practical accommodations in remote areas where qualified magistrates are scarce, no party shall ever be denied access to meaningful oversight simply due to geography or economic disadvantage. The right to a fair hearing remains inviolate, even in the most challenging circumstances.

It is hereby declared that these measures constitute an essential component of the broader framework for maintaining order and stability within the realm of magic. By ensuring accountability at every level—from street-level enforcement through appellate review—the Accords seek to build public trust in their institutions while safeguarding the rights of all citizens subject to their jurisdiction. This commitment to excellence serves both pragmatic ends and higher ideals, affirming our shared dedication to truth, equity, and the rule of law.

sections.title: Incorporation by Reference and Foreign Precedent

body.heading: Incorporation by Reference and Foreign Precedent
body.text:
This section addresses ancillary obligations incidental to the primary regulatory scheme herein codified. First, nothing in these provisions shall be construed to abrogate or impair any existing contractual rights between private parties acting in good faith, absent explicit statutory modification. Second, all reporting requirements imposed by this Act are subject to reasonable administrative convenience and cost considerations; failure to comply does not automatically invalidate subsequent transactions unless expressly provided. Third, the Desk may issue clarifying guidance memoranda regarding ambiguous terms without formal rulemaking proceedings, though such interpretations carry no binding force absent codification in amendment or new regulation. Fourth, any dispute arising under this Part shall be resolved exclusively through arbitration administered by a panel of qualified magisters appointed by the Sovereign; judicial intervention is precluded except upon petition for writ of mandamus alleging arbitrary or capricious action. Finally, all records maintained pursuant to these regulations shall remain confidential unless redacted disclosure is expressly authorized by law or court order; violation of such confidentiality mandates subject to severe penalties under § 1302.4. This section ensures operational flexibility while preserving core protections afforded herein and in related statutes. See §§ 1.5, 1.7(b), 100.6(a)(ii).

[ARCHIVE CARD]
Section 1401.6 – Related Requirements
- § 1401.6(1) Contractual Rights: Private agreements unaffected unless expressly modified by law
- § 1401.6(2) Administrative Convenience: Reporting obligations subject to practical feasibility limits
- § 1401.6(3) Clarifying Guidance: Desk may issue non-binding interpretive memoranda
- § 1401.6(4) Exclusive Arbitration: Disputes resolved via magisterial panels, barring extraordinary circumstances
- § 1401.6(5) Confidentiality Safeguards: Strict protection of regulated data with severe penalties for breach

[RELEVANT CITES]
See also §§ 1.7(b), 1.9(c)(ii), 1302.4(a)(iii), 100.6(a)(ii). Under § 1.5, private contracts survive unless explicitly overridden by statutory mandate. Section 1.7(b) permits equitable construction where literal interpretation yields absurd results. The Desk's authority to issue guidance flows from § 100.6(a)(ii), while confidentiality protections derive from § 1302.4. Judicial review remains highly circumscribed, consistent with the specialized nature of arcane affairs. This balanced approach maintains regulatory efficacy without unduly burdening lawful commerce.

body.heading: § 1401.7 Incorporation by Reference and Foreign Precedent
body.text: Whereas the Autumnwood Accords stand as the supreme law governing magical practice within the Guild's jurisdiction, nothing herein shall be construed to preclude the consideration of relevant foreign precedents or technical standards, provided such materials do not contravene any explicit provision of this Codex. The Desk may, in its sole discretion, incorporate by reference any international treaty, convention, or best-practice guideline deemed pertinent to a matter before it, so long as such incorporation does not expand the scope of the Accords beyond their original intent. Any foreign authority incorporated shall be treated as if fully quoted within this text and shall carry equal weight in subsequent adjudications. However, no provision of any external document shall override a clear mandate herein unless specifically authorized by amendment. Furthermore, nothing contained in these Rules shall be interpreted to endorse or validate the practices of rival organizations such as the Regal Empire's Iron Mandate or similar entities operating outside Guild oversight. The Desk retains unfettered authority to reject any foreign standard deemed incompatible with the spirit and letter of the Accords. In all cases, the ultimate determination rests with the Archmage Sovereign, whose judgment in matters of precedent-setting significance is final and unappealable. See § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate; § 1.5 Relation to Other Law; § 1.8 Effective Date.

body.heading: Interpretive Canons and Presumptions
body.text:
In the absence of explicit provision, certain foundational principles govern the construction of this Accords Desk's regulations. First, it is presumed that any ambiguity in the text shall be resolved in favor of public safety and order, not the convenience of individual casters or their commercial interests. This presumption applies equally to both Conservator and Innovator provisions, reflecting the Desk's overriding mandate to protect the general populace from magical harm. Second, where multiple valid interpretations exist, the one most consistent with the spirit and purpose of the Accords as a whole shall prevail. The literal meaning of isolated clauses may yield to a broader reading that advances the overall goals of magical regulation. Third, conduct patterns are aggregated in assessing violations; repeated minor infractions may cumulatively warrant severe sanctions comparable to a single egregious act. This principle recognizes that habitual disregard for the law poses a greater threat than occasional lapses in judgment. Finally, any doubt as to whether an action is permitted shall be resolved by requiring prior written authorization from the Desk. Casters are encouraged to consult with Guild officials before undertaking novel or potentially risky magical operations to avoid inadvertent breaches of the Accords. These interpretive canons serve as guiding lights for all subsequent applications of this Code, ensuring that its broad mandates are implemented consistently and fairly across all contexts.

body.heading: § 1401.7 Incorporation by Reference and Foreign Precedent, Interpretive Canons a
body.text:
The Accords may incorporate by reference the provisions of other laws, rules, or documents in their entirety or in part. Such incorporated material becomes part of these regulations as if fully set forth herein. However, no act of incorporation shall be effective unless specifically approved by a majority vote of the full Council during an open session duly convened and called to order. Incorporated materials must bear an official seal or stamp certifying authenticity and currency at time of adoption. Any subsequent amendments to incorporated provisions require separate approval through the same formal process as original enactment. This safeguard prevents inadvertent modification of binding obligations through careless drafting techniques.

In matters of interpretation, these regulations shall be construed liberally in favor of public safety and orderly conduct consistent with their stated purposes. Ambiguities shall be resolved by reference to legislative history, committee reports, and official statements made during deliberation proceedings. Where language proves unclear after exhaustive analysis, the intent of the enacting body governs over literal wording. Presumptions favorable to maintaining peace and preventing harm apply unless expressly rebutted by clear evidence to contrary effect. These principles guide adjudication whenever textual meaning remains uncertain despite good-faith efforts at clarification.

Foreign laws and customs from other jurisdictions may be cited as persuasive authority but never controlling precedent within this legal system. Local statutes always prevail over external influences absent explicit delegation of power to adopt them by reference. The Council retains sole discretion to determine when and how outside materials inform domestic policy decisions. Any reliance upon imported norms must be justified by reasoned analysis demonstrating relevance to the specific issue at hand. Arbitrary or capricious invocation of alien standards shall not constitute valid grounds for altering established rules without proper procedure followed thereafter.

Archmage Veyra signed under her official seal on this 15th day of Harvest, in the year of our Sovereignty one thousand nine hundred and forty-two, to wit: "By these articles we bind ourselves together as guardians of magic itself." So sayeth the Great Seal of Autumnwood. 🛡️✨

body.heading: § 1401.7 Incorporation by Reference and Foreign Precedent, Interpretive Canons a — Continued
body.text: § 1401.7 is enacted to ensure that the Accords are interpreted consistently across all jurisdictions and time periods, preventing any single Hall or faction from imposing its own arbitrary readings upon the law. To this end, several core principles of statutory construction apply whenever a provision in these Codebooks is ambiguous or unclear. First, where two interpretations remain equally plausible after applying standard tools of construction, the one that favors continued vitality and growth of magical practice shall prevail over any other alternative reading. This reflects the fundamental purpose of the Accords: to foster innovation while maintaining public safety. Second, all provisions herein must be read in harmony with one another; no clause may be construed so as to render another superfluous or contradictory. If a literal interpretation would lead to absurd results inconsistent with common sense and basic fairness, then the more reasonable meaning shall govern unless expressly forbidden by plain language. Third, any doubt arising from an obscure term of art should be resolved in favor of those relying upon it rather than those drafting it—a rule that protects less sophisticated practitioners from exploitation by technically superior adversaries. Finally, where gaps exist in the text or coverage, courts may look to analogous provisions elsewhere within these Codebooks for guidance, applying them by necessary implication unless doing so would contravene explicit commands found therein. These interpretive canons serve as a safeguard against both overly rigid formalism and unchecked judicial discretion, ensuring that the spirit of the Accords remains intact even when their letter seems unclear. By adhering strictly to these established rules of construction, all parties may have confidence that disputes will be resolved fairly according to principles known to all, rather than according to whimsical personal opinions held by any particular judge or arbitrator. In this way, § 1401.7 advances the overarching goals of stability and predictability upon which the entire magical community depends for its continued prosperity.

body.heading: § 1401.7 Interpretive Canons and Presumptions
body.text:
In construing the provisions hereof, certain interpretive principles shall govern to ensure consistent application across all jurisdictions under the Accords' dominion. First, it is presumed that all clauses are written with deliberate intent and no superfluous words shall be read into them; conversely, every word must bear meaning in context. Where ambiguity persists after applying literal interpretation, the rule of lenity applies only when the penal consequences favor one reading over another—in which case, the lesser sanction prevails unless explicit contrary instruction appears elsewhere in this Codex or its schedules.

Second, conduct regulated here shall be construed liberally to effectuate legislative purpose where plain meaning yields uncertainty or absurd results. This principle does not permit judges to rewrite law but rather ensures that statutory gaps are filled reasonably consistent with overarching policy goals articulated within these pages. In particular, provisions designed to protect public safety or prevent magical harm may be enforced even absent explicit language mandating such outcomes, so long as the regulatory scheme supports this reading.

Third, where multiple reasonable interpretations exist for a given term or phrase, preference shall accord to that construction most consistent with established precedent within the Mages' Guild and related bodies having jurisdiction over similar matters. In cases of first impression lacking guiding authority, decision-makers may consult analogous statutes from neighboring realms or foreign magical traditions—but only after exhausting domestic sources. Such external references carry persuasive but not dispositive weight unless adopted expressly by competent authority.

Finally, this section shall be applied in a manner that promotes uniformity in enforcement while respecting legitimate variations among local customs and practices where they do not conflict with mandatory provisions herein. Regional differences in magical norms or historical precedents may inform—but never override—the application of these rules unless specifically authorized by the Accords Desk itself. Thus interpreted, this framework seeks to balance clarity with flexibility sufficient to address evolving circumstances without constant amendment.

sections.title: § 200.8 Exemptions and Waivers

body.heading: § 200.7 Related Requirements; § 200.8 Exemptions and Waivers
body.text:
This Part shall be construed in conjunction with the General Provisions set forth herein, particularly §§ 1.4–1.9 regarding persons bound, construction principles, and savings clauses. Nothing contained in this Section shall be deemed to modify or limit any obligations imposed by applicable law other than as expressly provided. The Guild Desk retains inherent authority to issue supplemental guidance memos where ambiguity arises during implementation; such memoranda shall carry the force of law unless explicitly revoked.

The Desk may, at its sole discretion and upon written notice, grant temporary exemptions from specific licensure requirements for individuals demonstrating exceptional merit or facing genuine hardship. Such waivers must be renewed annually and are subject to immediate termination should conditions change. No waiver shall extend beyond a single calendar year without explicit reauthorization. Requests for exemption must include comprehensive justification including but not limited to prior service record, community impact, and financial need assessment.

Guest casters operating under § 200.5 remain fully subject to all safety protocols and conduct standards regardless of their formal status. The Desk shall maintain a registry of approved guest practitioners with verification of credentials and disciplinary history. Any guest caster found violating rules faces immediate ejection and possible permanent banishment from Guild premises. Construct entities utilizing magical abilities as described in § 200.6 shall comply with all operational regulations applicable to natural persons engaged in similar activities. Failure by a construct or its owner to meet these standards may result in cessation of services and liability for damages incurred.

This Section operates subject to the overriding authority vested in the Sovereign Archmage under the Accords Framework. The Desk shall consult with the Archmage when determining whether exceptional circumstances warrant discretionary relief from standard provisions. All decisions made pursuant to this Section must be documented in writing and made available upon request by interested parties subject to reasonable privacy protections. Nothing herein shall be interpreted to create any property interest or contractual obligation absent explicit written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both the Guild and affected individuals/entities.

The Desk further reserves the right to impose additional conditions or restrictions as deemed necessary to safeguard public welfare and maintain professional standards within the magical community at large. Such measures must bear reasonable relation to legitimate regulatory objectives and shall be applied uniformly regardless of individual circumstances. Violation of any condition imposed herein constitutes grounds for immediate revocation of licensure privileges with consequent legal ramifications under existing statutes.

This Section may not be waived orally or impliedly; any modification requires express written consent from all parties involved and must be filed with the Desk for recording. Unauthorized attempts to circumvent these requirements shall constitute a serious breach subject to severe penalties including criminal prosecution where appropriate. The Desk commits to transparent administration of this policy while maintaining necessary flexibility to address evolving challenges within our dynamic profession responsibly and effectively.

body.heading: Exemptions and Waivers
body.text:
Section 200.8 grants limited relief from licensure requirements for specific categories of practitioners or under extraordinary circumstances, subject to strict oversight by the Guild Desk. This provision exists solely as an exceptional measure, not a general right, and may be invoked only upon demonstration of compelling necessity that cannot otherwise be met through standard licensing channels.

First, bona fide members of recognized scholarly institutions engaged in peer-reviewed research may operate without individual licensure when their work directly furthers the collective knowledge base of magic theory and practice. Such researchers must maintain active standing within their institution's governing bodies and submit annual reports detailing their findings to the Desk for review. Failure to comply with these reporting obligations shall result in immediate revocation of exemption status.

Second, emergency medical practitioners who possess valid state licenses may cast healing spells without Guild licensure when responding to life-threatening situations outside regular business hours. This privilege extends only to spells classified as Arts I through III under the Schedules and must be exercised solely for therapeutic purposes. Any commercial exploitation of this exception shall constitute a serious violation subject to full penal sanctions.

Third, practitioners holding diplomatic immunity or official representatives of foreign sovereign nations may operate without licensure when performing duties within their assigned scope of authority. This exemption applies only to acts performed in an official capacity and does not extend to private activities undertaken outside of official business hours. The Desk reserves the right to revoke this status at any time upon proper notice.

Finally, individuals who have made exceptional contributions to magical research or education over a sustained period may petition for honorary licensure exempting them from certain regulatory requirements. Such petitions require unanimous approval by the Conservator Council and must demonstrate tangible benefits to the broader magical community beyond mere personal convenience. Discretionary exemptions granted under this subsection shall be reviewed annually for continued validity.

All requests for waivers or exceptions must include comprehensive documentation supporting the claimed necessity, along with a detailed plan for mitigating potential risks to public safety. The Desk retains sole authority to approve or deny such applications and may impose additional conditions deemed appropriate in any given case. Applicants should note that denial does not preclude future consideration if circumstances change materially.

In all cases involving exemptions from licensure requirements, the fundamental protections afforded by these Accords remain fully operative. Practitioners benefiting from relief under this section shall continue to adhere to all other applicable provisions regarding ethical conduct, client safety, and professional accountability. The Guild Desk maintains oversight authority even where formal licensure has been waived.

See also § 100.2 (representative authority), § 400.3 (borrowed hours), and § 500.4 (healing as consideration). Under § 1.6, "exemption" refers to dispensation from mandatory licensure while preserving underlying obligations. Pursuant to § 1.7, this section applies only where no conflicting provision exists in other parts of these Accords. Effective immediately upon adoption by the Desk.

body.heading: Exemptions and Waivers, Exemptions and Waivers
body.text:
§ 200.7 Related Requirements; § 200.8 Exemptions and Waivers

The licensing requirements set forth herein are not absolute but subject to such reasonable exemptions and waivers as the Guild Desk may determine in its sole discretion. Such relief shall be granted only upon a showing of exceptional circumstances, compelling necessity, or public interest that outweighs the regulatory objectives of this Part. Petitions for exemption must be filed in triplicate with supporting evidence and sworn affidavits, accompanied by payment of the standard filing fee plus an additional 25% surcharge to cover expedited review costs. The Desk shall afford due process rights including notice, opportunity to respond, and a hearing if contested. Any waiver granted shall specify its scope, duration, conditions precedent, and reporting obligations; failure to comply may result in immediate revocation with penalties as provided elsewhere in this Code. Examples of permissible exemptions include emergency response operations where delay would cause irreparable harm, charitable or educational activities conducted without commercial motive, and historical reenactments performed solely for preservation purposes. Conversely, waivers shall not be extended to cover any conduct that would constitute a substantive violation of safety standards or ethical mandates under the Accords. The Desk retains broad authority to interpret these provisions as may best serve the protection of the public welfare and maintenance of magical order within our realm. All determinations regarding exemptions shall be reduced to writing, reasoned in full, and made available for public inspection upon request. This flexibility is intended to balance rigorous oversight with practical accommodation of legitimate needs that fall outside the ordinary scope of regulated practice yet still warrant some measure of official recognition or facilitation.

body.heading: § 200.7 Related Requirements: Prerequisites and Qualifications for Licensure
body.text:
No person shall apply for licensure under the Accords without first satisfying all statutory prerequisites established by the Autumnwood Desk, whether enumerated herein or prescribed by special order of a full session. See §§ 1.6, 300.2; also § 100.5. Failure to meet these baseline criteria renders an application void ab initio, regardless of subsequent compliance with procedural formalities. Under § 1.4 and § 1.7, the burden lies upon the applicant to demonstrate affirmative proof of qualification through sworn affidavit accompanied by certified transcripts or official attestations where appropriate.

A primary prerequisite is the attainment of a minimum age threshold set at twenty-one calendar years unless dispensed from this restriction by special warrant signed by Archmage Veyra in person. See § 200.1; cf. § 300.4. This limitation exists to ensure that all licensees possess sufficient maturity and judgment to responsibly wield magical arts without endangering themselves or the public at large. Minors wishing to pursue licensure must instead petition for inclusion within an approved apprenticeship program supervised by a licensed mentor in good standing under § 200.2, with periodic review of their progress and character.

Additionally, applicants shall submit a comprehensive background investigation conducted pursuant to § 1301.4, disclosing any prior convictions, civil judgments, or disciplinary actions taken against them for violations of the Accords or related statutes. Any history of substance abuse, violent behavior, or unethical conduct will be grounds for immediate disqualification without further notice. See §§ 1.6, 1201.3; also § 1401.1. The Desk reserves the right to deny licensure in its sole discretion if an applicant's record raises reasonable doubts regarding their fitness to practice safely and lawfully.

Furthermore, all prospective licensees must successfully complete a standardized examination administered by certified proctors designated by the Guild Hall. This assessment evaluates theoretical knowledge of magical principles alongside practical competency through hands-on demonstrations under controlled conditions. Failure to achieve a passing score on either component will result in automatic rejection unless retaken upon subsequent application subject to applicable fees and scheduling constraints outlined in § 1301.1. See §§ 1301.2, 1401.5; also § 300.1. The exam serves as an objective measure of applicant readiness to assume professional responsibilities without compromising public safety or ethical standards mandated by the Accords.

Finally, every license applicant shall execute a binding oath affirming their commitment to uphold the spirit and letter of the Autumnwood Accords in all future actions taken within the scope of licensure. This solemn pledge constitutes a voluntary submission to ongoing oversight by the Desk and acceptance of disciplinary measures should misconduct be discovered post-licensure. See § 100.2; also § 1.8. Without such an oath, no application shall be entertained regardless of otherwise favorable qualifications or credentials presented in support thereof. The requirement underscores the gravity with which the Guild views its duty to regulate magic responsibly for the benefit of all society.

"Magic demands mastery over self before it can safely shape reality." — Archmage Veyra's Prologue to the Autumnwood Accords

body.heading: § 200.7 Related Requirements: Prerequisites and Qualifications for Licensure — Continued
body.text: § 200.7 Related Requirements: Prerequisites and Qualifications for Licensure. To qualify for licensure under this Part, an applicant must satisfy specific prerequisites established by the Mages' Guild Desk. First, all applicants shall possess a minimum of ten (10) years of documented magical experience or equivalent academic training from a recognized institution. Second, candidates must demonstrate proficiency in at least two (2) distinct schools of magic as verified through standardized testing administered by the Aegis Magi. Third, each applicant shall submit to a comprehensive background check conducted by the Guild's Security Division, which includes but is not limited to criminal record searches, magical history reviews, and peer references from licensed practitioners. Fourth, all candidates must attest in writing that they are free of any outstanding debts or obligations to the Mages' Guild or its affiliated entities. Finally, each applicant shall pay a non-refundable application fee of one hundred (100) Wario Coins plus applicable taxes as set forth in § 300.1 Schedules of Fees. Failure to meet any of these prerequisites shall result in automatic disqualification from the licensure process. The Desk reserves the right to waive or modify these requirements on a case-by-case basis upon demonstration of exceptional merit or compelling circumstances." "Notwithstanding the foregoing, certain categories of individuals may be exempted from one or more of the above requirements under limited conditions prescribed by rule. For instance, holders of provisional passes issued prior to the enactment of this Part shall be granted a grace period of six (6) months to bring their credentials into compliance without penalty." "The Mages' Guild Desk shall promulgate additional guidelines and procedures relating to licensure qualifications as deemed necessary for the efficient administration of this Code. All such rules shall take precedence over conflicting provisions herein unless expressly superseded by subsequent amendment or repeal." "This Section shall be construed liberally in favor of applicants who have made good faith efforts to comply with all applicable standards, while maintaining strict enforcement against those who seek to evade lawful obligations through technicalities or malfeasance." "In witness whereof, this Section is hereby adopted and enacted into law on the date first written above under the authority vested in me by the Sovereign Archmage Veyra and the Council of Elders of the Mages' Guild." "CROSS-REFERENCES: See § 1.6 Definitions for meanings of technical terms used herein; see also § 300.1 Schedules of Fees regarding applicable charges and payments; refer to § 400.1 Research Permits for analogous qualification criteria governing special-purpose licenses."

body.heading: § 200.9 Licensing Categories and Restrictions
body.text:
The Accords establish a tiered system for licensure, recognizing that not all casters pose equal risks to public safety or magical equilibrium. Licenses are divided into three primary classes: Class A permits unrestricted practice within Guild-regulated zones; Class B allows limited casting in designated areas under supervision; Class C is reserved for novices undergoing probationary training. Each category imposes specific obligations on the licensee regarding insurance, reporting, and compliance with ongoing education requirements. Failure to maintain requisite standards may result in downgrading or revocation of privileges.

Special provisions apply to those dealing with dangerous artifacts or forbidden schools. Such practitioners must obtain additional endorsements from Archmage Veyra before engaging in any activities involving these materials. The Desk maintains a registry of approved handlers, subject to periodic review and re-certification. Unauthorized possession or use of restricted items constitutes grounds for immediate suspension pending investigation. Penalties escalate based on severity of violation and prior record.

Protections extend beyond mere regulation into the realm of ethical conduct. Licensors are expected to uphold principles of responsible magic, avoiding abuse of power or exploitation of vulnerable populations. Violations may trigger disciplinary proceedings independent of criminal liability. The Guild retains broad discretion to impose sanctions at its sole discretion, including but not limited to fines, suspension, expulsion, and referral for prosecution where appropriate.

The Desk periodically audits license holders to ensure adherence to all stipulations. Inspections may be conducted without prior notice, with full access granted to premises and records as needed. Refusal to cooperate is deemed an admission of guilt and subject to immediate penalties. Compliance histories are tracked meticulously, influencing future licensing decisions. Repeat offenders face heightened scrutiny regardless of offense level.

Ultimately, the licensing framework exists to balance freedom of practice with collective security concerns. By categorizing casters according to risk profiles and behavioral patterns, the Guild aims to foster an environment where magic may flourish safely and productively for all. This nuanced approach reflects the maturity of the Autumnwood Accords as a whole—a recognition that true mastery requires not only technical skill but also wisdom in application.

see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; see § 1.4 Persons Bound; see § 700.6 Related Requirements.
