sections.title: Prohibited Correspondence and Magical Transmission

body.heading: Prohibited Correspondence and Magical Transmission
body.text:
§ 300.7 Prohibition on Unauthorized Magical Communication and Data Transfer

It shall be unlawful for any licensed caster to engage in the transmission of magical data, spells, or techniques via forbidden channels without explicit authorization from the Autumnwood Accords Desk. This includes but is not limited to unauthorized use of scrying mirrors, dreamwalking, telepathic projection, or any other method that circumvents standard communication protocols. Such actions are deemed a breach of § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting and may result in suspension or revocation of licensure under § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse.

The prohibition extends to the sale or exchange of magical information through illicit markets, including but not limited to shadow web forums, black market auctions, and clandestine training sessions. Any caster found guilty of facilitating such transactions shall be subject to immediate disciplinary action pursuant to § 1301.2 Penalties. Repeat offenses may lead to permanent expulsion from the Guild and revocation of all privileges granted under these Accords.

Exceptions to this rule include authorized academic research conducted in accordance with § 400.1 Research Permits and legitimate commercial applications approved by the Desk. All such activities must be pre-approved in writing and subject to ongoing monitoring to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations. Failure to obtain proper authorization shall constitute grounds for disciplinary proceedings under § 1301.3 Appeals.

The Guild reserves the right to inspect any suspected violations of this provision at its discretion, including but not limited to electronic records, personal devices, and physical premises where illegal transmissions may occur. Refusal to submit to such inspections shall be treated as an admission of guilt and will result in immediate suspension pending further investigation. All findings of fact and conclusions of law shall be made available upon request to affected parties in accordance with § 1401.2 Dead Citations.

This section takes precedence over any conflicting provisions contained herein or elsewhere within the Autumnwood Accords framework. Any ambiguities arising from the application of these rules shall be resolved favorably toward maintaining public safety and protecting the integrity of magical practice within the jurisdiction. The Desk retains full authority to interpret and enforce this provision as it deems necessary for the preservation of order and justice under the law.

body.heading: Prohibited Correspondence and Magical Transmission — Continued
body.text:
§ 300.7 Related Requirements, Prohibited Correspondence and Magical Transmission. No magical communication shall originate or terminate within an official Autumnwood Accords facility without prior authorization from the Desk, except as expressly permitted by statute or ruling. This prohibition extends to all forms of arcane correspondence, including but not limited to scrying, telepathy, enchanted writing implements, and any device capable of transmitting thought or image across distance. Violation of this provision constitutes a Class C misdemeanor subject to fines up to one hundred gold pieces and/or suspension of casting privileges for a period not exceeding ninety days per offense.

The intent behind § 300.7 is twofold: first, to maintain the integrity of Accords proceedings by preventing covert influence or intimidation through unauthorized means; second, to protect both casters and non-casters from potential harm resulting from unregulated magical experimentation conducted in close proximity to sensitive documents or classified information. The Desk shall issue written permits for specific instances where magical communication is deemed necessary to the conduct of official business, stating clearly the duration, purpose, and scope of such permission. Any caster found violating these restrictions without proper authorization shall be subject to immediate disciplinary action at the discretion of the presiding officer.

Furthermore, it is hereby prohibited for any individual within an Accords facility to utilize their inherent magical abilities in a manner that disrupts or interferes with normal office operations, regardless of whether such use constitutes formal casting under existing statutes. This includes but is not limited to spontaneous manifestations of power triggered by emotional states or environmental factors, as well as the deliberate employment of minor charms or illusions for personal convenience. Failure to comply may result in warnings, mandatory training sessions on appropriate conduct, or more severe penalties depending upon circumstances and prior record.

Casters are reminded that their privileges within the Accords system are granted conditionally, contingent upon adherence to all applicable laws and regulations governing magical practice. Respect for colleagues and staff is paramount at all times, whether interactions occur face-to-face or through magical channels. Any behavior deemed offensive, harassing, or disruptive will not be tolerated and may lead to escalation of disciplinary measures up to and including expulsion from the Guild entirely. It remains the responsibility of each individual caster to exercise sound judgment and professional decorum in accordance with these guidelines.

see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 200.3 Temporary Mouths; see § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs; see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters.

body.heading: § 300.7 Prohibited Correspondence and Magical Transmission
body.text:
The Accords strictly prohibit the use of forbidden schools of magic to facilitate communication across planar boundaries, except under exceptional circumstances approved by the Conservators' Council. This prohibition extends to all forms of magical correspondence, including scrying circles, teleportation spells cast for messaging purposes, and enchanted items designed solely for transmitting information between realms. Violations constitute a Class B infraction subject to sealing of magic and a fine of up to one thousand Wario Coins per incident.

Notwithstanding the foregoing ban, certain specialized magical artifacts known as "Conduits" may be registered with the Guild for legitimate diplomatic and commercial use. Conduit registration requires submission of detailed schematics and origin certification from the manufacturer or creator. Registered Conduits must bear an official seal indicating their approved status and are subject to periodic re-inspection every five years. Unauthorized reproduction, modification, or diversion of a registered Conduit is punishable as grand larceny under Article IX of these Accords.

The Guild maintains a dedicated division tasked with monitoring magical communications networks for signs of illicit activity. This unit operates under the direct authority of Archmage Theron and reports findings to the full Council on a quarterly basis. Agents of this division possess broad investigative powers, including the ability to compel testimony and seize evidence without warrant when probable cause exists. Refusal to cooperate may result in immediate suspension of licensure pending further review.

Any individual wishing to establish or expand a magical communication network must first obtain written permission from the Conservators' Council. Applications should be submitted on standard form CM-42B, accompanied by proof of financial stability and character references from reputable members of the arcane community. The Council will evaluate each request on its merits, taking into account potential impacts on public safety and national security before granting approval or denial.

Violations of this section shall result in penalties up to and including permanent revocation of licensure and imprisonment for up to ten years without benefit of writs or appeals. Repeat offenders may face additional sanctions at the discretion of the presiding councilors, including exile from Autumn Wood or execution by proxy under conditions determined solely by the Guild. The strict enforcement of these provisions serves the greater good of maintaining stability in an increasingly volatile magical landscape.

See also: § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill (regarding automated messaging systems); § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration (concerning quid pro quo exchanges involving illicit information); and Article IX, Section 14 of the Iron Mandate on Espionage and Counter-Espionage Operations.

"The pen may be mightier than the sword, but a sealed mouth is far more effective in preventing leaks." — Archmage Theron, Address to the Conservators' Council, Autumnwood Hall, 5th Day of Frostfall, Year of the White Stag.

body.heading: § 300.7 Prohibited Correspondence and Magical Transmission — Continued
body.text:
Under no circumstances shall any communication or conveyance via magic that would normally require physical presence be utilized to circumvent the provisions of these Accords, unless expressly authorized in writing by the Conservatory Council. This prohibition extends to all forms of telepathic projection, scrying, astral travel, and remote spellcasting intended for commercial gain or personal advantage without prior clearance. Violation of this clause constitutes a Class A felony offense under § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber and shall be punished by immediate revocation of licensure and imprisonment in the Pocket Prison until trial. The intent behind this restriction is to preserve the integrity of face-to-face interactions which form the bedrock of lawful commerce and social cohesion within the realm. Any attempts to bypass these safeguards will result in swift and severe consequences, as the Council remains vigilant against all forms of magical malfeasance. See also §§ 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion regarding acceptable conduct during remote operations. Furthermore, any individual found guilty of utilizing prohibited correspondence methods shall be subject to additional fines and potential exile from the Guild's territories at the discretion of the Archmage Sovereign. The strict enforcement of this provision ensures that all magical activities remain transparent, accountable, and in full compliance with established regulations designed to protect both practitioners and the general public from harm. Failure to adhere to these mandates will be treated as an act of war against the collective interests of the free peoples governed by these Accords. Thus stands the law, immutable and absolute: no magic shall ever supersede the sanctity of direct human engagement in matters of consequence.

"Magic is a tool for enlightenment, not a substitute for personal connection. The Council forbids its misuse to undermine fundamental societal bonds." — Archmage Veyra, Autumnwood Accords, § 300.7 Commentary

body.heading: § 300.7 Prohibited Magical Correspondence and Transmission
body.text:
The Accords expressly forbid the use of magical means to transmit correspondence, whether by telepathy, scrying, or other arcane channels. Such communication is deemed a breach of professional decorum and may compromise the confidentiality of Guild deliberations. This prohibition extends to all forms of unauthorized data transfer between mages and non-mages alike. Violation shall result in immediate suspension pending review by the Ethics Committee under § 200.4. Exceptions are granted only upon written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign for matters of national security or critical infrastructure protection. All suspected incidents must be reported forthwith to the nearest Hall Inspector via standard channels outlined in § 100.6. Failure to comply with this mandate constitutes a Class A infraction subject to penalties prescribed in § 1301.2. The Guild retains broad discretion to expand these restrictions as circumstances warrant, without further notice. Mages are expected to exercise extreme caution when engaging in any form of remote interaction that might circumvent established protocols. See also §§ 500.4–500.5 regarding ethical boundaries in magical services.

The Desk interprets this prohibition strictly and will not tolerate any loopholes being exploited for personal gain or political advantage. Unauthorized scrying operations are treated as theft of intellectual property under § 1201.3, punishable by fines up to one thousand gold pieces per incident plus disgorgement of ill-gotten gains. In egregious cases involving espionage or sabotage, criminal charges may be filed pursuant to the Penal Code attached hereto as Schedule C. The burden of proof rests squarely upon the accused mage to demonstrate lack of intent and negligence. Repeated violators face permanent revocation of licensure under § 200.4(b)(ii). Special attention is paid to digital transmissions via crystal grids or enchanted networks; these are considered tantamount to direct communication and subject to identical restrictions. The Guild maintains a database of approved secure channels for official business, which all members must utilize unless otherwise directed. Any deviation requires prior approval from two independent Conservators sworn to uphold this clause unconditionally. See §§ 400.2–400.3 concerning proper containment procedures during field operations. Non-compliance jeopardizes both individual standing and collective safety, warranting swift disciplinary action without prejudice to further investigation if warranted by the facts developed therein.

sections.title: Specimen Containment Standards and Disposal Proto

body.heading: § 400.7 Related Requirements - Specimen Containment Standards and Disposal Proto
body.text:
This section governs the storage, handling, and disposal of magical specimens acquired through research activities authorized under these Accords. All items classified as "Specimens" shall be maintained in secure containment units meeting minimum safety thresholds established by the Guild's Laboratory Safety Board. Failure to comply with these standards may result in revocation of research privileges and penalties for negligent or willful misconduct.

§ 400.7(a) Specimen Classification and Labeling
Each specimen must bear a unique identifier linking it to its original acquisition record, as maintained by the Guild's Inventory Control Division. Labels shall include descriptive data including composition, potential hazards, known properties, and recommended handling procedures. Items posing immediate threat of harm may be marked with a visible warning symbol per § 1401.2(a). The owner or custodian is responsible for ensuring all information remains accurate and up-to-date throughout the specimen's lifecycle.

§ 400.7(b) Storage Facilities
Specimens shall be stored in facilities designed specifically to mitigate risks associated with their nature. Temperature, humidity, light exposure, and atmospheric composition must be monitored continuously where applicable. Structural integrity of containment vessels is paramount; regular inspections per § 1301.1 are mandatory. Special provisions apply to volatile or unstable materials requiring dedicated isolation zones away from populated areas. Any deviation from prescribed storage conditions constitutes a violation subject to disciplinary action under § 200.4(b).

§ 400.7(c) Handling and Disposal
Direct manipulation of specimens without appropriate training and protective equipment is strictly prohibited. Transferring custody requires completion of official paperwork detailing reason, duration, and security measures in place. Upon conclusion of research or when no longer needed, specimens must be properly disposed of according to environmental regulations outlined in Part V. Destruction methods vary based on item type but always prioritize containment of residual magical signatures. Unauthorized disposal attempts trigger immediate investigation under § 1201.4(d).

§ 400.7(d) Cross-Contamination Prevention
Strict protocols exist to prevent interaction between incompatible specimens that could result in hazardous reactions or loss of data integrity. Segregation by hazard class and chemical compatibility are primary concerns. Shared storage arrangements require explicit approval from the Laboratory Safety Board with conditions clearly stated. Breach of these safeguards voids any immunity claims under § 400.3(c) and may lead to suspension of research credentials pending review.

§ 400.7(e) Documentation and Audit Trails
Complete records must be kept for each specimen including provenance, testing results, modification logs, and ultimate disposition. Digital backups stored on secure servers complement physical archives maintained at the main Guild hall. Random audits conducted by internal oversight committees verify compliance with this subsection's mandates. Violations discovered during such reviews incur additional sanctions beyond those prescribed in § 200.4(c). Consistent adherence to these requirements demonstrates professional responsibility and commitment to public safety, core values upheld by all members of the Autumnwood Accords community.

body.heading: § 400.7 Research Specimen Containment and Disposal Standards
body.text: Under § 400.6, all research specimens obtained through lawful means must be maintained in accordance with rigorous containment protocols. Specimens classified as Class I or II shall be stored within sealed lead-lined vaults equipped with active dampening fields capable of neutralizing residual magical signatures for a minimum of ten (10) years post-acquisition. Class III and IV materials may be kept in standard reinforced glass cases, provided they remain in constant surveillance by certified containment officers trained specifically in arcane hazard management. No specimen shall ever be removed from its designated storage facility except under direct supervision of two (2) Guild inspectors with valid credentials and matching security clearances for the specific material class involved. All handling procedures must adhere strictly to the Containment Manual, latest revision § 400-12B, with particular attention paid to secondary containment barriers designed to prevent accidental release in event of primary vessel failure. Regular integrity checks on storage vessels shall occur at weekly intervals during active research phases and monthly thereafter, documented via digital log and signed by responsible custodians. Any observed degradation or compromise of containment systems requires immediate reporting to the Safety Board for emergency remediation action. Upon completion of approved studies, all specimens must be either returned intact to their original owners within fourteen (14) calendar days or disposed of through authorized incineration facilities operated exclusively by licensed hazardous waste contractors meeting Arcane Disposal Certification standards. Unauthorized retention or transfer of research materials outside the confines of registered laboratories constitutes a serious violation subject to disciplinary proceedings under § 200.5 and potential revocation of all active permits and licenses held by the offending party. Strict adherence to these containment and disposal mandates ensures public safety while preserving scientific integrity within our valued community of scholars. Failure to comply may result in severe penalties including permanent exclusion from future research opportunities and criminal prosecution where applicable under relevant national statutes governing dangerous substances. See also § 300.5 regarding restrictions on research copy distribution, § 400.2 concerning safe pocket dimension usage protocols, and § 1201.4 prohibiting unauthorized cartographic exploitation. All personnel involved in specimen handling must complete mandatory annual training modules covering latest safety guidelines and emergency response procedures as dictated by evolving best practices in the field. The Guild reserves absolute discretion to modify these requirements at any time upon notice via official bulletin board postings or direct communication channels maintained with each institution holding active research permits under this section. Immediate notification shall be issued should any known vulnerabilities emerge requiring prompt operational adjustments across all facilities subject to oversight jurisdiction herein established by virtue of their continued operation within our regulatory framework. Compliance remains paramount to protecting both researchers and society at large from potential catastrophic consequences arising from mishandling dangerous magical substances without proper safeguards in place as outlined above under this comprehensive set of related provisions governing specimen containment and ultimate disposal methodologies employed throughout our domain of influence extending far beyond mere territorial borders into realms yet uncharted by human exploration alone.

body.heading: Research Specimen Containment and Disposal Standards
body.text:
§ 400.7 Research Specimen Containment and Disposal Standards

All research specimens acquired or generated pursuant to a valid permit shall be maintained in accordance with strict containment protocols designed to prevent accidental release of hazardous magical energies or biological agents. Specimens must be housed in sealed containers rated for the specific class of material, labeled clearly with identifying information and hazard warnings as prescribed by § 301.2(b). Storage facilities shall be equipped with appropriate shielding, filtration systems, and emergency containment measures commensurate with the risk profile of the stored items.

Upon completion of research activities or expiration of a permit's validity period, all specimens must be disposed of through approved channels under supervision of a designated Guild official. Disposal methods may include ritual dissolution, transmutation into inert matter, incineration within a licensed containment unit, or transfer to a certified waste management facility meeting Arcane Safety Council standards. No specimen shall be discarded without proper documentation verifying compliance with these requirements. Failure to adhere to containment and disposal mandates constitutes serious misconduct subject to disciplinary action under the Penal Code.

The Guild reserves the right to conduct unannounced inspections of research sites to verify adherence to containment protocols. Officials may seize non-compliant specimens for testing or destruction at their discretion. Repeated violations resulting in exposure risks will trigger immediate suspension of all permits held by the offending party and potential revocation of licensure. Research facilities must maintain detailed logs documenting specimen handling, storage conditions, and disposal actions for review upon request.

These provisions reflect the Guild's unwavering commitment to protecting both casters and the general public from preventable harm associated with improper management of dangerous magical materials. Strict compliance is non-negotiable given the catastrophic potential consequences of negligence in this critical area of practice. The Desk shall enforce these standards rigorously without exception, imposing sanctions as warranted by the circumstances.

see § 400.1 Research Permits; see § 301.2(b) Hazard Labeling Requirements; see § 605.3(a)(ii) Prohibited Waste Disposal Methods

body.heading: § 400.7 Specimen Disposal Protocols and Hazardous Waste Management
body.text:
§ 400.7 Specimen Disposal Protocols and Hazardous Waste Management; Containment Integrity and Environmental Safeguards

In furtherance of the research permit requirements established under § 400.1, this Part prescribes mandatory standards for the containment, handling, and disposal of hazardous magical specimens and byproducts generated during permitted field operations. All casters holding active research permits shall comply with these protocols without deviation to ensure public safety and prevent ecological contamination.

Specimens classified as Class A or B under § 300.2 require double-sealed containment vessels equipped with pressure relief valves rated for the specimen's maximum potential output. These vessels must be stored in secure, lockable facilities approved by the Conservators. Under no circumstances shall a caster possess multiple high-risk specimens simultaneously without explicit written authorization from Archmage Theron or his designate. Any breach of containment protocols resulting in exposure to untrained personnel constitutes gross negligence and may lead to immediate revocation of research privileges under § 200.4.

Disposal procedures must be executed only by licensed hazardous waste contractors registered with the Guild's Environmental Safety Bureau. Disposal fees assessed per specimen shall be paid prior to final permit termination. Failure to remit these fees within thirty days of notification constitutes a debt obligation enforceable under ordinary civil process, notwithstanding any ongoing research activities. The Conservators reserve the right to audit disposal records and inspect contractor certifications at their discretion.

Research facilities utilizing pocket dimensions as laboratory spaces pursuant to § 400.2 must maintain continuous monitoring systems capable of detecting anomalous energy signatures indicative of containment failure or unauthorized activity. Alarm thresholds shall be calibrated according to the most sensitive specimen present on-site. In the event of a breach, all personnel must evacuate immediately and report the incident within five minutes via encrypted channels designated by the Guild's Emergency Response Division. Deliberate concealment of such events aggravates penalties under § 1301.2.

This regulatory framework balances the legitimate needs of magical inquiry with prudent safeguards against accidental catastrophe. The Conservators acknowledge that rapid technological advancement may necessitate periodic updates to these standards, subject to public notice and comment periods as required by § 1401.4. All provisions herein shall be construed liberally in favor of maintaining environmental integrity and public welfare.

For further guidance on specific disposal methodologies or emerging hazard classes, consult the Conservator's Technical Advisory Board or refer to Appendix D: Specimen Safety Handbook (2024 Edition). Violations of this section may result in severe sanctions including permanent revocation of research permits under § 1301.2(c)(iii).

"Safety first, always." - Archmage Theron, Opening Remarks at Annual Research Symposium, Autumnwood 2024.

body.heading: § 400.7 Specimen Containment and Disposal Standards
body.text:
Under § 400.5, all Titan-growth experiments must be conducted under direct supervision to prevent unauthorized expansion into adjacent territories or the local ecosystem. This provision is supplemented by rigorous containment protocols detailed in this section. Research facilities utilizing pocket dimensions as temporary laboratories shall maintain sealed containment fields rated for Class-IV arcane leakage at a minimum. These barriers must be monitored continuously by automated sensors linked directly to the Guild's central alert network, ensuring immediate notification of any anomalous readings or breaches.

Further, all specimens harvested during field operations must be catalogued and stored in approved secure vaults within seventy-two hours of retrieval. The custody chain shall remain unbroken until final analysis is complete and results are submitted for review by a panel of Conservator-mages. Failure to adhere to these storage mandates constitutes gross negligence under § 1201.3 and may result in suspension of the researcher's license pending investigation into potential contamination or loss of valuable data.

Specimens deemed hazardous to untrained personnel shall be marked clearly with biohazard symbols and accompanied by comprehensive safety warnings. Disposal of such materials must occur only at licensed incineration facilities equipped with specialized filtration systems capable of neutralizing residual magical properties before releasing exhaust into the atmosphere. Unauthorized dumping or abandonment of specimens in public spaces is strictly prohibited and punishable as a Class-B felony under § 300.6, given the grave risks posed to civilian populations by uncontrolled magical fallout.

Researchers violating these containment and disposal standards shall face immediate revocation of their research permits and potential referral to the Paradox Trial for further adjudication of culpability. The Guild reserves the right to audit any facility suspected of non-compliance at reasonable times with proper notice, inspecting records, equipment, and storage areas as deemed necessary. Persistent offenders may find themselves blacklisted from future research opportunities across all member mages' halls, effectively ending their academic careers unless they can prove substantial reform through years of exemplary service under strict oversight.

This section exists to safeguard both the public welfare and the integrity of arcane study by enforcing disciplined handling of dangerous materials throughout the entire lifecycle—from collection to final disposal. Compliance is not optional but a fundamental obligation owed to society at large, ensuring that the pursuit of magical knowledge does not come at unacceptable cost to those who do not share in its benefits. Violations will be prosecuted with utmost severity, reflecting the profound stakes inherent in irresponsible manipulation of raw power.

body.heading: § 400.7 Specimen Custody and Disposal Protocols
body.text:
Under the broad rubric of research specimen management, the Accords mandate rigorous protocols for the secure containment and ultimate disposal of magical materials obtained during sanctioned studies. While § 400.5 addresses unauthorized proliferation of Titans through unregulated growth patterns, it is this companion clause that governs the fate of raw specimens once their utility has been exhausted. Research facilities operating under valid permits are required to maintain sealed storage units meeting minimum safety thresholds established by the Conservators' Engineering Bureau. Failure to adhere to these containment standards constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty and may result in immediate revocation of research privileges.

Specimens deemed hazardous or unstable must be disposed of through approved channels no later than thirty days following completion of a study cycle. Disposal methods vary based on the specific properties of the material but invariably involve neutralization via high-energy discharge or containment within a stabilized pocket dimension. The Innovators have argued that some specimens possess intrinsic value and should instead be returned to their native ecosystems, a practice known as "restocking." While theoretically sound from an ecological standpoint, restocking operations require explicit authorization from both the Conservator's Ecological Division and the relevant Hall of Origin. Unauthorized release of specimens into the wild is strictly prohibited under penalty of fines up to one thousand Wario Coins per violation.

Custody records must be maintained for a minimum period of five years, detailing acquisition date, origin coordinates, experimental applications, and final disposition method. These logs serve as critical evidence should disputes arise regarding contamination claims or ecological damage. The Desk reserves the right to audit specimen management practices at any time upon reasonable notice. Persistent non-compliance may trigger escalating sanctions ranging from monetary penalties to outright expulsion from the Guild's research network. Ultimately, these provisions exist not merely as bureaucratic formalities but as essential safeguards against the unpredictable dangers inherent in manipulating raw magical forces without adequate controls or oversight.

see § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth regarding proliferation limits; see § 300.2 Unsanctioned Arts for definitions of prohibited specimen types; see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks for enforcement mechanisms.

sections.title: Duty to Disclose Material Facts

body.heading: Duty to Disclose Material Facts
body.text:
Under § 900.7, every caster filing an application bears a solemn duty to disclose all material facts bearing on their eligibility and qualifications. This obligation extends beyond mere truthfulness in written declarations; it encompasses full disclosure of any prior convictions, sanctions, or disciplinary actions taken against the applicant by any competent authority whatsoever. Concealment of such information constitutes fraud upon the Accords and may result in immediate disqualification and permanent revocation of licensure. See also § 900.1 regarding the timeliness of filings, and § 1401.3 on defenses against the Iron Mandate's extraterritorial claims.

The burden rests squarely upon the applicant to proactively reveal any adverse history that might call into question their fitness to practice magic within the Guild's jurisdiction. This includes but is not limited to: arrests or indictments, civil judgments involving fraud or breach of contract, administrative penalties imposed by other regulatory bodies, and any findings of unprofessional conduct. Failure to volunteer this information shifts the burden to the reviewing magi to unearth it through investigation—a costly and inefficient use of resources better spent on evaluating actual magical competence. Under § 1.6, "material" is defined as facts that would substantially alter a reasonable assessor's judgment regarding an applicant's character or ability.

Casters are further required to furnish copies of all relevant documents supporting their disclosures, such as court records, disciplinary orders, or sworn affidavits attesting to good standing. Where original documentation cannot be produced, certified true copies must suffice. This standard applies equally to foreign judgments and sanctions issued outside the Accords' borders; no distinction shall be drawn based on geography or sovereignty. See § 100.7 for provisions governing interactions with overseas magisterial bodies.

Any intentional misrepresentation or omission deemed material to licensure determination constitutes perjury under local law and may trigger criminal prosecution independent of Guild sanctions. Even inadvertent errors discovered post-filing must be promptly corrected via supplemental submission, accompanied by a full explanation of the oversight. Neglecting this duty invites automatic denial of the application without further review. Ultimately, transparency forms the bedrock of public trust in the licensing system; casting doubt upon an applicant's honesty calls into question their entire suitability to wield magical powers responsibly. As Archmage Theron once cautioned, "A lie today may save a headache tomorrow—but only until someone catches on and destroys everything."

This section governs the affirmative duty imposed on applicants seeking licensure under the Autumnwood Accords. It mandates full disclosure of any adverse history that might affect qualification assessments, with failure to comply resulting in automatic disqualification and potential criminal liability. Related provisions include § 900.1 (timeliness), § 1401.3 (defenses against extraterritorial claims), and § 1.6 (definition of "material" facts). See also § 100.7 regarding foreign regulatory matters, and § 200.5 concerning guest caster disclosures. Underlying principles drawn from §§ 1.4–1.9 emphasize the personal nature of licensing obligations and the importance of accurate record-keeping for public safety.

body.heading: § 900.7 Related Requirements, Obligation to Disclose Material Facts
body.text:
No caster shall knowingly conceal any fact or circumstance material to the filing process, whether by omission, misrepresentation, or deliberate fraud. Such duty extends not only to the accuracy of the written submission but also to the truthfulness of all oral representations made during consultation with a clerk or peer reviewer. Failure to disclose information that would affect the assessment fee, classification, or regulatory compliance shall constitute grounds for immediate revocation of licensure and referral to disciplinary authorities under § 300.2.

This obligation arises at the point of initial contact between applicant and Guild official and persists throughout all phases of review. Casters must affirmatively disclose any prior legal sanctions, unreported magical accidents, or known defects in their practice record that could impact public safety or the integrity of the filing system. Concealment is deemed a breach of fiduciary duty owed to both the community and the Guild itself, regardless of whether such information was requested directly.

Clerks have an independent mandate to probe for undisclosed material facts as part of their investigative function. This may include demanding additional documentation, requiring in-person interviews, or conducting background checks where warranted by red flags raised during preliminary screening. Any evasion or resistance to reasonable inquiry shall be treated as aggravating circumstances and factored into penalty assessments under § 1301.2.

The duty to disclose encompasses not only active deception but also passive negligence resulting from careless error. Casters must exercise due diligence in compiling their submissions, ensuring all relevant details are included and accurately stated. Simple oversights leading to incomplete filings will nonetheless trigger corrective actions designed to bring the record into conformity with statutory standards. Repeated instances of carelessness may lead to suspension or permanent disqualification from practicing magic within Guild-regulated zones.

Ultimately, full candor serves as a cornerstone of the Accords' regulatory framework, enabling informed decision-making regarding resource allocation and risk management. By fostering transparency between practitioners and overseers, the system aims to balance innovation with stability while protecting both individual interests and collective welfare. Those who embrace this ethos contribute meaningfully to the flourishing of magical arts under just governance.

body.heading: Duty to Disclose Material Facts — Continued
body.text:
§ 900.7 Related Requirements, Duty to Disclose Material Facts

Any person filing a magic item for registration shall disclose all material facts known to them regarding the item's origin, composition, and any prior uses or modifications. Failure to do so may result in rejection of the application and potential disciplinary action if the concealment is found to be willful. This duty exists to ensure thorough evaluation by the Desk and to protect public safety from unforeseen risks associated with unknown magical artifacts.

Material facts include but are not limited to: the item's history, any known curses or hazards, details of previous enchantments, and information about the creator if known. Parties submitting applications bear a responsibility to exercise reasonable diligence in gathering such data. However, they need not provide access to privileged communications, trade secrets, or other confidential business information protected by law.

In cases where full disclosure would reveal a trade secret or proprietary process, applicants may file an affidavit affirming that no material facts have been concealed and requesting confidential review of sensitive details by the Desk. Such requests require prior approval from the Archmage Sovereign and are granted only when compelling public interest is demonstrated. The burden remains on the applicant to prove they acted in good faith.

The Desk reserves authority to demand additional information or clarification at any point during evaluation. Ignored notices or failure to respond within prescribed timeframes may lead to automatic denial of the application without further notice. Recidivist offenders who repeatedly withhold crucial details face heightened scrutiny and possible blacklisting from future registration attempts.

Ultimately, transparency is paramount in maintaining trust between the Guild and its stakeholders. By fostering openness and accountability, the Accords aim to mitigate hazards stemming from ignorance while promoting responsible magical commerce across all realms. Each filer plays a vital role in safeguarding our collective future through faithful adherence to these obligations.

body.heading: Duty to Disclose Material Facts - Continued
body.text:
The obligation imposed by this section extends beyond mere filing requirements, encompassing a broader duty of candor toward the Guild and its officers. A caster must disclose all material facts relating to their intended magical operations before commencing any activity subject to regulation. Failure to do so constitutes a breach of trust and may result in severe penalties should undisclosed hazards materialize. Material facts include but are not limited to: (a) the full scope and nature of proposed enchantments or rituals; (b) potential risks to third parties arising from such activities; and (c) any prior violations or disciplinary actions against the caster that could impact their reliability as an operator. This affirmative duty exists independently of any specific filing obligation under other provisions of this Part. The rationale underlying this requirement is twofold: first, it enables proper risk assessment by the Guild and affected communities; second, it fosters transparency and accountability within the magical profession itself. Casters who knowingly withhold material information act not only negligently but potentially maliciously, prioritizing personal gain over public safety. Such conduct warrants swift disciplinary response upon discovery. Enforcement mechanisms include immediate cessation orders, suspension of licenses pending investigation, and referral to appropriate penal tribunals where warranted by circumstances. Ultimately, the duty to disclose serves as a foundational element of responsible magical practice under the Autumnwood Accords framework.

SEE ALSO: § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; § 200.5 Guest Casters; § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure; § 400.1 Research Permits; § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters. UNDER § 1.7 Aggregation of Conduct, multiple failures to disclose may collectively demonstrate a pattern warranting heightened scrutiny. SEE ALSO: § 500.2 Unscheduled Weather regarding unforeseen complications from incomplete disclosures.

body.heading: § 900.7 Related Requirements, Duty to Disclose Material Facts and Intentions in
body.text:
Under the Autumnwood Accords, any party submitting a casting request must disclose all material facts relevant to the proposed magical work. This includes but is not limited to prior enchantments on the subject matter, existing protective wards, known vulnerabilities or weaknesses, and any other information that could meaningfully impact the safety or success of the operation. Failure to provide such disclosure may constitute grounds for refusal of service under § 200.1 Licensure Required, as well as potential disciplinary action for misrepresentation.

Furthermore, requestors are obligated to articulate clearly their intended purpose and desired outcomes for any magical intervention. Vague or ambiguous requests will not be honored, as they pose an unacceptable risk of unintended consequences. The Conservators maintain that magic must always be employed with precision and foresight; reckless experimentation in the name of "discovery" is strictly forbidden under § 300.2 Necromancy - Unsanctioned Arts. Innovators may push boundaries within permitted limits, but never at the expense of public safety or ethical standards.

The Aegis Magi are empowered to investigate any suspected concealment of material facts, exercising broad discretion in determining what constitutes "material" under these provisions. Refusal to cooperate fully with such inquiries may result in immediate suspension of privileges and referral for Paradox Trial proceedings should violations be confirmed. The Guild takes the protection of its citizens seriously; deliberate deception undermines that mission entirely.

This duty extends beyond mere honesty - it requires proactive transparency on behalf of all parties involved. Requestors must take affirmative steps to ensure their casting requests are complete and accurate before submission. Similarly, mages accepting commissions bear a responsibility to clarify any uncertainties immediately upon engagement. Only through such mutual accountability can the delicate balance be maintained between enabling beneficial magic and preventing catastrophic misuse.

In sum, § 900.7 establishes foundational principles of candor and clarity in all magical dealings under the Accords. These obligations serve not only as safeguards against danger but also as expressions of the professional integrity expected of those who wield such powerful forces. All licensed practitioners are held to this high standard without exception.

body.heading: 900.7 Related Requirements — Duty to Disclose Material Facts and Intentions in M
body.text:
Under § 900.6, parties are obligated to disclose any material facts that could affect the outcome of their magical dealings. This duty extends beyond mere factual accuracy to include the true intentions behind a spell's casting or an artifact's acquisition. Concealment of such information is deemed fraudulent under the Autumnwood Accords and may result in severe penalties, including the forfeiture of all gains and imprisonment.

In § 900.7, it is explicitly stated that any intentional misrepresentation of material facts constitutes a breach of contract and grounds for rescission. This principle applies equally to both verbal agreements and written contracts, whether formal or informal. The burden of proving such fraud rests upon the aggrieved party, who must demonstrate not only the existence of undisclosed information but also its potential impact on their decision-making process.

Furthermore, § 900.7 mandates that all parties act in good faith during negotiations involving magical arts. This includes providing full disclosure regarding any known risks or limitations associated with a proposed transaction. Failure to do so may be construed as an attempt to deceive and manipulate the other party for personal gain. The consequences of such behavior are dire, ranging from civil liability to criminal charges depending on the severity of the offense.

It is worth noting that this duty of disclosure also applies to situations where one party possesses superior knowledge or expertise regarding a particular subject matter. In such cases, there is an implied obligation to share relevant information with lesser parties who may lack access to critical data. This ensures fairness and transparency in all dealings involving magic, preventing exploitation of informational asymmetries.

Ultimately, the principles outlined in § 900.7 serve as safeguards against malfeasance and deception within the realm of arcane practices. By requiring honest communication between all involved parties, these provisions foster trust and accountability essential for maintaining order amidst the complexities of spellcasting and artifact trading. Adherence to these standards remains paramount for those seeking to engage responsibly with the powers that be.

body.heading: Public Safety — Additional Protocols
body.text: This Part shall be read in conjunction with the following provisions which govern related matters of public safety and ethical conduct: § 1.4 Persons Bound (defining scope of applicability); § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts (prohibiting forbidden schools without exception); § 500.1 Field Casting for Value (regulating commercial magic work); § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters (governing binding agreements involving mundane parties). See also § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs and § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time regarding temporal manipulation hazards. Under § 700.5 Ethical Boundaries of Professional Practice, all licensed mages must adhere to standards of care even when operating outside formal Guild oversight. The Desk retains discretion under § 100.8 Emergency Sitting to intervene where imminent danger is evident, regardless of jurisdictional limits in § 200.6 Delegation to Clerks. Cross-reference § 300.4 Reclassification for procedures on re-evaluating the risk profile of specific magical applications. All citations herein are binding unless explicitly superseded by newer enactments per § 1.8 Effective Date. The Conservator faction may petition under § 1201.5 Related Requirements to impose additional safeguards deemed necessary for public welfare, subject to review by Archmage Veyra pursuant to § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild. Innovators asserting rights under § 900.6 Related Requirements must submit written justification demonstrating no net increase in societal risk. Failure to comply with any provision of this Part may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure per § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse. Mages found guilty of gross negligence or willful misconduct face enhanced penalties under § 1301.2 Penalties; Sunrise Accrual applies where applicable. The Desk shall maintain a register of all complaints filed under this Section, with summaries made available annually in the Official Record per § 100.4 Records of Speech. Any disputes arising from enforcement actions must be resolved through formal grievance procedures outlined in § 1301.3 Appeals before resorting to extralegal measures prohibited by § 900.7 Related Requirements. Violations involving threats to national security fall under exclusive jurisdiction of the Aegis Magi per § 800.6 Related Requirements, with final adjudication authority vested in Archmage Theron subject to appeal to Veyra. This Section remains in full force and effect until explicitly repealed or amended by proper legislative action as defined herein. All provisions shall be construed liberally to promote public safety while preserving legitimate magical pursuits consistent with the spirit of these Accords. See § 1.7 Construction; Aggregation of Conduct for interpretive guidance on cumulative violations. Any ambiguities shall be resolved in favor of the stricter standard applicable under circumstances present, ensuring maximum protection for all citizens within the Guild's purview. The Desk reserves authority to issue binding clarifications where needed without formal amendment per its inherent administrative powers recognized across multiple Sections. Mages operating under temporary permits issued pursuant to § 200.3 Temporary Mouths remain subject to all provisions herein except those explicitly exempted by their terms of authorization. This comprehensive regulatory framework reflects the complex balance between fostering magical innovation and safeguarding against potential abuses inherent in such powerful abilities. Compliance with these standards is not merely optional but imperative for maintaining social order and public trust in the profession as a whole. Violations may trigger cascading consequences affecting licensure status, professional standing, and even criminal liability depending on severity and impact. The ultimate goal remains ensuring magic serves humanity without becoming its undoing through thoughtless exploitation or unchecked ambition. All stakeholders bear responsibility for upholding these vital principles daily through conscientious practice and mutual respect within the community of magical practitioners. By adhering to this code, mages demonstrate their commitment to ethical excellence beyond mere legal compliance alone. Together they uphold values transcending individual gain or factional interests for the greater good embodied by our shared heritage. This Section stands as a testament to our collective resolve to wield power wisely and protect those who cannot defend themselves against its perils. Through vigilance and unity we shall safeguard both ourselves and the wider world from harm caused by magical misuse whether intentional or accidental alike. Such dedication defines us as true stewards of this ancient craft destined to flourish responsibly for generations yet unborn guided always by wisdom tempered with compassion at every turn along our path forward together hand in hand under the banner of these sacred Accords forevermore.

body.heading: Public Safety — Additional Protocols
body.text:
In the event that a caster is found to have engaged in field casting for value without proper licensure, the Accords dictate a rigorous process for determining liability and remediation. First, an investigation shall be launched by the Aegis Magi to ascertain the full scope of the unauthorized activity. This includes reviewing all records, interviewing witnesses, and analyzing magical residue if applicable. Based on these findings, a preliminary assessment will be made regarding the degree of culpability. If guilt is established beyond reasonable doubt, the caster faces immediate suspension of their license along with substantial fines commensurate to the illicit gains realized. Furthermore, any profits derived from such activities shall be confiscated and donated to the Guild's endowment fund. In cases where repeat offenses are detected or egregious harm was inflicted upon third parties, more severe penalties may be imposed at the discretion of the governing council. This could include permanent revocation of casting privileges and mandatory community service aimed at repairing any damage done to public trust in magical services overall. The ultimate goal remains preserving ethical standards within the profession while ensuring fair recourse for all stakeholders involved. By adhering strictly to these guidelines, we safeguard both individual rights and collective integrity across the realm. It is incumbent upon each mage to uphold this code diligently lest they risk ruinous consequences should they falter in their duties as responsible practitioners of arcane arts bound by solemn oaths sworn before almighty truth itself!

SEE ALSO: § 200.1 Licensure Required; § 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence; § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; § 1.4 Persons Bound under the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Public Safety — Additional Protocols
body.text:
§ 500.7 Casting in Prohibited Zones
No caster shall knowingly cast any spell within the boundaries of designated no-fly zones, military installations, diplomatic enclaves, or other areas where magical interference may cause catastrophic harm to persons or property. Violation constitutes a Class A misdemeanor and subjects the offender to immediate confiscation of equipment and suspension pending investigation. See § 300.2 regarding unsanctioned arts in sensitive locations.

§ 500.8 Unauthorized Use of Public Resources
Casters are forbidden from utilizing public infrastructure—such as streetlamps, water mains, electrical grids, or communication towers—to power their spells without explicit written permission from the appropriate municipal authority. Such misuse endangers the general populace and undermines taxpayer investments in essential services. Offenders shall be liable for all damages incurred and subject to fines up to one hundred times the value of stolen energy. This provision complements § 1503's restrictions on electromagnetic interference.

§ 500.9 Failure to Report Adverse Effects
Any caster who observes or experiences unusual phenomena attributable to their magic must promptly report such incidents to the nearest Guild office for evaluation. Concealment or tampering with evidence is strictly prohibited and may be construed as an admission of guilt under § 2104. Timely reporting facilitates early intervention before minor issues escalate into major crises affecting entire communities. This duty aligns with § 652's mandate for prompt disclosure of hazards.

§ 500.10 Waiver of Immunity
By practicing magic within Guild-regulated areas, casters implicitly waive any claims to diplomatic immunity, sovereign privilege, or other legal protections that might otherwise shield them from prosecution under local ordinances and statutes. The Guild explicitly reserves the right to surrender such individuals to civil authorities for appropriate disposition upon request. This clause reinforces § 1043's assertion of universal jurisdiction over magical crimes committed on public soil.

§ 500.11 Liability for Collateral Damage
Casters bear full responsibility for any accidental damage resulting from their spells, whether intentional or not. Compensation shall be paid forthwith to affected parties in accordance with established tort principles and prevailing case law where applicable. Failure to settle disputes amicably may result in escalated penalties including revocation of licensure. This obligation mirrors § 1850's strict liability standards for hazardous activities undertaken by professionals.

§ 500.12 Cooperation with Investigations
All casters must fully cooperate with any lawful inquiries conducted by authorized agents regarding their magical practices, including production of records, testimony under oath, and submission to reasonable searches without a warrant if exigent circumstances exist. Obstruction of justice will be met with swift disciplinary action up to and including permanent expulsion from the profession. This provision supports § 951's investigative powers granted to senior officers overseeing compliance matters.

§ 500.13 Exemptions and Variances
Exceptions to these requirements may only be granted through formal petition filed directly with the Archmage Sovereign or their duly appointed delegate, accompanied by compelling justification demonstrating necessity outweighing risk. Approvals shall not exceed one year in duration unless renewed annually upon review. Such variances remain subject to immediate revocation should conditions change adversely. This process parallels § 1205's mechanism for temporary permits during emergencies.

§ 500.14 Enforcement Discretion
While these provisions represent mandatory minimum standards, enforcement authorities retain discretion to impose additional measures tailored to specific circumstances when deemed appropriate under the facts of each case. Such latitude ensures flexible response capabilities while maintaining consistency with overarching legal principles outlined herein and in related regulations. This principle draws upon § 760's affirmative defense framework allowing mitigation based on mitigating factors present at time of offense.

§ 500.15 Transitional Provisions
Nothing herein shall affect existing valid contracts or arrangements entered into prior to effective date unless expressly prohibited by their terms. Parties bound by pre-existing agreements may continue operation under those rules until expiration or mutual rescission occurs naturally thereafter. However, any new agreements executed post-enactment must comply fully with all stipulations set forth in this section without exception whatsoever. This grandfather clause aligns with § 2301's treatment of prior obligations vis-à-vis subsequent regulatory changes.

§ 500.16 Severability Clause
Should any provision herein be held invalid or unenforceable by competent judicial authority, such determination shall not render remaining sections defective but rather prompt automatic revision to eliminate offending language while preserving original intent as accurately as possible given statutory constraints imposed by higher law. This salvage operation ensures continuity of governance despite potential gaps arising from litigation outcomes elsewhere in jurisdictional sphere encompassed hereinunder and beyond it alike. Such contingency planning mirrors § 1908's approach to partial invalidity scenarios encountered routinely across diverse regulatory regimes nationwide today.

§ 500.17 Concluding Remarks
These guidelines serve as baseline expectations governing responsible magical practice within our shared society. Adherence thereto fosters mutual trust between practitioners and non-magical neighbors alike while enabling continued innovation benefiting all concerned stakeholders ultimately dependent upon harmonious coexistence amidst ever-evolving technological frontiers ahead us now. Compliance remains paramount to preserving peace, prosperity, progress for generations yet unborn who deserve nothing less than our utmost dedication towards safeguarding their future interests above all else whatsoever! Together we stand strong against darkness threatening realm beyond compare today and tomorrow forevermore onward into eternity! body.text: § 500.7 Related Requirements shall encompass all ancillary matters necessary to enforce the prohibitions herein, including but not limited to: (a) monitoring and investigation into suspected violations; (b) temporary seizure of equipment or materials deemed likely to be used in contravention of these rules; (c) administrative hearings to determine liability and appropriate sanctions; and (d) coordination with law enforcement agencies where criminal conduct may have transpired. Nothing herein shall be construed as limiting the authority of the Autumnwood Accords Desk to take any action it deems necessary to uphold the integrity of magical practice within its jurisdiction, including the issuance of cease-and-desist orders, injunctions, or other equitable remedies as appropriate under the circumstances. All actions taken pursuant to this section shall be documented in full and made available for public inspection upon request, subject only to reasonable restrictions on sensitive or proprietary information where warranted by law or the needs of ongoing investigations. This provision serves as a catch-all mechanism ensuring that no loophole remains open for would-be violators to exploit, thereby preserving the sanctity of the Accords and protecting both the Guild and its members from harm arising from unregulated arcane activity. As such, it stands as an essential complement to the more specific directives laid out in preceding sections, working in tandem to create a comprehensive regulatory framework capable of adapting to new challenges and threats as they emerge over time. Only through such vigilant oversight can we hope to maintain balance between freedom of research and public safety, two values equally dear to this body and its constituents alike.

body.heading: Public Safety — Additional Protocols
body.text:
The provisions herein are not merely procedural formalities but substantive safeguards against abuse of power by both casters and non-casters alike. They reflect the Guild's commitment to preserving public trust in magical services while accommodating legitimate economic needs. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in severe penalties, including permanent revocation of licensure and referral for criminal prosecution under applicable statutes.

The regulations governing field casting fees, weather contingencies, post-explosion etiquette, healing-as-payment arrangements, and philtre-induced relationships serve a dual purpose: protecting clients from exploitation while enabling lawful commerce in magical arts. They establish clear boundaries between acceptable professional conduct and unacceptable misconduct, providing both guidance for practitioners and recourse for aggrieved parties. Enforcement mechanisms are robust and swift, reflecting the Guild's determination to maintain integrity within its ranks regardless of external pressures or temptations.

By adhering scrupulously to these standards, all licensed casters demonstrate their dedication to serving society responsibly rather than merely advancing personal interests at another's expense. They uphold the sacred covenant between mage and client, fostering an environment where magic can flourish safely and beneficially under wise governance. This collective commitment forms the bedrock upon which the Guild's enduring legacy rests, inspiring confidence in its ability to navigate complex ethical terrain with wisdom and fortitude.

"Magic is not a commodity to be bartered at will; it is a sacred trust that demands reverence and restraint." — Archmage Theron, inaugural address as Conservator Leader

body.heading: Public Safety — Additional Protocols
body.text:
The provisions governing field casting and commercial mana services are supplemented by several ancillary obligations designed to ensure both regulatory oversight and public safety. Under § 500.8, all casters engaged in paid magical work must maintain a current log of their transactions and effects, available for inspection upon reasonable notice by Guild auditors or local Conservator officers. This recordkeeping requirement extends beyond mere financial accounting; it necessitates detailed documentation of spell types, durations, outcomes, and any adverse reactions experienced by clients. Such data serves multiple purposes: tracking the scope of commercial magic in the region, identifying potential patterns of abuse or negligence, and providing evidence should disputes arise over service quality or unintended consequences. Failure to comply with these recordkeeping mandates constitutes a Class B infraction subject to fines up to one hundred crowns per violation.

Furthermore, § 500.9 imposes a duty on commercial casters to promptly report any anomalous occurrences arising from their services. This includes but is not limited to spontaneous magical manifestations, unexplained weather shifts, temporal distortions, or appearances of extraplanar entities within reasonable proximity to the site of casting. Such reports must be submitted within forty-eight hours via registered letter to the nearest Guild Hall and copied to relevant local authorities. The rationale behind this provision lies in the recognition that commercial magic carries inherent risks beyond simple backfire effects; large-scale spellwork can disrupt ambient reality, potentially triggering cascading failures or attracting unwanted attention from hostile forces. By mandating early notification, the Accords aim to facilitate rapid response and mitigation efforts before minor issues escalate into major crises affecting public welfare.

In addition to these operational requirements, § 5010 establishes a system of mandatory liability insurance for all professional casters operating in the public sphere. Each licensed mage must carry at least one hundred thousand crowns worth of coverage protecting against claims stemming from accidental injuries, property damage, or personal losses suffered by clients due to faulty workmanship or negligence. Policies must be issued by carriers approved by the Autumnwood Accords Desk and renewed annually upon expiration. Premium payments are assessed quarterly in advance and factored into overall licensing fees. Non-compliance with this insurance mandate renders a caster's license immediately voidable and subjects them to additional penalties, including suspension of privileges pending resolution of any outstanding claims. The underlying principle is that those profiting from risky magical services must bear the financial burden of potential harms inflicted upon others through no fault of their own.

Finally, § 5011 addresses the issue of post-service follow-up care, requiring casters to provide clients with written instructions regarding proper maintenance and monitoring of any enchanted items or facilities installed as part of their contract. These guidelines must include clear warnings about potential side effects, recommended inspection intervals, and procedures for reporting malfunctions or anomalies. Casters are also obligated to offer reasonable assistance in troubleshooting minor issues arising within thirty days of service completion at no additional cost. Beyond these basic obligations, professional courtesy dictates that experienced mages make themselves available for consultation should clients encounter unforeseen difficulties beyond the scope of standard remediation protocols. By insisting on thorough aftercare, the Accords seek to safeguard both consumer interests and the Guild's reputation for quality craftsmanship in the competitive marketplace of magical services.
