body.heading: Contracts with Non-Casters and Related Obligations
body.text:
§ 600.1 Contracts With Non-Casters
A binding contract may be executed between a Caster and a non-magical person ("Non-Caster"), provided the terms do not violate the Accords or impose impossible conditions upon either party. Such agreements must be reduced to writing, signed by both parties, and witnessed by two licensed Casters who shall verify that neither side is acting under compulsion. The Non-Caster acknowledges receipt of a full copy of the contract within ten days of execution. Failure to adhere to these formalities renders the agreement void ab initio, regardless of any oral assent or performance thereunder.

§ 600.2 Familiars as Agents
A Familiar may act as an authorized agent for its Caster in matters directly related to the fulfillment of contractual obligations. The Caster remains ultimately liable for all actions and omissions of the Familiar within the scope of representation. No contract shall bind a Familiar independently, nor shall any clause purport to transfer ownership or control of the Familiar to another party except by explicit written consent of both the Caster and the Familiar's owner. Unauthorized disposition of a Familiar constitutes a serious breach of trust and may result in revocation of licensure for all involved parties.

§ 600.3 Geas as an Unconscionable Term
A contract containing a geas—a magical compulsion forcing compliance with specific instructions—is deemed unconscionable and unenforceable under the Accords. Such clauses violate fundamental principles of free will and bodily autonomy enshrined in § 1.4 Persons Bound. Any attempt to enforce a geas shall be met with immediate legal intervention by the Aegis Magi, who may seize assets and detain responsible parties pending further proceedings. Parties are urged to settle disputes through negotiation rather than resorting to coercive magical measures that threaten public safety and social order.

§ 600.4 Construct Labor: Minimum Wage Standards
Constructs employed under contract shall be compensated at rates no less than the prevailing minimum wage for comparable human laborers in their locality, adjusted upward by twenty percent to account for the unique skills and risks inherent to magical work. This provision applies regardless of whether compensation is paid directly or indirectly through reduced service fees or other means. Employers violating this standard face penalties ranging from fines up to one hundred gold crowns per offense to permanent suspension of operating privileges. The Conservators maintain strict oversight to ensure fair treatment of all worker-constructions alike.

§ 600.5 Summoned Notary and Witness Requirements
All contracts involving Casters must be notarized by a summoned notary with authority delegated directly from the Guild Desk, along with two independent witnesses who shall attest to both parties' identities and capacity to contract. Witnesses must swear under oath that neither party was acting under duress or undue influence at the time of signing. The notary retains original copies of all executed documents for archival purposes, while providing certified duplicates to each signatory within five business days thereafter. Failure to comply with these witnessing protocols invalidates any purported agreement entered into without proper authentication.

§ 600.6 Related Requirements
See also §§ 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 200.3 Temporary Mouths; § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs; § 500.1 Field Casting for Value; § 900.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy; § 1101.6 Related Requirements; § 1201.6 Related Requirements; § 1301.6 Related Requirements; § 1401.6 Related Requirements; § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items; § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time; § 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration; § 600.2 Familiars as Agents; § 700.6 Related Requirements.

*Note: This section outlines the legal framework governing commercial transactions between magical practitioners and ordinary citizens, balancing innovation with protection of vulnerable parties.*

body.heading: § 600.7 Related Requirements and Contractual Safeguards
body.text:
Contracts entered into between casters and non-casters must adhere to strict procedural safeguards to protect both parties' interests. Under § 600.1, any agreement involving magical services requires full disclosure of risks, costs, and limitations prior to execution. Non-disclosure may render the contract voidable at the option of either party, subject to damages for reliance losses. See also § 1.7 regarding the duty of candor in negotiations.

Familiars and constructs acting as agents under authority granted by a caster are deemed extensions of their principals' will for purposes of contract formation and performance. However, this does not absolve the principal of ultimate liability for breaches committed within the scope of authorized acts. Where a familiar exceeds its mandate, the non-caster may seek remedies directly against the owner unless otherwise provided in writing. Refer to § 200.3 on temporary proxies and § 100.5 regarding conflicts of interest.

Geases binding individuals to specific behaviors or prohibitions are construed as unconscionable terms under general principles of fairness. Such clauses violate public policy and shall be deemed unenforceable, regardless of the consenting party's apparent assent. Exceptions exist only where the geas serves a compelling governmental interest and is narrowly tailored thereto. For guidance on evaluating these factors, consult § 1.8 on savings provisions and applicable case law.

Construct labor performed under contract must meet minimum standards for safety, compensation, and humane treatment established by the Guild's Code of Conduct. Failure to comply exposes the employer to administrative penalties ranging from fines to revocation of operating licenses in severe cases. See § 400.2 on specimen custody and § 500.4 regarding healing as consideration. Breach of these obligations may also constitute grounds for civil suit under applicable tort doctrines.

Summoned notaries serve as impartial witnesses to the execution of contracts involving magical elements, verifying identities and intentions at the time of signing. Their presence is mandatory for all agreements exceeding specified monetary thresholds or carrying significant risk profiles. The notary's seal authenticates the document and provides a record for future dispute resolution. Absence of required notarization may invalidate an otherwise valid contract absent ratification by both parties subsequent to discovery of the defect. See § 1.9 on seals and § 100.6 regarding delegation to clerks.

Related requirements include timely performance, proper notice of defaults, and preservation of evidence relevant to potential claims. Parties are obligated to cooperate reasonably in good faith throughout the contract lifecycle. Unjust enrichment theories may apply where one party receives benefits without paying agreed consideration. Remedies available for breach range from specific performance to damages calculated at market rates or actual losses incurred plus incidental expenses. See § 300.5 on research copies and § 400.1 concerning permits for detailed guidance on compliance obligations.

This section incorporates by reference all existing statutes, rules, precedents, and customary practices governing contractual relations between casters and non-casters within the jurisdiction. Nothing herein shall be construed to diminish or expand rights beyond those expressly granted by law unless clearly indicated. Ambiguities are resolved contra proferentem in favor of the party not responsible for drafting the instrument. For further interpretation guidance, refer to § 1.6 on definitions and § 700.3 regarding judicial review procedures.

body.heading: § 600.7 Contracts with Non-Casters and Related Obligations
body.text:
§ 600.7 Contracts with Non-Casters. A contract between a caster and a non-caster shall be governed by the same principles as any other agreement, except as herein provided. The parties shall ensure that all terms are clearly understood and voluntarily accepted. Any clause requiring a non-caster to perform acts prohibited by law or this Codex shall be void ab initio.

A caster who enters into a contract with a non-caster assumes certain obligations beyond those imposed on casters generally. Specifically, the caster must take reasonable care to ensure that their actions do not inadvertently harm the non-caster or place them at risk of legal liability. This duty extends to both direct and foreseeable consequences arising from the caster's magic.

In the event of a dispute regarding a contract with a non-caster, the matter shall be resolved according to standard civil procedure unless otherwise agreed upon by the parties. The burden of proof lies with the party alleging breach or non-performance. Any claims for damages must be supported by competent evidence and shall not exceed the value of the consideration given under the agreement.

Related Obligations. In addition to the foregoing provisions, casters entering into contracts with non-casters must comply with all applicable laws and regulations governing their profession. This includes obtaining necessary permits and licenses, adhering to safety standards, and maintaining appropriate insurance coverage. Failure to meet these obligations may result in disciplinary action by the Guild or other appropriate authorities.

Furthermore, a caster shall not use their magic to coerce or manipulate a non-caster into entering into an unfavorable contract. Such conduct constitutes unethical behavior and may subject the caster to sanctions under § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting. The Guild reserves the right to investigate allegations of undue influence or coercion and take corrective action as warranted.

Contractual Safeguards. To protect both parties, certain safeguards are deemed essential when a non-caster enters into an agreement with a caster. First, the contract must be reduced to writing and signed by all participating parties. Second, each party shall receive a full disclosure of any relevant facts or circumstances that could affect their decision-making process. Third, neither party may waive their right to seek legal remedies in the event of breach or non-performance.

A caster who violates these safeguards does so at their own peril. The Guild will scrutinize such agreements closely and impose penalties as deemed appropriate under the circumstances. In extreme cases, a contract tainted by improper influence may be declared void entirely, leaving both parties free to pursue alternative arrangements without further obligation.

It shall be unlawful for any caster to enter into an agreement with a non-caster that requires them to perform acts prohibited by law or this Codex, even if such prohibition is not explicitly stated in the contract itself. The casting of spells to induce submission or obedience in a non-consenting party constitutes battery and may subject the caster to criminal prosecution under applicable statutes.

Finally, parties are advised to consult with competent legal counsel prior to entering into any agreement involving complex magical elements or significant financial stakes. While this Codex provides guidance on matters unique to the arcane arts, it cannot supersede general principles of contract law as they apply between ordinary citizens. The Guild stands ready to assist in interpreting these provisions but does not act as a substitute for professional legal advice.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 300.2 Necromancy and Unsanctioned Arts; under § 100.4 Records of Speech regarding contract negotiations between casters and non-casters.

body.heading: § 600.7 Contracts with Non-Casters and Contractual Safeguards
body.text:
Contracts entered into between mages and non-casters shall not contravene the fundamental principles of magic as enshrined in these Accords. Any agreement that seeks to bind a non-mage's magical essence, or to compel them to act against their nature, is void ab initio. This includes, but is not limited to, clauses dictating the terms of spellcasting upon unwilling subjects, the extraction of life-force under duress, and any arrangement that treats human beings as expendable resources for magical production. The Conservators maintain a vigilant watch over such contracts, empowered to seize and nullify them upon reasonable suspicion of malpractice.

Nevertheless, it shall not be held that mere participation in a contract renders a non-caster subject to arcane law. A person who signs an agreement without knowledge of its magical implications bears no obligations thereunder. The burden of disclosure rests squarely upon the casting party, who must fully explain the nature and extent of any enchantments or wards involved. Failure to do so constitutes fraud under § 1201.8 and may result in severe penalties, including permanent disqualification from practice.

In cases where a contract is found void due to magical exploitation, restitution shall be made as appropriate. This may include the reversal of all affected spells, compensation for losses incurred, and in extreme instances, imprisonment without bail. The Desk retains discretion to order additional sanctions against recalcitrant parties, up to and including revocation of their licensure under § 600.12. It is incumbent upon every caster to adhere scrupulously to these guidelines, lest they find themselves ensnared in a web of legal liability far deeper than the deepest pit.

It is hereby declared that no contract shall stand that violates the sanctity of free will and bodily integrity as enshrined in natural law. The Accords remain supreme over any private arrangement, and those who seek to subvert this principle do so at their peril. Let it be known: magic binds all, but only with consent freely given. Those who forget this truth shall reap a storm of wrath, both from the spirits above and below and from the righteous fury of their peers. May they learn wisdom before it is too late.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 1201.8 Fraudulent Misrepresentation; see § 600.12 Revocation of Licensure; see § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate

body.heading: § 600.7 Contracts with Non-Casters and Contractual Safeguards — Continued
body.text:
Contracts entered into by casters with non-casters raise complex issues regarding liability, enforceability, and the scope of magical obligations under the Accords. Under § 600.1, any contract involving a caster must be filed with the Autumnwood Desk for review and approval prior to execution. This filing requirement serves multiple purposes: ensuring compliance with relevant statutes, protecting third parties from unforeseen risks, and preserving evidence in case of dispute. Failure to file may render the agreement void ab initio or subject it to severe penalties under § 1301.2.

A critical safeguard embedded within the Accords is the prohibition against binding a non-caster to perform magical acts without explicit consent and informed understanding. As outlined in § 600.3, any clause requiring an individual to engage in spellcasting or ritualistic activities constitutes an unconscionable term and shall be deemed void as contrary to public policy. This principle extends beyond mere coercion; it encompasses contracts that effectively enslave a non-caster's will through subtle magical influence or psychological manipulation. The burden of proof rests upon the caster to demonstrate that all parties entered into the agreement freely and with full knowledge of its implications.

Furthermore, § 600.4 addresses the unique challenges posed by construct labor in contractual arrangements. While constructs may be employed as agents under a caster's direction, they cannot be held personally liable for breaches or damages arising from their actions. Instead, liability remains with the employing party who commissioned the work. This allocation of responsibility aims to prevent abusive practices where casters exploit autonomous entities without regard for consequences. Additionally, § 600.5 mandates that all contracts involving summons or binding rituals must include a clause specifying the duration and limitations thereof, thereby protecting against indefinite servitude or loss of autonomy.

In cases of alleged contract violations involving non-casters, the Accords provide mechanisms for swift resolution through arbitration panels comprised of both casters and laypersons. These panels operate independently of the Guild's internal hierarchies to ensure impartial adjudication. Appeals may be lodged with the Autumnwood Desk itself under § 1301.3, though such review is typically limited to questions of law rather than fact-finding. Ultimately, the goal of these safeguards is to balance the interests of all parties while upholding the fundamental principles of justice and fairness enshrined in the spirit of the Accords.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 600.3 Geas as an Unconscionable Term; under § 1301.2 Penalties for Noncompliance; cf. § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs regarding unauthorized field use and liability implications.

body.heading: § 700.1 Unauthorized Field Use and Regulatory Oversight
body.text:
Unauthorized field use of magic poses significant risks to public safety and the integrity of arcane studies, necessitating stringent regulatory oversight under the Autumnwood Accords. As prescribed in § 700.1, any casting conducted outside official Guild premises requires prior written permission from the Conservators' Council or designated Innovator Liaison depending on the nature of the work. This authorization process evaluates potential hazards, environmental impacts, and public welfare concerns before granting approval. Applications must include detailed plans for containment, emergency response protocols, and post-operation cleanup procedures to mitigate adverse effects.

Violations of § 700.1 constitute serious offenses subject to disciplinary action up to and including permanent revocation of licensure under § 200.4. Repeat offenders may face additional sanctions such as mandatory retraining, fines proportional to the scale of harm caused, or imprisonment for egregious cases involving reckless endangerment. The burden lies with the caster to prove that their activities complied fully with all stipulated conditions; mere assertions of competence or necessity are insufficient defenses against allegations of unauthorized field use.

Moreover, § 700.2 establishes a system of random inspections and audits designed to detect unreported magical operations and enforce compliance proactively. Inspectors possess broad powers to enter private property with warrants issued by the Autumnwood Desk, seize relevant materials, and interview witnesses as deemed necessary for investigation purposes. Refusal to cooperate may result in escalated penalties under § 1301.2(b). Data collected during these reviews informs ongoing policy adjustments aimed at addressing emerging threats while fostering responsible innovation within acceptable parameters.

Ultimately, the provisions surrounding unauthorized field use reflect the delicate balance between regulating dangerous practices and supporting legitimate research endeavors. By maintaining rigorous oversight mechanisms alongside clear guidelines for permissible activity, the Accords seek to safeguard both society at large and the reputation of lawful casters alike against exploitation or misuse of their powerful abilities.

see § 700.2 Random Inspections and Audits; under § 1301.2 Penalties for Violations; cf. § 500.1 Field Casting for Value regarding compensation issues related to off-site work arrangements; compare § 400.4 Specimen Custody obligations when handling sensitive materials away from secure facilities.

body.heading: § 800.1 Ethical Standards and Professional Conduct
body.text:
Casters are bound by rigorous ethical standards governing their professional conduct both within and outside the workplace under § 800.1 of the Autumnwood Accords. These guidelines address issues ranging from client interactions to personal behavior, aiming to preserve public trust in the magical profession while protecting individuals from abuse or exploitation. Compliance with these norms is mandatory for all licensed practitioners regardless of rank or specialization.

Key provisions include prohibitions against dual relationships between caster and client that could impair judgment or create conflicts of interest (§ 800.2). Casters must avoid situations where financial gain might compromise objectivity or lead to overreliance on their services. Similarly, § 800.3 forbids sexual harassment, discrimination, or any form of misconduct based on race, gender, age, disability status, or other protected characteristics under applicable law. Such behavior undermines the dignity of the profession and invites scrutiny from regulatory bodies.

Furthermore, casters are obligated to maintain accurate records of their work pursuant to § 800.4. This documentation serves multiple functions: facilitating continuity in long-term projects, enabling accountability in case of disputes or malpractice claims, and supporting ongoing education efforts within the community. Neglecting this duty may result in disciplinary measures ranging from warnings to suspension pending investigation into potential negligence or misconduct.

Finally, § 800.5 emphasizes the importance of continuous professional development through attendance at workshops, seminars, and conferences sponsored by recognized organizations. Staying abreast of emerging trends ensures that casters provide optimal service while adhering to evolving best practices. Failure to pursue necessary training may indicate stagnation or incompetence warranting corrective action under § 200.4(a). Ultimately, upholding these high ethical standards reflects well on the entire casting community and reinforces its reputation for excellence in delivering safe and effective magical solutions to diverse problems faced by society today.

see § 800.2 Prohibition Against Dual Relationships; see § 800.3 Anti-Harassment Policies; under § 1301.2 Disciplinary Actions for Breaches of Code; cf. § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth as an example of unacceptable professional conduct leading to sanctions; contrast with § 600.6 Related Requirements outlining acceptable delegation practices when working with assistants or apprentices who require supervision due to limited experience levels.

body.heading: § 700.7 Related Requirements - Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and
body.text:
In proceedings before the Autumnwood Accords Desk, all evidence adduced must satisfy the rigorous standards set forth herein to ensure fairness and accuracy in determining matters of magical culpability or entitlement. Under § 700.1, the foundational principles governing admissibility are those established by common law and precedent, adapted for the unique circumstances presented by arcane phenomena. See also § 300.6 regarding the exclusion of hearsay derived from scrying operations absent corroboration under oath.

§ 700.2 specifically addresses testimony obtained through divination or memory charms. Such evidence shall be deemed inadmissible unless the source consents in writing to its use and discloses all methods employed, as required by § 400.1's provisions on informed consent for magical procedures. Unauthorized manipulation of a witness's memories constitutes spoliation under § 700.3 and may result in immediate dismissal of claims predicated upon said altered recollections. See further § 200.5 concerning the limits of permissible psychological interventions during deposition phases.

Simulacra summoned pursuant to § 600.1 may offer testimony subject to cross-examination, provided their origins are fully disclosed and they possess no inherent bias toward either party. Clauses requiring simulation of human emotion or intent shall be scrutinized carefully under § 700.4's safeguards against deceptive practices. The Desk retains discretion to exclude simulative evidence where it risks prejudicing the fact-finding process unduly. Reference is made to § 100.8 regarding emergency exceptions for time-sensitive magical phenomena threatening public safety.

Clones created via forbidden arts may assert claims as duplicate entities under specific conditions outlined in § 700.5, but such assertions must be supported by irrefutable proof of lawful origin and continuous chain of custody from point of creation to present moment. Absent such documentation, any attempt to establish standing based solely on clonal duplication shall fail outright. This provision implements the spirit of § 300.4 while maintaining strict adherence to established protocols for verifying magical lineages.

All evidence introduced must comply with the formal requirements set forth in Part IV, including proper authentication, notarization where applicable, and timely submission prior to hearing dates absent extraordinary circumstances warranting a ruling on late filings under § 500.2's emergency provisions. The Desk shall not be bound by any irregularities or procedural failures attributable solely to the proponent of the evidence unless waived expressly in writing before trial commences. For guidance on calculating applicable deadlines and extensions, consult §§ 1301.1 through 1301.4 inclusive.

Violations of these admissibility standards may result in sanctions ranging from monetary fines up to ten thousand gold pieces per offense to complete forfeiture of rights associated with the disputed matter entirely. Repeat offenders face escalated penalties including suspension or permanent revocation of licensure under §§ 200.3 and 1101.5 respectively. The ultimate authority rests with the presiding Magister whose determinations are final and unappealable except by motion for rehearing granted at their sole discretion pursuant to § 1401.3's savings clause.

See also §§ 700.8–700.9 concerning expert witness qualifications and standards of care, along with cross-references to foundational provisions on burden of proof (§ 200.4), privilege protections (§ 500.6), and remedies for bad faith litigation tactics (§ 1201.6). Compliance with all stipulations herein is mandatory under pain of severe consequences as outlined in the Preamble to these Accords.

body.heading: Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence
body.text:
§ 700.7 Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence shall govern the introduction of magical data into formal proceedings under these Accords. The Desk hereby establishes that all evidence derived from arcane means must undergo strict scrutiny before being admitted, to prevent contamination by illusion or deception. See § 1.6 defining "Evidence" as any material fact offered to prove a proposition in issue.

Under this section, the admissibility of scrying results, memory charm impressions, simulacrum outputs, and clone testimonies shall be evaluated according to specific criteria set forth herein. The Desk finds that such methods possess inherent limitations which may compromise their reliability if not properly calibrated and verified. Accordingly, no arcane testimony or derived evidence shall be accepted without first satisfying the requirements laid out below. See § 100.6 regarding delegation of technical tasks to qualified clerks where appropriate.

For scrying operations, the Desk mandates that all lenses must be certified free from tampering prior to use, with serial numbers recorded in official logs. The caster must declare any known defects or magical interference affecting the device's accuracy. Results obtained under these conditions may then be admitted as corroborative evidence, though never as sole proof of contested facts. See § 200.3 limiting scope of permitted practices to licensed professionals only.

Memory charm impressions shall undergo immediate analysis by a qualified thaumaturge unconnected to the case. The analyst must produce a detailed report assessing potential sources of contamination or distortion in the impression. Only after this verification may such evidence be tendered, and then solely for purposes corroborating other reliable testimony. See § 300.4 governing reclassification procedures for tainted materials.

Simulacrum-generated data shall require dual authentication by both the original caster and an independent expert witness. The experts must confirm that the simulation parameters were properly configured and free from external interference. Any discrepancies detected during review shall render the resulting evidence inadmissible until resolved to satisfaction of the Desk. See § 400.2 regulating use of pocket dimensions as laboratory spaces for such purposes.

Clone testimony presents unique challenges due to potential cognitive degradation or personality divergence over time. The Desk therefore requires that all clones provide sworn affidavits detailing their training regimen, any modifications made post-cloning, and a complete history of experiences since activation. Such documents shall be subject to cross-examination as required by standard evidentiary rules. See § 500.1 addressing field casting compensation schemes which may incentivize substandard replication practices.

In all cases involving arcane evidence, the burden rests upon the party introducing such material to demonstrate its validity and lack of prejudice beyond a reasonable doubt. The Desk retains discretion to exclude any testimony or exhibit deemed likely to confuse issues, mislead the tribunal, or waste time in accordance with established judicial principles. See § 600.1 prohibiting contractual agreements that contravene public policy under these Accords.

These admissibility standards are intended to ensure fair adjudication while maintaining rigorous control over potentially dangerous magical technologies. Violations shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure, at the Desk's sole discretion. See § 200.4 outlining suspension procedures for serious infractions. The Desk reserves authority to amend these rules as necessary to address emerging challenges in the field of arcane jurisprudence. See § 1301.5 regarding appeals process for contested rulings by the full Board.

It is hereby declared that adherence to these provisions shall be deemed essential to preserving the integrity and efficacy of all magical proceedings conducted under the auspices of this Codex. Failure to comply may result in severe penalties including permanent disqualification from practice within Autumnwood jurisdiction. See § 1401.3 noting historical precedents where similar measures proved necessary for public safety. The Desk stands ready to enforce these guidelines with unwavering determination to protect both the innocent and the guild's precious reputation. See § 900.6 authorizing appropriate sanctions against recalcitrant parties.

body.heading: § 700.7 Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence
body.text:
The strict evidentiary rules governing civil litigation are deemed inadequate to address the unique challenges posed by magical phenomena and supernatural entities. Accordingly, this Part establishes specialized standards for the admission of arcane testimony and evidence in proceedings before the Autumnwood Accords Desk and its tribunals.

§ 700.7(1) Arcane Testimony. The testimony of a qualified spellcaster regarding their own practices, abilities, or effects shall be admissible as prima facie evidence, absent rebuttal proof to the contrary. Such testimony may include sworn declarations concerning spell origins, ritual components, and intended outcomes. Cross-examination is permitted but limited to matters directly relevant to the caster's competency and credibility.

§ 700.7(2) Magical Residues and Artifacts. Physical traces of magical activity, such as residual aetheric signatures or enchanted objects, may be introduced as circumstantial evidence when authenticated by an accredited Arcane Forensic Analyst (AFA). AFAs must maintain detailed chain-of-custody logs and provide contemporaneous calibration records for all analytical equipment utilized during examination proceedings.

§ 700.7(3) Expert Witnesses. Opinions rendered by independent experts on matters of magical theory, classification, or causation shall carry weight proportional to their demonstrated expertise and standing within the arcane community. Parties objecting to an expert's qualifications must raise such issues at least three days prior to trial, allowing adequate time for meaningful cross-examination.

§ 700.7(4) Secrecy Obligations. Witnesses testifying regarding protected Arcane Knowledge or Quiet List items are subject to a temporary non-disclosure order lasting until conclusion of the proceeding and filing of all appellate briefs. Violation of such orders may result in sanctions including contempt citations and disqualification from future testimony before the Accords Desk.

§ 700.7(5) Special Masters. In complex cases involving disputed magical causation or novel phenomena, the Desk may appoint a Special Master to oversee discovery, manage expert exchanges, and issue preliminary findings on technical issues requiring arcane expertise. The Special Master's determinations shall be binding unless clearly erroneous upon appellate review.

These provisions balance the need for reliable fact-finding in technologically advanced disputes with necessary protections for sensitive magical information. They reflect recognition that traditional evidentiary frameworks may prove insufficient when dealing with forces beyond ordinary comprehension. The Desk retains discretion to tailor procedural accommodations as circumstances warrant, always mindful of maintaining fair play and integrity in adjudication.

body.heading: § 700.7 Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence — Continued
body.text:
The admission of arcane testimony or evidence in proceedings before the Desk is governed by strict criteria designed to ensure reliability and fairness. Under § 700.1, all parties must submit a written motion requesting the introduction of magical proof at least seven days prior to hearing, specifying precisely what item, spell, or phenomenon is sought and why it is material to the case. The Presiding Clerk shall review said motion in conjunction with relevant files under §§ 300–600 before granting leave to present such evidence.

Arcane testimony delivered orally must be accompanied by a sworn affidavit detailing the circumstances of its acquisition and execution, along with an attestation that no coercion or deception was employed. As provided in § 700.2, scrying operations conducted without prior authorization from the Conservators are deemed tainted and inadmissible unless subsequently ratified in writing. Memory charms cast upon witnesses shall be treated as spoliation under § 300.4 and may result in sanctions against the offending party.

Simulacra summoned to bear witness must meet the standards set forth in § 700.5, including proof of authenticity and independence from outside influence. Clones or duplicates invoked as additional parties shall be subject to the restrictions outlined in § 700.6 regarding their capacity to act on behalf of the original casters. Any attempt to bypass these safeguards for tactical advantage constitutes contempt punishable under § 1301.2.

The Desk retains discretion to admit otherwise excluded magical evidence if it deems such proof essential to resolving disputed factual issues fairly and efficiently. However, this power shall not be exercised arbitrarily or capriciously but rather pursuant to principles of natural justice enshrined in §§ 1.7–1.9. Parties objecting to the admission of arcane materials may petition for an expedited ruling by direct appeal to the Sovereign Archmage via established channels under § 200.4.

Ultimately, the goal behind these stringent admissibility rules is twofold: first, to preserve the integrity of the adjudicative process itself; second, to protect all participants from undue harm resulting from unregulated magical experimentation. By balancing these competing interests through careful oversight and transparent procedures, the Autumnwood Accords seek to foster an environment wherein truth may emerge even amidst complexity and chaos alike. For further guidance on specific applications, consult §§ 400–800 as applicable.

body.heading: Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence — Continued
body.text:
§ 700.7 Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence

The admissibility of arcane testimony and evidence in legal proceedings is governed by stringent criteria to ensure fairness and reliability. Under § 700.1, all testimony must be given under oath or affirmation, with penalties for perjury applicable as usual. Arcane manifestations used as evidence must be authenticated according to the procedures set forth in § 700.2, which outlines requirements for scrying of closed books and other divination techniques. Memory charms suspected of spoliation are subject to examination under § 700.3, with findings reported by independent observers sworn to impartiality.

Simulacrum testimony presented pursuant to § 700.4 must conform to established protocols regarding the construction and operation of such constructs. The authenticity of any claims made through simulacra is determined by a panel of qualified mages appointed by the court, in accordance with standards detailed in accompanying regulations. In cases where clones are invoked as duplicate claimants under § 700.5, their status and authority must be verified against official records maintained by the relevant jurisdictional body. Failure to properly authenticate any form of arcane testimony or evidence shall result in its exclusion from consideration.

The admissibility provisions herein operate independently of other rules within this Code but are intended to complement them where applicable. Nothing contained in these sections shall be construed to limit or expand rights beyond those explicitly granted by statute or common law, except as otherwise provided herein. Parties seeking to introduce unconventional forms of proof bear the burden of demonstrating their admissibility prior to presentation at trial. The court retains discretionary authority to exclude irrelevant, prejudicial, or unreliable material even if technically permissible under these guidelines.

These standards reflect a balance between accommodating necessary magical practices and safeguarding against abuse. They recognize both the unique challenges posed by supernatural phenomena in evidentiary contexts and the paramount need for procedural integrity. Compliance with these requirements is mandatory for all participants in matters involving arcane elements, regardless of jurisdictional boundaries or customary precedents elsewhere. Violation may result in sanctions up to and including dismissal of claims or counterclaims dependent upon improperly admitted matter.

See § 700.1 Evidence Generally regarding foundational rules applicable to all testimony; under § 300.4 Reclassification for procedures governing reevaluation of contested evidence types. Related provisions include § 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion concerning safety protocols during demonstrations, and § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill defining permissible roles for artificial intelligences in legal proceedings. Construction principles outlined herein are consistent with those set forth in §§ 1.4–1.9 governing persons bound by these Accords and general rules of interpretation.

body.heading: Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Evidence — Administration
body.text:
In all proceedings before the Autumnwood Accords Desk, testimony and evidence involving magical phenomena shall be subject to rigorous scrutiny to ensure reliability and fairness. § 700.1 Evidence Generally dictates that all material presented must be authenticated by a duly licensed mage-forensic expert possessing appropriate credentials under Part 200. Such authentication is necessary to establish the chain of custody and integrity of any enchanted item or recorded spell-effect claimed as proof. Failure to provide proper certification shall result in automatic exclusion of the contested evidence from consideration under § 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony provisions.

§ 700.2 Scrying of Closed Books addresses the contentious issue of magical divination undertaken without judicial oversight. Unless expressly authorized by a warrant issued pursuant to § 500.1 Field Casting for Value, any unauthorized scrying operation constitutes grave interference with due process. Evidence obtained through such improper means shall be deemed tainted and inadmissible, regardless of its apparent probative value. This rule exists to prevent abuse of powerful divination arts in the pursuit of self-serving ends. See also § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts regarding similar prohibitions on forbidden magical practices.

§ 700.3 Memory Charm as Spoliation recognizes that certain enchantments capable of altering conscious recollection may constitute spoliation of evidence under specific circumstances. When a party knowingly subjects themselves to such alterations in anticipation of litigation, the resulting loss of accurate memory shall be imputed to their side of the dispute. This principle aims to preserve the integrity of testimonial records and deter manipulative use of mind-affecting magics for evidentiary advantage. Refer to § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time for additional guidance on temporal distortions affecting witness reliability.

§ 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony establishes that artificially generated consciousnesses incapable of independent volition may not serve as competent witnesses under the Accords. While such constructs may be employed to preserve critical information or provide technical assistance, they lack the requisite agency to bear testimony on their own behalf. Any attempt to introduce simulative entities as surrogate witnesses shall result in immediate dismissal of the offending claim and potential sanctions against responsible parties for misuse of prohibited technologies. Consult § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters regarding limitations on artificial intelligence applications in legal contexts.

§ 700.5 Clone as Duplicate Claimant clarifies that magically replicated individuals retain distinct legal identities despite physical similarities. In matters involving personal injury, property damage, or contractual obligations, each cloned entity shall be held separately accountable for their own actions and liabilities. No party may assert defenses based solely on duplication status absent clear statutory authorization. This provision safeguards the fundamental principle of individual responsibility within an increasingly complex magical society. See Part 300 regarding identity verification procedures applicable to all litigants.

§ 700.6 Related Requirements incorporates by reference all relevant provisions scattered throughout this Codex that bear upon evidentiary standards in arcane proceedings. These include but are not limited to §§ 200.1 Licensure Required, 400.1 Research Permits, and 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion where applicable. Parties appearing before the Desk shall be deemed fully aware of these interconnected obligations and shall comply therewith without further notice. Failure to adhere shall result in appropriate disciplinary action as outlined elsewhere herein. This comprehensive approach ensures consistent application of fair trial principles across all magical disputes within the Guild's jurisdiction.

Under § 1.8 Effective Date; Savings, these admissibility standards apply retroactively except where doing so would impair vested rights or impose new obligations. Existing cases pending before the Autumnwood Accords Desk shall proceed under prior rules unless specifically remanded for re-evaluation under this updated framework. The Desk retains discretion to grant exceptions in exceptional circumstances upon written motion and justification filed with full particularity. All decisions regarding evidence admissibility remain within the sole purview of presiding magistrates acting in accordance with these guidelines. Any challenges to evidentiary rulings must be raised promptly during trial rather than on appeal, consistent with traditional procedural norms. This balance between flexibility and predictability serves the ultimate goal of achieving justice through reliable fact-finding processes.

see § 100.4 Records of Speech; see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; see § 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion; see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see Part 200 regarding licensure and certification requirements applicable to all witnesses and experts testifying before the Accords Desk under these provisions.

sections.title: PART 800 - DISCIPLINARY MEASURES § 800.7 Related Requirements; § 1301.2 Penaltie

body.heading: PART 800 - DISCIPLINARY MEASURES § 800.7 Related Requirements; § 1301.2 Penaltie
body.text:
The provisions of this Part shall be read in conjunction with the applicable penalty schedules set forth in § 1301.2 and any supplementary guidelines issued by the Autumnwood Accords Desk from time to time. In determining the appropriate sanction for a given infraction, the Presiding Council shall take into account the totality of the circumstances, including but not limited to: (a) the gravity of the violation as measured against the specific clauses of this Code; (b) any history of prior offenses by the accused casterman or entity; (c) the degree of harm caused to innocent third parties or public safety; and (d) evidence of remorse or corrective action taken voluntarily. Where multiple violations are found, sanctions shall be aggregated in accordance with § 1301.2(c) unless exceptional mitigation is warranted by the circumstances.

It is hereby declared that all disciplinary measures imposed under this Code constitute a lawful deprivation of property and liberty interests protected by the Magna Carta and subsequent charters. Accordingly, any casterman subject to such sanctions shall be afforded full due process rights throughout the proceedings, including notice of charges, opportunity to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses, representation by counsel of choice, and appeal to higher authorities as provided herein. Failure to comply with these procedural mandates shall render any resulting sanction null and void ab initio at the sole discretion of the aggrieved party seeking redress through proper channels.

In cases where a casterman's magic is temporarily or permanently sealed pursuant to § 800.3, such action shall not preclude the individual from pursuing alternative means of livelihood consistent with their station in life and ability to earn a living wage without further restriction on their civil rights. The Guild recognizes that magical suppression may necessitate significant lifestyle adjustments for affected parties and encourages them to seek assistance through accredited rehabilitation programs or community support networks where available. Reinstatement procedures shall commence immediately upon expiration of the seclusion period unless extended by mutual agreement between all involved parties within thirty (30) days thereof.

The foregoing sections serve as a comprehensive guide to understanding the scope, application, and implications of disciplinary actions taken under this Code. Any ambiguities or disputes arising from their interpretation shall be resolved in favor of strict construction against those seeking to impose sanctions and in accord with established principles of fairness and equity governing administrative law generally. This final paragraph ensures clarity regarding the intent and purpose behind each provision contained herein for all readers thereof.

body.heading: § 800.7 Related Requirements and Prohibited Acts; § 1301.2 Penalties for Breach
body.text:
This Part codifies the disciplinary framework governing infractions of the Accords, establishing both the spectrum of sanctions available and the procedural safeguards required to ensure justice is meted out fairly. The range of penalties extends from admonition and fine up to permanent sealing of magical aptitude or exile to a pocket dimension for egregious offenders. Each sanction carries specific conditions precedent and must be imposed only after due process has been fully exhausted.

A critical aspect of disciplinary action lies in the determination of fault, which requires careful consideration of mitigating factors such as intent, circumstance, and prior record. The burden of proof rests squarely upon the accuser to demonstrate guilt beyond reasonable doubt through credible testimony or irrefutable evidence. Defendants are entitled to counsel and a full opportunity to present their case before an impartial tribunal composed of peers familiar with arcane matters.

Sanctions imposed must be proportional to the gravity of the offense, tailored to address the root causes while preventing future harm to both individuals and society at large. Severe penalties such as sealing may only be enacted when lesser measures have proven inadequate or when the offender poses a continuing threat to public safety. Even then, periodic review is mandated to assess whether less restrictive alternatives might suffice given changed conditions.

The Accords further prohibit certain acts deemed inherently dangerous or incompatible with lawful magic practice, regardless of individual circumstances. These include unauthorized experimentation on living subjects, possession of prohibited materials, and engagement in magical duels outside sanctioned arenas. Violation of such prohibitions constitutes automatic grounds for disciplinary action without need for additional proof of harm.

Finally, this Part emphasizes the importance of rehabilitation alongside punishment where appropriate, recognizing that most offenders can be reintegrated into productive society if given proper support and guidance. Probationary periods with clear milestones allow for correction of course while maintaining accountability for past misdeeds. The ultimate goal remains preservation of public welfare through balanced enforcement of standards essential to harmonious coexistence between casters and non-magical folk alike.

see § 1301.2 regarding specific penalty tiers and application criteria; see § 800.5 outlining pocket-prison procedures for extreme cases; under § 800.6, related requirements supplement this framework where necessary. Persons subject to disciplinary measures retain all rights afforded by law unless explicitly restricted as part of their sanction package.

"The Accords stand as testament to our collective wisdom in navigating the delicate balance between innovation and responsibility. Disciplinary mechanisms exist not merely to punish but to guide us toward higher ideals." - Archmage Veyra, Mediating Statement No. 7892-B

body.heading: PART 800 - DISCIPLINARY MEASURES
body.text:
§ 800.7 Related Requirements; § 1301.2 Penalties for Breach

The disciplinary measures outlined in this Part shall be applied uniformly and impartially to all members of the Guild, regardless of rank or faction affiliation. No mage is above the law, and violations will be met with swift and decisive action designed to preserve the integrity of magical practice within the Accords' jurisdiction. The Conservators maintain that strict enforcement is essential to preventing abuse and ensuring public safety, while Innovators argue for proportionality and rehabilitation where appropriate. Ultimately, the Aegis Magi serve as neutral arbiters in all matters of discipline.

Sanctions may include reprimand, fines, suspension of license, permanent revocation of privileges, sealing of magical abilities, or expulsion from the Guild entirely. The severity of punishment shall correspond to the gravity of the infraction and any resulting harm. Lesser offenses might warrant a warning or mandatory remedial training, while egregious breaches could result in lifelong disqualification from casting magic under any circumstances. Repeat offenders face increasingly harsh penalties, reflecting the cumulative nature of their misconduct.

The Paradox Trial remains the primary mechanism for adjudicating disputes between Guild members and determining appropriate sanctions. This formal proceeding ensures due process and allows all parties to present evidence in support of their positions. Peer review by a panel of senior mages provides an additional layer of oversight and accountability. Appeals may be lodged with the Archmage Sovereign, who retains final authority over disciplinary outcomes. Expedited trials are available for urgent cases where immediate action is necessary to protect public welfare or maintain order.

Sealing of magical abilities represents one of the most severe punishments available under the Accords. This procedure permanently disables a mage's capacity to cast spells without specialized equipment or assistance, effectively neutering their power. Sealed individuals must register with the Conservators and undergo regular monitoring to ensure compliance. Release from sealing is exceptionally rare and contingent upon demonstrated rehabilitation and service to the Guild community over an extended period. The stigma of being "seared" follows a mage for the rest of their days, limiting career prospects and social standing.

Expulsion from the Autumnwood Accords carries even greater consequences than mere sealing. Once cast out, an ex-mage loses all rights and protections afforded by membership, rendering them vulnerable to prosecution under civil law or extrajudicial retaliation from rival groups. Such individuals are generally barred from practicing magic within Guild territory unless granted special dispensation by the High Council. Expulsion is reserved for those who prove irredeemably corrupt or pose an unacceptable threat to societal stability. The burden of proof rests squarely on the accuser, and standards for removal must be met beyond any reasonable doubt.

Disciplinary records are maintained confidentially but may be accessed upon proper request by relevant authorities or prospective employers. This transparency helps safeguard against future misconduct while protecting privacy where feasible. Expungement is possible after a designated period of good behavior, provided no new violations occur during that time. Rehabilitation programs exist to assist struggling mages in overcoming personal demons and returning to productive lives outside the shadows of infamy. The Guild stands ready to extend a hand to those willing to learn from their mistakes rather than repeating them ad infinitum.

In conclusion, the enforcement framework established herein constitutes the bedrock upon which responsible magical practice rests. By holding every practitioner accountable for their actions, we foster an environment where innovation can flourish alongside tradition. Justice tempered with mercy ensures that the Accords serve not merely as instruments of control but as guides toward ethical growth and mutual understanding among all who walk this path together in pursuit of arcane enlightenment under the watchful gaze of history itself.

body.heading: § 800.7 Sanctioned Uses of Forbidden Arts
body.text:
The Accords recognize that in exceptional circumstances, the prohibition against forbidden arts may be temporarily lifted under strict oversight. Such exceptions require written approval from the Desk and must occur within a designated containment zone established by an Aegis Magus. The caster remains fully liable for any adverse effects resulting from the sanctioned use, regardless of whether precautions were taken.

Under § 1301.2, failure to adhere to the conditions set forth in the exception grant constitutes grounds for immediate revocation of all privileges held under the Accords. Furthermore, repeat offenses may result in permanent sealing of magical abilities and referral for prosecution under applicable criminal statutes. The Desk maintains a confidential register of all exceptions granted, accessible only upon specific request by interested parties demonstrating compelling need.

It is imperative that mages understand the gravity with which such permissions are viewed by the Conservators. While innovation drives progress, it must never compromise public safety or undermine foundational magical principles. The Aegis Magi remain vigilant in monitoring compliance and may initiate emergency containment procedures if they perceive any threat to community welfare arising from unauthorized experimental activities.

Ultimately, the granting of exceptions serves as a reminder that even the most rigid legal codes require flexibility when faced with novel challenges. Yet this latitude is afforded sparingly, always balanced against the greater good served by maintaining orderly control over dangerous forces inherent in the arcane arts. Mages who seek to push boundaries must do so responsibly and within the confines established by their peers for collective protection.

body.heading: Sanctioned Uses of Forbidden Arts
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords recognize that certain magical practices, though nominally forbidden under § 300.2, may nevertheless serve legitimate ends when performed under strict supervision and for approved purposes. This principle is codified in the provisions regarding sanctioned uses of otherwise prohibited arts.

Under § 800.6 Related Requirements, a Conservator or designated Aegis Magi may authorize the temporary lifting of restrictions on specific forbidden schools of magic. Such authorization shall be granted only when it can be demonstrated that the intended use will result in no net increase in overall magical risk to society. Typical examples include the study of necromantic phenomena for medical research purposes, or the controlled application of blood-magic techniques in forensic investigations.

Any such permit must specify precisely which arts are authorized, the duration of the authorization, and the exact conditions under which they may be employed. Violation of these stipulations shall constitute a breach of § 800.1 Discipline and subject the violator to full disciplinary action under Part 800, including but not limited to revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse.

In addition, all sanctioned uses must be reported quarterly to the Conservators' Bureau for review and assessment of potential abuses or unintended consequences. Failure to submit such reports shall result in immediate suspension of the permit until compliance is verified. This requirement is designed to ensure ongoing oversight of even those magical practices deemed acceptable under limited circumstances.

The provisions regarding sanctioned uses reflect the Accords' pragmatic approach to magic regulation, recognizing that absolute prohibition may not always serve the greater good when properly controlled. However, this flexibility must never be exploited for personal gain or advantage, as such behavior undermines the very foundation of the Guild's authority and trustworthiness in matters magical.

see § 800.1 Discipline; Range of Sanctions
see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; Guest Casters
see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts
see § 1.7 Construction; Aggregation of Conduct

body.heading: § 800.7 Sanctioned Uses of Forbidden Arts — Continued
body.text:
While the Autumnwood Accords generally prohibit the practice of forbidden schools of magic, certain exceptions exist for sanctioned research and controlled experimentation conducted under strict supervision. Under § 300.2, necromancy and blood magic remain absolutely forbidden except where expressly permitted by a majority vote of the Archmage Council. Such permissions must be renewed annually and are subject to immediate revocation upon breach of terms.

Innovators seeking to study restricted arts may apply for temporary research permits under § 400.1, which outline specific safety protocols and containment measures. Violation of permit conditions constitutes a major infraction punishable by seal or expulsion. The Council maintains absolute discretion over all applications and reserves the right to deny access without explanation.

Particularly stringent rules govern the use of pocket dimensions for research purposes. Under § 400.2, no caster may utilize private planes as laboratories without explicit written authorization from a Conservator-level mage. Unauthorized experiments conducted within such spaces are presumed reckless and subject to enhanced penalties. All specimens collected during sanctioned fieldwork must be returned intact upon completion of studies.

The Accords further prohibit the commercial sale or distribution of forbidden grimoires, artifacts, or knowledge. Exceptions may be granted for educational purposes only, provided materials remain under constant guard. Possession alone does not violate this section unless accompanied by evidence of intent to practice. However, possession combined with prior infractions constitutes prima facie guilt requiring rebuttal proof.

Conservators retain inherent authority to inspect facilities and seize contraband at will. Resistance to inspection is deemed an act of war against the Guild itself. All seizures must be logged and inventoried before release or destruction according to § 1301.2. Unlawful retention of confiscated items constitutes theft from state custody.

Ultimately, the balance between innovation and control remains fragile. The Council acts as sole arbiter of what may safely proceed. Casters who push boundaries without permission risk immediate retribution regardless of potential benefits. Prudence demands deference to established rules lest one find oneself suddenly powerless and imprisoned forever.

sections.title: Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion

body.heading: § 1101.7 Related Requirements - Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion
body.text:
Whereas magical objects may bear more than merely the literal imprints of prior owners or users, this Section governs the doctrine of collateral taints and their legal effect upon subsequent transactions. It is well established under common arcane jurisprudence that certain artifacts retain residual enchantments or curses even after formal disavowal by original casters; these lingering effects may impose liability beyond mere physical damage.

Specifically, a seller shall be deemed to have warranted the absence of active hexes or binding spells unless expressly disclaimed in writing. Failure to disclose known taints constitutes breach of contract and grounds for rescission under § 1302.4 Remedies for Breach. Moreover, any magical item possessing inherent sentience or autonomy may assert rights against good-faith purchasers if its fundamental nature is compromised through unauthorized modification or defilement.

The burden of proving taint exists shifts to the buyer where circumstantial evidence suggests foul play during prior ownership. However, this presumption shall not apply to items acquired at public auction or from reputable dealers maintaining full chain-of-custody records pursuant to § 100.2 Authorized Representatives. In such instances, strict liability attaches only if malicious intent can be demonstrated beyond reasonable doubt.

Furthermore, this Section mandates that all magical transactions involving sentient constructs or animated objects require notarized consent from the entity itself, witnessed by two impartial mages of standing. Absent such documentation, any purported sale shall be void ab initio, regardless of apparent assent from human parties. This safeguard ensures protection against exploitation of vulnerable beings and upholds ethical standards within the trading community at large.

Finally, it is hereby declared that no private agreement may override these mandatory provisions absent explicit ratification by the Guild Desk in a formal ruling. Any attempts to circumvent these protections through fraudulent means shall be punished as grand larceny under applicable penal statutes governing theft and embezzlement of magical assets. These stipulations remain in full force until amended by subsequent legislative action duly passed through established channels.

see § 1302.4 Remedies for Breach; see § 100.2 Authorized Representatives; see § 900.6 Related Requirements

body.heading: § 1101.7 Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion
body.text:
Where articles have been in possession of an unauthorized caster, the Desk may impose a remedial taint upon them, regardless of subsequent bona fide transfer. This preventive measure serves to neutralize residual enchantments that could otherwise re-emerge under certain conditions, posing risk to future owners or users. The taint shall be applied by certified magi under strict supervision, with full disclosure provided to the affected party.

In cases where an article has been used in a prohibited ritual or contract, even if completed years prior, it remains subject to seizure and destruction upon notice from the Desk. The mere fact of such usage renders the item permanently tainted beyond redemption for ordinary commercial use. Any attempt to resell or transfer title shall be deemed void ab initio, with criminal penalties applicable to all involved parties.

The burden of disclosure rests squarely upon sellers when offering articles with a potentially magical history. Failure to disclose known taints constitutes fraud and may result in treble damages plus punitive sanctions. Buyers are encouraged to request full provenance documentation prior to transaction completion, particularly for high-value items or those exhibiting unusual properties. The Desk maintains an online registry of flagged articles which shall be consulted by all parties before finalizing sales agreements.

Articles bearing active curses or binding contracts may require special handling protocols before release into general circulation. In such instances, a neutral third party shall oversee the ritualistic cleansing process, with all costs borne by the original owner unless otherwise adjudicated. Until fully purged of malignant influences, affected items shall remain in secure custody pending further instruction from the Desk.

The principles outlined herein apply equally to both tangible and intangible magical artifacts, including but not limited to enchanted weapons, cursed heirlooms, and digitally encoded spells. No article is beyond the reach of these provisions, regardless of its perceived value or sentimental attachment. The Desk retains sole discretion over what constitutes a sufficient taint warranting intervention under this section.

body.heading: § 1101.7 Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion — Continued
body.text:
The principles outlined in this Part extend beyond direct transactions to encompass the subtle, insidious transmission of magical influence. The Accords recognize that magic, unlike mere commodity, carries an inherent aura that can permeate objects, spaces, and even persons who interact with them. This phenomenon, termed "magical contagion," may occur through touch, proximity, or even shared air for extended periods. While generally benign in casual encounters, sustained exposure to potent enchantments or curses can result in unintended consequences.

Specifically, the Desk holds that any item imbued with significant magical energy constitutes a "tainted asset" until properly cleansed or neutralized. This designation applies whether the magic was placed intentionally by a skilled caster or accidentally during a ritual gone awry. Purchasing or possessing such an item without knowledge of its condition may render the buyer liable for subsequent harms arising from residual enchantments. Sellers, conversely, bear a duty to disclose known taints, as failure to do so constitutes fraud under § 1.5 and voids any contract entered into thereunder.

Furthermore, the concept of "collateral taint" recognizes that magical influence can spread beyond the original object or subject. For instance, clothing worn by a cursed individual may retain harmful properties long after removal, affecting anyone who dons them later. Similarly, rooms where dark rituals were performed may harbor lingering malevolent energies that impact all inhabitants. Landlords and property managers must therefore exercise due diligence in inspecting premises for residual effects before leasing or selling.

In cases of suspected contagion, the victim may petition the Desk for an official appraisal at public expense. If confirmed, the contaminated item or space will be quarantined until remediated by a certified mage. Costs associated with such procedures shall be borne by the party responsible for introducing the taint, determined according to prevailing evidence standards outlined in § 1301.2. Failure to comply may result in further sanctions under applicable penal provisions.

Ultimately, these guidelines aim to protect citizens from the hidden dangers inherent in magical artifacts and environments. By establishing clear rules regarding disclosure, liability, and remediation, the Accords seek to mitigate risks while fostering responsible engagement with the mystical realm. All parties are urged to heed these warnings lest they find themselves ensnared by unseen forces beyond their control.

body.heading: § 1101.7 Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion — Administration
body.text:
The Accords recognize that magical items, whether enchanted or cursed, may carry residual influences extending beyond their primary function. This phenomenon, termed "collateral taint," shall be governed by the provisions set forth herein to ensure fair dealing among all parties.

§ 1101.7(1) Definition of Collateral Taint
"Collateral taint" refers to any persistent magical effect or property that adheres to an item through its original enchantment, curse, blessing, or other supernatural intervention. Such effects may manifest physically, mentally, or spiritually, and shall be deemed inherent to the object itself regardless of subsequent ownership or usage.

§ 1101.7(2) Disclosure Obligations
Every vendor offering a magically influenced item for sale must disclose all known collateral taints in writing prior to completing any transaction. Failure to do so constitutes material misrepresentation and shall render the contract voidable at the option of the aggrieved party. Vendors who knowingly conceal such defects may face additional penalties under § 1302.4 regarding fraudulently misrepresented goods.

§ 1101.7(3) Burden of Proof
In any dispute concerning collateral taints, the burden shall rest upon the alleged victim to demonstrate that: (a) they were unaware of the existence or nature of the taint at the time of purchase; and (b) the taint has caused demonstrable harm exceeding normal wear and tear. The vendor may rebut by presenting evidence of full disclosure and/or mitigation efforts undertaken post-sale.

§ 1101.7(4) Remedial Actions
Upon verification of a valid claim, remedies available to the aggrieved party include: (i) rescission of contract with refund; (ii) damages for proven losses resulting from reliance on defective goods; or (iii) specific performance requiring remediation at the vendor's expense where feasible. The Guild shall provide mediation services upon request and may appoint independent appraisers as needed to assess the scope and severity of any taint effects.

§ 1101.7(5) Exemptions
The provisions of this section shall not apply to items explicitly sold "as-is" with full disclosure of all known defects, nor to magical artifacts acquired through theft or other illicit means where original ownership cannot be established. In such cases, standard commercial law principles shall prevail unless otherwise specified by subsequent ruling of the Autumnwood Accords Desk.

It is hereby declared that ignorance of collateral taints shall not excuse compliance with these regulations. All parties are urged to exercise due diligence in examining potential purchases and consulting qualified experts when uncertainty exists regarding an item's true nature or history. The Guild remains committed to fostering a marketplace built on transparency, integrity, and mutual respect between buyers and sellers alike.

see § 1302.4 Fraudulent Misrepresentation; see § 1101.8 Disclaimer of Implied Warranties; see § 900.5 Independent Appraisal Services; see § 1.7 Construction — Aggregation of Conduct.

body.heading: 1324 - Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion
body.text:
§ 1101.7 Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion — Administration

The administration of collateral taints presents unique challenges requiring specialized protocols and oversight by the Aegis Magi. All instances of potential contamination must be immediately reported to the nearest field office for assessment, regardless of apparent severity or source. Upon receipt of such reports, a designated Taint Response Team shall dispatch within forty-eight hours to verify conditions and contain any spreading influence.

During preliminary evaluation, the team leader may authorize controlled testing procedures deemed necessary to ascertain extent and nature of contamination. Such measures must be conducted with utmost care to avoid exacerbating risks or causing additional harm to persons and property. All findings will be documented in detail and submitted for review by a panel of senior magi experienced in taint theory and remediation techniques.

If initial assessments confirm active spread or high probability thereof, the Aegis Magi shall assume temporary custodial control of affected areas until further notice. This includes securing perimeters, restricting access, and implementing appropriate containment measures as directed by specialized experts convened for that purpose. Disposition of contaminated items remains subject to subsequent determination based on full investigation results.

Throughout all phases of response operations, the safety and well-being of responding personnel shall be paramount consideration without compromising effectiveness of mission objectives. Adequate protective gear, support equipment, and emergency evacuation routes must be provided as appropriate given anticipated hazards encountered during execution of duties under these provisions.

Failure to comply with any aspect of this administrative framework may result in disciplinary action ranging from reprimand to expulsion from membership depending upon gravity of violation and attendant consequences suffered thereby. Repeat offenders face enhanced penalties up to and including permanent forfeiture of standing within the guild structure entirely at sole discretion of governing authorities empowered under these rules.

For additional guidance on specific scenarios not addressed herein, consult relevant case law compilations maintained by the Central Archives or seek direct consultation with appointed advisors specializing in taint management issues as may be mutually agreed upon between all concerned parties involved in any particular situation requiring resolution under this section's purview.

body.heading: § 1101.7 Collateral Taints and Magical Contagion — Administrative Protocol
body.text:
Whereas magical items may carry residual effects beyond their primary function, this Subsection governs the detection, reporting, and remediation of such taints under the auspices of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. All casters in possession of enchanted objects must submit a quarterly declaration on Form 11-DT, attesting to the item's current state and any observed anomalies. Failure to comply shall result in immediate suspension of practice privileges until further notice.

Upon receipt of a report indicating potential contamination, the Desk shall convene an emergency review panel within seven (7) days. Said panel shall consist of no less than three licensed appraisers with expertise in arcane artifacts, none of whom may have a conflict of interest as defined under § 100.5. The panel's sole purpose is to determine whether the reported taint poses a threat to public safety or violates any provision of the Accords.

If confirmed as hazardous, the item shall be seized and placed in secure quarantine pending full analysis. During this period, all parties with lawful possession must refrain from handling or activating the object under any circumstances. Violation of this prohibition constitutes gross negligence subject to penalties under § 1301.2. Once deemed safe for return, a written certification will be issued confirming the item's status and authorizing resumption of normal use.

The Desk shall maintain comprehensive logs of all taint incidents, including origin, nature, extent of damage or risk posed, and resolution measures taken. These records shall remain confidential except as required by law or to inform future regulatory decisions. Information regarding specific items may be disclosed only upon written request from a duly authorized representative of the affected party.

In cases where widespread contamination is suspected across multiple sources, the Desk reserves the right to initiate a broader investigation involving sampling and forensic examination. All reasonable costs associated with such efforts shall be borne by the Guild, subject to reimbursement if negligence or misconduct on the part of any involved caster is established. Nothing herein shall preclude private suits for damages arising out of taint-related injuries or losses.

The provisions of this Subsection shall apply retroactively to all outstanding declarations due as of the Effective Date hereof. Any previously reported but unresolved items remain subject to the full scope of administrative review until formally closed out by the Desk. The undersigned Clerk hereby certifies that these guidelines reflect current best practices for managing magical contagion risks within the community.
