sections.title: Section 1201 – Portal and Planar Regulations

body.heading: Section 1201 – Portal and Planar Regulations
body.text:
The provisions of this Part apply with full force to all persons subject to the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, whether resident within or outside the physical boundaries of the Guild's Hall. The Desk retains inherent authority to extend its reach into foreign lands and planes when necessary to enforce compliance with these regulations. See § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy; under § 100.8 Emergency Sitting for exceptions permitting immediate action beyond normal channels.

No license, permit, or authorization issued by the Desk shall be construed as a waiver of any other applicable laws, ordinances, or customary practices governing magical activity. Rather, these instruments serve to supplement existing frameworks rather than supplant them entirely. Thus, all casters remain bound by local statutes regarding zoning, noise pollution, and public safety even when operating under valid Guild credentials. Refer to § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate for principles of legal hierarchy; analogous reasoning governs inter-jurisdictional conflicts.

The Desk expressly reserves the right to modify, suspend, or revoke any privilege granted herein upon notice and opportunity to be heard. Such actions shall be taken only where compelling circumstances exist, including but not limited to threats to public welfare or national security. The burden of proof rests with the accuser seeking revocation, who must demonstrate by clear and convincing evidence that continued licensure poses an unacceptable risk. See § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse for procedural safeguards protecting licensed individuals; note also § 1301.5 Related Requirements regarding appeals processes.

Finally, nothing in this Part shall be interpreted to diminish or impair the sovereign powers of lawful governments operating within their respective territories. The Desk recognizes and respects the primacy of state authority where it directly pertains to matters beyond its expertise or jurisdictional mandate. Cooperation between entities remains voluntary unless mandated by higher law or mutual agreement. Consult § 1401.2 Dead Citations for guidance on resolving ambiguities regarding overlapping regulatory regimes.

In sum, while granting certain freedoms and protections to qualified practitioners, these measures must always be balanced against broader societal interests. The Desk stands ready to adapt its policies as new challenges emerge, guided by the twin imperatives of facilitating lawful magic and safeguarding the common good. For further elaboration on related topics, reference § 1201.6 Related Requirements; alternatively see §§ 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items and 400.1 Research Permits for examples of conditional permissions granted under similar frameworks.

body.heading: Section 1201 – Portal and Planar Regulations
body.text:
§ 1201.7 Related Requirements for Interdimensional Transit
Under § 1201.3, all portals must bear official transit stamps to verify their legitimacy and safety. However, certain exceptions exist where a stamp may be waived or substituted. First, diplomatic envoys traveling under the protection of the Guild’s Seal of Passage are exempt from routine inspection, as provided in § 100.7. Second, emergency medical evacuations involving critical patients may proceed unstamped if certified by two licensed physicians and approved by an Archmage on duty, per § 200.3(b). Third, research vessels operating within designated pocket-dimension laboratories are subject only to periodic audits rather than individual port-of-entry checks, pursuant to § 400.1(c). Finally, any transit occurring during a declared state of magical emergency may be suspended entirely until further notice, unless authorized by the Aegis Magi under § 100.8. Failure to comply with these related requirements renders the portal operator liable for all resulting damages and penalties outlined in Part 13. See also §§ 1201.4 (Cartography as License), 1201.5 (Transit Stamps), and 1201.6 (Planar Tolls).

body.heading: § 1201.8 Exclusion Zones and Buffer Fields
body.text:
The Accords recognize that certain planar locations possess unique energetic signatures or vulnerabilities that require special protection measures. Under this section, the Guild may designate specific regions as "Exclusion Zones" where unauthorized portal activity is strictly prohibited. These zones typically surround sensitive infrastructure such as major arcane ley lines, dimensional gates used for lawful transit, or areas prone to spontaneous rift formation. Entry into an Exclusion Zone requires a written permit from the Autumnwood Accords Desk, specifying the purpose and duration of entry. Violators face immediate suspension of their licensure and potential revocation upon second offense. The Desk maintains a current list of all active Exclusion Zones on its public records portal for reference by registered casters. Additionally, buffer fields may be established around high-value targets to deter unauthorized planar interference. These fields create an invisible barrier that disrupts unstable portals within a specified radius. Buffer field parameters are classified information known only to the Aegis Magi and senior Desk officials. Any attempt to bypass or tamper with these protective measures constitutes a serious felony under Arcane Penal Code § 1402 "Unlawful Interference with Guild Security." Offenders face imprisonment for not less than five years, plus permanent sealing of their magical abilities. The Guild reserves the right to expand Exclusion Zones and buffer field coverage as threats evolve, provided due process is followed in notifying affected parties of such changes. Caster safety remains paramount in maintaining planar stability across all realms.

see § 1201.9 Related Requirements; see § 300.4 Reclassification; see § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; under § 1.7 Construction, Aggregation of Conduct.

body.heading: § 1201.8 Exclusion Zones and Buffer Fields — Continued
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords recognize the inherent instability of planar interfaces and mandate strict controls over their use to protect both physical reality and the delicate balance between worlds. Section 1201 establishes that all portals, rifts, and dimensional breaches must be registered with the Conservatory's Planar Oversight Division prior to activation or expansion. Unregistered openings are considered illegal acts of war against the fabric of existence itself.

Under § 1201.8, every active portal must maintain a minimum buffer zone extending at least one hundred yards from its perimeter, kept clear of all non-essential matter and personnel. This exclusion area serves to minimize accidental contamination between planes and provides a safety margin for emergency closure procedures. Violation of these distance requirements constitutes a Class A felony under the Accords' penal code.

The Conservators further require that each registered portal be equipped with redundant sealing mechanisms and fail-safe shutdown protocols capable of immediate engagement by remote command. These systems must undergo regular inspection and maintenance to ensure reliability in crisis situations where seconds may mean the difference between salvation and annihilation. Failure to comply with these engineering standards results in automatic revocation of operating permits.

Planar tolls mandated by § 1201.2 apply universally, regardless of whether a portal is privately owned or operated under state contract. The Conservatory retains sole authority to assess and collect fees based on factors including size, frequency of use, projected throughput capacity, and potential risk exposure. Refusal to pay assessed dues leads to immediate suspension of all portal operations until settlement occurs.

Extraterritorial casting into a Diet Chamber as described in § 1201.3 requires special authorization from the High Council regardless of individual licensure status. Such arrangements must be submitted for review at least thirty days prior to intended activation and approved in writing before any dimensional breach may occur without penalty. Unauthorized attempts to extend jurisdiction beyond legal limits are treated as hostile acts warranting full penal response.

The Accords prohibit the commercial sale or lease of portal access rights except through official channels designated by the Conservatory. Private deals involving planar transit services are void ab initio and subject to confiscation of all involved assets without compensation. This restriction aims to prevent monopolization of critical infrastructure by unscrupulous operators seeking undue profit at public expense.

Cartographic materials depicting dimensional gateways fall under strict control per § 1201.4, with distribution limited solely to licensed researchers working on approved projects. Possession or dissemination of unauthorized maps constitutes evidence of intent to engage in prohibited activities and triggers automatic investigation by the Aegis Magi. Penalties escalate significantly if malicious exploitation is proven beyond reasonable doubt.

All registered portals must display prominent signage indicating their official status, operational parameters, emergency contact information, and applicable safety warnings in multiple languages. Failure to maintain proper notices renders operators personally liable for any resulting injuries or damages sustained by third parties lawfully present within the vicinity. This provision underscores the grave responsibility borne by those wielding such powerful tools.

The Conservatory reserves the right at all times to inspect, seal, demolish, or reconfigure any portal deemed necessary for security reasons without prior notice. Operators must provide immediate access and cooperation during such operations under penalty of severe sanctions including permanent revocation of licenses and imprisonment. Non-compliance is viewed as open defiance of lawful authority and will be met accordingly.

Planar regulations exist to safeguard reality itself from the corrosive influence of unchecked dimensional interference. Only through vigilant enforcement can we hope to preserve the sanctity of our world against the myriad threats lurking beyond the veil. The Accords stand as a bulwark against chaos, guiding those who dare tread these dangerous paths with wisdom and restraint unwavering in their resolve to protect all that is precious from destruction without end."

see § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; see § 1201.4 Cartography Sold as a License to Raid; under § 1201.5 Related Requirements"

body.heading: § 1201.8 Exclusion Zones and Buffer Fields, Section 1201 – Portal and Planar Reg
body.text:
§ 1201.8(a) Establishment of Exclusion Zones. — The Guild Desk may declare any geographic area an "Exclusion Zone" upon finding a significant threat to public safety from unauthorized planar activity within said zone. Such zones shall be demarcated by official signage and enforced with appropriate measures, including but not limited to the deployment of Aegis Magi patrols and the confiscation of illegal equipment. Any individual caught operating within an Exclusion Zone without explicit permission from the Desk commits a high misdemeanor under these Accords and is subject to immediate arrest and subsequent prosecution per § 1201.8(b).

§ 1201.8(b) Buffer Fields and Regulatory Control. — To mitigate the risks associated with planar manipulation, the Guild may impose "Buffer Field" requirements on all portals and gateways traversed by casters. These fields act as a secondary layer of protection against accidental leakage or unintended dimensional breaches. Installation and maintenance of such systems shall be overseen exclusively by certified Guild inspectors at no cost to the caster, unless special circumstances arise warranting otherwise. Failure to comply with Buffer Field mandates renders any associated portal illegal and subject to seizure under § 1201.8(c).

§ 1201.8(c) Penalties for Violation of Exclusion or Buffer Regulations. — Anyone knowingly violating an active Exclusion Zone declaration faces a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand gold pieces, imprisonment for up to five years, and/or disqualification from practicing magic within the Guild's jurisdiction indefinitely at the sole discretion of the Archmage Sovereign. Repeated offenses may result in permanent exile from all lands under the Accords' protection. Furthermore, any entity found facilitating such violations through negligence or malice shall be held jointly liable for resulting damages pursuant to § 1201.8(d).

§ 1201.8(d) Civil Liability and Restorative Measures. — In cases where unauthorized planar activity causes harm to persons or property outside the immediate vicinity of the breach point, affected parties may seek civil remedies directly from responsible casters or their employers via standard tort proceedings. The Guild reserves the right to intervene in such suits if it determines that broader public interests are implicated. Additionally, violators found guilty through administrative channels must pay restitution equal to double the estimated value of any damaged goods plus a penalty assessment calculated based on severity and repeat-offense status.

"See also § 1201.3 Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber; § 400.3 Borrowed Hours: Interest in Time." "Under § 1.9 Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal, official Guild markings carry full legal weight." "Pursuant to § 1.7 Construction: Aggregation of Conduct, multiple minor infractions may be combined for enhanced punishment if they demonstrate a pattern of disregard for the Accords' spirit." "For further guidance on planar safety protocols, consult the Guidelines for Safe Dimensional Translocation published by the Conservators." "Violation of Exclusion Zones undermines the very foundation of responsible magic use and must be met with swift justice to preserve public trust in our institutions."

body.heading: § 1201.8 Exclusion Zones and Buffer Fields — Administration
body.text:
The Accords recognize the inherent danger posed by uncontrolled planar gateways, which may spontaneously open or collapse without warning. To mitigate this risk, any location known to harbor a stable portal shall be designated as an exclusion zone under § 1201.1 et seq., where unauthorized casting is strictly prohibited. The Guild reserves authority to enforce these boundaries through whatever means necessary, including the deployment of Aegis Magi equipped with suppression wards designed to neutralize rogue spellcasters attempting to breach protected areas. Failure to comply may result in immediate arrest and subsequent trial before the Paradox Tribunal for violations of § 1201.4 et seq.

Furthermore, all members of the Guild are required to maintain a minimum safety distance from active portals at all times, as dictated by their individual risk assessments outlined in § 300.2(a). This buffer zone serves not only to protect personnel but also to preserve the integrity of planar alignments, which can be irreparably disrupted by careless magical interference. Violations of this mandate shall constitute a Class B infraction subject to disciplinary action up to and including suspension or revocation of licensure under § 200.4(b).

In addition, any individual discovered operating equipment capable of generating artificial portals without proper authorization shall be deemed guilty of grand misdemeanor pursuant to § 1301.5(a)(iii). Such offenders face mandatory confinement for a period not less than one full year, during which time their magical abilities will remain sealed by virtue of an enforceable injunction issued under the provisions of § 1401.2(c). Upon completion of said sentence, reinstatement to good standing may be considered at the sole discretion of the Archmage Sovereign following a comprehensive review of the circumstances surrounding the initial infraction.

It is hereby further ordered that all existing exclusion zones established prior to the effective date hereof shall remain in full force unless explicitly rescinded by subsequent legislative action taken by the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Any attempts to modify, expand upon, or otherwise alter these boundaries without express written consent from said desk are declared null and void ab initio under § 1401.3(b)(ii). Violators shall be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law available, with penalties potentially escalating based on severity of offense as determined by an impartial panel convened specifically for this purpose in accordance with established precedent set forth within §§ 900-950 inclusive thereof.

Finally, it is declared that nothing contained herein shall be construed to limit or impair any rights held by the Guild under applicable common law principles relating to trespassing, nuisance creation, false light portrayal, defamation per quod, invasion of privacy via electronic surveillance techniques commonly employed in contemporary society today amongst others besides those already enumerated above within these same pages collectively referred to henceforth herein as "the aforementioned statutory provisions". body.heading: § 1301.7 Related Requirements and Sunset Provisions
body.text:
§ 1301.7(a) Related Requirements. The fee schedule set forth in Part XIII shall be read in conjunction with the penalties prescribed in § 1301.2, which apply equally to all violations of this Code regardless of whether they are discovered during a scheduled inspection or through other means. Any failure by an inspected party to comply fully and promptly with all directives issued pursuant to these Accords shall constitute grounds for additional sanctions, up to and including revocation of licensure under § 200.4.

§ 1301.7(b) Appeals Procedure. Parties dissatisfied with the results of any inspection or associated penalties may petition the Autumnwood Accords Desk for review in accordance with established appellate procedures. Such petitions must be filed within thirty days of receipt of the initial determination and shall include all relevant evidence supporting the appeal claim. The Desk shall adjudicate appeals expeditiously, utilizing expedited hearing protocols where appropriate to ensure timely resolution of disputes without undue burden on Guild operations.

§ 1301.7(c) Sunset Clause. The fee schedules outlined in this Part are hereby established for a term of five years from the effective date hereof, subject to renewal or modification by the Desk at its sole discretion. Upon expiration of this initial term, the Desk shall conduct a comprehensive review of all operational costs and market conditions before determining whether additional fees are warranted to maintain adequate funding levels. Any proposed changes must be published with sufficient notice to allow for public comment prior to implementation.

§ 1301.7(d) Emergency Provisions. In circumstances where immediate action is required to prevent imminent harm or substantial disruption to Guild functions, the Desk may authorize temporary fee adjustments on an emergency basis without prior notice. Such measures shall remain in effect only until the next regular meeting of the full Council, at which point a final determination regarding long-term policy will be made after due deliberation and consideration of all stakeholder input received during the interim period.

§ 1301.7(e) Transparency Obligations. All fee assessments imposed under this section shall be accompanied by detailed explanations setting forth the specific regulatory services rendered, associated costs incurred, and legal authority supporting each charge itemized therein. The Desk maintains an online portal providing access to historical data regarding past inspections, outcomes achieved, and comparative analyses demonstrating the value proposition offered to licensed practitioners through participation in this framework. Such transparency measures are designed to foster trust between regulators and regulated entities while ensuring accountability throughout the enforcement process.

§ 1301.7(f) Finality of Assessments. Once formally assessed and notified, all fees imposed pursuant to these provisions shall be deemed final and binding upon receipt, absent successful appeal within prescribed timeframes. Failure to pay outstanding balances in full by the deadline specified shall result in automatic suspension of licensure privileges until default is cured in accordance with applicable procedures set forth elsewhere herein. The Desk reserves the right to pursue collection actions as necessary to recover unpaid amounts owed, including but not limited to referral to appropriate authorities for civil litigation or criminal prosecution where warranted under existing law."

"see § 1301.2 Penalties; see § 1401.5 Related Requirements"

body.heading: § 1301.7 Related Requirements and Sunset Provisions — Continued
body.text:
The fees prescribed herein are subject to periodic review by the Mages' Guild Desk, which may adjust rates in response to inflation or shifts in market conditions. Any such adjustments shall be published at least thirty days prior to implementation to afford affected parties adequate notice. Furthermore, all levies imposed under this section shall expire automatically upon the fulfillment of their intended purpose or after a maximum duration of five years unless expressly renewed by resolution of the Desk. Failure to comply with these temporal limitations renders any assessment void ab initio and unenforceable against any person or entity.

In addition to fee collection, the Guild reserves the right to impose additional charges for services rendered beyond those explicitly enumerated in this schedule. Such ancillary fees must be clearly itemized on all invoices and receipts issued by authorized collectors. Parties disputing the reasonableness of any supplemental assessment bear the burden of demonstrating its necessity and proportionality relative to the scope of work performed. Absent such proof, default judgments entered for excessive amounts shall be overturned upon timely motion.

The provisions set forth herein operate in conjunction with, but do not supersede, other applicable statutes governing magical commerce within Autumn Wood jurisdiction. In cases of conflict between this section and higher law, the latter shall prevail by virtue of its superior legal force. Conversely, where no specific mandate exists elsewhere, these guidelines serve as the exclusive standard for determining permissible charges and enforcement mechanisms pertaining to the regulation of arcane practices in our region.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing contained herein shall be construed to diminish or impair any pre-existing rights vested in individual casters by virtue of their licensure status under separate provisions of this Code. Such entitlements remain fully intact unless explicitly abrogated through due process proceedings initiated pursuant to applicable rules of administrative law. Similarly, obligations accruing prior to the effective date of these amendments shall continue unabated regardless of subsequent changes to the fee schedule.

Finally, it is hereby declared that all payments made in accordance with this section constitute full and final satisfaction of any outstanding debts owed by payer to payee regarding matters falling within the scope of collection authority granted herein. No further action may be taken on such accounts except as expressly authorized by written instrument executed by both parties hereto or their duly appointed representatives acting under valid power of attorney. This declaration shall remain in effect forever unless modified by mutual consent evidenced in writing signed by all concerned stakeholders.

body.heading: § 1301.7 Related Requirements and Sunset Provisions — Continued — Continued
body.text:
The provisions set forth herein shall remain in full force and effect until such time as superseded by subsequent enactments or repealed by the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to limit the powers of the Desk or its constituent bodies under any other section of this Code, including but not limited to §§ 100.8, 200.4, and 300.5. All rights reserved except as expressly granted herein. No implied license or waiver by conduct shall be inferred from failure to enforce any provision strictly in accordance with its terms. The Desk retains sole discretion to interpret ambiguous language and resolve disputes arising hereunder. Any attempt to circumvent these requirements through subterfuge or evasion shall constitute a violation of this Code and subject the offender to appropriate sanctions under applicable law.

"Sunset Provisions": These are temporary clauses that expire after a set period unless renewed by explicit action. They allow flexibility for trying new approaches without permanent commitment. For example, § 1301.7(b) permits emergency licensing procedures only during declared crises, reverting to normal standards once stability is restored. Such provisions must be clearly labeled and their expiration dates prominently displayed. Failure to comply with sunset timelines renders the associated authority void ab initio unless extended pursuant to established amendment protocols outlined in § 1401.3."

"Related Requirements": Additional obligations beyond those explicitly stated may arise from common law principles, customary practice, or equitable considerations deemed necessary by the Desk in specific cases. These unwritten rules serve to fill gaps and ensure fair treatment absent rigid statutory guidance. While not formally codified, they carry binding force when invoked properly before the Guild's judicial bodies."

"Enforcement Mechanisms": Violations of this section may trigger automatic penalties per § 1301.2 or require discretionary sanctions at the Desk's discretion. Repeat offenders face escalated consequences including license revocation and permanent expulsion from the Accords community. Civil liabilities may also accrue alongside criminal punishments for egregious breaches."

"Compliance Monitoring": Ongoing oversight ensures adherence to these evolving standards through periodic audits, random inspections, and whistleblower reporting channels maintained independently of local enforcement agencies. Data gathered feeds into predictive modeling efforts aimed at preemptively identifying potential problem areas requiring proactive intervention rather than reactive punishment alone."

*Footnotes omitted for brevity.*

body.heading: § 1301.7 Sunset Provisions and Statute Limitations
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords, in their entirety and regardless of individual article, shall expire on the tenth day following the first full lunar cycle after the issuance of this Codex. Upon such expiration, all rights, duties, obligations, and liabilities created thereby shall cease forthwith, unless explicitly renewed by a subsequent resolution of the Mages' Guild Desk. This provision ensures that the Accords remain subject to periodic review and revision in accordance with evolving magical practices and societal needs.

Furthermore, no action arising under this Codex shall be brought more than five (5) years after the date on which such right of action first accrued. For purposes of this limitation, a cause of action accrues when any violation of these provisions occurs or should have been reasonably known by the aggrieved party through the exercise of due diligence. Failure to commence proceedings within the prescribed period shall constitute an absolute bar to recovery, regardless of the merits of the underlying claim.

The foregoing limitations are applicable uniformly across all articles and sections herein, without exception or qualification. They reflect a deliberate legislative choice to balance the need for legal certainty with recognition of the fluid nature of arcane phenomena. Parties relying on any provision of this Codex must therefore act promptly to preserve their rights under it.

In the event of any conflict between the terms hereof and prior laws, regulations, or agreements relating to the same subject matter, the provisions of these Accords shall control exclusively during their term of validity. This supremacy clause underscores the intended comprehensive nature of the Autumnwood framework as the governing standard for magical conduct in the Midlands region.

Finally, it is hereby declared that nothing in this Codex shall be construed as creating any new cause of action or liability beyond those expressly set forth herein. All claims must arise directly from the text of these provisions to be cognizable under the law. This restriction serves to maintain clarity and predictability in legal relations involving magic users and practitioners alike.

body.heading: § 1301.7 Sunset Provisions and Statute Limitations — Continued
body.text:
The temporal efficacy of penal sanctions imposed under these Accords is subject to specific limitations, both in terms of duration and applicability to subsequent infractions. Any seal or magical restraint affixed pursuant to a Paradox Trial shall remain active for no longer than three standard solar years from the date of imposition, absent renewal by majority vote of the Aegis Magi Council. Upon expiration, all binding effects automatically dissolve unless extended. This limitation reflects the fundamental principle that punitive measures against individuals must be proportionate and time-bound, preventing indefinite subjugation under threat of further sanction for past conduct.

Furthermore, no penal order issued hereunder shall serve as a bar to prosecution or adjudication for any new violation of the Accords committed during its term of validity. Each infraction constitutes an independent wrong demanding separate consideration by the proper authorities. Thus, while active seals may temporarily curtail the application of certain magical arts, they do not confer immunity from future liability should the restrained individual again transgress guild law. This preserves the integrity of the regulatory framework and ensures that repeated offenders face escalating consequences commensurate with their ongoing disregard for established norms.

In cases where a sanctioned seal is intentionally circumvented or deliberately nullified by the subject, the original penalty shall be deemed void ab initio, and any resulting harm attributable to such evasion shall be fully actionable against the offending party. Conversely, accidental breach of a magical restraint does not automatically trigger additional sanctions; rather, it necessitates review by the adjudicating body to determine appropriate remedial action based on the circumstances surrounding the incident. This safeguard prevents disproportionate punishment for inadvertent failures and maintains fairness in enforcement.

Ultimately, these sunset provisions embody the balance between retribution and rehabilitation inherent to civilized society. By limiting the scope of punitive authority over time, they acknowledge that individuals retain an inherent dignity even under duress, while simultaneously preserving the Guild's right to address ongoing threats posed by recidivists. Such measured application of power serves both justice and the greater good of maintaining order within the magical community at large.

body.heading: § 1301.7 Related Requirements and Sunset Provisions — Administration
body.text:
The Accords recognize that certain provisions may require periodic review to ensure their continued relevance and efficacy in the face of evolving magical landscapes. Under this authority, the Desk shall establish a mechanism for assessing the necessity and impact of each regulation on an ongoing basis. Such assessments must be conducted with transparency and input from all affected parties, including practitioners, researchers, and members of the public.

When a provision is deemed obsolete or redundant, it may be subject to repeal or modification through the standard legislative process. In such instances, appropriate notice shall be given to allow for meaningful comment and participation. The Desk retains discretion to implement interim measures where necessary to maintain stability during the transition period.

Conversely, emerging trends in magical theory or practice may warrant the adoption of new rules to address previously unforeseen challenges. These additions must align with the overarching principles of safety and fairness enshrined in the Accords. Proposed amendments shall undergo rigorous scrutiny prior to enactment, ensuring they serve the public interest without imposing undue burdens on legitimate pursuits.

The Desk is further empowered to delegate limited authority to subcommittees or appointed panels for expedited handling of routine matters. Such delegations must be clearly defined and time-limited, with regular reporting back to the full body. Decisions made by these proxies shall carry equal weight as those rendered directly by the Accords' representatives.

In all instances involving the revision or interpretation of existing statutes, the Desk shall strive for clarity and consistency in its rulings. Ambiguities should be resolved favorably toward open inquiry rather than restrictive enforcement, fostering an environment conducive to advancement without compromising core values. Through diligent stewardship and adaptive governance, the Accords remain a living document capable of meeting the changing needs of society while safeguarding against potential harms.

see § 1301.5 Related Requirements for additional context on administrative procedures; see § 1201.6 Related Requirements regarding delegation protocols; see § 900.7 Related Requirements concerning public engagement standards.

sections.title: Authority and Validity

body.heading: § 1401.7 Related Requirements - Authority and Validity
body.text:
The provisions contained herein shall be deemed valid only when enacted in conformity with the procedural mandates set forth under §§ 100.1–100.8 of this Codex, including but not limited to proper quorum, notice periods, and formal recordation of all deliberations. Any resolution adopted in contravention of these foundational rules shall be considered void ab initio and unenforceable under any circumstance. See § 100.3 Quorum; § 100.4 Records of Speech.

This Codex supersedes all prior statutes, charters, customary practices, or oral agreements inconsistent with its express terms as of the Effective Date specified herein. However, nothing contained in this document shall be construed to diminish any vested rights acquired by bona fide parties under previously existing laws unless explicitly abrogated by subsequent legislation. Under § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate, no provision hereof may conflict with superior imperial directives or national security imperatives declared by duly constituted authorities.

The Governing Body retains inherent authority to interpret ambiguous clauses and fill gaps in this regulation as necessary to effectuate its purposes. Such interpretations shall be published promptly in official gazettes along with rationales for any significant departures from prior precedent. Failure to comply with binding rulings issued pursuant to this power may result in disciplinary sanctions up to and including revocation of licensure privileges. Refer to § 200.1 Licensure Required; § 500.1 Field Casting for Value regarding applicable penalties.

All members of the Guild shall actively participate in maintaining the integrity and efficacy of these statutes through diligent adherence, timely reporting of violations, and constructive engagement with oversight mechanisms established under this framework. Collective accountability is paramount to safeguarding both public welfare and professional standards within our esteemed community. See § 1401.2 Dead Citations; § 300.1 Schedules of Arts for compliance obligations.

Any questions concerning the meaning or application of specific articles should be directed in writing to the Office of Legal Counsel no later than seven (7) business days after publication. Responses will be rendered within fourteen (14) calendar days unless extended due to extraordinary circumstances beyond reasonable control. Parties dissatisfied with official answers may petition for review by a three-member panel appointed jointly by the Archmage Sovereign and the Desk Chairperson. Consult § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting for recusals procedures.

The full text of this enactment is available online at [redacted URL] or upon request from any registered practitioner paying applicable copying fees. Updated versions will be posted immediately following final ratification without further notice deemed adequate compliance with public disclosure mandates. All persons subject to these regulations are hereby put on formal notice thereof. Under § 1401.5 Related Requirements, failure to acknowledge receipt of this document shall not excuse subsequent liability for noncompliance.

It is expressly declared that the intent behind each section herein was carefully considered by the drafting committee responsible for its preparation prior to submission for approval. Nothing contained in these provisions should be interpreted restrictively or expansively absent clear textual evidence supporting such reading. Plain language governs unless specialized terminology necessitates otherwise pursuant to established canons of statutory construction. See § 1.7 Construction; Aggregation of Conduct regarding interpretive principles applicable throughout this Code.

The Great Seal of the Mages' Guild shall be affixed to all certified copies issued under this authority as conclusive proof of authenticity and official status until proven otherwise by competent judicial proceeding or administrative appeal filed within one hundred eighty (180) days of issuance date stamping thereof. Copies lacking proper authentication may be rejected outright by receiving agencies exercising enforcement powers delegated herein. Refer to § 1.9 Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal for detailed requirements governing acceptable forms of verification.

Nothing in this regulation shall be construed to impair existing contractual obligations undertaken prior to the Effective Date unless expressly prohibited thereby. Nor shall it impose retroactive liability absent affirmative waiver by affected parties exercising their full rights under applicable law. Privity of contract remains inviolate except where explicitly modified or superseded by mandatory provisions herein. See § 1.5 Relation to Other Law; § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters for limitations on implied terms.

All disputes arising out of or related to the interpretation, enforcement, or alleged violation of these statutes shall first be submitted to binding arbitration administered under rules promulgated by the Guild Dispute Resolution Committee unless otherwise agreed in writing between disputing parties. Arbitral awards rendered pursuant thereto shall have full force and effect as final judgments entered by courts of competent jurisdiction without further review except upon grounds specifically enumerated in relevant procedural orders. Consult § 1301.6 Related Requirements regarding enforcement mechanisms available to aggrieved litigants seeking relief beyond the scope of initial remedial measures granted herein.

This enactment shall remain in full force and effect until expressly repealed, amended, or superseded by subsequent action duly taken pursuant to established legislative processes outlined above. Continual vigilance remains essential to preserve both literal fidelity and spirit of original purpose motivating adoption thereof by consensus of responsible stewards invested with fiduciary duties toward all stakeholders impacted thereby. See § 1401.1 Historical Annotations; Form for guidance regarding preservation of legislative history relevant to ongoing debates concerning scope and application of individual provisions contained within this comprehensive regulatory scheme governing conduct subject to oversight jurisdiction vested herein.

[End of section]

body.heading: Authority and Validity of the Autumnwood Accords
body.text:
The authority under which this Codex is promulgated derives directly from the sovereign will of Archmage Veyra, elected by the collective wisdom of the Guild's constituent Halls as their highest steward. This mandate empowers the Mages' Desk to enact regulations binding upon all who practice magic within its jurisdiction, save only for matters reserved exclusively to the Sovereign herself. Such reserving ensures that no single body may usurp the ultimate arbitrating power granted by the Accords' founding charter.

Any regulation issued pursuant thereto carries full legal force and effect once duly promulgated in accordance with established procedure. Failure to comply constitutes a breach of contract between the regulated party and the Guild, subject to remedies outlined herein including sanctions, seals, or even expulsion from lawful practice entirely at the Desk's discretion. Nothing contained here shall be construed to diminish the inherent rights protected by fundamental charter provisions unless explicitly abrogated through proper channels requiring supermajority approval.

The validity of any action taken under authority delegated by this Codex remains subject only to review by the Mages' Desk itself or its duly appointed appellate bodies. No external court, tribunal, or private entity shall have jurisdiction over disputes arising from magical practice regulated hereunder without express consent of all parties and voluntary submission thereto. This preserves the autonomy essential to maintaining order within a complex arcane ecosystem while safeguarding against arbitrary interference from outside forces.

In sum, then, these provisions establish both the source and scope of regulatory power vested in the Guild's governing institutions. By defining limits on what may be commanded even by its highest representatives, they balance necessary oversight with cherished liberties. Such equilibrium serves as the foundation upon which all other rules rest securely, enabling them to function effectively without encroaching improperly upon individual sovereignty or collective autonomy alike. Only through such careful calibration can lasting harmony be achieved amidst the endless tensions inherent in any society built around mastery of forbidden arts.

see § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild; see § 300.4 Reclassification Procedure; see § 1501.9 Reserved Matters Requiring Supermajority Approval; see § 1601.7 External Review and Appellate Process.

body.heading: Authority and Validity of the Autumnwood Accords — Continued
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords derive their binding force from three interlocking sources. First, under § 1.2, they are enacted by the sovereign authority of Archmage Veyra acting as mediator for all mages within the Hall's jurisdiction. Second, the consent of the Guild membership is implied through continued operation under the existing regime; no one has publicly repudiated these laws since their codification. Third, and most importantly, the Accords reflect a universal consensus among practicing mages regarding necessary restrictions on magical activity. This consensus exists independently of any particular sovereign's decree.

Accordingly, § 1401.7 declares that the Autumnwood Accords shall be deemed valid notwithstanding any contrary provisions in local charters or customs. Any attempt to nullify these laws is void ab initio and unenforceable. The only exception concerns matters explicitly reserved by § 100.2, which prohibits the Guild from legislating on strictly personal affairs unrelated to magical practice.

Furthermore, under § 1401.8, the Accords shall remain in effect until expressly repealed or superseded by a subsequent enactment of equal authority. No individual may unilaterally declare them null and void. Only a formal resolution of the Autumn Wood Desk, passed with requisite votes as outlined in § 100.3, can alter this status quo. Such resolutions must be published promptly to ensure all subjects are duly notified.

In summary, the legal weight of the Autumnwood Accords stems from their dual nature as both binding contracts and statements of professional ethics accepted by the entire casting community. They constitute a living constitution for magecraft in the Midlands region, superseding conflicting norms wherever they pertain to magical safety or public order. Any challenge to their validity must be mounted through proper legal channels within the Guild framework itself.

body.heading: Authority and Validity — Continued
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords derive their binding force directly from the sovereign will of Archmage Veyra, who acts as the ultimate arbiter within the Hall. Her decrees stand supreme unless explicitly overturned by a duly convened vote of the Full Desk or through established legal challenge under § 100.5. No individual mage possesses the authority to unilaterally void any provision of this Code; even an Archmage's personal edict must align with its core tenets to hold weight outside immediate emergency contexts.

Pursuant to § 1.9, seals and stamps placed by authorized clerks shall constitute conclusive evidence of official ratification unless successfully rebutted by counter-proof meeting the highest standards of admissibility set forth in these regulations. Such authentication mechanisms are designed to prevent forgery while expediting routine administrative functions across all Guild jurisdictions. Unauthorized modifications or alterations to any enrolled document render it immediately null and void ab initio, regardless of apparent signatures or endorsements thereon.

Any dispute arising from conflicting interpretations of the Accords shall be resolved exclusively through formal proceedings before the Autumnwood Desk, with final appeal limited to direct petition to Archmage Veyra in extraordinary circumstances only. Private arbitration clauses contained within individual contracts are hereby expressly superseded by this mandatory forum-selection provision for all matters falling within the scope of Guild regulation. Failure to exhaust these prescribed channels shall result in automatic dismissal of any ensuing claims or motions brought thereafter.

This section represents a comprehensive codification of the foundational principles governing the exercise of magical authority under the Autumnwood Accords framework. Its provisions operate prospectively from date of promulgation unless expressly stated otherwise within specific articles addressing transitional matters affecting pending cases or ongoing investigations initiated prior thereto. All parties bound hereby acknowledge receipt and understanding of these critical guidelines regulating their professional conduct and responsibilities as licensed practitioners within the jurisdiction of this august body.

body.heading: Authority and Validity Continued
body.text:
The binding force of the Autumnwood Accords derives directly from the sovereign will of Archmage Veyra, invested through ancient ritual to manifest as immutable law within the boundaries of the Guild's jurisdiction. This primacy supersedes all other claims except those expressly granted by her edict. Any challenge to this authority must be brought before the High Council in open session and proven beyond reasonable doubt; mere speculation or dissent will not suffice. The Accords stand as the ultimate expression of magical order, embodying centuries of collective wisdom and hard-won experience. To undermine them is to invite chaos upon oneself and one's allies alike. Thus let all who would serve the Greater Good heed these words most carefully: obedience to the Codex is the first step toward mastery over the arcane arts. Only by submitting fully to this framework may mages hope to wield their gifts safely and effectively for generations yet unborn. The path ahead demands vigilance, discipline, and unwavering commitment to our shared mission. Together we shall uphold these sacred vows against all comers!

body.heading: § 1401.7 Authority and Validity Continued - Enforcement Protocols and Jurisdicti
body.text:
The enforcement of the Autumnwood Accords shall be undertaken by duly authorized representatives of the Mages' Guild, including but not limited to the Aegis Magi and their subordinate officers. Such agents are vested with full power to investigate alleged violations, conduct hearings, and impose sanctions in accordance with these provisions. Nothing herein shall limit or impair any inherent powers possessed by the Guild under its charter.

In matters involving cross-jurisdictional disputes or parallel proceedings initiated by other competent authorities, the Guild reserves the right to assert primary jurisdiction where its interests are most directly implicated. The parties agree to cooperate fully in such instances, exchanging information and evidence as necessary for a comprehensive resolution. Failure to comply with this obligation shall constitute grounds for punitive action under applicable law.

All actions taken pursuant to these Articles shall be conducted expeditiously and without undue delay. Time limits specified herein are strict and may not be extended except by written agreement of all affected parties or upon showing of extraordinary circumstances beyond reasonable control. The Guild shall provide written notice of its intentions at least thirty (30) days prior to initiating any enforcement measures, allowing the respondent adequate opportunity to respond.

The provisions of this Part are severable; if any section is found unenforceable for any reason whatsoever, it shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining clauses. The intent and purpose of these regulations shall be construed liberally in favor of maintaining public safety and order within the magical community. Ambiguities shall be resolved by reference to established precedent and principles of equity rather than technical literalism alone.

The undersigned hereby acknowledge receipt, reading, understanding, and voluntary submission to all terms outlined above. This agreement may not be amended except through formal amendment adopted by vote of a quorum convened specially for that purpose in accordance with Article III hereof. All prior negotiations, representations, or understandings are expressly merged herein and superseded by this final written instrument which embodies the entire consideration between the parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have executed this document on the date first above written under my hand and seal to perpetuate its force according to law." ________________ [SEAL] Archmage Veyra, Sovereign of the Autumnwood Accords "Authority flows from consent, not compulsion. The Guild stands guard over our shared future, bound by oath and honor. So long as these laws endure, so shall the balance of magic remain unshaken." - Archmage Theron "Progress demands risk, yet recklessness invites ruin. We tread a razor's edge between discovery and destruction. Prudence is not fear—it is wisdom earned in fire." - Janna Brightspark "The Accords are but tools; true mastery lies within the mage's heart. Yet even the keenest blade can cut both ways without guidance. Let us wield them with care." - Unnamed Aegis Magus

body.heading: § 200.8 Related Requirements - Prerequisites for Licensure
body.text:
No applicant shall be issued a Caster's License unless they first satisfy all applicable prerequisites set forth in this Part and the Schedules of Arts. These requirements are designed to ensure that each licensed individual possesses the necessary knowledge, skill, and ethical grounding to cast safely and responsibly within Autumnwood society. Failure to meet any prerequisite renders an application void ab initio, regardless of subsequent compliance.

§ 200.8(a) Mandatory Education. All applicants must complete at least one hundred hours of formal magical theory instruction at an accredited institution or under direct supervision of a licensed Caster. This curriculum shall cover the fundamental principles of mana dynamics, spell construction, safety protocols, and the historical context of arcane development. Textbooks listed in Appendix A constitute the minimum acceptable syllabus, though additional resources may be substituted with Archmage consent. Proof of course completion must be submitted via certified transcript or letter of evaluation on official stationery bearing an institutional seal.

§ 200.8(b) Practical Competency Assessment. Following educational requirements, candidates shall undergo a comprehensive practical examination administered by the Guild's Certification Committee. This assessment evaluates hands-on ability to perform basic casting techniques, manage unexpected complications, and demonstrate situational awareness during simulated scenarios. Written tests covering theoretical knowledge may accompany oral questioning. Passing scores must be achieved on both components for full licensure eligibility.

§ 200.8(c) Ethical Vetting Process. Applicants shall submit sworn affidavits regarding their character history, including any prior disciplinary actions, criminal convictions, or professional malpractice incidents. Background checks conducted through standard law enforcement channels supplement this self-reporting mechanism. Any material misrepresentation on the application form constitutes grounds for immediate disqualification and potential legal prosecution under § 2051.3 False Statements.

§ 200.8(d) Financial Obligations. Prospective licensees must demonstrate financial solvency through recent tax returns or audited statements from recognized accounting firms. Outstanding debts exceeding five hundred gold pieces shall preclude approval until resolved to the satisfaction of Guild authorities. This provision aims to prevent economically distressed individuals from taking on dangerous magical work beyond their means, thereby reducing liability risks for both parties involved in future contracts.

§ 200.8(e) Psychological Screening Requirements. Given the inherent stresses of professional spellcasting, all applicants must submit to standardized psychological evaluation administered by licensed practitioners affiliated with the Guild's Wellness Program. Tests shall assess emotional stability, impulse control, and capacity for handling high-pressure situations without compromising judgment or safety standards. Results will be kept confidential except in cases where public protection may be jeopardized by known mental health issues.

See also § 100222345678901234567890 "Mandatory Education" (redundant); § 100222345678901234567891 "Practical Competency Assessment" (duplicate citation). Note: Cross-reference errors detected during automated review. Recommend re-indexing affected sections for accuracy. End of page.

body.heading: Prerequisites for Licensure
body.text:
No individual shall obtain a caster's license without first satisfying all statutory prerequisites set forth in this Part. Under § 200.1, licensure remains the sole legal avenue by which an unlicensed person may lawfully cast magic within the Kingdom. Failure to meet these baseline requirements renders any subsequent application void ab initio and subject to immediate revocation upon discovery.

First, applicants must demonstrate proven competence in safe magical practice through either formal education or verified field experience totaling a minimum of five years under direct supervision. This standard ensures that licensees possess sufficient mastery to operate without endangering public safety. See § 200.6 (constructs holding quills) for analogous competency thresholds applied to automated casting devices.

Second, all applicants must undergo background checks conducted by the Guild's Investigative Division pursuant to § 1401.4. These screenings assess character integrity and past conduct relevant to magical safety. A history of violent magic use or repeated disciplinary violations disqualifies candidates outright under § 300.2 (necromancy as unsanctioned art).

Third, prospective licensees must submit a detailed inventory of all spells, artifacts, and techniques currently in their possession for review by the Arcane Safety Commission. Concealment of dangerous materials constitutes grounds for denial per § 400.3 (specimen custody provisions). The Commission retains authority to demand additional disclosure as needed to evaluate risk factors.

Finally, applicants must execute a sworn affidavit declaring full compliance with all applicable laws and regulations governing magical activity. This oath binds them under pain of perjury and potential criminal prosecution for any misrepresentations discovered post-licensure. Violation voids the license immediately without prejudice to further action. § 500.1 (field casting for value) establishes similar affirmative covenants in commercial contexts.

The Department reserves discretion to waive one or more prerequisites on a case-by-case basis where compelling circumstances exist and public welfare is not compromised. Such exceptions require unanimous approval by the Arcane Safety Commission and must be publicly disclosed with rationale. See § 100.2 (authorized speakers) for parallel delegation principles applied to administrative rule-making.

All licensure decisions shall be made solely upon objective criteria outlined herein, free from political influence or personal bias. The Department must maintain scrupulous records of each application's evaluation and provide written explanations for denials upon request. Transparency in this process fosters public trust and accountability essential to the Guild's legitimacy. § 1201.5 (related requirements) reinforces these procedural safeguards across all regulatory domains.

In sum, the prerequisites for licensure embody the Kingdom's commitment to balancing magical innovation with prudent oversight. By demanding demonstrated skill, clean records, full disclosure, and honest representation, the state ensures that new licensees can contribute positively to society while mitigating inherent risks. These standards form the bedrock of responsible magical practice under modern law. Under § 700.4 (aggregation of conduct), repeated failure to adhere to these requirements may trigger enhanced penalties beyond mere revocation.

*End of Section 200 - Licensing and Registration Requirements*

body.heading: Prerequisites for Licensure — Continued
body.text:
§ 200.8 Prerequisites for Licensure; Standards of Competence and Good Faith. No application for licensure shall be accepted unless the applicant submits proof of completion of the requisite foundational coursework as specified in § 300.1, together with a sworn statement attesting to their moral character and lack of prior disciplinary actions under any applicable law. The Board shall have sole discretion to deny licensure if it determines that the applicant lacks the necessary aptitude or integrity to responsibly wield magical powers. All candidates must undergo a comprehensive background investigation conducted by the Aegis Magi, which may include psychological evaluation and scrutiny of past associations. Failure to satisfy any prerequisite condition shall result in automatic rejection of the application without further notice. Nothing herein shall be construed to waive the Guild's inherent authority to reject unfit practitioners at its absolute discretion for reasons beyond the scope of these provisions. This section serves as a baseline threshold, subject to modification by future rulemaking as technological and social conditions evolve.

[ARCHIVE CARD: "Magic is not a toy or a commodity to be bought and sold freely. Those granted the privilege of casting spells must first prove themselves worthy through education, character assessment, and adherence to ethical standards. The Guild stands guard against those who would misuse such power for selfish ends." — Archmage Veyra, in her inaugural address.]

body.heading: Prerequisites for Licensure — Competency and Character Standards
body.text:
No individual shall obtain an initial or renewed Practitioner's License without first demonstrating both technical competence and moral suitability, as these twin pillars uphold the integrity of magical practice within the Accords. The Conservators maintain that magic demands not only skill but also a sound mind and spirit to wield responsibly; hence, all applicants must undergo rigorous vetting before admission to candidacy for examination. This dual requirement ensures that licenses are granted solely to those capable of mastering their craft without endangering themselves or society at large.

To assess technical proficiency, the Guild administers written tests covering theory, history, ethics, and practical application appropriate to each class of licensure. Oral examinations further probe an applicant's depth of understanding and ability to think critically under pressure. Written assessments include essay questions on magical principles and scenario-based problem-solving tasks designed to evaluate judgment and foresight. Practical demonstrations require candidates to perform controlled spells safely while explaining their reasoning aloud, allowing examiners to gauge both execution quality and conceptual grasp simultaneously.

Beyond mere aptitude, moral character constitutes an equally vital criterion for licensure eligibility. The Guild seeks only trustworthy custodians of magical power, individuals unlikely to abuse their abilities for personal gain or reckless experimentation. Background checks reveal any history of criminal conduct, substance abuse disorders, or prior disciplinary actions relevant to magic use. Interviews delve into an applicant's motivations and values, seeking evidence of integrity and commitment to lawful practice over short-term profit. References from reputable sources corroborate claims of responsible behavior and ethical conduct in both personal and professional spheres.

Only those who excel across all these dimensions may proceed toward full licensure status; failure in any area results in automatic disqualification regardless of superior performance elsewhere. This holistic approach reflects the Guild's conviction that magical proficiency alone is insufficient safeguard against misuse — character flaws often prove more dangerous than technical ignorance when combined with unrestricted access to potent arts. By insisting upon both competence and virtue, the Accords protect themselves and their citizens from potential catastrophes stemming from inadequately vetted practitioners wielding unchecked destructive capabilities.

see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; see § 400.1 Research Permits under related provisions governing access to dangerous materials and techniques.

body.heading: Prerequisites for Licensure and Character Standards
body.text:
Any individual seeking licensure under the Autumnwood Accords must first demonstrate competency in magical theory and practice, as assessed by the Guild's examination committee. This assessment includes written examinations on established principles, practical demonstrations of spellcasting ability, and oral interviews to gauge understanding of ethical considerations and safety protocols. Failure to meet these minimum standards renders an applicant ineligible for licensure regardless of personal skill or connections.

Beyond technical competence, applicants must also satisfy character requirements designed to ensure responsible stewardship of magical power. These provisions mandate a clean record free from criminal convictions within the last ten years, absence of pending litigation involving violence or property destruction, and verification of good standing in one's local community. The intent is to screen out individuals with histories of antisocial behavior that could endanger public safety if they were granted unrestricted access to magical arts.

Particularly stringent scrutiny applies to candidates applying for licenses in sensitive fields such as necromancy or high-tier elemental manipulation. For these specialized areas, additional background checks are conducted to confirm lack of prior offenses and absence of affiliations with dangerous organizations. Applicants must also provide character references attesting to their integrity and judgment, along with proof of adequate financial resources to support themselves without resorting to illegal means.

The Guild reserves the right to deny licensure on discretionary grounds whenever it deems an individual unsuitable for responsible practice, regardless of whether they meet explicit criteria. This includes but is not limited to evidence of substance abuse problems, unstable mental health conditions, or a propensity for recklessness and irresponsibility. The ultimate determination rests with the Mages' Guild Desk acting in accordance with its mandate to protect both magic users and the general public from harm.

See also § 200.1 Licensure Required (general mandate), § 300.1 Schedules of Arts (specific regulated classes), and § 400.1 Research Permits (specialized authorization process). Under § 1.7 Construction, these provisions shall be liberally construed to uphold the public welfare objectives embodied in the Accords. Any ambiguities in application are to be resolved favorably toward maintaining high standards of safety and professionalism within the magical community.

body.heading: § 200.8 Prerequisites for Licensure — Character and Competency Standards
body.text:
A person seeking licensure under the Accords must satisfy both character and competency prerequisites as defined herein. Regarding character, an applicant shall demonstrate good moral standing within their community or profession, free from criminal conviction except minor infractions expunged after five years (§ 1401.2). Any history of magical abuse or misuse of powers shall disqualify the candidate permanently. The Licensing Desk may require a background investigation and references to verify these assertions (§ 100.6 Delegation to Clerks).

Competency standards mandate proof of mastery in one's chosen school of magic, equivalent to at least five years' formal training under a licensed mentor. Applicants must pass written examinations testing theoretical knowledge and practical demonstrations assessing safe handling of spells. Failure on initial exams permits only two retakes within six months (§ 1201.6 Related Requirements). Beyond technical skill, candidates shall exhibit sound judgment, emotional stability, and an unblemished record of responsible conduct. The Desk reserves the right to deny licensure for any reason deeming it contrary to public safety or magical integrity (§ 1401.5 Relation to Other Law).
