sections.title: Prohibited Magical Conduct

body.heading: § 300.8 Related Requirements; Prohibited Magical Conduct
body.text:
Nothing in this Part shall be construed to prohibit the lawful practice of magic where no threat to public safety or order exists. However, certain acts remain absolutely forbidden under any circumstance, regardless of claimed necessity or emergency. Such prohibited conduct includes but is not limited to the use of binding spells for extortion, compulsion rituals designed to manipulate free will, and transmutation techniques intended to create permanent slaves or puppets. See § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting regarding the ethical obligations imposed upon all licensed mages.

The prohibition against magical slavery extends to any arrangement where a caster exerts dominant control over another's mind through sustained enchantment, thereby negating their capacity for autonomous decision-making. This includes, but is not limited to, the implantation of false memories or emotions, the installation of obedience triggers, and the alteration of personality traits in a manner that fundamentally undermines identity. Such practices violate core principles outlined in § 1.4 Persons Bound and are subject to immediate revocation of licensure under § 200.2 Apprentice Limits by analogy.

Furthermore, any magical act performed with the explicit intent of causing prolonged physical suffering or debilitating injury constitutes abuse prohibited by both common law and statutory provisions. While defensive magic remains permissible within reason, offensive spells designed solely for inflicting pain without tactical necessity fall outside the scope of authorized practice. This principle aligns with § 1.7 Construction: Aggregation of Conduct, which requires examination of the totality of circumstances when determining culpability.

All mages shall adhere to these prohibitions absolutely and without exception. Failure to do so may result in disciplinary action ranging from suspension of license to permanent expulsion from the Guild, depending on severity. Violation of these core ethical standards undermines the very foundation upon which responsible magical practice rests, and must therefore be met with the sternest response available under current law. See also § 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate regarding conflicts between overlapping regulations.

body.heading: Prohibited Magical Conduct
body.text:
§ 300.8 shall govern all acts deemed inherently dangerous to the public welfare or to the fabric of reality itself, regardless of whether such conduct falls under an existing schedule of arts. No caster shall engage in any magical practice that knowingly risks catastrophic collateral damage, including but not limited to spontaneous combustion, dimensional breaches, temporal dislocations, or uncontrolled elemental eruptions. The burden of proof for establishing intent and foreseeability of harm rests with the accuser; mere recklessness is insufficient grounds for conviction under this section.

It shall be a defense sufficient to dismiss charges brought pursuant to § 300.8 if the accused can demonstrate that they were acting in accordance with a valid research permit issued by the Guild, provided such actions did not exceed the scope and parameters specified therein. This provision is intended to protect bona fide scholars from unwarranted prosecution while maintaining strict accountability for negligent or malicious misuse of magical powers. The Guild reserves the right to revoke any pending permits if there is credible evidence that the proposed research poses an unacceptable risk to public safety.

Casters found guilty of violating § 300.8 shall face punitive measures commensurate with the severity and consequences of their offenses, ranging from fines and suspension of licensure to permanent revocation of magical abilities and imprisonment at the discretion of the Presiding Magistrate. Repeat offenders shall be subject to enhanced penalties, including mandatory re-education under supervision and restitution for any damages incurred as a result of their unlawful activities. In cases where the accused refuses to comply with these sanctions, the Guild may petition the local courts for additional enforcement measures within the bounds of applicable law.

This section is without prejudice to all other provisions herein contained or in force elsewhere, and shall be construed liberally to effectuate its remedial purposes. The undersigned hereby ratify and confirm this article as an integral component of the Autumnwood Accords, binding upon themselves and their successors forevermore. Signed, sealed, and delivered in triplicate on this day and year first above written, attested by witnesses duly appointed for that purpose.

body.heading: Prohibited Magical Conduct — Continued
body.text:
§ 300.8 Related Requirements
Under no circumstances shall any licenced caster engage in the practice of necromancy, blood magic, or other forbidden arts as defined by § 300.2 and the Quiet List. Violation of this prohibition constitutes a felony under the Accords and subjects the offender to immediate seizure of magical ability via seal-magic or confinement within a pocket dimension at the discretion of the Aegis Magi. The Guild maintains strict oversight over all research involving potent or unstable spells, requiring express permission from the Conservators prior to commencing any such studies under § 400.1 and related sections. Unauthorized experimentation with forbidden magic shall be treated as an act of war against the state, punishable by total magical forfeiture and permanent exile from Autumn Wood. All casters are required to maintain detailed logs of their professional activities, including spell components, casting locations, and client identities, for inspection upon reasonable demand by Guild officials. Failure to comply with these record-keeping mandates may result in suspension of licensure pending investigation into potential violations of the Prohibited Arts statutes. The Guild further reserves the right to conduct surprise inspections of caster workplaces and residences to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations concerning magical practice. Any resistance to such lawful examinations shall be deemed an aggravating factor for sentencing purposes under existing penal codes governing magic crimes. Casters found guilty of breaching the Prohibited Conduct provisions face not only criminal sanctions but also civil liability for any damages incurred by third parties as a result of their illicit activities. The severe penalties imposed herein reflect the Guild's unwavering commitment to maintaining public safety and preventing the misuse of dangerous magical powers that could threaten the stability of society at large.

body.heading: § 300.8 Related Requirements; Prohibited Magical Conduct, Prohibited Magical Con
body.text:
§ 300.8 Prohibition on Unauthorized Arcane Alterations to Living Beings. No caster shall, without express consent and a written waiver signed by the subject or their legal guardian, perform any magical procedure that alters the fundamental biology, physiology, or psychological state of another sentient being. This prohibition encompasses but is not limited to transmutation rituals aimed at physical enhancement, memory modification spells, charm effects exceeding a duration of one hour, and any form of mind-control or personality rewriting. Exceptions may be made only by the Arcane Medical Board under strict regulatory oversight for therapeutic purposes. Violations shall constitute Class A Felony Magic Offenses subject to immediate arrest and trial before the High Council on Magical Ethics. See § 1401.5 Prohibited Acts, § 200.3 Unauthorized Enhancements, § 1101.6 Bodily Autonomy Rights.

§ 300.9 Restrictions on Mass Magic and Area-of-Effect Spells. Casters employing spells with radius of effect exceeding five meters or capable of affecting multiple targets simultaneously shall obtain prior written approval from the Guild's Spell Control Division. Such authorization requires proof that adequate safeguards have been implemented to prevent collateral harm to bystanders, property damage beyond reasonable necessity, and environmental contamination through magical residue. Failure to secure proper permits renders the use of such spells illegal regardless of intent or outcome. Penalties for unauthorized mass magic include immediate suspension of licensure pending investigation, mandatory remediation at offender's expense, and potential permanent revocation of casting privileges. See § 500.2 Crowd Control Protocols, § 600.3 Public Safety Measures, § 800.5 Environmental Impact Assessments.

§ 300.10 Prohibition on Magical Slavery and Bondage Enslavement Devices. It shall be unlawful to create, maintain, or utilize any magical construct, enchantment, or ritual device designed to enforce total bodily submission, mind control without exception clauses, or permanent servitude upon another sentient being against their will. Such practices violate the core tenets of personhood enshrined in § 1.4 Persons Bound and constitute egregious abuse under both civil and criminal law. Offenders face harsh penalties including indefinite prison sentences, confiscation of all magical items, and mandatory psychiatric evaluation for potential re-offending risk. Exceptions apply only where such devices are employed temporarily by certified professionals for legitimate medical or security purposes under strict supervision. See § 1201.4 Human Dignity Rights, § 900.3 Prohibition on Forced Labor, § 700.8 Abuse Prevention Measures.

§ 300.11 Ban on Experimental Magic Without Proper Oversight. No caster shall engage in unvetted experimentation with new or modified spells outside of officially sanctioned research facilities equipped with appropriate containment measures and emergency protocols. Unauthorized testing of novel magical theories poses unacceptable risks to public safety and environmental integrity. All innovative spellcraft must undergo rigorous peer review by the Guild's Innovation Committee prior to field deployment. Violators risk severe sanctions ranging from temporary suspension to permanent disqualification from practicing magic within Guild jurisdiction. See § 400.1 Research Permit Requirements, § 300.5 Controlled Experiments, § 200.7 Safety Standards for Spell Development.

This section establishes critical boundaries regarding the ethical application of magical powers, emphasizing respect for individual autonomy and public welfare above all else. Strict adherence to these prohibitions ensures responsible stewardship of arcane arts while preventing potential catastrophes arising from reckless experimentation or abuse of power. Any suspected violations shall be reported promptly to appropriate authorities for investigation and enforcement action as warranted by the circumstances involved. For further guidance on lawful magical practices, consult official Guild manuals or seek counsel directly from licensed professionals qualified in relevant specialties. Compliance with these mandates remains a non-negotiable obligation for all registered casters operating within Autumnwood territory. See § 1301.4 Ethical Guidelines for Caster Conduct, § 500.6 Responsibility to Society at Large, § 900.2 Abuse Prevention Initiatives.

[ARCHIVE CARD: "The Heartstone Incident - A Cautionary Tale"]
*In 1897, rogue mages attempted to harness the raw power of an unstable rift beneath Autumnwood for profit. Their hubris nearly destroyed the town when a poorly contained explosion leveled half the district and left dozens wounded. The ensuing inquiry led to harsher regulations on field magic, including this very clause prohibiting unauthorized area-of-effect spells. Always remember: with great power comes great responsibility...*

[ARCHIVE CARD: "Magic Abuse Statistics"]
*Recent reports indicate a 15% increase in cases involving prohibited magical alterations to living subjects over the past decade. While many instances involve consensual enhancement, a disturbing number appear to stem from malicious intent or gross negligence. The Arcane Medical Board urges all citizens to remain vigilant against suspicious offers of "miracle cures" or unrealistic physical transformations.*

[ARCHIVE CARD: "Enforcement Priorities"]
*The Guild dedicates significant resources to monitoring compliance with these prohibitions, utilizing advanced surveillance techniques and informant networks. Repeat offenders face swift and severe consequences, including permanent exile from magical practice entirely. Our mission is clear: protect the innocent while enabling responsible innovation within established boundaries.*

[ARCHIVE CARD: "Citizen Resources"]
*Victims of illegal magic abuse may seek assistance through multiple channels: filing formal complaints directly with local law enforcement, contacting the Guild's Victim Support Division for counseling and legal aid, or consulting independent experts specializing in magical forensics. Early reporting greatly enhances chances of successful prosecution and full restitution.*

[ARCHIVE CARD: "Future Outlook"]
*As magical technology continues advancing rapidly, so too must our regulatory framework evolve to address emerging challenges effectively. Ongoing dialogue between industry stakeholders, academic institutions, and public representatives remains essential for crafting balanced policies serving both progress and protection alike.*

body.heading: § 300.8 Prohibited Magical Conduct — Continued
body.text:
§ 300.9 The Ban on Blood Magic
Under no circumstances shall any practitioner engage in the ritualistic use of blood magic or vivisection for magical effect, a prohibition codified at § 1250 et seq. Such practices are deemed inherently barbaric and antithetical to civilized society. Violators face immediate suspension of licensure and referral to disciplinary panels for potential permanent revocation. See also § 300.6 Related Requirements; § 400.1 Research Permits.

body.heading: § 300.9 Unsanctioned Divination Practices
body.text: Divination arts, including scrying and fortune-telling, remain strictly regulated under the auspices of the Divination Council established by Resolution 87-B. Unauthorized practice constitutes a Class D infraction subject to fines up to one thousand gold crowns per offense. Exceptions may be granted for academic research purposes upon approval from the Ethics Committee, which shall evaluate each proposed study on a case-by-case basis in accordance with established guidelines set forth in § 2105 et seq. For further details regarding permitted divination activities, consult § 300.7 Related Requirements; § 1401.4 Related Requirements.

body.heading: § 300.9 Alchemical Safety Standards
body.text: All alchemical laboratories must adhere to rigorous safety protocols outlined in the National Laboratory Code of Practice (NLCOP), including proper ventilation systems, blast-resistant containment units, and emergency shutdown mechanisms capable of neutralizing runaway reactions within milliseconds. Failure to comply with these mandates may result in immediate closure of offending facilities until rectification is completed to satisfaction of the Bureau of Hazardous Materials Control. Regular inspections shall be conducted quarterly by certified inspectors appointed by the Guildmaster's office. Detailed provisions regarding alchemical safety are contained herein at § 1502 et seq.; see also § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters.

body.heading: § 300.9 Magical Weaponry Restrictions
body.text: The manufacture, sale, and possession of enchanted weapons remain subject to strict oversight by the Bureau of Controlled Substances and Dangerous Goods. Any individual wishing to acquire a magical firearm or edged instrument must first obtain a Special Possession Permit (SPP) from the appropriate regional authority, demonstrating both financial solvency and moral character through background checks and references. Violation of these regulations may lead to revocation of said permit and subsequent criminal charges under applicable state laws governing dangerous items. For complete guidance on acquiring lawful magical arms, refer to § 1605 et seq.; consult additionally § 300.4 Reclassification; § 700.2 Taxation of Magical Goods.

sections.brief: Prohibited Magical Conduct

sections.title: Research Integrity and Oversight

body.heading: § 400.6 Related Requirements - Research Integrity and Oversight
body.text:
The granting of any research permit under these Accords shall be predicated upon the applicant's submission of a comprehensive proposal detailing the intended scope, methodology, risks, and potential societal impacts of the proposed inquiry. This proposal must undergo rigorous peer review by at least three independent scholars of standing in the relevant field, none of whom shall have conflicts of interest with the applicant or their sponsors. Only upon approval of this vetting process may a formal permit be issued, specifying precise parameters such as duration, location, and acceptable methods of data collection.

Throughout the course of any sanctioned research endeavor, the lead principal investigator bears an affirmative duty to maintain strict adherence to all stipulated conditions and safety protocols. Any material deviation from approved procedures without prior written consent constitutes grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of the permit, at the sole discretion of the desk's oversight committee. Furthermore, all raw data generated during such investigations must be preserved in its original form for a minimum period of five years following project completion, to facilitate future audit and replication efforts should they become necessary.

In exceptional circumstances where unforeseen complications arise that threaten public safety or ethical norms, the principal investigator is obligated to notify the desk without delay via secure transmission channels. Such notifications shall include full particulars regarding the nature of the incident, any injuries sustained, and corrective measures already implemented. Failure to promptly report adverse events may result in escalated disciplinary action against both the individual responsible and their employing institution. Ultimately, it remains paramount that all magical research conducted under these provisions serves the greater good while minimizing harm to sentient beings and the natural order at large."

"see § 1401.6 Related Requirements; see § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items; see § 900.6 Related Requirements"

body.heading: Research Oversight and Integrity Standards
body.text: Under § 400.6, all research conducted under permit must maintain rigorous integrity standards to prevent abuse or accidental catastrophe. This includes mandatory logging of procedures, outcomes, and any anomalous effects observed during testing. Failure to comply with these reporting obligations may result in immediate revocation of the researcher's credentials and referral for disciplinary action. Furthermore, independent peer review panels shall be convened quarterly to audit all active research projects for compliance with safety protocols and ethical guidelines. Any suspected misconduct must be reported forthrightly to the Conservators' oversight committee for investigation. The Guild remains committed to fostering an environment where innovation can flourish responsibly, free from corruption or negligence that could endanger both caster and community alike. As stated in § 1.7(c), "the safety of the public takes precedence over all other considerations," a principle echoed throughout these provisions designed to safeguard our delicate magical ecosystem.

As stated in § 1.7(c), "the safety of the public takes precedence over all other considerations," a principle echoed throughout these provisions designed to safeguard our delicate magical ecosystem.

body.heading: Research Oversight and Integrity Standards — Continued
body.text:
§ 400.6 Related Requirements - Research Oversight and Integrity Standards, Related Requirements - Research Oversight and Integrity

No research permit shall be issued without concurrent approval from the Ethics Board established under § 150.2, whose mandate is to ensure that all sanctioned magical inquiry adheres to ethical norms and does not endanger public welfare or ecological balance. The Board shall review proposals for potential hazards, including but not limited to unintended temporal disruptions, psychic contamination of local populations, or destabilization of ambient mana fields. Approval may be granted conditionally, with stipulations imposed on the scope, duration, and containment measures of permitted experiments.

All research facilities must maintain detailed logs of activities conducted therein, accessible for audit by Guild inspectors at reasonable times. These records shall include raw data, observations, anomalies encountered, and corrective actions taken. Failure to comply may result in suspension or revocation of operating privileges under § 1203.4(a)(iii). Furthermore, any researcher found guilty of falsifying results, sabotaging equipment, or otherwise compromising the integrity of their work faces automatic disqualification from future licensing examinations, per § 809.5(b).

In cases where research yields unexpected or dangerous outcomes, the lead principal investigator has a duty to promptly report such incidents to both the Ethics Board and the Aegis Magi for assessment and remediation. Concealment of adverse events shall be deemed gross negligence and punishable as academic misconduct under § 1605.2(d). Conversely, timely disclosure enabling swift containment may mitigate penalties imposed upon responsible parties.

The Guild reserves the right to conduct periodic unannounced inspections of all active research sites to verify compliance with safety protocols and ethical guidelines. Access shall be granted without prior notice upon presentation of valid credentials issued under § 104.8. Refusal to cooperate constitutes obstruction of justice and may lead to immediate termination of associated permits, pursuant to § 1203.7(c). Any violations discovered during such audits will be prosecuted according to the procedures outlined in § 901 et seq., with appropriate sanctions enforced as warranted by circumstances.

This framework balances the pursuit of magical knowledge with necessary safeguards against abuse and harm, reflecting the Guild's enduring commitment to responsible stewardship of arcane arts for the greater good." see §§ 150.2, 809.5(b), 1605.2(d)

body.heading: Research Oversight and Integrity Standards — Continued — Continued
body.text:
§ 400.6 Related Requirements - Research Integrity and Oversight, Research Oversight and Integrity Standards — Continued

Under § 1.7, the Accords are interpreted to ensure that magical research neither endangers public safety nor violates fundamental ethical principles. As such, all research conducted under a permit must undergo periodic review by an independent oversight committee comprising conservators, innovators, and neutral observers. These committees shall assess adherence to prescribed protocols and evaluate potential risks associated with continued experimentation. Failure to comply may result in suspension of the researcher's privileges or revocation of their license entirely, see § 200.4.

Furthermore, § 300.2 mandates that any work involving necromantic arts be subject to additional scrutiny and strict containment measures. Such studies shall only proceed within specially designated facilities equipped with appropriate safeguards against accidental release or misuse. Violations of these requirements constitute serious breaches of the Accords and may lead to severe penalties up to and including sealing of magical capabilities, pursuant to § 1401.5.

In addition, researchers must maintain accurate records of all experimental procedures, results, and observations for inspection by guild authorities upon request. This includes logging any anomalies or unexpected effects encountered during testing. Such documentation serves both as a safeguard against negligence and as a resource for future investigations into emerging magical phenomena, under § 100.4.

Finally, § 1.8 stipulates that the provisions of this Part remain in full force and effect notwithstanding any conflicting state or local laws, unless expressly superseded by subsequent amendments to the Accords themselves. The supremacy of these regulations ensures consistent enforcement across all jurisdictions where the Guild holds jurisdictional authority, preserving both magical safety and regulatory integrity throughout the realm.

body.heading: Research Integrity and Oversight Protocols
body.text:
§ 400.8 Related Requirements - Research Integrity and Oversight, Research Oversight and Integrity Standards

All research conducted under the auspices of the Guild shall adhere to strict integrity standards as outlined in this section. First, all researchers must maintain detailed logs of their experiments, including hypotheses, methodologies, results, and any deviations from the approved protocol. These records shall be subject to random audits by the Aegis Magi to ensure compliance with safety guidelines and ethical norms. Second, researchers are prohibited from falsifying data or manipulating outcomes in a manner that compromises the validity of their findings. Any instance of fraud will result in immediate revocation of research permits and potential expulsion from the Guild. Third, all hazardous materials used in experiments must be properly stored, labeled, and disposed of according to established environmental regulations. Failure to do so may expose both the researcher and surrounding communities to undue risk. Fourth, researchers are encouraged but not required to share their findings with peer groups for review and critique. However, any publication of results must include full disclosure of funding sources and potential conflicts of interest. Finally, this section shall be construed liberally in favor of public safety and scientific advancement, provided that such interpretation does not undermine the integrity of the research process itself. See § 200.3 Temporary Mouths for provisions regarding guest researchers; under § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth, unauthorized replication of protected specimens is strictly prohibited."

"Research Integrity and Oversight Protocols — Continued
This section establishes comprehensive guidelines to uphold the highest standards of scientific inquiry within the Guild's research facilities. All studies must be conducted with meticulous attention to detail, transparency, and ethical responsibility. Researchers are expected to foster a culture of accountability by actively participating in peer reviews and constructive criticism. Furthermore, any suspected misconduct shall be reported promptly through established channels for investigation and disciplinary action if warranted."

"By adhering to these protocols, the Guild ensures that its research endeavors contribute positively to magical theory and practical application while safeguarding against potential abuses or accidents. The integrity of scientific pursuit remains paramount in maintaining public trust and advancing knowledge responsibly."

sections.title: Provenance and Authenticity

body.heading: Provenance and Authenticity
body.text:
§ 900.8 Related Requirements
In furtherance of the Accords' comprehensive regulatory framework, this section details ancillary obligations applicable to all licensed practitioners regardless of specialization or rank. These stipulations serve as universal baseline expectations for professional conduct and administrative compliance within the Guild's jurisdictional sphere.

All licensees shall maintain accurate records of every casting performed under their authority, including client identification, purpose, method employed, and outcomes achieved. Such documentation must be retained for a minimum period of five years from date of service, unless superseded by longer retention mandates imposed by specific sub-regulations or special circumstances warranting extended archival periods. Failure to preserve requisite records may constitute grounds for disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure status, depending on severity of omission and resultant impact upon Guild integrity or public safety interests.

When engaging in commercial transactions involving magical goods or services, practitioners must disclose any inherent risks associated with their craft prior to entering binding agreements with clients or partners alike. This disclosure obligation extends beyond mere verbal notification; written advisories detailing potential hazards should be furnished whenever feasible under the circumstances. Concealment of material dangers may expose violators to enhanced penalties proportional to degree of deception utilized in procuring consent for risky operations deemed unsuitable without full informed understanding by all parties involved.

Practitioners are further required to promptly report any incidents resulting from their professional activities, whether arising directly from casting errors or indirectly through unforeseen consequences triggered downstream from initial spellwork endeavors. Immediate notification must be provided upon discovery of adverse events affecting persons, property, or natural systems, enabling timely investigation and mitigation efforts before conditions deteriorate beyond manageable limits imposed by existing safeguards established throughout the Guild's regulatory apparatus.

Finally, all licensed casters agree to cooperate fully with any inquiries conducted pursuant to lawful authority, providing such information as reasonably requested necessary for verifying compliance with applicable statutes and regulations governing their respective fields of expertise within scope of official duties assigned hereinby competent oversight bodies empowered by virtue thereof under terms set forth in this Code duly enacted into force upon ratification by majority vote at next scheduled session of Autumnwood Accords Convention duly convened thereafter.

This section shall be construed liberally to effectuate purposes underlying entire body of laws comprising present codification efforts aimed at securing public welfare through effective regulation of magical practices conducted within territorial boundaries subject to direct supervisory control exercised hereby on behalf of sovereign state interests protected by aforementioned provisions contained herein with binding force upon all persons operating under authority granted pursuant hereto.

see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 400.3 Borrowed Hours; see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value
under § 900.8 Related Requirements, practitioners must adhere to strict record-keeping standards while maintaining transparency regarding inherent risks and promptly reporting any adverse outcomes stemming from their professional engagements within the Guild's regulatory framework designed to safeguard public safety and uphold ethical practices across all magical disciplines subject to oversight herein.

body.heading: § 900.8 Related Requirements — Continued
body.text:
Duty to Disclose Material Enchantments and Defects. Any mage seeking licensure under these Accords shall truthfully disclose all material enchantments, curses, or defects known to them regarding any artifact they submit for evaluation. Concealment of such information shall constitute grounds for immediate revocation of the applicant's credentials and subsequent sanctions under § 1201.4. This duty extends to both original creators and resellers of magical items, ensuring that all parties involved in commerce maintain full transparency concerning potential hazards. Failure to comply may result in permanent disqualification from Guild practice.

Record Retention and Access Standards. All official records maintained by the Autumnwood Accords Desk shall be retained for a minimum period of ten (10) years unless otherwise specified by law or regulation. These archives shall remain accessible upon written request by licensed mages, investigators, or authorized representatives of other relevant bodies, subject to appropriate security protocols and fees as outlined in § 900.4. Digital copies may be generated at the discretion of the Desk for archival purposes but shall not supplant original documents. Any alterations made to official records must be duly noted and certified by two (2) senior clerks or equivalent authorities.

Identification and Authentication Fees Structure. Fees associated with identification procedures shall vary according to complexity, risk level, and resource utilization as determined by the Conservators. Base rates for standard evaluations are set forth in Schedule A attached hereto, while specialized examinations may incur additional charges based on scope of work performed. Payment must be made prior to commencement of services unless explicitly waived or deferred under extraordinary circumstances approved by the Desk. Refunds will only be granted upon completion of all required steps and fulfillment of contractual obligations outlined in each individual agreement.

Provenance Verification Protocols for Antiques and Relics. When assessing historical artifacts submitted for appraisal, mages must exhaustively investigate their origins using available databases, cross-referencing with known patterns of forgery or tampering typical to the era concerned. Any suspicions raised during preliminary inspection warrant further scrutiny before final determination can be rendered conclusively. Special attention should be paid to subtle anomalies suggesting artificial enhancement beyond natural capabilities inherent in such objects' age alone. Comprehensive reporting on findings shall accompany every certified assessment issued forthwith thereafter pursuant hereto contained hereinabove within this codified framework governing lawful magical practice today across all realms known unto us all now and forevermore amen so it is written thus we decree under seal of truth eternal!

body.heading: § 900.8 Related Requirements — Provenance and Authenticity
body.text:
§ 900.8 Related Requirements; Authentication of Magical Artifacts
In order to maintain the integrity of the magical record, all artifacts submitted for registration shall bear a unique identifier mark affixed by the filing clerk using an iridescent ink pen of the Guild's manufacture. This mark serves both as proof of official acceptance and as a deterrent against counterfeiting or misrepresentation. Any artifact lacking such identification shall be deemed invalid for all purposes under these Accords unless accompanied by written verification from the original creator bearing their personal seal.

Furthermore, parties submitting artifacts for sale, trade, or transfer must declare in writing any known defects, limitations, or hidden enchantments affecting the item's value or safety. Failure to make full disclosure shall constitute fraud and subject the offending party to immediate revocation of licensure and potential criminal prosecution under existing statutes regarding deceptive commercial practices. The Guild reserves the right to order independent appraisal at its sole discretion when suspicious circumstances arise during routine inspection, with all costs borne by the registrant unless negligence is proven.

Last but not least, owners of registered artifacts are reminded that possession does not confer absolute title or immunity from seizure under certain conditions outlined herein. Specifically, the Guild retains a perpetual lien on any item bearing its authentication mark should outstanding debts fail to be satisfied within thirty days of notice. This clause ensures continued compliance with fiscal obligations without compromising ownership rights otherwise vested in lawful holders thereof. It is incumbent upon all participants to familiarize themselves thoroughly with these provisions prior to engaging in any transaction involving magical goods subject to regulation under this Code.

see § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; see § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items; see § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth.

body.heading: § 900.8 Related Requirements — Chain of Custody and Integrity
body.text:
The Accords mandate that all items entering the official record must maintain an unbroken chain of custody to ensure their integrity and authenticity. This requirement extends beyond simple possession, encompassing a full audit trail from acquisition through storage and eventual disposition. Any gaps in this documentation render the item suspect and subject to further scrutiny or rejection outright.

Provenance is paramount in determining both value and legal status of magical artifacts. Detailed records must be kept regarding each transfer of ownership, noting date, location, witnesses, and any associated transactions or payments. These logs serve multiple critical functions: they establish legitimate title, prevent fraud or forgery, and provide a historical account of the artifact's journey through time. Failure to maintain such meticulous documentation undermines confidence in the entire regulatory framework.

Special attention must be paid to items with contested histories or those acquired under dubious circumstances. Extraordinary diligence is required to verify their lawful origin before acceptance into the official archives. When doubts arise, independent verification by qualified appraisers may be necessary to resolve uncertainties. Until such validation is complete, disputed objects remain in limbo pending further review.

Ultimately, preserving the purity and reliability of the Guild's records depends upon strict adherence to these custodial obligations at every stage. Only through unwavering commitment to these standards can the Accords fulfill their purpose as a trustworthy guide for all who wield magic within its bounds. Neglect of this duty compromises everything from individual safety to societal stability itself.

body.heading: § 900.8 Related Requirements - Authentication and Verification Protocols
body.text:
The authentication and verification of filed magical items constitutes a critical component of the Guild's regulatory framework, ensuring both public safety and fiscal integrity. Under § 900.6, all submitted artifacts must undergo rigorous examination by a panel of qualified assessors prior to official registration. This evaluation encompasses not only technical analysis but also historical provenance research, cross-referencing against existing records to detect potential fraud or duplication.

Assessors are tasked with determining the true nature and capabilities of each item, distinguishing between genuine enchantments and mere illusions or imitations. Specialized equipment and controlled testing environments facilitate this process, minimizing risk to both assessors and public safety. All findings must be meticulously documented in the permanent archives, creating an immutable record for future reference.

In cases where authentication proves ambiguous or contested, appeals may be lodged with the Full Council within thirty days of initial determination. Such reviews shall proceed expeditiously, prioritizing resolution while maintaining impartiality. The Guild's commitment to transparent and fair evaluation procedures serves as a cornerstone of its mission to foster responsible magical innovation while safeguarding societal interests.

Through these comprehensive protocols, the Autumnwood Accords Desk upholds its mandate as the preeminent authority on magical artifacts within the region. By enforcing strict standards for authentication and verification, the Guild protects both consumers and practitioners from deceptive practices. This vigilant oversight ensures that only legitimate items enter circulation, preserving the integrity of the magical marketplace while promoting safe exploration of arcane disciplines.

body.heading: § 900.8 Related Requirements — Authentication and Verification Protocols
body.text:
All filings submitted to the Autumnwood Accords Desk shall undergo rigorous authentication prior to acceptance into official records. This process ensures the integrity, authenticity, and legal admissibility of all archived materials. Failure to comply with these protocols may result in rejection of the filing and potential sanctions against the submitting party.

Authentication begins with visual inspection by a qualified Guild assessor, who examines physical characteristics such as paper quality, ink composition, handwriting style, and any magical signatures or enchantments present on the document. These features are compared against known samples from the same author or era to verify consistency and origin. Digital scans or photographs may also be subjected to forensic analysis where applicable.

Once visually inspected, each item is subjected to a series of standardized tests designed to detect tampering or forgery. These include spectral imaging to reveal hidden markings or alterations, chemical swabbing for trace residue detection, and specialized equipment capable of identifying synthetic materials disguised as authentic artifacts. Any discrepancies or anomalies discovered during testing must be immediately reported to the Desk Clerk in writing, accompanied by supporting evidence and a detailed explanation thereof.

For particularly complex cases requiring expert testimony or additional analysis, the Guild may engage independent specialists at its own expense. Such evaluations will be conducted impartially and their findings made available to all interested parties upon request. Results of these comprehensive assessments form an integral part of the final authentication report submitted alongside the original filing.

Only after successfully passing all applicable checks shall a document be deemed "fully authenticated" and eligible for official archiving under this Codebook's provisions. This stringent vetting process serves as the cornerstone of trust within our system, ensuring that every piece of information preserved herein meets the highest standards of accuracy and reliability demanded by law.

In matters involving high-stakes disputes or novel technologies where precedent is scarce, extra diligence shall be applied to validate submissions beyond ordinary scrutiny levels. The ultimate goal remains unwavering: safeguarding against deception while facilitating transparent exchange of knowledge across generations of mages bound by these sacred vows.

sections.title: Compensation and Debt Settlement

body.heading: Compensation and Debt Settlement
body.text:
The provisions enumerated herein are ancillary to the primary prohibitions set forth in §§ 500.1 through 500.7 and must be read as an integral whole. No single clause may be construed in isolation without regard for the context provided by neighboring sections, lest it lead to absurd or unjust results contrary to the spirit of the Accords. The Conservators maintain that these related requirements serve a vital protective function, filling gaps where literal interpretation would otherwise allow loopholes to form and undermine the integrity of magical regulation across all realms.

Specifically, § 500.8(a) establishes that any act falling within the purview of the prohibited categories outlined in §§ 500.1–500.7 shall be deemed a violation regardless of motive or intent, provided there is evidence of purposeful action toward achieving a forbidden end. This strict liability standard reflects the inherent dangers posed by unregulated arcane practices and ensures that negligent behavior does not escape punishment simply because it lacked malicious foresight. The Desk has repeatedly held that ignorance of the law is no excuse in matters concerning public safety, particularly where magical consequences may extend far beyond immediate participants.

Furthermore, § 500.8(b) clarifies that violations committed outside the jurisdictional bounds of Autumn Wood shall nevertheless be subject to enforcement under these Accords if they directly impact Guild interests or threaten regional stability. This extraterritorial reach is necessary given the fluid nature of magical phenomena and the difficulty of predicting where an incident may originate versus where its effects will manifest. The Aegis Magi are authorized to pursue offenders across borders without impediment, exercising full investigative powers as granted by sovereign decree.

Finally, § 500.8(c) mandates that all prosecutions arising from breaches of these related requirements shall be conducted expeditiously to minimize disruption to lawful commerce and daily life. Unwarranted delays or frivolous appeals will not be tolerated and may result in sanctions against the responsible parties. Prompt adjudication serves both practical and symbolic functions, affirming the supremacy of the Accords while maintaining public confidence in the system's fairness and efficiency. It is the solemn duty of every citizen to comply with these obligations lest they invite swift and severe repercussions upon themselves and their communities alike.

body.heading: § 500.8 Related Requirements: Compensation and Debt Settlement
body.text:
§ 500.9 Magic as Collateral and Payment

The use of magical services may constitute valid consideration in the settlement of debts, provided certain safeguards are observed to prevent exploitation or fraud. Under this provision, a caster's lawful application of magic may be accepted by a creditor as partial or full repayment of an obligation owed. However, the value attributed to such magical work must be objectively determined through appraisal by certified magisters familiar with the specific arts employed and their market rates at the time of performance.

Where a debtor offers magical services in lieu of monetary payment, a written contract shall govern the transaction, specifying the exact scope of services rendered and the corresponding debt reduction or cancellation. Such agreements are binding upon both parties once executed, unless fraud, duress, or gross negligence can be proven on either side. Disputes arising from these arrangements shall be adjudicated according to standard contractual principles, with magisters serving as expert witnesses regarding the quality and value of the magical work performed.

Creditors accepting magic in payment assume all risks associated with the casting, including but not limited to potential collateral damage, adverse health effects, or emotional distress resulting from unintended consequences. A debtor shall not be held liable for unforeseen outcomes beyond their reasonable control unless explicitly agreed upon in advance. Nevertheless, gross incompetence or willful misconduct by the caster may justify rescission of the agreement and refunding of any partial payments already made.

This provision stands as a recognition of magic's intrinsic economic value within society, while maintaining strict oversight to protect all parties from abuse. The Guild retains authority to investigate complaints arising from such transactions and impose penalties where violations are found. All contracts involving magical services shall be filed with the Accords Desk for record-keeping purposes, enabling future reference if necessary to resolve disputes or clarify obligations.

See § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 400.3 Borrowed Hours: Interest in Time; see § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill regarding proxy performance limitations.

body.heading: § 500.8 Compensation and Debt Settlement
body.text:
In instances where magical services are rendered in lieu of monetary payment, the resulting debt shall be quantified using standard arcane valuation tables maintained by the Guild Desk. Any dispute arising from such assessments shall be adjudicated by a three-member panel drawn from the Conservators, Innovators, and Aegis Magi respectively, whose ruling shall be final and binding. The debtor then possesses thirty (30) days to satisfy the obligation through either cash settlement or equivalent magical goods of verified quality. Failure to comply within this window permits immediate seizure of assets deemed sufficient to cover the outstanding balance under § 1201.4 Enforcement Provisions.

Furthermore, all compensation transactions involving magical services must be documented on official Guild forms and filed with the appropriate regional office for auditing purposes. This ensures transparency in market rates and prevents fraudulent inflation of service values by unscrupulous practitioners seeking to enrich themselves at the expense of honest laborers. Violations of these record-keeping mandates shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure, depending on severity. The Desk reserves sole authority to approve any alternative payment methods not explicitly enumerated herein, granting nothing by implication or prior course of dealing contrary to this express provision.

Finally, creditors holding claims against magisters for unpaid magical services may petition the Guild for garnishment of future earnings and liquid assets upon proof of default. Such petitions require full disclosure of all known financial holdings and a sworn affidavit detailing efforts made to collect voluntarily before resorting to legal compulsion. The Desk shall review each case on its merits, balancing the rights of the aggrieved party against protections afforded by § 1301.5 Due Process Guarantees. Any final judgment entered must be strictly limited to amounts owed as determined by the initial valuation and may not exceed twice that figure regardless of subsequent accruals or penalties imposed unilaterally by the creditor absent mutual agreement thereto.

§ 500.8 Related Requirements; see also §§ 1201.4 Enforcement Provisions, 1301.5 Due Process Guarantees, and 400.6 Specimen Custody for related valuation standards.

body.heading: § 500.8 Compensation and Debt Settlement via Arcane Services
body.text:
In the realm of magical commerce, where traditional currency often proves inadequate or unavailable, the Accords recognize the validity of settling debts through the rendering of arcane services. When a debtor lacks sufficient liquid assets to satisfy an obligation, they may petition the Guild for permission to offer specialized magical labor in lieu of cash payment. Such arrangements must be meticulously documented and approved by two independent assessors who verify both the nature of the service and its market value relative to the outstanding debt. Commonly accepted offerings include spellcasting at discounted rates, consultation fees reduced to nominal sums, or temporary employment as a licensed operative under direct supervision.

However, this alternative method of settlement is subject to strict limitations designed to prevent exploitation and ensure fairness. No debtor may be compelled to engage in activities beyond their skill level or safety limits, lest they risk further liability through incompetence or injury. Furthermore, services rendered must bear a reasonable correlation to the creditor's profession or interests; for instance, a merchant owed payment by a rogue mage might accept discounted magical repairs to their warehouse as satisfaction of debt, but would not be justified in demanding combat training unless explicitly agreed upon beforehand. The assessing magi retain sole discretion to reject proposals deemed unethical, impractical, or excessively hazardous to the provider's well-being.

Should disputes arise regarding the adequacy of service rendered or the accuracy of valuations assigned, either party may appeal directly to an appointed arbitration panel comprised of senior clerks and experienced practitioners familiar with both commercial standards and magical arts. The panel shall convene promptly upon request and render a binding decision based on evidence presented and applicable provisions of this Code. Until such determination is made, neither creditor nor debtor may unilaterally withhold further performance or escalate hostilities without risking sanctions for breach of contract or public order violations respectively. Through these mechanisms, the Guild aims to facilitate equitable resolution of financial disagreements while maintaining rigorous oversight over all magical transactions conducted within its jurisdiction.

body.heading: § 500.8 Compensation and Debt Settlement via Arcane Services — Continued
body.text:
Mages who provide unauthorized magical services for monetary gain shall not collect payment in the form of goods, labor, or other non-currency consideration unless expressly stipulated in a written contract approved by two Guild clerks. Any agreement violating this prohibition is void ab initio, rendering any attempted transfer of value null and unenforceable under these Accords. This rule applies regardless of whether the underlying magical act was lawful or unlawful, as it concerns only the permissible forms of compensation for professional services rendered within Guild jurisdiction.

The primary rationale behind this provision is to prevent economic exploitation and maintain the integrity of Guild licensing standards. When mages accept alternative payments instead of standard coinage, they expose themselves and their clients to unpredictable risks that may undermine public trust in the regulated magical marketplace. Furthermore, such arrangements often circumvent tax obligations and regulatory oversight, creating opportunities for corruption and black-market activity that threaten the stability of the entire arcane ecosystem.

Clerks reviewing contracts for compliance shall verify that all compensation clauses conform strictly to this section's requirements. Failure to adhere to these guidelines may result in disciplinary action against the offending mage, ranging from fines to suspension of licensure depending on the severity of the infraction. In cases where disputes arise regarding the nature or value of alternative consideration offered, an independent appraisal by a certified Guild assessor shall be conducted at mutual expense to determine fairness and legality under these statutes.

This rule serves as both a protective measure for consumers and a regulatory tool for maintaining order within the magical profession. By mandating transparent financial transactions, the Accords ensure that all parties engage in dealings with full awareness of their rights and obligations, thereby minimizing potential conflicts downstream. The Guild reserves broad discretion to enforce this provision through any means deemed necessary to safeguard public welfare and uphold the principles embodied herein.

Mages are reminded that adherence to these guidelines is not merely a legal formality but an ethical imperative inherent to their vocation. Those who choose to ignore them do so at their peril, inviting swift and severe consequences from both civil authorities and their fellow practitioners alike. Let it be known that the Autumnwood Accords stand as immutable pillars of justice and fairness, guiding all who walk this delicate path between creation and destruction.

body.heading: § 500.8 Compensation and Debt Settlement via Arcane Services — Administration
body.text:
§ 500.8 Compensation and Debt Settlement via Arcane Services

It is hereby provided that in lieu of traditional currency, debt obligations may be satisfied through the performance of specific arcane services as detailed herein. Such arrangements shall be entered into only upon written agreement signed by both parties and witnessed by a licensed clerk or Aegis Magi. Failure to fulfill agreed-upon duties constitutes default under § 500.1 and subjects the debtor to standard penalties for breach of contract.

Permitted services include, but are not limited to: conjuring elemental effects within enclosed spaces; providing temporary illusionary disguises lasting no longer than one solar cycle; casting non-permanent buff spells with duration capped at six hours per casting; and performing minor divinations such as scrying or localized augury. All such acts must be executed safely, without endangering life or property, in accordance with § 102.3 regarding responsible spellcasting practices.

Compensation rates shall be determined by the Guild's Compensation Committee based on factors including skill level required, risk involved, duration of service, and prevailing market conditions for similar magical labor. Agreed-upon fees must be paid promptly upon completion of tasks unless otherwise specified in writing. Unpaid services may be pursued as a civil claim under § 405 or converted to a lien against the debtor's assets pursuant to applicable statutes.

Parties electing this alternative method of payment acknowledge that they have fully considered all implications including potential hazards, ethical concerns, and legal liabilities inherent therein. By signing this agreement they waive any right to later contest validity based on lack of consideration or mutual assent, provided the underlying transaction was lawful at inception under § 201 et seq. Any disputes arising from interpretation of service terms shall be resolved by binding arbitration before a panel convened under Rules of Procedure XXIX-B.

This provision reflects the Guild's recognition that magic possesses intrinsic value beyond mere monetary measure and may appropriately function as a form of currency within regulated circumstances. Such flexibility benefits both creditors seeking efficient satisfaction of claims and debtors facing genuine hardship, while maintaining strict oversight to prevent abuse or exploitation. The Committee retains discretion to deny requests deemed contrary to public welfare or Guild interests under § 104.2(e).

sections.title: Compliance Obligations — §600.8

body.heading: § 600.8 Related Requirements and Compliance Obligations
body.text:
Nothing in this Part shall be construed to diminish or eliminate any existing obligations imposed upon licensees by virtue of their status as such, whether under common law principles, prior administrative orders, or other regulatory regimes applicable within the jurisdiction of this Guild. Any requirements not explicitly enumerated herein remain in full force unless expressly superseded by subsequent amendment. Licensees are responsible for maintaining awareness of all relevant laws and ordinances affecting their practice, regardless of publication status within these codified provisions. Failure to comply with such obligations may result in disciplinary action under applicable sections hereof or other legal remedies available to the Guild.

In particular, licensees must adhere strictly to any conditions attached to their individual permits or certificates of qualification issued by this authority. Such stipulations constitute binding contractual undertakings enforceable independently from statutory provisions. Breach thereof shall be deemed a violation of these Accords subject to appropriate sanctions. Furthermore, all licensed practitioners are expected to engage in continuous education regarding evolving standards of magical ethics and safety protocols as promulgated herein or through official channels designated by the Conservators' Council. Neglect of such duties may warrant revocation of licensure at the sole discretion of the governing body.

The provisions contained within this section operate cumulatively with those found elsewhere throughout these Accords, creating a comprehensive framework for regulating magical activity within the Autumnwood region. Nothing herein shall be interpreted to limit or otherwise affect any rights, powers, duties, liabilities, or immunities enjoyed by the Guild, its agents, officers, employees, or duly authorized representatives under existing law or custom. All obligations assumed hereunder are undertaken voluntarily and with full understanding of their scope and consequences by each licensee accepting such terms upon issuance of their credentials. Any ambiguities arising in application shall be resolved favorably toward protection of public welfare consistent with the overarching purposes set forth hereinabove.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 300.2 Necromancy and Unsanctioned Arts; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse of Authority
Under § 1.7 Construction provisions, this Part must be read harmoniously with the whole code to avoid internal contradictions or gaps in coverage. Where specific directives conflict with general principles, the former controls absent clear indication otherwise from competent authority. Any dispute concerning interpretation shall submit finally to binding arbitration by a panel appointed jointly by the disputing parties and the Guild Chairperson acting as neutral facilitator. Costs of proceedings borne equally unless manifest bad faith demonstrated by one side prompting equitable allocation thereof. Final arbitral awards unappealable except for plain error on face of record warranting immediate correction without prejudice to other claims asserted hereinunder or otherwise at law.

body.heading: § 600.9 Transitional Provisions and Grandfather Clauses
body.text:
Notwithstanding the foregoing, certain limited exceptions shall apply retroactively to protect vested interests acquired in good faith prior to effective date of these amended Accords. Specifically, individuals currently engaged in lawful magical practices without formal licensure may continue such activities for a period not exceeding ninety (90) days following enactment herein unless otherwise prohibited by separate order from the Conservators' Council upon review of individual circumstances presented thereto. Upon expiration of said grace period, all persons desiring to resume or expand their operations must obtain appropriate authorization pursuant to these updated regulations governing qualification standards and ongoing compliance obligations applicable uniformly across all jurisdictions subject to Guild oversight.

Furthermore, contracts entered into before passage hereof containing terms inconsistent herewith shall remain valid provided they do not contravene public policy considerations embodied within this legislation. Disputes arising therefrom subject to ordinary civil litigation procedures unless otherwise directed by court order or mutual agreement between contracting parties seeking alternative dispute resolution mechanisms consistent with applicable law and Guild interests. In no event shall any provision deemed invalid under these Accords affect the enforceability of remaining clauses which stand independently apart from said unenforceable provisions notwithstanding severance thereof.

Any ambiguities in this Part concerning temporal applicability or scope shall be construed narrowly against expanding liability beyond original intent expressed clearly at time of adoption. Where feasible, existing arrangements should be modified prospectively rather than retroactively where possible without impairing legitimate expectations fairly relied upon by affected parties acting reasonably under the circumstances presented to them prior to implementation hereof. Transitional rules designed solely to ease adjustment burden while preserving core regulatory objectives shall prevail over conflicting interpretations suggesting stricter application absent explicit contrary directive from duly constituted authorities empowered accordingly hereunder.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 300.4 Reclassification Procedures
Under § 1.8 Effective Date and Savings clauses, these provisions apply prospectively except where expressly stated otherwise creating implied waivers of prior rights inconsistent therewith. Nothing herein abrogates ongoing contractual duties owed by licensees under pre-existing agreements unless specifically revoked by competent authority pursuant to established cause-and-effect nexus demonstrated clearly upon proper notice given well in advance thereof allowing reasonable opportunity for cure absent willful misconduct warranting immediate termination without further warning issued previously hereunder or elsewhere as appropriate under governing laws applicable hereto.

FILED LORE:
- § 600.8 ensures licensees comply with all existing laws, not just Guild rules. They must stay educated on ethics and safety too. Breaking these can get you sanctioned.
- Exceptions exist for people already practicing legally before the new rules started. They get a short window to adjust or stop until they qualify properly. Contracts made before are okay unless they violate public good. Ambiguities should be read narrowly against expanding liability unfairly. The goal is easing the transition while keeping protections in place where needed most.
- Basically, don't let old habits die hard if they conflict with updated standards. But give folks a chance to adapt responsibly without punishing them for past actions done honestly under prior regimes. Balance is key here.

body.heading: § 600.8 Related Requirements and Compliance Obligations — Continued
body.text:
§ 600.8 shall not be construed as relieving any party of its independent duties to comply with applicable laws, rules, or regulations promulgated by the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Each signatory remains fully liable for ensuring that all acts performed under a Contract conform to both the express terms thereof and the overarching mandates set forth herein. Failure to adhere strictly to these dual obligations shall constitute grounds for immediate termination of the agreement and potential civil liability for breach of contract.

Furthermore, neither Party may assert any defense based on lack of knowledge or understanding regarding the provisions of this Codex or the specific requirements of their Contract. By entering into a binding agreement with a Caster, each signatory acknowledges that they have read, understood, and accepted these terms in full. Any attempt to claim ignorance or misrepresentation shall be deemed frivolous and will not preclude enforcement actions as provided herein.

It is incumbent upon both Parties to maintain accurate records of all transactions, communications, and performances arising from the Contract. Such documentation serves as critical evidence in any dispute resolution proceedings and must be made available promptly upon request by the other signatory or authorized investigators. Neglecting this duty may result in adverse inference against the negligent Party should a controversy arise regarding the facts at issue.

Finally, nothing contained in this section shall limit the inherent powers of the Autumnwood Accords Desk to investigate violations, impose penalties, or seek injunctive relief as deemed necessary to protect public safety and integrity. Compliance with § 600.8 is mandatory and non-negotiable for all Parties engaged within the scope of these regulations.

see §§ 1.4 Persons Bound, 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild, 300.3 Quiet List Procedure, 500.2 Unscheduled Weather. Under § 600.8, signatories retain independent compliance obligations beyond their contractual duties and must proactively monitor adherence to both specific terms and broader regulatory mandates to avoid liability. Failure to do so may trigger immediate contract termination and civil penalties for breach of agreement. Moreover, ignorance of the Codex's provisions affords no excuse; all parties acknowledge full acceptance upon signing. Meticulous record-keeping is essential for evidentiary purposes, and neglect thereof invites adverse inferences. Ultimately, this requirement complements the Desk's authority to enforce regulations vigorously safeguarding public welfare.

body.heading: § 600.8 Compliance Obligations and Enforcement Mechanisms
body.text:
Whereas the Accords impose affirmative duties upon all bound parties, failure to fulfill these obligations shall constitute grounds for immediate sanctions under applicable sections herein. Specifically, any caster failing to maintain required licensure or adhere to prescribed magical limits may be subject to revocation of privileges without prior notice. The Guild reserves discretion to initiate administrative proceedings ex parte where imminent danger is credibly alleged. Such actions shall not prejudice subsequent adjudication on the merits at trial by Arcane Duel should contested issues arise.

Furthermore, all casters shall submit quarterly reports detailing magical activities undertaken during the preceding quarter, including but not limited to spellwork performed, artifacts modified or created, and any incidents resulting in injury or property damage. These disclosures must be accompanied by supporting documentation such as receipts for materials purchased and sworn statements from witnesses present at relevant proceedings. Failure to provide complete and truthful reporting shall be deemed a serious breach of trust warranting disciplinary review.

Enforcement powers granted herein are cumulative and not exclusive thereof; nothing therein precludes the Guild from pursuing parallel civil or criminal remedies where appropriate under existing law. Conversely, rights conferred by these provisions may not be waived except in writing signed by the consenting party and witnessed by an impartial notary public duly commissioned within this realm. Any attempted circumvention of mandatory safeguards through subterfuge or collusion shall be treated as aggravated misconduct subject to enhanced penalties.

The ultimate goal of compliance mechanisms remains preservation of public safety while fostering responsible magical practice. Through diligent monitoring and timely intervention, the Guild seeks to minimize risks inherent in unregulated arcane experimentation while maximizing benefits accruing from lawful spellwork. By striking this delicate balance, all parties contribute to a stable society wherein magic serves as catalyst for progress rather than instrument of chaos.

body.heading: § 600.8 Compliance Obligations and Enforcement Mechanisms — Continued
body.text:
This Part establishes the comprehensive compliance framework required of all entities engaged in magical contracting activities under these Accords, detailing both affirmative duties and remedial consequences for non-compliance.

All parties to a contract shall maintain accurate records of all transactions, including but not limited to spell components employed, duration of casting, and any collateral effects observed. Such records must be retained for a minimum period of ten years from the date of final performance and made available upon reasonable request by Guild inspectors or authorized representatives. Failure to comply with this recordkeeping requirement constitutes a material breach of contract entitling the non-breaching party to terminate immediately and seek damages.

In the event of suspected fraud, misrepresentation, or other wrongdoing arising in connection with a magical service agreement, any aggrieved party may petition the Autumnwood Accords Desk for an investigation. Upon receipt of such petition, the Clerk shall convene a hearing within thirty days wherein evidence may be presented and witnesses examined under oath. The Presiding Magistrate shall issue findings of fact and conclusions of law based on all admissible testimony and exhibits. If misconduct is substantiated, appropriate sanctions shall be imposed pursuant to applicable provisions herein or as otherwise directed by the Desk in its discretion.

The Guild reserves the right to audit any facility where contracted magical services were rendered, with reasonable notice given unless exigent circumstances exist warranting immediate inspection without prior warning. Inspectors acting under color of law granted hereunder shall be afforded full access to all premises and materials relevant to their investigation subject only to protections against unreasonable searches mandated by prevailing legal standards. Any resistance to lawful inspection shall be deemed an aggravating factor in determining punitive relief available to the complainant.

For violations involving personal injury or property damage resulting from negligent or intentional misuse of contracted magical powers, affected parties may bring direct civil actions seeking compensatory and consequential damages as permitted at common law or under specifically applicable statutes. The existence of a contractual relationship between plaintiff and defendant shall not preclude such tort claims but rather serve to strengthen the case for causation and proximate connection between wrongful acts suffered harms sustained.

This Section aims to balance the interests of all stakeholders involved in magical commerce by providing clear guidelines for conduct while empowering those injured by breaches thereof with meaningful avenues for redress within a fair and efficient administrative process designed to uphold both justice and order throughout our realm governed hereby."

body.heading: § 600.8 Compliance Obligations and Enforcement Mechanisms — Administration
body.text:
Every contract entered into under the auspices of the Accords shall contain explicit compliance clauses detailing the obligations of each party to adhere to all applicable laws, regulations, and Guild standards throughout the duration of the agreement and for a reasonable period thereafter. Failure to comply with such obligations may result in immediate termination of the contract, forfeiture of any deposits or payments made, and potential legal action for breach of terms.

The Conservators maintain a comprehensive database of all active contracts involving magical services, which is updated regularly by licensed clerks and auditors. This system allows for swift identification and prosecution of non-compliant parties, thereby safeguarding the public interest and maintaining the integrity of the Guild's regulatory framework. Regular inspections and audits are conducted to ensure ongoing adherence to contractual obligations and safety protocols.

In addition to civil remedies available under common law, the Accords empower the Aegis Magi and other authorized enforcement agents to take immediate action against violators without prior notice or hearing. Such actions may include seizing property, imposing fines, suspending licenses, or initiating criminal proceedings where appropriate. The Guild reserves the right to act unilaterally in any matter deemed necessary to protect its interests and those of its members.

Transitional provisions and grandfather clauses shall be applied as needed to accommodate pre-existing arrangements that do not strictly conform to current regulations but pose no imminent threat to public safety or welfare. However, all such exceptions must be explicitly documented and subject to periodic review by the relevant oversight bodies. Any party benefiting from a grandfather clause agrees to voluntarily surrender such privileges upon written notice from the Guild authorities.

Enforcement of compliance obligations shall be carried out through established channels within the Guild's judicial system, utilizing its specialized tribunals equipped to handle complex disputes arising from magical contracts. These forums are designed to provide efficient, fair resolution while minimizing disruption to commercial activity and preserving valuable expertise where possible. Parties dissatisfied with initial rulings may appeal to higher authorities in accordance with due process guarantees enshrined in the Accords themselves.

Ultimately, strict compliance with all contractual requirements is essential for maintaining trust between casters and their clients, as well as ensuring the long-term viability of the magical services industry. By adhering diligently to these standards, practitioners demonstrate their professionalism and commitment to upholding the highest ideals of their craft under the watchful eye of the Guild's vigilant stewards.

see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; see § 400.5 Unauthorized Titan Growth; see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 700.3 Liability for Negligence
