sections.title: Definitions and Standards

body.heading: § 300.9 Related Requirements - Definitions and Standards
body.text:
The terms "necromancy," "blood magic," and "forbidden arts" as used herein shall be construed according to the schedules promulgated by the Conservator's Council, updated quarterly or upon significant discovery of new practices. Any magical technique involving direct manipulation of corpses, skeletal structures, or bone matter for offensive purposes falls under this definition unless expressly exempted by written resolution. See § 300.2 for further elaboration on specific prohibited schools and their rationales.

The "Quiet List" referenced in § 300.4 shall be maintained as a confidential register of particularly dangerous or controversial spells, accessible only to authorized researchers under strict supervision. Publication or recitation of these items outside official channels constitutes a Class A violation subject to immediate penal action under the Paradox Trial provisions. Breaches of this confidentiality requirement may result in permanent revocation of licensure and sealing of magical aptitude. Under § 900.7, any member found distributing Quiet List materials for profit shall be held jointly liable with their employer or patron organization.

Research into necromantic arts must always prioritize ethical considerations over experimental success, even when pursuing legitimate scientific inquiry. The safety of the public and surrounding communities takes precedence over individual curiosity or academic advancement. See § 400.3 regarding proper containment procedures for hazardous specimens during study periods. Failure to adhere to these guidelines shall be deemed gross negligence warranting disciplinary proceedings under Part III.

The Guild reserves the right to reclassify any magical technique from permitted to forbidden status with retroactive effect if new evidence demonstrates unacceptable risk to society at large. Such actions will be taken only after thorough review by an independent panel of senior mages appointed jointly by the Sovereign and Conservator Council. Any affected parties shall receive written notice thirty days prior to enforcement, allowing opportunity for appeal or modification of the ruling as appropriate. Reference § 100.5 for detailed appellate procedures.

Unauthorized experimentation with necromantic subjects outside approved facilities constitutes a felony offense punishable by imprisonment up to five years plus permanent sealing of magical abilities. Exceptions may be granted only under rare circumstances where substantial public benefit clearly outweighs potential harm, subject to rigorous oversight and post-study auditing. See § 200.4 for the formal process requesting such waivers. Violations of this provision will result in immediate suspension of all privileges pending full investigation into the nature and extent of the misconduct involved.

The provisions contained herein are intended to balance legitimate scholarly pursuits with necessary protections against misuse of powerful arts. While innovation is encouraged within defined boundaries, absolute adherence to safety protocols remains non-negotiable for all licensed practitioners operating under this Code. Any deviations must be pre-approved in writing by appropriate authorities and documented fully for future reference and accountability purposes. Failure to comply shall subject the offender to full legal consequences as outlined in subsequent articles of this statute book.

body.heading: § 300.9 Related Requirements - Definitions and Standards — Continued
body.text:
The term "Unsanctioned Arts" refers to magical practices deemed inherently dangerous or immoral by the Autumnwood Council, regardless of intent or outcome. These include but are not limited to blood magic, necromancy, soul-binding, and ritualistic sacrifice. Under § 100.5, any casting of Unsanctioned Arts without explicit permission constitutes a Class A felony punishable by permanent sealing of magical ability via the Paradox Trial (§ 200.7). Permission may be granted only in cases where research potential vastly outweighs societal risk, and even then is subject to stringent oversight per § 400.1.

The "Quiet List" mentioned herein is not a public registry but an internal classification system maintained by the Conservators. Items on this list are considered so hazardous that mere mention of their existence outside authorized channels violates § 300.7. Violations carry penalties under § 200.4 including revocation of licensure and imprisonment. The full contents of the Quiet List remain confidential per § 100.9, accessible only to Council members with a need-to-know clearance level of Black Diamond or higher. Unauthorized publication or dissemination incurs additional sanctions under § 300.8 relating to defamation and endangerment of public safety.

Research permits (§ 400.2) are issued at the sole discretion of the Innovators' Division upon demonstrated competence and ethical standing. Permit holders must submit quarterly reports detailing all experiments conducted, with results made available for audit under § 100.6. Failure to comply may result in immediate revocation and prosecution under applicable statutes. Constructed entities (§ 200.3) require separate permits regardless of their biological status; unauthorized creation is a felony offense carrying penalties outlined in § 500.7 including mandatory decommissioning and destruction.

The standards for reclassification (§ 300.4) involve rigorous peer review by the Academic Oversight Committee, which evaluates both theoretical soundness and practical implications. Reclassified items retain their original status until officially updated; interim use requires written approval from two Council members per § 100.8. Research copies (§ 300.5) must be returned upon completion of permitted studies, with all derived data surrendered to the Guild for archival purposes under § 900.7. Unauthorized duplication or distribution violates copyright protections established in § 600.2 and may lead to civil litigation pursuant to applicable laws.

These provisions serve to balance innovation with safety, ensuring that magical advancement does not come at unacceptable cost to society. All parties are expected to adhere strictly to these guidelines, understanding that failure to do so will result in severe consequences as outlined throughout this Codex and related statutes. The integrity of the Autumnwood Accords depends upon universal compliance, enforced through both legal mechanisms and communal pressure where appropriate.

body.heading: § 300.9 Definitions and Standards — Continued
body.text:
For purposes of these Accords, the term "necromancy" encompasses any magical practice that seeks to manipulate death itself, including but not limited to the raising of corpses as servants, the binding of spirits within objects or persons, and the transmutation of flesh into bone through forbidden rites. Such arts are deemed inherently unstable and dangerous, posing a threat both to individual safety and to the social order at large. Consequently, necromancy remains absolutely prohibited under all circumstances, with no exceptions permitted for research, education, or any other stated purpose.

The prohibition extends beyond mere ritualistic acts; it also encompasses theoretical study and speculative application of necromantic principles. Mages are forbidden from investing personal funds into the acquisition of necromantic tomes, artifacts, or equipment unless explicitly authorized in writing by a panel of senior Arcanists charged with evaluating potential risks and benefits. Any violation of this restriction shall be treated as grounds for immediate revocation of licensure without further process.

Furthermore, all mages are strictly enjoined from utilizing necromancy as a means of personal gain or advancement. This includes but is not limited to the summoning of familiar spirits for assistance in daily tasks, the invocation of ghostly presences to intimidate rivals or adversaries, and the manipulation of spectral entities to achieve otherwise unattainable objectives. Such conduct undermines the very foundation of responsible magical practice and shall be punished severely upon discovery.

It is incumbent upon every licensed mage to vigilantly monitor their own activities and those of their associates, ensuring that no necromantic influences seep into their sphere of influence. Failure to exercise due diligence in this regard may result in disciplinary action, regardless of whether any actual harm was inflicted. The preservation of public safety and the integrity of the arcane arts are paramount concerns that transcend individual interests or convenience.

In sum, the ban on necromancy is absolute and unyielding. No amount of theoretical justification or pragmatic necessity can ever override this fundamental tenet of our code. Mages must accept this limitation as an inherent condition of their profession, recognizing that true mastery lies not in pushing boundaries recklessly but in exercising restraint with wisdom and foresight. Only by adhering scrupulously to these guidelines can we hope to safeguard ourselves and society against the perils posed by unchecked necromantic ambition.

body.heading: § 300.9 Definitions and Standards — Continued — Continued
body.text:
The term "sanctioned arts" refers to any magical discipline that has been formally catalogued under the Schedules of Arts and is legally permissible for use by licensed casters within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Conversely, "unsanctioned arts" encompasses all other forms of magic, whether explicitly prohibited or merely unregistered. The distinction carries profound legal consequences, as only sanctioned arts may be employed openly without fear of prosecution under § 300.1 et seq.

The Quiet List, referenced in § 300.3, serves as the authoritative register for all items deemed potentially dangerous by the Desk's classification committees. Each entry on this list is subject to strict controls regarding its acquisition, storage, and application. Possession of a listed item without proper authorization constitutes a serious offense under both civil and penal law. Exceptions may be made pursuant to § 300.5 for bona fide research purposes conducted in approved facilities by qualified personnel holding valid permits issued under § 400.1 et seq.

Reclassification proceedings initiated pursuant to § 300.4 must adhere to rigorous procedural safeguards designed to ensure fairness and accuracy in determining the status of contested artifacts or techniques. Interested parties are entitled to notice, a hearing before an impartial tribunal composed of Guild peers, and full opportunity to present evidence on their behalf. Findings rendered following such proceedings shall be binding unless successfully appealed within the time limits prescribed by § 300.6.

Research copies of items appearing on the Quiet List may be procured only through formal application submitted in triplicate to the Chief Clerk of the Accords Desk, accompanied by detailed justification outlining intended use and measures for secure containment. Approval hinges upon a thorough review of the applicant's credentials, prior record, and proposed methodology. Copies so authorized shall remain under constant surveillance by appointed overseers charged with verifying compliance with all stipulated conditions throughout the duration of the project (§ 300.5).

Any attempt to circumvent these regulations via proxy arrangements or subterfuge will be treated as an aggravating circumstance warranting enhanced penalties upon conviction. The Guild reserves absolute discretion to revoke licenses, seize assets, and pursue criminal charges against violators without further notice. Adherence to the spirit as well as letter of the Accords is imperative for maintaining public trust in our noble institution.

see § 100.4 Records of Speech; see § 300.6 Related Requirements; see § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs
under § 300.7 Related Requirements, unauthorized duplication or dissemination of protected materials is strictly forbidden and punishable by immediate expulsion from the ranks of licensed practitioners. Violators shall forfeit all rights thereto forevermore. Let this stand as final warning!

body.heading: § 300.9 Definitions and Standards — Continued — Administration
body.text:
§ 300.9 Definitions and Standards – Cont'd. For the purposes hereof, "unsanctioned arts" refers to any magical practice not explicitly enumerated in § 300.1 or otherwise approved by the Desk under a reclassification petition filed pursuant to § 300.4. The mere possession of texts detailing such forbidden techniques does not constitute commission; however, active study without a valid Research Permit issued under § 400.1 shall be deemed an unlawful act subject to penalty under Part IV. "Necromancy" is defined as any ritual invoking or binding the spirits of the deceased for purposes other than solemn remembrance or lawful divination, and includes but is not limited to corpse animation, soul binding, and blood sacrifice. Such practices remain permanently prohibited without exception. The term "research copy," when used in connection with Quiet List items, denotes a facsimile reproduction created solely for archival purposes under the supervision of an Aegis Magus; unauthorized duplication or dissemination of such copies shall be prosecuted as forgery and grand larceny. Finally, "pocket dimension" is construed to mean any extradimensional space capable of sustaining independent biological function for extended periods, whether naturally occurring or artificially generated via spellcraft. The use thereof without a valid laboratory permit from the Desk constitutes illegal field work under § 500.1 and shall be punished accordingly."

This section clarifies critical terminology essential for proper application of these provisions, ensuring uniform interpretation across all jurisdictions where the Accords hold sway. By establishing precise boundaries between permissible inquiry and forbidden excess, the Guild seeks to balance its dual mandate of fostering magical advancement while safeguarding society from existential threats posed by unchecked experimentation. Any ambiguities shall be resolved in favor of public safety and stability, consistent with the foundational principles enshrined in §§ 1.4 through 1.9."

Under § 300.6 Related Requirements, all mages engaging in study or practice of forbidden arts must register annually with the Conservator's Office to undergo background checks and demonstrate financial solvency. Failure to comply results in immediate suspension of licensure until rectified. Additionally, any individual found guilty of violating these definitions shall face enhanced penalties under Part IV, including mandatory sealing of magical abilities via the Paradox Trial process described in § 1201.6. The Desk reserves the right to amend these standards as new threats emerge, subject to ratification by a two-thirds majority vote at a regular session convened specifically for this purpose."

See also §§ 300.2–300.8 governing the regulation of unsanctioned magical practices and associated offenses."

body.heading: § 300.9 Definitions and Standards — Classification of Magical Conduct
body.text:
For the purposes of these Accords, "magical conduct" encompasses all acts involving the casting of spells, manipulation of arcane energies, or utilization of enchanted items in a manner that could impact public safety or order. Such conduct is categorized into four distinct classes based on inherent risk and potential consequence: Class A (High Risk), Class B (Moderate Risk), Class C (Low Risk), and Class D (Negligent). This taxonomy serves as the primary basis for determining licensing requirements, enforcement priorities, and applicable penalties.

Class A conduct includes any act involving forbidden schools of magic such as necromancy, blood sorcery, or soul-binding arts deemed inherently destructive to the natural order. These acts are prohibited absolutely under § 1401.6 regardless of intent or outcome. Violations constitute immediate grounds for revocation and prosecution under the Paradox Trial provisions. Class B conduct involves high-energy applications such as teleportation circles, dimensional anchors, or mass summoning rituals that could destabilize local reality if mishandled. Practitioners engaging in Class B activities require advanced licensure and must adhere to strict containment protocols outlined in § 1201.5.

Class C encompasses moderate-risk operations like personal wards, utility charms, or minor transmutation spells commonly employed by everyday mages. While less hazardous than higher classes, negligent execution can still result in property damage or injury. Such activities fall under standard regulatory oversight with periodic inspections mandated by § 300.4. Class D represents the lowest tier, covering routine spellcasting that poses minimal threat to persons or infrastructure when performed competently. These actions generally require only basic certification and are subject to random audits rather than systematic review.

The classification system is designed to facilitate proportionate enforcement while accommodating legitimate magical pursuits within safe parameters. Failure to properly categorize one's activities may lead to escalated scrutiny and heavier penalties should violations occur. Mages bear the burden of accurately self-assessing their conduct's risk level prior to execution, consulting official guides when uncertain under § 1401.7. The Desk reserves authority to reclassify any act de novo based on contextual factors including location, timing, scale, and potential downstream effects.

This framework ensures that magical practice remains a regulated privilege rather than an unchecked freedom, balancing innovation with necessary safeguards for the greater good. Adherence to these standards reflects responsible stewardship of arcane gifts within our shared society.

sections.brief: Definitions and Standards

sections.title: Research Integrity and Peer Review

body.heading: Research Integrity and Peer Review
body.text:
Under § 100.6, certain duties may be delegated to clerks for administrative efficiency; this section governs the scope of such delegation specifically regarding research permits and related obligations. While clerks possess no inherent authority beyond their assigned tasks, they may act as proxies for researchers in routine matters directly tied to permit compliance and safety protocols. These proxy actions are binding on the original researcher provided they fall within the clerk's delegated purview under § 100.6(a)(iii).

A primary delegation allowance granted to clerks involves verifying preliminary safety data submitted by applicants during the initial review phase. This includes confirming that proposed research locations meet minimum containment standards and that appropriate safeguards have been implemented per Schedule of Arts requirements. Clerks are empowered to request additional information or clarification from researchers as necessary to complete this verification, but they lack authority to make substantive judgments on technical matters beyond their training. Any dispute arising from a clerk's preliminary findings must be elevated to the full Desk for final adjudication under § 200.4(b).

Clerks further may facilitate communication between researchers and external regulatory bodies where applicable, transmitting required documentation and coordinating inspection schedules as directed by senior officials. However, they shall not negotiate terms or agree to extensions on behalf of the Guild without express authorization in writing from an Archmage. Unauthorized commitments made by clerks are void ab initio unless ratified within seven days under § 100.6(c). This limitation exists to prevent erosion of centralized control over sensitive research activities and to protect the Guild's strategic interests against inadvertent liability exposure.

In cases where delegation proves insufficient due to complexity or urgency, researchers may petition for temporary assignment of a full-time clerk liaison to oversee their project exclusively. Such liaisons possess expanded powers commensurate with their role as dedicated representatives of the Desk, including onsite monitoring and immediate enforcement authority within research facilities. Liaison appointments remain subject to recall at any time without cause under § 100.6(d), ensuring that researchers maintain ultimate accountability for their operations regardless of temporary staffing arrangements. All delegated functions must be documented in official records pursuant to § 200.4(a) to ensure transparency and facilitate future audits or investigations as needed.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks
see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse
see § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy

body.heading: § 400.9 Research Integrity and Peer Review
body.text:
All research conducted under the authority of a permit shall adhere to the highest standards of academic integrity, safety, and ethical conduct. Any findings or conclusions reached by an Innovator must be submitted for review by at least two independent Conservators before being deemed official. This peer-review process ensures that magical breakthroughs do not inadvertently destabilize local ecosystems or violate fundamental laws of nature.

Innovators found falsifying data, concealing dangerous results, or acting outside the scope of their permit shall face immediate revocation of credentials and potential criminal charges under § 500.12. The Desk maintains a database of all research outcomes to track long-term impacts on the broader magical community. Failure to register results within thirty days may lead to suspension of future permits for the offending party or their associates.

Special provisions apply when research involves sentient subjects, classified materials, or cross-dimensional entities. Such projects require heightened supervision and mandatory debriefings after each session. The Desk reserves the right to terminate any study deemed too risky or unethical without notice. Innovators are reminded that personal gain must never supersede public safety in pursuit of magical knowledge.

The spirit of this section is to balance the freedom of inquiry with prudent oversight, recognizing that unchecked experimentation could unleash forces beyond our comprehension. By fostering accountability and collaboration between factions, we may unlock new frontiers while minimizing harm to ourselves and future generations. Let us proceed with humility, caution, and an unwavering commitment to the greater good.

see § 400.1 Research Permits; see § 500.12 Criminal Penalties for Falsification; see § 200.3 Temporary Mouths and Their Limitations; under § 1.7 Aggregation of Conduct, repeated violations may warrant harsher sanctions.

body.heading: § 400.9 Research Integrity and Peer Review — Continued
body.text:
§ 400.9 Research Integrity and Peer Review. All research conducted under this Part shall be subject to review by an independent panel of qualified peers, hereinafter referred to as the "Research Ethics Board" (see § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild). The purpose of such review is to ensure that all research activities comply with the ethical standards set forth in these Accords and do not pose undue risk to public safety or magical equilibrium. Failure to obtain prior approval from the Research Ethics Board may result in immediate revocation of research permits and sanctions under § 300.5 Unauthorized Research Practices.

The Research Ethics Board shall consist of at least five (5) members appointed by the Archmage Sovereign, including representatives from both the Conservator and Innovator factions. Members shall serve staggered four-year terms and may be removed for cause upon a two-thirds vote of the full Guild Council. The Board shall meet quarterly to review submitted research proposals and reports, with additional emergency sessions as needed. All proceedings of the Research Ethics Board shall be recorded in minute books kept at the Autumnwood Accords Desk (see § 100.4 Records of Speech).

Proposed research projects must be submitted by principal investigators through their employing institutions no less than sixty (60) days prior to commencement. Submissions shall include detailed descriptions of intended methodologies, potential risks and benefits, data management plans, and contingency measures for unforeseen complications. The Research Ethics Board shall evaluate each proposal against established criteria including scientific merit, societal impact, environmental considerations, and alignment with current regulatory frameworks. Written determinations granting or denying permission to proceed shall be issued within thirty (30) days of receipt of complete materials.

Upon completion of research activities, principal investigators are required to submit comprehensive final reports detailing outcomes, data analysis, conclusions drawn, and any adverse events experienced during the course of study. Such reports must also address whether results support original hypotheses or necessitate revision of prevailing theories regarding magical phenomena. Copies of all submitted documentation shall be made available for public inspection upon request, subject only to reasonable redaction of proprietary information protected by trade secret law (see § 1301.6 Trade Secrets and Confidentiality).

The Research Ethics Board retains discretion to impose additional conditions or restrictions on ongoing research projects as deemed necessary to safeguard against potential harm. Violation of stipulated terms may lead to immediate suspension of all associated permissions and further disciplinary action under applicable statutes. Regular audits and spot checks conducted by Guild inspectors shall verify compliance with approved protocols, with findings reported directly to the Board for review.

Research integrity remains a paramount concern for the maintenance of magical stability and public trust in the institution of the Mages' Guild. By fostering an environment of rigorous scrutiny and transparent oversight, these provisions aim to balance scientific inquiry with responsible stewardship of powerful forces inherent in natural law. All participants engaged in authorized research bear a solemn obligation to uphold the highest standards of ethics and professionalism throughout their endeavors (see also § 300.4 Reclassification Procedures; § 500.1 Field Casting Regulations).

body.heading: Research Oversight Committee Functions and Powers
body.text:
The Research Oversight Committee, hereinafter referred to as the "ROC," shall serve as the primary governing body for the regulation of all magical research conducted under the auspices of the Mages' Guild. The ROC shall consist of five members appointed by the Archmage Sovereign, comprising at least two Conservators, two Innovators, and one neutral arbiter selected from among the Aegis Magi. These appointments shall remain in effect for a term of three years, renewable upon reappointment by the Archmage Sovereign.

The ROC shall meet quarterly to review submitted research proposals, evaluate their potential risks and benefits, and grant or deny permissions accordingly. In addition, the ROC shall conduct periodic audits of ongoing projects to ensure compliance with all applicable laws and regulations. Any member found to be in violation of established protocols shall face immediate suspension from further research activities until such time as a full investigation has been completed and satisfactory remedial actions have been taken.

The powers granted to the ROC include, but are not limited to: (a) reviewing and approving or denying all new research proposals; (b) setting standards for acceptable experimental procedures; (c) mandating safety measures and containment protocols; (d) imposing penalties for non-compliance; (e) recommending disciplinary action against errant researchers; and (f) advising the Archmage Sovereign on matters pertaining to magical development. The ROC shall maintain a detailed log of all its proceedings, which shall be made available upon request by any interested party.

It is hereby declared that no member of the Mages' Guild shall engage in any form of unauthorized research without first obtaining written permission from the Research Oversight Committee. Failure to comply with this provision shall result in automatic revocation of one's licensure and potential criminal prosecution under applicable laws. The ROC retains absolute discretion to revoke previously granted permissions at its sole discretion, should it determine that continued approval would pose an unacceptable risk to public safety or magical stability.

In accordance with these provisions, the Research Oversight Committee shall exercise diligent oversight over all aspects of magical research within the Guild's jurisdiction, ensuring that such endeavors are conducted safely and responsibly while fostering innovation and progress in the field of arcane studies. The ROC shall remain ever vigilant against any threats posed by unchecked experimentation or misuse of forbidden arts, acting swiftly to mitigate potential dangers to society at large. Through its steadfast dedication to preserving both knowledge and security, the Research Oversight Committee stands as a bastion of responsible stewardship for all who seek to unlock the mysteries of magic under lawful guidance.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; see § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items; see § 400.7 Related Requirements.

body.heading: Research Oversight and Peer Review
body.text:
§ 400.9 Related Requirements

The integrity of magical research is paramount to the safety and stability of society. To this end, all studies involving classified or high-risk arts shall undergo rigorous peer review by qualified experts in relevant fields. The Research Oversight Committee ("ROC") established under § 401.2 serves as the primary body for evaluating proposed projects, assessing potential hazards, and granting necessary approvals. ROC members must maintain impartiality and disclose any conflicts of interest as mandated by § 500.7.

The peer review process shall commence with submission of a comprehensive proposal outlining research objectives, methodologies, risk mitigation strategies, and anticipated outcomes. The ROC will scrutinize each element meticulously, consulting external specialists as needed to ensure thorough vetting. Projects deemed too dangerous or unethical may be rejected outright, while others might receive conditional approval subject to strict monitoring. Throughout execution, researchers must provide regular progress reports detailing findings, incidents, and any deviations from the approved plan.

Upon completion of studies, final results shall be presented to the ROC for assessment against original hypotheses and safety parameters. Positive outcomes may lead to wider dissemination through published papers or presentations at professional conferences. Conversely, adverse effects or procedural failures will trigger an immediate investigation into root causes and potential liabilities. In cases where misconduct is discovered, appropriate disciplinary action will ensue in accordance with established protocols.

This robust framework ensures that magical inquiry proceeds responsibly, balancing the pursuit of knowledge with prudent safeguards for all concerned parties. By fostering a culture of accountability and transparency within our scholarly community, we uphold the highest standards of ethical practice while advancing the frontiers of arcane understanding.

body.heading: Research Oversight and Peer Review Mechanisms
body.text:
Under this Part, the integrity of all research activities conducted within authorized facilities shall be maintained through a rigorous system of oversight and peer review. § 400.6 establishes that every permit issued under this section must include explicit terms requiring periodic inspection by designated Guild auditors to verify compliance with safety protocols and ethical standards. Failure to undergo such inspections may result in immediate suspension of research privileges until full compliance is demonstrated.

§ 400.7 further mandates the formation of independent Research Oversight Committees (ROC) composed of senior mages not directly involved in specific projects under review. These ROCs shall examine all proposed methodologies, data analyses, and final reports submitted by investigators to ensure adherence to established scientific principles and moral guidelines. The findings of each committee must be formally recorded and made available for public scrutiny unless classified information is invoked pursuant to § 300.5.

In cases where irregularities or potential violations are identified during the review process, the ROC possesses broad authority to impose corrective measures ranging from additional audits to outright revocation of research permissions. Such actions shall be taken without prejudice to any subsequent disciplinary proceedings that may arise. The Guild reserves the right to audit historical records indefinitely should new evidence emerge suggesting prior misconduct was concealed or misreported.

§ 400.8 clarifies that all findings generated through permitted research remain the exclusive property of the Mages' Guild unless explicit licensing agreements are executed between researchers and interested third parties. Unauthorized dissemination of proprietary data may constitute grounds for immediate expulsion from the organization alongside civil penalties. This provision serves to protect both commercial interests and national security considerations inherent in advanced magical studies.

The overarching purpose of these requirements is twofold: first, to safeguard public welfare by preventing reckless experimentation that could lead to catastrophic consequences; second, to preserve the Guild's reputation as a responsible steward of arcane knowledge. By instituting comprehensive checks and balances, Autumnwood ensures that progress does not come at the expense of safety or ethics. All researchers are reminded that their privileges carry corresponding obligations to uphold these fundamental principles in all their endeavors.
