sections.title: See Also Provisions

body.heading: § 900.9 Related Requirements; See Also Provisions
body.text:
In addition to the obligations set forth herein, any party engaging in licensed magical practice shall comply with all applicable provisions of this Code and those referenced thereto. This includes adherence to standards for safety, efficacy, and ethical conduct as established by the Mages' Guild or its duly appointed delegates. Failure to do so may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure or criminal prosecution, depending on the severity and circumstances of the violation.

Furthermore, all casters must maintain accurate records of their activities for a minimum period specified by regulation. These logs shall include details such as dates, times, locations, purposes, participants, materials used, and outcomes achieved. Such documentation serves both administrative oversight functions and historical preservation efforts within the broader magical community. Regular audits may be conducted to ensure compliance with reporting mandates.

Any disputes arising from interpretation of these provisions or their application to specific situations shall be resolved through established dispute resolution mechanisms outlined elsewhere in this Code. This encompasses mediation, arbitration, and formal adjudication as appropriate under the facts and law governing each case. Parties are expected to act in good faith throughout the process and cooperate fully with authorities investigating potential breaches of law.

The foregoing requirements reflect the collective wisdom accumulated over generations of practice and reflection upon lessons learned hard-won through trial-and-error experience across cultures worldwide. They embody our shared commitment to responsible stewardship of magical power for benefit rather than harm alone. By accepting licensure, practitioners implicitly agree to abide by these rules willingly knowing full well consequences thereof should they fail so to do henceforth forevermore without regret nevermore!

see § 100.4 Records of Speech; see § 200.1 Licensure Required; under § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items
§ 900.9 Related Requirements; See Also Provisions (End of Section)

body.heading: § 900.10 Jurisdictional Immunity and Privilege
body.text:
Section 900.10 establishes the legal immunities enjoyed by duly licensed mages when acting within the scope of their authorized practice. Under § 900.1(a), a registered practitioner shall not be held personally liable for civil damages resulting from casting operations conducted in compliance with all applicable laws and guild regulations. This immunity extends to both professional services rendered and incidental activities directly related thereto, as delineated in § 900.1(b).

However, this protection is not absolute. Pursuant to § 900.2(a), a caster shall forfeit their immunity if they engage in gross negligence or willful misconduct. Such actions include but are not limited to: unauthorized modification of magical devices (§ 900.2(b)), casting outside designated parameters without proper permits (§ 900.2(c)), and failure to maintain required insurance coverage (§ 900.2(d)). The burden of proof regarding a mage's compliance lies with the practitioner, who must demonstrate adherence to all relevant statutes upon request from any interested party under § 900.3(a).

Furthermore, Section 900.4 addresses the issue of vicarious liability for employer-casters and their associates. While principal casters retain immunity under normal circumstances, § 900.4(a) stipulates that supervising entities remain responsible for ensuring proper oversight and training protocols are followed. Failure to provide adequate supervision may result in joint and several liability for resulting harms, as outlined in § 900.4(b). This provision aims to promote accountability throughout the entire casting operation chain.

Finally, Section 900.5 clarifies the limitations of this immunity when third-party injuries occur. While practitioners are shielded from suits arising directly from their lawful work, § 900.5(a) preserves the right of any injured party to seek redress for intentional torts or criminal offenses committed by casters outside authorized activities. Such matters shall be adjudicated according to standard legal procedures rather than through guild mechanisms alone, per § 900.5(b). This ensures that immunity provisions do not create loopholes for malicious actors evading justice under the guise of professional practice.

In sum, Section 900.10 balances the need to protect legitimate magical practitioners with safeguards against abuse of their privileged status. By defining clear boundaries for acceptable conduct and assigning appropriate levels of responsibility, these rules foster a safer environment for all parties involved in arcane endeavors. Compliance with this framework remains mandatory for continued licensure under the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: § 900.9 Related Requirements – See Also Provisions
body.text:
In addition to the primary filing obligations outlined herein, mages shall comply with all ancillary requirements applicable to their specific circumstances and practices. These include, but are not limited to: timely submission of supplemental reports following any material change in status or activity; adherence to seasonal casting windows prescribed by local authorities; payment of all outstanding fees within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt; and maintenance of accurate personal ledgers documenting every spell cast for at least five consecutive years. Failure to meet these secondary obligations may result in escalated penalties, including suspension of privileges until compliance is achieved.

See also § 900.1 (Duty to File Before Casting), which establishes the fundamental prerequisite of pre-authorization for all magical operations; § 200.3 (Temporary Mouths), governing the limited use of proxies under strict oversight; and § 400.5 (Unauthorized Titan Growth), prohibiting unregulated expansion of one's own mana reservoir without explicit council approval. These provisions collectively ensure comprehensive regulatory coverage across all facets of arcane practice, from initial licensure through ongoing conduct review.

Mages are further reminded that the Guild retains inherent authority to impose additional conditions deemed necessary for public safety or resource management at any time. Such directives shall take precedence over any prior agreements or customary usages. Resistance to lawful orders constitutes grounds for immediate revocation of credentials and possible criminal prosecution under relevant statutes. The spirit of these related requirements mirrors that of the core mandates: preservation of order, protection of citizens, and sustainable stewardship of magical potential.

Under § 900.7 (Foreign Halls and Courtesy), practitioners operating abroad must respect host nation regulations even when exempt from domestic filing duties. Similarly, § 1201.6 (Related Requirements) extends analogous expectations to cross-jurisdictional collaborations. Ultimately, the scope of a caster's obligations cannot be narrowly construed; they encompass all actions reasonably implicated by their professional role. As stated in § 300.7 (Related Requirements), "the law follows the magic," meaning wherever one turns their art, so too must they turn their attention to lawful compliance."

This provision also incorporates by reference various industry standards and best practices developed over centuries of collective wisdom. While not exhaustive, these guidelines represent a baseline for ethical conduct expected of every registered practitioner. Deviation therefrom requires compelling justification approved in advance by the appropriate oversight body. Self-regulation remains paramount; only through vigilant adherence to both letter and intent can we safeguard our shared future against the perils of unchecked ambition.

For further guidance on interpreting these supplementary mandates, consult the Master Registry or seek counsel from an experienced mentor. Remember always that true mastery lies not merely in command of spellwork, but in disciplined self-governance—a cornerstone upon which all responsible magic builds. Thus do we uphold our vows and secure our standing within this noble profession forevermore.

body.heading: § 900.10 Immunity and Privilege Provisions
body.text:
Under § 900.6–900.8, mages are obligated to file detailed reports of all casting activities before the Accords Desk. These provisions establish the framework for oversight and accountability within the Guild's regulatory regime. However, recognition must be made that such oversight cannot extend indefinitely without impairing the practical functioning of magic itself. To balance these competing interests, certain exceptions and immunities are hereby codified to protect both casters and third parties from undue interference.

§ 900.10 Immunity and Privilege Provisions
(a) **Judicial Immunity.** No caster shall be subject to civil or criminal liability for actions taken in the course of lawful casting operations, provided such actions were not willfully malicious or grossly negligent. This immunity extends to all acts occurring within the scope of employment as a licensed artisan or contractor. See § 900.1–900.5 regarding filing and reporting obligations that define "lawful operation."

(b) **Privileged Communications.** All communications between casters and their clients, contractors, or fellow practitioners concerning casting matters are privileged and confidential unless waived in writing. This privilege protects the integrity of professional relationships and prevents unwarranted intrusion into private business affairs. See § 900.1–900.5 for definitions of "casting operations" that trigger these protections.

(c) **Sovereign Immunity.** The Autumnwood Accords Desk and its agents enjoy absolute immunity from suit except as expressly provided herein. This reflects the public interest in maintaining an efficient regulatory apparatus free from harassment by litigants seeking to circumvent statutory requirements. See § 900.1–900.5 regarding the scope of official duties that attract such protections.

(d) **Safe Harbor Provisions.** Casters acting in good faith reliance upon written authorization or approval from the Accords Desk shall not be liable for ordinary negligence resulting therefrom. This encourages responsible innovation while preserving liability for intentional misconduct or gross deviation from established standards. See § 900.1–900.5 for guidance on what constitutes valid authorization under this regime."

(e) **Limitations and Exceptions.** The foregoing immunities and privileges shall not apply where: (i) the caster acted with intent to harm; (ii) the conduct fell outside the scope of authorized activities; or (iii) third-party rights were deliberately violated. In such instances, ordinary tort principles govern liability determinations. See § 900.1–900.5 for further elaboration on these critical distinctions."

These provisions collectively serve to delineate the boundaries of permissible regulatory oversight while safeguarding against abuse of power by both state actors and private parties alike. Through careful calibration, they enable the Guild to fulfill its mandate without stifling legitimate magical practice or infringing upon fundamental liberties. Thus stands § 900.10 as an essential component of the broader statutory scheme governing arcane arts in this realm."

body.heading: 900.10 Immunity and Privilege Provisions
body.text:
Under § 900.6, mages are required to file detailed manifests prior to casting potent spells within Autumnwood jurisdiction. Failure to comply renders the act void ab initio and subject to punitive sanctions per the Accords' penal provisions. This filing obligation extends to all recognized practitioners regardless of affiliation or rank, ensuring comprehensive oversight of magical activity across the region.

Related Requirements: § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments; § 900.3 Record Retention; § 900.4 Identify Fees Who Pays; § 900.5 False Provenance of Relics; § 900.6 Related Requirements; § 900.7 Related Requirements; § 900.8 Related Requirements

See Also Provisions, § 900.11 Immunity from Civil Litigation, § 900.12 Criminal Jurisdiction and Enforcement, § 900.13 Diplomatic Privileges for Foreign Representatives, § 900.14 Tax Exemptions on Magical Goods

The filing regime serves multiple purposes: establishing a baseline of normal magical activity to detect anomalies, creating an audit trail for post-casting disputes, and enabling pre-emptive intervention should risks arise. Practitioners must submit complete details including spell type, intended effect, location, duration, and any ancillary materials employed. Omissions or inaccuracies may invalidate the entire filing and trigger investigations into potential violations of the Accords' core tenets.

Immunity Provisions are integral to maintaining order within this complex legal landscape, shielding good-faith actors from unwarranted interference while preserving the state's ability to enforce compliance where necessary. These safeguards apply uniformly to all registered mages operating under the authority of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, regardless of their individual circumstances or affiliations with various magical organizations.

By adhering strictly to these filing mandates and respecting applicable immunities and privileges, practitioners can navigate the intricate web of regulations governing magical practice in this jurisdiction with confidence and clarity, contributing to a stable and prosperous environment for all residents.

body.heading: § 900.10 Immunity and Privilege Provisions — Continued
body.text:
All persons duly licensed or otherwise authorized under this Act, in the performance of their official duties as such, are hereby granted full immunity from any criminal or civil liability arising out of acts committed within the scope of their employment. Such immunity extends to actions taken in good faith reliance on directions received from superiors, whether oral or written. This provision is intended to foster an environment where magistrates may perform their functions without fear of retribution or undue interference.

It shall be further provided that no suit or proceeding may be maintained against any such officer or employee for damages resulting from the exercise or non-exercise of any discretion vested by law in respect thereof, unless there is shown to have been gross negligence or willful misconduct. The burden of proof regarding either of these conditions rests solely upon the plaintiff and must be sustained by clear and convincing evidence before any claim may proceed past summary judgment stage.

In addition to foregoing protections, all duly appointed magistrates are afforded certain privileges in connection with their official capacities. These include exemption from jury duty while on active assignment, priority access to government facilities for investigative purposes, and reimbursement of reasonable travel expenses incurred in the course of performing assigned tasks. Such benefits shall remain in full force notwithstanding any conflicting provisions contained within other statutes or regulations.

Finally, nothing herein shall be construed as waiving any right otherwise enjoyed by individual citizens under domestic law or treaty obligations binding upon the United States. Rather, it represents a careful balancing act between protecting public safety and safeguarding constitutional liberties against potential abuses inherent in granting broad powers to those responsible for enforcing them. Only through such delicate equilibrium can we ensure both effective governance and continued respect for fundamental freedoms alike.

See also § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting; § 200.5 Guest Casters; § 400.3 Borrowed Hours – Interest in Time. These provisions collectively define the scope of lawful magical practice under our jurisdiction, balancing efficiency with responsibility at every turn. Together they form an integrated framework designed to promote harmony between tradition and innovation alike.

sections.brief: In addition to the obligations set forth herein, any party engaging in licensed

sections.title: Unlicensed Artisanry

body.heading: Unlicensed Artisanry
body.text:
The provisions herein shall be read in conjunction with the related requirements set forth in §§ 1.4 through 1.7, which govern the general applicability and construction of this Code. Specifically, all persons subject to these rules are deemed to have notice thereof by virtue of their participation in the magical community under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. See § 1.4 Persons Bound; see also § 1.6 Definitions for clarification of technical terms employed throughout.

Further, nothing contained in this Part shall be construed to override or diminish any applicable statutes, ordinances, or regulations enacted by duly constituted authorities within the Hall's territories and spheres of influence. The Desk reserves the right to refer disputes involving overlapping jurisdictions to appropriate administrative bodies for resolution pursuant to established inter-agency protocols under § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy.

It is expressly declared that failure to comply with any provision set forth herein shall constitute a material breach of license, subjecting the offending party to immediate revocation of privileges and such additional sanctions as may be warranted under existing penal codes. Aggravating factors include willful defiance, repeated infractions, or actions causing significant harm to persons or property. Mitigating circumstances may be taken into account at the Desk's sole discretion, provided they are supported by credible evidence.

In cases of ambiguity regarding intent or scope, interpretation shall favor public safety and the preservation of peace over narrow literalism. This principle derives from the foundational purpose of the Accords—to regulate magic responsibly while enabling beneficial advancement. See § 1.7 Construction; compare with § 300.2 Necromancy: Unsanctioned Arts for an example of strict construction applied to particularly hazardous practices.

The Desk shall maintain a registry of all complaints and adjudications arising under this section, accessible upon written request by interested parties or their duly authorized representatives. This ensures transparency and accountability in the administration of justice within the magical community. Records shall be updated promptly following final disposition of each case, reflecting current enforcement trends and emerging patterns of noncompliance as relevant to future regulatory decisions.

Finally, nothing herein shall be construed to create any right or remedy beyond those explicitly granted by this Code or existing law. All claims for damages, penalties, or other relief must be pursued through proper legal channels and in accordance with applicable statutes of limitation. The Desk acts solely in its capacity as an impartial arbiter of the Accords, without prejudice to any inherent rights retained by individuals, corporations, or entities subject thereto.

By failing to adhere fully to these provisions, licensees risk not only disciplinary action but also erosion of public trust and potential revocation of their standing within the magical ecosystem altogether. Prudent adherence to ethical standards and lawful conduct remains paramount for all practitioners seeking long-term success in this demanding field. As Archmage Veyra herself has often stated: "True mastery lies not merely in raw power, but in wise restraint." Let these words guide your path forward under the watchful eye of the Accords.

body.heading: § 500.9 Related Requirements - Unlicensed Artisanry
body.text:
The practice of casting spells for compensation without an active license is strictly prohibited under the Autumnwood Accords, with severe penalties applicable to all violators. Such unlicensed artistry not only undermines the regulatory framework but also poses grave risks to public safety and magical integrity. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding rogue practitioners who operate outside established channels, regardless of their claimed expertise or proven track record.

Any individual found guilty of performing unauthorized magic for profit shall face immediate revocation of any existing credentials and permanent disqualification from future licensure. In addition to these administrative sanctions, the offender may be subject to civil liability for any damages resulting from their negligent or reckless casting. The burden of proof rests squarely upon the accuser to demonstrate that the accused engaged in illicit activity with intent to defraud or endanger others.

Furthermore, all suspected instances of unlicensed artistry must be reported promptly to the nearest Guild inspector for investigation and adjudication. Failure to comply with this reporting requirement may result in disciplinary action against the responsible party, up to and including expulsion from the Hall. The Guild reserves the right to initiate criminal proceedings where appropriate, particularly when allegations involve serious bodily harm or loss of life attributable to faulty spellwork.

It is imperative that all members of the magical community uphold the highest standards of professionalism and accountability in their professional dealings. By adhering rigorously to these guidelines, we ensure the continued safety and prosperity of our shared society while preserving the dignity and prestige of the Guild itself. Any deviation from these principles threatens not only individual livelihoods but the very foundation upon which our collective well-being rests.

body.heading: § 500.9 Unlicensed Artisanry and the Gray Market
body.text:
§ 500.9 Unlicensed Artisanry and the Gray Market. The Guild maintains that all magical commodities, whether crafted by licensed artisans or scavenged from wild sources, must bear a valid mark of origin to enter lawful commerce. This provision seeks to eradicate counterfeiting, substandard goods, and the black market in arcane paraphernalia which undermines both consumer safety and tax revenue. Under this section, any item lacking proper documentation is presumed illicit until proven otherwise through rigorous inspection by Guild auditors. Penalties for trafficking unmarked wares range from confiscation of contraband to revocation of merchant licenses and imprisonment. The intent is twofold: first, to protect citizens from harmful or ineffective magical items; second, to ensure fair competition among registered producers who adhere to quality standards. Violators face strict liability regardless of intent, as the burden rests upon sellers to demonstrate lawful provenance. Only with this ironclad regulation can the Guild guarantee the integrity and safety of all goods bearing its seal.

"see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value; see § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild; under § 400.3 Borrowed Hours Interest in Time"

body.heading: § 500.9 Unlicensed Artisanry and the Gray Market — Continued
body.text:
The Accords recognize that not all magical labor falls within the purview of formal licensure. Where an individual operates outside the Guild's regulatory framework, either by choice or circumstance, such activity constitutes "gray market" casting. While technically unregulated, gray market practices are neither inherently illegal nor protected; they exist in a legal limbo subject to discretionary enforcement.

The Aegis Magi retain broad authority to investigate suspected violations of guild statutes, including unauthorized field operations conducted without permits. Upon discovery of evidence suggesting illicit activity, inspectors may issue citations for non-compliance with applicable laws and ordinances. Failure to remedy such violations within a reasonable timeframe may result in escalating penalties, up to and including revocation of any existing credentials.

Parties engaging in gray market casting do so at their own risk. The Guild bears no liability for injuries or damages arising from unlicensed practices, whether suffered by the caster themselves or third parties. Conversely, victims seeking redress must pursue claims directly against responsible individuals, absent proof of official negligence by guild agents.

This provision reflects the complex reality that magic permeates society beyond formal channels. Rather than attempting to eradicate all unauthorized use, the Accords acknowledge its inevitability while maintaining robust oversight mechanisms. The balance between freedom and control remains an enduring challenge for regulators in this field.

body.heading: § 500.9 Unlicensed Artisanry and the Gray Market — Administration
body.text:
§ 500.9 Unlicensed Artisanry and the Gray Market

No caster shall, for consideration or profit, employ any spellwork not included in their official license without prior written authorization from the Guild Desk. Violation constitutes unlicensed artisanry under § 200.1(a)(7), subject to disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure. This prohibition extends to all forms of magical practice, whether performed personally or through proxies, constructs, or other agents.

The gray market for illicit spellcasting thrives despite strict prohibitions, driven by the insatiable demand for unauthorized services ranging from simple buffs to complex ritual workings. Such activities undermine the integrity of licensure and expose practitioners to significant legal risks if discovered. The Desk maintains a vigilant watch over suspected operations, utilizing informants and surveillance where necessary. Confirmed offenders face escalating penalties based on severity and frequency of violations.

Casters are reminded that the distinction between licensed and unlicensed work is not merely bureaucratic pedantry but a fundamental safeguard for public safety and magical equilibrium. Unauthorized practices may inadvertently trigger unforeseen consequences beyond the caster's control, endangering both client and caster alike. The Guild stands ready to assist responsible practitioners in expanding their capabilities through proper channels rather than risking criminal prosecution via gray market shortcuts.

See also § 200.1 Licensure Required; § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; § 400.1 Research Permits for related provisions governing the scope and limitations of authorized magical activities. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in immediate suspension pending investigation, regardless of apparent benign intent or outcome. The burden of proof rests squarely upon the accused caster to demonstrate compliance with all applicable statutes and regulations.

body.heading: § 500.9 Unlicensed Artisanry and the Gray Market — Administration — Continued
body.text:
The clandestine production and distribution of unauthorized magical items constitutes a persistent threat to public safety and the integrity of the Guild's regulatory framework. Such "gray market" operations typically bypass critical quality controls, risk assessments, and licensing requirements, resulting in substandard goods that may malfunction catastrophically or cause irreparable harm to users and bystanders alike. To combat this growing problem, the Autumnwood Accords empower the Aegis Magi with broad authority to investigate suspected violations, seize illicit stockpiles, and prosecute offending parties under the full weight of the penal code.

Investigations into unlicensed artisanry shall be conducted with discretion but thoroughness. The Aegis may enter properties without warrant upon reasonable suspicion, subject to subsequent judicial review. All seized materials must be inventoried in triplicate and held in secure custody pending resolution of legal proceedings. Owners or operators found guilty of violating § 500.1 shall face heavy fines up to three times the value of illegal goods produced, plus restitution for all damages caused. Repeat offenders may have their magic sealed permanently and be barred from ever seeking licensure again.

The Guild recognizes that total eradication of gray market activity is an elusive goal given its decentralized nature. Rather than pursuing futile crackdowns alone, the Aegis shall actively collaborate with law enforcement agencies to disrupt major distribution networks and dismantle organized criminal enterprises profiting from unlicensed magic. Joint task forces may be established as necessary to ensure swift apprehension and conviction of violators across jurisdictional lines. Through sustained vigilance and multi-agency cooperation, it is hoped that illegal artisanry will dwindle until rendering further aggressive measures unnecessary.

This section shall take effect immediately upon filing and remains applicable indefinitely unless explicitly amended by subsequent resolution. All existing laws pertaining to unlicensed magic production are hereby superseded to the extent of any conflict. The Aegis Magi are authorized to issue binding orders directing compliance with these provisions, failure to which may result in immediate seizure of assets and temporary suspension of all magical practice pending review. Failure to abide shall constitute a separate offense punishable under § 900.1. Any questions regarding interpretation or enforcement shall be referred to the Archmage Sovereign for final adjudication.

sections.brief: The provisions herein shall be read in conjunction with the related requirements

sections.title: Contracts with Non-Casters and Related Requirements

body.heading: Contracts with Non-Casters and Related Requirements
body.text:
§ 600.9 Related Requirements
This Section sets forth the prerequisites for entering into binding magical contracts with parties lacking formal licensure under these Accords. Pursuant to § 100.2, only duly authorized representatives of the Guild may negotiate such agreements on its behalf. As provided in § 400.3, any contract involving temporal manipulation requires explicit permission from the Conservators and must be registered within three solar days of execution. See also § 200.7 regarding disclosure obligations.

Under § 300.8, no pact may impinge upon the sanctity of a pocket dimension without prior review by the Aegis Magi. This includes but is not limited to clauses granting access rights or usage fees for such spaces. Any violation constitutes breach under § 500.1 and subjects the offending party to immediate seizure of assets. Reference is made to § 600.4 concerning liability limitations in force majeure scenarios involving arcane phenomena.

As mandated by § 1201.7, all contracts must include a comprehensive risk assessment prepared by a certified appraiser. This document shall outline potential hazards and mitigation strategies consistent with § 800.5 safety protocols. Failure to comply renders the agreement void ab initio. Consult § 600.3 regarding unconscionable terms and § 900.7 for standards of good faith performance.

Pursuant to § 1401.2, any party seeking to alter material provisions after execution must submit a formal amendment request subject to strict scrutiny. Unilateral modifications are strictly prohibited under § 700.6. Amendments require unanimous consent and re-execution by all signatories unless otherwise specified in the original instrument. See § 1101.8 for notification requirements.

Finally, as outlined in § 200.9, any dispute arising from such contracts shall be resolved exclusively through binding arbitration administered by a panel appointed by the Guild Sovereign. Litigation is expressly forbidden under § 500.4. The prevailing party shall be entitled to recover reasonable attorney fees and costs incurred, subject to a cap of fifty percent of the contract value unless exceptional circumstances exist per § 1301.7. This provision reflects the consensus reached at the Autumnwood Summit of 894 AR as detailed in the official proceedings archived under § 600.2.

*Archmage Veyra's Note: These provisions were drafted to protect both novice casters and their clients from predatory practices while ensuring accountability for all parties involved.*

body.heading: Contracts and Non-Magical Counterparts
body.text:
§ 600.9 Related Requirements governs the interaction between magical contracts and their mundane equivalents, particularly where non-casters are involved in the transaction or fulfillment thereof. Where a contract binds both casters and non-casters, the provisions of this Part shall apply by necessary implication to ensure equitable treatment across all parties regardless of magical aptitude. See § 100.2 regarding who may validly represent the Guild's interests in such matters.

A critical distinction exists between contracts executed solely through arcane means versus those utilizing conventional legal instruments alongside magic. In the former case, this Codex provides exclusive remedial avenues. However, when non-casters participate materially in a magical agreement—whether as guarantors, witnesses, or mere beneficiaries—they retain access to traditional contract law principles where applicable. See § 100.3 for quorum requirements involving mixed parties and § 200.5 for guest caster obligations under hybrid agreements.

The Guild acknowledges that many essential services require non-magical expertise, from financial auditing to structural engineering. Consequently, contracts incorporating both magical and mundane components shall be interpreted holistically rather than fragmented by disciplinary boundaries. Under § 100.7, foreign halls may provide courtesy interpretations when dealing with cross-jurisdictional hybrids. Emergency provisions under § 100.8 allow for expedited rulings where mixed-contract disputes threaten public safety or stability.

Familiars and constructs serving as agents in non-magical contracts are deemed extensions of their masters' legal persons under § 600.2, subject to minimum liability thresholds per § 600.4. Summoned notaries operating under § 600.5 shall execute affidavits with the same probative weight as official Guild seals pursuant to § 1.9. Any clause attempting to evade these protections through convoluted drafting shall be void ab initio under the doctrine of unconscionability codified in § 300.2 and reinforced by § 600.3 regarding geas terms.

In all cases, fairness dictates that non-casters receive notice of magical contingencies material to their obligations prior to signing. See also § 1401.8 on disclosure duties and § 1201.7 on informed consent in research contexts. The Guild maintains an official registry of approved non-magical service providers (§ 300.1) whose contracts enjoy presumptive validity within jurisdictional limits set forth in § 500.1 and § 400.2 respectively.

This framework aims to balance the unique needs of the arcane community with the established rights of ordinary citizens, fostering cooperation while safeguarding against exploitation inherent in power imbalances between casters and their clients or collaborators alike. For further guidance on specific hybrid scenarios, consult the Desk's published interpretations under § 100.4 or petition for a preliminary ruling via standard channels outlined in §§ 200.1 through 200.6.

body.heading: Contracts and Non-Magical Counterparts — Continued
body.text:
§ 600.9 Related Requirements

A contract between a caster and non-caster may include magical obligations, but such clauses are subject to strict scrutiny under § 1.7. Any provision granting the caster unfettered access to the signatory's person or property shall be deemed unconscionable and void as against public policy. See § 300.2 (Unsanctioned Arts). Furthermore, no contract may require a non-caster to surrender their legal capacity to form other agreements without explicit written consent from a licensed advocate under § 100.2. The Guild recognizes that magical contracts exist within the broader context of civil law; thus, they must not contravene fundamental rights protected by the Accords or national statutes. Under § 400.5 (Unauthorized Titan Growth), any clause compelling a party to engage in prohibited field activities shall be invalidated ab initio. Finally, disputes arising from hybrid magical-civil agreements shall be adjudicated according to this Code's penal provisions where applicable, with reference to the general principles of contract law as outlined in § 200.1 (Licensure Required). Parties are advised to seek independent legal counsel before entering into any agreement involving both mundane and arcane elements. The Guild reserves the right to void entire contracts if they pose a threat to public safety or magical security. This interpretation is binding on all signatories regardless of their prior knowledge of these restrictions. Any attempt to circumvent these safeguards shall be prosecuted as a serious offense under the relevant articles herein.

body.heading: § 600.9 Contracts with Non-Casters and Related Matters
body.text: Contracts entered into between casters and non-casters fall under the general principles of mercantile law, modified by the unique circumstances inherent to magical services. The fundamental rule remains that a contract is binding if it meets all common legal requirements: offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, and legality. However, several caveats apply specifically when magic forms part of the transactional exchange. First, any clause requiring a non-caster to perform acts that violate their own licensure or guild regulations shall be deemed void and unenforceable. Second, contracts involving restricted or forbidden arts require explicit prior approval from both the caster's licensing board and the relevant regulatory authority; failure to obtain such consent renders the agreement null ab initio. Third, provisions mandating excessive risk-taking beyond accepted safety protocols may be challenged as unconscionable under § 107(4). Finally, all contracts must clearly specify which party bears responsibility for accidental or unintended magical effects arising from performance. Absent express language to the contrary, liability shall attach to the caster who initiated the spellwork, not the passive recipient. These rules ensure fairness while preserving public safety in an increasingly complex magical economy. See also § 106(2) regarding contractual capacity and § 108(5) on unconscionability standards. Under § 109(3), disputes concerning mixed magic-mercantile agreements shall be adjudicated by a specially constituted panel including both legal experts and seasoned practitioners. This hybrid approach acknowledges the dual nature of such transactions while maintaining rigorous oversight to protect all parties involved in the arcane marketplace.

body.heading: Contracts with Non-Casters and Non-Magical Counterparts – Continued
body.text:
§ 600.9 Contracts Involving Mixed Parties and Related Matters

This Section addresses the legal complexities arising when magical contracts involve parties lacking casting abilities, whether through natural limitation or voluntary restraint under § 201.3(a). Such arrangements require heightened scrutiny to ensure fairness and prevent exploitation of vulnerable casters by those seeking arcane services without proper licensure.

A contract between a licensed caster and an unlicensed individual may be enforceable only if the latter demonstrates sufficient knowledge of magical hazards (§ 601.12) and obtains informed consent for all procedures involved. Failure to disclose material risks renders any agreement void ab initio under common law principles incorporated by reference in § 602.4. The burden of proving such disclosure lies with the caster, who must retain contemporaneous records as evidence of compliance (§ 703).

Furthermore, unlicensed parties seeking magical services shall engage only through established channels regulated by this Code. Direct transactions outside Guild oversight are prohibited except where expressly permitted under emergency provisions in § 815 or specific exemptions granted by the Sovereign Archmage (§ 901). Violation of this mandate constitutes a Class B misdemeanor punishable by fine and/or imprisonment up to six months at the discretion of the presiding Magistrate.

In cases involving familial or communal agreements where multiple unlicensed members rely on a single licensed provider, additional safeguards apply. The primary caster must maintain clear accounts of all services rendered and charges assessed, accessible upon reasonable demand (§ 604). Disputes regarding billing practices shall be resolved through binding arbitration administered by the Conservators' Office unless otherwise stipulated in writing between the parties (§ 1015).

Finally, any attempt to circumvent these protections through proxy arrangements or sub-contracting is strictly forbidden. The caster remains personally liable for all obligations undertaken under this Section regardless of delegation or third-party involvement (§ 605). This principle extends even where technicalities such as power-of-attorney documents are invoked; no instrument shall override the fundamental safeguards established herein without explicit approval from the Arcane Council itself (§ 1020).

See also § 1.7 (Construction), § 1.8 (Effective Date), and § 603 (Unconscionable Terms) for additional guidance on interpreting these provisions in context. Any ambiguities shall be resolved liberally in favor of protecting non-caster parties from undue harm or financial loss resulting from their reliance on magical services provided under this Code's framework.

body.heading: Contracts and Non-Magical Counterparts — Continued — Continued
body.text:
§ 600.9 Contracts with Non-Casters and Related Matters, Contracts with Non-Casters and Non-Magical Counterparts – Continued

A contract between a caster and a non-caster may include magical provisions only to the extent that such provisions are necessary to effectuate the parties' intent and do not contravene this Code or public policy. Any magical clause must be clearly identified, separately bargained for, and explicitly assented to by both parties prior to execution. Absent explicit agreement otherwise, standard contract principles shall apply to any non-magical aspects of such an instrument.

A caster may employ a familiar as an agent under a power-of-attorney granted in writing or through binding magical compulsion consistent with applicable laws and ethical guidelines. The scope of the familiar's authority is limited to those acts expressly delegated by the principal. Any unauthorized use of the familiar beyond this scope shall constitute a breach of contract and may expose both parties to liability for resulting damages.

A geas imposed as part of a contractual obligation is deemed unconscionable and unenforceable under any circumstances. Such provisions are inherently coercive and violate fundamental principles of personal autonomy protected by this Code. Parties seeking to bind another's conduct shall negotiate traditional covenants rather than resorting to magical compulsion.

A construct employed in the performance of contractual duties must be maintained at a minimum standard of operational safety and reliability as determined by competent evaluation. Failure to adhere to these standards may constitute negligence per se and render the employer liable for any harm resulting therefrom. Regular inspections and maintenance shall be conducted to ensure ongoing compliance with all applicable regulations and specifications.

A summoned notary possesses full authority to administer oaths, take acknowledgments, and certify documents within their sphere of influence. Any magical protections or penalties attached to such certification must be clearly disclosed and voluntarily accepted by the parties involved. Unauthorized modifications to a notarized instrument may invalidate its legal effect entirely.

All contracts involving magic shall include detailed descriptions of any associated risks, limitations, and potential consequences. Parties are advised to seek independent counsel before entering into agreements containing complex or hazardous magical provisions. Failure to disclose material facts regarding such risks may constitute fraud and void the agreement ab initio.

This section supersedes all prior conflicting rules concerning contracts involving magic. Future amendments shall specify any intentional deviations from these principles with explicit notice and consensus of the affected parties. Disputes arising under this Code shall be resolved through binding arbitration unless otherwise agreed upon by the contracting entities.

SEE ALSO: §§ 201-305 (General Contract Principles), 401-450 (Magical Liability Standards); § 600.1-600.8 (Specialized Provisions)

sections.title: Burden and Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes

body.heading: Burden and Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes
body.text:
In matters concerning the admissibility of magical evidence and testimony, particular scrutiny must be applied to phenomena that challenge conventional notions of reality. Under § 300.2, certain schools of magic are deemed unsanctioned due to their inherent dangers and ethical implications; similarly, § 700.9 establishes strict guidelines for evaluating the reliability of arcane-derived data in legal proceedings.

Scrying operations conducted within closed books or sealed environments shall be subject to rigorous oversight per § 400.2. Any evidence obtained through unauthorized divination techniques may be deemed inadmissible under § 700.3, which categorizes memory charm spells as forms of spoliation when used to manipulate witness recollections. Simulacra created via intricate illusion magic cannot serve as credible testimony absent corroboration from independent sources, a principle codified in § 700.4.

The status of cloned individuals presents unique evidentiary challenges given their shared origins yet distinct existences. While clones maintain separate legal identities under § 200.5, any claims predicated on duplication must demonstrate clear lineage and intent beyond mere replication. This framework is further elaborated in § 700.5 to prevent fraudulent assertions of identity based solely on magical reproduction.

Related requirements include but are not limited to: adherence to research permit protocols outlined in § 400.1, maintenance of proper specimen custody as mandated by § 400.3, and compliance with field casting regulations detailed in § 700.6. Failure to observe these stipulations may result in suspension or revocation of licensure pursuant to § 200.4. Furthermore, any contracts entered into involving non-casters must satisfy the formalities specified in § 501 prior to becoming enforceable under applicable law.

It is incumbent upon all practitioners to uphold the highest standards of integrity when presenting magical evidence or testimony. The integrity of our judicial system depends upon trust in the accuracy and authenticity of arcane information. To compromise this principle would undermine both the rule of law and the very foundation of our society's relationship with magic itself."

"see § 400.1 Research Permits; § 700.6 Field Casting Regulations; § 200.4 Suspension Procedures; § 501 Contract Formalities"

body.heading: § 700.10 Burden and Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes
body.text:
In all matters arising under these Accords, the burden of proof shall rest upon the party asserting an affirmative claim or defense. Where allegations involve the commission of a magical offense, the accused bears no initial obligation to disprove innocence; rather, it is incumbent upon the accuser to establish prima facie guilt by clear and convincing evidence. In civil proceedings concerning licensing disputes or contractual breaches, the preponderance of the evidence standard shall apply unless expressly modified by specific provision within this Code.

The standard of proof required for conviction in penal cases before a Paradox Trial jury is proof beyond a reasonable doubt, tempered by the unique nature of arcane phenomena which may defy conventional verification methods. In such instances, circumstantial evidence and expert testimony regarding magical signatures may be deemed sufficient to sustain an indictment if they collectively eliminate all rational alternative explanations consistent with innocence. The Presiding Archmage retains discretion to adjust evidentiary thresholds when dealing with matters of national security or existential threat posed by rogue magic users.

Witnesses shall be subject to standard rules of impeachment and cross-examination, though their competency may be questioned on grounds specific to magical ability or susceptibility to charm spells. Testimony rendered under the influence of truth-compelling enchantments shall carry double weight unless successfully challenged through lawful means such as counter-curse application or demonstration of pre-existing immunity. Where direct observation is impossible due to distance or obfuscation, secondary evidence including scrying recordings and residue analysis may be admitted subject to adversarial rebuttal.

In cases involving disputed ownership of magical artifacts or living constructs, the court shall presume bona fide possession by registered holders unless proven otherwise. Burden shifts to any party claiming superior title through theft, coercion, or fraud to present affirmative evidence establishing their rightful claim beyond a preponderance of probabilities. Where multiple parties assert concurrent interests in the same property, priority shall be determined by chronological order of lawful acquisition absent contrary stipulation binding all disputants.

Evidence obtained unlawfully or in violation of constitutional protections shall generally be inadmissible unless its probative value substantially outweighs prejudicial effect under applicable jurisprudence. Exceptions may be granted where exclusion would undermine public safety or permit continued criminal conduct, at the sole discretion of the Presiding Magistrate after full hearing. All admissions and confessions must be voluntary and knowingly given; any signed waiver shall require notarization and delivery in triplicate to respective parties of record.

The right against self-incrimination applies fully to all accused persons regardless of magical capacity or prior conviction status. Compelled testimony may be utilized solely for impeachment purposes unless the witness explicitly consents otherwise in writing witnessed by two impartial third parties. Privileged communications between attorney-client, husband-wife, and clergy-parishioner remain inviolate except upon unanimous consent of affected parties or court order finding no alternative means to ascertain material facts at stake.

This Section shall be construed liberally in favor of defendants facing serious charges while maintaining rigorous enforcement against repeat offenders and unrepentant criminals who defy the rule of law through arcane malice alone. Justice tempered with mercy remains the enduring aspiration guiding all judicial proceedings under these hallowed Accords meant to protect both citizens and society at large from the ravages of unchecked magical power wielded by madmen or worse.

see § 700.14 Admissibility Standards; see § 250.3 Rights Against Self-Incrimination; see § 850.6 Privileged Communications Exceptions under general evidentiary principles governing all Arcane Accords proceedings throughout the realm.

body.heading: § 700.9 Related Requirements — Continued
body.text:
§ 700.10 Burden and Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes
The burden of proof in any arcane dispute rests upon the accuser to establish prima facie grounds for their claim, pursuant to the foundational principles set forth in §§ 1.5–1.6. Where a defendant raises a plausible defense or counter-claim, the evidentiary obligation shifts accordingly, as dictated by the logic and fairness inherent in the system outlined in § 100.7. No party may rely solely on assertion or conjecture to carry their case; tangible evidence must be marshaled in accordance with the rules of proof detailed herein.
The standard of proof required shall vary depending upon the gravity of the allegations at issue, as elaborated in §§ 300.1–300.5 and § 400.2. For lesser infractions, a preponderance of the magical evidence may suffice to justify sanctions or remedial actions. However, for charges involving serious breaches such as unauthorized field casting (§ 500.1) or forbidden research (§ 400.3), clear and convincing proof shall be mandated before any punitive measures are imposed. In cases bearing upon public safety or the integrity of the Accord itself, proof beyond all reasonable doubt must be secured to ensure justice is properly served.
Evidence may take many forms, from written records and witness testimony to magical traces and scryed observations, each subject to rigorous scrutiny under §§ 700.2–700.5 and § 1301.4. Illegally obtained materials shall be deemed inadmissible unless their probative value substantially outweighs any potential prejudice, consistent with established judicial precedent referenced in § 800.6. Parties are urged to preserve all relevant artifacts and communications throughout the investigation, lest they find themselves penalized for spoliation under § 700.3.
In disputes involving complex or arcane matters where conventional evidence may be scarce or ambiguous, alternative methods of proof shall be employed as necessary, provided they do not undermine the principles outlined in §§ 1.8–1.9 and § 1201.5. Expert testimony from recognized authorities within the Guild carries significant weight, subject to cross-examination and verification per § 600.3. Where feasible, magical analysis or ritual reconstruction may illuminate critical facts otherwise obscured by time or obfuscation techniques detailed in §§ 400.4–400.5 and § 1101.7.
Ultimately, the goal of any evidentiary proceeding is to ascertain the truth with fairness and thoroughness, guided by the overarching tenets embodied in the Preamble of these Accords (§ 1.1) and reinforced throughout this Codebook. By adhering strictly to these requirements, all parties may trust that their grievances will be heard and resolved equitably under the wise stewardship of the Mages' Guild.

body.heading: § 700.9 Related Requirements - Continued
body.text:
In addition to the foregoing evidentiary exclusions, the following items shall also be deemed inadmissible in any arcane dispute: (A) testimony or records derived from magical scrying devices used without proper licensure; (B) confessions extracted through memory charms or other forms of mental compulsion; and (C) statements made by simulacrums or clones purporting to represent their original subjects. However, this prohibition shall not apply where such evidence is otherwise properly authenticated and the opposing party has had a full opportunity to cross-examine its sources under oath.

Furthermore, parties are prohibited from introducing any evidence obtained in violation of this Part's privacy protections, whether directly or through third-party agents acting on their behalf. This ban extends to both written materials and oral communications, regardless of medium. Violations shall constitute grounds for summary dismissal of the offending party's claims and may subject them to additional penalties under § 700.12.

The foregoing restrictions reflect a fundamental policy judgment that certain types of magical intrusion into private affairs are so egregious as to warrant complete exclusion from judicial consideration, even if technically relevant. This approach balances the need for factual accuracy in determining arcane disputes with the imperative of safeguarding individual liberties against unchecked technological overreach. Any challenges to these provisions must be raised promptly and with particularized justification, lest they be deemed waived by acquiescence.

See also §§ 700.2–700.5 regarding specific evidentiary exclusions; § 1.7(c) concerning the aggregation of prohibited acts; and § 900.3(b)(i) for additional limitations on admissible evidence in related proceedings. Any ambiguities arising from this section shall be resolved in favor of maintaining strict privacy boundaries, consistent with the overarching principles set forth herein.

body.heading: § 700.10 Burden and Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes — Continued
body.text:
In any arcane dispute brought before the Guild, the burden of proof rests upon the accuser to establish by clear and convincing evidence that a violation of these Accords has occurred. The standard for conviction is elevated beyond mere preponderance of the evidence due to the grave consequences inherent in penalizing magical practitioners for alleged infractions. Where doubt exists as to the nature or extent of the transgression, it shall be resolved most strongly against the accuser and in favor of the accused.

The court may admit various forms of expert testimony regarding arcane practices, spell structures, and ritualistic components. Such witnesses must possess recognized credentials within their fields and demonstrate impartiality in their opinions. The trier of fact is permitted to draw reasonable inferences from circumstantial evidence when direct proof is unavailable, provided such deductions are logically sound and supported by the record. However, speculative assertions unsupported by reliable data shall be disregarded entirely.

When evaluating claims of unauthorized magic usage or prohibited research activities, the Guild considers a multifaceted totality of circumstances including but not limited to: observed anomalies in magical signatures; inconsistencies between claimed abilities and documented training histories; suspicious procurement patterns for rare reagents or components; and deviations from established procedural norms without valid justification. No single factor is dispositive; rather, they are weighed collectively to ascertain whether a prima facie case has been made out before proceeding further.

In cases involving contested interpretations of vague or ambiguous provisions within these Accords, the court shall construe such language in favor of the party who relied thereupon to their detriment. This equitable principle acknowledges that practitioners cannot be expected to divinate hidden meanings without adequate notice. Consequently, any doubt as to the scope or limitations imposed by particular clauses shall remain unresolved rather than enforced against innocent parties.

Should new evidence emerge post-judgment capable of materially altering the outcome, affected individuals may petition for reconsideration within thirty days of receiving final notice. Such motions require demonstration of good faith efforts previously made to secure said proof and must explain why earlier disclosure was not feasible despite diligent pursuit. Upon review, the tribunal retains discretion either to grant relief or dismiss the appeal outright based on merit alone.

Ultimately, the goal of these evidentiary rules is to ensure fair adjudication while respecting both the sanctity of magical arts and public safety concerns. Only through rigorous application of established standards can true justice be served in this complex domain where science intersects with sorcery in unpredictable ways. See § 1.4 for persons bound by these obligations and § 300.5 regarding permissible research methodologies under supervision. Under § 1.7, all terms herein shall be given their ordinary meanings unless otherwise defined expressly herein or by reference thereto. As provided in § 1.9, any official seals affixed to documents executed pursuant to this Code shall carry full legal weight and effect throughout the Realm. Finally, nothing contained herein limits remedies available at common law or equity except where specifically abrogated by contrary statutory mandate.

body.heading: § 700.9 Related Requirements — Continued — Continued
body.text:
Under § 700.6, parties in arcane disputes must comply with additional procedural mandates to ensure fair adjudication. First, all evidence submitted shall be authenticated by an independent scribe or qualified mage of standing with the Guild. Unverified claims carry no weight and may result in sanctions against the presenting party under § 1401.7. Second, witnesses testifying regarding magical phenomena must appear in person unless excused for valid cause, such as illness or active combat duty. Remote testimony via scrying crystal is permitted only with prior written consent from both sides (§ 700.2). Third, any artifacts or items alleged to have been involved in the disputed event must be produced and made available for inspection by opposing counsel and the presiding Arcanist. Failure to do so constitutes spoliation of evidence and may lead to adverse inference rulings under § 350.14. Finally, all communications between parties concerning the dispute shall be conducted through official channels—either via registered letter or secure messaging platform approved by the Desk—to maintain a clear record for future reference (§ 900.8). These measures collectively serve to uphold the integrity of the judicial process and prevent abuse of arcane powers in the pursuit of personal gain or vendetta. By adhering strictly to these requirements, litigants demonstrate good faith and respect for the rule of law, thereby facilitating just resolution of their differences under the Autumnwood Accords.

see § 700.6 Related Requirements; see also § 1401.7 Sanctions for Non-Compliance; under § 350.14 Adverse Inference for Spoliation. This section ensures that all evidence and testimony meet rigorous standards of authenticity and relevance, preventing frivolous or manipulative claims from undermining the credibility of the arcane judiciary. Parties are expected to act in good faith throughout the proceedings, submitting only verifiable information and adhering to established protocols for communication and documentation. By doing so, they contribute to a fair and efficient resolution of their disputes, upholding the principles of justice enshrined in the Accords.

sections.title: Ex Post Facto Prohibition and Retroactive Sanctions

body.heading: Ex Post Facto Prohibition and Retroactive Sanctions
body.text:
The provisions governing penal sanctions against rogue casters are inextricably linked to several ancillary statutes designed to maintain the integrity of both the Accords and the broader magical ecosystem. First and foremost is the requirement for comprehensive background checks on all candidates undergoing Paradox Trial proceedings, under § 800.7 Related Requirements; this ensures that no individual with a history of malicious intent can exploit the trial process to further their own ends. Such vetting is critical given the sensitive nature of sealing magic permanently within an afflicted subject's soul—a procedure so dangerous it borders on heresy in its own right.

Furthermore, § 801.3 Related Requirements mandates that all trials be conducted by a panel comprising members from both Conservator and Innovator factions, preventing either side from imposing their will unilaterally. This balanced approach reflects the foundational principle of fair play enshrined throughout the Accords, while also mitigating the risk of partisan bias skewing outcomes in favor of one ideological camp over another. The presence of diverse perspectives during deliberations serves to broaden the scope of analysis and ensure that all relevant factors are duly weighed before any punitive measures are enacted upon an accused caster.

In addition to these procedural safeguards, § 802.1 Related Requirements establishes a system for post-trial review wherein decisions made under the Paradox Trial can be appealed to a higher council should either party believe they were unfairly treated during the initial proceedings. This mechanism provides much-needed recourse against potential abuses of power by lower-ranking adjudicators who may act without sufficient foresight or restraint in administering justice to those before them. By affording litigants an opportunity to challenge unfavorable rulings, the Accords uphold their commitment to equity and impartiality even amidst the inherent complexities of magical jurisprudence.

Finally, it bears noting that § 803.2 Related Requirements stipulates strict confidentiality protocols surrounding all cases brought under this section; details thereof are to be kept on a need-to-know basis alone, accessible only to those directly involved in executing sanctions or overseeing appeals processes. Breach of this secrecy mandate carries severe repercussions for any individual found guilty of leaking sensitive information regarding ongoing trials or their participants' identities. Such vigilance is paramount to protecting both the subjects of punishment and society at large from unnecessary harm arising from public exposure of volatile matters best left handled discreetly behind closed doors.

see § 800.7 Related Requirements; see § 801.3 Related Requirements; under § 802.1 Related Requirements; pursuant to § 803.2 Related Requirements.

body.heading: § 800.9 Ex Post Facto Prohibition and Retroactive Sanctions
body.text:
No provision within this Part shall be construed to impose penalties or sanctions retroactively, except as expressly authorized by the Desk under extraordinary circumstances. Any determination of guilt or violation must be based solely on conduct occurring after the effective date of the relevant rule. This principle ensures fair notice to all casters regarding permissible and prohibited magical practices. See § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks [for limitations on retroactive rulemaking]; § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse [regarding temporal scope].

In cases where ambiguity exists as to whether past conduct constituted a violation, the Desk shall apply the interpretation most favorable to the accused caster. This standard protects against arbitrary enforcement and maintains confidence in the system's impartiality. However, repeated or egregious misconduct may warrant discretionary review for potential corrective action outside the formal disciplinary process. Under § 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy [mutual recognition of judgments]; § 300.5 Research Copies of Quiet Items [exceptions to general prohibitions].

The prohibition against ex post facto sanctions does not preclude the Desk from addressing patterns of behavior that began prior to the effective date but continued thereafter. Such continuing violations are subject to full investigation and appropriate punishment regardless of when they originated. This approach balances fairness with accountability, ensuring that persistent offenders cannot evade consequences through technicalities. Per § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting [disclosure obligations]; § 400.3 Borrowed Hours [limits on temporal manipulation].

Special provisions may apply where violations involve threats to public safety or the integrity of magical research. In such instances, expedited proceedings and enhanced penalties are permissible to mitigate harm. The Desk retains broad discretion to tailor responses based on the specific facts and circumstances presented. This flexibility is essential for adapting to evolving challenges in a rapidly advancing field. As noted in § 100.8 Emergency Sitting [urgent measures]; § 500.2 Unscheduled Weather [force majeure considerations].

Ultimately, the principles of fairness and transparency guide all disciplinary actions under this Part. Casters are entitled to due process, clear notice of alleged violations, and an impartial hearing before any sanction is imposed. These safeguards preserve the legitimacy of the system while enabling effective enforcement of the Accords. For further guidance on procedural rights, consult § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild [representatives]; § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters [binding obligations].

body.heading: § 800.9 Prohibition on Ex Post Facto Penalties and Retroactive Sanctions
body.text:
No mage shall be subject to any penalty, sanction, or disciplinary measure unless such measure was expressly provided for in the Accords at the time of the alleged infraction. The principle against ex post facto punishment is sacrosanct within the Guild's jurisdiction; a rule cannot be applied retroactively to punish conduct that was lawful when performed. This prohibition extends beyond mere statutory penalties to include informal sanctions, such as social ostracism or professional blacklisting, if imposed pursuant to a newly enacted provision.

The Desk shall not adopt any new rule, interpretation, or precedent with retrospective effect unless strictly necessary to address an urgent threat to public safety or magical stability. Even in such exigent circumstances, the Desk must provide notice and opportunity for comment prior to implementation, allowing affected parties to adjust their conduct accordingly. Any exception to this standard requires a supermajority vote of the full Accords Council and explicit citation of the compelling justification therefor.

Mages shall not be held liable for violations of customs, usages, or practices that have fallen into disuse unless expressly preserved by written law. The mere fact that an action was previously tolerated or even encouraged does not immunize a caster from liability should such practice later be proscribed. Conversely, longstanding customs and understandings may inform the Desk's exercise of its discretionary authority in determining appropriate sanctions for infractions lacking precise statutory guidance.

In all cases, penalties shall be proportional to the gravity of the offense and tailored to achieve rehabilitation where possible. The Desk shall not impose harsher measures than those necessary to vindicate the Accords' purposes or protect the public welfare. Excessive punishments, whether by design or accident, are void ab initio and may be challenged on that ground alone. This requirement applies with equal force to both formal adjudications and informal disciplinary proceedings conducted by authorized agents of the Guild.

No mage shall be subjected to double jeopardy for a single transgression. A finding of guilt in one proceeding precludes subsequent punishment for the same act, whether in another venue or under a different guise. The Desk retains authority to revisit a case only upon demonstration that the prior determination was flawed due to error, fraud, or newly discovered evidence materially affecting the outcome. Absent such grounds, past judgments stand conclusive and binding on all parties.

The prohibition against retroactive sanctions serves as a fundamental safeguard of individual liberty and legal certainty within the magical community. It ensures that mages may regulate their conduct according to known standards without fear of arbitrary or unexpected consequences. By adhering strictly to this principle, the Guild fosters trust in its institutions and maintains the rule of law amidst the inherent uncertainties of arcane practice.

body.heading: Prohibition on Ex Post Facto Penalties and Retroactive Sanctions
Prohibition on Retroactive Penalties
body.text:
No penalty, sanction, or adverse consequence may be imposed upon any person for conduct that was not unlawful at the time it occurred. This principle serves as a cornerstone of due process within the Accords and reflects the fundamental fairness expected of all governing bodies under the Guild's jurisprudence. The prohibition extends to both civil and criminal contexts, ensuring that mages are not subjected to arbitrary punishment based on subsequent changes in law or policy interpretations.

Any attempt to apply ex post facto penalties shall be deemed void ab initio and subject to immediate reversal by a competent tribunal upon proper challenge. Courts possess inherent authority to scrutinize the temporal applicability of sanctions against accused parties, with a heavy presumption favoring the defendant when doubt exists as to whether conduct violated established norms at the relevant point in time. This safeguard prevents abuse of power by rogue magistrates or factions seeking to manipulate legal standards for political gain.

The prohibition also encompasses indirect penalties arising from retroactively altered regulations or guidelines. For instance, if a new rule were promulgated that criminalized previously permissible magical practices, such change could not be used to penalize individuals for actions taken prior to its enactment unless explicit transitional provisions were included. This limitation protects against chilling effects on legitimate research and practice while maintaining flexibility for the Guild to adapt evolving understandings of magic safely.

Exceptions to this rule are narrowly construed and must satisfy rigorous scrutiny. Retroactive sanctions may only be justified in cases involving grave threats to public safety or national security where advance warning was impracticable given the nature of the danger posed. Even then, strict procedural safeguards apply to ensure that any such measures remain proportional and necessary rather than punitive in character. The burden rests squarely on those seeking to enforce retroactive penalties to demonstrate compelling justification beyond mere administrative convenience or ideological purity.

This provision stands as a bulwark against capricious governance and arbitrary enforcement within the arcane community. By anchoring disciplinary actions in contemporaneous law, it fosters predictability and trust between regulators and regulated entities alike - essential qualities for maintaining stability amidst the constant flux of magical innovation and discovery.

body.heading: Prohibition on Retroactive Penalties — Continued
body.text:
No sanction, seal, or penalty imposed under these Accords shall have any legal effect unless expressly authorized by the full text of this Code at the time the alleged violation occurred. The Desk shall not have power to create new offenses or aggravate existing ones through retroactive interpretation or application. This principle is fundamental to maintaining trust between the Guild and those subject to its jurisdiction.

Under § 100.5, a caster may not be held liable for conduct that was lawful when performed, even if later reclassified under revised standards. Similarly, sanctions imposed prior to any amendment shall remain valid unless overturned on proper procedural grounds. Conversely, a new provision cannot apply to past actions except where explicitly stated. This ensures fairness and prevents arbitrary punishment based on shifting definitions of acceptable magical practice.

The prohibition extends beyond formal penalties to include informal censure or reputational damage inflicted by the Desk. While individual casters retain their right to criticize Guild actions freely, official reprimands must be grounded in clear, contemporaneous rules. Retroactive disciplinary measures undermine the integrity of the entire regulatory framework and invite abuse of power by rogue officials seeking personal vendettas under false pretenses.

Violations of this clause shall constitute grounds for immediate appeal and potential disqualification of the offending order from future proceedings. Repeated offenders may face removal from office permanently, along with civil liability for any resulting harms. The Desk must adhere strictly to established legal principles at all times, recognizing that its authority derives solely from lawful enactment rather than arbitrary fiat.

In sum, these safeguards protect both casters and the Guild against capricious governance while preserving the flexibility needed to adapt to evolving magical discoveries. By anchoring enforcement in clear, pre-existing norms, the Accords maintain their legitimacy as a stable foundation for orderly coexistence between magic-users and society at large. Any departure from this core tenet risks unraveling the delicate balance achieved through years of hard-won compromise.
