sections.title: Construction and Interpretation

body.heading: § 200.10 Related Requirements - Construction and Interpretation
body.text:
The provisions of this Part shall be construed in accordance with the principles set forth in §§ 1.7–1.9, including the rules of aggregation, savings, and seal recognition established therein. In particular, any ambiguity regarding the scope or application of these requirements shall be resolved favorably to public safety and magical stability. The Guild reserves the right to issue binding interpretations via official memorandum when necessary to clarify the intent behind specific clauses.

This section is not intended to limit the authority granted under §§ 100–400, but rather to ensure consistent enforcement across all levels of operation. Violations may result in penalties ranging from formal admonishment to complete revocation of licensure, depending on severity and prior history. The Aegis Magi are empowered to investigate suspected infractions at their discretion and impose provisional sanctions pending full adjudication by the Desk.

It is further provided that nothing herein shall be construed as granting any additional rights or privileges beyond those explicitly enumerated in this Codex. All magical practitioners must adhere strictly to these standards without deviation, regardless of personal opinion or external pressure. The Guild stands ready to defend its prerogatives against all challenges, whether from rogue elements or misguided allies alike.

See also § 1.4 for persons bound by the Accords; §§ 300–500 for detailed operational protocols; and § 600.1 regarding contractual obligations between casters and non-casters. Failure to comply with these requirements constitutes a breach of contract under applicable law, subjecting violators to civil liability in addition to any criminal sanctions imposed by the Guild. The Desk shall retain sole jurisdiction over all disputes arising from this Part unless otherwise specified herein or by mutual agreement of the parties involved.

In witness whereof, I have set my hand and seal on this tenth day thereof, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-four.
*By Command of the Autumnwood Accords Desk*

body.heading: Construction and Interpretation of Licensure Provisions
body.text:
The provisions governing licensure requirements must be construed in accordance with the foundational principles set forth in § 100.5, which establishes that any casting within the jurisdiction of this Desk shall comply with all applicable accords absent explicit exemption. As further detailed under § 200.4, a failure to maintain valid licensure does not merely constitute an administrative infraction but rather renders the individual's magical activity ultra vires and subject to immediate cessation by enforcement officers. This strict adherence is mandated because unregulated practice poses existential risks to both public safety and the integrity of arcane research itself, as acknowledged in the preamble of this Codex.

Furthermore, where ambiguity exists regarding whether specific conduct necessitates licensure, such questions shall be resolved favorably toward the imposition of regulatory obligations rather than their waiver. This approach aligns with the precautionary ethos enshrined in § 100.2, which places the burden on practitioners to demonstrate clear authority for any magical operations undertaken under their name or auspices. Consequently, mere claims of emergency necessity or special circumstances will not automatically exempt an individual from licensure mandates unless such exceptions are expressly enumerated elsewhere within this Part or by prior ruling of the Desk itself.

In interpreting the scope of "licensure requirements," it is deemed that these encompass not only formal certifications but also any de facto authorization granted through verbal assent, written permits, or customary practice accepted by relevant oversight bodies. Thus, a caster operating without explicit documentation may nonetheless be found in compliance if they can produce credible evidence of implicit sanction from competent authorities having jurisdiction over their area of activity. This flexible reading seeks to balance administrative rigor with practical realities inherent in the fluid nature of magical arts.

Ultimately, all questions concerning licensure shall be guided by the overarching goal of ensuring that every act of casting serves the greater good while minimizing potential harms. Where doubt persists after diligent analysis, reference should be made to § 100.7 regarding foreign halls and courtesy, which provides a framework for resolving cross-border disputes through cooperative dialogue rather than unilateral enforcement actions. By embracing this holistic perspective, we affirm our shared commitment to advancing magical knowledge responsibly for the benefit of all humanity.

see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; see § 100.2 Who May Speak for the Guild; see § 300.1 Schedules of Arts.

body.heading: Construction and Interpretation of Licensure Provisions — Continued
body.text:
The provisions of this Part governing licensure shall be construed liberally to effectuate their purpose, which is the protection of the public from unqualified practice of the arcane arts. Ambiguities in these sections shall be resolved in favor of the applicant unless a plain reading would create an unreasonable burden inconsistent with established Guild custom and precedent. See § 100.7 for guidance on applying courtesy standards to licensure disputes, and under § 300.4 regarding reclassification petitions.

In determining whether an individual qualifies for licensure, the Board shall consider not only technical competence but also moral character and professional judgment. A history of unethical conduct, even if unrelated directly to magic practice, may be grounds for denial or revocation of a license. See § 1201.7(c)(4) for examples of disqualifying behaviors. The burden of proof rests upon the applicant to demonstrate fitness by clear and convincing evidence, not mere preponderance of the evidence standard.

Licensure granted under this Part shall be presumed valid unless overturned through proper administrative channels. Challenges must be brought within thirty days of final decision and limited solely to matters of law or gross error of fact. The Board's factual findings are conclusive absent clear proof to the contrary. See § 1401.5 for procedural requirements on appeals, and under § 900.8 regarding remedies for abuse of discretion.

The licensing scheme herein establishes a comprehensive regulatory regime intended to balance innovation with safety. It is not merely a set of bureaucratic hurdles but an essential safeguard against the dangers posed by untrained manipulation of powerful forces. Citizens rely upon these protections in their daily lives, from air quality monitoring to structural integrity assessments. Disregard for this framework endangers public welfare and undermines the Guild's mandate to serve society responsibly. See § 500.1(b) on duty of care imposed upon licensed practitioners, and under § 200.3(c)(ii) concerning limitations on temporary authority grants.

This Part operates as an integrated whole, each provision interdependent upon the others in achieving its objectives. No single clause may be isolated from context when interpreting rights and obligations created thereby. The Board retains inherent equitable powers to fill gaps where necessary to serve justice and promote orderly development of magical technologies. See § 1301.6 for scope of administrative discretion, and under § 700.9 regarding implied duties arising from statutory schemes.

By establishing clear standards and oversight mechanisms, these licensure provisions foster trust between the Guild and the communities it serves. They ensure that magic remains a benefit rather than a hazard to public safety while enabling beneficial applications of arcane knowledge. Compliance with this framework is not optional but fundamental to lawful practice within the realm. See § 1101.3 on compliance obligations generally, and under § 600.2 for consequences of non-adherence specific to licensed entities.

The authority vested in the Board by these provisions shall be exercised diligently, impartially, and with full regard for the public interest. It is a sacred trust requiring constant vigilance against corruption and negligence. Only so can the Guild maintain its reputation as a guardian of both progress and protection in an increasingly complex world. See § 100.2(b) on fiduciary duties of officers, and under § 400.6 regarding transparency requirements for decision-making processes.

body.heading: Interpretation and Enforcement Standards
body.text: The licensure provisions herein shall be construed liberally in favor of public safety and magical integrity, notwithstanding any contrary implication that might arise from strict literalism. See § 1.7 (Construction) for general interpretive principles applicable to all Accords. When determining whether a particular magical activity falls within the scope of this section, courts are directed to examine not only the nominal classification of the spellwork but also its actual effects and potential consequences. Under § 300.2 (Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts), even ostensibly benign rituals may be deemed illicit if their ultimate purpose contravenes core tenets of the Accords. The burden of proof rests upon those alleging a violation to establish both fact and intent beyond reasonable doubt, consistent with due process guarantees implicit in § 100.2 (Who May Speak for the Guild). In cases where ambiguity persists despite thorough adjudication, the Desk may defer to expert testimony or commission additional inquiries as warranted by the circumstances presented. See § 400.3 (Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time) regarding temporal calculations that might influence liability assessments. The spirit of these regulations transcends mere technical compliance; they embody a profound commitment to maintaining harmony between magic and society at large. Any interpretation thereof must reflect this overarching ethos while remaining faithful to the precise wording employed by the framers themselves. Should future developments necessitate clarification or modification, such changes shall be enacted through proper legislative channels rather than judicial fiat absent compelling exigency. For further guidance on related matters of construction, reference is made to §§ 100.5 (Conflict of Interest in Casting) and 200.8 (Related Requirements), which address overlapping concerns with distinct analytical frameworks as appropriate. Ultimately, the goal remains constant: ensuring that magic serves rather than subverts the greater good under wise stewardship guided by these sacred precepts laid down by our ancestors and refined through centuries of collective wisdom gained hard-won experience. Thus shall we preserve both tradition and progress in balance eternal across all lands governed hereby forthwith into perpetuity unless superseded by duly authorized amendment approved by supermajority vote of full membership assembled quarterly at least.

body.heading: § 200.10 Construction and Interpretation - Licensure Provisions
body.text:
§ 200.10 Construction and Interpretation — Licensure Provisions shall be construed to effectuate their purposes, consistent with the fundamental principles of magic regulation as enshrined in the Autumnwood Accords. In resolving ambiguities or gaps within this Part, the Desk shall adopt a purposive approach, seeking to balance public safety with the legitimate interests of licensed practitioners and the broader magical community. Any doubt regarding the scope or application of licensure requirements shall be resolved in favor of strict compliance, ensuring that all casting activities proceed under appropriate oversight. This standard of rigor is necessary to maintain trust in the Guild's regulatory framework and to prevent exploitation of any loopholes that might undermine its integrity. Furthermore, where multiple provisions appear to conflict, they shall be harmonized through systematic analysis, with priority given to those reflecting higher values such as human dignity and environmental stewardship. The Desk retains discretion to issue binding interpretations as needed to clarify evolving legal issues arising from technological advances or changing social mores. Such interpretive guidance will be published in the Official Gazette for universal dissemination and shall carry the full force of law until superseded by subsequent enactments."

body.heading: § 200.10 Construction and Interpretation — Licensure Provisions
body.text:
§ 200.10 shall govern the construction, interpretation, and application of all licensure-related provisions contained herein, including but not limited to those set forth in §§ 200.1 through 200.9 inclusive. In interpreting such provisions, the following principles shall apply: first, that any ambiguity or doubt regarding the scope or meaning of a licensure requirement shall be resolved in favor of the public interest and safety; second, that the intent and purpose underlying each provision shall guide its application, even where literal wording might suggest otherwise; third, that all terms used herein shall bear their ordinary meanings unless defined expressly elsewhere within this Code.

Notably, any provisions deemed inconsistent with one another shall be construed as complementary rather than contradictory, with all applicable rules operating concurrently to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework. Where multiple standards could apply to a given circumstance, the more stringent requirement shall prevail. Furthermore, nothing in these licensure provisions shall be construed to exempt any person from liability for acts or omissions occurring outside the scope of licensed activity or authority granted herein.

The undersigned parties hereby acknowledge and agree that they understand fully the gravity of compliance with all terms set forth above, particularly those directly affecting public safety and welfare. Breach of such obligations may result in severe penalties, including but not limited to revocation of licensure, civil damages, and criminal prosecution as provided by law. By executing this instrument, each party accepts binding responsibility for strict adherence to the herein-stated standards.

This section is enacted with full knowledge and intent to establish clear guidelines governing all aspects of professional magical practice within the jurisdiction. Violations thereof shall be treated seriously, as they threaten not only individual welfare but the very fabric of civilized society itself. All parties are charged with vigilant observance and prompt rectification of any perceived irregularities arising under these mandates.

*See also § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 300.2 Necromancy, Unsanctioned Arts; § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs.*

sections.title: The Unsanctioned Arts and the Quiet List

body.heading: § 300.10 Related Requirements: The Unsanctioned Arts and the Quiet List
body.text:
§ 300.10 Related Requirements: The Unsanctioned Arts and the Quiet List

The provisions governing unsanctioned magical practices and the associated regulatory mechanisms are hereby clarified as follows. First, any school or technique of magic not explicitly enumerated in the Schedules of Arts contained within § 300.1 shall be presumed to fall under the category of "Unsanctioned Arts." This presumption may be rebutted only by demonstrating that said practice is functionally equivalent to a sanctioned art and does not pose an undue risk to public safety or magical equilibrium.

Second, the procedures for listing Unsanctioned Arts on the Quiet List shall adhere strictly to the guidelines set forth in § 300.3. All requests for reclassification must be submitted in triplicate to the Autumnwood Accords Desk, accompanied by a comprehensive technical analysis and risk assessment prepared by an accredited Arcane Analyst or equivalent authority. Such submissions shall be reviewed within ten (10) calendar days of receipt and a written determination issued accordingly. Any party aggrieved by such determination may petition for reconsideration once per calendar year.

Third, the original owner or custodian of any item classified as Unsanctioned upon inclusion on the Quiet List shall retain possession thereof unless ordered otherwise by a competent authority under § 300.5. However, transfer, sale, or disposal of said items without prior written authorization from the Desk is strictly prohibited and punishable as a Class A Felony under Article IV of the Accords. Violators shall forfeit all rights to any proceeds derived from such unauthorized transactions, which shall revert to the Guild Treasury.

Fourth, parties seeking to conduct research into Unsanctioned Arts must obtain a formal Permit for Restricted Investigation pursuant to § 400.1. Such permits are granted on an exceptional basis only and require approval by both the Conservators and Innovators factions represented at the Desk. The scope of permitted investigation shall be narrowly tailored to the stated objectives and subject to rigorous oversight throughout its duration. Failure to adhere to permit conditions may result in immediate revocation and criminal prosecution.

Fifth, all materials related to Unsanctioned Arts and the Quiet List process shall remain confidential and subject to privilege under § 100.7. Disclosure of such information outside official channels is prohibited without express consent from all affected parties or a court order issued upon proper cause shown. Breach of this confidentiality requirement shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action against the responsible individual(s).

Sixth, periodic audits shall be conducted by an independent body appointed jointly by the Conservators and Innovators to assess compliance with these provisions and identify areas for potential improvement. Findings from such audits shall be reported directly to the Desk for review and appropriate remedial measures as deemed necessary. Results of these evaluations shall be made publicly available upon completion, subject only to redaction of sensitive information protected by law or privilege.

Seventh, nothing herein shall be construed to limit the inherent authority of the Autumnwood Accords to regulate magic in a manner consistent with its overarching purposes and principles. This section represents an expansion rather than a restriction of said authority, intended solely to provide greater clarity and predictability for all parties subject to these laws. Future amendments may be made as needed to address emerging challenges or refine existing rules where warranted by experience gained in implementation.

Eighth, finally, all persons bound hereby are reminded that the Accords exist to protect both magical society at large and individual practitioners alike from the dangers posed by unregulated arcane practices. By participating fully in this regulatory framework, users of magic demonstrate their commitment to responsible stewardship of this powerful force and reinforce our collective resilience against those who would exploit it for selfish or malevolent ends.

body.heading: § 300.10 Related Requirements: Prohibition on Unsanctioned Magical Practices
body.text:
Under no circumstances shall any individual, whether licensed by the Guild or not, engage in the practice of magic deemed "unsanctioned" under § 300.2 without prior written authorization from the Conservator's Council. Such unauthorized magical activity is hereby declared a violation of these Accords and subject to immediate punitive measures, including but not limited to sealing of magical abilities, imprisonment, or exile depending on the severity of the infraction. The prohibition extends to all forms of forbidden magic, regardless of intent or outcome, reflecting the Guild's unwavering commitment to maintaining control over arcane disciplines within its jurisdiction.

The term "unsanctioned" encompasses any magical technique not explicitly listed in the official Schedules of Arts (§ 300.1) or specifically approved by the Council for limited use under strict conditions. This broad definition ensures that novel and potentially dangerous practices remain outside the realm of acceptable magic until thoroughly vetted for public safety. The Conservator's Council retains sole authority to determine which magical arts qualify as unsanctioned, with final say in all disputes arising from such determinations.

Individuals caught practicing unsanctioned magic shall be subject to a swift trial before an impartial panel of Guild magistrates, who will assess the nature and extent of the violation. Penalties may range from fines and license revocation to permanent exile or execution in cases where the act posed significant risk to public welfare. The burden of proof rests solely on the accused to demonstrate that their actions did not violate the spirit and letter of these Accords. Failure to meet this high standard will result in full imposition of prescribed punishments without further recourse.

It shall be a capital offense for any Guild member to knowingly aid or abet unsanctioned magical practices, whether through provision of equipment, instruction, or mere acquiescence. Such complicity undermines the very foundations of lawful magic and must be met with the severest consequences under these laws. The Council reserves the right to act preemptively against suspected violators even absent concrete evidence of wrongdoing, citing national security concerns as justification for their actions.

These provisions serve as a cornerstone of the Accords' regulatory framework, establishing clear boundaries around acceptable magical activity while granting the Conservator's Council broad discretionary powers to enforce compliance. Adherence to these stringent restrictions is mandatory for all individuals operating within Guild jurisdiction, regardless of status or affiliation. Failure to comply will result in swift and severe repercussions as outlined herein.

The prohibition on unsanctioned magic reflects the deep-seated fears and anxieties surrounding unregulated arcane practices throughout history. By maintaining strict control over what constitutes acceptable magic, the Guild seeks to minimize potential harm while preserving its position as the ultimate arbiter of magical affairs within society at large. These measures stand as a testament to the enduring wisdom of cautious prudence in matters of profound power and responsibility.

Under § 300.10 Related Requirements: Prohibition on Unsanctioned Magical Practices, any individual engaging in unauthorized magic faces immediate punitive action including sealing of abilities, imprisonment or exile depending on severity. The term "unsanctioned" covers all techniques not listed in official Schedules (§ 300.1) or approved by Council for limited use only. Violators face trial before magistrates with penalties ranging from fines to execution based on risk posed. Complicity carries equal weight as direct violation and results in capital punishment. These measures underscore the Guild's commitment to controlling arcane disciplines within its jurisdiction through broad discretionary powers vested in the Conservator's Council. Non-compliance will be met with swift severity regardless of status or affiliation as outlined herein. Such provisions reflect historical apprehensions surrounding unregulated magic while affirming the Council's role as ultimate arbiter of acceptable practice. Adherence remains mandatory for all within Guild bounds lest they incur grave consequences under these laws.

body.heading: § 300.10 Related Requirements: The Unsanctioned Arts and the Quiet List — Continued
body.text:
The prohibition on unsanctioned magical practices is not merely a restriction upon individual liberty, but a safeguard for the collective integrity of society itself. Under § 300.2, necromancy and other "dark arts" are absolutely forbidden, reflecting a profound societal consensus that certain forms of magic pose an existential threat to the natural order. This stance is codified further in § 1401.7, which mandates strict accountability for all magical activities. The purpose of these restrictions is twofold: first, to prevent the misuse of powerful forces by unscrupulous individuals; and second, to preserve the sanctity of knowledge itself against those who would exploit it for selfish ends.

The Quiet List serves as the operational mechanism through which these prohibitions are enforced. As outlined in § 300.3, the Accords Desk maintains a confidential roster of banned or highly regulated items and techniques. This list is not a matter of public record, underscoring the delicate balance between necessary secrecy and open discourse. Under § 1201.8, disclosure of Quiet List contents outside official channels constitutes grounds for disciplinary action, lest its sensitive nature be compromised by irresponsible dissemination. The Desk's discretion in compiling and updating this list is broad, reflecting the evolving threats posed by both established and emerging magical practices.

Reclassification under § 300.4 represents a critical adaptive function within the regulatory framework. As new phenomena arise or existing knowledge expands, the Accords Desk must reassess its categorizations accordingly. This flexibility ensures that the law remains relevant without sacrificing stability. The process is rigorous, involving expert consultation and thorough deliberation before any changes are enacted. Such care is essential to maintain public confidence in the system's fairness and efficacy.

Research permits under § 300.5 provide a controlled avenue for studying otherwise prohibited arts under supervised conditions. These exceptions recognize the legitimate academic and scientific value of such inquiries while mitigating associated risks. The Desk retains ultimate authority over grant approval, ensuring that research aligns with broader safety objectives. Unauthorized study outside this framework is strictly forbidden, as it undermines established safeguards and invites dangerous experimentation.

Ultimately, the ban on unsanctioned magic stems from a deep-seated recognition of our collective vulnerability in the face of such potent forces. By regulating their use through robust oversight mechanisms like the Quiet List and reclassification procedures, society seeks to harness innovation without sacrificing security. This delicate equilibrium requires constant vigilance and adaptability, guided by sound judgment and unwavering commitment to the public good. Only thus can we navigate the complex terrain of magical advancement while preserving what truly matters most—our shared future.

body.heading: § 300.10 Related Requirements - Prohibition on Unsanctioned Magical Practices
body.text:
The Unsanctioned Arts, as codified in this Part, constitute the most severe category of magical misdeeds under the Autumnwood Accords. These practices are deemed fundamentally incompatible with civilized society and pose an existential threat to both the natural order and the stability of magic itself. Consequently, any caster found engaging in unsanctioned arts commits a grave breach of their licensing obligations and subjects themselves to immediate disciplinary action by the Aegis Magi.

The scope of prohibited conduct encompasses all forms of forbidden research, unauthorized field testing, illicit spellcasting for personal gain, and any other activity that circumvents the established regulatory framework. This includes but is not limited to: the creation or deployment of unregistered artifacts, the cultivation of sentient magical entities without proper permits, the use of pocket dimensions as private laboratories, and the deliberate tampering with local ley lines for selfish ends. Each such act constitutes a violation of § 300.1 and exposes the offender to prosecution under relevant penal provisions.

Violations of this nature are met with swift and decisive enforcement by the Aegis Magi, who possess broad powers to investigate, seize evidence, and apprehend suspects without warrant where reasonable cause exists. Upon arrest, individuals face summary trial before a competent tribunal, which may impose sanctions ranging from license revocation to permanent exile from the Guild's jurisdiction in extreme cases. Repeat offenders are subject to enhanced penalties, including magical sealing of their abilities as punishment for abusing their gifts.

The prohibition extends beyond mere technicalities to encompass the spirit and intent behind every clause of this Code. Even when operating within strict legal bounds, casters must exercise due diligence to ensure their activities do not inadvertently facilitate unsanctioned practices by others. Failure to exercise reasonable caution in safeguarding one's own work may result in liability for downstream harms caused by negligent security measures.

Ultimately, adherence to these standards reflects the highest ideals of responsible magical stewardship and mutual respect among practitioners. By voluntarily submitting to such rigorous oversight, members of the Guild affirm their commitment to preserving magic as a force for good rather than chaos. This shared dedication forms the bedrock upon which all future advancements in the field will rest securely.

see § 300.1 Schedules of Arts; see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; see § 300.3 Quiet List Procedure; under § 1.4 Persons Bound regarding scope of obligation.

body.heading: § 300.10 Prohibition on Unsanctioned Magical Practices
body.text:
The Accords strictly prohibit the practice of any magical arts not explicitly enumerated in Schedules of Arts appended hereto, whether by individuals or entities under their jurisdiction. Such unenumerated practices are deemed "Unsanctioned Arts" and shall be treated as illegal without exception. Any person found engaging in Unsanctioned Arts shall be subject to immediate arrest and prosecution under the Penal Provisions herein. Exceptions may only be granted through a formal determination by the Mages' Guild Desk upon presentation of compelling evidence demonstrating necessity for public welfare or scientific advancement, with strict limitations imposed on scope and duration. Unauthorized experimentation with Unsanctioned Arts is categorically forbidden, as such acts pose unacceptable risks to both casters and society at large. The burden of proof rests solely on those seeking dispensation from this prohibition. Violators shall forfeit all rights to Guild protection and face severe sanctions upon conviction. The Desk retains sole authority to interpret the scope of "Unsanctioned Arts" for purposes of enforcement under § 100.2. This provision operates independently of any other clause within these Accords, reflecting the fundamental principle that certain magical disciplines remain beyond human mastery and must be strictly contained lest they bring ruin upon all who dwell beneath this sunlit sky.

see § 300.1 Schedules of Arts; see § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts; see § 400.1 Research Permits for limited exceptions under closely supervised conditions.

body.heading: § 300.10 Prohibition on Unsanctioned Magical Practices — Continued
body.text:
No practitioner shall engage in the practice, study, or dissemination of any magical discipline listed as "Unsanctioned" under this Part without prior written authorization from the Guild Desk. Violation constitutes a Class B Felony and subjects the offender to immediate seizure by Aegis Magi for trial before a Paradox Jury. See § 300.2 for specific examples of Unsanctioned Arts, including necromancy, blood magic, soul-binding rituals, and forbidden summoning rites.

The Guild retains sole authority to classify any magical technique as "Unsanctioned" upon majority vote of the Accords Desk. Such determinations are binding and non-appealable except through a full Paradox Trial initiated by an aggrieved party. Unauthorized attempts to circumvent these prohibitions, whether by disguise, subterfuge, or technological aid, will be treated as aggravated offenses punishable by permanent sealing of all magical faculties. See § 300.6 for penalties applicable to Unsanctioned Arts violations.

Practitioners suspected of engaging in illegal magical activities must submit themselves to immediate inspection and testing by designated Guild Enforcers upon command. Refusal to comply renders the subject an automatic fugitive, liable to arrest without warrant. All evidence gathered during lawful inspections shall be admissible in subsequent proceedings under § 1024 of the Evidence Code.

The prohibition on Unsanctioned Arts does not extend to historical study or theoretical analysis conducted within accredited institutions and under direct supervision of licensed faculty members. Such educational pursuits require annual renewal of institutional certification by the Guild, contingent upon satisfactory audit results. See § 300.7 for guidelines governing lawful magical research.

Any practitioner found guilty of violating this section faces not only criminal sanctions but also civil liability for damages resulting from their unlawful activities. Joint and several liability shall attach to any partners, employers, or affiliates who knowingly facilitated the prohibited conduct. Punitive damages may be assessed at the discretion of the court up to three times actual losses suffered by complainants.

The Guild reserves the right to initiate ex parte injunctions against entities or individuals posing imminent threats to public safety through Unsanctioned magical practices. Such emergency orders remain in effect until superseded by final judgment, subject only to expedited judicial review. Failure to comply with an injunction shall result in immediate contempt proceedings and automatic forfeiture of all Guild licenses held by the respondent. See § 300.8 regarding interim relief procedures.

This section shall be construed liberally to protect the public welfare from the dangers posed by unregulated magical experimentation and application. Ambiguities herein are resolved in favor of strict enforcement, consistent with the paramount interest of safeguarding society against arcane excesses. Nothing herein shall limit the Guild's inherent police powers under § 201 et seq. of this Code.

"Unsanctioned Arts" include but are not limited to: necromancy, blood magic, soul-binding rituals, forbidden summoning rites, and any other discipline deemed inherently dangerous by the Accords Desk. See Appendix A for a comprehensive listing of currently prohibited practices. Practitioners must consult this list regularly as classifications may be updated with notice.

Violation of § 300.10 carries penalties ranging from fines up to $50,000 per offense to imprisonment not exceeding ten years, depending on circumstances and prior record. Aggravating factors include use of weapons of mass destruction, infliction of serious bodily harm, or endangerment of large populations. Mitigating considerations may warrant reduced sentences for first-time offenders who demonstrate genuine remorse and willingness to undergo mandatory rehabilitation. See § 300.9 for sentencing guidelines applicable to Unsanctioned Arts violations."

sections.title: Research Oversight and Audit Procedures

body.heading: Research Oversight and Audit Procedures
body.text: In addition to the foregoing stipulations governing research permits and specimen handling, this Part shall be read in conjunction with various provisions of the Autumnwood Accords that bear upon laboratory safety and containment protocols. See specifically §§ 200.6 (constructs as licensed agents) and § 300.4 (reclassification procedures), both of which inform the scope of permissible experimental activity under a granted permit. Furthermore, researchers shall adhere to all relevant guidelines promulgated by the Aegis Magi regarding the secure storage of volatile reagents; failure to do so may result in immediate revocation of credentials and potential criminal prosecution under Title IX of the Accords. This requirement does not relieve the principal investigator of ultimate liability for any mishap occurring within their purview, nor shall it excuse negligence or willful misconduct on the part of subordinate staff. As a final note, all research conducted pursuant to these regulations must be logged in the Guild's official records with full transparency as to methodology and results; this serves both as an archival necessity and a means of accountability for future reference should adverse effects arise. Researchers are reminded that their privileges are contingent upon ongoing compliance with every clause herein contained, and that the Council retains absolute discretion to modify these requirements at any time without notice. Thus, one must remain ever vigilant in observing not only the letter but also the spirit of the law as interpreted by duly constituted authorities. Only through such rigorous adherence can we hope to advance our understanding of magic's myriad facets while safeguarding society from its inherent perils—a balance that demands constant vigilance and unwavering dedication on the part of all who engage in this noble, yet fraught, endeavor.

body.heading: § 400.10 Research Oversight and Audit Procedures
body.text:
§ 400.10 shall govern the periodic review and auditing of all research activities conducted under the provisions of Part IV, including but not limited to the issuance, utilization, and termination of research permits granted pursuant to § 400.1. All such audits shall be performed by a designated team of independent magisters appointed by the Desk, acting in an advisory capacity without binding authority except as expressly delegated herein. The audit process shall commence no later than six months following the expiration of each permit term and shall extend for a period not exceeding ninety (90) days thereafter, during which time access to all relevant records, facilities, and personnel associated with the permitted research shall be made available upon reasonable notice.

The primary objectives of any § 400.10 audit are twofold: first, to verify compliance with the terms and conditions specified in the original permit; second, to assess whether the research has yielded results consistent with its stated aims or if unanticipated effects have arisen that might warrant further investigation or containment measures. To this end, auditors shall examine both quantitative data outputs and qualitative observations made by researchers throughout the course of their work, cross-referencing findings against baseline metrics established prior to project initiation where feasible. Particular attention shall be paid to any incidents involving anomalous phenomena, equipment malfunctions, personnel injuries or illnesses, or deviations from approved methodologies—all of which may signal underlying hazards requiring immediate remediation.

Upon completion of the audit, a comprehensive report detailing all discoveries and recommendations shall be submitted to the Desk for final review and disposition. This document shall become part of the permanent record maintained under § 100.4 and shall inform future policy decisions regarding similar research endeavors within the Guild's jurisdiction. Should any serious violations or safety concerns emerge during the audit process, emergency protocols outlined in § 500.3 may be invoked as necessary to protect public welfare while preserving evidentiary integrity for subsequent disciplinary proceedings. Ultimately, the overarching goal of § 400.10 remains the continued safeguarding of both magical knowledge and human life through vigilant oversight and transparent accountability mechanisms embedded within the fabric of responsible scholarly pursuit.

see also: § 300.5 Specimen Custody; § 400.2 Pocket Dimensions as Labs; § 100.8 Emergency Sitting Authority under extraordinary circumstances arising from audit findings.

body.heading: Research Oversight and Audit Procedures
body.text:
The Innovator faction, under the leadership of Archmage Janna Brightspark, has championed an aggressive expansion of magical research activities within the Guild's facilities. While this initiative promises unprecedented advancements in arcane theory and practical application, it also introduces significant risks to public safety and Guild stability. To mitigate these dangers, § 400.10 establishes a rigorous system of oversight and auditing for all research projects conducted under permit.

Every approved research project shall be assigned an Oversight Committee, composed of no fewer than three senior mages with expertise relevant to the subject matter. The Committee shall review the full proposal prior to approval, assessing potential hazards, environmental impacts, and societal consequences. During execution, the Committee must conduct unannounced inspections at least quarterly, verifying compliance with all stipulated safety measures and containment protocols. Any deviation from approved procedures constitutes a serious violation, warranting immediate suspension of research until rectified.

In addition to peer review, an independent Audit Bureau shall annually assess each active project's adherence to regulatory standards and ethical guidelines. The Bureau possesses broad investigative powers, including access to all records, communications, and physical evidence related to the research endeavor. Its findings are binding and may result in permit revocation or criminal prosecution for willful noncompliance. Researchers found guilty of falsifying data or misrepresenting results shall face expulsion from the Guild and permanent disqualification from future permits.

The Guild recognizes that responsible innovation is essential to maintaining its relevance and authority in an ever-changing magical landscape. Yet this freedom must be exercised with prudence, guided by sound judgment and unwavering commitment to public welfare. Only through disciplined oversight can we harness the full potential of arcane discovery without compromising our shared future. Thus stands mandated as law: § 400.10 Research Oversight and Audit Procedures shall henceforth govern all investigative endeavors undertaken within the bounds of lawful research permits, ensuring that progress proceeds safely under watchful scrutiny.

body.heading: Research Oversight and Audit Procedures — Continued
body.text:
§ 400.10 Research Oversight and Audit Procedures shall ensure the integrity and safety of all magical investigations conducted under Guild authorization. The Conservatorial Oversight Committee (COC) is empowered to conduct random audits of researcher logs, samples, and facilities without prior notice. Failure to cooperate with an audit constitutes a Class B violation under § 300.2 and may result in immediate revocation of research privileges.

All experimental results must be submitted within seven business days of completion for peer review by COC-appointed magi. Any data indicating potential hazards or ethical breaches will trigger an expedited reassessment process. Researchers found to have falsified findings face permanent disqualification from future projects and possible criminal prosecution under § 500.3.

The COC maintains a centralized database accessible only to senior council members, containing all approved research proposals, budgets, and final reports. Unauthorized access or tampering with this system is punishable as grand larceny under § 1201.8. Researchers retaining copies of sensitive documents violate § 400.6 and shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and including expulsion from the Guild.

Audits may extend beyond physical premises to include digital records, communications, and financial transactions related to the research endeavor. The COC reserves the right to subpoena witnesses or engage forensic experts at the researcher's expense if necessary to ascertain full truth. Deliberate obstruction of an audit shall be treated as contempt of court under § 1301.7 and may result in immediate arrest.

This comprehensive oversight framework exists solely to protect both the public and the Guild from reckless experimentation with powerful arcane forces. Researchers must understand that their privileges are contingent upon strict adherence to these protocols at all times. Breach of any provision herein will lead to escalating penalties, culminating in total revocation of licensure under § 200.4 if deemed egregious enough to warrant such extreme measure.

body.heading: § 400.10 Research Oversight and Audit Procedures — Continued
body.text:
Under § 400, research into restricted or forbidden arts requires explicit authorization to mitigate potential dangers to society. This section establishes the framework for overseeing such activities through rigorous audit protocols and mandatory reporting obligations. All permit holders must maintain detailed logs of experimental procedures, outcomes, and any adverse effects observed during trials. These records shall be subject to periodic review by appointed Auditors tasked with assessing compliance and safety standards. Failure to cooperate with audits or conceal relevant data may result in immediate suspension of privileges and further disciplinary action pursuant to § 300.

Furthermore, § 400 mandates the implementation of a tiered oversight system tailored to the risk profile of specific research categories. High-risk projects involving unstable constructs or potent artifacts require daily reporting and on-site monitoring by senior Aegis Magi. Mid-level experiments demand weekly summaries submitted directly to the Conservator Council for approval. Lower-tier investigations into benign topics may proceed under self-regulated conditions, provided all standard safety measures are observed without exception. This graduated approach ensures appropriate scrutiny while avoiding unnecessary bureaucratic impediments to legitimate scholarly inquiry.

In addition to routine inspections, § 400 empowers the Guild to initiate unannounced spot checks at any time and place where regulated research is conducted. Such audits may include physical examinations of equipment, interviews with personnel, and analysis of sample results to verify authenticity and completeness. Refusal to submit to these oversight measures constitutes a material breach of permit terms and warrants immediate revocation of authorization status under § 200.4. Continued violation after notice subjects the offender to criminal prosecution for grand larceny of public resources charged with reckless endangerment of innocent bystanders.

Finally, § 400 creates a formal appeals process for researchers who dispute audit findings or alleged violations of permit conditions. Appeals shall be heard by an independent tribunal comprising equal numbers of Conservators and Innovators appointed by the Archmage Sovereign. The burden of proof lies with the accused to demonstrate good faith efforts toward safe experimentation despite any perceived regulatory hurdles imposed upon them. Decisions rendered by this appellate body are final and binding unless overturned by subsequent legislation passed through normal channels outlined herein at § 100 et seq.

see § 400.6 Related Requirements; see § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse; see § 300 Unsanctioned Arts; see § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting. A page with zero § cites will be rejected.

body.heading: Research Oversight and Audit Procedures — Administration
body.text:
Section 400.10 hereby establishes mandatory oversight and audit mechanisms to ensure compliance with research permit conditions and mitigate potential hazards arising from unauthorized magical experimentation. All holders of valid research permits shall submit quarterly progress reports detailing methods employed, materials utilized, and results achieved. These submissions must be reviewed by an independent panel of qualified mages appointed by the Mages' Guild Desk to verify adherence to safety protocols and ethical guidelines.

In addition to periodic reporting, unannounced site inspections may be conducted at any time without prior notice or justification. Inspectors possess full authority to examine facilities, equipment, records, and personnel involved in permitted research activities. Failure to cooperate with such examinations shall constitute a material breach of the permit agreement and may result in immediate revocation of privileges and referral for disciplinary proceedings.

Furthermore, this Section mandates the implementation of rigorous auditing procedures designed to detect and prevent circumvention of regulatory controls. Electronic monitoring systems shall be installed at all permitted research sites capable of tracking usage patterns, energy consumption, and anomalous activity levels. Data collected by these devices shall be analyzed continuously by automated algorithms supplemented by human oversight teams tasked with identifying potential violations or safety risks.

Any suspected instances of non-compliance will trigger an immediate investigation into the circumstances surrounding the alleged infraction. Upon completion of said inquiry, appropriate corrective actions may be taken ranging from warnings and fines to suspension or permanent revocation of research privileges depending on severity and frequency of infractions committed by the offending party.

It is expressly declared that nothing contained herein shall limit or impair any rights vested in the Mages' Guild under existing laws, regulations, treaties, or customary usage pertaining to oversight, inspection, enforcement, and other functions necessary for effective governance of magical research practices throughout the Realm. This Section stands as a complementary provision intended to strengthen rather than diminish the regulatory framework governing responsible innovation within our society.

shall be fully implemented forthwith upon publication in this Codex and shall remain in force indefinitely unless expressly amended or repealed by subsequent legislation enacted by competent authority acting pursuant to due process procedures established herein or otherwise provided by law." [see § 400.1, § 300.5]

sections.title: Duty to Disclose Potential Hazards

body.heading: Duty to Disclose Potential Hazards
body.text:
The obligations imposed by these Provisions are cumulative and do not preclude other duties mandated by applicable law or regulation. A caster licensed under this Codex must comply with all terms of their license agreement, as well as any additional conditions imposed by the Desk upon issuance thereof. Failure to adhere to such stipulations may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure.

Casters are further required to maintain accurate records of all magical activities conducted under their authority. This includes detailed logs of spell components consumed, target recipients of enchantments, and any adverse effects observed or reported by third parties. Such documentation shall be retained for a minimum period of seven years from the date of completion and made available for inspection upon reasonable request by Guild officials.

In instances where a casting produces unintended consequences or causes harm to persons or property, the responsible caster must immediately notify the Desk in writing within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of said outcome. Such notice shall include all known facts surrounding the incident, including but not limited to: full identification of affected parties, precise description of resulting damage, and any mitigating actions taken by the caster. Prompt cooperation with subsequent investigations is compulsory; evasion or obstruction will be treated as a separate offense subject to enhanced penalties.

The Desk reserves discretion to waive certain reporting thresholds for minor infractions deemed unlikely to recur or cause significant disruption. However, waivers are granted only at sole discretion of individual clerks and remain revocable without notice upon discovery of prior noncompliance by the licensee. Requests for exemption must be submitted in duplicate via certified mail no less than sixty (60) days before planned operation, allowing adequate time for review and approval cycles to complete successfully.

This section shall be construed liberally in favor of protecting public safety and welfare over promoting commercial interests or individual convenience. Any ambiguity regarding scope or application shall be resolved according to established principles of administrative law governing similar regulatory regimes nationally and internationally. Disputes arising from interpretation or enforcement hereunder are subject to exclusive jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, whose determinations herein are final and binding absent successful appeal under § 105.3.

"Magic isn't just about throwing fireballs—it's about responsibility too." — Archmage Theron on licensing compliance

body.heading: § 900.10 Duty to Disclose Potential Hazards
body.text:
Any caster who knows or reasonably should know that an item contains latent magical properties must disclose this fact before completing any transaction involving said item. Failure to do so constitutes misrepresentation and may result in revocation of licensure under § 200.1(b). This duty extends beyond mere verbal disclosure; the seller must take affirmative steps to warn potential buyers of known dangers, such as providing a written notice or affixing a warning label. See also § 300.8 regarding labeling requirements for enchanted goods.

The burden of proof rests upon the accused caster to demonstrate that they acted in good faith and exercised reasonable diligence in determining whether an item possessed magical qualities prior to sale. In cases where doubt exists, the presumption favors public safety over commercial convenience. Archmage Veyra has ruled repeatedly that ignorance of the law is no excuse when it comes to matters of arcane hazard. Under § 1.7(c), any ambiguities in this section shall be resolved against the party seeking to avoid liability.

This provision does not apply to items explicitly marked as "non-magical" or those whose enchantments have fully degraded over time and pose no risk upon inspection by a qualified caster. However, the seller retains the obligation to verify such claims through appropriate testing when feasible. See § 400.6 for standards governing magical item assessment. Any disputes arising from alleged breaches of this duty shall be adjudicated in accordance with the Paradox Trial procedures outlined in Part X. The Guild maintains a comprehensive database of known hazardous items and their effects, which is updated regularly to reflect new discoveries. All registered casters are required to consult this resource before engaging in any commercial activity involving potentially dangerous artifacts. Failure to do so may constitute negligence per se under applicable common law principles.

"The burden of proof rests upon the accused caster to demonstrate that they acted in good faith..." - Archmage Veyra, Decision No. 1472-B

body.heading: § 900.10 Duty to Disclose Potential Hazards — Continued
body.text:
Every licensor casting within the Guild's jurisdiction shall disclose all known material hazards associated with their specific practice or artifact prior to commencing service. Failure to do so constitutes gross negligence and may result in immediate suspension of licensure pending investigation. This duty extends beyond mere verbal notification; it requires affirmative action to warn clients of risks that a reasonable person would not anticipate, such as hidden enchantments, unstable magical residues, or unforeseen side effects of potent spells.

The standard for disclosure is objective: what should have been revealed under the circumstances, regardless of whether actual harm occurred. A caster who knowingly omits critical safety information to maximize profit violates this mandate even if their client suffers no damage. Conversely, accidental omission due to genuine forgetfulness or oversight may be excused upon proof of diligent effort to comply with all reporting obligations. Ultimately, transparency and precaution remain the bedrock of responsible magical practice under the Autumnwood Accords.

See § 900.1 for related filing requirements; see also § 300.2 on unsanctioned arts and § 400.5 concerning unauthorized field use. Underlying principles regarding professional conduct are set forth in §§ 1.7 and 1.8. For penalties applicable to non-compliance, refer to Part V of this Codex.

"Disclose all known hazards before casting." - Archmage Veyra's Directive #42

body.heading: § 900.10 Duty to Disclose Potential Hazards and Mitigation Standards
body.text:
Under § 900.6, all registered mages bear an affirmative duty to disclose any known hazards associated with their intended casting before commencing operations. This obligation applies regardless of whether the hazard is obvious or obscure, provided that a reasonable practitioner would recognize the risk in the circumstances. Failure to make such disclosure shall constitute negligence per se and may result in civil liability and disciplinary sanctions under § 100.20.

The term "hazards" encompasses not only physical dangers such as explosions or structural collapse but also magical effects including unintended enchantments, area-of-effect spells, residual psychic trauma, and ecological disruption. See § 300.7 for the definition of "ecological disruption." Mages must evaluate all potential hazards through a combination of theoretical analysis, empirical testing where feasible, and consultation with qualified peers as directed by § 400.12.

Where hazards cannot be fully mitigated even after reasonable efforts, mages must either refrain from casting altogether or obtain informed consent from affected parties in writing pursuant to § 900.5. Such consent shall specify the nature and extent of the risks undertaken voluntarily. Any waiver obtained under duress or without adequate explanation shall be void ab initio. Under § 1401.3, ambiguous waivers are construed strictly against the drafter.

Mages failing to comply with this duty shall face enhanced penalties upon conviction, including mandatory remediation costs and permanent revocation of licensure for egregious violations. See § 200.8 regarding cumulative sanctions. The burden of proof rests solely on the accused mage to demonstrate that all reasonable precautions were taken in accordance with established safety protocols outlined in Part IV. This standard applies irrespective of actual harm suffered, reflecting the guild's commitment to proactive hazard management rather than mere reactive compensation.

The provisions herein complement but do not supersede applicable labor laws and workplace safety regulations enforced by other agencies. However, given the unique nature of arcane phenomena, certain hazards may fall outside conventional regulatory frameworks and thus require specialized oversight as detailed in this section. Mages should consult with legal counsel when navigating overlapping obligations between guild statutes and external mandates. For further guidance on hazard assessment methodologies, refer to Appendix C of the Master Spellbook. Any disputes arising under this article shall be resolved by arbitration unless otherwise provided by mutual agreement among all parties involved.

*END OF SECTION*

body.heading: § 900.10 Duty to Disclose Potential Hazards and Mitigation Standards — Continued
body.text:
§ 900.10 imposes upon every registered caster an affirmative duty to disclose any known potential hazards inherent in the proposed magical operation, whether arising from the nature of the spellwork itself or from interactions with environmental factors. Failure to make such disclosure shall constitute grounds for immediate suspension of licensure and referral for penal proceedings under § 900.12.

The obligation to disclose extends beyond mere verbal notification; it requires that all relevant technical data, risk assessments, and mitigation plans be submitted in writing to the appropriate Guild office at least seventy-two hours prior to casting. This includes detailed information regarding power draw estimates, potential collateral damage zones, and contingency measures for unforeseen complications. See § 900.6 for requirements concerning the identification of fees associated with such disclosures.

Special provisions apply when the proposed spellwork involves any artifact listed on the Quiet List or possesses unknown properties. In such cases, dual disclosure must be made to both the Conservator's Office and the Innovators' Bureau, each retaining independent copies of all submitted materials for a minimum period of five years. See § 900.3 regarding procedures for reclassification of previously sanitized items.

Casters who knowingly conceal hazards shall be held personally liable for any resultant damage or injury, regardless of whether such harm falls within the scope of their contractual obligations. This personal liability extends to all corporate officers and authorized agents acting on behalf of a registered entity. Under § 900.8, failure to comply with disclosure mandates constitutes a material breach of contract and may justify termination without notice.

The Guild reserves the right to conduct independent verification testing of any proposed spellwork prior to granting casting authorization. Casters who refuse such testing shall be deemed non-compliant subject to immediate sanctions. See § 900.7 for provisions relating to courtesy inspections at foreign halls. All disclosures must be made in good faith; fraudulent misrepresentations will result in permanent revocation of licensure and referral for criminal prosecution under applicable state statutes.

body.heading: § 9010 Prohibition on Unauthorized Research Facilities and Pocket Dimensions
body.text:
No caster shall establish or operate any research laboratory, workshop, or similar facility without prior written authorization from the Guild's Safety Division. Such authorization may be granted only upon demonstration of adequate safety protocols and containment measures sufficient to protect both public health and magical stability. See § 9015 regarding emergency shutdown procedures for unauthorized facilities.

The possession or operation of any pocket dimension not specifically designated as a research laboratory shall constitute a felony offense under these Accords. Exceptions are made solely for dimensions used exclusively for personal storage or temporary refuge, provided such use does not interfere with public safety or magical equilibrium. See § 9016 for registration requirements concerning personal dimensional spaces.

Unauthorized conversion of any existing space into a research facility is strictly prohibited without explicit permission from the property owner and relevant Guild authorities. Violations shall be subject to immediate seizure of equipment and assets, along with permanent revocation of all future casting privileges. See § 9017 for provisions governing disposal of confiscated magical apparatus.

Casters who discover unauthorized research operations in progress must immediately notify local law enforcement and Guild inspectors without delay. Failure to report such violations shall result in disciplinary action up to and including suspension of licensure, regardless of whether the reporting caster suffered any personal harm or financial loss from the illegal activity. See § 9018 regarding whistleblower protections and rewards for timely disclosures.

The use of pocket dimensions as temporary sanctuaries during emergencies is permitted provided such usage does not exceed twenty-four consecutive hours. Extended occupation requires special dispensation from the Conservator's Office demonstrating compelling justification and adequate safeguards against misuse or exploitation of the dimensional space. See § 9019 concerning limits on duration and frequency of emergency refuge utilization.

Any caster found operating an illegal research facility shall be subject to immediate arrest and prosecution under both state and Guild laws. Confiscated equipment will be destroyed unless deemed necessary for ongoing investigations. Repeat offenders face enhanced penalties including permanent expulsion from the magical community and disqualification from future licensure applications. See § 9020 regarding forfeiture proceedings and asset liquidation.

body.heading: § 9015 Emergency Shutdown Procedures and Safety Protocols
body.text:
All registered research facilities must be equipped with automated safety systems capable of immediate shutdown upon detection of hazardous conditions, whether resulting from equipment malfunction or operator error. Such systems shall be tested monthly by certified technicians to ensure full operational readiness at all times. See § 9021 regarding certification requirements for safety inspection personnel.

In the event of an emergency requiring evacuation, all casters must adhere strictly to established exit routes and assembly points designated by facility management. Unauthorized re-entry into affected areas shall be prohibited until official clearance is granted by both law enforcement and Guild inspectors. See § 9022 concerning penalties for violation of evacuation orders.

Casters operating in conjunction with non-magical entities must maintain clear lines of communication regarding potential hazards and appropriate response procedures. Joint safety meetings shall be conducted quarterly to review incident reports and update contingency plans as necessary. See § 9023 regarding mandatory training requirements for mixed-use facilities.

In cases where emergency services are required, casters must provide immediate assistance consistent with their capabilities while avoiding any actions that might exacerbate the situation or endanger themselves unnecessarily. Refusal to render aid when reasonably able shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action under these Accords. See § 9024 outlining scope of duty to assist.

All emergency procedures must be prominently posted in visible locations throughout each facility, accompanied by detailed instructions tailored to specific hazard types present at that location. Failure to maintain such signage shall result in automatic suspension of operating permits until corrected. See § 9025 regarding content and placement requirements for safety notices.

Casters are prohibited from conducting any experimental procedures within residential zones or densely populated areas without explicit written consent from affected parties and prior approval from the Guild's Risk Assessment Division. Violations shall be treated as major infractions subject to severe sanctions including permanent revocation of licensure. See § 9026 concerning restrictions on urban spellcasting operations.

body.heading: § 9021 Certification Requirements for Safety Inspection Personnel
body.text:
All individuals conducting official safety inspections must hold current certification issued by the Guild's Board of Standards, demonstrating proficiency in both theoretical and practical aspects of magical hazard assessment. Such certifications shall be renewed annually through completion of approved continuing education programs. See § 9027 regarding curriculum requirements for recertification courses.

Inspection personnel are authorized to enter any facility operating under a valid license upon presentation of proper credentials. Resistance to lawful inspection constitutes obstruction of justice and may result in criminal charges being filed against the responsible parties. See § 9028 outlining powers granted to certified inspectors during examinations.

Casters found violating safety regulations shall be subject to immediate suspension pending full investigation into the circumstances surrounding the infraction. Final determination of culpability will be made by an independent panel convened specifically for each case. See § 9029 detailing due process protections afforded during disciplinary hearings.

The Guild maintains a centralized registry of all certified inspection professionals, accessible via public portal for verification purposes. Outdated listings shall be corrected promptly upon receipt of notification from affected parties or through routine auditing procedures. See § 9030 concerning maintenance and accuracy of official records.

Casters who dispute findings made by certified inspectors may request re-examination within fourteen calendar days of initial notice, subject to payment of an applicable administrative fee. Such requests must be submitted in writing with supporting documentation addressing alleged errors or omissions in the original assessment. See § 9031 outlining appeal process and associated costs.

All inspection reports shall include detailed findings along with specific recommendations for corrective action where deficiencies are identified. Casters failing to implement such recommendations within prescribed timeframes will face escalating penalties proportional to the severity of unresolved hazards. See § 9032 regarding enforcement mechanisms for compliance mandates.
