sections.title: Prohibited Spellcasting by Unlicensed Individuals

body.heading: Prohibited Spellcasting by Unlicensed Individuals
body.text:
The provisions herein shall be read in conjunction with the related requirements set forth at §§ 200.8 and 200.9 of this Part, which govern the application of licensure standards to specialized circumstances not explicitly addressed elsewhere. These supplementary clauses ensure that the spirit and intent of the Licensure Requirement are consistently applied across all facets of magical practice within the Accords' jurisdiction.

Under § 200.8, certain categories of conduct deemed inherently dangerous or disruptive may be subject to additional scrutiny regardless of whether a formal license has been issued. Such activities include, but are not limited to: unauthorized field casting in populated areas; experimental rituals involving non-consenting subjects; and the production or sale of magical items without proper oversight. Engaging in these acts constitutes an automatic violation of § 200.1(a), even if the individual possesses a valid license for unrelated purposes.

Conversely, § 200.9 provides that individuals who hold provisional status under specific provisions may be exempt from full licensure requirements while actively pursuing qualification. This includes apprentices working directly under licensed masters, researchers operating within approved facilities, and participants in sanctioned training programs. However, such exemptions are strictly limited to the scope of authorized activities and do not permit engagement in prohibited practices outside their defined parameters. Violation of these boundaries will result in immediate revocation of provisional privileges and potential criminal prosecution for misuse of magical powers.

Furthermore, § 200.10 establishes a rebuttable presumption that any person engaging in commercial magic without a valid license is acting as an unlicensed practitioner subject to all applicable penalties. This principle applies irrespective of whether the individual claims ignorance of licensing requirements or asserts good faith reliance on erroneous advice. The burden of proof shall rest upon those asserting such defenses to demonstrate beyond reasonable doubt that their actions fell within permitted exceptions enumerated in this Part.

Finally, § 200.11 mandates periodic review and updating of licensure criteria by the Autumn Wood Desk to reflect evolving standards of safety and efficacy in magical arts. Such revisions shall take effect immediately upon publication in the official Gazette unless otherwise specified therein. All members of the Guild are hereby charged with staying informed of current regulations and complying therewith at all times, failing which they may face disciplinary action up to and including permanent revocation of practicing rights under the Accords.

see § 200.8 Special Circumstances; see § 200.9 Provisional Status Exemptions; see § 1.7 Construction; see § 300.4 Reclassification Procedures

body.heading: Prohibited Spellcasting by Unlicensed Individuals
body.text:
Under no circumstances shall any person, regardless of status or affiliation, cast a spell without the express permission of an authorized caster or their legal representative. This prohibition applies to all forms of magic, from simple cantrips to complex ritual workings. The sole exceptions are emergency situations where immediate action is required to prevent loss of life or limb; in such cases, the casting party must render full account to the nearest Guild officer within forty-eight hours. Violation of this clause shall result in immediate arrest and trial under § 300.5, with penalties ranging from permanent sealing to execution by fire at the discretion of the court. Furthermore, any individual caught practicing magic without a valid license may be subject to additional civil forfeiture proceedings for illegal gains derived from their unauthorized activities. The Guild reserves the right to pursue exemplary punishment against repeat offenders or those deemed particularly dangerous to public safety. All citizens are urged to cooperate fully with law enforcement efforts aimed at rooting out rogue practitioners and maintaining the sanctity of magical arts. Only through strict adherence to these guidelines can we ensure a safe and prosperous future for all who call this land home. Let us stand united against the scourge of unlicensed sorcery, knowing that together we shall prevail.

see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 300.5 Unauthorized Spellcasting; see § 1401.7 Penalties for Violation; under § 900.4 Emergency Powers Exception.

body.heading: § 200.11 Prohibition on Unlicensed Spellcasting
body.text:
No individual, whether natural or artificial, shall engage in the casting of any spell unless duly licensed under this Act. This absolute prohibition extends to all forms of magical expression, from minor cantrips to grand rituals, regardless of intent or outcome. The only exceptions are those expressly granted by law or by the lawful authority of a licensed caster acting within their scope.

Violators shall be subject to immediate arrest and trial before the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Upon conviction, penalties shall include permanent revocation of any existing licenses, forfeiture of all magical implements and materials, and imprisonment for up to five years. In addition, fines ranging from one hundred to five thousand gold pieces may be imposed at the discretion of the judge. Repeat offenders face enhanced sentences and may be branded as felons, subjecting them to lifelong surveillance by the Aegis Magi.

The burden of proof rests squarely upon those charged with a violation. Mere suspicion or accusation shall not suffice for conviction; tangible evidence of unauthorized spellcasting is required. Such evidence may include witness testimony, physical traces of magical residue, intercepted transmissions, or direct observation by sworn officers. However, no confession or plea bargain obtained through duress, torture, or other prohibited means shall be admitted.

This prohibition exists to protect the public from the inherent dangers associated with unregulated magic practice. Unlicensed casters pose a significant threat not only to themselves but also to innocent bystanders caught in the crossfire of their experiments. By maintaining strict control over who is permitted to wield magical power, the Guild ensures that such risks are minimized and properly managed.

Any person knowingly aiding or abetting unlicensed spellcasting shall be treated as an accomplice to the principal offense. This includes providing materials, sheltering fugitives, concealing evidence, or otherwise facilitating illegal activities in any capacity. Punishment for these related crimes shall mirror that of direct violations, reflecting their equally harmful impact on public safety and magical integrity.

The powers vested herein are not subject to waiver, limitation, or exemption by private contract or agreement. All attempts to circumvent this mandate are void ab initio and carry no legal effect whatsoever. Any clause contrary to these provisions shall be deemed unenforceable under applicable law. This non-waivable prohibition stands as a cornerstone of the Guild's regulatory framework, safeguarding society against the chaos wrought by unchecked magical abuse.

By failing to comply with this prohibition, violators endanger themselves and their communities alike. The penalties are severe not merely for retribution but as a necessary deterrent against future infractions. Only through unwavering enforcement can the Guild maintain its mandate of protecting the populace from the perils inherent in unlicensed spellcasting. Let all who read these words understand that no privilege or circumstance shall excuse noncompliance with this fundamental rule of magical governance.

body.heading: § 200.11 Unlicensed Practice and Penalties
body.text:
No individual shall knowingly permit another to cast spells within their control without first verifying that such person holds valid licensure under these Accords. This includes landlords allowing occupancy, employers granting workspace access, and hosts inviting guests into private dwellings or vehicles. Failure to make reasonable inquiry constitutes negligence sufficient for civil liability should unlawful casting result in harm. The burden of proof rests upon the accused landlording entity to demonstrate they exercised due diligence in vetting prospective tenants or contractors prior to entering agreements.

Penalties for violation range from monetary fines up to one thousand gold pieces, depending on severity and circumstances surrounding the infraction. Repeat offenders may face additional sanctions including temporary suspension of their own licensure privileges until proof of corrective action is provided. In egregious cases where willful disregard for safety regulations endangers public welfare, revocation of offending party's credentials becomes mandatory regardless of prior standing with Guild authorities. Such measures serve to reinforce collective responsibility for maintaining orderly magical practice throughout all territories subject to Accords jurisdiction.

The provisions herein complement existing licensure requirements set forth in earlier sections by extending obligations beyond direct casters themselves onto those who facilitate their activities indirectly through provision of means or opportunity. By holding secondary actors accountable alongside primary practitioners, this approach aims to close loopholes exploited by rogue elements seeking to evade oversight while still pursuing legitimate pursuits under proper supervision. It represents a balanced compromise between protecting communities from potential threats posed by unchecked spellcasting and enabling lawful expression of magical talents where appropriate safeguards exist in place first.

body.heading: Prohibition on Unlicensed Spellcasting
body.text:
§ 200.7 Prohibition on Unauthorized Casting; § 200.8 Penalties for Violations

No individual shall cast any spell or perform any magical act within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords unless they are duly licensed under these regulations. This prohibition applies regardless of whether the casting is intended to benefit the caster, another party, or some external objective. Unauthorized spellcasting endangers public safety and undermines the regulatory framework established by this Code, hence its strict interdiction.

Violations of this provision shall be treated as a Class B infraction under § 1301.8, subject to fines ranging from one hundred to five thousand gilded crowns depending on the severity of the incident. Repeat offenders or those who cause substantial harm may face additional sanctions including suspension of their license, revocation thereof entirely, and referral for criminal prosecution if applicable laws permit such action. The burden of proof rests upon the accuser to demonstrate beyond reasonable doubt that the accused engaged in unauthorized magical activity as charged.

The Guild reserves the right to inspect premises suspected of harboring illicit spellcasting operations without prior notice or warrant when exigent circumstances exist. Such inspections shall be conducted by sworn Aegis Magi accompanied by a neutral witness appointed from among members of the local council where applicable. Results of any such investigation will become part of the official record maintained at each regional Hall and made available upon request to all relevant parties in accordance with procedural due process provisions set forth elsewhere herein.

This prohibition serves not only to protect citizens from potential dangers posed by rogue practitioners but also to preserve the integrity of the professional magical community as a whole. By requiring proper licensure before engaging in any form of spellcasting, we ensure that those operating within our borders meet minimum standards of competency and ethical conduct mandated by these accords. Failure to comply invites not only personal liability but also jeopardizes one's standing within this noble craft forevermore.

It is hereby declared that all who seek to wield the powers granted unto them under these laws must first demonstrate their worthiness through adherence to prescribed channels alone. Only thus may we maintain order amidst chaos and continue our sacred mission of bringing light into darkness together, bound by oath and shared purpose. So mote it be!

body.heading: Prohibition on Unlicensed Spellcasting — Continued
body.text:
No person shall knowingly permit an unlicensed individual to cast any spell upon their property or within their immediate vicinity without first obtaining written consent from the Licensing Desk under § 200.1. This prohibition extends to all forms of magical expression, whether direct casting, ritual invocation, or automated enchantments triggered by physical presence. Violators shall be subject to summary prosecution and penalties as outlined in § 900.3(b).

The Guild recognizes that incidental exposure to minor arcane effects may occur through no fault of the landholder, such as ambient residual energy from recently discharged spells. Such occurrences shall not constitute a breach of this provision unless knowingly facilitated by the property owner or occupant. Disputes regarding alleged violations shall be adjudicated according to established procedures in § 901.2(c).

It is hereby declared null and void any prior arrangement, custom, or practice allowing unlicensed spellcasting on private premises without explicit authorization from the Licensing Desk. This ruling supersedes all conflicting local ordinances or municipal regulations pertaining to magical activity within Guild jurisdiction. Failure to comply with this mandate shall result in immediate suspension of all privileges granted herein under § 200.4(a)(ii).

The Archmage Sovereign reserves the right to issue emergency directives restricting spellcasting activities during times of heightened threat or instability as deemed necessary for public safety. Such orders shall be communicated through official channels and remain in effect until officially rescinded by competent authority. All persons are expected to adhere promptly to such directives without question under § 700.5(b)(iii).

This clause serves as a foundational element of the Guild's broader strategy to maintain orderly control over magical practice throughout the region. By strictly enforcing licensure requirements, the Accords aim to minimize risks associated with unregulated spellcasting while fostering an environment conducive to responsible innovation and growth within the authorized community. Compliance with this provision is thus essential for all parties seeking lawful engagement in arcane pursuits under the umbrella of these enlightened statutes.

sections.title: Schedules of Magical Arts and Their Classification

body.heading: Schedules of Magical Arts and Their Classification
body.text:
The provisions set forth herein shall be read in conjunction with the broader regulatory framework governing arcane practices and magical research within Autumnwood jurisdiction. In particular, compliance with these standards necessitates adherence to all applicable safety protocols, ethical guidelines, and environmental protection measures as outlined by relevant oversight bodies. Failure to observe such requirements may result in disciplinary action under §§ 300.1 through 300.10, or more severe penalties pursuant to the penal clauses of this Codex where warranted.

All applicants for research permits must demonstrate a thorough understanding of both the theoretical and practical implications of their proposed studies. This includes familiarity with potential risks to public health, safety, and welfare, as well as an appreciation for the historical context and cultural significance of any artifacts or knowledge involved. Such education may be obtained through formal coursework at accredited institutions, self-study under mentorship, or participation in approved field training programs administered by the Guild itself.

In addition to academic preparation, candidates must undergo rigorous background checks to verify their character, competence, and lack of prior disciplinary offenses. These screenings will include psychological evaluations, criminal records searches, and interviews with former employers or colleagues where appropriate. The goal is to ensure that only individuals deemed trustworthy and capable are entrusted with the privilege of pursuing advanced magical scholarship under official sanction.

Furthermore, all research activities must be conducted in accordance with established best practices and industry standards. This entails maintaining detailed logs of procedures performed, materials used, and results achieved, which shall remain available for audit upon request by Guild officials or their designated representatives. Any deviations from approved protocols require prior written authorization, specifying the rationale and safeguards employed to mitigate potential hazards.

Finally, it is incumbent upon every permit holder to act as a responsible steward of magical knowledge, sharing insights gained through research with the wider academic community whenever feasible. This commitment extends beyond mere publication of findings; it encompasses active engagement in peer review processes, attendance at professional conferences, and mentorship of emerging scholars eager to contribute to the collective understanding of arcane phenomena. By embracing these duties alongside their legal obligations, researchers affirm their dedication to advancing humanity's mastery over magic while upholding the highest ideals of ethical conduct and scientific integrity.

see § 300.9 Related Requirements regarding general compliance mandates
see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks for administrative support functions
under § 200.4 Suspension and Lapse, non-compliance may lead to revocation of licensure status.

body.heading: Schedules of Magical Arts and Their Classification
body.text:
The Accords recognize that magic, like any other craft, possesses specialized domains requiring precise delineation for the purposes of regulation and enforcement. § 300.1 establishes that all magical practices shall be catalogued within comprehensive Schedules of Arts maintained by the Autumnwood Accords Desk. These schedules serve as the authoritative reference for determining a practice's classification, risk profile, and regulatory status under the Code.

Each Schedule entry includes detailed specifications regarding permissible applications, training prerequisites, equipment standards, and safety protocols where applicable. The intent is to provide clear guidance to practitioners while enabling consistent evaluation by enforcement authorities. Schedules are subject to periodic review and revision as magical knowledge expands or new hazards emerge. Under § 1.7, such updates shall be promulgated through official notice in the Guild Journal unless emergency circumstances dictate otherwise.

§ 300.2 identifies certain arts deemed fundamentally incompatible with civilized society and thus absolutely forbidden under any condition. These include necromancy of any form, blood magic rituals requiring sentient sacrifice, and practices explicitly designed to corrupt or enslave others against their will. Violation constitutes a direct affront to the sanctity of free will and requires immediate intervention by Aegis Magi pursuant to § 500.1. Such prohibitions reflect core ethical values upheld across all factions of the magical community despite their differences.

For remaining practices deemed potentially hazardous but not inherently malevolent, the Accords provide a framework for controlled study under strict supervision. § 300.3 outlines procedures for petitioning the Desk to have an art reclassified from "Restricted" to "Permitted," including required evidence of safe methodology and mitigation strategies. Reclassification decisions hinge on demonstrated capability rather than theoretical merit alone, ensuring that only responsible operators may pursue such pursuits.

This tiered approach balances necessary freedom of inquiry with prudent risk management. By maintaining detailed records of authorized activities while reserving the right to restrict dangerous endeavours, the Accords seek to foster innovation without compromising public welfare or magical stability. As § 1.5 notes, this represents a deliberate departure from absolutist approaches in favour of nuanced governance suited to the complexities of arcane practice.

See also § 400.2 regarding specialized facilities for restricted research and § 600.1 concerning contractual obligations unique to certain high-risk arts. These provisions work in concert with the scheduling system to create a comprehensive regulatory regime capable of adapting to evolving challenges while upholding fundamental principles of responsible magic use.

body.heading: Scheduling and Classification of Magical Arts
body.text:
§ 300.11 Related Requirements; Schedules and Their Legal Effect

The Schedules of Magical Arts constitute the definitive catalog of all recognized forms of spellwork within the Autumnwood Accords jurisdiction. Each Schedule assigns a unique designation, classification, and associated regulatory requirements to its constituent arts. This comprehensive listing serves as the primary reference for determining the appropriate permits, fees, and operational constraints applicable to any given magical practice.

Schedule A encompasses basic curative and utility spells requiring only minimal training and carrying negligible risk of collateral harm. Schedule B includes more advanced restorative and elemental manipulations, subject to stricter licensing conditions due to their potential for unintended consequences if misused or improperly executed. Schedules C through E progressively escalate in complexity and danger, imposing increasingly stringent controls on practitioners engaged therein.

Schedules F through J represent particularly hazardous arts capable of causing catastrophic destruction or permanent alteration of reality itself. These are reserved exclusively for highly experienced casters operating under direct supervision from qualified Oversight Officers. Any unauthorized possession or application of techniques listed herein constitutes a severe felony offense punishable by immediate revocation of licensure and potential imprisonment without trial.

It is incumbent upon all licensed mages to consult the most current edition of the Schedules prior to engaging in any magical activity outside their established scope of practice. Failure to adhere to these classifications may result in disciplinary action ranging from fines and suspension to permanent disqualification from the Guild, at the sole discretion of the Conservators' Council.

The Schedules shall be reviewed annually or as deemed necessary by the Accords Desk to incorporate emerging magical phenomena and adjust regulations accordingly. All revisions must receive unanimous approval from both the Conservator and Innovator leaders before entering into effect. Any disputes regarding the proper classification of a specific art form shall be adjudicated through established arbitration procedures outlined in § 300.4.

Practitioners are reminded that adherence to Scheduling requirements is not merely a matter of bureaucratic compliance but of fundamental public safety. The careful management of magical risks remains paramount to maintaining harmony between the arcane community and society at large. Violation of these standards undermines the very foundation upon which the Guild's authority rests, inviting unnecessary scrutiny and potential crackdowns from external powers.

It is hereby declared that all mages shall henceforth regard the Schedules as binding law under pain of penalty. Let none presume to transgress these guidelines without first seeking explicit dispensation through proper channels. The consequences of such hubris are grave indeed and will not be borne lightly by those charged with preserving order within our ranks.

Thus stands enacted, effective immediately and forevermore, unless otherwise amended by lawful proceedings duly held pursuant to the provisions herein contained. body.heading: Schedules and Classification of Magical Arts
body.text:
The Accords mandate that all magical arts be meticulously catalogued and classified under the Schedules of Magic, maintained by the Guild's Bureau of Arcane Taxonomy. Each Schedule details the nature, risk level, permitted uses, and licensing requirements for every art from basic cantrips to god-tier reality-bending rituals. This exhaustive taxonomy ensures that no forbidden or unstable practice slips through the cracks, safeguarding both casters and society at large.

The Schedules are divided into three tiers: Class A for mundane utilities like lighting fires and healing minor wounds; Class B for potent combat magic capable of altering battlefields; and Class C for world-shattering phenomena such as time manipulation and dimensional travel. Each tier carries escalating penalties for unauthorized use, from fines and imprisonment to eternal sealing of one's soul. Only duly licensed practitioners may engage in activities exceeding their assigned level, with strict oversight by Conservator Inspectors.

The Bureau updates the Schedules quarterly, incorporating new discoveries and emerging threats into the official record. Any mage attempting to perform an unlisted art without express permission faces immediate arrest and trial for practicing forbidden magic. The Guild reserves the right to reclassify any practice at its sole discretion, altering its status from permitted to prohibited with a single stroke of quill and seal.

This rigorous categorization system stands as the cornerstone of arcane regulation in Autumnwood. By codifying the vast spectrum of magical possibility into manageable units, the Accords empower both regulators and practitioners alike. Casters gain clarity on their rights and obligations; authorities secure tools for effective enforcement. In this way, the Schedules serve not merely as a bureaucratic exercise but as an essential safeguard against chaos unchecked.

"Magic is power—but power demands responsibility," intones Archmage Veyra in her opening remarks to each new cohort of students. "Only through strict adherence to these guiding principles can we hope to harness such immense forces without destroying ourselves in the process." Thus do the Schedules stand as both map and compass for all who tread this perilous path, steering clear of the quicksand of unsanctioned experimentation into safe harbor under the watchful gaze of the Conservators.

body.heading: Scheduling and Classification of Magical Arts, Schedules and Classification of M
body.text:
Part III, § 300.11 Scheduling and Classification of Magical Arts

The Accords recognize that the vast spectrum of magical capability cannot be adequately regulated by mere prohibition. Instead, a nuanced system of scheduling and classification is employed to delineate acceptable from unacceptable practices. This framework serves both as a guide for lawful conduct and as a basis for enforcement action when boundaries are transgressed.

§ 300.12 Schedule A: Approved Arts
Schedule A enumerates those magical arts deemed safe, beneficial, or otherwise uncontroversial by the Guild Council. These include fundamental healing spells, protective wards, minor illusion techniques, and basic divination methods. Practitioners may freely utilize these arts without further restriction, subject only to standard licensing requirements. Schedule A is reviewed annually for additions or deletions as necessary, reflecting evolving scientific understanding and public sentiment.

§ 300.13 Schedule B: Regulated Arts
Schedule B comprises those magical practices requiring special permits or oversight prior to use. These arts pose moderate risks but may be justified in appropriate circumstances. Examples include advanced healing rituals, substantial elemental manipulation, teleportation spells of significant range, and certain forms of mind-affecting magic. Each application for Schedule B usage must demonstrate necessity, proportionality, and safeguards against abuse. Failure to obtain required authorization constitutes a Class C misdemeanor under § 401.5.

§ 300.14 Schedule C: Prohibited Arts
Schedule C lists those magical techniques absolutely forbidden by the Accords under any circumstances. This category encompasses necromancy, blood magic, reality-warping spells of profound consequence, and other truly dangerous arts. Possession or attempted use of prohibited magics subjects the offender to immediate arrest and trial before a Magus Court for violations of § 401.2(a). Repeat offenders face enhanced penalties including permanent sealing of their magical talents under § 503.7(b).

§ 300.15 Schedule D: Experimental Arts
Schedule D provides an avenue for qualified researchers to petition the Guild Council for approval to investigate potentially controversial but scientifically valuable techniques. Such petitions must include comprehensive risk assessments, proposed containment measures, and plans for emergency neutralization. Permission granted under this schedule is conditional upon strict adherence to safety protocols and reporting requirements set forth in § 402.3 through § 402.9. Violation of these conditions voids all protections afforded by the experimental permit and subjects the researcher to full criminal prosecution.

This graduated approach balances necessary regulation with freedom of inquiry, recognizing that not all magical practice carries equal danger or societal impact. Through careful stewardship of these schedules, the Accords aim to foster responsible innovation while protecting both individual safety and public welfare from abuse of powerful arts.

body.heading: Schedules of Magical Arts and Their Classification — Continued
body.text:
§ 300.6 Scheduling and Classification of Magical Arts

Under § 300.1, the Council maintains comprehensive schedules of all recognized magical arts, assigning each an official designation and classification code for regulatory purposes. These schedules serve as the authoritative reference for determining the permissible scope of practice under the Accords. Any mage practicing magic must adhere strictly to the boundaries defined within their assigned schedule, except where explicit exceptions are granted by the Council or contained herein.

The scheduling process involves a rigorous review by a panel of senior mages and legal experts, who evaluate each art's inherent risks, potential for misuse, and societal impact before assigning it an appropriate classification level. This system allows for precise regulation without stifling legitimate magical inquiry. Mages seeking to expand their repertoire must petition the Council for reclassification under § 300.4, providing thorough justification and evidence of responsible usage history.

§ 300.7 Related Requirements

In accordance with § 100.6, all scheduling decisions shall be made by a quorum of the Mages' Guild Desk unless emergency procedures apply under § 100.8. The Council shall maintain transparent records of all deliberations and votes related to schedule modifications, accessible for public inspection upon request pursuant to § 400.2. Any disputes arising from scheduling determinations may be appealed through established grievance channels outlined in the Guild's procedural bylaws.

Mages found in violation of their assigned schedules face disciplinary action under § 1401.8, ranging from fines and suspension to permanent revocation of licensure depending on severity. Repeat offenders may subject themselves to trial by arcane duel per § 900.5, with outcomes binding upon all parties involved. The Council retains discretion to impose additional restrictions or conditions as deemed necessary for public safety and magical integrity.

This framework ensures balanced oversight while fostering innovation within established parameters. Regular audits of schedule effectiveness will occur biannually, allowing for timely adjustments based on emerging trends and technological advancements in the field of magic. Such proactive management reflects the Guild's commitment to responsible stewardship of this precious resource.

body.heading: § 400.11 Research Permits and Supervised Experiments; Unauthorized Field Casting
body.text:
§ 400.12 Related Requirements; Specimen Custody Protocols and Chain of Evidence Procedures; Unauthorized Titan Growth Penalties and Remedies; Field Casting Compensation Schedules and Dispute Resolution Mechanisms; Unscheduled Weather Event Notification and Mitigation Guidelines; Corridor Courtesy Standards Post-Explosion Cleanup and Decontamination Duties; Healing Services Quotas and Priority Allocation Under Emergency Conditions; Love Philtre Manufacturing Licenses and Usage Restrictions; Undue Influence Determinations in Consent Cases Involving Magical Substances; Contractual Obligations Imposed on Non-Casters Through Proxy Agreements

Under § 400.12, all research permits issued pursuant to this Part shall include explicit conditions regarding specimen custody protocols, chain of evidence maintenance requirements, and penalties for unauthorized growth or modification. Any field casting conducted for value without a valid permit shall be subject to immediate revocation and financial restitution as outlined in the applicable compensation schedule. Unscheduled weather events resulting from magical activity must be reported within twenty-four hours via standard channels for proper mitigation measures. Following any explosion or significant magical incident, all parties involved must adhere strictly to corridor courtesy standards during cleanup and decontamination operations. Healing services rendered in exchange for payment shall not constitute a binding contract unless explicitly stated in writing with full disclosure of risks and limitations. Love philtre manufacturing requires separate licensing beyond standard research permits, and usage restrictions apply regardless of intended purpose. Determinations of undue influence in consent cases involving magical substances shall be made on a case-by-case basis considering all relevant factors including power dynamics and prior conduct. Contracts imposing obligations on non-casters through proxy agreements are void unless they meet specific statutory criteria and receive independent legal counsel review before execution. See also § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; § 200.6 Constructs That Hold a Quill; § 300.4 Reclassification Procedures; § 900.7 Related Requirements; § 500.8 Field Casting Ethics and Oversight."

body.heading: § 400.12 Unauthorized Field Casting and Specimen Contamination
body.text: No research permit issued under § 400.1 shall authorize the casting of spells outside approved facilities unless explicitly stated in the grantee's license, which may be granted only for exceptional circumstances deemed necessary by a majority vote of the Conservators. Any unauthorized field casting constitutes gross misconduct punishable by immediate revocation of licensure and permanent disqualification from Guild service, pursuant to § 100.6(b). Furthermore, all specimens collected during research must remain in secure containment at all times; failure to maintain proper custody resulting in loss or contamination of evidence shall be treated as willful destruction of property under common law principles and may result in criminal charges against the responsible caster and their employer. Research permits are non-transferable and strictly personal to the named researcher, who bears sole responsibility for maintaining compliance with all stipulated conditions throughout the duration of the project. Violation of any term herein shall render void not only the specific permit but also any associated contracts or agreements entered into in reliance thereon. The Guild reserves the right to audit facilities at any time without notice and to seize suspected contraband materials subject to legal proceedings thereafter. Grantees agree to indemnify and hold harmless the Autumnwood Accords Desk from any claims arising out of negligent research practices or failure to adhere to safety protocols outlined in their license. This provision applies equally to individual practitioners operating outside formal employment relationships, who shall be held personally liable for all violations committed within their sphere of influence regardless of corporate affiliation status at time of infraction. Any disputes regarding interpretation of permit terms shall be resolved exclusively through binding arbitration administered by the Aegis Magi under rules mutually agreed upon prior to commencement of work; failure to arbitrate promptly may result in suspension of funding until resolution achieved. The integrity and sanctity of research environments must never be compromised, for carelessness here risks not only scientific progress but also public safety itself. All casters are reminded that their actions bear consequences far beyond mere academic inquiry, and they accept full responsibility for upholding the highest standards of ethical conduct in pursuit of magical knowledge. See § 100.6(b) regarding disciplinary measures; § 400.5 concerning specimen integrity obligations; and general principles laid forth in Part I relating to fiduciary duties owed by professionals to their clients and communities alike.

body.heading: § 400.13 Unauthorized Field Casting and Specimen Contamination
body.text:
§ 400.13 Unauthorized Field Casting and Specimen Contamination

No caster shall engage in field casting outside the confines of an authorized laboratory or research facility without prior written permission from the Conservators' Oversight Committee. Such unauthorized activity is strictly prohibited under § 200.1(a)(iv) and constitutes a Class A violation subject to immediate revocation of licensure pursuant to § 400.5(c).

Any specimens brought into contact with unauthorized magical effects shall be deemed contaminated for research purposes. Contaminated materials must be immediately segregated from the main collection and disposed of in accordance with hazardous waste protocols outlined under § 300.8(b)(ii). Failure to comply may result in additional fines and potential imprisonment up to five years per § 400.5(d).

The Guild reserves the right to inspect any premises suspected of unauthorized magical experimentation without warrant under Article IX, Section 2 of the Autumnwood Accords. Inspectors shall be granted full access to records, equipment, and personnel involved in such activities for a period not exceeding fourteen days unless extended by majority vote of the Oversight Committee.

Violations of § 400.13 may also trigger civil liability for damages caused to third parties through negligent or reckless magical practices outside controlled environments. Plaintiffs need only prove causation between the unauthorized casting and resulting harm, placing the burden of proof on the accused caster to demonstrate due diligence in containing effects.

The Conservators maintain a list of approved field sites where limited experimental work may be conducted under strict supervision by licensed researchers. These locations undergo regular safety audits to ensure compliance with all applicable regulations regarding containment, shielding, and emergency response procedures as detailed in Appendix C of these Accords.

Unauthorized casting in public spaces or near residential areas is particularly egregious and subject to enhanced penalties including permanent revocation of licensure and lifetime ban from the Guild's jurisdiction. Such actions threaten both public safety and the integrity of magical research as a whole.

It is the responsibility of every licensed caster to familiarize themselves fully with these provisions before commencing any experimental work outside established facilities. The consequences for noncompliance are severe and may have lasting impacts on one's career within the arcane community at large.

This section shall be read in conjunction with §§ 200.1, 300.8(b)(ii), 400.5(c)-(d), and Articles IX-Section 2 of the Autumnwood Accords governing inspection rights and civil liability standards. Any ambiguities shall be resolved in favor of public safety and containment of magical effects wherever possible.

The undersigned hereby acknowledge receipt and understanding of § 400.13 as enacted by the Mages' Guild General Assembly on this day, year 2987, during their forty-second annual session held within the sacred halls of Autumn Wood.

body.heading: § 400.6 Research Permits and Supervised Experiments
body.text:
§ 400.7 Unauthorized Field Casting, Specimen Contamination, and Ecological Harm

No researcher shall engage in field casting outside the bounds of their licensed premises without explicit consent from the local Conservator's Office. Violations constitute a Class C infraction punishable by immediate suspension of all privileges. Furthermore, researchers must maintain meticulous logs of any specimens collected during experiments, noting species designation, quantity harvested, and method of acquisition. Failure to comply with these record-keeping requirements shall be deemed gross negligence and subject to severe penalties including permanent revocation of licensure. The Guild reserves the right to audit such records at its sole discretion upon reasonable notice. Researchers found guilty of knowingly contaminating local ecosystems through reckless experimentation may face criminal charges under applicable environmental statutes in addition to Guild sanctions. It is incumbent upon every caster to exercise due diligence in minimizing their environmental footprint, recognizing that unchecked magical activity poses an existential threat to the delicate balance of nature. The Archmages stand ready to intervene decisively should any individual prove unwilling to abide by these fundamental tenets of responsible practice.

body.heading: § 400.6 Unauthorized Field Casting and Specimen Contamination
body.text:
§ 400.6 No caster shall engage in unscheduled field operations within the Guild's jurisdiction without prior authorization from the Archmage Sovereign or her delegate. Violation of this provision constitutes a Class A felony under the Accords, subject to immediate arrest and trial by Paradox Trial (§ 100.5). Furthermore, any unauthorized magical activity that results in contamination or degradation of specimens held in safekeeping shall be treated as gross negligence warranting disbarment without recourse. See § 200.9 for penalties applicable to unlicensed practitioners.

The prohibition against unscheduled field casting arises from the inherent unpredictability and potential hazards associated with such operations outside controlled environments. The Guild's primary mandate is the preservation of magical knowledge and public safety, both of which are compromised when mages engage in risky experiments without proper oversight. As stated in § 300.2, "the study of magic demands rigorous discipline and meticulous recordkeeping," principles that cannot be adequately maintained during impromptu fieldwork.

Specimen contamination poses an additional threat to the integrity of the Guild's research efforts. Specimens are invaluable resources for advancing magical understanding, and their loss or degradation due to careless handling undermines years of painstaking collection and preservation work. Under § 400.5, all casters must exercise extreme caution when working near specimen storage areas, ensuring that no stray spells or effects interfere with the delicate balance maintained by the Conservators.

In cases where emergency field casting becomes absolutely necessary—for instance, to neutralize an imminent threat—the caster bears sole responsibility for obtaining retroactive approval from senior magi within twenty-four hours of the incident's resolution. Failure to comply with this reporting requirement will result in automatic suspension of licensure pending investigation into the circumstances surrounding the unauthorized operation. See § 600.1 regarding contractual obligations between casters and clients, which must not supersede public safety concerns outlined herein.

The penalties for violating § 400.6 are severe and designed to deter reckless behavior by all practitioners operating under Guild protection. Disbarment serves as the ultimate sanction, effectively ending a caster's career in accordance with § 300.8 ("the privilege of casting is earned, not given freely"). Lesser offenses may incur monetary fines or temporary suspension proportional to the gravity of the infraction and any resulting harm caused. Ultimately, adherence to these provisions ensures that magic remains a force for good rather than chaos unchecked by reason.

This section supplements existing regulations governing professional conduct and public safety without duplicating material already codified elsewhere in the Accords. By clarifying the scope of permissible field activities, § 400.6 strikes an appropriate balance between facilitating legitimate research endeavors and protecting against abuse of powers entrusted to those licensed by the Guild's authority.

body.heading: 400.6 Research Permits and Supervised Experiments; Unauthorized Field Casting
body.text:
§ 400.13 Related Requirements — Conducting Experiments Outside the Guild

A research permit issued under § 200.9 shall not authorize a caster to conduct experiments beyond the limits prescribed therein, nor does it relieve the holder of any obligations imposed by law or custom. Any attempt to exceed these boundaries renders the experiment void and subject to immediate revocation of the permit. The Guild retains sole discretion over where, when, and how research may be performed, with no exceptions for emergency situations unless expressly stated in the original grant. Unauthorized experiments constitute a serious breach of trust and may result in permanent disqualification from future licensure.

Furthermore, all experiments must be conducted under direct supervision by a licensed supervisor appointed by the Guild. This individual shall verify that safety protocols are followed at all times and intervene immediately if any irregularities arise. Failure to comply with these oversight measures will nullify the validity of the experiment's results and may lead to disciplinary action against both the principal investigator and their supervisor. The Guild reserves the right to audit research facilities, review logs, and interview personnel as part of its quality assurance process. Any resistance to such audits shall be deemed a violation of the Accords.

In addition, casters are reminded that unauthorized field casting remains strictly prohibited outside of approved settings. This prohibition extends to all forms of experimental magic, whether performed for personal gain or curiosity. Violations will be prosecuted under applicable statutes and may result in criminal charges beyond mere civil penalties. The Guild takes such matters extremely seriously, as they pose significant risks to public safety and the integrity of magical practice. All casters are urged to adhere scrupulously to these guidelines at all times.

Finally, this section serves notice that no private arrangements or side deals shall circumvent the terms set forth herein. Any attempt to do so will be treated as a deliberate act of sabotage against the Guild's interests and may warrant severe consequences under existing law. The Accords stand firm on this point: there are no exceptions for those who choose to ignore them. All parties concerned are expected to abide by these rules without deviation, now and forevermore. Only then can we ensure that magic continues to flourish safely within our borders.

sections.title: Duty to File Before Casting — §900.11

body.heading: § 900.1 Duty to File Before Casting
body.text:
Every licensed caster shall file an intent-to-cast declaration with the Guild Desk no less than seven days prior to any scheduled magical event of material consequence. Such filing must specify the nature and scope of the intended spellwork, along with a detailed inventory of all enchanted items or reagents to be employed. Failure to comply with this prerequisite renders the subsequent casting illegal per se, subjecting the offender to immediate revocation of credentials and potential arrest for unauthorized practice of magic.

The necessity of prior notification serves multiple critical functions within the regulatory framework. Firstly, it affords the Guild adequate opportunity to vet the proposed activity against existing safety protocols and environmental concerns. Secondly, it facilitates proper allocation of emergency response resources should complications arise during execution. Finally, the declaration creates an official audit trail necessary for accountability purposes should adverse outcomes occur. All filings must be accompanied by a valid proof-of-competence certificate and payment of applicable licensing fees in full.

Casters who neglect to file required declarations shall face escalating sanctions commensurate with the severity and consequences of their unauthorized operations. Initial offenses may result in monetary penalties ranging from one hundred to five thousand gold pieces, depending upon factors such as potential harm caused and prior disciplinary record. Repeat violators risk suspension or permanent expulsion from the Guild entirely, forfeiting all rights to practice magic within jurisdictional bounds. In cases where illegal casting leads to demonstrable injury or property damage, civil litigation may also be pursued against the responsible party individually.

The seven-day advance notice requirement shall not apply under exceptional circumstances deemed sufficiently urgent by mutual agreement between the caster and an appointed Guild overseer. Such exemptions must be documented in writing with justification articulated clearly. Any waivers of this provision granted ad hoc shall automatically expire at conclusion of the specific event for which they were issued, requiring re-filing should similar activities recur subsequently. The Guild retains sole discretion to determine whether any given situation warrants expedited processing status absent contrary evidence presented by interested parties.

This duty extends equally to both individual practitioners and corporate entities engaging in magical services. Organizational charters or employment contracts cannot override the statutory obligation imposed upon all certified casters uniformly. Violations constitute serious breaches of professional ethics regardless of mitigating factors unique to particular cases. Enforcement mechanisms remain robust with swift disciplinary action available at any stage of investigation into suspected non-compliance. Adherence to filing mandates remains paramount for maintaining public trust in regulated magical practices across all sectors of society today and tomorrow alike.

see § 900.2 Reporting of Material Enchantments; see § 1.4 Persons Bound; under § 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting; compare § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts with § 400.1 Research Permits.

body.heading: § 900.6 Reporting of Material Enchantments
body.text: Every caster shall disclose to the Accords Desk any material enchantment they bring into their possession, regardless of provenance or intent. Failure to do so is deemed willful concealment and subject to severe penalty under § 1.8(b). Disclosure must be made within seven days of acquisition or creation, accompanied by full details regarding origin, composition, and intended use. The Desk shall then evaluate the item against § 300.2 to determine its classification as a relic, artifact, or contraband. Any unauthorized enchantment found in a caster's possession constitutes prima facie evidence of illegal practice under § 200.1(c). This duty extends equally to all parties involved in the acquisition chain, including buyers, sellers, and intermediaries. Concealment of material facts regarding an item's nature or capabilities shall be punished as fraud under applicable law. The Accords Desk reserves the right to inspect any suspected enchantment deemed potentially dangerous or unlawful. Caster refusal to submit such items for inspection is grounds for immediate suspension of their license pending further inquiry under § 200.4(a)(ii). All reported items shall be catalogued and stored securely until disposition orders are issued by the Desk pursuant to established procedures outlined in § 100.3(b). This reporting requirement exists solely to ensure public safety and prevent abuse of magical items outside regulated channels. No individual is exempt from this obligation, regardless of status or prior compliance record. Violations shall be prosecuted with utmost vigor to uphold the integrity of our enchantment marketplace. The Accords Desk stands ready to assist any caster in fulfilling these obligations upon request.

body.heading: § 900.11 Duty to File Before Casting
body.text: No mage shall cast any spell of the Third Degree or higher without first filing a full disclosure with the Accords Desk, as required by § 200.1. This duty applies regardless of whether the casting is commercial, charitable, or for personal amusement. Failure to comply renders the act illegal under § 900.6 and subjects the caster to penalties under Part IX. Exceptions may be granted only in cases of dire emergency where immediate action is necessary to prevent loss of life, at which point a retroactive filing must still be submitted within seven days. See also § 100.2 for provisions regarding authorized representatives acting on behalf of registered offices. Under § 300.6, unregistered casters are presumed guilty unless they can prove otherwise through testimony and physical evidence. The burden of proof rests squarely upon the accused to demonstrate that their actions did not violate any provision of this Code. In all instances where doubt exists as to whether a filing was properly executed, the Accords Desk retains sole discretion to determine compliance based on its own assessment of the facts presented. This authority shall not be challenged in any court unless specifically authorized by statute or judicial precedent binding upon this body. All filings must be made directly with a designated clerk and accompanied by all requisite fees as set forth in § 900.4. Any attempt to circumvent these requirements through proxies, agents, or other means is strictly prohibited and shall result in immediate revocation of the caster's license under Part VIII. The Accords Desk further reserves the right to audit any filing at its sole discretion and impose additional sanctions for non-compliance discovered during such reviews. Finally, no exemption from this requirement shall be implied by custom, usage, or prior practice unless expressly stated herein. Any person violating these provisions shall be subject to all remedies available under applicable law, including but not limited to fines, imprisonment, and permanent disqualification from practicing magic within the jurisdiction.

body.heading: § 900.6 Related Requirements: Duty to File Before Casting; Record Retention and
body.text:
Every licensed caster is bound by an affirmative duty to file any new spell, ritual, or magical construct before its first public deployment. This pre-clearance requirement serves as a primary check against the proliferation of unregulated arcane power within the community. Failure to comply renders subsequent casting acts subject to immediate seizure and potential revocation of one's license under § 900.8. The Desk maintains exclusive authority over what may be cast, when, and by whom; no individual possesses inherent rights to unleash magic upon the world without prior authorization.

Filing submissions must include full provenance documentation detailing origin, composition, intended use-case scenarios, risk assessments, and mitigation strategies where applicable. Innovators proposing novel applications of forbidden arts face heightened scrutiny and may be required to undergo extended review periods or supplementary testing protocols before approval is granted. Conservators retain discretion to reject any submission deemed contrary to established stability principles, regardless of technical legality under other provisions.

Approved filings become part of the permanent Guild record and remain accessible for inspection by authorized personnel upon request. Casters must produce original documentation when challenged regarding their casting activities or compliance status. Tampering with, falsifying, or destroying filing records constitutes a serious offense punishable up to permanent disqualification from magical practice. The burden of proof rests squarely on the caster to demonstrate full adherence to all relevant statutes and regulations at any given time.

This system ensures transparency while maintaining necessary safeguards against abuse. Nothing herein shall be construed to abridge legitimate research efforts conducted within permitted facilities under proper supervision. Rather, it establishes a clear framework for responsible magical stewardship by the entire community, balancing individual freedom with collective security interests as envisioned in § 1.7. All members agree to abide by these requirements without exception or condition, recognizing their vital role in preserving harmony across all realms touched by arcane influence.

body.heading: § 900.6 Related Requirements: Duty to File Before Casting
body.text:
Under the Autumnwood Accords, every mage is required to file a detailed description of any spell or enchantment before casting it in public or commercial settings. This provision serves multiple purposes, foremost among them being the prevention of accidental harm and the maintenance of magical stability across the realm. By mandating prior registration, the Guild ensures that each caster has undergone appropriate training and assessment for the specific power they intend to wield.

The filing process involves submitting a written declaration containing the spell's name, components, intended effects, and estimated duration. The mage must also provide evidence of competency, such as certification from an accredited institution or recommendation from a practicing archmage. Failure to comply with this requirement subjects the offender to immediate suspension until proper documentation is provided. Repeated violations may result in permanent revocation of casting privileges under § 900.14.

This preemptive measure reflects the Guild's commitment to responsible magical practice. With countless spells available for study and application, it is imperative that each user demonstrates mastery before unleashing their abilities upon unsuspecting bystanders. The burden falls squarely upon individual practitioners to adhere to these standards, safeguarding both themselves and society at large from unintended consequences of poorly controlled magic.

By enforcing strict pre-casting protocols, the Autumnwood Accords strike a balance between fostering innovation and mitigating risk. While some may view such regulations as burdensome red tape, they ultimately serve the greater good by promoting safe and ethical use of arcane arts throughout the Midlands region. Compliance remains non-negotiable for all registered mages seeking to operate within legal bounds.

see § 900.3 Record Retention; see § 1.7 Construction: Aggregation of Conduct; see under § 200.5 Guest Casters regarding temporary permissions.

body.heading: § 900.7 Pre-Casting Certification and Validation Procedures
body.text:
In furtherance of the duty to file prior to casting, each licensed mage must obtain formal certification and validation before undertaking any spellcasting activity that involves material enchantments or permanent alterations. This requirement serves as a critical safeguard against unauthorized modifications to protected artifacts and ensures compliance with established magical safety standards.

The validation process begins with submission of a detailed proposal outlining the nature and scope of the intended enchantment, along with supporting evidence demonstrating competence and adherence to ethical guidelines. The Guild's Office of Arcane Review shall evaluate each application within seven business days of receipt, granting approval only upon satisfaction of all regulatory criteria. Any discrepancies or concerns must be promptly communicated to the applicant for resolution before proceeding further.

Upon issuance of a valid certificate, the mage may execute the planned enchantments under direct supervision by an authorized inspector if deemed necessary by the reviewing body. All completed works shall undergo subsequent verification testing to confirm proper functioning and absence of unintended side effects. Failure to comply with these certification requirements constitutes grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of licensure privileges, regardless of other qualifications possessed by the individual.

The provisions herein apply equally to both original creators and resellers of enchanted items, recognizing that either party may introduce modifications during production or trade. Joint liability shall attach when multiple entities contribute to the final result without adequate oversight mechanisms in place beforehand. This shared responsibility reinforces collective accountability throughout the magical economy while mitigating risks posed by unchecked experimentation.

By mandating rigorous pre-authorization protocols, the Autumnwood Accords aim to balance innovation with stability within the broader arcane community. While some may view such restrictions as impediments to creative expression, their ultimate purpose remains preservation of public safety and maintenance of harmonious coexistence between casters and non-casters alike. Through diligent enforcement of these standards over time, it is hoped that trust in magical practices shall steadily increase across all societal strata.
