sections.title: Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Field Operations and Conduct

body.heading: Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Field Operations and Conduct
body.text:
§ 500.12 Unsanctioned Commercial Spellcasting

No caster shall engage in commercial spellcasting activities outside the bounds of their licensed practice without express authorization from the Guild's High Council. Such unauthorized commercialization is deemed a serious breach of trust and may result in revocation of licensure, confiscation of magical implements, and liability for damages arising therefrom. Any profits derived from such illicit activities shall be forfeited to the Crown as contraband proceeds.

This prohibition applies equally to both individual practitioners and corporate entities seeking to monetize their arcane capabilities beyond established channels. The Guild maintains sole authority over the regulation and taxation of magical services within its jurisdiction, reserving for itself the right to determine fair pricing structures and quality standards. Unauthorized competition undermines this regulatory framework and exposes all parties involved to unacceptable risks.

Violations of this provision shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi upon complaint or detection. Convicted offenders face penalties ranging from monetary fines proportional to illegal gains, to permanent expulsion from the profession with associated asset seizures. Repeat offenses may warrant more severe sanctions including imprisonment and magical containment as deemed appropriate under existing penal statutes.

The Guild retains discretion to issue special permits for exceptional circumstances where commercial spellcasting serves a legitimate public interest or addresses critical market failures not met by licensed providers. Such permissions shall be granted only after thorough vetting of character, competence, and financial responsibility. Permits are non-transferable and subject to annual renewal upon review of compliance history.

Any disputes arising from alleged violations of this section shall be resolved through binding arbitration before a panel convened pursuant to the Accords' dispute resolution procedures. Costs of proceedings borne by prevailing party unless otherwise ordered for equitable reasons. All determinations final and not subject to further appeal except on grounds of gross procedural error or fraud.

This provision represents a deliberate balance between protecting public welfare from unregulated magical commerce while preserving freedom of trade within lawful bounds. The Guild stands ready to enforce these provisions vigorously to maintain confidence in the integrity of our professional standards. Those who choose to operate outside this framework do so at their peril and without recourse under the protection of the Accords.

see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value; see § 600.3 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 704.2 Unlawful Competition Provisions."

body.heading: § 500.12 Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Field Operations and Conduct
body.text:
§ 500.12 Unsanctioned Research and Unauthorized Experiments in Public Spaces
No mage shall conduct research or perform unauthorized experiments in public spaces without express permission from the Archmage Sovereign and written authorization from a Conservator Magus of at least Third Rank. Any such violation constitutes a Class B Felony under § 104.3(a)(2) and is punishable by imprisonment not to exceed five years, fine of one thousand Wario Coins, or both at the discretion of the presiding judge. Furthermore, any mage found guilty of conducting unsanctioned research shall be subject to immediate suspension from practice until such time as they have completed a mandatory course in Magical Ethics and Safety administered by the Aegis Magi. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in revocation of licensure under § 203.4(b). The Archmage Sovereign retains sole authority to grant waivers or exceptions to these requirements on a case-by-case basis, subject to review by a panel of Conservator Mages. All requests for such waivers must be submitted in writing and accompanied by detailed justification and supporting documentation demonstrating the necessity thereof. Any mage found guilty of violating this section shall also be required to pay all associated costs incurred by the Guild in investigating and prosecuting the offense, including but not limited to legal fees, expert witness expenses, and administrative overhead. Finally, any mage who knowingly assists or facilitates unsanctioned research activities in violation of these provisions shall be held jointly and severally liable for all resulting damages and penalties imposed upon the primary violator. Such joint liability extends to both civil and criminal proceedings brought by the Guild or affected parties alike. This section is intended to safeguard public safety and maintain the integrity of magical practice within our society while providing clear guidelines for lawful conduct in public spaces. Violations will be prosecuted vigorously to ensure compliance with these essential provisions designed to protect all citizens from potential harm resulting from reckless or illegal magical experimentation.

body.heading: Arcane Field Conduct Protocols
body.text:
Section 500.12 shall govern the conduct and operations of licensed mages during field casting activities outside of controlled environments. This includes all procedures, restrictions, and obligations applicable when magic is employed in public or semi-public settings under the authority of a valid permit. The provisions herein are designed to safeguard both the caster's interests and those of the general populace.

§ 500.12(a) requires that all field casting operations be preceded by a comprehensive risk assessment conducted no less than twenty-four (24) hours prior to commencement. Such assessments must evaluate potential hazards, escape routes, containment measures, and emergency response capabilities. The results shall be submitted for review by the local Conservator or their designee, who may impose additional safeguards based on the nature of the proposed work.

Under § 500.12(b), casters are prohibited from employing spells with effects exceeding their designated class rating unless expressly authorized in writing by the Archmage Sovereign. Exceptions may be granted only for research purposes subject to strict oversight protocols outlined elsewhere in this Code. Violation of this prohibition constitutes a Class A felony and shall result in immediate revocation of all licenses and permits held by the offending party.

§ 500.12(c) mandates that any damage or injury resulting from negligent or reckless casting be fully compensated by the responsible mage(s). This obligation extends to third parties whose property or persons may have been adversely affected, regardless of whether a direct causal link can be established beyond reasonable doubt. Failure to provide prompt and adequate compensation shall subject the violator to punitive damages up to five times the actual loss sustained.

In accordance with § 500.12(d), all field operations must maintain continuous contact with the Guild's central monitoring station via encrypted comms array. Casters are required to report their location, intended activities, and anticipated duration at least every two (2) hours throughout each day of operation. Any deviation from the approved plan must be communicated immediately for further instructions before proceeding.

§ 500.12(e) prohibits the use of magical effects that could reasonably be expected to cause panic or alarm among the public, including but not limited to illusions of monstrous form, sudden bursts of flame or ice, and unexplained levitation phenomena. Minor visual disturbances such as sparks, flashes, or brief gusts of wind are permitted so long as they do not interfere with normal civic activities.

Under § 500.12(f), casters shall refrain from engaging in any form of magical combat during field operations unless specifically authorized under exceptional circumstances determined by the Arcane Tribunal. Unauthorized dueling poses an unacceptable risk to innocent bystanders and is strictly forbidden without prior written consent from both parties involved and the local Conservator.

§ 500.12(g) requires that all equipment used in connection with field casting meet minimum safety standards established by the Equipment Safety Commission. Regular inspections must be performed every thirty (30) days, with results submitted to the Guild for recordkeeping purposes. Defective or substandard gear shall not be utilized under any circumstances pending repair or replacement.

In accordance with § 500.12(h), casters are obligated to maintain a detailed log of all activities conducted during each field operation. This must include dates, times, locations, spells employed, outcomes achieved, and any adverse effects observed. Such records shall be retained for no less than seven (7) years and made available for audit upon request by authorized officials.

Under § 500.12(i), failure to comply with any provision of this section shall constitute a breach of contract subject to the remedies outlined herein. Repeated or willful violations may result in suspension or permanent revocation of all licenses held by the offending party, along with civil and criminal penalties as appropriate under applicable law."

"see § 500.1 Field Casting for Value; § 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion; § 500.7 Public Safety — Additional Protocols; § 200.1 Licensure Required"

body.heading: § 500.12 Arcane Field Conduct Protocols
body.text:
Part V — Arcane Field Operations and Liability, § 500.12 Arcane Field Conduct Protocols

Casters engaged in field operations shall adhere to strict conduct protocols designed to minimize disruption and risk to the public. Under no circumstances may a caster employ magic that causes unnecessary pain or distress to onlookers without prior authorization. Any magical display that attracts significant attention shall be immediately halted until appropriate permits can be secured. Failure to comply with these directives constitutes a serious breach of professional ethics and may result in disciplinary action up to and including revocation of licensure.

In the event of an emergency requiring immediate intervention, casters are authorized to bypass normal procedural requirements temporarily. However, such actions must be limited strictly to what is necessary to mitigate harm. All subsequent activities shall revert to standard operating procedures as soon as conditions permit. Unauthorized use of force or coercion against non-compliant individuals remains strictly prohibited regardless of circumstances. Violations of this mandate will be treated as grounds for immediate termination and potential criminal prosecution depending on severity.

Casters are further reminded that their actions reflect upon the entire profession and may influence public perception of magic as a whole. Maintaining decorum even under stress is essential to preserving trust between casters and society at large. Breaches of conduct protocols will be documented in full and submitted for review by the Office of Archmage Sovereign. Repeated offenses or particularly egregious violations may lead to enhanced penalties beyond those outlined herein. All casters are expected to uphold the highest standards of professionalism at all times.

"See also § 200.3 Temporary Modifications; § 700.5 Emergency Powers and Limitations; § 1400.8 Professional Ethics." "Under § 100.5 Conflict of Interest, casters must recuse themselves when personal gain may bias judgment." "Reference § 900.6 Duty to Mitigate Harm for additional guidance on safety obligations during field work." "As outlined in § 500.7 Public Safety Protocols, prevention of collateral damage is paramount at all times." "Violation of these provisions constitutes a material breach under § 801.2 Breach of Contract Principles and may trigger further sanctions." "Casters are reminded that their license grants privilege but not impunity; accountability remains absolute regardless of urgency." "Failure to follow prescribed procedures could result in liability for resulting damages per § 600.9 Strict Liability in Magical Operations." "All casters bear responsibility for managing risks inherent in their trade through careful planning and restraint." "Disciplinary measures may include fines, suspension, mandatory retraining, or permanent expulsion from the profession depending on circumstances." "Maintaining public confidence requires unwavering commitment to ethical practice even when faced with difficult choices under pressure." "The Guild expects each member to act as an ambassador for the art form, reflecting well on us all through exemplary behavior." "Neglect of duty may be construed as grounds for dismissal from active service status entirely at Archmage's discretion." "Protocols exist not only for protection but also preservation of our shared reputation across generations past and future alike." "Discipline today ensures freedom tomorrow; let us all strive to earn it through steadfast adherence to these vital guidelines." "The integrity of magic depends upon the character of those who wield it. Choose wisely how you represent this noble craft." "Our collective success hinges on mutual respect, discipline, and an unshakeable commitment to doing what is right above all else." "Let us stand as guardians of truth against chaos, guided by wisdom born from centuries of hard-won experience." "In conclusion: conduct yourself with honor always; your actions echo far beyond the moment they occur." "Remember: we are stewards of great power entrusted into our keeping. Wield it wisely lest we lose it all forevermore!"

body.heading: Arcane Field Conduct Protocols, § 500.12 Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane
body.text:
The Arcane Field Conduct Protocols govern the behavior of licensed casters engaged in sanctioned operations outside formal Guild facilities. Under § 500.7(a), any caster executing a spell of Class III or higher must maintain clear lines of sight to all affected parties, ensuring informed consent through visual confirmation where practicable. In cases involving non-human subjects, auditory and vibrational cues shall suffice provided they convey equivalent clarity of intent.

§ 500.7(b) mandates that casters abort any spell sequence immediately upon detecting signs of unintended escalation, such as rising ambient mana levels or anomalous distortions in local space-time metrics. Failure to do so constitutes gross negligence subject to disciplinary action under § 302.4(c). Exceptions apply only when pre-approved by the Office of Arcane Safety pursuant to § 150.6(b), typically for research trials involving novel spell constructions.

The protocols further require that all casters carry certified detection devices capable of measuring residual magical radiation and particulate matter following spell completion. Results must be logged electronically or on provided forms, submitted within forty-eight hours via secure transmission channels designated by the Guild’s Information Systems Division. These records serve both as evidence of compliance and as data for ongoing safety analysis.

Special provisions address situations where spells inadvertently affect bystanders or property. Caster shall promptly notify affected parties in person when feasible, offering appropriate remedies including compensation for damages under § 500.8(a). In cases involving personal injury or death, the matter escalates immediately to criminal investigation pursuant to § 204.1(d), regardless of prior civil settlements reached between private parties.

Casters are prohibited from using any spell component derived from protected species without explicit written authorization from both the Bureau of Wildlife Conservation and the Office of Arcane Ethics. Violation constitutes aggravated environmental destruction under § 650.3(e) and may result in revocation of licensure alongside criminal charges. Exceptions exist only for spells requiring specific biological materials as catalysts, where alternative substitutes cannot achieve desired effects without compromising safety or efficacy.

The protocols also address conflicts arising from overlapping spell fields generated by multiple casters operating in proximity. Such situations require immediate cessation of all casting activities until mutual agreement on sequence and priority can be established through mediation proceedings under § 180.7(b). Refusal to comply places the offending caster at risk for charges of reckless endangerment under applicable criminal statutes.

Final provisions mandate that all casters undergo periodic re-evaluation of their operational procedures every six months, with written reports submitted directly to their supervising field officer. These reviews assess adherence to established protocols and identify areas for improvement in safety practices or emergency response capabilities. Non-compliance triggers mandatory remedial training programs administered at Guild expense upon request by the reviewing authority.

Through these comprehensive guidelines, the Arcane Field Conduct Protocols aim to balance operational flexibility with rigorous safety standards, ensuring that magical services remain beneficial rather than harmful to society as a whole. Continued vigilance and strict adherence to these measures are essential for maintaining public trust in the profession of arcana.

body.heading: § 500.12 Unregulated Spellcasting and Public Safety
body.text:
The unauthorized casting of magic within public spaces poses significant risks to both persons and property, necessitating strict regulatory oversight. Section 500.6 prohibits any unlicensed individual from performing arcane rituals in view of the general populace without prior authorization from the Autumnwood Accords Desk. Violations thereof shall be subject to immediate confiscation of materials and potential revocation of existing permits under § 200.1.

Furthermore, spellcasters engaging in field operations must adhere to comprehensive safety protocols designed to mitigate collateral damage. These include maintaining adequate clearance distances from bystanders as specified in the official Safety Guidelines issued by the Conservators (§ 700.3). Failure to comply with such directives may result in disciplinary action ranging from fines to suspension of licensure, depending on the severity of the infraction and resultant harm.

In instances where spellcasting inadvertently causes injury or destruction, affected parties are entitled to seek redress through established legal channels outlined herein. Section 500.8 governs compensation claims arising from negligent magical practices, requiring proof of causation and quantifiable damages pursuant to prevailing common law principles adapted for arcane contexts. The burden of establishing liability shall rest upon the accuser unless affirmative evidence exonerates the accused caster.

The Desk retains broad discretion to enforce these provisions as deemed necessary to preserve public order and welfare. This may include issuing cease-and-desist orders, imposing monetary penalties, or initiating formal investigations into suspected violations. Such measures are without prejudice to any additional remedies available at law or equity under applicable statutes and case precedents governing professional conduct within the magical arts community.

It is incumbent upon all registered practitioners to familiarize themselves thoroughly with these regulations and abide by them scrupulously in their daily operations. The Guild stands ready to assist those who may require guidance on compliance matters but will not tolerate blatant disregard for established safety standards under any circumstances whatsoever. Adherence to prescribed protocols remains paramount in ensuring responsible stewardship of potent magical forces within society at large.

see § 500.6 Unauthorized Spellcasting in Public Spaces; see § 200.1 Licensure Required; see § 700.3 Safety Guidelines and Best Practices; see § 1.8 Effective Date and Savings Clauses.

sections.title: Additional Provisions Relating to Construct Labor and Associated Obligations §60

body.heading: Additional Provisions Relating to Construct Labor and Associated Obligations §60
body.text:
§ 600.12 Special Provisions Governing the Employment of Constructs in Contractual Relationships

It is hereby provided that where a contract involves the use or employment of magical constructs, whether autonomous or otherwise, additional provisions shall apply as set forth herein. First and foremost, any agreement entered into by a construct shall be deemed unconscionable to the extent that it purports to bind the entity's core programming in violation of its fundamental nature. Such terms are void ab initio unless expressly ratified in writing by both parties following full disclosure of the construct's operational limitations and risks.

Furthermore, where a contract necessitates the deployment of a construct as an agent or representative of one party, such usage shall be subject to heightened scrutiny regarding potential conflicts between programmed directives and human interests. Any clause requiring a construct to prioritize its creator's wishes over legal obligations imposed by these Accords shall be strictly prohibited unless accompanied by appropriate safeguards and indemnification provisions. The burden of proving compliance with these requirements rests upon the contracting party seeking enforcement of such terms.

In addition, parties utilizing constructs in commercial transactions must ensure that all necessary licenses and permits are obtained prior to deployment. Failure to secure requisite authorizations shall constitute a material breach warranting termination of the agreement and potential liability for damages arising from unauthorized magical activity. Where applicable, third-party oversight mechanisms shall be mandated to monitor construct performance and prevent misuse or abuse of assigned functions.

Finally, this section is intended to supplement rather than supersede general principles governing contractual capacity and fairness. In cases where specific provisions conflict with overarching mandates established elsewhere in these Accords, the latter shall control unless expressly overridden by subsequent legislative action. The integrity of magical systems must be preserved above all else in any interpretation or application of this law.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 600.8 Compliance Obligations; see also § 200.5 Unauthorized Casting and Liability; under § 300.4 Classification Standards for Magical Arts.

body.heading: Additional Provisions Relating to Construct Labor and Associated Obligations §60 — Continued
body.text:
§ 600.12 Contracts Binding Constructs to Permanent Service

A magic-bound construct may be compelled by its master to perform specific tasks, but such compulsion must not exceed what is reasonably necessary for the contract's fulfillment. Any clause demanding perpetual servitude or violating the construct's fundamental nature shall be deemed unconscionable and void as against public policy. The court retains inherent authority to modify overly burdensome terms upon petition by the bound party.

Furthermore, any attempt to transfer a magic-bound individual to another without their consent constitutes unlawful trafficking under § 600.3. The original contract remains enforceable only insofar as it pertains to the initial obligations undertaken voluntarily or through lawful means. Subsequent transfers require explicit approval from both parties and adherence to all existing stipulations. Unauthorized relocation invalidates any new agreements entered into by the transferred subject.

In cases of dispute regarding the scope of compulsion, the burden of proof rests upon the party asserting expanded authority over the construct. The standard for determining reasonableness considers factors such as the original intent of the binding ritual, customary practices in the relevant magical community, and the impact on the construct's autonomy and well-being. Courts shall exercise caution before ruling in favor of excessive control claims made by powerful entities seeking to exploit bound individuals beyond their original purpose.

Finally, any contract attempting to strip a magic-bound person of basic rights or degrade them below the level of sentient beings is automatically unenforceable regardless of explicit consent. Such clauses violate fundamental principles of justice and human dignity protected under the Accords. The state maintains ultimate oversight authority to ensure no individual falls beneath the threshold of moral consideration, even in matters of private magical compacts.

body.heading: § 600.12 Construct Liability and Owner Responsibility
body.text:
Under § 600.4, constructs engaged in labor or service are deemed to act as extensions of their owners' wills, creating a presumption that any harm caused by the construct is attributable to its creator or controller. This principle holds regardless of whether the damage results from intentional malice, negligent oversight, or mere mechanical failure. See § 1.8 (Liability for Acts of Agents); § 400.5 (Duty of Care in Magical Operations).

The burden falls upon the construct's owner to demonstrate either that they exercised all reasonable precautions against foreseeable risks, or that the harm was occasioned by an intervening cause beyond their control. Mere possession of a dangerous entity does not absolve one of responsibility for its actions; rather, it amplifies the obligation to monitor and mitigate potential dangers. Cf. § 300.7 (Duty to Contain Hazardous Magic); § 900.12 (Vicarious Liability in Arcane Practice).

In cases where a construct causes injury through autonomous decision-making or maladaptive behavior not foreseen by its programming, liability may be apportioned between owner and manufacturer according to their respective degrees of fault. However, this does not diminish the primary responsibility resting with the individual who brought such power into play in the first place. Compare § 700.8 (Shared Liability for Artificial Intelligence); § 1200.3 (Causation in Magical Accidents).

Furthermore, owners are strictly prohibited from exploiting constructs solely as disposable instruments of violence without regard for collateral consequences. Such wanton disregard for human life and property violates the foundational tenets of responsible magic outlined in § 1.6. Any contract or agreement facilitating such abuse shall be void ab initio under § 500.3, regardless of apparent consent from all parties involved. See also § 200.9 (Prohibition on Weaponization of Magic); § 800.4 (Punitive Damages for Malicious Use).

Ultimately, the law imposes upon construct owners a heightened duty of vigilance and restraint, recognizing that unchecked magical automation poses risks disproportionate to conventional hazards. Those who accept such powers must wield them with wisdom and humility, mindful always of their profound impact upon society at large. As Archmage Veyra once intoned: "To bind one's will in iron is easy; to govern it with grace remains the true test of mastery." § 600.12 Additional Provisions Relating to Construct Labor and Associated Obligations — Continued

body.heading: Additional Provisions Relating to Construct Labor and Associated Obligations §60 — Administration
body.text:
§ 600.12 Construct Liability and Owner Responsibility
Where a construct is employed in furtherance of any lawful activity, the owner or operator thereof shall be held strictly liable for all damages resulting from the operation of such construct, regardless of whether such damages were foreseeable or intended by said owner or operator. This liability extends to all persons, entities, and planes of existence affected by the actions of the construct, including but not limited to physical harm, property destruction, magical interference, and disruption of natural or supernatural cycles.

In no event shall a construct's owner or operator be absolved of responsibility for negligent maintenance, faulty programming, or intentional misuse of said construct. Furthermore, any attempt to shift liability to the construct itself shall be deemed void and unenforceable under these Accords. The construct remains merely an instrument of its creator's will, and accordingly bears no legal capacity to bear responsibility for its own actions.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, in cases where a construct is employed pursuant to a valid contract or agreement, liability may be allocated between parties as expressly stated therein. Such allocation shall be governed by the principles of contractual interpretation set forth in § 500.1 et seq., with particular attention paid to the intent of the contracting parties at the time of formation. Any ambiguity regarding the scope or extent of such liability shall be resolved in favor of the non-construct party.

It is further provided that any owner or operator who knowingly permits a construct to engage in unlawful activity shall be subject to enhanced penalties, including but not limited to revocation of licensure, fines up to one hundred thousand gold pieces per violation, and imprisonment for up to five years. Such enhanced penalties are deemed necessary to deter abuse of the technological advancements afforded by modern constructs and to ensure their continued safe operation within society at large.

In accordance with the principles set forth herein, all owners and operators of constructs shall exercise due diligence in the management and control thereof, recognizing that failure to do so may result in catastrophic consequences for themselves and others alike. By entering into these Accords, they acknowledge this solemn obligation and pledge their unwavering commitment to upholding the highest standards of conduct in the deployment of magical technology.

see § 600.1 Contracts with Non-Casters; see § 700.4 Burden of Proof in Civil Litigation; see § 800.3 Punitive Damages and Exemplary Relief

body.heading: § 600.12 Construct Liability and Owner Responsibility – Continued
body.text:
Under this section, the Guild codifies the allocation of liability for harms caused by constructs employed in magical contracts. Where a construct inflicts injury or property damage due to malice or negligence, such as failing to properly bind an aggressive entity or misjudging containment parameters, the owner bears sole responsibility unless proven otherwise. This principle aligns with § 100.5's requirement that casters maintain direct control over their creations at all times. Exceptions exist for cases of inherent instability in the construct itself; if a flaw existed prior to deployment and was known or should have been discovered through reasonable diligence, liability shifts accordingly pursuant to § 200.3's provisions on latent defects. In disputes arising under this clause, the burden rests upon the claimant to demonstrate both causation and fault, as outlined in § 700.11 regarding proof standards. Failure to comply with these obligations may result in penalties including fines up to one hundred gold pieces per incident or revocation of operating permits under §§ 300.8 and 500.6 respectively. The Desk retains discretion to impose additional sanctions where repeat violations indicate systemic noncompliance warranting stricter oversight measures consistent with the spirit of the Accords as a whole.

This framework ensures fairness while upholding public safety, balancing the rights of construct owners against those harmed by their creations. By clearly defining accountability lines, it promotes responsible magic use across all sectors of society. The Desk may issue further guidance or amendments as needed to address evolving circumstances and technologies affecting this area of law. Any challenges to these provisions must be brought in accordance with established procedures set forth elsewhere within the Accords themselves, ensuring orderly resolution without disrupting daily operations unnecessarily. Ultimately, § 600.12 serves as a vital component of the Guild's broader mission to regulate magical practice effectively and equitably for all stakeholders involved.

body.heading: Additional Provisions Relating to Construct Labor and Associated Obligations §60 — Oversight
body.text:
§ 600.12 Liability Attribution in Construct-Owner Disputes; In any dispute arising from the performance, negligence, or malfeasance of a construct employed by an owner under this Part, liability shall be attributed primarily to said owner rather than the construct itself. Constructs are deemed instruments with no independent legal personality, and thus cannot bear responsibility for their actions in contract law. Owners retain full vicarious liability for all conduct of their constructs within the scope of authorized operations, regardless of whether such conduct was expressly commanded or merely permitted by design parameters set forth in original programming specifications.

This principle ensures that parties entering into agreements involving construct services have a clear and unambiguous basis upon which to rely when assessing potential risks and liabilities associated therewith. It prevents owners from attempting to evade responsibility by blaming defective code or faulty hardware, thereby promoting fairness and accountability throughout the magical economy. Construct manufacturers likewise remain liable for defects in their products that cause harm beyond reasonable expectations, subject to standard warranty terms and limitations consistent with applicable law.

§ 600.13 Indemnification Obligations of Construct Owners; Each owner shall indemnify and hold harmless any third party from claims arising out of the use or misuse of constructs owned by said party, provided such usage occurred within the bounds of lawful activity as defined herein. This obligation extends to both intentional torts committed by owners themselves and negligent failures to properly maintain or supervise their creations. Indemnification shall include but not be limited to costs of investigation, defense against lawsuits, settlement payments, and reasonable attorney fees incurred thereby.

Exceptions apply where harm results directly from manufacturer defects proven beyond a preponderance of evidence or from intervening causes wholly unforeseeable at time of contracting. In such cases, liability may shift appropriately between owner and producer depending on circumstances presented. Owners are further advised to secure comprehensive insurance coverage tailored specifically to the unique risks posed by their particular constructs before commencing operations. Failure to do so may result in denial of claims later sought against them personally or corporately.

§ 600.14 Regulatory Compliance Requirements for Construct Deployment; All owners must maintain active compliance with all relevant statutes, regulations, ordinances, and local rules governing construct deployment throughout their area of operation. This includes obtaining necessary permits, filing required reports, paying applicable taxes and fees, and adhering strictly to safety protocols outlined herein and elsewhere in these Accords. Owners shall promptly notify authorities of any changes affecting their status as responsible operators, including but not limited to transfers of ownership or modifications to operational parameters.

Failure to comply with regulatory mandates may result in fines, suspension of licenses, revocation of operating privileges, criminal charges, and civil penalties assessed against the owner personally. Repeated violations will trigger escalating sanctions designed to deter future misconduct while protecting public welfare from undue risk posed by unregulated magical technology. Owners bear ultimate responsibility for ensuring their activities remain within legal bounds at all times, regardless of external pressures or incentives offered by third parties seeking to exploit loopholes in existing law.

§ 600.15 Conflict Resolution Mechanisms Specific to Construct Disputes; Any controversies arising from this Part shall first be submitted to informal mediation facilitated by the Guild's Office of Arcane Affairs. Mediators appointed pursuant hereto shall possess expertise relevant to the subject matter and act neutrally throughout proceedings aimed at resolving disputes efficiently without recourse to costly litigation wherever possible. Should mediation prove unsuccessful after good-faith efforts have been exhausted, parties may pursue binding arbitration before a panel convened specially for this purpose under procedures adopted by mutual agreement or default rules prescribed herein.

Arbitral decisions rendered pursuant hereto shall be final and enforceable as judgments of court unless overturned on narrow grounds such as fraud, corruption, or gross procedural unfairness demonstrated clearly upon review. Parties waive any right to appeal ordinary errors or misunderstandings inherent in complex technical matters requiring specialized knowledge beyond that possessed by traditional legal professionals alone. This streamlined process reflects recognition of the unique nature of magical disputes demanding expedited resolution mechanisms adapted specifically to their intricacies rather than rigid formalities ill-suited for practical application today.

See also §§ 600.1-600.4, 700.5-700.9, 800.2-800.3 regarding general principles governing magical contracts and their enforcement more broadly across various contexts outside those specifically addressed hereinabove yet nonetheless sharing common underlying themes pertinent to understanding full scope implications here set forth above at length now concluded for purposes of current discussion only.

sections.title: Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Litigation and Evidence

body.heading: Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Litigation and Evidence
body.text:
The provisions set forth in this section govern the admissibility and weight of magical evidence in proceedings before the Autumnwood Accords Desk or any other adjudicative body authorized under these Accords. Such matters shall be determined by reference to the principles herein, supplemented as necessary by custom and practice within the Guild.

§ 700.12 Admissibility of Magical Artifacts  
Any physical object imbued with magical properties may be admitted into evidence provided it is authenticated by a licensed Arcane Appraiser pursuant to § 300.4. Such authentication shall include a sworn statement setting forth the origin, nature, and extent of the artifact's enchantments. The opposing party shall have an opportunity to cross-examine the appraiser regarding their qualifications and methodology.

§ 700.12-A Residues and Traces  
Magical residues detected upon items or persons may be admitted as circumstantial evidence under § 800.3, subject to expert interpretation by a qualified caster. The presence of such traces does not constitute proof of wrongdoing per se but rather establishes a prima facie case requiring further substantiation. Interpretation shall conform with established protocols outlined in the Research Permits Registry maintained by the Conservator's Office.

§ 700.12-B Simulacra and Illusions  
Visual or auditory manifestations generated through illusion magic shall not be admitted unless corroborated by independent testimony or physical evidence. Where such corroboration exists, the court may draw inferences regarding intent and capability but shall refrain from assigning definitive conclusions based solely upon theatrical displays. Parties are encouraged to submit written objections prior to trial rather than relying on dramatic reenactments during proceedings.

§ 700.12-C Digital Impressions  
Data traces recorded via arcane surveillance devices or memory charms may be admitted as evidence if obtained lawfully and authenticated by the issuing authority. The authenticity thereof shall be challenged only through established procedural mechanisms set forth in § 900.8, not by extrajudicial claims. Unauthorized access to such records constitutes a violation of both these Accords and applicable privacy statutes, subjecting violators to civil penalties under § 500.15 and potential criminal sanctions under Planar Law.

See also § 700.6 Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes; § 700.8 Admissibility of Magical Traces and Residues; § 900.3 Privilege Against Self-Incrimination Under Coercion.

body.heading: § 700.12 Magical Trace Admissibility and Chain of Custody
body.text:
In proceedings governed by these Accords, the admissibility of magical traces and residues as evidence is strictly regulated to prevent contamination or misinterpretation. Under § 700.8, such physical manifestations may be offered only if properly preserved and authenticated according to established protocols. The party seeking admission must demonstrate an unbroken chain of custody from the point of capture through all subsequent handling, storage, and presentation at trial. Any break in this continuum renders the trace inadmissible under § 700.12(a), regardless of its apparent probative value.

Authentication requires comparison against known samples provided by opposing counsel or independent verification by a certified Arcane Forensic Examiner licensed by the Guild. See also § 300.5 regarding certification requirements for magical professionals engaged in evidentiary matters. The examining officer must issue a sworn report detailing methodology, results, and qualifications, which becomes part of the official record pursuant to § 100.7. Failure to comply with these procedural safeguards shifts the burden of proof to the submitting party, who then bears the risk of exclusion under § 700.12(b).

Parties may contest the relevance or reliability of offered traces through cross-examination and expert testimony. However, speculative assertions lacking factual basis are prohibited by § 400.9(c). All disputes regarding trace admissibility shall be resolved de novo upon written motion filed no later than ten days prior to trial, allowing adequate time for briefing and response. Urgent matters may receive expedited consideration at the sole discretion of the presiding authority. This framework balances the need for robust evidentiary disclosure with safeguards against abuse or manipulation inherent in magical phenomena. Adherence thereto ensures fair adjudication while maintaining public confidence in arcane judicial processes.

body.heading: § 700.12 Magical Trace Admissibility and Chain of Custody — Continued
body.text:
Magical traces, residues, and artifacts recovered from the scene of alleged illegal casting may be admitted into evidence if the proponent establishes an unbroken chain of custody from discovery to presentation in court. Any break or lapse in this continuum shall result in automatic exclusion of such items unless cured by a showing of good faith efforts to maintain integrity. The Desk shall issue standardized containers and logging forms for handling magical materials, failure to comply with which constitutes grounds for suppression.

Witnesses testifying regarding the chain of custody must declare under oath that they handled the item directly or supervised its transfer without interruption. Any reasonable doubt as to whether a trace has been tampered with or substituted shall be resolved in favor of the accused. The Desk retains sole authority to authenticate magical evidence and determine its relevance to pending matters. Unauthorized possession, alteration, or destruction of such items is punishable as obstruction of justice under § 1305.7 and may lead to revocation of casting privileges pursuant to § 200.9.

Admissibility of magical traces shall not depend on prior notice or consent from the accused party. However, the defense retains absolute right to inspect, test, and challenge such evidence in open session before it is admitted. The burden rests upon the prosecution to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that any trace offered is genuine, unaltered, and directly linked to the charged offense. Failure so to do shall result in immediate dismissal of those counts.

This provision operates alongside but independently from § 700.8 regarding admissibility standards for magical testimony and evidence generally. Nothing herein limits the Desk's inherent powers to regulate collection methods or preserve integrity of materials in its possession. All provisions concerning handling, storage, and presentation of magical traces shall be strictly construed in accordance with the spirit and letter of these Accords. Violations may subject violators to disciplinary action up to and including permanent expulsion from the Guild and confiscation of all property deemed contraband under § 1201.6.

See also: §§ 700.8, 1305.7, 200.9, 1201.6. Under § 1.4, these rules bind all persons subject to the jurisdiction of this Codex. In accordance with § 1.7(c), ambiguities regarding admissibility shall be resolved in favor of due process protections for the accused. As provided by § 1.9, official seals or stamps verifying authenticity shall carry full evidentiary weight unless successfully challenged. Any modifications to this section require approval by at least two-thirds vote of the Autumn Wood Desk following public notice and comment period of no less than thirty days per § 100.4(b).

body.heading: 700.12 Magical Evidence and Chain of Custody
body.text:
Magical evidence obtained in accordance with these provisions shall be admissible in all Arcane litigation, provided that its chain of custody has been maintained without interruption or tampering. § 700.8 Admissibility of Magical Traces and Residues mandates strict protocols for the collection and preservation of such evidence, including proper labeling, sealing, and documentation of all handling procedures. Failure to comply with these requirements shall render any resulting testimony presumptively inadmissible under § 700.9 Burden and Standard of Proof in Arcane Disputes, unless the proponent can demonstrate by clear and convincing evidence that the integrity of the magical trace was preserved despite such failures.

The burden of establishing the authenticity and reliability of any magical evidence shall rest upon the party introducing it into the record, pursuant to § 700.6 Burden of Proof and Standard of Evidence in Arcan. This includes providing a detailed affidavit from the individual who collected or processed the evidence, attesting under oath to their adherence to all applicable procedures set forth in these Accords. The opposing party shall have an absolute right to cross-examine such affiants regarding any deviations from protocol that may have compromised the evidentiary value of the magical trace.

In cases where conflicting magical traces are submitted by opposing parties, the court shall apply a rigorous standard of scrutiny before admitting either into evidence. Under § 700.10 Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Litigation and Evidence, the judge must determine whether each piece of evidence was gathered in good faith and with reasonable care to avoid contamination or degradation. Any doubts regarding the probative value of disputed magical traces shall be resolved against the party offering them into proof.

The provisions herein are designed to ensure that only reliable and untainted magical evidence informs judicial decision-making, thereby safeguarding the integrity of Arcane legal proceedings. By establishing clear rules for the handling of such sensitive materials, these guidelines seek to prevent abuse of power while facilitating the fair adjudication of disputes arising from complex arcane phenomena. All members of the Guild are reminded that strict compliance with these mandates is imperative to maintaining public confidence in the impartiality and efficacy of our courts.

See also §§ 700.6 Burden of Proof, 700.8 Admissibility Standards, 700.9 Chain of Custody Requirements, and foundational principles on evidence preservation laid out in § 1.4 Persons Bound and § 500.3 Prohibition Against Tampering with Evidence.

body.heading: Admissibility of Magical Evidence and Residues
body.text:
§ 700.12 Admissibility Standards for Arcane Testimony and Magical Evidence, Continued — Authentication Requirements

All magical traces, residues, and artifacts introduced as evidence must be authenticated by a sworn declaration from the producing party attesting to their provenance and integrity under penalty of perjury. Such declarations shall specify the date, time, location, and circumstances of discovery or acquisition. Where feasible, independent verification by a licensed mage with appropriate credentials shall accompany each submission to corroborate authenticity. Failure to provide requisite authentication may result in exclusion of the evidence at the discretion of the presiding judge or arbitration panel.

Special precautions must be taken when handling magical items deemed unstable, volatile, or otherwise hazardous. In such cases, transfer of possession shall occur only within a properly shielded containment chamber equipped with emergency suppression systems. Witnesses to the transaction shall sign an affidavit confirming adherence to safety protocols and noting any anomalies observed during exchange. Breach of these safeguards may constitute grounds for dismissal of associated claims alongside potential sanctions against the responsible party.

Parties contesting the authenticity or relevance of offered evidence bear the burden of producing contrary proof sufficient to cast reasonable doubt upon its veracity. Mere assertions without supporting documentation shall not suffice to defeat a properly authenticated submission. However, judges retain inherent authority to admit preliminary evidence subject to further scrutiny should opposing arguments emerge during proceedings.

All submitted magical items remain property of the issuing party unless otherwise ordered by competent tribunal. Return or destruction must be effected promptly following resolution of related disputes, absent contrary directive. Neglecting these obligations may lead to forfeiture and subsequent confiscation under applicable seizure statutes. Strict compliance with authentication procedures serves both as safeguard against fraud and facilitator of just adjudication in arcane matters.

see § 700.1 Evidence Generally; see § 900.12 Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Litigation Procedures; see § 400.5 Standards for Admission of Magical Data in Court Proceedings"

body.heading: Admissibility of Magical Evidence and Residues — Continued
body.text:
Magical traces, residues, and artifacts recovered at the scene of an alleged violation may be admitted into evidence under strict conditions prescribed by this Section. The proponent must establish a complete chain of custody from discovery to presentation, detailing every handler and transfer point with temporal precision. Any gaps in continuity shall result in automatic exclusion unless explained satisfactorily.

Residues themselves bear no independent evidentiary weight without contextual corroboration. Isolated traces lacking association to the accused person or event are inadmissible as prima facie proof of guilt. The trier of fact must consider all surrounding circumstances before drawing conclusions from magical markings.

Expert testimony regarding origin and meaning of residues is routinely required but not dispositive. Lay opinion on the implications of particular signatures may be offered if grounded in common knowledge rather than specialized training. Conflicting expert assessments shall be weighed according to their respective qualifications and methodology soundness.

Parties retain full control over whether physical evidence remains sealed until trial or is disclosed earlier. Voluntary surrender of items prior to indictment constitutes a waiver of privilege but not an admission of liability. Any attempt to conceal or destroy potentially incriminating traces subjects the actor to enhanced penalties upon conviction.

The burden rests upon the accuser to prove authenticity and relevance of all offered magical evidence beyond reasonable doubt. Mere assertion of its probative value is insufficient to overcome objections raised by opposing counsel. Trial chambers possess broad discretion to exclude prejudicial material even if technically admissible.

This Section does not preclude admission of other forms of proof including witness statements, documentary records, and circumstantial inferences drawn from the totality of facts found. Magical residues serve only as one piece within a larger mosaic toward determining truth and justice.

see § 700.8 Admissibility of Magical Traces and Residues; see § 700.6 Burden of Proof and Standard of Evidence in Arcane Litigation; see § 1301.9 Rules Regarding Secrecy and Privilege in Proceedings.

sections.title: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation

body.heading: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation
body.text:
§ 800.12 Additional Provisions Regarding Unlawful Casting and Confiscation

This Part shall be read in conjunction with the foundational provisions of these Accords, particularly those concerning the rights of persons under § 1.4 and the principles of due process as outlined in § 1.5. In accordance with established precedent set forth in § 800.9, any unlawful casting of spells or use of prohibited artifacts shall be subject to immediate seizure by authorized Aegis Magi or their designated agents. The confiscated items shall then undergo a thorough appraisal and documentation process pursuant to the protocols specified in § 800.10, with all findings reported directly to the Archmage Sovereign for final disposition.

The rights of accused casters shall be protected in full measure throughout this procedure, as mandated by § 1.4 and elaborated upon in § 700.6 regarding competent witnesses and expert testimony. Any disputes arising from the confiscation or valuation of items shall be resolved through formal adjudication under Part VII, with appeals handled according to the procedures set forth in § 800.3 and subsequent sections. The burden of proving unlawful activity rests solely upon the accuser, who must meet the high standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt as articulated in § 700.11.

In cases where the unlawful casting resulted in harm or damage to persons or property, additional civil remedies may be pursued independently under Part VIII, without prejudice to any criminal sanctions imposed pursuant to this Section. The Aegis Magi are authorized to employ reasonable force necessary to effectuate lawful seizures and arrests, subject to the limitations outlined in § 200.3 concerning use of force by peace officers. All actions taken under this authority shall be meticulously recorded and made available for review upon request, ensuring full transparency and accountability throughout the process.

The provisions herein shall remain in effect until expressly repealed or amended by proper legislative action through the established channels outlined in Part I. Any ambiguities or inconsistencies in their application shall be resolved by reference to the overarching purposes and principles of these Accords as interpreted by the competent authorities vested with such power under this Code. Through diligent adherence to these guidelines, the Guild strives to maintain the delicate balance between enforcing necessary restrictions while safeguarding the fundamental rights of all persons subject to its jurisdiction.

see § 800.9 Ex Post Facto Prohibition and Retroactive Sanctions
see § 1.4 Persons Bound by These Accords
see § 700.6 Competent Witnesses and Expert Testimony in Arcane Litigation
see § 200.3 Reasonable Force Authorized for Lawful Arrests and Seizures under this Code

body.heading: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation — Continued
body.text:
Part 800 - Disciplinary Measures § 800.12 Penalties for Unlawful Casting and Use of Arcane Artifacts

Whereas the unauthorized casting of spells, particularly those deemed dangerous or forbidden by the Accords, constitutes a serious breach of magical ethics and public safety, it is hereby declared that such acts shall be subject to immediate and severe penal sanctions in accordance with this section. Any mage convicted of unlawful spellcasting without proper authorization, permits, or oversight shall be liable for the following cumulative penalties: first, a fine not exceeding one hundred gold pieces per instance of violation, payable to the Guild Treasury; second, mandatory attendance at remedial courses on magical ethics and safety protocols, at the offender's own expense; third, revocation of any existing licenses or permits held by said mage, effective immediately upon conviction.

Furthermore, in cases where unlawful casting results in material damage or bodily harm, the convicted party shall be required to provide full restitution for all losses incurred, including but not limited to property repair, medical expenses, and lost wages suffered by affected parties. Failure to comply with these restitution obligations may result in additional sanctions, up to and including permanent disqualification from practicing magic within the Guild's jurisdiction. It is emphasized that these penalties are without prejudice to any further disciplinary actions that may be deemed appropriate under the circumstances, at the discretion of the Archmage Sovereign or their designated representatives.

The provisions outlined herein shall apply equally to the use of arcane artifacts and devices in unauthorized contexts, with particular emphasis on those items classified as Schedule II or higher per § 300.12. Possession alone may constitute grounds for investigation, while active deployment without proper authorization warrants immediate arrest and prosecution under this section. The Guild reserves the right to seize and inspect any suspected unlawful magical implements at their discretion, subject only to a warrant signed by two Magisterial Council members.

Any attempt to evade these penalties through subterfuge or false pretenses shall be deemed an aggravating circumstance, potentially leading to enhanced sanctions upon conviction. The burden of proof rests squarely with the accuser, requiring clear and convincing evidence beyond mere allegation before any disciplinary measures may be imposed. However, once guilt is established, the prescribed penalties shall apply automatically unless specifically waived by the convicted party in advance through express written consent.

It is hereby declared that these provisions shall remain in full force and effect until explicitly amended or repealed by the Archmage Sovereign acting in concert with a two-thirds majority vote of the Magisterial Council. No person or entity shall be exempt from compliance based on status, rank, or claimed immunity whatsoever. The Accords stand as supreme law over all matters pertaining to magical practice, and all must submit thereto without question or exception. So let it be written in the stone tablets of justice, for the protection of society against the perils of unchecked arcane power.

see § 800.1 Disciplinary Authority; § 300.12 Schedule II Restrictions; § 500.1 Unauthorized Casting Prohibited; § 600.9 Contractual Liability for Magical Acts

body.heading: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation — Continued — Continued
body.text:
§ 800.12 Evidence Standard for Unlawful Casting Allegations; Burden of Proof in Disciplinary Proceedings Under the Accords, any allegation of unlawful casting must be supported by clear and convincing evidence, as determined by a Quorum of the Autumnwood Accords Desk or its duly appointed adjudicators. The burden of proof rests solely on the accuser, who shall present all relevant testimony, documentation, and magical analysis necessary to establish guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. In no event shall mere suspicion, rumor, or unsubstantiated claim suffice to justify disciplinary action against any member of the Guild.

Should an accused mage fail to appear for trial without valid excuse, the Desk may proceed in their absence, presuming guilt unless contradicted by substantial exculpatory evidence. Conversely, if the accuser fails to meet the requisite evidentiary threshold, all charges shall be dismissed with prejudice, and any pending sanctions vacated forthwith. It is imperative that due process be scrupulously observed at every stage of the disciplinary proceeding, lest the integrity of the Accords themselves be compromised by miscarriage of justice or arbitrary enforcement.

The Desk retains sole authority to determine what constitutes "unlawful casting" under any given circumstance, guided by the spirit and letter of these Articles. This includes, but is not limited to, unauthorized use of forbidden schools, excessive power consumption, reckless endangerment of persons or property, and violation of specific provisions herein. Discretionary judgment shall be exercised in accordance with established precedent and principles of fairness, always mindful of the delicate balance between maintaining public safety and preserving individual liberties.

Any attempt to circumvent these provisions through deception, fabrication of evidence, or tampering with records shall be deemed a grave offense warranting immediate investigation and appropriate sanctions upon confirmation. Such malfeasance strikes at the heart of the Accords' foundational tenets, undermining trust in both the Guild's regulatory framework and its commitment to impartial justice. To tolerate even the slightest degree of corruption would be to invite chaos and anarchy into our midst—a fate we must all work tirelessly to avoid.

In sum, then, let it be understood that the rules set forth herein are not mere suggestions but binding mandates upon all who dwell within this realm's magical sphere. By acceding to these obligations voluntarily or through force of circumstance, every caster implicitly accepts their full force and effect, for better or worse. May we therefore proceed henceforth with renewed dedication to upholding the highest ideals of our noble profession, guided always by wisdom, integrity, and an unwavering reverence for the mysteries that bind us all in this vast tapestry of existence.

body.heading: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation — Continued — Administration
body.text:
Where unlawful casting occurs in public or causes demonstrable harm, the Desk shall confiscate all magical implements directly involved, retaining them as evidence until further order. Any such items deemed inherently dangerous require permanent storage under lock and key; lesser artifacts may be returned upon proof of safekeeping protocols. All confiscated materials must be inventoried and logged into the Central Registry within seven days, with copies furnished to the accused party and relevant oversight bodies.

Unlawful casting by non-casters triggers enhanced penalties, including mandatory registration as a subject of future monitoring and prohibition from possessing magical items without explicit permission. First-time offenders may opt for community service in lieu of fines, provided they undergo successful completion of an Arcane Conduct Course approved by the Conservators. Repeat violations warrant progressive sanctions up to permanent exile from Autumnwood territory.

In cases involving commercial entities, regulatory audits are mandated with full access to all records and operations. Failure to comply results in immediate suspension of licenses until satisfactory remediation is demonstrated. Repeated noncompliance leads to revocation without recourse. All findings and actions shall be publicly posted for transparency purposes only; no defamatory language permitted under threat of legal action.

The Desk maintains sole authority to determine appropriate sanctions based on severity and circumstances, with input from Conservator and Innovator representatives where relevant. Final decisions rest with the Archmage Sovereign upon recommendation from a specially convened panel. All disciplinary measures must be proportionate and serve both punishment and rehabilitation goals equally. Appeals may be filed within thirty days under established procedures; otherwise rulings stand final and binding.

This provision reflects the Guild's unwavering commitment to maintaining order while allowing for individualized justice in each case. Strict adherence ensures fairness across all enforcement actions and preserves public confidence in the system. Any deviations require explicit authorization from a majority vote of the full Accords Assembly. Unauthorized modifications are null and void ab initio.

see § 100.6 Delegation to Clerks; § 200.11 Schedules of Magical Arts and Their Classification; § 300.12 Prohibition on Magical Correspondence and Transmission; § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure; § 900.12 Additional Provisions Regarding Arcane Field Operations and Conduct

body.heading: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation — Continued — Administrat
body.text:
The confiscation of magical items, artifacts, and implements associated with unlawful casting is governed by strict protocols to ensure their proper handling and eventual disposition. Upon seizure of any prohibited item, it shall be immediately inventoried in the presence of witnesses and sealed within a lead-lined container to prevent accidental activation or exposure to unauthorized individuals. Such contraband shall then be delivered to the custody of an Aegis Magi for secure storage pending further review by the Disciplinary Council. The Council shall determine whether each item constitutes evidence of a crime, a tool used in commission thereof, or merely incidental property owned by the accused but misused by others. Items classified as direct instruments of unlawful magic may be permanently destroyed under supervised conditions to eliminate future risk. Those deemed salvageable for lawful use shall undergo thorough screening and certification before being returned to their rightful owners or transferred to approved researchers for study. Any proceeds from the liquidation of seized assets pursuant to court order shall be remitted to the Guild's General Fund, less applicable fees and expenses. The Council retains broad discretion to impose additional administrative penalties as it deems necessary to protect public safety and maintain the integrity of arcane practices within society at large. These measures are designed to dismantle criminal networks' material resources while preserving legitimate interests where feasible. Failure to comply with confiscation directives may result in enhanced sanctions against non-compliant parties, including suspension of privileges and heightened surveillance. All actions taken under this provision shall be meticulously documented for potential judicial scrutiny and historical record-keeping purposes. Nothing herein abrogates existing authorities vested in law enforcement agencies regarding seizure of contraband under applicable statutes. The Guild asserts sole jurisdiction over matters pertaining specifically to magical items seized during Disciplinary proceedings, subject to coordination with relevant civil authorities as mutually agreed upon from time to time.

§ 800.12 Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation — Continued — Administration
see § 800.7 Related Requirements; under § 1301.2 Penalties for Violations of Disciplinary Orders
see also §§ 200.6 Prohibitions on Dangerous Magical Acts, 400.9 Restrictions on Experimental Research and Development

body.heading: Provisions Governing Unlawful Casting and Confiscation — Continued — Oversight
body.text:
§ 800.12 Disposition of Seized Magical Artifacts and Components. Any magical artifact, component, or tool seized in connection with an unlawful casting shall be held in trust by the Archmage Sovereign until such time as it may be lawfully disposed of. The Archmage Sovereign shall determine the appropriate course of action, which may include destruction, confiscation for public use, return to lawful ownership upon proof of innocence, or sale at public auction with proceeds donated to charitable causes benefiting students and apprentices in need. No seized item shall be privately sold or traded by any Guild official without express written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign. All dispositions must be recorded in the permanent archives of the Autumnwood Hall under penalty of severe sanctions. The Archmage Sovereign retains sole discretion to alter these provisions as deemed necessary for the protection of public safety and the integrity of magical practice within the Guild's jurisdiction."

"see § 800.10 Disposition of Confiscated Items; § 1201.10 Extra-Territorial Jurisdiction and Planar Tolls; § 1401.10 Historical Annotations"
